For now I could stretch out my hand and strike you and your people with pestilence, and you would be cut off from the earth. But for this reason I have raised you up, to show in you my power, and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth. Do you still detain my people and will not let them go? Behold, tomorrow at this same hour I will cause it to rain very heavy hail, such as has not been in Egypt from the day it was founded until now. Send therefore now and gather your cattle and all that you have in the field, for every man and beast and all that is in the field and not brought home, the hail shall fall upon them and they shall die. He that feared the word of the Lord among the servants of Pharaoh made his servants and his cattle flee into houses. But he that regarded not the word of the Lord left his servants and his cattle in the field. And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch out your hand toward heaven, that there may be hail in all the land of Egypt upon men and upon beasts and upon every herb of the field throughout the land of Egypt. And Moses stretched out his rod toward heaven, and the Lord sent thunder and hail and fire running along the ground, and the Lord rained hail upon the land of Egypt. And the hail and fire mixed together were so grievous that there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation. And the hail smote throughout all the land of Egypt all that was in the field, both man and beast. And the hail smote every herb of the field and broke every tree of the field. Only in the land of Goshen where the children of Israel were, was there no hail. And Pharaoh sent and called for Moses and Aaron and said to them: I have sinned this time. The Lord is righteous, and I and my people are wicked. Pray to the Lord that there be no more mighty thunderings and hail, and I will let you go and you shall stay no longer. And Moses said to him: As soon as I am gone out of the city I will spread out my hands to the Lord, and the thunder shall cease and there shall be no more hail, that you may know that the earth is the Lord's. But as for you and your servants, I know that you do not yet fear the Lord God. And the flax and the barley were struck, for the barley was in the ear and the flax was in bud. But the wheat and the rye were not struck, for they were not yet grown up. And Moses went out from Pharaoh and from the city and spread out his hands to the Lord, and the thunder and hail ceased and the rain was no longer poured upon the earth. And when Pharaoh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunder had ceased, he sinned yet more and hardened his heart, he and his servants. Neither did Pharaoh let the children of Israel go, as the Lord had spoken by Moses.

And the Lord said to Moses. Chapter 10. Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the heart of his servants, that I might show these my signs before him, and that you may tell in the hearing of your son and of your son's son what things I have wrought in Egypt, and my signs which I have done among them, that you may know that I am the Lord. And Moses and Aaron came in to Pharaoh and said to him: Thus says the Lord God of the Hebrews: How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go that they may serve me. But if you refuse to let my people go, behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your borders, which shall cover the face of the earth so that one cannot see the earth, and

Exodus.

They shall eat what remained from the hail. For it shall devour all the trees that grow in the fields, and shall fill your houses, and the houses of all your servants, and of all the Egyptians: as neither your fathers nor your grandfathers have seen, since the day they were born upon the earth until this day. And he turned away and went out from Pharaoh. And the servants of Pharaoh said to him: How long shall we endure this scandal? Let the people go, so that they may sacrifice to the Lord their God. Do you not see that Egypt is ruined? And Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, and he said to them: Go and sacrifice to the Lord your God. But who are they that shall go? Moses said: We will go with our young and our old, with our sons and daughters, with our flocks and herds, for it is a feast of the Lord our God. And Pharaoh answered: So be the Lord with you, as I shall let you go with your little ones. It is clear that you have evil intent. It shall not be so: go you that are men, and sacrifice to the Lord, for this is what you yourselves desired. And they were cast out immediately from Pharaoh's presence. And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come upon the land and devour every herb that is left after the hail. And Moses stretched his rod over the land of Egypt, and the Lord brought a burning wind all that day and night, and when it was morning, the burning wind had raised the locusts. And they came up over the whole land of Egypt and rested in all the borders thereof, innumerable: such as had not been before that time, nor shall be after. And they covered the whole face of the earth, laying waste everything. So all the grass of the earth was devoured, and whatever fruit was on the trees, which the hail had left. Nothing green remained on any tree or herb of the earth in all of Egypt.

Then Pharaoh in great haste called Moses and Aaron, and said to them: I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you. Forgive me this sin also this time, and pray to the Lord your God to take away from me this death. And Moses went out from Pharaoh and prayed to the Lord. And the Lord made a very strong west wind blow, and it took the locusts and cast them into the Red Sea. There remained not one locust in all the borders of Egypt. And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he did not let the children of Israel go. And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and let there be darkness over the land of Egypt so thick that it may be felt. And Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven, and there came horrible darkness in all the land of Egypt. For three days no man saw his brother, nor moved himself from the place where he was. But wherever the children of Israel dwelt, there was light. And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron and said to them: Go, sacrifice to the Lord. Let your flocks and herds remain: let your little ones go with you. Moses said: You shall also give us sacrifices and burnt offerings, that we may sacrifice to the Lord our God. All our flocks shall go with us. There shall not a hoof be left behind, for they are necessary for the worship of the Lord our God: especially since we do not know what must be offered until we come to the very place. And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he would not let them go. And Pharaoh said to Moses: Get away from me, and beware that you see my face no more. On whatever day you shall appear before me, you shall die. Moses said: So shall it be as you have spoken, I will see your face no more. Chapter 11.
And the Lord said to Moses: I will yet bring one more plague upon Pharaoh

. Exodus .

and Egypt: and after these things he will let you go, and will thrust you out. You shall say to all the people: Let every man ask of his neighbor, and every woman of her neighbor, vessels of silver and of gold, and garments. And the Lord will give favor to his people in the sight of the Egyptians. And Moses was a very great man in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh's servants and of all the people. And he said: Thus says the Lord: At midnight I will enter into Egypt. And every firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne, even to the firstborn of the handmaid who is at the mill, and all the firstborn of the cattle. And there shall be a great cry in all the land of Egypt, such as never was before, nor ever shall be. But among all the children of Israel, not a dog shall bark, from man even to beast: that you may know how wonderful a difference the Lord makes between the Egyptians and Israel. And all these your servants shall come down to me, and shall worship me, saying: Go forth, you and all the people that is under you. After that we shall go out. And he went out from Pharaoh very angry. And the Lord said to Moses: Pharaoh will not hear you, that many signs may be done in the land of Egypt. And Moses and Aaron did all the wonders and signs that are written, before Pharaoh: and the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the children of Israel go out of his land. CHAPTER XII.

And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt: This month shall be to you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year. Speak to the whole assembly of the children of Israel, and say to them: On the tenth day of this month let every man take a lamb by their families and houses. But if the number is less than may suffice to eat the lamb, he shall take his neighbor who is joined to his house, according to the number of souls which may be enough to eat the lamb. And the lamb shall be

without blemish: a male of one year. According to which rite also you shall take a kid: and you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month: and the whole multitude of the children of Israel shall sacrifice it in the evening. And they shall take of the blood and put it upon both the side posts and on the upper door posts of the houses, wherein they shall eat it. And they shall eat the flesh that night, roasted at fire, and unleavened bread with wild lettuce. You shall not eat thereof anything raw, nor boiled in water, but only roasted at fire: the head with the feet and the entrails thereof. Neither shall there remain anything of it until morning. If there be anything left, you shall burn it with fire. And thus you shall eat it: with your loins girded, and shoes on your feet, holding staves in your hands, and you shall eat in haste: for it is the Phase (that is, the Passage) of the Lord. And I will pass through the land of Egypt that night, and will kill every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast: and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments: I am the Lord. And the blood shall be unto you for a sign in the houses where you shall be: and I shall see the blood, and shall pass over you: and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I shall strike the land of Egypt. And this day shall be for a memorial to you: and you shall keep it as a feast to the Lord in your generations, with an everlasting observance. Seven days shall you eat unleavened bread. In the first day there shall be no leaven in your houses. Whoever shall eat anything leavened, that soul shall perish out of Israel, from the first day until the seventh day. The first day shall be holy and solemn, and the seventh day shall be kept with the same solemnity. You shall do no work in them, except those things that belong to eating: and you shall observe unleavened bread. For on this same day I will bring your army out of the land of Egypt: and

Exodus.

Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel: let them turn back and encamp before Phihahiroth, which is between Migdol and the sea, over against Baal-zephon. In its sight you shall pitch your tents over against the sea. And Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel: They are hemmed in by the land, the desert has shut them in. And I will harden his heart, and he will pursue you, and I will be glorified in Pharaoh and in all his host, and the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord. And they did so. And it was told the king of Egypt that the people had fled. And the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was changed toward the people, and they said: What have we done, that we let Israel go from serving us? And he made ready his chariot, and took all his people with him. And he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt, and captains over all of them. And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued after the children of Israel. And the children of Israel went out with a high hand. And the Egyptians pursued after them, and overtook them encamping by the sea. All the horses and chariots of Pharaoh, and his entire army, were at Phihahiroth, before Baal-zephon. And when Pharaoh drew near, the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and behold, the Egyptians were marching after them, and they were very afraid. And they cried out to the Lord, and they said to Moses: Were there no graves in Egypt, that you have taken us away to die in the wilderness? Why did you do this to us, to bring us out of Egypt? Is not this the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying: Leave us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians? For it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness. And Moses said to the people: Fear not. Stand still and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will show to you today. For the Egyptians whom you have seen today, you shall see them no more forever. The Lord will fight for you, and you shall hold your peace. And the Lord said to Moses: Why do you cry to me? Speak to the children of Israel, that they go forward. And lift up your rod, and stretch out your hand over the sea, and divide it, and the children of Israel shall go on dry ground through the midst of the sea. And I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians, and they shall follow them, and I will get glory over Pharaoh, and over all his host, and over his chariots, and over his horsemen. And the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, when I have gotten glory over Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen. And the angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, removed and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud went from before their face and stood behind them. And it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel. And the cloud was dark to the Egyptians but gave light by night to the Israelites, so that the one did not come near the other all that night. And when Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, the Lord drove the sea back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land. And the waters were divided. And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground, and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left. And the Egyptians pursued and went in after them into the midst of the sea, all Pharaoh's horses, his chariots, and his horsemen. And in the morning watch, the Lord looked down upon the host of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of cloud, and confused the host of the Egyptians, and took off their chariot wheels, so that they drove them heavily. And the Egyptians said: Let us flee from before Israel, for the Lord fights for them against the Egyptians. And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch out your hand over the sea, that the waters may come back upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots, and upon their horsemen. And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its full depth at the break of dawn.

. Exodus .

And the Egyptians fleeing met the waters, and the Lord overwhelmed them in the midst of the waves. And the waters returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen of all the army of Pharaoh who had followed them into the sea: not so much as one of them remained. But the children of Israel had walked on dry land through the midst of the sea, and the waters were a wall to them on the right hand and on the left. Thus the Lord delivered Israel that day out of the hands of the Egyptians: and they saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore. And Israel saw the great work which the Lord had done against the Egyptians, and the people feared the Lord, and they believed the Lord and his servant Moses. Chapter 15. Then Moses and the children of Israel sang this song to the Lord, and said: Let us sing to the Lord, for he is gloriously magnificent: the horse and his rider he has thrown into the sea. The Lord is my strength and my praise, and he has become my salvation. This is my God and I will glorify him: the God of my father, and I will exalt him. The Lord is as a man of war: Almighty is his name. Pharaoh's chariots and his army he has cast into the sea: his chosen captains are drowned in the Red Sea: the depths have covered them, they sank to the bottom like a stone. Your right hand, O Lord, is magnificent in strength: your right hand, O Lord, has slain the enemy. And in the multitude of your glory you have overthrown your adversaries: you sent your wrath, which devoured them like stubble. And with the blast of your fury the waters were heaped together: the flood stood upright as a heap: the depths were congealed in the heart of the sea. The enemy said: I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoils: my soul shall be filled. I will draw my sword: my hand shall destroy them. Your wind blew and the sea covered them: they sank like lead in the mighty waters. Who is like to you among the strong, O Lord: who is like to you, glorious in holiness, terrible and praiseworthy, working wonders? You stretched out your hand, and the earth swallowed them. In your mercy you have guided the people which you have redeemed: and in your strength you have carried them to your holy habitation. Nations rose up and were angry: sorrows took hold of the inhabitants of Philistia. Then the princes of Edom were troubled: trembling seized the stout men of Moab: all the inhabitants of Canaan became stiff. Let fear and dread fall upon them, in the greatness of your arm: let them become immovable as a stone: until your people pass over, O Lord, until this your people pass over, whom you possess. You shall bring them in and plant them in the mountain of your inheritance, in the most firm habitation which you have made for yourself, O Lord: your sanctuary, O Lord, which your hands have established. The Lord shall reign forever and ever. For Pharaoh went in on horseback with his chariots and horsemen into the sea: and the Lord brought back the waters of the sea upon them: but the children of Israel walked on dry land in the midst of it. So Mary the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand: and all the women went forth after her with timbrels and with dances: and she led them in song, saying: Sing to the Lord, for he is gloriously magnificent: the horse and his rider he has thrown into the sea. Then Moses led Israel onward from the Red Sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Sur. And they marched three days through the wilderness and found no water. And they came to Mara, and they could not drink the waters of Mara because they were bitter. Wherefore he gave a name also suitable to the place, calling it Mara, that is, bitterness. And the people murmured against Moses, saying: What shall we drink? But he cried to the Lord, who showed him a piece of wood: which when he had cast into the waters, they were turned into sweetness.

Exodus.

These are the statutes and ordinances, and there he tested them, saying: If you will listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and do what is right before him, and obey his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of the diseases upon you that I put upon Egypt. For I am the Lord your healer. Then the children of Israel came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there by the water. Chapter 16.

And the whole congregation of the children of Israel set out from Elim and came to the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they had departed from the land of Egypt. And the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness. And the children of Israel said to them: Would that we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the pots of meat and ate bread to the full. For you have brought us out into this wilderness to kill this whole assembly with hunger. Then the Lord said to Moses: Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you. Let the people go out and gather a day's portion every day, that I may test them, whether they will walk in my law or not. On the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it shall be twice as much as they gather daily. And Moses and Aaron said to all the children of Israel: In the evening you shall know that the Lord has brought you out of the land of Egypt, and in the morning you shall see the glory of the Lord, because he has heard your murmuring against the Lord. For what are we, that you murmur against us? And Moses said: The Lord will give you meat to eat in the evening, and in the morning bread to the full, because the Lord has heard your murmurings which you murmur against him. For what are we? Your murmuring is not against us but against the Lord. And Moses said to Aaron: Say to the whole congregation of the children of Israel: Come near before the Lord, for he has heard your murmuring. And as Aaron spoke to the whole congregation of the children of Israel, they looked toward the wilderness, and behold, the glory of the Lord appeared in the cloud. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: I have heard the murmuring of the children of Israel. Speak to them and say: At evening you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be filled with bread, and you shall know that I am the Lord your God. In the evening quail came up and covered the camp, and in the morning dew lay around the camp. And when the dew had gone up, there was on the face of the wilderness a fine, flake-like thing, fine as frost on the ground. When the children of Israel saw it, they said to one another: Manna — which means: What is this? For they did not know what it was. Moses said to them: This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat. This is what the Lord has commanded: Gather of it, each one of you, as much as he can eat; an omer per person, according to the number of persons, each of you shall take for those in his tent. And the children of Israel did so; they gathered, some more, some less. But when they measured it with an omer, whoever had gathered much had nothing left over, and whoever had gathered little had no lack. Each of them gathered as much as he could eat. And Moses said to them: Let none of it be left till the morning. But they did not listen to Moses. Some left part of it till the morning, and it bred worms and stank. And Moses was angry with them. Morning by morning they gathered it, each as much as he could eat; but when the sun grew hot, it melted. On the sixth day they gathered twice as much food.

Exodus.

These were double portions: that is, two gomors for each person. All the leaders of the assembly came and told Moses. He said to them: This is what the Lord has spoken. Tomorrow is the rest of the holy sabbath of the Lord. Bake what you will bake today, and boil what you will boil; and whatever remains, lay it up for yourselves to be kept until the morning. They did so as Moses commanded, and it did not rot, nor was there any worm in it. Moses said: Eat it today, because today is the sabbath of the Lord: today you will not find it in the field. Six days you shall gather it: but on the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord, therefore you shall find none. And it came to pass that on the seventh day some of the people went out to gather and they found none. And the Lord said to Moses: How long will you refuse to keep my commandments and my laws? See that the Lord has given you the sabbath, and therefore on the sixth day he gives you double bread. Let every man stay in his own place: let no man go out of his place on the seventh day. And the people rested on the seventh day. And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna. And it was like coriander seed, white, and the taste thereof was like to flour with honey. And Moses said: This is the word which the Lord has commanded: Fill a gomor of it, and let it be kept for your generations hereafter, that they may know the bread wherewith I fed you in the wilderness, when you were brought forth out of the land of Egypt. And Moses said to Aaron: Take a vessel and put manna into it, as much as a gomor can hold: and lay it up before the Lord, to be kept for your generations, as the Lord commanded Moses. And Aaron laid it up in the tabernacle to be kept. And the children of Israel ate manna forty years, until they came to a habitable land. They were nourished with this food until they reached the borders of the land of Canaan. Now a gomor is the tenth part of an ephah. Chapter XVII. And all the multitude of the children of Israel set forward from the desert of Sin, by their marches according to the word of the Lord, and encamped in Raphidim, where there was no water for the people to drink. And the people quarreled with Moses, and said: Give us water that we may drink. And Moses said to them: Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you tempt the Lord? So the people thirsted there for water, and murmured against Moses, saying: Why did you make us come out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our livestock with thirst? And Moses cried to the Lord, saying: What shall I do with this people? Yet a little more and they will stone me. And the Lord said to Moses: Go before the people and take with you some of the elders of Israel: and take in your hand the rod wherewith you struck the river, and go. Behold I will stand there before you, upon the rock Horeb: and you shall strike the rock, and water shall come out of it that the people may drink. Moses did so before the elders of Israel. And he called the name of that place Temptation: because of the quarreling of the children of Israel, and because they tempted the Lord, saying: Is the Lord among us or not? Then Amalek came and fought against Israel in Raphidim. And Moses said to Joshua: Choose men and go out and fight against Amalek: tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the rod of God in my hand. Joshua did as Moses had spoken and fought against Amalek. And Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill. And when Moses lifted up his hands, Israel prevailed: but if he let them down a little, Amalek prevailed. And Moses' hands were heavy. So they took a stone and placed it

. Exodus .

Over all Israel he appointed them as leaders of the people — tribunes, centurions, those over fifty, and those over ten — who judged the people at all times. Whatever was more serious they brought to him, but easier matters they decided themselves. And he dismissed his kinsman, who departed and returned to his own land.

In the third month of the departure of Israel from the land of Egypt, on that very day, they came into the wilderness of Sinai. Setting out from Rephidim and arriving at the wilderness of Sinai, they encamped in the same place; and Israel pitched its tents there, opposite the mountain. Moses went up to God, and the Lord called to him from the mountain, saying: "This is what you shall say to the house of Jacob, and announce to the children of Israel: You yourselves have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I carried you on eagle's wings and took you to myself. If therefore you will hear my voice and keep my covenant, you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. These are the words you shall speak to the children of Israel." Moses came and called together the elders of the people, and set forth all the words which the Lord had commanded him. And all the people answered together: "Everything the Lord has said, we will do." When Moses brought back the words of the people to the Lord, the Lord said to him: "Now I will come to you in a dense cloud, so that the people may hear me speaking with you, and may believe you forever." Moses then reported the words of the people to the Lord, who said to him: "Go to the people and sanctify them today and tomorrow; let them wash their garments and be ready for the third day. For on the third day the Lord will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people. You shall set boundaries for them all around and warn them: Take care not to go up the mountain or touch its border. Whoever touches the mountain shall surely die. No hand shall touch him, but he shall be stoned or shot with arrows — whether beast or man, he shall not live. When the ram's horn sounds a long blast, they may go up the mountain." Moses came down from the mountain to the people and sanctified them. They washed their garments, and he said to them: "Be ready for the third day; do not approach your wives."

By the third day it was morning, and there was thunder and lightning and a very thick cloud over the mountain, and the sound of a very loud trumpet, so that all the people in the camp trembled. Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain. Mount Sinai was completely wrapped in smoke, because the Lord had descended upon it in fire; and the smoke went up like the smoke of a furnace. The whole mountain shook violently, and the sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder. Moses spoke and God answered him. The Lord descended on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain, and called Moses to the top of the mountain. When Moses had gone up, the Lord said to him: "Go down and warn the people, lest they break through to see the Lord and many of them perish. And let the priests who approach the Lord sanctify themselves, lest the Lord break out against them." Moses said to the Lord: "The people cannot come up to Mount Sinai, for you yourself warned us, saying: Set boundaries around the mountain and consecrate it." The Lord said to him: "Go, get down, and then come up, you and Aaron with you. But do not let the priests or the people break through to come up to the Lord, lest he break out against them." So Moses went down to the people.

. Exodus .

He shall provide the girl with marriage rights and clothing, and he shall not deny the price of her purity. If he does not do these three things, she shall go out free, without payment. Whoever strikes a man intending to kill him shall surely die. But if he did not lie in wait, but God delivered him into his hand, I will appoint for you a place where he may flee. If anyone schemes and kills his neighbor deliberately, you shall take him even from my altar to die. Whoever strikes his father or his mother shall surely die. Whoever curses his father or his mother shall surely die. Whoever steals a man and sells him, if he is found in his hand, shall surely die. If men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone or with his fist, and he does not die but is confined to bed: if he rises again and walks outside with his staff, the one who struck him shall be clear, only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall provide for his healing. If a man strikes his male or female servant with a rod, so that he dies under his hand, he shall be punished. However, if he survives a day or two, he shall not be punished, for he is his property. If men fight and hurt a pregnant woman so that she gives birth prematurely, yet no lasting harm follows, he shall be punished according to what the woman's husband demands and as the judges determine. But if any lasting harm follows, then you shall give life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, burn for burn, wound for wound, stripe for stripe. If a man strikes the eye of his male or female servant and destroys it, he shall let him go free for the sake of his eye. If he knocks out the tooth of his male or female servant, he shall let him go free for the sake of his tooth. If a bull gores a man or woman to death, the bull shall surely be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the bull shall not be held responsible. But if the bull had a habit of goring in the past, and its owner had been warned but did not confine it, and it kills a man or woman: the bull shall be stoned, and its owner shall also be put to death. If a ransom is imposed on him, then he shall give for the redemption of his life whatever is demanded of him. Whether it gores a son or a daughter, he shall be dealt with according to the same judgment. If the bull gores a male or female servant, the owner shall give thirty shekels of silver to their master, and the bull shall be stoned. If a man opens a pit or digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or donkey falls into it: the owner of the pit shall make it good; he shall give money to their owner, and the dead animal shall be his. If one man's bull injures another's bull so that it dies: then they shall sell the live bull and divide its price equally, and the dead animal they shall also divide. But if it was known that the bull had been in the habit of goring in the past, and its owner has not kept it in: he shall pay bull for bull, and the dead animal shall be his own. Chapter XXII.

If a man steals an ox or a sheep and kills it or sells it, he shall restore five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep. If a thief is caught breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there shall be no bloodguilt for him. But if it happens after sunrise, there shall be bloodguilt. He who stole shall make full restitution; if he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft. If the stolen animal is found alive in his possession, whether it is an ox or donkey or sheep, he shall pay double. If a man causes a field or vineyard to be grazed over, or lets his animal loose and it feeds in another man's field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard. If fire breaks out and catches in thorns so that the stacked grain

Exodus

...or those grazing in fields: he who kindled the fire shall pay the damage. If anyone entrusts money or goods to a neighbor for safekeeping, and they are stolen from the one who received them: if the thief is found, he shall pay double. If the thief is not found, the master of the house shall be brought before God and shall swear that he did not lay his hand on his neighbor's goods — whether ox, donkey, sheep, garment, or anything that could cause loss. The case of both parties shall come before God, and whoever God declares guilty shall pay double to the other. If anyone gives his neighbor a donkey, ox, sheep, or any animal to keep, and it dies or is injured or is driven away without anyone witnessing it: an oath before the Lord shall be made between them that he did not lay hands on his neighbor's goods, and the owner shall accept the oath, and no restitution shall be required. But if it was stolen, he shall make restitution to the owner. If it was torn by a beast, let him bring evidence of what was killed, and he shall not restore it. If anyone borrows an animal from his neighbor and it is injured or dies while the owner is not present, he shall be required to make restitution. But if the owner was present, he shall not restore it — especially if it was hired, for the hire covers the loss. If a man seduces a virgin who is not yet betrothed and lies with her, he shall provide her dowry and take her as his wife. If her father refuses to give her to him, he shall pay money equal to the dowry of virgins. You shall not permit a sorceress to live. Whoever lies with an animal shall be put to death. Whoever sacrifices to other gods shall be killed, except to the Lord alone. You shall not oppress a stranger, nor afflict him, for you yourselves were strangers in the land of Egypt. You shall not afflict any widow or orphan. If you afflict them, they will cry out to me, and I will hear their cry, and my anger will blaze and I will strike you with the sword, and your wives shall become widows and your children fatherless. If you lend money to my poor people who dwell with you, you shall not act as a creditor to them, nor charge them interest. If you take your neighbor's garment as a pledge, you shall return it to him before sunset. For it is his only covering, the cloak for his body; in what else shall he sleep? And if he cries out to me, I will hear him, for I am compassionate. You shall not revile God, nor curse a ruler of your people. You shall not delay to offer your tithes and firstfruits. The firstborn of your sons you shall give to me. Likewise with your oxen and sheep. Let them remain seven days with their mother; on the eighth day you shall give them to me. You shall be holy people to me. You shall not eat meat torn by beasts in the field; you shall throw it to the dogs.

Chapter 23

You shall not spread a false report. Do not join hands with a wicked man to be a malicious witness. You shall not follow a crowd in doing evil, nor in a lawsuit side with the majority so as to pervert justice. You shall not show partiality to a poor man in his lawsuit. If you come across your enemy's ox or donkey going astray, you shall bring it back to him. If you see the donkey of one who hates you lying down under its burden, you shall not leave him; you shall surely help him. You shall not pervert justice for the poor. Keep far from falsehood. Do not kill the innocent and righteous, for I will not acquit the wicked. And you shall not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and subverts the cause of the righteous. You shall not oppress a foreigner. You know the heart of a foreigner, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. For six years you shall sow your land and gather its produce, but in the seventh year you shall let it rest and lie fallow, so that the poor of your people may eat;

Exodus.

And they were obedient. He then took the blood and sprinkled it upon the people. And he said: This is the blood of the covenant which the Lord has made with you concerning all these words. And Moses went up, and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel: and they saw the God of Israel. Under his feet there was as it were a work of sapphire stone, and as it were the clear sky. And upon the nobles of the children of Israel he laid not his hand: and they saw God, and did eat and drink. And the Lord said to Moses: Come up to me on the mountain and be there: and I will give you two tables of stone and the law and the commandments which I have written, that you may teach them to the children of Israel. And Moses rose up and Joshua his minister: and Moses going up into the mountain of God, said to the ancients: Wait here until we return to you. You have Aaron and Hur with you: if any question shall arise, you shall refer it to them. And when Moses had gone up, a cloud covered the mountain: and the glory of the Lord dwelt upon Sinai, covering it with a cloud for six days. And on the seventh day he called him out of the midst of the cloud. And the sight of the glory of the Lord was like a burning fire upon the top of the mount, in the eyes of the children of Israel. And Moses, entering into the midst of the cloud, went up into the mountain: and he was there forty days and forty nights. Chapter 25.

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, that they bring firstfruits to me. From every man that offers of his own accord, you shall take them. And these are the things you must receive: Gold and silver and brass: violet and purple and scarlet twice dyed, and fine linen, and goats' hair: and rams' skins dyed red, and violet colored skins: and setim wood: oil to make lights: spices for ointment, and for sweet smelling incense:

Onyx stones and precious stones for the adorning of the ephod and the rational. And they shall make me a sanctuary, and I will dwell in the midst of them. According to all the likeness of the tabernacle which I will show you, and of all the vessels for the worship thereof: and thus you shall make it. Frame an ark of setim wood, the length whereof shall be two cubits and a half: the breadth, a cubit and a half: the height likewise, a cubit and a half. And you shall overlay it with the purest gold within and without: and over it you shall make a golden crown round about. And you shall cast four rings of gold, which you shall put at the four corners of the ark. Two rings shall be on the one side, and two on the other. You shall make bars also of setim wood: and shall overlay them with gold. And you shall put them in through the rings that are in the sides of the ark, that it may be carried on them. And they shall always be in the rings, and they shall never be drawn out of them. And you shall put in the ark the testimony which I will give you. You shall make also a propitiatory of the purest gold: the length thereof shall be two cubits and a half, and the breadth a cubit and a half. You shall make also two cherubims of beaten gold, on the two sides of the oracle. Let one cherub be on the one side, and the other on the other. Let them cover both sides of the propitiatory, spreading their wings, and covering the oracle, and let them look one towards the other, their faces being turned towards the propitiatory wherewith the ark is to be covered, in which you shall put the testimony that I will give you. Thence will I give orders, and will speak to you over the propitiatory, and from the midst of the two cherubims, which shall be upon the ark of the testimony, all things which I will command the children of Israel by you. You shall make a table also of setim wood of two cubits in length, and a cubit in breadth, and a cubit and a half in height: and you shall overlay it with the finest gold, and you shall make to it a golden ledge round about: and to the ledge itself

· Exodus ·

a crown of a hand's breadth in height all around, and over it a golden border. You shall also make four golden rings, and place them on the four feet of the table, two on each side. Below the crown shall be golden rings, through which the poles are inserted to carry the table. You shall also make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, so that the table may be carried. You shall make its plates and dishes, its pitchers and bowls with which to pour drink offerings; you shall make them of pure gold. And you shall set the bread of the Presence on the table before me always. You shall also make a lampstand of pure hammered gold: its shaft and its branches, its cups, its buds and its flowers shall be of one piece with it. Six branches shall extend from its sides, three branches from one side and three branches from the other. Three cups made like almond blossoms, each with a bud and a flower, on one branch; and three cups made like almond blossoms, each with bud and flower, on the other branch—so for the six branches extending from the lampstand. And on the lampstand itself there shall be four cups made like almond blossoms, with their buds and flowers, and a bud under each pair of the six branches extending from it. Their buds and their branches shall be of one piece with it, all of it a single piece of hammered pure gold. You shall make its seven lamps, and set up its lamps so that they give light. Its tongs and their trays shall be of pure gold. It shall be made of a talent of pure gold, with all these utensils. See that you make them after the pattern shown to you on the mountain. Chapter 26.
Moreover, you shall make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twisted linen and blue and purple and scarlet thread; with artistic designs you shall weave them.

The length of each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits; and every one of the curtains shall have the same measurements. Five curtains shall be coupled to one another, and the other five curtains shall be coupled to one another. And you shall make loops of blue on the edge of the outermost curtain of each set, so that they may be coupled together. You shall make fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that is at the end of the second set, so that the loops are opposite each other. You shall also make fifty clasps of gold, to couple the curtains together with the clasps, so that it may be one tabernacle. You shall make curtains of goat's hair for the tent over the tabernacle: eleven curtains you shall make. The length of each curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits; all eleven curtains shall have the same measurements. Five curtains you shall couple together by themselves, and six curtains by themselves; and you shall double over the sixth curtain at the front of the tent. You shall make fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in one set and fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the other set. You shall also make fifty bronze clasps to fasten the tent together so that it is one. The extra length of the curtains of the tent, the half-curtain that remains, shall hang over the back of the tabernacle. The cubit on one side and the cubit on the other side of what remains in the length of the curtains of the tent shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle, on one side and the other, to cover it. You shall also make a covering of rams' skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather. You shall make upright frames for the tabernacle of acacia wood; each frame shall be ten cubits long and one and a half cubits wide. Each frame shall have two tenons for joining one to another;

Exodus.

They serve to join one board to another. And in this manner all the boards shall be prepared. There shall be twenty boards on the south side facing toward the south, for which you shall cast forty silver bases, so that two bases may be set under each board on the two sides. Likewise on the second side of the tabernacle toward the north there shall be twenty boards with forty silver bases, two bases under each board. On the west side of the tabernacle you shall make six boards, and again two others at the corners behind the tabernacle, which shall be joined together from the bottom to the top, and one coupling shall hold them all. Thus the two boards that are placed in the corners shall be equal. And there shall be in all eight boards, with their silver bases, sixteen in number, reckoning two bases under each board. You shall also make bars of setim wood, five to hold together the boards of one side of the tabernacle, and five others on the other side, and as many on the west side, which shall be thrust through the middle of the boards from one end to the other. The boards themselves you shall overlay with gold, and shall cast golden rings through which the bars may be drawn, and you shall cover the bars themselves with plates of gold. And you shall set up the tabernacle according to the pattern that was shown to you on the mountain. You shall make also a veil of violet and purple and scarlet twice dyed and fine twisted linen, wrought with embroidery and goodly variety: which you shall hang before four pillars of setim wood, which themselves shall be overlaid with gold, and shall have golden heads but silver bases. And the veil shall be hung on with rings, and within it you shall place the ark of the testimony, by which the sanctuary and the holy of holies shall be divided. You shall set the propitiatory upon the ark of the testimony.

In the holy of holies: and the table outside the veil, and on the side of the tabernacle southward the candlestick. The table shall stand on the north side. You shall make also a hanging for the door of the tabernacle of violet and purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen wrought with needlework, and you shall overlay with gold five pillars of setim wood before which the hanging shall be drawn, whose heads shall be of gold but their bases of brass. Chapter 27.

You shall make also an altar of setim wood, which shall be five cubits long and as many broad, that is, four-square, and three cubits high. And there shall be horns at the four corners of the same, and you shall cover it with brass. And you shall make for the uses thereof pans to receive the ashes, and tongs and fleshhooks and firepans: all its vessels you shall make of brass. And a grate of brass in the manner of a net: at the four corners of which shall be four rings of brass, which you shall put under the hearth of the altar. And the grate shall reach to the middle of the altar. You shall make also two bars for the altar of setim wood, which you shall cover with plates of brass: and you shall draw them through rings, and they shall be on both sides of the altar to carry it. You shall not make it solid but hollow and empty within, as it was shown to you on the mountain. You shall make also the court of the tabernacle: on the south side toward the meridian there shall be hangings of fine twisted linen of a hundred cubits long for one side, twenty pillars with as many bases of brass, whose heads with their engraving shall be of silver. Likewise on the north side there shall be hangings of a hundred cubits long, twenty pillars and as many bases of brass, and their heads with their engraving of silver. But on the west side there shall be hangings of fifty cubits

. Exodus .

For each of the twelve tribes. You shall make for the breastplate chains linked to one another, of the purest gold; and two golden rings, which you shall place at the two ends of the breastplate; and the golden chains you shall fasten to the rings that are at the edges of it; and you shall attach the two ends of the chains to the two clasps, on either side of the ephod, toward the front. You shall also make two golden rings, which you shall place at the two ends of the breastplate, on its inner edge, which faces the ephod; and two more golden rings, which are to be placed on either side of the ephod below, toward the front, near its joining, above the skillfully woven band of the ephod; so that the breastplate shall be bound by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a violet cord, and remain fastened above the skillfully woven band of the ephod, so that the breastplate does not come loose from the ephod. So Aaron shall carry the names of the sons of Israel on the breastplate of judgment over his heart when he enters the sanctuary, as a memorial before the Lord continually. And you shall put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim, and they shall be over Aaron's heart when he goes in before the Lord; and Aaron shall carry the judgment of the sons of Israel over his heart before the Lord continually. You shall make the robe of the ephod all of violet; and in the middle of it there shall be an opening for the head, with a woven border around the opening, like the opening of a coat of mail, so that it does not tear. And on the hem of it you shall make pomegranates of violet, purple, and scarlet, with golden bells between them all around; a golden bell and a pomegranate alternating, all around the hem of the robe.

And Aaron shall wear it when he ministers, so that its sound may be heard when he goes into the holy place before the Lord and when he comes out, so that he does not die. You shall also make a plate of pure gold, and engrave on it, like the engraving of a signet, "Holy to the Lord." You shall fasten it on a violet cord, and it shall be on the turban; it shall be on the front of the turban. It shall be on Aaron's forehead, so that Aaron may take away the iniquity of the holy things that the sons of Israel consecrate as their holy gifts; it shall always be on his forehead, that they may be accepted before the Lord. You shall weave the tunic of fine linen, and make a turban of fine linen, and make a sash, the work of an embroiderer. You shall also make tunics of fine linen for Aaron's sons, and make sashes for them and make caps for them, for glory and beauty; and you shall put them on Aaron your brother and on his sons with him, and anoint them and ordain them and consecrate them, that they may serve me as priests. And you shall make for them linen undergarments to cover their naked flesh, reaching from the waist to the thighs; they shall be worn by Aaron and by his sons when they enter the tent of meeting or when they come near the altar to minister in the holy place, so that they do not bear guilt and die. This shall be a perpetual statute for him and for his descendants after him. Chapter 29.

This is what you shall do to them to consecrate them as my priests: Take one young bull and two rams without blemish, and unleavened bread, and cakes of unleavened bread mixed with oil, and wafers of unleavened bread spread with oil. You shall make them of fine wheat flour, and place them in a basket. And you shall present the bull and the two rams, and Aaron and his sons, at the entrance of the tent of meeting. When you have washed Aaron and his sons with water, you shall clothe Aaron with the sacred garments, that is, the linen undergarments and the tunic, and

. Exodus .

upon the ephod and the breastplate, which you shall bind with the girdle: and you shall put the miter upon his head, and the holy plate upon the miter. And you shall pour the oil of anointing upon his head: and by this rite shall he be consecrated. You shall also bring his sons, and clothe them with linen tunics, and gird them with a girdle, Aaron and his sons, and put mitres upon them: and they shall be priests to me by a perpetual ordinance. After you have consecrated the hands of Aaron: you shall apply him and the calf before the tabernacle of testimony. And Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of it: and you shall kill it in the sight of the Lord, before the door of the tabernacle of testimony: and you shall take of the blood of the calf and put it upon the horns of the altar with your finger: and the rest of the blood you shall pour at the bottom of it. You shall also take all the fat that covers the entrails, and the caul of the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and offer them upon the altar as a burnt offering: but the flesh of the calf, and its hide, and its dung, you shall burn outside the camp, because it is for sin. You shall also take one ram: upon the head of which Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands: and when you have killed it, you shall take of its blood and pour it round about the altar: and you shall cut the ram into pieces, and having washed the entrails and feet, you shall put them upon the cut pieces, and upon its head: and you shall offer the whole ram as a burnt offering upon the altar. It is an oblation to the Lord, a most sweet savour of the victim of the Lord. You shall also take the other ram: upon the head of which Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands. And when you have immolated it, you shall take of its blood and put it upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron and of his sons, and upon the thumbs of their right hands and the great toes of their right feet: and you shall pour the blood round about upon the altar. And taking of the blood that is upon the altar, and of the oil of anointing, you shall sprinkle Aaron and his vestments,

his sons and their vestments. And when they have been consecrated, both they and their vestments, you shall take the fat of the ram, the rump, and the fat that covers the vitals, and the caul of the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and the right shoulder, because it is a ram of consecration: and one loaf of bread, and a cake made with oil, and a wafer out of the basket of unleavened bread that is set before the Lord. And you shall put all upon the hands of Aaron and his sons, and shall sanctify them lifting them up before the Lord. And you shall take them again from their hands, and burn them upon the altar for a burnt offering, a most sweet savour before the Lord, because it is his oblation. You shall also take the breast of the ram with which Aaron was consecrated: and you shall sanctify it, lifted up before the Lord, and it shall fall to your share. And you shall sanctify the consecrated shoulder also which was separated from the ram of the consecration of Aaron and of his sons: and they shall fall to Aaron and his sons by a perpetual right from the children of Israel: because they are the first-fruits and the beginnings of their peace offerings which they offer to the Lord. The holy vestment that Aaron wears shall his sons have after him, that they may be anointed in it, and their hands consecrated. The son that shall be priest in his place among his sons, shall put it on for seven days: and he that shall enter the tabernacle of testimony to minister in the sanctuary shall wear it. The ram of the consecration you shall take, and shall boil its flesh in a holy place: and Aaron and his sons shall eat it. The loaves also that are in the basket, in the entry of the tabernacle of testimony: that they may be a placeable sacrifice, and the hands of those who offer may be sanctified. A stranger shall not eat of them, because they are holy. But if any of the flesh of the consecration, or of the bread, remain until the morning, you shall burn the remainder with fire: it shall not be eaten, because it is sanctified.

Exodus.

All that I command you, you shall do for Aaron and his sons. For seven days you shall consecrate their hands, and each day you shall offer a bull as a sin offering for atonement. You shall cleanse the altar when you make atonement upon it, and anoint it to sanctify it. For seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and sanctify it, and the altar shall be most holy. Whatever touches the altar shall be made holy. Now this is what you shall offer on the altar: two yearling lambs each day, continually — one lamb in the morning, and the other lamb at evening — with a tenth part of fine flour mixed with beaten oil, enough for a fourth part of a hin, and wine for a drink offering, of the same measure, for one lamb. The other lamb you shall offer at evening, according to the manner of the morning offering and its drink offering, for a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the Lord. It is a continual burnt offering throughout your generations at the entrance of the tent of meeting before the Lord, where I will meet with you and speak with you there. There I will meet with the children of Israel, and the altar shall be sanctified by my glory. I will sanctify the tent of meeting and the altar; I will also sanctify Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests. I will dwell among the children of Israel and will be their God. And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I might dwell among them. I am the Lord their God.

You shall also make an altar to burn incense upon, of acacia wood. It shall be one cubit long and one cubit wide — it shall be square — and two cubits high; its horns shall be of one piece with it. You shall overlay it with pure gold, its top and its sides all around and its horns, and you shall make for it a molding of gold all around. And you shall make two golden rings for it under its molding on two opposite sides,

so that poles may be inserted through them to carry it. The poles shall be made of acacia wood and overlaid with gold. And you shall place the altar before the veil that is before the ark of the testimony, before the mercy seat that is over the testimony, where I will meet with you. And Aaron shall burn fragrant incense on it; every morning when he tends the lamps he shall burn it, and when Aaron sets up the lamps at twilight, he shall burn it, a regular incense offering before the Lord throughout your generations. You shall not offer unauthorized incense on it, nor a burnt offering, nor a grain offering, and you shall not pour a drink offering on it. Aaron shall make atonement on its horns once a year; with the blood of the sin offering of atonement he shall make atonement for it once in the year throughout your generations. It is most holy to the Lord. The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: When you take a census of the children of Israel according to their number, each one shall give a ransom for his life to the Lord when you number them, so that there may be no plague among them when you number them. This is what each one who is numbered shall give: half a shekel according to the shekel of the sanctuary — the shekel is twenty gerahs — half a shekel as an offering to the Lord. Everyone who is numbered, from twenty years old and above, shall give the Lord's offering. The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less than half a shekel, when you give the Lord's offering to make atonement for your lives. You shall take the atonement money from the people of Israel and shall use it for the service of the tent of meeting, so that it may bring the people of Israel to remembrance before the Lord, to make atonement for your lives. The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: You shall also make a basin of bronze, with its stand of bronze, for washing. You shall put it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and you shall put water in it. Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet from it. When they enter the tent of meeting, or when they approach the altar,

· Exodus ·

For in these days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested from all his work. And when the Lord had finished speaking in this manner with Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him two stone tablets of testimony, written by the finger of God. Chapter XXXI.

But the people, seeing that Moses was slow to come down from the mountain, gathered against Aaron and said: Come, make us gods who will lead us. As for this man Moses, who brought us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of him. And Aaron said to them: Take the golden earrings from the ears of your wives and your sons and daughters, and bring them to me. The people did as he commanded, bringing their earrings to Aaron. And when he had received them, he fashioned them with a graving tool and made a molten calf. And they said: These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before it, and made proclamation saying: Tomorrow is a feast of the Lord. Rising early the next day, they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play. And the Lord spoke to Moses saying: Go, come down; for your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, have sinned. They have quickly turned away from the path that I showed them. They have made for themselves a molten calf and have worshipped it, and sacrificing to it have said: These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. And again the Lord said to Moses: I see that this is a stiff-necked people. Let me alone, that my anger may blaze against them and I may destroy them, and I will make of you a great nation. But Moses prayed to the Lord his God, saying: Why, O Lord, does your anger blaze against your own people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt with great strength and with a mighty hand? Lest Egypt say: He cunningly brought them out, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them from the earth. Let your anger be quieted, and be appeased over the wickedness of your people. Remember Abraham and Isaac and Israel your servants, to whom you swore by your own self, saying: I will multiply your descendants as the stars of heaven, and all this land that I have spoken of I will give to your descendants, and they shall possess it forever. And the Lord was appeased, so that he would not do the evil he had threatened against his people. And Moses turned and went down from the mountain, carrying the two tablets of testimony in his hands, written on both sides, and made by the work of God. The writing also of God was engraved upon the tablets. And Joshua, hearing the noise of the people shouting, said to Moses: There is the sound of battle in the camp. He answered: It is not the cry of those urging on to fight, nor the cry of those fleeing in defeat, but the sound of singing that I hear. And as he drew near the camp, he saw the calf and the dancing, and his anger blazed hot, and he threw the tablets out of his hands and broke them at the foot of the mountain. And he took the calf which they had made and burned it, and ground it to powder, which he scattered upon the water, and gave it to the children of Israel to drink. And Moses said to Aaron: What did this people do to you, that you have brought so great a sin upon them? And Aaron answered: Let not my lord be angry. You yourself know this people, that they are prone to evil. They said to me: Make us gods who will lead us. For as for this Moses, who brought us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of him. And I said to them: Which of you has gold? They took it off and gave it to me, and I threw it into the fire, and this calf came out. Therefore seeing

Exodus

Moses saw that the people were naked, for Aaron had stripped them of their ornaments on account of their shameful conduct, and had set them up naked before their enemies. Standing at the gate of the camp, he said: "If anyone is on the Lord's side, let him come to me." And all the sons of Levi gathered around him. He said to them: "Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Let every man put his sword upon his thigh. Go back and forth from gate to gate throughout the camp, and let each man kill his brother, his friend, and his neighbor." The sons of Levi did as Moses commanded, and about three thousand men fell that day. And Moses said: "You have consecrated your hands to the Lord today, each one at the cost of his son and his brother, so that a blessing may be given to you." The next day Moses said to the people: "You have committed a very great sin. I will go up to the Lord; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin." So Moses returned to the Lord and said: "Oh, these people have committed a very great sin, and have made for themselves gods of gold. Yet now, if you will forgive their sin — but if not, please blot me out of your book which you have written." The Lord said to Moses: "Whoever has sinned against me, I will blot out of my book. Now go, lead the people to the place I told you of. My angel will go before you. Nevertheless, in the day when I visit, I will visit their sin upon them." And the Lord struck the people because of what they did with the calf which Aaron made.

Chapter XXXIII.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: "Go, depart from here, you and the people whom you have brought up out of the land of Egypt, to the land which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying: 'To your descendants I will give it.' I will send an angel before you, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, so you may enter a land flowing with milk and

honey. For I will not go up among you, because you are a stiff-necked people, lest I destroy you along the way." When the people heard this bad news, they mourned, and no one put on his ornaments. The Lord said to Moses: "Say to the children of Israel: You are a stiff-necked people. If for a single moment I were to go up among you, I would destroy you. Now take off your ornaments, so that I may know what to do with you." So the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb onward. Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, far off from the camp, and he called it the Tent of Meeting. Everyone who sought the Lord would go out to the Tent of Meeting, which was outside the camp. Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise and stand, each at his tent door, and watch Moses until he had gone into the tent. When Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would descend and stand at the entrance of the tent, and the Lord would speak with Moses. All the people would see the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, and they would rise and worship, each at his tent door. Thus the Lord used to speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. When Moses returned to the camp, his assistant Joshua son of Nun, a young man, would not depart from the tent. Moses said to the Lord: "You tell me to lead this people, but you have not let me know whom you will send with me. Yet you have said, 'I know you by name, and you have also found favor in my sight.' If I have found favor in your sight, please show me your ways, that I may know you, so that I may find favor in your sight. Consider too that this nation is your people." The Lord said: "My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest."

Exodus.

And Moses said: If you yourself do not go before us, do not bring us up from this place. For how shall it be known that I and your people have found favor in your sight, unless you go with us, so that we may be glorified above all the people that are upon the face of the earth? And the Lord said to Moses: This word also, which you have spoken, will I do. For you have found grace before me, and I know you by name. And he said: Show me your glory. He answered: I will show you all good, and I will proclaim the name of the Lord before you: and I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will be merciful to whom it pleases me. And again he said: You cannot see my face, for no man shall see me and live. And again: Behold, there is a place with me, and you shall stand upon a rock. Chapter XXXIV.

And after this he said: Hew for yourself two tables of stone like unto the former: and I will write upon them the words that were in the tables which you broke. Be ready in the morning, that you may immediately go up into mount Sinai, and you shall stand with me on the top of the mount. Let no man go up with you, and let no man be seen throughout all the mount: neither let the oxen nor the sheep feed before it. He cut out therefore two tables of stone, such as had been before, and rising up early he went up into mount Sinai, as the Lord had commanded him, carrying with him the two tables of stone. And when the Lord had descended in a cloud, Moses stood with him, calling upon the name of the Lord. And as he passed before him, he said: O the Lord, the Lord God, merciful and gracious, patient and of much compassion, and true: who keepest mercy unto thousands, who takest away iniquity, and wickedness, and sin, and no man of himself is innocent before you: who renderest the iniquity of the fathers to the children, and to the grandchildren, unto the third and fourth generation. And Moses making haste, bowed down to the earth, and adoring said: If I have found grace in your sight, O Lord, I beseech you that you will go with us: for it is a stiffnecked people: and take away our iniquities and sin, and possess us. The Lord answered: I will make a covenant in the sight of all; I will do signs such as were never seen upon the earth, nor in any nations: that this people, in the midst of whom you are, may see the terrible work of the Lord that I will do. Observe all things that I have commanded you this day; I myself will cast out before your face the Amorite, and the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite. Take care you never join in friendship with the inhabitants of that land, which may be your ruin: but destroy their altars, break their statues, and cut down their groves. Adore not any strange god. The Lord his name is Jealous: he is a jealous God. Make no covenant with the men of those countries: lest, when they have committed fornication with their gods, and have adored their idols, some one call you to eat of the things sacrificed. Neither shall you take a wife for your son of their daughters: lest after they themselves have committed fornication, they make your sons also to commit fornication with their gods. You shall not make to yourself any molten gods. You shall keep the feast of unleavened bread. Seven days shall you eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, in the time of the month of new corn: for in the month of spring you came out of Egypt. All of the male kind that opens the womb shall be mine. Of all beasts, both of oxen and of sheep, it shall be mine. The firstborn...

. Exodus .

If you bring back the sheep. But if you do not pay the price for it, you shall kill it. You shall redeem the firstborn of your sons; and none shall appear before me empty-handed. Six days you shall work, but on the seventh day you shall rest from plowing and harvesting. You shall keep the feast of weeks, the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the feast when the year turns at the time of its completion. Three times in the year shall all your males appear before the Lord God almighty, the God of Israel. For I will cast out nations before you and enlarge your borders; no one shall covet your land when you go up to appear before the Lord your God three times in the year. You shall not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, nor shall the sacrifice of the feast of Passover remain until morning. The firstfruits of your land you shall bring to the house of the Lord your God. You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk. And the Lord said to Moses: Write these words, for in accordance with them I have made a covenant with you and with Israel. So Moses was there with the Lord forty days and forty nights; he neither ate bread nor drank water, and he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten commandments. When Moses came down from Mount Sinai, he held the two stone tablets of the testimony, and he did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had been talking with God. When Aaron and the children of Israel saw Moses, and that the skin of his face shone, they were afraid to come near him. But Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the rulers of the congregation returned to him, and Moses spoke with them. Afterward all the children of Israel came near, and he gave them in commandment all that the Lord had spoken with him on Mount Sinai. When Moses had finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face. But whenever Moses went in before the Lord to speak with him, he took the veil off until he came out, and he would come out and speak to the children of Israel what he had been commanded. And the children of Israel saw the face of Moses, that the skin of Moses' face shone; and Moses would put the veil over his face again, until he went in to speak with him. Chapter 35.

And Moses gathered all the congregation of the children of Israel together and said to them: These are the things which the Lord has commanded to be done. Six days work shall be done, but on the seventh day there shall be to you a holy day, a sabbath of rest to the Lord; whoever does any work on it shall be put to death. You shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations on the sabbath day. And Moses spoke to all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying: This is the thing which the Lord commanded: Take from among you an offering to the Lord. Whoever is of a willing heart, let him bring it as an offering to the Lord: gold, and silver, and bronze; blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen; and goats' hair; and rams' skins dyed red, and blue skins; and acacia wood; and oil for the light; and spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet incense; and onyx stones and stones to be set for the ephod and for the breastplate. Let every skilled person among you come and make all that the Lord has commanded: the tabernacle, its tent and its covering, its clasps and its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its bases; the ark and its poles, the mercy seat, and the veil of the covering; the table and its poles, and all its utensils, and the showbread; the lampstand for the light and its utensils and its lamps, and the oil for the light; the altar of incense and its poles; the anointing oil and the sweet incense; the hanging for the door at the entrance of the tabernacle; the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils; the basin and its base; the hangings of the court with its pillars and its bases, the hanging for the gate of the court,

Exodus

...of the forecourt: the pegs of the tabernacle and the courtyard with their cords: the vestments used in the ministry of the sanctuary: the vestments of Aaron the high priest and of his sons, so that they may perform the priestly office for me. And all the multitude of the children of Israel departed from Moses's presence, and they offered with willing and devout hearts their firstfruits to the Lord for making the work of the tabernacle of the covenant. Whatever was needed for worship and for the sacred vestments, men and women together brought: bracelets and earrings, rings and armlets. Every vessel of gold was set apart as an offering to the Lord. Whoever had violet, purple, scarlet, fine twisted linen, goat hair, rams' skins dyed red, and violet skins: silver and gold objects they brought to the Lord, and acacia wood for various uses. But also the skilled women who knew how to spin gave: violet, purple, scarlet, and fine linen, and goat hair, all offering freely of their own accord. The leaders brought onyx stones and gems for the ephod and the breastplate, and spices and oil for the lamps and for preparing the anointing oil and the incense of sweetest fragrance. All men and women with devoted heart brought offerings so that the works could be made which the Lord had commanded through Moses. All the children of Israel dedicated voluntary gifts to the Lord. And Moses said to the children of Israel: Behold, the Lord has called by name Bezalel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur of the tribe of Judah, and has filled him with the spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding, knowledge and all manner of skill, to devise and to carry out work in gold, silver and bronze, to cut stones and do carpentry. Whatever can be craftily invented, he has set it in order.

Also Oholiab, son of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan. Both he has instructed with wisdom to make the work of the craftsman, embroiderer, and weaver in violet, purple, scarlet, fine linen, and to weave all things and to devise new patterns. Chapter XXXVI.

So Bezalel and Oholiab worked, and every man of wise heart to whom the Lord had given wisdom and understanding to know how to do all manner of work for the service of the sanctuary, in accordance with all that the Lord had commanded. And when Moses had called Bezalel and Oholiab and every skilled man in whose heart the Lord had put wisdom, and all who willingly offered themselves to come to the work to do it: he delivered to them all the offerings which the children of Israel had brought. Yet the people continued to bring free offerings every morning. So all the craftsmen who were doing all the work of the sanctuary came, each from the work he was doing, and said to Moses: The people bring much more than enough for the service of the work which the Lord commanded to make. And Moses gave commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp: Let neither man nor woman bring any more offerings for the sanctuary. So the people were restrained from bringing, for the material they had was sufficient for all the work to be done, and too much. And all the wise-hearted men among those who did the work of the tabernacle made ten curtains of fine twisted linen, violet, purple, and scarlet, with cherubim skillfully embroidered. Each curtain measured twenty-eight cubits in length and four cubits in width; all the curtains were of the same measure. He joined five curtains to one another, and the other five curtains he joined to one another. He made loops of violet on the edge of the outermost curtain of the one set, and likewise on the edge of the outermost curtain of the other set, so that the loops would be opposite each other and could be coupled together.
