He also made fifty golden clasps which held the loops of the curtains together so that the tabernacle became one. He also made eleven curtains of goats' hair...

. Exodus .

for covering the roof of the tabernacle. Each curtain was thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. All the curtains were of the same measure. He joined five of them together, and the other six separately. He made fifty loops on the edge of one curtain, and fifty loops on the edge of the other curtain, so that they could be joined to one another; and fifty bronze clasps to fasten the covering, so that it would be one whole. He also made a covering for the tabernacle of rams' skins dyed red, and above that another covering of hides of sea cows. He made upright frames for the tabernacle of acacia wood. Each frame was ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide. Each frame had two projecting pegs, so that one frame was joined to another. He made all the frames of the tabernacle in this way. He made twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle, with forty silver bases under them, two bases under each frame, one for each peg. For the north side he made twenty frames with forty silver bases, two bases under each frame. For the west end of the tabernacle, that is, the side facing the sea, he made six frames, and two frames for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear. These were joined at the bottom and joined at the top to a single ring. He made both corners this way: there were eight frames in all, with sixteen silver bases, two under each frame. He also made five crossbars of acacia wood to hold the frames of one side of the tabernacle, five crossbars for the other side,

and five crossbars for the west end of the tabernacle facing the sea. He also made a middle bar to pass through the frames from one end to the other. He overlaid the frames with gold, made their rings of gold as holders for the crossbars, and overlaid the crossbars with gold. He made the veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, with cherubim worked into it by a skilled craftsman. He made four posts of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold, with gold hooks, and cast four silver bases for them. He made a curtain for the entrance to the tent of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer, and five posts with hooks for them. He overlaid the tops of the posts and their bands with gold, and their five bases were bronze. Chapter 37.

Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high. He overlaid it with pure gold, inside and out, and made a gold molding around it. He cast four gold rings for it and fastened them to its four feet, with two rings on one side and two rings on the other. Then he made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold. He inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry it. He made the atonement cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide. Then he made two cherubim out of hammered gold at the ends of the cover, one cherub on one end and the second cherub on the other end.

. Exodus .

He made two cherubim of gold at the two ends of the mercy seat, with their wings spread out, covering the mercy seat, facing one another. He made the table of acacia wood, two cubits long, one cubit wide, and one and a half cubits high. He overlaid it with pure gold and made a gold molding around it. He made a rim around it a handbreadth wide, and a gold molding around the rim. He cast four gold rings for it and fastened them at the four corners where the four legs were, close to the rim, to hold the poles for carrying the table. He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold. And he made the vessels for the table: its plates and dishes and bowls and flagons with which to pour drink offerings, of pure gold. He made the lampstand of pure gold, hammered. Its base, shaft, cups, calyxes, and flowers were all one piece with it. Six branches extended from its sides, three from one side and three from the other. Three cups shaped like almond blossoms with calyxes and flowers were on one branch, and three cups shaped like almond blossoms with calyxes and flowers on the other branch — so for all six branches extending from the lampstand. On the shaft there were four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with their calyxes and flowers. There was a calyx under each pair of the six branches extending from the lampstand. Their calyxes and their branches were all one piece with it, the whole of it a single piece of hammered pure gold. He made its seven lamps and its tongs and its trays of pure gold. It was made of a talent of pure gold with all its utensils. He made the altar of incense of acacia wood, one cubit square and two cubits high, its horns of one piece with it. He overlaid it with pure gold, its top and around its sides and its horns. He made a molding of gold around it and two golden rings under its molding on two opposite sides of it, to hold the poles by which to carry it. He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold. He made the anointing oil also, and the pure fragrant incense, according to the work of the perfumer. Chapter XXXVIII.

He made the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood, five cubits square and three cubits high, with horns at each of the four corners, and he overlaid it with bronze. He made all the utensils for the altar: the pots, the shovels, the basins, the forks, and the fire pans. He made for the altar a grating of bronze network, placed under its ledge, extending halfway down. He cast four rings on the four corners of the bronze grating as holders for the poles. He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze and put them through the rings on the sides of the altar to carry it. He made it hollow, with planks, and it was empty inside. He also made the basin of bronze and its stand of bronze, from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting. He made the court: for the south side the hangings of the court were of fine twined linen, a hundred cubits long, with twenty pillars of bronze and their bases of bronze. The capitals of the pillars and their fillets were of silver. For the north side the hangings, pillars, and bases were of the same measurement and workmanship.

. Exodus .

The tent pegs were of metal. In the area facing west there were fifty cubits of curtains, ten columns with their bases, and the capitals of the columns, and the entire lattice-work was of silver. And around the circuit, fifty cubits of curtains were prepared: of which, fifteen cubits of curtains with three columns and their bases formed one side; and on the other side, because he made the entrance to the tabernacle between them, there were likewise fifteen cubits of curtains with three columns and their bases. All the curtains of the court were woven of twisted linen. The bases of the columns were of bronze; but their capitals with their rings were of silver, and he also overlaid the columns of the court with silver. In the entrance he made a screen of embroidered work in violet, purple, scarlet, and twisted linen: it was twenty cubits long, and five cubits high, according to the measure of all the curtains of the court. The columns in the entrance were five, with their bronze bases; their capitals and their rings were of silver. He made the tent pegs of the tabernacle and of the court all around of bronze. These are the furnishings of the tabernacle of testimony, as they were counted according to the command of Moses, for the service of the Levites by the hand of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest: which Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, had completed as the Lord commanded through Moses: with Oholiab son of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan joined to him as a partner, who was himself a skilled craftsman in wood, and an embroiderer in violet, purple, scarlet, and fine linen. All the gold that was spent in the work of the sanctuary — and that which was offered as gifts — was twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty shekels, according to the measure of the sanctuary.

Now the offering from those who passed through the counting from twenty years old and upward: from six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty armed men. There were also one hundred talents of silver from which were cast the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the entrance where the veil hangs. One hundred bases were made from one hundred talents, one talent for each base. From the one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels he made the capitals of the columns, overlaying them with silver. The bronze that was offered amounted to seventy-two thousand shekels, from which were cast the bases at the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony, and the bronze altar with its grating, and all the vessels that belong to its service, and the bases of the court all around its entrance, and the tent pegs of the tabernacle and of the court around it. Chapter 39.

Of violet, purple, scarlet, and fine linen he made the vestments for Aaron to wear when he ministered in the holy place, as the Lord had commanded Moses. He made the ephod of gold, violet, purple, scarlet crimson, and twisted linen by the work of a skillful embroiderer. He cut thin plates of gold and drew them into threads, to be woven into the violet, purple, and scarlet, and the fine linen, with artistic design. He made shoulder pieces joined to its two edges, that it might be fastened together. The skillfully woven band on it was of the same workmanship and materials: gold, violet, purple, scarlet, and fine linen twisted, as the Lord had commanded Moses. He prepared two onyx stones, enclosed in settings of gold, engraved like the engravings of a signet, with the names of the sons of Israel. Six names on one stone and six on the other, according to their birth order. He placed them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the sons of Israel, as the Lord had commanded.

Exodus.

The Lord spoke to Moses. He made the breastplate with skilled work, like the work of the ephod: of gold, violet, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen. It was square and doubled, a span in length and a span in width. They set in it four rows of gems. In the first row was a sardius, a topaz, and an emerald; in the second row, a carbuncle, a sapphire, and a jasper; in the third row, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst; in the fourth row, a chrysolite, an onyx, and a beryl. They were enclosed and set in gold in their settings. The twelve stones were engraved with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, each with its own name for each of the twelve tribes. They also made for the breastplate small chains of pure gold, twisted like cords, and two golden rings and two golden hooks. They put the rings on the two edges of the breastplate, and fastened the two gold chains to the rings at the edges of the breastplate. The two ends of the chains they attached to the two hooks on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, in the front. They made two more golden rings and put them on the bottom of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on the inside, close to the seam, above the skillfully woven band of the ephod. They bound the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a lace of violet, so that it would lie on the skillfully woven band of the ephod, and so that the breastplate would not come loose from the ephod, as the Lord had commanded Moses. He made the robe of the ephod of woven work, all of violet, and the opening of the robe in the middle of it, like the opening in a coat of mail, with a woven binding around the opening, so that it would not tear. On the hem of the robe they made pomegranates of violet, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen. They also made bells of pure gold and put the bells between the pomegranates all around the hem of the robe, between the pomegranates: a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe, to be worn for ministering, as the Lord had commanded Moses. They also made the tunics of fine linen,

woven for Aaron and his sons, and the turbans with their crowns of fine linen, and the linen undergarments of fine twisted linen, and the sash of fine twisted linen, violet, purple, and scarlet, embroidered with needlework, as the Lord had commanded Moses. They also made the plate of the sacred crown of pure gold, and wrote on it an inscription like the engraving of a signet: "Holy to the Lord." And they tied to it a lace of violet to fasten it on the turban above, as the Lord had commanded Moses. Thus all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting was finished. The people of Israel did according to all that the Lord had commanded Moses. And they brought the tabernacle to Moses, the tent and all its furnishings: its clasps, its frames, its bars, its pillars, and its bases; the covering of rams' skins dyed red and the covering of goatskins; the veil of the screen; the ark of the testimony with its poles and the mercy seat; the table with all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence; the pure lampstand with its lamps set on it and all its utensils, and the oil for the light; the golden altar, the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance of the tent; the bronze altar, and its grating of bronze, its poles, and all its utensils; the basin and its stand; the hangings of the court, its pillars, and its bases, and the screen for the gate of the court, its cords, and its pegs. Not one thing was lacking of all that the Lord had commanded Moses. And the people of Israel, that is Aaron and his sons, brought the vestments used by the priests in the sanctuary, as the Lord had commanded Moses. When Moses had seen all the work, and behold, they had done it as the Lord had commanded, Moses blessed them. Chapter 40.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: On the first day of the first month you shall erect the tabernacle of the tent of meeting. And you shall put in it the ark of the testimony, and you shall screen the ark with the veil. And you shall bring in the table and

Leviticus

upon it that which has been properly commanded. The lampstand shall stand with its lamps, and the golden altar on which incense is burned before the ark of testimony. You shall place the curtain at the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony, and before it the altar of burnt offering. The basin between the altar and the tabernacle, which you shall fill with water. And you shall surround the court with curtains, and its entrance. And taking the oil of anointing, you shall anoint the tabernacle with all its vessels to sanctify it: the altar of burnt offering and all its vessels: the basin with its base. You shall consecrate all things with the oil of anointing: that they may be the holy of holies. And you shall bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the tabernacle of testimony, and having washed them with water, you shall clothe them with the holy vestments: that they may minister to me: and their anointing may avail to an everlasting priesthood. Moses did all that the Lord had commanded. So in the first month of the second year, on the first day of the month, the tabernacle was set up. And Moses erected it and laid the boards and the bases and the bars, and set up the pillars and spread the covering over the tabernacle, putting over it an additional cover, as the Lord had commanded. He placed the testimony in the ark, putting beneath the staves, and the oracle above. And when he had brought the ark into the tabernacle of testimony, he hung the veil before it to fulfill the command of the Lord. He set the table also in the tabernacle of testimony on the north side of the veil, arranging the loaves of bread upon it as the Lord had commanded Moses. He placed the lampstand in the tabernacle of testimony over against the table on the south side, setting up the lamps in order as the Lord had commanded. He put also the golden altar under the covering of the testimony before the veil, and burned upon it the incense of spices, as the Lord had commanded Moses. He put also the hanging at the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony, and the altar of burnt offering

in the vestibule of the testimony: offering upon it the burnt offering and sacrifices as the Lord had commanded. He set the basin between the tabernacle of testimony and the altar, filling it with water: and Moses and Aaron and his sons washed their hands and feet in it, when they went into the tent of covenant and came to the altar, as the Lord had commanded Moses. He set up the court round about the tabernacle and the altar, drawing the hanging at the entrance thereof. After all things were finished, the cloud covered the tabernacle of testimony, and the glory of the Lord filled it. And Moses could not enter the tent of the covenant, the cloud covering all things, and the majesty of the Lord shining, for the dense cloud had covered everything. Whenever the cloud removed from the tabernacle, the children of Israel set out by their companies. If it hung over, they remained in the same place. For the cloud of the Lord hung over the tabernacle by day, and the fire by night, in the sight of all the children of Israel throughout all their journeys.

Here ends Hellesmoth, that is Exodus.
Here begins Vagera, that is Leviticus, Chapter 1.

And the Lord called Moses, and spoke to him from the tabernacle of testimony, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: When any man among you shall offer a gift to the Lord from among the cattle, that is from the herds and flocks offering sacrifices: if his offering be a burnt offering from the herd, he shall offer a male without blemish at the door of the tabernacle of testimony, to make the Lord favorable to him. He shall put his hand upon the head of the offering, and it will be acceptable and help toward his atonement. And he shall immolate the calf before the Lord, and the sons of Aaron the priests shall offer the blood thereof, pouring it round about the altar which is before the door of the tabernacle.

Leviticus.

And having removed the hide of the offering, they shall cut the limbs and lay them upon the fire on the altar, upon the wood that is already arranged. The entrails and the feet being washed with water, the priest shall burn everything upon the altar for a burnt offering, a sweet-smelling savor to the Lord. If his offering to the Lord is from the flock, whether of sheep or of goats, for a burnt offering, he shall offer a male without blemish, and shall slaughter it at the side of the altar northward before the Lord. And the sons of Aaron the priest shall sprinkle his blood round about upon the altar. And he shall cut it into pieces, with its head and its fat, and the priest shall lay them in order on the wood that is on the fire upon the altar. But the inwards and the legs shall be washed with water, and the priest shall bring it all and burn it upon the altar: it is a burnt offering, a sweet savor to the Lord. And if his offering to the Lord is a burnt sacrifice from birds, whether of turtledoves or young pigeons, the priest shall bring it to the altar, and twist off its head and burn it on the altar, and its blood shall be drained on the side of the altar. And he shall take away its crop with its feathers and cast it beside the altar eastward, in the place where the ashes are cast. And he shall split it at its wings but not divide it asunder, and the priest shall burn it upon the altar, upon the wood that is upon the fire: it is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a sweet savor to the Lord. Chapter 4.
Chapter 4. When a soul offers an oblation of a grain offering to the Lord, his offering shall be of fine flour. And he shall pour oil upon it and put frankincense on it, and bring it to Aaron's sons the priests. And one of them shall take a handful of the flour and of the oil, with all the frankincense, and the priest shall burn it as a memorial offering on the altar, an offering of a sweet savor to the Lord. What remains of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons.

It is most holy, of the offerings of the Lord made by fire. When you bring an offering baked in the oven, it shall be of fine flour: unleavened cakes mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers anointed with oil. If your offering is a grain offering cooked on a griddle, it shall be of fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened. You shall divide it into pieces and pour oil on it: it is a grain offering. And if your offering is a grain offering cooked on a pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil. You shall bring the grain offering made of these things to the Lord, and it shall be presented to the priest, who shall take it to the altar. And the priest shall take from the grain offering its memorial portion and burn it on the altar, an offering of a sweet savor to the Lord. What is left of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons: it is most holy, of the offerings of the Lord made by fire. No grain offering which you shall bring to the Lord shall be made with leaven, for you shall burn no leaven nor any honey in any offering of the Lord made by fire. As for the offering of the firstfruits, you shall offer them to the Lord, but they shall not ascend to the altar for a sweet savor. Every offering of your grain offering you shall season with salt; you shall not allow the salt of the covenant of your God to be lacking from your grain offering. With all your offerings you shall offer salt. And if you offer a grain offering of your firstfruits to the Lord, you shall offer for the grain offering of your firstfruits green heads of grain roasted on the fire, grain beaten from full heads. And you shall put oil on it and lay frankincense on it, for it is a grain offering. And the priest shall burn the memorial portion of it, part of its beaten grain and part of its oil, with all the frankincense: it is an offering made by fire to the Lord. Chapter 3.

Now if his offering for the peace offering to the Lord is from the herd, whether male or female, he shall offer it without blemish before the Lord. And he shall lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the door of the tabernacle of meeting; and Aaron's sons the priests shall sprinkle the blood all around on the altar. Then he shall offer from the sacrifice of the peace offering as an offering made by fire to the Lord, the fat

January. I.

which covers the vitals, and whatever fat is within, the two kidneys with the fat that covers the flanks, and the lobe of the liver with the kidneys, shall he burn upon the altar as a burnt offering, with wood laid upon the fire, as an offering of a sweet savor to the Lord. But if his offering for a peace sacrifice to the Lord be of the flock, whether male or female, it shall be without blemish. If he brings a lamb as his offering before the Lord, he shall lay his hand upon the head of his offering and kill it at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. And Aaron's sons shall sprinkle the blood thereof round about upon the altar. And of the peace sacrifice he shall offer as a fire offering to the Lord: the fat and the whole rump, taken off close by the backbone, and the fat that covers the inwards, and the two kidneys with the fat that is on them by the flanks, and the lobe above the liver, with the kidneys. And the priest shall burn it upon the altar as food for the fire offering of the Lord. If his offering be a goat, then he shall offer it before the Lord, and lay his hand upon its head and kill it before the tabernacle of the congregation. And the sons of Aaron shall sprinkle the blood thereof round about upon the altar. And he shall offer from it, for a food offering by fire to the Lord: the fat that covers the belly, and all the fat that is within, the two kidneys and the fat that is on them by the flanks, and the lobe of the liver with the kidneys. And the priest shall burn them upon the altar as food, a fire offering of a sweet savor. All the fat belongs to the Lord forever, throughout your generations in all your dwellings. You shall eat neither fat nor blood. Chapter IIII.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel. If a soul shall sin through ignorance against any of the commandments of the Lord concerning things which ought not to be done, and shall do any of them: if the priest who is anointed shall sin, so as to bring guilt on the people, then let him offer for his sin which he has sinned a young bullock without blemish to the Lord. And he shall bring the bullock to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation before the Lord, and shall lay his hand upon the head of the bullock, and shall kill the bullock before the Lord. And the anointed priest shall take some of the blood of the bullock, and bring it into the tabernacle of the congregation. And he shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord, before the veil of the sanctuary. And he shall put some of the blood upon the horns of the altar of sweet incense before the Lord, which is in the tabernacle of the congregation. And all the remaining blood of the bullock he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. And all the fat of the bullock for the sin offering shall he take from it: the fat that covers the inwards, and all the fat that is upon the inwards, and the two kidneys and the fat upon them by the flanks, and the lobe above the liver with the kidneys — as it is taken from the bullock of the sacrifice of peace offerings — and the priest shall burn them upon the altar of burnt offering. But the skin of the bullock and all its flesh, with its head and its legs and its entrails and its dung, even the whole bullock shall he carry out beyond the camp to a clean place, where the ashes are poured out, and burn it on the wood with fire. If the whole congregation of Israel sins through ignorance, and the thing is hidden from the assembly, and they have done somewhat against any of the commandments of the Lord concerning things which ought not to be done, and are guilty; then when the sin which they have committed becomes known, the congregation shall offer a young bullock for a sin offering. They shall bring him to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and the elders of the congregation shall lay their hands upon the head of the bullock before the Lord. And when the bullock is killed before the Lord, the anointed priest shall bring some of the bullock's blood into the tabernacle of the congregation, and the priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord, before the veil. And he shall put some of the blood upon the horns of the altar which is before the Lord

January, folio f.

in the tabernacle of testimony. The remaining blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offerings, which is at the door of the tabernacle of testimony. And he shall take all its fat and burn it upon the altar: doing thus with this calf as he did before: and the priest shall make atonement for them and the Lord will be merciful to them. And he shall carry the calf outside the camp and burn it as he burned the first calf: for it is the sin offering for the congregation. If a ruler has sinned and done one of many things through ignorance that the law of the Lord forbids, and has afterward come to know his sin: he shall offer as his gift a male goat without blemish, and he shall lay his hand upon the head of the goat. And he shall slay it in the place where they slay the burnt offering before the Lord: for it is a sin offering. Then the priest shall dip his finger in the blood of the sin offering and touch the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and he shall pour out its blood at the base of the altar. And all its fat he shall burn upon the altar, as the fat of the peace offering; thus the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin, and it shall be forgiven him. And if anyone of the common people sins through ignorance in doing any of the things which the Lord has commanded not to be done, and is guilty: when he comes to know his sin he shall bring as his offering a female goat without blemish: and he shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slay it in the place of burnt offering. And the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and touch the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and he shall pour out its blood at the base of the altar. And all its fat he shall remove, as fat is removed from the peace offerings, and he shall burn it upon the altar for a pleasing odor to the Lord; and the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be forgiven. But if he brings a lamb as his sin offering, it shall be a female without blemish:

he shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slay it as a sin offering in the place where they slay the burnt offering. Then the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and touch the horns of the altar of burnt offering and pour out its blood at the base of the altar. And all its fat he shall remove as the fat of the lamb is removed from the sacrifice of peace offerings, and the priest shall burn it on the altar upon the offerings made by fire to the Lord; and the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin and he shall be forgiven. Chapter 6.

And if a soul sins and hears the voice of an oath, and he is a witness, whether he has seen or known of it: if he does not tell it, he shall bear his iniquity. A soul that touches any unclean thing, whether the carcass of an unclean beast or the carcass of unclean livestock or the carcass of unclean swarming things, and if he is unaware: when he comes to know it he shall be guilty. Or if he touches human uncleanness, of whatever sort the uncleanness is with which one becomes unclean, and if he is unaware, when he comes to know it he shall be guilty. Or if a soul swears, speaking rashly with his lips to do evil or to do good, any sort of rash oath that people swear, and it is hidden from him, when he comes to know it he shall be guilty in any of these: when he is guilty in any of these he shall confess the sin he has committed, and he shall bring to the Lord as his penalty for the sin that he has committed, a female from the flock, a lamb or a goat, for a sin offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin. But if he cannot afford a lamb, then he shall bring to the Lord as his penalty for his sin two turtledoves or two pigeons, one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering. He shall bring them to the priest, who shall offer first the one for the sin offering: he shall wring its head from its neck but shall not sever it, and he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood shall be drained out at the base of the altar: for it is a sin offering. And the other he shall offer as a burnt offering according to the rule; and the priest shall make atonement for him

Leviticus

and for his sin, and it shall be forgiven him. But if his hand cannot find two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he shall offer for his sin the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour. He shall put no oil upon it, nor shall he place any frankincense thereon, because it is for sin. He shall deliver it to the priest, who shall take a handful of it as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar, as a memorial for him who offered it, making atonement for him; and the remainder shall belong to the priest as his portion. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: If a soul sins and transgresses by error in those things which are holy to the Lord, he shall offer for his trespass a ram without blemish from the flock, valued in silver shekels according to the shekel of the sanctuary; and he shall make restitution for the harm he has done and shall add a fifth part on top of it, giving it to the priest, who shall make atonement for him with the ram of the trespass offering, and it shall be forgiven him. And if a soul sins and does any of the things which the Lord has forbidden and does not know it, yet is guilty, he shall bear his iniquity. He shall bring to the priest a ram without blemish from the flock, according to the value of the trespass, who shall make atonement for him for the thing done unknowingly, and it shall be forgiven him, because he sinned in error before the Lord. Chapter VI.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: When a soul sins and acts unfaithfully against the Lord by deceiving his neighbor regarding a deposit entrusted to him, or by robbing him, or by extortion, or by finding lost property and lying about it, or by swearing falsely in any of all the things that people do to sin in this way: being convicted of the offense, he shall restore all that he took by fraud in full, adding a fifth part more, and giving it to the one whom he wronged.

And for his sin he shall offer a ram without blemish from the flock, valued according to the measure of the trespass, to the priest, who shall make atonement for him before the Lord, and he shall be forgiven for all the things he did in sinning. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Command Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the burnt offering. The burnt offering shall remain on the hearth of the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it. The priest shall put on his linen garment and linen breeches, and he shall take up the ashes to which the fire has reduced the burnt offering on the altar and put them beside the altar. Then he shall put off his garments and put on other garments, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place, where they shall be burned up completely. The fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it; it shall not go out. The priest shall add wood to it every morning, and he shall lay the burnt offering in order on it and shall burn on it the fat of the peace offerings. Fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not go out. This is the law of the grain offering and the drink offerings that the sons of Aaron shall offer before the Lord and before the altar. The priest shall take up a handful of the fine flour of the grain offering and its oil and all the frankincense that is on the grain offering and burn it on the altar as a memorial portion, a pleasing aroma to the Lord. What is left of it Aaron and his sons shall eat without leaven. It shall be eaten in the court of the tabernacle of meeting. It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it as their portion of my offerings made by fire; it is most holy, like the sin offering and the trespass offering. Every male among the children of Aaron shall eat of it. It shall be a statute forever in your generations concerning the offerings made by fire to the Lord. Everyone who touches them shall be holy. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: This is the offering of Aaron and his sons, which they shall offer to the Lord on the day when he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour they shall offer

Leviticus.

similar in the perpetual sacrifice. Its middle part in the morning and its middle in the evening: which is fried in a pan sprinkled with oil. The priest who has succeeded his father by right shall offer it warm as a most sweet aroma to the Lord, and shall burn it entirely on the altar. For every sacrifice of the priests is consumed by fire, and no one shall eat from it. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and his sons. This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where the burnt offering is sacrificed, it shall be slaughtered before the Lord. It is most holy. The priest who offers it shall eat it in a holy place, in the court of the tabernacle. Whatever touches its flesh shall be made holy. If any of its blood is sprinkled on a garment, it shall be washed in a holy place. The earthen vessel in which it was cooked shall be broken; but if it was cooked in a bronze vessel, it shall be scoured and rinsed with water. Every male of the priestly family shall eat of it, for it is most holy. But the sin offering whose blood is brought into the tabernacle of testimony to make atonement in the sanctuary shall not be eaten, but shall be burned with fire. Chapter 7.
This also is the law of the guilt offering. It is most holy. Therefore where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the guilt offering shall also be slaughtered. Its blood shall be sprinkled around the altar. They shall offer from it the tail and the fat that covers the entrails: the two kidneys and the fat that is by the flanks, and the appendage of the liver with the kidneys; and the priest shall burn them on the altar. It is an offering made by fire to the Lord for a guilt offering. Every male among the priests shall eat of it in a holy place, for it is most holy. As with the sin offering, so with the guilt offering; the same law applies to both. The priest who offers it shall have it. The priest who offers the burnt offering shall have its hide. And every grain offering that is baked in the oven, or prepared in a pan or on a griddle, shall belong to the priest who offers it, whether it is mixed with oil or dry. The daughters of Aaron shall share equally among the sons. This is the law of the peace offering which is offered to the Lord. If it is offered for thanksgiving, he shall offer unleavened loaves mixed with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and loaves of fine flour mixed with oil, along with leavened bread with the sacrifice of thanksgiving of his peace offerings; and from these he shall offer one as a contribution to the Lord, and it shall belong to the priest who sprinkles the blood of the peace offering. The flesh of the thanksgiving peace offering shall be eaten on the day it is offered, and none of it shall be left until morning. But if the offering is a vow or a freewill offering, it may be eaten on the day it is offered, and what remains may be eaten the next day. But whatever remains on the third day shall be burned with fire. If any of the flesh of the peace offering is eaten on the third day, the offering shall not be accepted, nor shall it be credited to the one who offered it; rather, it shall be an abomination, and whoever eats of it shall bear his iniquity. Flesh that touches anything unclean shall not be eaten; it shall be burned with fire. As for the clean flesh, anyone who is clean may eat it. But the person who eats of the flesh of the peace offering that belongs to the Lord, while in a state of uncleanness, that person shall be cut off from his people. And whoever touches anything unclean, whether the uncleanness of a person or an unclean animal or any unclean abomination, and eats of the flesh of the peace offering that belongs to the Lord, that person shall be cut off from his people. And the Lord spoke to Moses saying: Speak to the children of Israel. The fat of the ox and the sheep and

Leviticus, Chapter II (continuing) / Chapter VIII

You shall not eat the fat of goats. The fat of a dead animal, or of one taken by a beast, you may use for various purposes. But whoever eats the fat that ought to be offered as a burnt offering to the Lord shall perish from his people. You shall not eat the blood of any animal, whether of sheep or of cattle. Every soul that eats blood shall perish from among his people. And the Lord spoke to Moses saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say: Whoever offers a peace offering to the Lord, let him also offer a sacrifice, that is, its libations. He shall hold in his hands the fat of the offering and the breast. And when both have been consecrated before the Lord, he shall hand them to the priest, who shall burn the fat upon the altar; but the breast shall belong to Aaron and his sons. The right shoulder also from the peace offerings shall go as a first portion to the priest. He who offers the blood and fat of the sons of Aaron shall have the right arm as his portion. For the breast of elevation and the arm of separation I have taken from the children of Israel out of their peace offerings, and have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons, as a due forever from all the children of Israel. This is the anointing of Aaron and of his sons in the ceremonies of the Lord, on the day when Moses presented them to serve as priests, and which the Lord commanded to be given them by the children of Israel: a perpetual observance throughout their generations. This is the law of the burnt offering and of the sacrifice for sin and for trespass, and for consecration, and for the peace offerings which the Lord appointed to Moses on Mount Sinai, when he commanded the children of Israel to offer their oblations to the Lord in the desert of Sinai. Chapter VIII.
And the Lord spoke to Moses saying: Take Aaron with his sons, their vestments and the anointing oil, a calf for a sin offering, two rams, a basket of unleavened bread, and gather all the congregation to the door of the tabernacle. Moses did as the Lord commanded, and when all the assembly was gathered before the door of the tabernacle, he said: This is the thing which the Lord has commanded to be done. And immediately he presented Aaron and his sons. When he had washed them, he clothed the high priest with the linen tunic, girding him with a sash, and clothing him with the blue robe, and placed the ephod upon him, binding it with the girdle and fastening the breastplate, in which was the doctrine and truth. He placed the miter upon his head, and upon the miter opposite the forehead he put the golden plate consecrated in holiness, as the Lord had commanded him. He took also the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle with all its furnishings. And when he had sanctified and sprinkled the altar seven times, he anointed it and all its vessels, and the laver with its base he sanctified with oil. And pouring it upon Aaron's head, he anointed and consecrated him. He also presented his sons, and clothed them with linen tunics and girded them with sashes, and placed mitres upon them, as the Lord had commanded. He offered also the calf for sin. And when Aaron and his sons had laid their hands upon its head, he slaughtered it, and drawing the blood, he dipped his finger and touched the horns of the altar all around. When the altar had been expiated and sanctified, he poured the remaining blood at the base of the altar. But the fat that was over the entrails, and the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, he burned upon the altar; but the calf with its hide and flesh and dung he burned outside the camp, as the Lord had commanded. He offered also a ram for a burnt offering. And when Aaron and his sons had laid their hands upon its head, he slaughtered it and poured its blood around the altar. And the ram...

Leviticus.

Cutting it into pieces, he burned its head and the fat upon the fire, first washing the entrails and the feet. And he burned the whole ram upon the altar, because it was a burnt offering of most sweet savor to the Lord, as the Lord had commanded him. He also offered the second ram in the consecration of the priests, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands upon its head. And when Moses had slaughtered it, he took of the blood and touched the tip of Aaron's right ear and the thumb of his right hand, and likewise his right foot. He also presented the sons of Aaron. And after he had touched the tip of the right ear of each of them and the thumbs of their right hands and feet, he poured the rest of the blood upon the altar round about. But the fat and the rump and all the fat that covers the entrails, and the caul of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat and the right shoulder he set apart. Then, taking from the basket of unleavened bread that was before the Lord a loaf without leaven and a cake spread with oil and a wafer, he put them upon the fat and the right shoulder, handing all together to Aaron and his sons. Who, after they had lifted them before the Lord, offered them again taken from their hands upon the altar as a burnt offering, because it was the oblation of consecration for a sweet savor, a sacrifice to the Lord. And Moses took a portion of it, elevating it before the Lord from the consecration ram, for his own portion, as the Lord had commanded him. And taking the ointment and the blood that was upon the altar, he sprinkled it upon Aaron and his vestments, and upon his sons and their garments. And after he had sanctified them in their vestments, he commanded them, saying: Cook the flesh before the door of the tabernacle and there eat it. The breads also of consecration eat, which are put in the basket, as the Lord commanded me,

saying: Aaron and his sons shall eat them. Whatever shall remain of the flesh and the breads, fire shall consume. And you shall not go out of the door of the tabernacle for seven days, until the day when the time of your consecration is fulfilled. For in seven days the consecration is completed, as it is now: that the rite of sacrifice may be fulfilled. Day and night you shall remain in the tabernacle, observing the watches of the Lord, lest you die. So the Lord commanded me. And Aaron and his sons did all the things which the Lord spoke by the hand of Moses. Chapter IX.

And on the eighth day Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel, and said to Aaron: Take from the herd a calf for sin, and a ram for a burnt offering, both without blemish, and offer them before the Lord. And to the children of Israel you shall speak, saying: Take a goat for sin and a calf and a lamb, both of a year old and without blemish, for a burnt offering; also a bullock and a ram for peace offerings, and immolate them before the Lord, offering in the sacrifice of each a libation of flour sprinkled with oil. For this day the Lord will appear to you. They brought therefore all things that Moses had commanded before the door of the tabernacle, and all the multitude standing there, Moses said: This is the word which the Lord has commanded; do it and his glory will appear to you. And he said to Aaron: Go to the altar and offer your sin offering. Offer a burnt offering and pray for yourself and for the people. And when you have slaughtered the people's sacrifice, pray for them, as the Lord has commanded. And Aaron went to the altar and immolated the calf for his own sin, and his sons brought to him the blood of it. He dipped his finger in it and touched the horns of the altar, and poured the rest at the foot of it. The fat also and the little kidneys and the caul

Leviticus.

He burned upon the altar the fat that was on the liver, as the Lord had commanded Moses. And he burned the flesh and the hide with fire outside the camp. He slaughtered the burnt offering. And his sons brought him the blood, which he poured around the altar. They also presented the burnt offering cut into pieces, with the head and the individual limbs, and he burned them all upon the altar, having first washed the intestines and the feet with water. And for the sin of the people he killed a goat, and set up the altar for a burnt offering, adding libations to the sacrifice, which were offered together, and he burned them upon the altar, apart from the ceremonies of the morning burnt offering. He also slaughtered an ox and a ram as peace offerings for the people. And his sons brought him the blood, which he poured around the altar; and the fat of the ox, and the tail of the ram, and the kidneys with their fat, and the caul of the liver they placed upon the breasts. And when the fat was burned upon the altar, Aaron waved the breasts and the right shoulders before the Lord, as Moses had commanded. And extending his hand to the people he blessed them; and having completed the offerings for sin, the burnt offerings, and the peace offerings, he came down. And Moses and Aaron went into the tabernacle of testimony, and afterward they came out and blessed the people. And the glory of the Lord appeared to all the multitude; and behold, fire came out from the Lord and consumed the burnt offerings and the fat upon the altar. When the crowd saw this, they praised the Lord, falling on their faces.

Now Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took their censers and put fire in them and incense upon it, offering before the Lord strange fire, which he had not commanded them. And fire came out from the Lord and devoured them, and they died before the Lord. Then Moses said to Aaron: This is what the Lord spoke, saying: I will be sanctified in those who approach me, and I will be glorified in the sight of all the people. And Aaron was silent. And Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, the uncle of Aaron, and said to them: Go and carry your brothers from before the sanctuary outside the camp. And they went forward and carried them as they lay, clothed in their tunics, and threw them outside the camp, as Moses had said. And Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar his sons: Do not uncover your heads and do not tear your garments, lest you die, and indignation arise upon all the congregation. But let your brothers and all the house of Israel mourn for the burning which the Lord has kindled; but you shall not go out from the door of the tabernacle, lest you die: for the anointing oil of the Lord is upon you. And they did according to the word of Moses. And the Lord spoke to Aaron, saying: Do not drink wine or anything that can make you drunk, you and your sons, when you enter the tabernacle of testimony, lest you die: this is a perpetual statute for your generations, that you may have knowledge to discern between the holy and the profane, between the unclean and the clean; and that you may teach the children of Israel all the statutes which the Lord has spoken to them by the hand of Moses. And Moses spoke to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his remaining sons: Take the grain offering that remains of the offering of the Lord and eat it without leaven beside the altar: for it is most holy. And you shall eat it in a holy place, which has been given to you and to your sons, from the offerings of the Lord: as I have been commanded. The breast also that is waved...

Leviticus.

And the ram that was set apart you shall eat in a most clean place, you and your sons and your daughters. For it has been set aside for you and your children from the peace offerings of the children of Israel, because the breast that was waved and the shoulder that was offered have been brought before the Lord, and by perpetual law they belong to you and your children, as the Lord has commanded. But Moses sought diligently for the goat that had been offered for sin, and found it had been burned; and he was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron who remained, saying: Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy place? For it is most holy, and was given to you to bear the iniquity of the congregation, and to make atonement for them before the Lord. Seeing that its blood was not brought into the sanctuary, you should have eaten it in the sanctuary, as was commanded to me. Aaron replied: Today they have offered their sin offering and their burnt offering before the Lord, and such things as these have happened to me. How could I have eaten the sin offering today? Would it have been pleasing to the Lord? And when Moses heard this, he was satisfied. Chapter 11.

The Lord spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying: Speak to the children of Israel. Keep all the things I have written for you, that I may be your God. These are the animals which you may eat of all the animals on earth: whatever has a divided hoof and chews the cud among the animals, that you shall eat. But whatever chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof, such as the camel and others, you shall not eat; consider it unclean. The rock badger, because it chews the cud but does not divide the hoof, is unclean; the hare also, for it chews the cud but does not divide the hoof; and the pig, which divides the hoof but does not chew the cud: of their flesh you shall not eat.

Do not touch their carcasses, for they are unclean to you. Of those that live in the water, these you may eat: whatever has fins and scales, whether in the seas or in the rivers and lakes, you shall eat. But whatever does not have fins and scales, of those that move in the waters and of living things, they shall be an abomination to you. You shall not eat their flesh, and you shall avoid their dead bodies. Everything in the water that has no fins and scales shall be unclean to you. These are the birds you shall not eat, and which shall be avoided: the eagle, the griffon vulture, the osprey, the kite, and the vulture according to its kind; every raven according to its kind; the ostrich, the nighthawk, the seagull, and the hawk according to its kind; the little owl, the cormorant, the ibis, the swan, the pelican, the porphyrion, the heron, the plover according to its kind; the hoopoe also, and the bat. All flying creatures that go on four feet shall be an abomination to you. Yet among the flying creatures that go on four feet, you may eat those which have legs above their feet with which to leap upon the earth: such as the locust in its varieties, the grasshopper, the cricket, and the katydid, each according to its kind. But all other flying creatures which have four feet shall be an abomination to you; and whoever touches their dead body shall be unclean until evening. And if it is necessary to carry any part of their dead body, he shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. Every animal that has a hoof but does not divide it, and does not chew the cud, shall be unclean; and whoever touches it shall be unclean.

Leviticus.

male or female. But if his means are not sufficient to offer a lamb, he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons: one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for her and she shall be clean. Chapter 13.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: When a person has on the skin of their body a swelling or a scab or a bright spot, and it becomes an infection of leprosy, they shall be brought to Aaron the priest, or to one of his sons the priests. When the priest examines the diseased area on the skin and the hair in the diseased area has turned white, and the disease appears to be deeper than the skin of the body, it is a leprous disease; the priest shall examine it and pronounce the person unclean. But if the bright spot is white on the skin of the body and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and the hair on it has not turned white, the priest shall confine the diseased person for seven days, and examine them on the seventh day. If the disease has not spread in the skin and has not grown in the skin, the priest shall confine the diseased person for another seven days; and on the seventh day the priest shall examine them again. If the spot is dim and has not spread in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce them clean; it is only a scab, and the person shall wash their clothes and be clean. But if the scab spreads further in the skin after the person has been shown to the priest for their cleansing, they shall appear again before the priest; the priest shall pronounce them unclean. If a leprous disease is in a person, they shall be brought to the priest; the priest shall examine them. If there is a white swelling in the skin and it has turned the hair white, and there is raw flesh in the swelling, it is a chronic leprous disease in the skin of the body; the priest shall pronounce them unclean. The priest shall not confine them, for they are already unclean. But if the leprosy breaks out in the skin, and it covers all the skin of the diseased person from head to foot, as far as the priest can see,

the priest shall examine them; and if the leprosy has covered all their body, he shall pronounce the diseased person clean of the disease; since it has all turned white, they are clean. But if raw flesh ever appears on them, they shall be unclean; when the priest sees the raw flesh, he shall pronounce them unclean. Raw flesh is unclean; it is leprosy. But if the raw flesh turns again and is changed to white, they shall come to the priest; the priest shall examine them, and if the disease has turned white, the priest shall pronounce the diseased person clean; they are clean. When the skin of one's body has a boil that has healed, and in the place of the boil there is a white swelling or a reddish-white spot, it shall be shown to the priest. The priest shall examine it; and if it appears to be lower than the skin and its hair has turned white, the priest shall pronounce them unclean; it is a leprous disease, broken out in the boil. But if the priest examines it and the hair on it is not white, and it is not lower than the skin but is dim, the priest shall confine them for seven days; if it spreads in the skin, the priest shall pronounce them unclean; it is diseased. But if the spot remains in one place and does not spread, it is the scar of the boil; the priest shall pronounce them clean. If a person has on the skin of their body a burn by fire, and the raw flesh of the burn becomes a bright spot, reddish-white or white, the priest shall examine it. If the hair in the bright spot has turned white and it appears deeper than the skin, it is leprosy; it has broken out in the burn, and the priest shall pronounce them unclean; it is a leprous disease. But if the priest examines it and the hair in the spot is not white, and it is no deeper than the skin but is dim, the priest shall confine them for seven days. If it spreads further in the skin, the priest shall pronounce them unclean; it is a leprous disease. But if the spot remains in its place and does not spread in the skin but has faded, it is a swelling from the burn; the priest shall pronounce them clean, for it is the scar of the burn. When a man or woman has a disease on the head or in the beard, the priest shall examine them.

Leviticus.

And if the affected area is lower than the rest of the skin, and the hair has turned yellow and thin, it shall defile them, for it is leprosy of the head and beard. But if he sees that the area of the spot is equal to the surrounding skin and the hair is black, he shall shut them up for seven days, and on the seventh day he shall examine them. If the spot has not spread and the hair has not changed color and the area of the sore is level with the surrounding skin, the man shall be shaved, except for the place of the sore, and he shall be shut up for another seven days. If on the seventh day the sore appears to have remained in its place and has not spread in the skin, he shall pronounce him clean, and the person shall wash his clothes and be clean. But if after his cleansing the spot spreads again in the skin, he shall no longer inquire whether the hair has turned yellow, for he is manifestly unclean. But if the spot stays and the hair in it is black, the priest shall know that the person is healed and shall pronounce him clean. A man or woman in whose skin a brightness appears: the priest shall look at them. If it appears somewhat dim and white on the skin, it is not leprosy but a bright spot, and the person is clean. If hair falls from the head, he is bald and is clean. And if the hair falls from the front of the head, he is forehead-bald and is clean. But if in the baldness or forehead-baldness there appears a white or reddish color, and the priest sees it, he shall condemn him without doubt for leprosy, which has arisen in his baldness. Whoever therefore is marked with leprosy and is separated at the judgment of the priest shall have his clothes torn, his head bare, his mouth covered, and shall cry out that he is defiled and unclean. All the time that he is a leper and unclean, he shall dwell alone outside the camp. Any woolen or linen garment that has leprosy in the warp or woof,

or in the skin or anything made of skin, if a white or reddish spot appears in it, it shall be considered leprosy and shown to the priest. The priest shall examine it and shut it up for seven days, and on the seventh day he shall look again; if he finds that the leprosy has spread, it is a persistent plague and he shall declare it unclean, and everything in which it is found shall be burned with fire. But if he sees that it has not spread, he shall order them to wash the thing in which the leprosy is, and he shall shut it up another seven days. And when he sees that the appearance has not returned to its former state and yet the leprosy has not spread, he shall declare it unclean and shall burn it with fire, because the leprosy has penetrated the surface of the garment or throughout it. But if the affected area appears dimmer after the garment has been washed, he shall tear it out and separate it from the whole. But if it appears again in those places that were formerly clean, it is a spreading leprosy and shall be burned with fire. If it has ceased, he shall wash with water those parts that are clean and it shall be clean. This is the law of leprosy for woolen and linen garments, of warp and woof, and of all things made of skin, for determining whether they are clean or unclean. Chapter XIV.

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: This is the rite for a leper when he is to be cleansed. He shall be brought to the priest. The priest shall go outside the camp and if he finds that the leprosy has been healed, he shall take for the one being purified two living birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop. He shall order one of the birds to be slaughtered over an earthen vessel containing living water. He shall take the living bird with the cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop, and dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird, and sprinkle the one to be cleansed seven times, that he may be lawfully purified, and he shall release

Leviticus.

and let the living bird fly away into the open field. And he that is to be cleansed shall wash his clothes, and shave off all his hair, and wash himself in water, and he shall be clean; and after that he shall come into the camp, but shall remain outside his tent seven days. And on the seventh day he shall shave all the hair off his head and his beard and his eyebrows, even all his hair he shall shave off. And he shall wash his clothes, and wash his flesh in water, and he shall be clean. And on the eighth day he shall take two male lambs without blemish, and one ewe lamb of the first year without blemish, and three tenth parts of fine flour for a meal offering, mingled with oil, and one log of oil. And the priest that makes him clean shall present the man that is to be made clean, and those things, before the Lord, at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. And the priest shall take one male lamb, and offer him for a trespass offering, and the log of oil, and wave them for a wave offering before the Lord. And he shall slay the lamb in the place where he shall kill the sin offering and the burnt offering, in the holy place; for as the sin offering is the priest's, so is the trespass offering — it is most holy. And the priest shall take some of the blood of the trespass offering, and the priest shall put it upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot. And the priest shall take some of the log of oil, and pour it into the palm of his own left hand. And the priest shall dip his right finger in the oil that is in his left hand, and shall sprinkle of the oil with his finger seven times before the Lord. And of the rest of the oil that is in his hand shall the priest put upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot, upon the blood of the trespass offering. And the remnant of the oil that is in the priest's hand he shall pour upon the head of him that is to be cleansed, and the priest shall make an atonement for him before the Lord. And the priest shall offer the sin offering, and make an atonement for him that is to be cleansed from his uncleanness; and afterward he shall kill the burnt offering. And the priest shall offer the burnt offering and the meal offering upon the altar, and the priest shall make an atonement for him, and he shall be clean. But if he is poor, and cannot afford these things, then he shall take one lamb for a trespass offering to be waved, to make atonement for him, and one tenth part of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal offering, and a log of oil, and two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, such as he is able to afford; and one shall be a sin offering, and the other a burnt offering. And he shall bring them on the eighth day for his cleansing to the priest, to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, before the Lord. And the priest shall take the lamb of the trespass offering, and the log of oil, and the priest shall wave them for a wave offering before the Lord. And he shall kill the lamb of the trespass offering, and the priest shall take some of the blood of the trespass offering, and put it upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot. And the priest shall pour of the oil into the palm of his own left hand. And the priest shall sprinkle with his right finger some of the oil that is in his left hand seven times before the Lord. Then the priest shall put of the oil that is in his hand upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot, in the place of the blood of the trespass offering. And the rest of the oil that is in the priest's hand he shall put upon the head of him that is to be cleansed, to make an atonement for him before the Lord. And he shall offer one of the turtledoves, or of the young pigeons, such as he can afford; one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering, with the meal offering; and the priest shall make an atonement for him that is to be cleansed before the Lord. This is the law of him in whom is the plague of leprosy, whose hand is not able to afford the full rite for his cleansing. And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: When you come into the land of Canaan, which I give to you for a possession, and I put the plague of leprosy in a house of the land of your possession, then he that owns the house shall come and tell the priest, saying: There seems to me to be a kind of plague in the house. Then the priest shall command that they empty the house, before the priest goes in to see the plague, so that all that is in the house be not made unclean; and afterward the priest shall go in to see the house. And he shall look on the plague, and if the plague be in the walls of the house with hollow spots, greenish or reddish, which in sight are lower than the wall,

Leviticus.

the remainder of its surface: he shall go out of the door of the house and shut it up for seven days. And returning on the seventh day, he shall look at it. If the leprosy has spread, he shall remove the stones on which the leprosy is, and cast them outside the city into an unclean place. And the house shall be scraped on the inside around about, and the dust of the scraping shall be scattered outside the city in an unclean place, and other stones shall be put in the place of those that were taken away, and the house shall be plastered with other mortar. But if after the stones have been taken out and the dust scraped off and it has been plastered with other earth, the priest comes in and sees that the leprosy has returned and that the walls are covered with spots, it is a persistent leprosy and the house is unclean. It shall be destroyed immediately, and its stones and timbers and all the dust shall be carried outside the city to an unclean place. Whoever enters the house while it is shut up shall be unclean until evening; and whoever sleeps or eats in it shall wash his clothes. But if the priest goes in and sees that the leprosy has not spread in the house after it was plastered, he shall declare it clean, because the leprosy is healed. And for its purification he shall take two birds, cedar wood, crimson thread, and hyssop. He shall sacrifice one bird in an earthen vessel over running water, and take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the crimson thread, and the living bird, and dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in the running water, and sprinkle the house seven times. He shall purify the house with the blood of the bird and with the running water, and with the living bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the crimson thread. And he shall let the living bird go free outside the city into the open field, and make atonement for the house, and it shall be clean. This is the law for every kind of leprosy and itch, for leprosy of garments and houses, for scars and eruptions and spots,

to show when something is shining and changing into various colors, so that it can be known whether it is clean or unclean.

The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When any man has a discharge from his body, his discharge is unclean. And this is how his uncleanness in his discharge will be judged: whether his body runs with his discharge, or his body has stopped from his discharge, it is his uncleanness. Every bed on which he lies shall be unclean, and every place on which he sits shall be unclean. Whoever touches his bed shall wash his clothes and bathe himself in water and be unclean until evening. Whoever sits on anything on which he sat shall wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening. Whoever touches his body shall wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening. If the man with the discharge spits on one who is clean, he shall wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening. Any vessel of earth that he touches shall be broken, and every vessel of wood shall be rinsed in water. Any saddle on which he rides shall be unclean, and whatever is under him shall be unclean until evening. Whoever carries any of these things shall wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening. Whoever touches him without having rinsed his hands shall wash his clothes and bathe in water and be unclean until evening. An earthen vessel which he touches shall be broken, but a wooden vessel shall be rinsed with water. When the man with the discharge is cleansed of his discharge, he shall count for himself seven days for his cleansing, and wash his clothes and bathe his body in running water, and he shall be clean. On the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, and come before

Leviticus.

He shall go beyond the veil into the holy place, and shall place upon the fire the incense of sweet spices, so that its cloud and vapor may cover the oracle that is above the testimony, lest he die. He shall take of the blood of the calf and sprinkle it with his finger seven times toward the mercy seat on the east side. And when he has killed the goat for the sin offering, he shall bring its blood within the veil, as he did with the blood of the calf, and sprinkle it upon the mercy seat, and shall cleanse the sanctuary from the uncleannesses of the children of Israel, and from their transgressions, and all their sins. According to this rite he shall do in the tabernacle of the testimony, which is established among them in the midst of their encampment. No man shall be in the tabernacle when the high priest enters the sanctuary, to pray for himself and for his household and for all the congregation of Israel, until he comes out. And when he comes out to the altar that is before the Lord, he shall pray for himself, and taking the blood of the calf and the goat shall pour it upon the horns of the altar round about, and sprinkling with his finger seven times shall cleanse and sanctify it from the uncleannesses of the children of Israel. After he has cleansed the sanctuary and the tabernacle and the altar, then he shall offer the live goat: and laying both hands upon its head he shall confess all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions and sins, and placing them upon its head shall send it away into the wilderness by a man who is in readiness. And when the goat has carried all their iniquities into a desolate land, and has been let go in the wilderness, Aaron shall return to the tabernacle of the testimony: and putting off the vestments which he had worn when he entered the sanctuary, and leaving them there, he shall wash his flesh in a holy place and put on his own garments. And after he has come out and offered the burnt offering for himself and for the people, he shall pray for himself.

And the fat that is offered for sin he shall burn upon the altar. But he who let the scapegoat go shall wash his clothes and his body with water, and so shall enter into the camp. The calf and the goat that were sacrificed for sin, and whose blood was brought into the sanctuary to make atonement, shall be carried outside the camp and burned with fire — their hides, their flesh, and their dung: and whoever burns them shall wash his clothes and his flesh with water, and afterward he may enter the camp. This shall be an everlasting statute for you. In the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall afflict your souls, and shall do no work, whether it be a native or a stranger that sojourns among you. For on this day shall atonement be made for you to cleanse you; from all your sins you shall be clean before the Lord. It is a sabbath of rest to you, and you shall afflict your souls by a perpetual ordinance. The priest who is anointed and consecrated to serve as priest in his father's place shall make atonement, and shall put on the linen garments, the holy vestments: and he shall cleanse the sanctuary and the tabernacle of the testimony and the altar, and the priests and all the people. And this shall be an everlasting statute for you, to make atonement for the children of Israel once a year for all their sins. And he did as the Lord commanded Moses. Chapter XVII.

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and to his sons, and to all the children of Israel, and say to them: This is the word which the Lord has commanded, saying: Whatever man of the house of Israel kills an ox or a lamb or a goat in the camp, or outside the camp, and does not bring it to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation to offer an offering to the Lord, blood shall be imputed to that man. As if

Leviticus.

whoever sheds blood shall be cut off from among his people. Therefore the priests must offer the children of Israel the sacrifices they slaughter in the field, so that they may be sanctified to the Lord before the door of the tabernacle of testimony, and offer them as peace offerings to the Lord. The priest shall pour the blood upon the altar of the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of testimony, and shall burn the fat for a sweet savor to the Lord, so that they no longer offer their sacrifices to the demons with whom they have fornicated. This shall be a perpetual ordinance to them and their descendants. And you shall say to them: Whoever of the house of Israel or of the strangers who dwell among you offers a burnt offering or sacrifice and does not bring it to the door of the tabernacle of testimony to offer it to the Lord shall be cut off from his people. Whatever person of the house of Israel or of the strangers who dwell among you eats any blood, I will set my face against that soul and will cut him off from among his people, because the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you upon the altar to make atonement for your souls, for it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul. Therefore I said to the children of Israel: No person among you shall eat blood, nor shall any stranger who dwells among you eat blood. Whoever of the children of Israel or of the strangers who dwell among you hunts and catches any beast or bird that may be eaten shall pour out its blood and cover it with dust. For the life of all flesh is its blood. Therefore I said to the children of Israel: You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood; whoever eats it shall be cut off. Anyone, whether native or stranger, who eats that which died of itself or was torn by beasts shall wash his clothes and bathe himself in water, and shall be unclean until evening, and then shall be clean. But if he does not wash or bathe his body, he shall bear his iniquity.

Chapter 18.

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: I am the Lord your God. You shall not do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you lived, nor shall you do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you; you shall not walk in their statutes. You shall observe my judgments and keep my ordinances, and walk in them. I am the Lord your God. Keep my statutes and my judgments, which if a man does, he shall live by them. I am the Lord your God. None of you shall approach anyone who is near of kin to him, to uncover their nakedness. I am the Lord. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father or the nakedness of your mother; she is your mother, you shall not uncover her nakedness. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife; it is your father's nakedness. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister, whether born of your father or your mother, whether born at home or elsewhere; you shall not uncover their nakedness. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, for their nakedness is your own. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife's daughter, begotten by your father, for she is your sister; you shall not uncover her nakedness. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister; she is your father's close relative. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, for she is your mother's close relative. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's brother, nor shall you approach his wife; she is your aunt. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law; she is your son's wife; you shall not uncover her nakedness. And the wife of your brother

Leviticus.

You shall be mindful of the injuries of your fellow citizens. You shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am the Lord. Keep my laws. You shall not cause your animal to mate with animals of another kind. You shall not sow your field with different seed. You shall not put on a garment woven of two kinds of material. If a man lies with a woman who is a bondwoman, even though she is of noble status, not yet redeemed or given her freedom, both shall be punished but shall not be put to death, because she was not free. For his offense he shall bring a ram to the door of the tabernacle of testimony, and the priest shall pray for him and for his sin before the Lord, and it shall be forgiven him and his sin pardoned. When you enter the land and plant fruit-bearing trees, you shall remove their first fruits. The fruit they produce shall be unclean to you; you shall not eat of them. In the fourth year all their fruit shall be consecrated and praised to the Lord. In the fifth year you shall eat the fruit, gathering all that they produce. I am the Lord your God.
