You shall not eat meat with blood. You shall not practice divination or observe omens. You shall not round off the hair on your temples or clip the edges of your beard. You shall not make cuts in your flesh for the dead, nor tattoo yourselves with marks. I am the Lord. Do not prostitute your daughter, lest the land be polluted and filled with wickedness. Keep my sabbaths and reverence my sanctuary. I am the Lord. Do not turn to wizards or consult mediums, lest you be defiled by them. I am the Lord your God. Rise before the aged and honor the person of the elder, and fear your God. I am the Lord. If a foreigner lives in your land and dwells among you, do not reproach him; he shall be among you as a native-born, and you shall love him as yourself. For you also were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God. Do not commit iniquity in judgment, in measurement, in weight, or in quantity. You shall have just balances, and equal weights, a just bushel, and an equal measure. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. Keep all my commandments and all my judgments and do them. I am the Lord. Chapter 20.

And the Lord spoke to Moses saying: Say to the children of Israel: Whoever of the children of Israel, or of the foreigners who dwell in Israel, gives any of his children to Moloch shall be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him, and I will set my face against him and cut him off from among his people, because he gave his child to Moloch, defiling my sanctuary and profaning my holy name. And if the people of the land ignore the man who gives his offspring to Moloch and do not put him to death, then I will set my face against that man and his family, and will cut off both him and all who follow him in prostituting themselves to Moloch from among their people. Any person who turns to wizards and soothsayers and prostitutes himself with them: I will set my face against that person and cut him off from among his people. Sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I am the Lord your God. Keep my commandments and do them. I am the Lord who sanctifies you. Whoever curses his father or mother shall be put to death. He who has cursed father or mother: his blood shall be upon him. If a man commits adultery with another man's wife and has committed adultery with his neighbor's wife:

January.

of his neighbor: death by dying: and the adulterer and adulteress. He who lies with his stepmother and uncovers the shame of his father: both shall die. Their blood shall be upon them. If anyone lies with his daughter-in-law, both shall die, for they have committed a wicked act. Their blood shall be upon them. He who lies with a male as with a woman: both have committed an abomination: they shall die. Their blood shall be upon them. He who takes a wife and her mother does a wicked deed. Fire shall burn among them: and such wickedness shall not remain in your midst. He who lies with a beast shall surely die: and you shall kill the beast. A woman who approaches any beast: she shall be killed with it. Their blood shall be upon them. He who takes his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother, and sees her nakedness and she sees his shame: they have committed a wicked thing. They shall be cut off in the sight of their people: because they uncovered one another's nakedness, they shall bear their iniquity. He who lies with a woman in her menstrual period and uncovers her nakedness: he has uncovered her fountain of blood: both shall be cut off from their people. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister or your father's sister. He who does this has uncovered his own flesh: both shall bear their iniquity. He who lies with his uncle's wife and uncovers the shame of his kinsman: both shall bear their sin. They shall die without children. He who takes his brother's wife does an unlawful thing: he has uncovered his brother's shame: they shall be without children. Keep therefore my statutes and all my judgments and do them: lest the land where I am bringing you to dwell vomit you out also. Do not walk in the ordinances of the nations

which I am about to drive out before you. For they have done all these things: and I abhor them. But to you I say: Possess their land, which I will give to you as a heritage: a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the Lord your God, who has separated you from other peoples. Separate therefore the clean beast from the unclean, and the clean bird from the unclean. Do not defile your souls in beast or bird or anything that creeps on the ground: which I have shown to be unclean. You shall be holy to me: for I the Lord am holy: and I have separated you from other peoples that you should be mine. A man or woman who has a spirit of divination or of soothsaying: they shall die: they shall stone them. Their blood shall be upon them. Chapter 21.

And the Lord said to Moses: Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: A priest shall not defile himself at the death of any of his people: except for his close relatives, that is, for his father and mother, and for his son and daughter, his brother also, and for his virgin sister who has not been married to a man: but not among the chiefs of his people shall he defile himself. They shall not shave their head, nor their beard: nor shall they make any cuttings in their flesh. They shall be holy to their God: and shall not profane his name. For they offer the offerings of the Lord made by fire and the bread of their God: therefore they shall be holy. A harlot or a vile prostitute he shall not take to wife: nor one who has been put away from her husband: because he is consecrated to his God: and he offers the bread offerings. Be holy therefore: for I the Lord your God am holy, who sanctify you. If a priest's daughter is found to have committed fornication: and has dishonored the name of her father: she shall be consumed by fire. The high priest, that is the chief priest among his brothers: upon whose head the anointing oil

Januus.

and the oil and whose hands are consecrated in the priesthood. He shall also be clothed in proper vestments: he shall not uncover his head: nor tear his garments: and he shall not go near any dead person at all. Even for his father and mother he shall not be defiled: neither shall he go out of the sanctuary, lest he defile the sanctuary of the Lord: for the oil of the holy anointing of his God is upon him. I am the Lord. He shall take a virgin as his wife. But a widow, and one that is divorced, and defiled, and a harlot he shall not take: but a maiden of his own people: lest he mingle the seed of his race with the common people of his kind: for I am the Lord who sanctify him. And the Lord spoke to Moses saying: Speak to Aaron: Whosoever of your seed throughout their families shall have a blemish, he shall not offer bread to his God: neither shall he approach to minister to him. If he be blind, if he be lame, if he have a little or a great or a crooked nose: if he have a broken foot, or hand: if he be crookbacked, or blear-eyed, or have a white speck in his eye, or a continual scab, or a dry scurf in his body, or a rupture: Whosoever of the seed of Aaron the priest shall have a blemish: he shall not approach to offer sacrifices to the Lord, nor bread to his God. He shall eat nevertheless of the loaves that are offered in the sanctuary: yet so that he enter not within the veil, nor approach to the altar, because he has a blemish: lest he should defile my sanctuary. I am the Lord who sanctify them. Moses therefore told this to Aaron and to his sons and to all Israel: all the things that had been commanded him. LXXII.

And the Lord spoke to Moses saying: Tell Aaron and his sons to beware of those things that are consecrated of the children of Israel: and let them not defile my holy name in what they offer to me. I am the Lord. Say to them and to their descendants: Every man of your race who approaches to those things that are consecrated, which the children of Israel have offered to the Lord, in whom there is uncleanness: shall perish before the Lord. I am the Lord. A man of the seed of Aaron who is a leper, or who suffers a flow of seed, shall not eat of those things that are sanctified to me, until he be healed. He who touches any unclean thing upon a corpse, and he from whom seed goes out in intercourse: and he who touches a reptile: and whatever thing is unclean, whose touch is defiling: shall be unclean until evening: and shall not eat of the things that are sanctified: but when he has washed his flesh with water and the sun is set: then being purified he shall eat of the sanctified things: because it is his food. That which died of itself and that which was taken by a beast they shall not eat: nor shall they be defiled therewith. I am the Lord. Let them keep my precepts, that they may not fall into sin and die in the sanctuary when they have defiled it. I am the Lord who sanctify them. No stranger shall eat of the sanctified things. A sojourner of the priest and a hired servant shall not eat of them. But he whom a priest has bought, and he that is born in his house: these shall eat of them. If the daughter of a priest be married to any of the people: she shall not eat of those things that are sanctified, nor of the firstfruits. But if she be a widow, or divorced, and having no children return to her father's house: she shall eat of her father's bread as a maiden was wont to do. No stranger has authority to eat thereof. He who eats of the sanctified things through ignorance: shall add the fifth part with that which he ate: and shall give it to the priest into the sanctuary: that they may not defile the sanctified things of the children of Israel which they offer to the Lord: lest perhaps they bear the iniquity of their trespass, when they shall have eaten the sanctified things. I am the Lord who sanctify them. And the Lord spoke

Numbers.

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the children of Israel, and say to them: Any man of the house of Israel or of the strangers who dwell among you, who offers his offering — whether it be a vow or a freewill offering, whatever he offers to the Lord as a burnt offering — it must be a male without blemish from the cattle, sheep, or goats. If it has a defect, you shall not offer it, for it will not be acceptable. And whoever offers a peace offering to the Lord, fulfilling a vow or as a freewill offering, whether from the cattle or the sheep, it must be perfect to be acceptable. There shall be no defect in it. If it is blind, or broken, or has a scar, or scabs, or mange, or scurvy, you shall not offer it to the Lord, nor shall you place any such on the altar as an offering to the Lord. A bull or a lamb that has a limb too long or too short you may offer as a freewill offering, but it shall not be accepted as a vow. That which has bruised, crushed, broken, or cut genitals you shall not offer to the Lord; and in your land you shall not do this. Nor shall you accept from the hand of a foreigner bread for your God, whatever it may be; for their corruption and blemish are in them; they shall not be accepted from you. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: When a bull, or a sheep, or a goat is born, it shall be seven days under its mother; and from the eighth day and onward it will be accepted as an offering to the Lord. But whether it is a cow or a sheep, you shall not slaughter it and its young on the same day. When you sacrifice a thank offering to the Lord, that it may be acceptable, you shall eat it on the same day; nothing shall remain until the next morning. I am the Lord. Keep my commandments and do them. I am the Lord. Do not profane my holy name,

that I may be sanctified among the children of Israel. I am the Lord who sanctifies you, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord. Chapter 23.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: These are the feasts of the Lord which you shall proclaim as holy convocations. These are my feasts. Six days work shall be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of rest and shall be called holy. You shall do no work on it. It is the Sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings. These then are the feasts of the Lord, holy convocations, which you shall proclaim in their appointed times: On the fourteenth day of the first month at evening is the Lord's Passover; and on the fifteenth day of this same month is the Feast of Unleavened Bread to the Lord. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread. The first day shall be a solemn and holy one for you. You shall do no servile work on it, but shall offer a sacrifice made by fire to the Lord for seven days. The seventh day shall also be more solemn and holy; and you shall do no servile work on it. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When you have entered the land which I will give you and have reaped its harvest, you shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest to the priest. He shall wave the sheaf before the Lord so that it may be acceptable for you; on the day after the Sabbath he shall wave it. And on the same day on which the sheaf is consecrated, a male lamb without blemish of the first year shall be offered as a burnt offering to the Lord; and with it drink offerings — two tenths of fine flour mingled with oil, as an offering by fire to the Lord for a sweet aroma — also a drink offering of wine, a quarter of a hin. You shall not eat bread, or parched grain, or green ears from the harvest until the day you bring

January.

and to your God. This is a perpetual commandment throughout your generations and in all your dwellings. You shall count from the day after the sabbath on which you offered the sheaf of firstfruits, seven full weeks, until the day after the seventh week, fifty days; and then you shall offer a new sacrifice to the Lord. From all your dwellings you shall bring two loaves of bread as a firstfruits offering, made of two tenths of fine flour, leavened, baked as firstfruits to the Lord. Along with the bread you shall offer seven unblemished yearling lambs, one young bull, and two rams; these shall be a burnt offering to the Lord with their drink offerings, a pleasing aroma to the Lord. You shall also offer one male goat for a sin offering, and two yearling lambs as peace offerings. The priest shall wave them along with the bread of firstfruits before the Lord; these shall be holy to the Lord for the priest. And you shall proclaim this same day a holy convocation; you shall do no laborious work on it. This is a perpetual statute in all your dwellings throughout your generations. When you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not reap your field to its very edge, nor shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest; you shall leave them for the poor and the stranger. I am the Lord your God. The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel: In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall observe a sabbath rest, a memorial proclaimed with the blowing of trumpets, a holy convocation. You shall do no laborious work on it, and you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord. The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: On the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement; it shall be a holy convocation for you, and you shall afflict your souls, and you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord. You shall do no work on that day,

for it is the Day of Atonement, on which atonement is made for you before the Lord your God. Any person who is not afflicted on that day shall be cut off from among his people, and whoever does any work on that day, I will destroy that person from among his people; you shall do no work at all. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings. It is a sabbath of solemn rest for you, and you shall afflict your souls; on the ninth day of the month beginning at evening, from evening to evening, you shall celebrate your sabbath. The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month there shall be the feast of Tabernacles for seven days to the Lord. On the first day there shall be a holy convocation; you shall do no laborious work on it. For seven days you shall offer burnt offerings to the Lord. On the eighth day you shall hold a holy convocation and offer a burnt offering to the Lord; it is a solemn assembly, and you shall do no laborious work on it. These are the appointed feasts of the Lord which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, to offer burnt offerings to the Lord, burnt offerings and grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings, each on its proper day, besides the sabbaths of the Lord, and besides your gifts, and besides all your vowed offerings, and besides all your freewill offerings which you give to the Lord. So on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the produce of the land, you shall celebrate the feast of the Lord for seven days. On the first day shall be a rest, and on the eighth day shall be a rest. On the first day you shall take for yourselves the fruit of beautiful trees, branches of palm trees, boughs of leafy trees, and willows of the brook, and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God for seven days. You shall celebrate it as a feast to the Lord for seven days in the year. A perpetual statute

Leviticus.

It shall be in your generations. In the seventh month you shall celebrate feasts and you shall dwell in tabernacles for seven days. Everyone who is of the nation of Israel shall dwell in tabernacles: so that your descendants may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in tabernacles when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God. And Moses spoke of the feasts of the Lord to the children of Israel. Chapter 24.

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Command the children of Israel that they bring to you the purest and clearest oil of olives, to make the lamps burn continually outside the veil of testimony in the tabernacle of the covenant. And Aaron shall set them from evening until morning before the Lord: by a perpetual rite and custom in your generations. They shall place the most pure lampstand always in the sight of the Lord. You shall also take fine flour and bake twelve loaves of bread: each of which shall have two tenths. And you shall place them in two rows, six in each row, upon the most pure table before the Lord, and you shall put pure frankincense upon them: that they may be a memorial of the oblation of the Lord. Every sabbath they shall be changed before the Lord: received from the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant. And they shall belong to Aaron and his sons, that they may eat them in the holy place: because it is most holy of the sacrifices of the Lord by a perpetual right. Now there went out a son of a woman of Israel, whom she had born of an Egyptian father, among the children of Israel, and he quarreled in the camp with a man of Israel. And when he had blasphemed the name of the Lord and cursed it, he was brought to Moses. His mother was named Salumith, the daughter of Dabri, of the tribe of Dan. And they put him in prison, until they might know what the Lord would command. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Bring forth the blasphemer outside the camp: and let all who heard him lay their hands upon his head

and let all the multitude stone him: and you shall speak to the children of Israel. Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin: and he that blasphemes the name of the Lord shall be put to death. All the congregation shall stone him. Whether he be a native or a stranger, he that blasphemes the name of the Lord shall be put to death. He that strikes and kills a man shall be put to death. He that kills an animal shall restore another in its place, life for life. He that causes a blemish to any of his fellow citizens: as he has done, so shall it be done to him. Fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth shall he restore. Whatever blemish he has inflicted, the same shall be required of him in return. He that strikes a beast shall restore another. He that strikes a man shall be punished. Let there be equal justice among you: whether the stranger or the native commits an offense: because I am the Lord your God. And Moses spoke to the children of Israel: and they brought forth him that had blasphemed outside the camp and they stoned him. And the children of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses. Chapter 25.

And the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and you shall say to them: When you have entered the land which I will give you, the land shall rest for a sabbath to the Lord. For six years you shall sow your field and for six years you shall prune your vineyard and shall gather its fruits. But in the seventh year there shall be a sabbath rest for the land: a sabbath to the Lord. You shall not sow your field nor prune your vineyard. What grows of itself you shall not reap: nor shall you gather the grapes of your undressed vine. It shall be a year of rest for the land. But they shall be food for you: for you and your servant, and for your handmaid and your hired servant: and for the stranger who dwells among you. For your beasts and the cattle all things that

Leviticus.

they shall provide you food. You shall also count seven weeks of years for yourself, that is seven times seven years, which together make forty-nine years, and you shall sound the trumpet on the tenth day of the seventh month on the Day of Atonement throughout all your land. You shall sanctify the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty to all the inhabitants of the land. It is the Jubilee. Each of you shall return to his own property and each of you shall return to his own family, because it is the Jubilee, the fiftieth year. You shall not sow, nor reap what grows by itself in the field, nor gather the grapes of the untrimmed vines, for it is the Year of Jubilee, but you shall eat directly what you take from the fields. In the Year of Jubilee, all shall return to their possessions. When you sell anything to your neighbor or buy from him, do not wrong your brother, but according to the number of years after the Jubilee you shall buy from him, and according to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you. The more years remaining after the Jubilee, the greater the price; the fewer the years, the less the price, for it is the number of crops he is selling you. Do not oppress one another, but fear your God, for I am the Lord your God. Keep my statutes and observe my ordinances and carry them out, so that you may live in the land securely, and the land will yield its fruit and you shall eat your fill and live there without fear. And if you say, what shall we eat in the seventh year if we do not sow or gather our crops, I will send my blessing upon you in the sixth year, so that it will produce a crop sufficient for three years. When you sow in the eighth year, you will still be eating the old crop until the ninth year when its harvest comes in. The land shall not be sold permanently, because it is mine and you are but aliens and tenants. Therefore throughout the land that you hold, you shall provide for the redemption of the land. If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his property, his nearest redeemer shall come and redeem what his brother has sold. If a man has no one to redeem it, but he himself prospers and finds sufficient means to redeem it, let him calculate the years since the sale and pay back the balance to the man to whom he sold it, and so return to his possession. But if he does not have sufficient means to recover it, then what he sold shall remain in the hand of the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. In the Jubilee it shall be released, and he shall return to his property. If a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, he may redeem it within a whole year after its sale. If it is not redeemed within a full year, then the house in the walled city shall belong permanently to the buyer and his descendants; it shall not be released in the Jubilee. But houses in villages without walls around them shall be treated as open fields; they may be redeemed, and they shall be released in the Jubilee. As for the cities of the Levites, the Levites shall forever have the right of redemption. Such property as may be redeemed from the Levites—houses in their cities—shall be released in the Jubilee, because the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the people of Israel. But the open land around their cities may not be sold, for that is their permanent possession. If your brother becomes poor and cannot maintain himself with you, you shall support him as though he were a stranger and a sojourner, and he shall live with you. Take no interest from him, nor profit, but fear your God, that your brother may live beside you. You shall not lend him your money at interest, nor give him your food for profit. I am the Lord your God.

Leviticus.

These things I will do to you: I will visit you swiftly with poverty and burning fever that will consume your eyes and waste your souls. You will sow your seed in vain, for your enemies will devour it. I will set my face against you, and you will fall before your enemies, and those who hate you will rule over you. You will flee when no one pursues you. But if even then you do not obey me, I will multiply your punishments sevenfold for your sins, and I will break down the pride of your stubbornness. I will make the sky above you like iron and the earth beneath you like bronze. Your labor will be spent in vain; the ground will not yield its produce, nor will the trees give their fruit. If you walk contrary to me and refuse to listen to me, I will add plagues upon you sevenfold according to your sins. I will send wild animals against you, which will devour you and your livestock, and reduce your numbers, and your roads will become desolate. And if even after this you will not accept discipline but walk contrary to me, then I will also walk contrary to you and will strike you sevenfold for your sins, and I will bring a sword upon you in vengeance for my covenant. When you retreat into your cities, I will send pestilence among you, and you will be delivered into the hands of your enemies; after I break your staff of bread, ten women will bake bread in a single oven and dole it out by weight, and you will eat and not be satisfied. But if even after all this you do not listen to me and still walk contrary to me, I will walk contrary to you in fury, and I will discipline you sevenfold for your sins, so that you shall eat the flesh of your sons and daughters. I will destroy your high places and cut down your idols. You will fall among the ruins of your idols, and my soul will abhor you; I will lay your cities waste and make your sanctuaries desolate, and I will not smell your sweet-smelling offerings. I will devastate your land, and your enemies who settle in it will be appalled by it. I will scatter you among the nations and draw out the sword after you, and your land shall be desolate and your cities ruined. Then the land shall enjoy its sabbaths throughout the days of its desolation, while you are in the land of your enemies. The land shall rest and enjoy its sabbaths, because it did not rest during your sabbaths when you were dwelling in it. And those of you who survive, I will bring fear into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a driven leaf will terrify them so that they flee as if from a sword, and they will fall when no one is pursuing them, stumbling over one another as if fleeing from a battle, even though no one is chasing them. You will not be able to stand before your enemies. You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will consume you. And those who remain of you will waste away in their iniquity in the land of your enemies, and also in the iniquities of their ancestors they shall waste away with them. Then they will confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors for the treachery they committed against me, and for walking contrary to me. So I also walked contrary to them and brought them into the land of their enemies — until their uncircumcised heart is humbled and they make amends for their iniquity. Then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land. The land shall be abandoned by them and shall enjoy its sabbaths while it lies desolate without them, and they shall make amends for their iniquity, because they spurned my ordinances and their soul abhorred my statutes. They shall then pray for their sins, because they rejected my judgments and despised my laws.

Leviticus.

they were despised. Yet even though they were in the land of their enemies, I did not utterly reject them or consume them so as to make void my covenant with them. For I am the Lord their God, and I will remember my former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, to be their God. I am the Lord God. These are the judgments and commandments and laws that the Lord established between himself and the children of Israel on Mount Sinai, through Moses. Chapter XXVII.

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When a man shall make a vow and promise his soul to God, he shall give a price according to the estimation. If it is a male from twenty years old to sixty years old, he shall give fifty shekels of silver according to the measure of the sanctuary; if a woman, thirty. From the fifth year to the twentieth year, a male shall give twenty shekels, a female ten. From one month to the fifth year, for a male five shekels shall be given, for a female three. For those sixty years and older, a male shall give fifteen shekels, a female ten. If he is poor and cannot pay the estimation, he shall stand before the priest, and however much the priest determines he can pay, that much he shall give. An animal that may be sacrificed to the Lord, if anyone vows it, shall be holy and may not be exchanged: neither the worse for the better nor the better for the worse. But if he exchanges it, both that which was exchanged and that for which it was exchanged shall be consecrated to the Lord. An unclean animal that cannot be sacrificed to the Lord, if anyone vows it, shall be brought before the priest, and the priest shall judge whether it is good or bad, and shall set the price. If the one who offered it wishes to give it, he shall add a fifth part above the estimation. If a man vows his house

and sanctifies it to the Lord, the priest shall consider it whether it is good or bad, and it shall be sold at the price determined by the priest. But if he who vowed it wishes to redeem it, he shall add a fifth part above the estimation, and he shall have the house. If he vows a field of his possession and consecrates it to the Lord, the price shall be estimated according to the measure of the seed. If thirty bushels of barley are sown on the land, it shall be sold for fifty shekels of silver. If he vows the field from the beginning of the jubilee year, it shall be valued at whatever it is worth. But if he vows it some time after, the priest shall reckon the money according to the number of years remaining until the jubilee and it shall be deducted from the price. If he who vowed it wishes to redeem the field, he shall add a fifth part of the estimated money and shall keep possession of it. But if he does not wish to redeem it, and it has been sold to any other person, he who vowed it may no longer redeem it. For when the jubilee comes, the field shall be sanctified to the Lord, and the consecrated possession belongs to the priests. If a field that was purchased and is not part of the original possession is sanctified to the Lord, the priest shall reckon the price according to the number of years until the jubilee, and he who vowed it shall give it to the Lord. In the jubilee year it shall return to the former owner who sold it, who held it as part of his possession. All estimations shall be weighed according to the shekel of the sanctuary. A shekel has twenty obols. No one may sanctify and vow the firstborn, which already belongs to the Lord, whether it be ox or sheep: it is the Lord's. But if it is an unclean animal, he who offered it shall redeem it at its estimated value and shall add a fifth part of the price. If he does not wish to redeem it,

Numbers.

He may sell it to another for whatever price it is valued at. Whatever anyone dedicates to the Lord — whether a person, an animal, or a field — shall not be sold or redeemed; everything once dedicated is most holy to the Lord. No person who has been devoted to destruction may be ransomed; he must be put to death. All the tithes of the land, whether of the produce of the ground or of the fruit of the trees, belong to the Lord; they are holy to the Lord. If a man wishes to redeem any of his tithes, he must add a fifth of the value to it. All the tithe of herds and flocks, every tenth animal that passes under the shepherd's rod, shall be holy to the Lord. He must not inspect whether it is good or bad, nor shall he exchange it. If he does exchange it, then both it and the substitute shall be holy and cannot be redeemed. These are the commandments that the Lord gave to Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai. Here ends the Book of Leviticus. Here begins the Book of Numbers. Chapter 1.

The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting, on the first day of the second month in the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt, saying: Take a census of all the congregation of the people of Israel, by their clans and families, recording the names of every male one by one, from twenty years old and upward, all in Israel who are able to go to war. You and Aaron shall list them, company by company. And there shall be with you a man from each tribe, each man being the head of the house of his fathers. These are their names: From the tribe of Reuben, Elizur the son of Shedeur. From the tribe of Simeon, Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai. From the tribe of Judah, Nahshon the son of Amminadab. From the tribe of Issachar, Nethanel the son of Zuar. From the tribe of Zebulun, Eliab the son of Helon.

From the sons of Joseph: from the tribe of Ephraim, Elishama the son of Ammihud. From the tribe of Manasseh, Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur. From the tribe of Benjamin, Abidan the son of Gideoni. From the tribe of Dan, Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai. From the tribe of Asher, Pagiel the son of Ochran. From the tribe of Gad, Eliasaph the son of Deuel. From the tribe of Naphtali, Ahira the son of Enan. These were the ones chosen from the congregation, the princes of their ancestral tribes, the heads of the clans of Israel. Moses and Aaron took these men who had been designated by name, and they assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second month, and the people registered themselves by their clans and families and the names of their individuals from twenty years old and upward, as the Lord had commanded Moses. Those who were listed of the tribe of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, by their generations and families and fathers' houses, according to the number of names, head by head, every male from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war: those listed of the tribe of Reuben were forty-six thousand five hundred. Of the sons of Simeon, by their generations and families and fathers' houses, those of them who were listed, according to the number of names, head by head, every male from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war: those listed of the tribe of Simeon were fifty-nine thousand three hundred. Of the sons of Gad, by their generations and families and fathers' houses, according to the number of names, every male from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war: those listed of the tribe of Gad were forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty. Of the sons of Judah, by their generations and families and fathers' houses, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and upward, every one able to go to war: those listed were seventy-four thousand six hundred. Of the sons of Issachar, continued...

Numbers.

...their generations and families and houses of their kindred, by name, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war, those numbered were fifty-four thousand and five hundred.
Of the children of Zebulun, by their generations and families and houses of their kindred, those numbered by name from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war, were fifty-seven thousand and four hundred.
Of the children of Joseph, of the children of Ephraim, by their generations and families and houses of their kindred, those numbered by name from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war, were forty thousand and five hundred.
Furthermore, of the children of Manasseh, by their generations and families and houses of their kindred, those numbered by name from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war, were thirty-two thousand and two hundred.
Of the children of Benjamin, by their generations and families and houses of their kindred, those numbered by name from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war, were thirty-five thousand and four hundred.
Of the children of Dan, by their generations and families and houses of their kindred, those numbered by name from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war, were sixty-two thousand and seven hundred.
Of the children of Asher, by their generations and families and houses of their kindred, those numbered by name from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war, were forty-one thousand and five hundred.
Of the children of Naphtali, by their generations and families and houses of their kindred, those numbered by name from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war, were fifty-three thousand and four hundred.
These are those who were numbered by Moses and Aaron and the twelve princes of Israel, each by the houses of their kindred. And the total number of the children of Israel by their families and houses, from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go to war in Israel, was six hundred and three thousand, five hundred and fifty men.
But the Levites were not numbered among them by their families.
And the Lord spoke to Moses saying: Do not number the tribe of Levi, nor count their sum among the children of Israel; but you shall appoint them over the tabernacle of testimony, and over all its vessels and all things that belong to it. They shall carry the tabernacle and all its furniture, and they shall minister in it and shall camp around the tabernacle. When the camp is to move, the Levites shall take down the tabernacle; and when it is to be set up, they shall erect it. Any outsider who comes near shall be put to death. The children of Israel shall camp each by his own standard and division. The Levites shall set up their tents around the tabernacle, lest there be wrath upon the congregation of the children of Israel; and they shall keep watch over the tabernacle of testimony.
And the children of Israel did according to all that the Lord commanded Moses.

Chapter 2.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: The children of Israel shall camp each by his own standard, under the ensigns of their fathers' houses, around the tabernacle of the covenant.
On the east side, Judah shall pitch his tents by his divisions, and the leader of the children of Judah shall be Nahshon the son of Amminadab; and the total of his division, those numbered, were seventy-four thousand and six hundred.
Next to him those of the tribe...

Numbers.

Issachar: whose prince was Nathanael son of Zuar; and the whole number of his fighting men was fifty-four thousand four hundred. In the tribe of Zebulun the prince was Eliab son of Helon; and all of the army of fighting men from his tribe was fifty-seven thousand four hundred. Those who were enrolled in the camps nearby were a hundred and eighty-six thousand four hundred; and they shall march out first by their companies. In the camp of the sons of Reuben on the southern side the prince shall be Elizur son of Shedeur; and the whole army of his fighting men who were counted was forty-six thousand five hundred. Next to him the camp of Simeon: whose prince was Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai; and the whole army of his fighting men who were counted was fifty-nine thousand three hundred. In the tribe of Gad the prince was Eliasaph son of Deuel; and the whole army of his fighting men who were counted was forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty. All who were counted in the camp of Reuben were fifty-one thousand four hundred and fifty; they shall march in second place by their companies. The tabernacle of testimony shall be lifted up by the offices of the Levites and their companies. As it is set up, so shall it be taken down. Each shall go to their own places and ranks. On the western side shall be the camp of the sons of Ephraim: whose prince was Elishama son of Ammihud. The whole army of his fighting men who were counted: forty thousand five hundred. And with them the tribe of the sons of Manasseh: whose prince was Gamaliel son of Pedahzur; and the whole army of his fighting men who were counted was thirty-two thousand two hundred. In the tribe of the sons of Benjamin the prince was Abidan son of Gideoni; and the whole army of his fighting men who were counted: thirty-five thousand four hundred. All who were counted in the camp of Ephraim were one hundred and eight thousand one hundred; they shall march third by their companies. On the northern side the camp of Dan: whose prince was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai. The whole army of his fighting men who were counted: sixty-two thousand seven hundred. Next to him the tribe of Asher: whose prince was Pagiel son of Ocran. The whole army of his fighting men who were counted: forty-one thousand five hundred. From the tribe of the sons of Naphtali the prince was Ahira son of Enan. The whole army of his fighting men: fifty-three thousand four hundred. All who were counted in the camp of Dan were a hundred and fifty-seven thousand six hundred; and they shall march last. This is the number of the sons of Israel divided by their households and families into companies: six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty. But the Levites were not counted among the sons of Israel. For so the Lord had commanded Moses. And the sons of Israel did all that the Lord had commanded. The camps were set up by their companies, and each went forward by his family and household. Chapter III.

These are the generations of Aaron and Moses on the day that the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai; and these are the names of the sons of Aaron. His firstborn Nadab; then Abihu; and Eleazar; and Ithamar. These are the names of the sons of Aaron the priests who were anointed; and whose hands were filled and consecrated to serve as priests. But Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the Lord, and therefore they ministered without

Numbers

to their children: and Eleazar and Ithamar, sons of Aaron their father, served as priests. The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Bring the tribe of Levi near and set them before Aaron the priest, that they may serve him and keep watch on behalf of the whole congregation before the tabernacle of testimony, guarding all the vessels of the tabernacle, serving in the service of the tabernacle. You shall give the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they are wholly given to him from among the children of Israel. But Aaron and his sons you shall appoint over the priestly service. Any outsider who comes near shall be put to death. The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the children of Israel; the Levites shall be mine. For every firstborn is mine. On the day I struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to myself every firstborn in Israel, both man and beast. They are mine: I am the Lord. The Lord spoke to Moses in the desert of Sinai, saying: Number the sons of Levi by their fathers' houses and by their families; every male from one month old and upward you shall number. Moses numbered them as the Lord commanded, and the sons of Levi were found, by their names: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei. The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to their fathers' houses. Of Gershon came the families of the Libnites and the Shimeites; the number of males from one month old and upward was seven thousand five hundred. These clans were to camp on the west side of the tabernacle, under the leadership of Eliasaph son of Lael, and they were to keep watch over the tabernacle of the covenant—the tabernacle itself, its covering, the screen at the entrance of the tabernacle of the congregation, the hangings of the court,

and the curtain at the entrance of the court which is around the tabernacle and the altar, and all the service relating to these. The family of Kohath was to include the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites. The families of the Kohathites numbered, counting every male from one month old and upward, eight thousand six hundred; they were to keep guard over the sanctuary, camping on the south side of the tabernacle. The leader of the Kohathite clans was to be Elizaphan son of Uzziel, and they were to care for the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the vessels of the sanctuary used in ministry, and all the service related to them. The chief leader of all the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, who was overseer of those who kept watch over the sanctuary. Of Merari came the families of the Mahlites and the Mushites; their males numbered from one month old and upward six thousand two hundred. The leader of the Merarites was Zuriel son of Abihail; they were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle. The Merarites were entrusted with the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, pillars, bases, and all the equipment related to their service, and the pillars of the court around it with their bases, pegs, and cords. Those who were to camp in front of the tabernacle, on the east side before the tabernacle of the covenant, were Moses and Aaron and his sons, who kept watch over the sanctuary on behalf of the children of Israel. Any outsider who came near was to be put to death. All the Levites whom Moses and Aaron numbered according to the commandment of the Lord, by their families, every male from one month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand. And the Lord said to Moses: Number all the firstborn males of the children of Israel from one month old and upward, and take a count of their names. And you shall take

Numbers

The Levites are mine in place of all the firstborn of the children of Israel. I am the Lord. And their cattle in place of all the firstborn cattle of the children of Israel. Moses numbered them as the Lord had commanded, all the firstborn males of the children of Israel by name, from a month old and upward, and the number came to twenty-two thousand two hundred and seventy-three. And the Lord said to Moses: Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the children of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites in place of their cattle, and the Levites shall be mine. I am the Lord. For the two hundred and seventy-three who exceed the number of the Levites among the firstborn of the children of Israel, you shall take five shekels apiece per head, according to the weight of the sanctuary. A shekel contains twenty obols. And you shall give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for those who are in excess. So Moses took the redemption money from those who were over and above those redeemed by the Levites, a total of one thousand three hundred and sixty-five shekels, according to the weight of the sanctuary, and gave it to Aaron and his sons according to the word which the Lord had commanded. Chapter 4.

And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: Take the sum of the sons of Kohath from among the Levites, by their families and by their fathers' houses, from thirty years old and upward, even to fifty years old, all who enter the service to do work in the tent of meeting. This is the service of the sons of Kohath in the tent of meeting concerning the most holy things. When the camp is to set out, Aaron and his sons shall go in and take down the veil of the screen and cover the ark of the testimony with it. Then they shall put on it a covering of fine leather, and shall spread over that a cloth entirely of blue, and shall put in its poles. And upon the table of showbread they shall spread a cloth of blue, and put on it the dishes, and the spoons, and the bowls, and cups for the drink offering; and the continual bread shall be on it. And they shall spread over them a cloth of scarlet, and cover the same with a covering of fine leather, and shall put in its poles. And they shall take a cloth of blue and cover the lampstand for the light, and its lamps, and its tongs, and its trays, and all the oil vessels by which they minister to it. And they shall put it and all its vessels within a covering of fine leather, and shall put it upon a carrying frame. And over the golden altar they shall spread a cloth of blue, and cover it with a covering of fine leather, and shall put in its poles. And they shall take all the vessels of ministry with which they minister in the sanctuary, and put them in a cloth of blue, and cover them with a covering of fine leather, and shall put them on a carrying frame. And they shall take away the ashes from the altar, and spread a purple cloth over it. And they shall put on it all its vessels with which they minister about it: the firepans, the fleshhooks, and the shovels, and the basins — all the vessels of the altar — and they shall spread on it a covering of fine leather, and put in its poles. And when Aaron and his sons have finished covering the sanctuary and all the furnishings of the sanctuary, when the camp is to set out, then the sons of Kohath shall come to carry them, but they shall not touch the holy things lest they die. These are the things in the tent of meeting that the sons of Kohath are to carry. The oversight of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest shall be the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering, the anointing oil, and the oversight of the whole tabernacle and all that is in it, the sanctuary and its furnishings. And the Lord spoke

Numbers

And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: Do not let the tribe of Kohath be cut off from among the Levites, but do this for them so that they may live and not die when they approach the most holy things. Aaron and his sons shall go in and assign each of them his work and his burden. Others shall not go in to look at the holy things even for a moment, lest they die. The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Take a census also of the sons of Gershon by their houses and families and clans, from thirty years old up to fifty years old. Number all who enter to do service in the tent of meeting. This is the service of the families of the Gershonites: they shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle and the covering of the tent of meeting, the other covering and the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting, the hangings of the court, and the screen for the entrance of the gate of the court which is around the tabernacle and the altar. All the vessels of the altar, the cords, and all the equipment for their service the sons of Gershon shall carry, and each shall be assigned his particular task. This is the service of the families of the Gershonites in the tent of meeting, and they shall be under the supervision of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. As for the sons of Merari, you shall number them by their families and their clans, from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who can enter the service, to do the work of the tent of meeting. These are their assigned duties for all their service in the tent of meeting: to carry the frames of the tabernacle, and its bars, pillars, and bases, and the pillars of the court all around with their bases, pegs, and cords, with all their equipment and all their accessories. You shall list by name the objects that they are required to carry. This is the service of the families of the sons of Merari, the whole of their service in the tent of meeting, under the direction of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. Moses and Aaron and the chiefs of the congregation numbered the sons of Kohath by their clans and their families, from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who could enter the service, for work in the tent of meeting; and those numbered were two thousand seven hundred and fifty. These were the numbered of the clan of Kohath, all who served in the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron numbered according to the commandment of the Lord by Moses. Those numbered of the sons of Gershon, by their families and their clans, from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who could enter the service for work in the tent of meeting: those numbered were two thousand six hundred and thirty. This is the numbering of the families of the Gershonites, all who served in the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron numbered according to the word of the Lord. Those numbered of the families of the sons of Merari, from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who could enter the service for work in the tent of meeting: those numbered were three thousand two hundred. These are the numbered of the families of the sons of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron numbered according to the word of the Lord by Moses. All those who were numbered of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron and the chiefs of Israel numbered, by their families and their clans, from thirty years old up to fifty years old, everyone who could come to do the work of service and the work of bearing burdens in the tent of meeting: those numbered were eight thousand five hundred and eighty. According to the word of the Lord they were each numbered by Moses, everyone according to his service and his burden, as the Lord commanded Moses. Chapter 5.
And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Command the people of Israel:

Numbers

...that they send out of the camp every leper, and everyone who has an issue of seed, and whoever is defiled by the dead. Both male and female shall you send out of the camp, that they defile not the camp when I dwell among you. And the children of Israel did so, and sent them outside the camp, as the Lord spoke to Moses. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel. When a man or woman shall commit any sin that men commit, and transgress against the Lord through negligence and be guilty, they shall confess the sin which they have done and shall make restitution for the wrong in full, and add to it a fifth part, and give it to whoever was wronged. But if the man have no kinsman to whom restitution may be made, the amount restored shall go to the Lord for the priest, besides the ram of atonement whereby atonement shall be made for him. And every offering of all the holy things of the children of Israel which they bring to the priest shall be his. And the Lord spoke to Moses saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: If any man's wife go astray and be unfaithful to him, and lie with another man carnally, and the thing be hidden from the eyes of her husband, and she be kept secret though she be defiled, and there be no witness against her, since she was not caught in the act: And the spirit of jealousy come upon him, and he be jealous of his wife who has defiled herself, or if the spirit of jealousy come upon him and he be jealous of his wife and she has not defiled herself: then shall the man bring his wife to the priest, and he shall bring her offering for her, the tenth part of an ephah of barley meal. He shall not pour oil upon it nor put frankincense on it, for it is an offering of jealousy, an offering of memorial, bringing iniquity to remembrance. And the priest shall bring her near and set her before the Lord. And the priest shall take holy water in an earthen vessel, and of the dust on the floor of the tabernacle the priest shall take and put it into the water.

And the priest shall set the woman before the Lord and uncover her head and put the offering of memorial in her hands, which is the jealousy offering. And the priest shall have in his hand the bitter water that causes the curse. And the priest shall adjure her and say: If no man has lain with you, and if you have not gone astray to uncleanness with another instead of your husband, be free from this bitter water that causes the curse. But if you have gone astray to another instead of your husband, and if you are defiled, and some man has lain with you besides your husband: then the priest shall adjure the woman with the oath of cursing, and shall say to the woman: The Lord make you a curse and an oath among your people; the Lord shall make your thigh to rot and your belly to swell. And this water that causes the curse shall go into your bowels to make your belly swell and your thigh to rot. And the woman shall say: Amen, amen. And the priest shall write these curses in a book and shall blot them out with the bitter water. And he shall cause the woman to drink the bitter water that causes the curse, and the water that causes the curse shall enter into her. Then the priest shall take the jealousy offering out of the woman's hand and shall wave the offering before the Lord and offer it upon the altar. And the priest shall take a handful of the offering as the memorial thereof and burn it upon the altar: and afterward shall cause the woman to drink the water. And when he has made her drink the water, then it shall come to pass, that if she be defiled and have done trespass against her husband, the water that causes the curse shall enter into her and become bitter, and her belly shall swell and her thigh shall rot; and the woman shall be a curse among her people. And if the woman was not defiled but is clean, then she shall be free and shall conceive. This is the law of jealousy. If a woman goes astray from her husband and is defiled, or if the spirit of jealousy comes upon a man and he is jealous of his wife: the priest shall apply all this law to her, and the husband shall be free from guilt...

Numbers

And she shall bear her iniquity. Chapter 6.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: When a man or woman shall make a vow to sanctify themselves and consecrate themselves to the Lord, they shall abstain from wine and everything that can cause intoxication. They shall not drink vinegar of wine, or vinegar of any other drink, nor anything that is pressed from the grape, nor shall they eat fresh or dried grapes all the days that they are consecrated to the Lord. During all the days of their separation, no razor shall pass over their head, until the day is completed during which they consecrate themselves to the Lord; they shall be holy, letting the locks of their hair grow. During all the time of their consecration, they shall not go near a dead body, nor defile themselves for their father or mother or brother or sister when they die, because the consecration of their God is upon their head. All the days of their separation they shall be holy to the Lord. If someone dies suddenly near them, defiling their consecrated head, they shall shave their head on the day of their cleansing, on the seventh day. On the eighth day they shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and the priest shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and make atonement for them because they sinned by reason of the dead body. They shall reconsecrate their head that same day and rededicate to the Lord the days of their separation, bringing a yearling lamb as a guilt offering, since the preceding days do not count because their consecration was defiled. This is the law for the Nazirite: when the days of their separation are completed, they shall bring them to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and they shall offer their gift to the Lord: one yearling male lamb without blemish as a burnt offering, one yearling ewe lamb without blemish as a sin offering, and one unblemished ram as a peace offering, along with a basket of unleavened bread, loaves of fine flour mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, along with their grain offerings and drink offerings. The priest shall present them before the Lord and offer the sin offering and the burnt offering. The ram shall be offered as a sacrifice of peace offering to the Lord, along with the basket of unleavened bread; the priest shall also offer its grain offering and drink offering. Then the Nazirite shall shave their consecrated head at the entrance of the tent of meeting, take the hair from their consecrated head and put it on the fire under the sacrifice of the peace offering. After the Nazirite has shaved their head, the priest shall take the boiled shoulder of the ram and one unleavened cake from the basket and one unleavened wafer, and place them on the hands of the Nazirite. Then the priest shall wave them as a wave offering before the Lord; they are holy and belong to the priest, together with the breast of the wave offering. After this the Nazirite may drink wine. This is the law for the Nazirite who vows their offering to the Lord in accordance with their separation, in addition to whatever else they can afford. In accordance with whatever vow they make, they shall do it according to the law of their separation. The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and his sons. Thus you shall bless the children of Israel: you shall say to them: The Lord bless you and keep you. The Lord make his face shine upon you and be gracious to you. The Lord lift up his countenance upon you and give you peace. So they shall put my name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them. Chapter 7.
On the day when Moses had finished setting up the tabernacle and had anointed and consecrated it with all its furnishings, and had anointed and consecrated the altar with all its utensils, the leaders of Israel and the heads of their clans, who

Numbers.

There were leaders over each tribe of those who had been counted, the total number being six wagons and eight with twelve oxen. The leaders brought two wagons and one ox each, and presented them before the tabernacle. And the Lord said to Moses: Receive these from them so that they may serve in the ministry of the tabernacle, and give them to the Levites according to the order of their ministry. And so Moses, having received the wagons and oxen, gave them to the Levites. He gave two wagons and four oxen to the sons of Gershon, according to what they needed; and four wagons and eight oxen he gave to the sons of Merari, according to their offices and duties, under the hand of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest. But to the sons of Kohath he gave no wagons or oxen, because they served in the sanctuary and carried its burdens on their shoulders. So the leaders brought offerings for the dedication of the altar on the day it was anointed, presenting their offerings before the altar. And the Lord said to Moses: The leaders shall offer their gifts one by one, each on his own day, for the dedication of the altar. On the first day, Nahshon the son of Amminadab of the tribe of Judah presented his offering: a silver dish weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, a silver basin of seventy shekels according to the weight of the sanctuary, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering; a golden bowl of ten shekels filled with incense; one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for a peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nahshon the son of Amminadab. On the second day, Nethanel the son of Zuar, leader of the tribe of Issachar, presented: a silver dish weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, a silver basin of seventy shekels

according to the weight of the sanctuary, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering; a golden bowl of ten shekels filled with incense; one ox, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for a peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nethanel the son of Zuar. On the third day, the leader of the sons of Zebulun, Eliab the son of Helon, presented: a silver dish weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, a silver basin of seventy shekels according to the weight of the sanctuary, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering; a golden bowl of ten shekels filled with incense; one ox, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for a peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Eliab the son of Helon. On the fourth day, the leader of the sons of Reuben, Elizur the son of Shedeur, presented: a silver dish weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, a silver basin of seventy shekels according to the weight of the sanctuary, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering; a golden bowl of ten shekels filled with incense; one ox, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for a peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Elizur the son of Shedeur. On the fifth day, the leader of the sons of Simeon, Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai, presented: a silver dish weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, a silver basin of seventy shekels —

Numbers.

seventy shekels by the weight of the sanctuary, each of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice; a golden mortar of ten shekels full of incense; one bull from the herd, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two bulls, five rams, five male goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai. On the sixth day, the leader of the sons of Gad, Eliasaph the son of Deuel, offered a silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels, a silver bowl of seventy shekels, by the weight of the sanctuary, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice; a golden mortar of ten shekels full of incense; one bull from the herd, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two bulls, five rams, five male goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Eliasaph the son of Deuel. On the seventh day, the leader of the sons of Ephraim, Elishama the son of Ammihud, offered a silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels, a silver bowl of seventy shekels, by the weight of the sanctuary, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice; a golden mortar of ten shekels full of incense; one bull from the herd, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the peace offerings, two bulls, five rams, five male goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Elishama the son of Ammihud. On the eighth day, the leader of the sons of Manasseh, Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur, offered a silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels, a silver bowl of seventy shekels by the weight of the sanctuary, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice; a golden mortar of ten shekels full of incense; one bull from the herd, one ram, one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the peace offerings, two bulls, five rams, five male goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur. On the ninth day, the leader of the sons of Benjamin, Abidan the son of Gideoni, offered a silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels, a silver bowl of seventy shekels by the weight of the sanctuary, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice; a golden mortar of ten shekels full of incense; one bull from the herd, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the peace offerings, two bulls, five rams, five male goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Abidan the son of Gideoni. On the tenth day, the leader of the sons of Dan, Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai, offered a silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels, a silver bowl of seventy shekels by the weight of the sanctuary, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice; a golden mortar of ten shekels full of incense; one bull from the herd, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the peace offerings, two bulls, five rams, five male goats, five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai. On the eleventh day, the leader of the sons of Asher, Pagiel the son of Ocran, offered a silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels, a silver bowl of seventy shekels by the weight of the sanctuary.

Numbers.

Seventy shekels according to the weight of the sanctuary: both full of fine flour mixed with oil as a sacrifice: a golden mortar weighing ten shekels full of incense: an ox from the herd, and a ram, and a year-old lamb as a burnt offering, and a goat for a sin offering: and for the peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five goats, five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Pagiel the son of Ochran. On the twelfth day the prince of the sons of Naphtali, Ahira the son of Enan, offered a silver bowl weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, a silver basin weighing seventy shekels according to the weight of the sanctuary: both full of fine flour mixed with oil as a sacrifice: a golden mortar weighing ten shekels full of incense: an ox from the herd, and a ram, and a year-old lamb as a burnt offering, and a goat for a sin offering: and for the peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five goats, five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Ahira the son of Enan. These things were offered at the dedication of the altar by the princes of Israel on the day when it was consecrated: twelve silver bowls, twelve silver basins, so that each bowl held thirty shekels of silver and each basin seventy shekels: all the silver of the vessels amounting to two thousand four hundred shekels by the weight of the sanctuary: twelve golden mortars full of incense, each weighing ten shekels by the weight of the sanctuary: all the gold of the mortars amounting in total: twelve oxen from the herd as burnt offerings, twelve rams, twelve year-old lambs, with their libations: twelve goats for a sin offering: for the peace offerings, twenty-four oxen, sixty rams, sixty goats, sixty year-old lambs.

These things were offered at the dedication of the altar when it was anointed. And when Moses entered the tabernacle of the covenant to consult the oracle, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat that was upon the ark of testimony between the two cherubim, and it spoke to him. Chapter 8.

The Lord spoke to Moses saying: Speak to Aaron and say to him: When you set up the seven lamps, let the lampstand be erected on the south side. Therefore command that the lamps face toward the north, toward the table of the bread of the Presence: the side toward which the lampstand faces shall give light. And Aaron did so and placed the lamps upon the lampstand as the Lord had commanded Moses. Now this was the workmanship of the lampstand: it was of beaten gold, both the central shaft and the branches that grew out from either side. According to the pattern that the Lord had shown Moses, so he made the lampstand. And the Lord spoke to Moses saying: Take the Levites from the midst of the children of Israel and purify them according to this rite. Let them be sprinkled with water of purification, and let them shave all the hair of their flesh. And when they have washed their garments and are cleansed, let them take an ox from the herd, and its offering of fine flour mixed with oil: and you shall take another ox from the herd for a sin offering: and you shall present the Levites before the tabernacle of the covenant, with all the congregation of the children of Israel assembled. And when the Levites are before the Lord, the children of Israel shall lay their hands upon them: and Aaron shall offer the Levites before the Lord as a wave offering from the children of Israel, that they may serve in his ministry. The Levites also shall lay their hands upon the heads of the oxen, of which you shall offer one for a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the Lord:

Numbers

...that you should pray for them. Present the Levites before Aaron and his sons, and consecrate those offered to the Lord. Separate them from the midst of the children of Israel so that they may be mine, and afterward they shall enter the tabernacle of the covenant to serve me. And you shall purify and consecrate them as an offering to the Lord, because they have been given to me as a gift by the children of Israel. I have taken them in place of the firstborn that open every womb in Israel. For all the firstborn of the children of Israel are mine, both of men and of animals. On the day that I struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated them to myself, and I took the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the children of Israel, and I gave them as a gift to Aaron and his sons from among the people, to serve me in behalf of Israel in the tabernacle of the covenant, and to make atonement for them, lest there should be a plague among them if they dared to approach the sanctuary. Moses and Aaron and all the congregation of the children of Israel did to the Levites as the Lord had commanded Moses. They were purified and washed their garments. Aaron presented them before the Lord, and he prayed for them that they might be purified to go into the tabernacle of the covenant before Aaron and his sons. As the Lord had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so was it done. And the Lord spoke to Moses saying: This is the law of the Levites. From twenty-five years old and upward they shall enter to serve in the tabernacle of the covenant. And when they have completed their fiftieth year of age, they shall cease to serve. They shall be servants of their brothers in the tabernacle of the covenant, keeping guard; but they shall not do the work itself. Thus you shall arrange the Levites in their duties. Chapter IX.

The Lord spoke to Moses in the desert of Sinai, in the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt, in the first month, saying: Let the children of Israel keep the Passover at its appointed time. On the fourteenth day of this month at evening, according to all its rites and ceremonies, you shall keep it. And Moses commanded the children of Israel to keep the Passover. And they kept it on the fourteenth day of the first month at evening in the desert of Sinai. According to all that the Lord had commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did. But there were certain men who were unclean because of a dead body, and could not keep the Passover on that day. They came before Moses and Aaron that day, and said to them: We are unclean because of a dead body. Why should we be kept from offering the gift of the Lord at its appointed time among the children of Israel? Moses answered them: Wait, and I will hear what the Lord will command concerning you. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel: If any man of you or of your descendants is unclean because of a dead body, or is on a journey far away, he shall still keep the Passover to the Lord. In the second month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, they shall keep it; they shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. They shall leave none of it until morning, nor break one of its bones. According to all the statutes of the Passover they shall keep it. But the man who is clean and is not on a journey and yet does not keep the Passover, that person shall be cut off from his people, because he did not bring the offering of the Lord at its appointed time. That man shall bear his sin. And if a stranger or foreigner lives among you, and wants to keep the Passover to the Lord, he shall do so according to the rite of the Passover and according to its statutes. You shall have the same statute for the stranger and for the native of the land. On the day that the tabernacle was erected, the cloud covered the tabernacle. And in the evening over the tent there was what appeared to be fire until...

Numbers

So it was done continually. By day the cloud covered it, and by night it had the appearance of fire. Whenever the cloud was lifted from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel would set out; and in the place where the cloud settled, there they would camp. At the command of the Lord they set out, and at his command they pitched their tents. All the days that the cloud rested over the tabernacle, they remained in the same place; and if it happened that the cloud stayed there for a long time, the children of Israel kept their duty to the Lord and did not set out. According to the Lord's command they would pitch their tents, and according to his command they would move on. So they were in the Lord's watches, under the hand of Moses.

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Make for yourself two silver trumpets of hammered work, by which you may call together the multitude when the camp is to be moved. When you sound them, all the assembly shall gather to you at the door of the tabernacle of the covenant. If you sound only one, the princes and the heads of the people of Israel shall come to you. But if the sound is prolonged and repeated, those who are camped on the east side shall move first. At the second sounding, those who are camped on the south shall march; and in the same way the rest shall sound their trumpets at the time of departure. But when the assembly is to be gathered together, you shall blow without the wailing sound. The sons of Aaron the priests shall blow the trumpets, and this shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations. When you go to war in your land against the enemy who oppresses you, you shall sound the alarm with the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the Lord your God, and you will be saved from your enemies.
