Also in your days of gladness and in your feasts and at the beginnings of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your peace offerings; they shall be a memorial for you before your God. I am the Lord your God.

In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud was lifted from the tabernacle of the covenant. And the children of Israel set out by their companies from the wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud rested in the wilderness of Paran. They set out first according to the commandment of the Lord by Moses; the sons of Judah went first by their companies, whose leader was Nahshon the son of Amminadab. In the tribe of the sons of Issachar, the leader was Nethanel the son of Zuar; and in the tribe of Zebulun, the leader was Eliab the son of Helon. Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the sons of Gershon and Merari set out, carrying the tabernacle. Next the sons of Reuben set out by their companies in their order, whose leader was Elizur the son of Shedeur. In the tribe of the sons of Simeon, the leader was Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai; and in the tribe of Gad, the leader was Eliasaph the son of Deuel. Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the sanctuary; and the tabernacle was set up before they arrived at the next camping place. Next the sons of Ephraim set out by their companies, whose leader was Elishama the son of Ammihud. And in the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, the leader

Numbers

Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was the leader. In the tribe of Benjamin the leader was Abidan son of Gideoni. The last to march were the sons of Dan, organized by companies; the leader of their forces was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai. In the tribe of the sons of Asher the leader was Pagiel son of Ochran; and in the tribe of the sons of Naphtali the leader was Ahira son of Enan. These were the encampments and marches of the sons of Israel, organized by companies, when they set out. Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, his father-in-law: We are setting out for the place that the Lord has promised us. Come with us and we will treat you well, for the Lord has promised good things to Israel. He replied: I will not go with you; I will return to my own land and my own kindred. Moses said: Please do not leave us, for you know where we should camp in the desert and you will serve as our guide. If you come with us, whatever good things the Lord grants us we will share with you. So they set out from the mountain of the Lord on a journey of three days, and the ark of the covenant of the Lord traveled before them for three days to find them a resting place. The cloud of the Lord was over them by day when they marched from the camp. Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say: Rise up, O Lord, and let your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate you flee before you. And when it came to rest, he said: Return, O Lord, to the countless thousands of Israel. Chapter 11. Meanwhile the people complained bitterly in the hearing of the Lord, as if grieving over their hardships. When the Lord heard it, his anger was kindled, and fire from the Lord burned among them and consumed the outskirts of the camp. When the people cried out to Moses, Moses prayed to the Lord, and the fire died down. That place was called Taberah, because the fire of the Lord had burned among them. The rabble among them had a strong craving, and the Israelites also began to weep again and said: Who will give us meat to eat? We remember the fish we ate freely in Egypt, and the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic. But now our strength is dried up, and there is nothing at all except this manna to look at. The manna was like coriander seed and its appearance was like that of bdellium. The people went about and gathered it and ground it in mills or beat it in mortars, then boiled it in pots and made cakes of it, and its taste was like cakes baked with oil. When the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna fell with it. Moses heard the people weeping throughout their clans, each at the door of his tent; and the anger of the Lord was greatly kindled, and Moses was also distressed. Moses said to the Lord: Why have you treated your servant so badly? Why have I not found favor in your sight, that you lay the burden of all this people on me? Did I conceive all this people? Did I give them birth, that you should say to me, "Carry them in your bosom as a nurse carries a nursing child," to the land that you promised on oath to their ancestors? Where am I to get meat to give to all this people? They keep weeping to me and saying, "Give us meat to eat." I am not able to carry all this people alone, for they are too heavy for me. If this is the way you are going to treat me, please kill me at once and let me find favor in your sight, so that I do not see my misery. And the Lord said to Moses: Gather for me seventy of the elders of Israel, whom you know to be the elders of the people and officers over them, and bring them to the entrance of

Numbers

of the tabernacle of the covenant; and stand there with me, that I may speak to you; and I will take of your spirit and give it to them, that they may bear with you the burden of the people, and you may not bear it alone. And you shall say to the people: Be sanctified. Tomorrow you shall eat meat. For I have heard you say: Who will give us meat to eat? It was well with us in Egypt. That the Lord may give you meat, and you may eat: not for one day, nor two, nor five, nor ten, nor twenty days, but even for a whole month, until it come out at your nostrils and become loathsome to you, because you have rejected the Lord who is among you, and have wept before him, saying: Why did we come out of Egypt? And Moses said: There are six hundred thousand footmen of this people, and do you say I will give them meat to eat for a whole month? Shall a multitude of sheep and oxen be killed, that it may suffice them? Or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together to fill them? And the Lord answered him: Is the hand of the Lord unable? You shall now see whether my word shall come to pass or not. Moses therefore came and told the people the words of the Lord, gathering together seventy men of the elders of Israel, and making them stand about the tabernacle. And the Lord came down in a cloud and spoke to him, taking away of the spirit that was in Moses and giving it to the seventy men. And when the spirit had rested on them, they prophesied, and did not cease. Now there remained in the camp two men, of whom one was called Eldad and the other Medad, upon whom the spirit rested—for they also had been among those enrolled—but they had not gone out to the tabernacle. And when they prophesied in the camp, a young man ran and told Moses, saying: Eldad and Medad prophesy in the camp.

Immediately Joshua the son of Nun, the minister of Moses and his chosen one, said: My lord Moses, forbid them. But he said: Why are you jealous for my sake? O that all the Lord's people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit upon them! And Moses returned into the camp, both he and the elders of Israel. Then a wind went out from the Lord and brought quails from the sea, and let them fall beside the camp, about a day's journey on this side and a day's journey on the other side, all around the camp, and about two cubits above the ground. And the people rose all that day and all night and all the next day, and gathered the quails. And they spread them out for themselves all around the camp. While the meat was yet between their teeth, before it was consumed, the anger of the Lord was kindled against the people, and the Lord struck the people with a very great plague. So that place was called the Graves of Craving, because there they buried the people who had craved. From the Graves of Craving the people journeyed to Hazeroth and remained there. Numbers 12.

And Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman whom he had married, for he had married a Cushite woman. And they said: Has the Lord indeed spoken only through Moses? Has he not spoken through us also? And the Lord heard it. Now the man Moses was very meek, more than all people who were on the face of the earth. And suddenly the Lord said to Moses and to Aaron and to Miriam: Come out, all three of you, to the tabernacle of meeting. And when they had come out, the Lord came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tabernacle and called Aaron and Miriam, and they both came forward. And he said: Hear my words. If there is a prophet among you, I the Lord make myself known to him in a vision, or I speak with him in

Numbers.

I speak to him in dreams. But my servant Moses is not such — he is faithful in all my house. I speak to him face to face, openly and not in riddles and figures, and he beholds the Lord. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses? And being angry, he departed from them. The cloud also withdrew that was over the tabernacle. And behold, Miriam appeared white with leprosy as snow. And when Aaron looked upon her and saw her struck with leprosy, he said to Moses: I beseech you, my lord, lay not upon us this sin, which we have foolishly committed: let her not be as one dead, and as an abortive that is cast forth from the mother's womb. And Moses cried to the Lord, saying: O God, I beseech you, heal her. And the Lord answered him: If her father had spit upon her face, ought she not to have been ashamed for seven days at least? Let her be separated seven days without the camp, and afterwards she shall be called back. Miriam therefore was put out of the camp seven days: and the people moved not from that place until Miriam was called back. ch. XIV.

Then they departed from Hazeroth and pitched their tents in the desert of Paran. And there the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Send men to explore the land of Canaan, which I will give to the children of Israel, one from each tribe, of each tribe a ruler. Moses did as the Lord commanded, sending from the desert of Paran men who were leaders, whose names are these: From the tribe of Reuben, Shammua the son of Zaccur; from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat the son of Hori; from the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh; from the tribe of Issachar, Igal the son of Joseph; from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Nun; from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti the son of Raphu; from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel the son of Sodi; from the tribe of Joseph, that is of Manasseh, Gaddi the son of Susi; from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel the son of Gemalli; from the tribe of Asher, Sethur the son of Michael; from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi the son of Vophsi; from the tribe of Gad, Geuel the son of Machi. These are the names of the men whom Moses sent to explore the land: and he called Hoshea the son of Nun, Joshua. Moses therefore sent them to explore the land of Canaan and said to them: Go up by the south side, and when you come to the mountains, view the land, what it is like, and the people that dwell therein, whether they are strong or weak, few or many; and the land itself, whether it is good or bad; what manner of cities, walled or without walls; and whether the soil is fat or barren, wooded or open. Be of good courage and bring us of the fruits of the land. Now it was the time when the first grapes are ripe. And when they had gone up, they explored the land from the desert of Zin to Rehob, as you go to Hamath. And they went up by the south side and came to Hebron, where were Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the sons of Anak; for Hebron was built seven years before Tanis, a city of Egypt. And they came to the brook of Eshcol, and cut down from thence a branch with one cluster of grapes, which two men carried on a staff; they took also of the pomegranates and of the figs. That place was called the brook Eshcol, because of the cluster which the children of Israel carried down from thence. And the spies, having surveyed the land in forty days, returned through all the region and came to Moses and Aaron and to all the congregation of the children of Israel in the desert of Paran, which is in Kadesh. And speaking to them and to all the multitude, they showed the fruits of the land and told them, saying: We came to the land to which you sent us, which indeed flows with

Numbers.

flowing with milk and honey, as can be known from these fruits: but it has very strong inhabitants, and great and walled cities. We saw there the offspring of Anak. Amalek dwells in the south, the Hittite and the Jebusite and the Amorite in the mountains. The Canaanite, however, lives by the sea and along the banks of the Jordan. Among these things Caleb, restraining the murmuring of the people that was rising against Moses, said: Let us go up and take possession of the land, for we are able to obtain it. But the others who had been with him said: We cannot go up to this people, for they are stronger than we. And they spread ill reports of the land which they had spied out to the children of Israel, saying: The land which we surveyed devours its inhabitants. The people we saw are of great stature. There we saw certain monsters of the children of Anak, of the race of giants: compared to whom we seemed like locusts. Chapter 14. And all the congregation lifted up their voices and wept that night: and the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying: Would that we had died in Egypt, and not in this vast wilderness. Would that the Lord does not bring us into this land, lest we fall by the sword, and our wives and children be led away captive. Is it not better to return to Egypt? And they said one to another: Let us make a captain and return to Egypt. When Moses and Aaron heard this, they fell prostrate on the ground before all the assembly of the children of Israel. But Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, who had also themselves explored the land, rent their garments: and spoke to all the multitude of the children of Israel saying: The land which we have surveyed is very good. If the Lord is pleased with us, he will bring us into it and give us a land flowing with milk and honey. Do not be

rebellious against the Lord: and do not fear the people of this land, for we can consume them like bread. All protection has departed from them: the Lord is with us, do not be afraid. And as all the multitude cried out and would stone them: the glory of the Lord appeared over the tabernacle of the covenant to all the children of Israel. And the Lord said to Moses: How long will this people detract from me? How long will they not believe me, for all the signs which I have done before them? I will strike them with pestilence and consume them: but I will make you a ruler over a nation greater and stronger than this. And Moses said to the Lord: That the Egyptians may hear, out of the midst of whom you brought forth this people: and the inhabitants of this land who have heard that you, O Lord, are among this people, and are seen face to face: and that your cloud protects them · and that you go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and in a pillar of fire by night: that you killed so great a multitude as if it were one man: and that the nations say: He was not able to bring the people into the land for which he had sworn: therefore he slew them in the wilderness. Let therefore the strength of the Lord be magnified, as you swore, saying: The Lord is patient and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity and wickedness, leaving no one unpunished: who visits the sins of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation: forgive, I beseech you, the sins of this people according to the greatness of your mercy, as you have been merciful to them from Egypt until this place. And the Lord said: I have forgiven according to your word. As I live: the glory of the Lord shall fill all the earth. But yet all the men who have seen my majesty and the signs which I did in Egypt and in the wilderness·

Numbers.

And they have put me to the test these ten times now, and have not obeyed my voice; they shall not see the land which I swore to their fathers, nor shall any of those who provoked me behold it. But my servant Caleb, who was filled with a different spirit and has followed me fully, I will bring into the land which he has explored, and his descendants shall possess it, because the Amalekite and the Canaanite dwell in the valleys. Tomorrow turn and set out into the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea. And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: How long shall this wicked multitude murmur against me? I have heard the complaints of the children of Israel. Say to them: As I live, says the Lord, as you have spoken in my hearing, so I will do to you. Your carcasses shall fall in this wilderness. All who were numbered among you, from twenty years old and upward, who have murmured against me, shall not enter the land over which I lifted my hand to make you dwell in it, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun. But your little ones, who you said would become prey, I will bring in, and they shall know the land which you rejected; but your corpses shall fall in this wilderness. Your children shall wander in the desert forty years and shall bear your unfaithfulness until your bodies are consumed in the desert; according to the number of forty days in which you spied out the land, a year shall be counted for each day. And for forty years you shall receive the penalty of your iniquities, and you shall know my vengeance. For as I have spoken, so will I do to all this wicked multitude that has risen against me; in this wilderness they shall waste away and die. So all the men whom Moses had sent to spy out the land, and who had returned and made all the congregation murmur against him by bringing back a bad report of the land, died; they died and were struck down before the Lord. But Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh survived among those who had gone to spy out the land. And Moses spoke all these words to all the children of Israel; and the people mourned greatly. And rising early in the morning they went up to the top of the mountain, saying: We are ready to go up to the place of which the Lord has spoken, for we have sinned. But Moses said: Why are you transgressing the command of the Lord? That will not prosper. Do not go up, for the Lord is not among you, lest you be struck down before your enemies. The Amalekite and the Canaanite are there before you, and you shall fall by the sword, because you have turned back from following the Lord, and the Lord will not be with you. But they presumed to go up to the top of the mountain. Nevertheless the ark of the covenant of the Lord and Moses did not depart out of the camp. Then the Amalekite and the Canaanite who dwelt in that hill country came down and defeated them, cutting them down as far as Hormah. Chapter 15.

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: When you come into the land you are to inhabit, which I am giving you, and you make an offering by fire to the Lord — a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering, or at your appointed feasts, to make a pleasing aroma to the Lord — from the herd or from the flock: whoever brings his offering, for a burnt offering or for a sacrifice, shall offer with it a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, a quarter of a hin; and wine for the drink offering, a quarter of a hin, you shall offer with the burnt offering or

Numbers

as a sacrifice. For each lamb and ram there shall be a similar offering of two tenths of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of oil, and a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord. When you prepare a burnt offering or a sacrifice for a vow or a peace offering from the herd, you shall offer with each bull three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil of half a hin of measure, and wine of the same measure as a drink offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord. You shall do likewise for each bull, ram, and lamb, whether native or alien. There shall be one statute and one ordinance for you and the alien living among you. The Lord spoke to Moses saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When you come into the land which I give you, and you eat of the bread of that land, you shall offer a portion as a contribution to the Lord. Just as you offer a contribution from the threshing floor, so also shall you offer a contribution from your dough to the Lord. Now if you inadvertently fail to observe all these commandments which the Lord has spoken to Moses — all that the Lord has commanded you through Moses, from the day the Lord gave command onward — and the congregation has forgotten to do it, then the whole congregation shall offer one bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord, along with its prescribed grain offering and drink offering, and one male goat as a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for all the congregation of the children of Israel, and they shall be forgiven, for it was unintentional; and they shall bring their offering, a food offering to the Lord, with their sin offering before the Lord for their unintentional sin. All the congregation of the children of Israel shall be forgiven, and the alien residing among you, because all the people were involved in the unintentional error. If only one person sins unintentionally, that person shall offer a female goat a year old as a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement before the Lord for the person who errs unintentionally; when atonement is made, the person shall be forgiven. You shall have one law for anyone who acts in error, whether native or alien. But whoever acts presumptuously, whether native or alien, reviles the Lord; that person shall be cut off from among the people. Because that person has despised the word of the Lord and has broken his commandment, that person shall be utterly cut off and shall bear the guilt. While the children of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath day. Those who found him gathering sticks brought him to Moses and Aaron and to all the congregation. They put him in custody, because it had not been made clear what should be done to him. The Lord said to Moses: The man shall be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him outside the camp. So all the congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him to death, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. The Lord said to Moses: Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them to make fringes on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and to put a cord of blue on the fringe at each corner. You shall have the fringe so that, when you see it, you will remember all the commandments of the Lord and do them, and not follow the desires of your own heart and your own eyes, which you are inclined to follow in pursuit of various lusts. So you shall remember and do all my commandments, and you shall be holy to your God. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God. Chapter XVI.

Now Korah, son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, rose up against Moses, along with two hundred fifty leaders of the congregation of the children of Israel, chosen from the assembly, prominent men at the time of the council, known by name

Numbers.

They were called together. And when they had risen up against Moses and Aaron, they said: It is enough for you, since all the multitude is holy, and the Lord is among them. Why do you raise yourselves above the congregation of the Lord? And when Moses heard this, he fell upon his face: and he spoke to Korah and to all the multitude. Tomorrow, he said, the Lord will show who belongs to him, and who is holy, and will bring them near to himself: and those he has chosen he will cause to come near to him. Do this therefore: Take every man his censer, Korah, and all your company; and put fire in them, and lay incense upon them before the Lord tomorrow: and the man whom the Lord chooses, he shall be holy. You take too much upon you, sons of Levi. And he said again to Korah: Hear now, sons of Levi. Is it too small a thing for you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to himself, to do the service of the tabernacle of the Lord, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them? And he has brought you near to him, and all your brethren the sons of Levi with you: and you seek the priesthood also: and all your company are gathered together against the Lord? And what is Aaron, that you murmur against him? And Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab. And they said: We will not come up. Is it a small thing that you have brought us out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness, unless you also make yourself a ruler over us? Moreover you have not brought us into a land that flows with milk and honey, or given us inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you put out the eyes of these men? We will not come up. And Moses was very angry, and said to the Lord: Do not respect their offering. You know that I have not taken one donkey from them, nor have I hurt one of them. And he said to Korah: You and all your company be before the Lord,

you and they, and Aaron, tomorrow. And take every man his censer and put incense in them, and bring before the Lord every man his censer, two hundred and fifty censers; and you and Aaron, each of you his censer. And they took every man his censer, and put fire in them, and laid incense upon them, and stood in the door of the tabernacle of the congregation with Moses and Aaron. And Korah gathered all the congregation against them to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: and the glory of the Lord appeared to all the congregation. And the Lord spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying: Separate yourselves from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment. And they fell upon their faces, and said: O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and will you be angry with all the congregation? And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the congregation, saying: Get away from around the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. And Moses rose up and went to Dathan and Abiram; and the elders of Israel followed him. And he spoke to the congregation, saying: Depart now from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, lest you be swept away in all their sins. So they got away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram on every side: and Dathan and Abiram came out, and stood in the door of their tents, and their wives, and their sons, and their little children. And Moses said: By this you shall know that the Lord has sent me to do all these works; for it is not from my own heart that I have done them. If these men die the common death of all men, and are visited after the visitation of all men, then the Lord has not sent me. But if the Lord make a new thing, and the earth open her mouth and swallow them up with all that belongs to them, and they go down alive into the pit, then you shall understand that these men have provoked the Lord. And it came to pass, as he had made an end of speaking all these words, that the ground split apart under them: and the earth opened her mouth

Numbers.

The earth swallowed them up along with their tents and all their possessions. They went down alive into the underworld, covered by the ground, and perished from the midst of the congregation. And all Israel that stood round about them fled at the cry of them as they perished, saying: Lest the earth swallow us up also. But a fire went out from the Lord and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who offered incense.

And the Lord spoke to Moses saying: Command Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest to take up the censers out of the burning, and scatter the strange fire on one side, because they are sanctified in the deaths of the sinners. And let him make them into broad plates and fasten them to the altar, because incense was offered in them to the Lord and they are sanctified, so that the children of Israel may see them for a sign and a memorial. So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers in which those whom the fire had devoured had offered, and he beat them into broad plates to fasten to the altar, that the children of Israel might have a reminder, so that no stranger who is not of the seed of Aaron should come near to offer incense to the Lord, and suffer the fate of Korah and his congregation, as the Lord spoke by the hand of Moses.

But on the next day all the congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron, saying: You have killed the people of the Lord. And when the congregation was gathered against Moses and against Aaron, they looked toward the tabernacle of meeting, and behold, the cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared. And Moses and Aaron came before the tabernacle of meeting. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Get away from this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment. And they fell on their faces. And Moses said to Aaron: Take a censer and put fire from the altar in it, put incense on it, and take it quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them,

for wrath has gone out from the Lord. The plague has begun. So Aaron took it as Moses commanded, and ran into the midst of the congregation; and already the plague had begun among the people. He put in the incense and made atonement for the people. And he stood between the dead and the living, so the plague was stopped. Now those who died in the plague were fourteen thousand seven hundred, besides those who died in the Korah affair. So Aaron returned to Moses at the door of the tabernacle of meeting, for the plague had stopped.

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, and get from each one of them a rod according to their fathers' house, from all their leaders according to their fathers' houses — twelve rods. Write each man's name on his rod. And you shall write Aaron's name on the rod of Levi. For there shall be one rod for the head of each father's house. Then you shall place them in the tabernacle of meeting before the testimony, where I meet with you. And it shall be that the rod of the man whom I choose will blossom; thus I will make to cease from Me the complaints of the children of Israel, which they make against you. So Moses spoke to the children of Israel, and each of their leaders gave him a rod, one rod for each leader according to their fathers' houses — twelve rods. And the rod of Aaron was among their rods. And Moses placed the rods before the Lord in the tabernacle of testimony. Now it came to pass on the next day that Moses went into the tabernacle of testimony, and behold, the rod of Aaron, of the house of Levi, had budded and put forth buds and bloomed blossoms and yielded ripe almonds. Then Moses brought out all the rods from before the Lord to all the children of Israel; and they looked, and each man took his rod. And the Lord said to Moses: Bring Aaron's rod back before the Testimony, to be kept as a sign against the rebels among the children of Israel, so that their complaints against me may cease,

Numbers

Your complaints will not cause you to die. And Moses did as the Lord commanded. And the children of Israel said to Moses: Behold, we are consumed, we all perish. Whoever approaches the tabernacle of the Lord dies. Are we all to be utterly destroyed?

And the Lord said to Aaron. Chapter 18.

You and your sons and your father's household with you shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary: and you and your sons together shall bear the sins of your priesthood. And your brothers also of the tribe of Levi, the scepter of your father, bring with you, and let them be joined to you and minister to you. But you and your sons shall minister in the tabernacle of testimony. And the Levites shall watch for your commands, and all the work of the tabernacle: only they shall not come near the vessels of the sanctuary and the altar, lest both they and you should die. They shall be with you, and watch over the tabernacle of the congregation, and all the service of the tabernacle: no stranger shall join himself with you. You shall watch over the sanctuary and the altar, lest wrath come upon the children of Israel. I have given you your brothers the Levites from among the children of Israel: they are a gift to the Lord, to do the service of the tabernacle. But you and your sons with you shall keep your priesthood in everything that belongs to the altar, and within the veil; and you shall do the service: I have given your priesthood to you as a gift for service: the stranger that comes near shall be put to death. And the Lord spoke to Aaron: Behold, I have given you the charge of my offerings. All things that are sanctified by the children of Israel I have delivered to you and your sons as a priestly due, an everlasting ordinance. These therefore shall you take of those things that are sanctified and offered to the Lord. Every offering and sacrifice and whatever is given to me for sin and trespass, which is rendered to me, shall be most holy for you and your sons:

It shall be yours and your sons'. You shall eat it in the sanctuary; the males only shall eat of it, because it is most holy to you. The firstfruits also, which the children of Israel shall vow and offer: I have given to you and to your sons and daughters as an everlasting right. He that is clean in your house shall eat of them. All the best of the oil and of the wine and of the wheat, the firstfruits of them which they shall give to the Lord, I have given to you. All the firstfruits of the land, which they bring to the Lord, shall be yours; he that is clean in your house shall eat of them. Everything that the children of Israel shall dedicate by vow shall be yours. Whatever first opens the womb, of all flesh which they offer to the Lord, whether of men or of animals, shall be yours: only you shall redeem the firstborn of man, and every firstborn of unclean animals you shall also redeem. And those that are to be redeemed shall be redeemed from a month old at your estimation, for the money of five shekels, according to the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs. But the firstborn of a cow, or the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat, you shall not redeem; they are holy: you shall sprinkle their blood upon the altar, and shall burn their fat for an offering made by fire, for a sweet savor to the Lord. And the flesh of them shall be yours, as the wave breast and the right shoulder are yours. All the offerings of the holy things which the children of Israel offer to the Lord, I have given to you and your sons and daughters with you, as an everlasting ordinance. It is a covenant of salt forever before the Lord for you and your descendants with you. And the Lord said to Aaron: You shall have no inheritance in their land, neither shall you have any part among them: I am your part and your inheritance among the children of Israel. And behold, I have given the children of Levi all the tithes in Israel for an inheritance, for their service which they serve, even the service of the tabernacle of the congregation, so that the children of Israel come no more near

Numbers

The children of Israel shall come to the tabernacle, and they shall not incur mortal sin; only the sons of Levi, who serve in the tabernacle and bear the sins of the people, shall have this duty, which is a perpetual ordinance for your generations. They shall possess nothing else, content with the tithe as an offering; what I have set apart for their use and necessaries. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Command the Levites and declare to them: When you receive from the children of Israel the tithes which I have given you, offer the firstfruits of them to the Lord, that is, a tenth part of the tenth, so that it may be counted to you as an offering of firstfruits, both from the threshing floors and from the winepresses and from all things from which you receive firstfruits to offer to the Lord, to give to Aaron the priest. All that you offer from your tithes you shall separate as gifts to the Lord; the best and choicest parts shall be set apart. And you shall say to them: When you offer the best and choicest parts from your tithes, it shall be counted to you as if from the threshing floor and the winepress you had offered firstfruits; and you may eat them in every place, both you and your households, for it is your wage for the ministry by which you serve in the tabernacle of testimony; and you shall not sin in this matter, keeping the best parts for yourselves, lest you defile the offerings of the children of Israel and die.

And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: This is the ordinance of the sacrificial law which the Lord has established. Command the children of Israel to bring to you a red heifer of full age, without blemish, upon which no yoke has been laid; and you shall deliver her to Eleazar the priest. She shall be led outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence; and he shall dip his finger in her blood and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the tabernacle of testimony, and burn her entirely in the sight of all, with her hide, her flesh, her blood, and her dung given to the flames.

The priest shall also cast cedarwood, hyssop, and twice-dyed scarlet into the fire consuming the heifer. Then he shall wash his garments and body in water, and afterward he may enter the camp, but he shall be unclean until evening. Likewise, he who burned her shall wash his garments and his body, and shall be unclean until evening. Then a clean man shall gather up the ashes of the heifer and put them outside the camp in a clean place, where they shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Israel as water of purification, for it is an offering for sin. And he who gathered the ashes of the heifer shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. This shall be a perpetual ordinance for the children of Israel and for the strangers who dwell among them. Whoever touches the dead body of any person shall be unclean for seven days; he shall be purified with this water on the third day and on the seventh day, and then he shall be clean. But if he is not sprinkled on the third day, he cannot be cleansed on the seventh day. Everyone who touches the body of a dead person and is not sprinkled with this mixture shall defile the tabernacle of the Lord and shall be cut off from Israel; because the water of purification was not sprinkled upon him, he shall be unclean, and his uncleanness shall remain upon him. This is the law for a person who dies in a tent: all who enter the tent and all vessels that are in it shall be unclean for seven days. Any open vessel with no cover fastened upon it shall be unclean. And whoever in an open field touches one that has been slain with a sword, or a dead body, or a bone of a man, or a grave, shall be unclean seven days. They shall take of the ashes of the sin offering and pour living water upon them in a vessel; then a clean person shall dip hyssop in the water and sprinkle it upon them.

Numbers.

Every tent and all furnishings, and the people who have been contaminated by such contact, shall be made clean: the world will purify the unclean on the third and seventh day. On the seventh day he shall wash himself and his garments, and he shall be unclean until evening. If anyone has not been cleansed in this way, that person shall be cut off from the congregation, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the Lord. The water of purification was not sprinkled on him. This shall be a permanent and lawful ordinance. Moreover, the one who sprinkles the water shall wash his garments. Whoever touches the water of purification shall be unclean until evening. Whatever the unclean person touches shall become unclean; and any soul that touches it shall be unclean until evening. Chapter 20.

Then the children of Israel and all the congregation came to the desert of Zin in the first month, and the people settled in Kadesh. And Miriam died there and was buried in that place. When the people were in need of water, they gathered against Moses and Aaron, and rising up in sedition they said: Would that we had perished among our brothers before the Lord. Why have you brought the congregation of the Lord into this wilderness, that both we and our cattle should die here? Why did you make us go up out of Egypt, and bring us to this evil place, which cannot be sown, nor brings forth figs, nor vines, nor pomegranates, and moreover has no water to drink? And Moses and Aaron, leaving the multitude, went into the tabernacle of the covenant, and fell upon the ground, and cried to the Lord, saying: O Lord God, hear the cry of this people, and open to them your treasury, a fountain of living water, that being satisfied, their murmuring may cease. And the glory of the Lord appeared over them. And the Lord spoke to Moses,

saying: Take the rod, and assemble the congregation, you and Aaron your brother, and speak to the rock before their eyes, and it shall yield water. When you have brought water out of the rock, all the multitude and their cattle shall drink. Moses therefore took the rod which was before the Lord, as he had commanded him. Having assembled the multitude before the rock, he said to them: Hear, you rebels and unbelievers. Can we bring water out of this rock for you? And when Moses had lifted up his hand and struck the rock twice with the rod, there came forth water in great abundance, so that the people and their cattle drank. And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Because you did not believe me, to sanctify me before the children of Israel, you shall not bring this congregation into the land which I will give them. This is the water of contradiction, where the children of Israel strove against the Lord, and he was sanctified in them. In the meantime Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom, to say: Thus says your brother Israel: You know all the toil that has come upon us: how our fathers went down into Egypt, and we dwelt there a long time, and the Egyptians afflicted us and our fathers: and how we cried to the Lord, and he heard us, and sent an angel who brought us out of Egypt. Behold, we are now in the city of Kadesh, which is at the edge of your borders. We beg you to let us pass through your land. We will not go through the fields or the vineyards, nor will we drink the water from your wells; we will go along the king's highway, turning neither to the right hand nor to the left, until we have passed through your territory. And Edom answered him: You shall not pass through me. If you attempt it, I will come out armed against you. And the children of Israel said: We will go by the highway; and if we and our cattle drink any of your water, we will pay you for it.

Numbers.

What is just. There shall be no difficulty in the price: let us pass through so quickly. But he answered: You shall not pass through. And immediately he came out against them with an infinite multitude and a strong hand, and would not consent to their plea to grant them passage through his borders. Therefore Israel turned away from him. And when they had moved camp from Kadesh, they came to Mount Hor, which is on the border of the land of Edom, where the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Let Aaron go to his people, for he shall not enter the land which I have given to the children of Israel, because he was unbelieving toward my word at the waters of contradiction. Take Aaron and his son with him, and lead them up to Mount Hor. And when you have stripped his father of his vestments, you shall put them on Eleazar his son, and Aaron shall be gathered to his people and die there. Moses did as the Lord commanded, and they went up Mount Hor before all the multitude. And when Aaron had been stripped of his vestments, he put them on Eleazar his son. And he died there on the top of the mountain, and Moses came down with Eleazar. And all the congregation seeing that Aaron was dead, wept for him thirty days throughout all their families. Chapter XXI.

When the Canaanite king of Arad, who dwelt in the south, heard that Israel came by the way of the spies, he fought against them, and conquering, took some of them captive. But Israel, binding himself by a vow to the Lord, said: If you deliver this people into my hand, I will utterly destroy their cities. The Lord heard the prayers of Israel, and delivered up the Canaanites, and they utterly destroyed them and their cities, and called the name of that place Hormah, that is, Anathema. And they set out from Mount Hor by the way that leads to the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom. And the people began to be weary of the journey and the labor, and speaking against

the Lord and Moses, said: Why did you bring us out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread, there is no water, and our soul loathes this very light food. Therefore the Lord sent among the people fiery serpents, and many of them were bitten and died. They came to Moses and said: We have sinned, because we have spoken against the Lord and against you. Pray that he may take away the serpents from us. Moses prayed for the people. And the Lord said to him: Make a bronze serpent and set it up as a sign. Whoever is bitten and looks upon it shall live. Moses therefore made a bronze serpent and set it up as a sign. When those who were bitten looked upon it, they were healed. And the children of Israel set out and camped in Oboth. And departing from there, they pitched their tents in Ije-abarim, in the wilderness that faces Moab toward the east. And moving from there they came to the valley of Zared. And setting out from there they camped on the other side of Arnon, which is in the desert and sticks out into the border of the Amorites. For Arnon is the border of Moab, dividing Moab from the Amorites. Therefore it is said in the book of the wars of the Lord: As he did in the Red Sea, so shall he do in the streams of Arnon. The rocks of the torrents were bowed down that they might rest in Arnon, and lie down in the borders of the Moabites. And in that place a well appeared, concerning which the Lord said to Moses: Gather the people together, and I will give them water. Then Israel sang this song: Let the well spring up. They sang together: A well which the princes dug, and the leaders of the multitude prepared, with the lawgiver and their staffs. From the wilderness to Mattanah, from Mattanah to Nahaliel, from Nahaliel to Bamoth. Bamoth is in the valley which is in the country of Moab, on the top of Pisgah, which looks toward

Numbers

Against the wilderness. Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying: Allow me, I pray, to pass through your land. We will not turn aside into the fields or vineyards, nor will we drink water from wells. We will travel by the royal road until we have passed through your territory. But he would not allow Israel to pass through his borders; rather he gathered his army and went out into the wilderness against them, and came to Jahaz and fought against them. He was defeated by the edge of the sword, and Israel possessed his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the sons of Ammon, for the border of the Ammonites was strongly fortified. Israel took all these cities, and dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon and all its villages. Now Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the king of Moab and taken all his land as far as the Arnon. Therefore it is said in a proverb: Come to Heshbon, let the city of Sihon be built and established. For fire went forth from Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon, and devoured Ar of Moab and the lords of the heights of Arnon. Woe to you, O Moab! You are destroyed, O people of Chemosh! He gave his sons as fugitives and his daughters as captives to Sihon king of the Amorites. Their yoke has perished from Heshbon to Dibon; they came weary to Nophah, which reaches to Medeba. So Israel dwelt in the land of the Amorites. And Moses sent to spy out Jazer, and they took its villages and drove out the Amorites that were there. Then they turned and went up by the way of Bashan; and Og king of Bashan came out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei. And the Lord said to Moses: Do not fear him, for I have given him into your hand, and all his people, and his land; and you shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt at Heshbon.

So they struck him and his sons and all his people, until there was not one survivor left, and they possessed his land. Then the Israelites set out and camped in the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho. Chapter 22.

Now Balak the son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites. And Moab was in great dread of the people, because they were many, and Moab was overcome with fear because of the people of Israel. And Moab said to the elders of Midian: This horde will now lick up all that is around us, as the ox licks up the grass of the field. So Balak the son of Zippor, who was king of Moab at that time, sent messengers to Balaam the son of Beor, who dwelt by the river in the land of the sons of Ammon, to call him, saying: Behold, a people has come out of Egypt; they have covered the face of the earth and they are settling opposite me. Come now, curse this people for me, since they are too mighty for me. Perhaps I shall be able to defeat them and drive them out of the land. For I know that whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed. So the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed with the fees for divination in their hands. They came to Balaam and told him the words of Balak. And he said to them: Stay here tonight, and I will bring you back word, as the Lord speaks to me. So the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam. And God came to Balaam and said: Who are these men with you? And he said: Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent to me, saying: Behold, a people has come out of Egypt and has covered the face of the earth. Come now, curse them for me; perhaps I shall be able to fight against them and drive them out. And God said to Balaam: You shall not go with them; you shall not curse the people, for they are blessed.

Numbers.

He rose in the morning and said to the princes: Go back to your land, for God has forbidden me to go with you. The princes returned and said to Balak: Balaam refused to come with us. Then Balak sent again more and more noble messengers than before. They came to Balaam and said: Thus says Balak son of Zippor: Do not delay in coming to me. I am prepared to honor you and will give you whatever you ask. Come and curse this people. Balaam answered: Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot change the word of the Lord my God, to speak more or less than He commands. But I ask you to stay here this night as well, so that I may know what the Lord will answer me again. God came to Balaam at night and said to him: If these men have come to call you, rise and go with them; yet only do what I shall command you. Balaam rose in the morning, saddled his donkey, and set out with them; and God was angry. The angel of the Lord stood in the road against Balaam, who was riding on his donkey, with two servants with him. When the donkey saw the angel of the Lord standing in the road with a drawn sword, she turned off the road and went into the field. Balaam beat her to bring her back to the road. Then the angel stood in a narrow pass between two walls that enclosed a vineyard. When the donkey saw the angel, she pressed herself against the wall and crushed Balaam's foot against it. He beat her again. And again the angel moved to a narrow place where there was no room to turn right or left. She stood still. When the donkey saw the angel standing there, she lay down under Balaam. Balaam was furious and beat her with his staff. Then the Lord opened the mouth of the donkey, and she spoke: What have I done to you?

Why have you struck me these three times? Balaam answered: Because you have mocked me. If I had a sword I would kill you. The donkey said: Am I not your own donkey, which you have always ridden to this day? Have I ever done such a thing to you before? He said: No. Then the Lord opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the angel of the Lord standing in the road with a drawn sword; and he bowed down and fell on his face. The angel said to him: Why have you struck your donkey three times? I came out to oppose you because your way is perverse and contrary to me. If the donkey had not turned aside from me these three times, I would have killed you and let her live. Balaam said: I have sinned, for I did not know that you stood in the road against me. Now, if it displeases you, I will go back. The angel said: Go with these men, but speak only what I tell you. So he went with the princes. When Balak heard this, he went out to meet him in the city of Moab, which is on the border of the Arnon. He said to Balaam: I sent messengers to call you. Why did you not come to me at once? Did you think I was not able to honor you? Balaam replied: Here I am. But can I say anything other than what God puts in my mouth? So they went together and came to the city on the far border of his kingdom. Balak slaughtered oxen and sheep and sent portions to Balaam and the princes who were with him. In the morning Balak took Balaam up to the high places of Baal, and from there he could see the outermost part of the people. Chapter twenty-three.

And Balaam said to Balak: Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams of the same number. And when he had done according to the word

· Numbers ·

77·

Balaam — they placed together a calf and a ram upon the altar. And Balak said to Balaam: "Stay here beside your burnt offering while I go; perhaps the Lord will meet me, and whatever he commands I will tell you." And when he had gone quickly, God met him. And Balaam said to him: "I have set up seven altars and laid a calf and a ram upon each." And the Lord put a word in his mouth and said: "Return to Balak, and speak these words." And returning, he found Balak standing beside his burnt offering, with all the princes of Moab. And Balaam took up his parable and said: "From Aram, Balak king of Moab has brought me, from the mountains of the east. Come, he said, curse Jacob for me; come, denounce Israel. How can I curse whom God has not cursed? How can I denounce whom the Lord has not denounced? From the top of the rocks I see him, from the hills I behold him. Behold, a people dwelling alone, not reckoning itself among the nations. Who can count the dust of Jacob, or number the fourth part of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my end be like theirs." Then Balak said to Balaam: "What have you done to me? I brought you to curse my enemies, and behold, you have blessed them." And he answered: "Can I say anything other than what the Lord puts in my mouth?" Then Balak said: "Come with me to another place from which you can see part of them, but not all of them, and curse them from there." And when he had brought him to the top of Mount Pisgah, Balaam built seven altars and offered a calf and a ram on each, and said to Balak: "Stand here beside your burnt offering while I go to meet him." And when the Lord met him and put a word in his mouth, he said: "Return to Balak and speak thus." And he returned and found him standing beside his burnt offering with the princes of Moab. And Balak said to him: "What has the Lord spoken?" And he took up his parable and said: "Rise up, Balak, and hear; listen to me, son of Zippor. God is not a man that he should lie, nor a son of man that he should change his mind. Has he spoken and will he not fulfill? Has he promised and will he not carry it out? I was brought here to bless; he has blessed and I cannot reverse it. He has not beheld iniquity in Jacob, nor has he seen trouble in Israel. The Lord their God is with them, and the shout of a king is among them. God brought them out of Egypt; he is for them like the horns of the wild ox. For there is no enchantment against Jacob, no divination against Israel. Now it shall be said of Jacob and Israel: 'What has God done!' Behold, the people rises as a lioness, and like a lion it lifts itself up. It will not lie down until it has devoured the prey and drunk the blood of the slain." Then Balak said to Balaam: "Neither curse them at all nor bless them at all." But Balaam answered: "Did I not tell you that whatever the Lord says, that I must do?" Then Balak said to him: "Come now, I will take you to another place; perhaps it will please God that you may curse them from there." And he brought him to the top of Mount Peor, which overlooks the wasteland, and Balaam said to him: "Build for me here seven altars and prepare seven bulls and seven rams." And Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar. Chapter 24.

When Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord to bless Israel, he did not go as at other times to seek omens, but set his face toward the wilderness, and lifting up

Numbers.

Israel saw with his eyes those dwelling in their tents by their tribes, and the spirit of God came upon him, and taking up his parable he said: Balaam the son of Beor has said, the man whose eye was closed has said, the hearer of the words of God who beholds the vision of the Almighty, who falls down with his eyes opened. How beautiful are your tents, O Jacob, and your tabernacles, O Israel, like shady valleys, like gardens by rivers, like the tabernacles which the Lord has pitched, like cedar trees beside the waters. Water shall flow from his bucket, and his seed shall be in many waters. His king shall be exalted above Agag, and his kingdom shall be lifted up. God brought him out of Egypt, whose strength is like a rhinoceros. He shall devour the nations of his enemies, and shall break their bones, and pierce them with his arrows. He couched, he lay down as a lion, and as a great lion: who shall stir him up? Blessed is he that blesses you, and cursed is he that curses you. And Balak's anger was kindled against Balaam, and he smote his hands together: and Balak said to Balaam, I called you to curse my enemies, but behold, you have altogether blessed them these three times. Therefore flee now to your place: I thought to promote you to great honor, but the Lord has kept you back from honor. Balaam said to Balak, Did I not also speak to your messengers which you sent to me, saying, if Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the commandment of the Lord, to do either good or bad of my own mind; but what the Lord says, that will I speak? And now behold, I go to my people: come, I will tell you what this people shall do to your people in the latter days. And he took up his parable and said: Balaam the son of Beor has said, the man whose eye was closed has said, the hearer of the words of God, who knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling into a trance, but having his eyes open. I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not near. There shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Scepter shall rise out of Israel, and shall strike through the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Seth. And Edom shall be a possession, and Seir also shall be a possession for his enemies; and Israel shall do valiantly. Out of Jacob shall come he that shall have dominion, and shall destroy the remnant of the city. And when he saw Amalek, he took up his parable and said, Amalek was the first of the nations; but his latter end shall be that he perish. And he looked on the Kenites, and took up his parable and said, Strong is your dwelling place, and you put your nest in a rock; nevertheless the Kenite shall be wasted, until Asshur shall carry you away captive. And he took up his parable and said, Alas, who shall live when God does this? And ships shall come from the coast of Italy, and shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict the Hebrews; and they too shall perish forever. And Balaam rose up and went and returned to his place: and Balak also went his way. Chapter 25.

And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, who called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods. And the people ate, and bowed down to their gods. And Israel joined himself to Baal-peor. And the Lord's anger was kindled against Israel; and the Lord said to Moses, Take all the chiefs of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel. And Moses said to the judges of Israel, Every one of you slay his men that have joined themselves to Baal-peor. And behold, one of the children of Israel came and brought to his brothers a Midianite woman in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the congregation of the children of Israel, who were weeping at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.

Numbers

When Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw this, he rose up from the midst of the congregation and took a spear in his hand; and he went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel and the woman, through her belly. So the plague was stopped from the people of Israel, and those who died by the plague were twenty-four thousand. And the Lord said to Moses: Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned away my wrath from the children of Israel, because he was zealous with my zeal among them, so that I did not consume the children of Israel in my zeal. Therefore say to him: Behold, I give to him my covenant of peace; and it shall be to him and to his descendants after him the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he was zealous for his God, and made atonement for the children of Israel. Now the name of the Israelite who was slain, who was slain with the Midianite woman, was Zimri, son of Salu, a leader of a father's house among the Simeonites. And the name of the Midianite woman who was slain was Cozbi, daughter of Zur, a leader of the people of a father's house in Midian. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Harass the Midianites and strike them; for they have harassed you with their wiles with which they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor, and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of the leader of Midian, their sister, who was slain on the day of the plague in the matter of Peor. Chapter 26.

After the blood of the wicked had been shed, the Lord said to Moses and to Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest: Take a census of all the congregation of the children of Israel, from twenty years old and upward, by their fathers' houses, all who are able to go to war in Israel. And Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them in the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho, saying to those who were twenty years old and upward, just as the Lord commanded. And these are their numbers: Reuben, the firstborn of Israel. The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, from whom the family of the Hanochites; Pallu, from whom the family of the Palluites; Hezron, from whom the family of the Hezronites; Carmi, from whom the family of the Carmites. These are the families of Reuben, and those numbered of them were forty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty. The son of Pallu was Eliab. The sons of Eliab were Nemuel, and Dathan, and Abiram. These are the Dathan and Abiram, who were chosen from the congregation, who strove against Moses and Aaron in the company of Korah, when they strove against the Lord, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up together with Korah, when that company died, when the fire devoured two hundred and fifty men; and they became a sign. Notwithstanding, the sons of Korah did not die. The sons of Simeon according to their families: Nemuel, from whom the family of the Nemuelites; Jamin, from whom the family of the Jaminites; Jachin, from whom the family of the Jachinites; Zerah, from whom the family of the Zerahites; Shaul, from whom the family of the Shaulites. These are the families of Simeon, and their total number was twenty-two thousand two hundred. The sons of Gad according to their families: Zephon, from whom the family of the Zephonites; Haggi, from whom the family of the Haggites; Shuni, from whom the family of the Shunites; Ozni, from whom the family of the Oznites; Eri, from whom the family of the Erites; Arod, from whom the family of the Arodites; Areli, from whom the family of the Arelites. These are the families of Gad, and their total number was forty thousand five hundred. The sons of Judah were Er and Onan, and Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. And the sons of Judah according to their families were: Shelah, from whom the family of the Shelanites; Perez, from whom the family of the Perezites; Zerah, from whom the family of the Zerahites. And the sons of

Numbers

Pharez: Hezron, from whom comes the family of the Hezronites; and Hamul, from whom comes the family of the Hamulites. These are the families of Judah, whose total number was seventy-six thousand five hundred. The sons of Issachar by their clans: Tola, from whom comes the family of the Tolaites; Puvah, from whom comes the family of the Punites; Jashub, from whom comes the family of the Jashubites; Shimron, from whom comes the family of the Shimronites. These are the clans of Issachar, whose number was sixty-four thousand three hundred. The sons of Zebulun by their clans: Sered, from whom comes the family of the Seredites; Elon, from whom comes the family of the Elonites; Jahleel, from whom comes the family of the Jahleelites. These are the clans of Zebulun, whose number was sixty thousand five hundred. The sons of Joseph by their clans: Manasseh and Ephraim. From Manasseh was born Machir, from whom comes the family of the Machirites. Machir begot Gilead, from whom comes the family of the Gileadites. Gilead had sons: Iezer, from whom comes the family of the Iezerites; and Helek, from whom comes the family of the Helekites; and Asriel, from whom comes the family of the Asrielites; and Shechem, from whom comes the family of the Shechemites; and Shemida, from whom comes the family of the Shemidaites; and Hepher, from whom comes the family of the Hepherites. Now Hepher's son Zelophehad had no sons, only daughters, whose names were: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. These are the families of Manasseh, and their number was fifty-two thousand seven hundred. The sons of Ephraim by their clans were these: Shuthelah, from whom comes the family of the Shuthelahites; Becher, from whom comes the family of the Becherites; Tahan, from whom comes the family of the Tahanites. And the son of Shuthelah was Eran, from whom comes the family of the Eranites. These are the clans of Ephraim, whose number was thirty-

two thousand five hundred. These are the sons of Joseph by their families. The sons of Benjamin by their clans: Bela, from whom comes the family of the Belaites; Ashbel, from whom comes the family of the Ashbelites; Ahiram, from whom comes the family of the Ahiramites; Shupham, from whom comes the family of the Shuphamites; Hupham, from whom comes the family of the Huphamites. The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: from Ard comes the family of the Ardites; from Naaman the family of the Naamites. These are the sons of Benjamin by their clans, whose number was forty-five thousand six hundred. The sons of Dan by their clans: Shuham, from whom comes the family of the Shuhamites. These are the clans of Dan by their families. All were Shuhamites, whose number was sixty-four thousand seven hundred. The sons of Asher by their clans: Imnah, from whom comes the family of the Imnites; Ishvi, from whom comes the family of the Ishvites; Beriah, from whom comes the family of the Beriites. The sons of Beriah: Heber, from whom comes the family of the Heberites; and Malchiel, from whom comes the family of the Malchielites. The name of Asher's daughter was Serah. These are the clans of Asher, and their number was fifty-three thousand four hundred. The sons of Naphtali by their clans: Jahzeel, from whom comes the family of the Jahzeelites; Guni, from whom comes the family of the Gunites; Jezer, from whom comes the family of the Jezerites; Shillem, from whom comes the family of the Shillemites. These are the clans of Naphtali by their families, whose number was forty-five thousand four hundred. This is the total of the sons of Israel who were counted: six hundred and one thousand seven hundred and thirty. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: The land shall be divided among these according to the number of names as an inheritance. To the larger group you shall give a larger inheritance, and to the smaller

. Numbers .

to the smaller, as they are now counted they must hand over possession: only so that the lot divides the land among the tribes and families. Whatever falls by lot, let more or fewer receive it accordingly. This also is the number of the sons of Levi by their families. Gershon, from whom the family of the Gershonites; Kohath, from whom the family of the Kohathites; Merari, from whom the family of the Merarites. These are the families of Levi: the family of Libnites, the family of Hebronites, the family of Mahlites, the family of Mushites, the family of Korahites. And Kohath begat Amram, who had for his wife Jochebed the daughter of Levi, who was born to him in Egypt. She bore to her husband Amram the sons Aaron and Moses, and Miriam their sister. From Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu and Eleazar and Ithamar; of whom Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the Lord. And all who were numbered were twenty-three thousand of the male sex, from one month old and upward; they were not enrolled among the children of Israel, because no inheritance was given them among the rest. This is the number of the children of Israel who were counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest in the plains of Moab above the Jordan near Jericho: among whom there was not one of those previously counted by Moses and Aaron in the desert of Sinai. For the Lord had foretold that they would all die in the wilderness. And none of them remained except Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun. Chapter XXVII.

Then came the daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, who was the son of Joseph — whose names were Mahlah, and Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah — and they stood before Moses and Eleazar the priest and all the leaders of the people at the door of the tabernacle of the covenant, and said: Our father

died in the desert, and he was not in the company that rose up against the Lord under Korah, but he died in his own sin. He had no male sons. Why should his name be taken away from his family, because he has no son? Give us a possession among the kinsmen of our father. And Moses brought their cause before the Lord. And the Lord said to him: The daughters of Zelophehad ask a just thing. Give them a possession among the kinsmen of their father, and let them succeed to his inheritance. And to the children of Israel you shall say this: When a man dies without a son, his inheritance shall pass to his daughter. If he has no daughter, his brothers shall be his heirs. But if he has no brothers, you shall give the inheritance to his father's brothers. And if he has no uncles, the inheritance shall be given to those who are nearest of kin to him. This shall be for the children of Israel a statute of judgment, as the Lord commanded Moses. The Lord also said to Moses: Go up into this mountain of Abarim, and behold from there the land which I will give to the children of Israel. And when you have seen it, you also shall be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was gathered: because you trespassed against me in the desert of Zin, in the strife of the congregation, and did not sanctify me before them at the waters. These are the waters of Meribah in Kadesh in the desert of Zin. And Moses answered the Lord: May the Lord God of the spirits of all flesh provide a man who may be over this multitude, and who may go out and go in before them, and lead them out and bring them in, that the congregation of the Lord be not as sheep without a shepherd. And the Lord said to him: Take Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and put your hand upon him. He shall stand before Eleazar the priest and all the congregation, and you shall give

Numbers.

his commandments before all the people, and a portion of your glory: so that all the congregation of the children of Israel may hear him. For whatever must be done, Eleazar the priest shall consult the Lord. At his word they shall go out and come in, he and all the children of Israel with him, and all the rest of the multitude. As Moses had commanded, as the Lord had instructed. And when he had taken Joshua, he set him before Eleazar the priest and before all the assembly, and laying his hands upon his head, he repeated all things that the Lord had commanded. Chapter 28.

The Lord also said to Moses: Command the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: My offering and my bread with the incense of a most sweet odor, offer to me in their seasons. These are the sacrifices which you shall offer. Two lambs of a year old without blemish every day for a continual burnt offering: one you shall offer in the morning, and the other in the evening: and a tenth part of an ephah of fine flour sprinkled with the purest oil, and a fourth part of a hin. It is a continual burnt offering which you offered at Mount Sinai for a most sweet odor of incense to the Lord. And you shall offer a fourth part of a hin of wine for libation for each lamb in the sanctuary of the Lord: and the other lamb you shall offer in the evening according to all the rite of the morning sacrifice and of its libations, for an offering of a most sweet odor to the Lord. On the sabbath day you shall offer two lambs of a year old without blemish, and two tenths of fine flour sprinkled with oil for a sacrifice, and the libations that are duly poured out for each sabbath as a continual burnt offering. In the beginning of your months you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord: two calves of the herd, one ram, seven lambs of a year old without blemish: and three tenths of fine flour sprinkled with oil for each calf: and two

tenths of fine flour sprinkled with oil for each ram: and one tenth of fine flour sprinkled with oil as a sacrifice for each lamb. It is a burnt offering of most sweet odor and an incense to the Lord. Their libations of wine shall be as follows: half a hin for each calf, one third of a hin for each ram, and one fourth for each lamb. This shall be the burnt offering for every month as each month succeeds through the year. And one goat shall be offered to the Lord for a sin offering as a continual burnt offering with its libations. In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, shall be the Passover of the Lord, and on the fifteenth day shall be the solemnity. For seven days they shall eat unleavened bread: the first day shall be venerable and holy. You shall do no servile work on it. And you shall offer a burnt offering, an incense to the Lord: two calves of the herd, one ram, seven lambs of a year old without blemish: and the sacrifices of each of them of fine flour sprinkled with oil: three tenths for each calf, two tenths for each ram, and one tenth of a tenth for each of the seven lambs: and one goat for sin to make atonement for you: besides the morning burnt offering which you shall always offer. So you shall do every day for seven days as the food of the offering by fire, for a most sweet odor to the Lord, which shall rise from the burnt offering and from the libations of each. The seventh day also shall be most celebrated and holy for you. You shall do no servile work on it. Also on the day of the firstfruits, when you offer new grain to the Lord after the weeks are complete, it shall be venerable and holy. You shall do no menial work on it. And you shall offer a burnt offering for a most sweet odor to the Lord: two calves of the herd, one ram, seven lambs of a year old

Numbers.

Seven unblemished ones, and in their sacrifices similar offerings of oil mixed with three tenths for each bull, two tenths for each ram, and one tenth for each lamb, of which seven lambs together, and a male goat as a sin offering — beyond the perpetual burnt offering and its libation. You shall offer all these unblemished animals with their libations. Chapter 29.

The first day of the seventh month likewise shall be holy and venerable for you. You shall do no servile work on it, for it is the day of the sounding of trumpets. And you shall offer a burnt offering as a most sweet savor to the Lord: one bull from the herd, one ram, and seven unblemished yearling lambs; and in their sacrifices, fine flour mixed with oil — three tenths for each bull, two tenths for the ram, one tenth for each of the seven lambs; and a male goat for sin, which is offered as atonement, in addition to the burnt offering of the new month with its sacrifices, and the perpetual burnt offering with its prescribed libations. With the same ceremonies you shall offer incense as a most sweet savor to the Lord. The tenth day of this seventh month shall also be holy and venerable for you, and you shall afflict your souls. You shall do no servile work on it. And you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord as a most sweet savor: one bull from the herd, one ram, seven unblemished yearling lambs; and in their sacrifices, fine flour mixed with oil — three tenths for each bull, two tenths for the ram, one tenth for each of the seven lambs; and a goat for sin — beyond what is customarily offered for transgression as atonement, and the perpetual burnt offering with its sacrifice and libations. On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, which shall be holy and venerable for you,

you shall do no servile work on it, but you shall celebrate a feast to the Lord for seven days. And you shall offer a burnt offering as a most sweet savor to the Lord: thirteen bulls from the herd, two rams, fourteen unblemished yearling lambs; and in their libations, fine flour mixed with oil — three tenths for each of the thirteen bulls, two tenths for each of the two rams, and one tenth for each of the fourteen lambs; and a male goat for sin — beyond the perpetual burnt offering, its sacrifice, and its libation. On the second day you shall offer twelve bulls from the herd, two rams, fourteen unblemished yearling lambs; and you shall celebrate their sacrifices and libations for each bull, ram, and lamb as is prescribed; and a male goat for sin, beyond the perpetual burnt offering with its sacrifice and libation. On the third day you shall offer eleven bulls, two rams, fourteen unblemished yearling lambs; and you shall celebrate their sacrifices and libations for each bull, ram, and lamb as is prescribed; and a male goat for sin, beyond the perpetual burnt offering with its sacrifice and libation.
