On the fourth day you shall offer ten bulls, two rams, fourteen unblemished yearling lambs; and you shall celebrate their sacrifices and libations for each bull, ram, and lamb as is prescribed; and a male goat for sin, beyond the perpetual burnt offering with its sacrifice and libation. On the fifth day you shall offer nine bulls, two rams, fourteen unblemished yearling lambs; and you shall celebrate their sacrifices and libations for each bull, ram, and lamb as is prescribed; and a male goat for sin, beyond the perpetual burnt offering with its sacrifice and

Numbers.

On the sixth day you shall offer eight bulls, two rams, fourteen yearling lambs without blemish, with their grain offerings and drink offerings as prescribed for the bulls, rams, and lambs; and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering. On the seventh day you shall offer seven bulls, two rams, fourteen yearling lambs without blemish, with the grain offerings and drink offerings prescribed for the bulls, rams, and lambs; and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering. On the eighth day, which is the most solemn assembly, you shall do no laborious work; you shall present a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord: one bull, one ram, seven yearling lambs without blemish, with their grain offerings and drink offerings as prescribed for the bull, ram, and lambs; and one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering. These you shall offer to the Lord at your appointed feasts, in addition to your vowed offerings and freewill offerings, whether for burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings, or peace offerings. Chapter 30.

Moses told the sons of Israel everything the Lord had commanded him, and he spoke to the leaders of the tribes of the sons of Israel. This is the word which the Lord has commanded: If a man makes a vow to the Lord, or swears an oath to bind himself by a pledge, he shall not break his word; he shall do according to all that proceeds out of his mouth. If a woman makes a vow to the Lord and binds herself by a pledge while she is in her father's house, in her youth, and her father hears her vow and the pledge by which she has bound herself, and her father says nothing to her, then all her vows shall stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself shall stand. Whatever she has vowed and sworn, she shall fulfill. But if her father opposes her on the day that he hears of it, none of her vows or her pledges by which she has bound herself shall stand; and the Lord will forgive her, because her father opposed her. If she is married and has made vows or uttered anything by which she bound herself, and the word has gone out of her lips binding her soul by an oath, and her husband hears of it and says nothing on the day he hears of it, then her vows shall stand and her pledges by which she bound herself shall stand. But if on the day her husband hears of it he opposes her and makes void the vow which she had made and the utterance by which she bound herself, the Lord will forgive her. If she vows and binds herself by an oath to afflict herself with fasting, or to abstain from other things, it shall be at her husband's discretion whether she shall or shall not fulfill it. But if her husband says nothing from day to day, then he confirms all her vows and all her pledges which are upon her; he has confirmed them, because he said nothing to her on the day he heard of them. But if he nullifies them after he has heard them, then he shall bear her guilt. These are the statutes which the Lord commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, and between a father and his daughter, while she is still in her youth in her father's house. Chapter 31.

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying: First take vengeance for the sons of Israel on the Midianites; afterward you shall be gathered to your people. Moses immediately said: Arm yourselves for battle so that you may carry out the Lord's vengeance on the Midianites. One thousand men from each tribe of Israel shall be chosen:

Numbers

Those who were apt for war. They gave a thousand from each tribe, that is twelve thousand armed for battle: Moses sent them with Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, with the sacred vessels and the trumpets to sound the charge. And when they had fought against the Midianites and conquered them, they killed all the males and their kings, namely Evi and Rekem and Zur and Hur and Reba, five princes of the people. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword. And they took captive the women and the children and all their cattle and all their flocks and all their goods. All the cities and villages and fortresses they burned with fire. And they took the spoil and everything they had captured, both of people and of animals, and brought them to Moses and Eleazar the priest and to all the assembly of the children of Israel. The remaining goods they brought to the camp on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan across from Jericho. Moses and Eleazar the priest and all the leaders of the congregation went out to meet them outside the camp. And Moses was angry with the officers of the army, with the captains over thousands and the captains over hundreds, who had come from the battle. Moses said to them: Why have you kept all the women alive? These are the ones who through Balaam's counsel caused the children of Israel to act treacherously against the Lord in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord. Now therefore, kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman who has known a man by sleeping with him. But all the young girls who have not known a man by sleeping with him, keep alive for yourselves. And remain outside the camp seven days. Whoever has killed any person, and whoever has touched any slain, purify yourselves on the third day and on the seventh day. And everything made of goatskins, hair, or wood shall be purified. Eleazar the priest also spoke to the men of war who had gone to battle: This is the ordinance of the law which the Lord commanded Moses. Only the gold and the silver, the bronze, the iron, the tin, and the lead, everything that may endure fire, you shall make go through fire, and it shall be clean; nevertheless it shall be purified with the water of purification; and all that cannot endure fire you shall make go through water. And you shall wash your garments on the seventh day, and you shall be clean; and afterward you shall come into the camp. The Lord also spoke to Moses saying: Count the total of the plunder that was taken, both of people and of animals, you and Eleazar the priest and the heads of the congregation; and divide the plunder into two parts, between those who took part in the war who went out to battle, and all the congregation. And levy a tribute for the Lord from the men of war who went out to battle: one out of every five hundred, of the people and of the cattle and of the donkeys and of the sheep. Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as an offering to the Lord. And from the children of Israel's half you shall take one out of every fifty, of the people, of the cattle, of the donkeys, and of the flocks, of all the livestock, and give them to the Levites who keep charge of the tabernacle of the Lord. And Moses and Eleazar did as the Lord commanded Moses. The plunder remaining from the spoil that the army took was: six hundred and seventy-five thousand sheep; seventy-two thousand cattle; sixty-one thousand donkeys; and thirty-two thousand persons in all, of women who had not known a man by sleeping with him. The half, the portion of those who had gone out to war, was in number three hundred and thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep; and the Lord's tribute of the sheep was six hundred and seventy-five. The cattle were thirty-six thousand, of which the Lord's tribute was seventy-two:

Numbers

of donkeys thirty thousand five hundred, one donkey per person. Of human persons sixteen thousand, thirty-two souls fell to the Lord's portion. Moses gave the tribute for the Lord to Eleazar the priest, as the Lord had commanded him, from the half belonging to the children of Israel, which he had set apart from those who had gone to war. But from the other half that fell to the rest of the multitude — that is, from the three hundred and seventy-seven thousand five hundred sheep, and from the thirty-six thousand cattle, and from the thirty thousand five hundred donkeys, and from the sixteen thousand persons — Moses took the fiftieth part and gave it to the Levites who kept watch over the tabernacle of the Lord, as the Lord had commanded. Then the commanders of the army, the tribunes and the centurions, came to Moses and said: We have counted the fighting men who were under our command, and not one of them is missing. Therefore we offer as a gift to the Lord what each of us found among the spoils: armlets and bracelets, rings, earrings, and necklaces, that you may pray for us to the Lord. Moses and Eleazar the priest received all the gold in its various forms, weighing sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifty shekels, from the tribunes and centurions. For each man had kept for himself whatever he had taken in the spoil. What was received was brought into the tabernacle of testimony as a memorial for the children of Israel before the Lord. [Chapter]

Now the children of Reuben and Gad had very large herds, and their livestock were without number. When they saw the lands of Jazer and Gilead, which were well suited for pasturing animals, they came to Moses and to Eleazar the priest and to the leaders of the congregation, and said: Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon,

Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon — the land which the Lord struck down before the congregation of Israel — is a land fit for livestock, and your servants have livestock. They begged: if we have found favor in your sight, let this land be given to your servants as a possession; do not make us cross the Jordan. Moses answered them: Shall your brothers go to war while you sit here? Why do you discourage the hearts of the children of Israel from going over into the land which the Lord has given them? Did not your fathers do the same, when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to explore the land? When they went up as far as the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land, they turned away the hearts of the children of Israel so that they would not enter the territory which the Lord had given them. And the Lord was angry and swore, saying: None of the men who came up out of Egypt, from twenty years old and upward, shall see the land which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they did not follow me fully — except Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, and Joshua the son of Nun, for they have followed the Lord fully. And the Lord was angry with Israel and made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until the whole generation that had done evil in his sight was consumed. And now you have risen up in your fathers' place, a brood of sinners, to further increase the Lord's fierce anger against Israel. For if you turn away from following him, he will again leave them in the wilderness, and you will destroy all this people. But they came forward and said: We will build sheepfolds here for our flocks and walled towns for our little ones, but we ourselves will march armed before the children of Israel until we have brought them to their place. Our little ones

· Numbers ·

ours and whatever we possess shall remain in the walled cities because of the dangers posed by the inhabitants. We will not return to our homes until the children of Israel have taken possession of their inheritance; and we seek nothing beyond the Jordan, because we already have our possession on the eastern side of it. Moses said to them: If you do what you promise and go armed before the Lord into battle, and every man of war crosses the Jordan until the Lord drives out his enemies, and all the land is subdued before him, then you will be free of guilt before God and before Israel; and you shall obtain the regions you desire before the Lord. But if you do not do what you say, there is no doubt that you will sin against the Lord; and know that your sin will find you out. Build cities for your little ones and folds and stables for your flocks and herds, and fulfill what you have promised. And the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben said to Moses: We are your servants. We will do what our lord commands. Our little ones and our wives and our flocks and herds we will leave in the cities of Gilead; but we your servants, all armed, will go forward to battle, as you, my lord, have spoken. Moses then commanded Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the families of Israel, and said to them: If the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben cross the Jordan with you, all armed for battle before the Lord, and the land is subdued before you, give them Gilead as a possession. But if they refuse to cross with you into the land of Canaan, let them receive a settlement among you.

And they crossed the Jordan. So Moses gave to the sons of Gad and of Reuben and to half the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and the land thereof with its cities throughout. The sons of Gad therefore built Dibon and Ataroth and Aroer and Roth and Sopham and Jazer and Jogbehah and Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran, fortified cities: and folds for their flocks. The sons of Reuben built Heshbon and Elealeh and Kiriathaim and Nebo and Baal-meon, their names being changed, and Sibmah: giving names to the cities they had built. Moreover the children of Machir son of Manasseh went into Gilead and took it, driving out the Amorite who was there. So Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he dwelt there. And Jair son of Manasseh went and took the villages thereof and called them Havvoth-jair, that is, the villages of Jair. Nobah also went and took Kenath with its villages and called it Nobah, after his own name. Chapter 33.

These are the stages of the children of Israel who went out of Egypt by their companies under the hand of Moses and Aaron, which Moses recorded according to the places of their encampments, which changed at the command of the Lord. They set out from Ramesses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the day after the Passover the children of Israel went out in triumph in the sight of all the Egyptians, while the Egyptians were burying their firstborn whom the Lord had struck down; for the Lord had also executed judgments upon their gods. They encamped at Succoth; from Succoth they came to Etham, which is on the edge of the wilderness. From there they went and came before Pi-hahiroth, which faces Baal-zephon, and they encamped before Migdol. Setting out from Pi-hahiroth they passed through

Numbers

the middle of the sea toward the wilderness; and they traveled three days through the desert of Etham and camped at Marah. They set out from Marah and came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there. Then they set out from there and camped by the Red Sea. They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the desert of Sinai; and from there they went out and came to Dophkah. They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush; and from Alush they pitched their tents at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink. They set out from Rephidim and camped in the desert of Sinai. And they left the desert of Sinai and came to the graves of craving; and from the graves of craving they camped at Hazeroth; and from Hazeroth they came to Rithmah. They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez; and from there they went out and came to Libnah. From Libnah they camped at Rissah; and from Rissah they came to Kehelathah. Then they set out and camped at Mount Shepher; they left Mount Shepher and came to Haradah. From there the travelers camped at Makheloth; and from Makheloth they came to Tahath. From Tahath they camped at Terah; and from there they pitched their tents at Mithkah, and from Mithkah they camped at Hashmonah; and from Hashmonah they came to Moseroth. And from Moseroth they camped at Bene-jaakan; and from Bene-jaakan they came to Mount Hor-haggidgad. Then they set out and camped at Jotbathah; and from Jotbathah they came to Abronah. And from Abronah they camped at Ezion-geber; and from there the travelers came to the desert of Zin — that is Kadesh. The people set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom. And Aaron the priest went up on Mount Hor at the command of the Lord, and he died there in the fortieth year after the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month, when he was one hundred and twenty-three years old. And the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard that the children of Israel had come. And they set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah; and from there they went out and came to Punon. They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth; and from Oboth they came to Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab. They set out from there and pitched their tents at Dibon-gad; and from there they went out and camped at Almon-diblathaim. From Almon-diblathaim they came to the mountains of Abarim, near Nebo; and from the mountains of Abarim they crossed to the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho. And they camped there from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim, in the plains of Moab; where the Lord spoke to Moses. Command the children of Israel and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan, drive out all the inhabitants of the land before you; destroy all their figured stones and all their cast idols, and demolish all their high places; and cleanse the land and settle in it, for I have given you the land to possess. You shall divide the land by lot according to your clans. To a larger group you shall give a larger inheritance, and to a smaller group you shall give a smaller inheritance. Wherever the lot falls for anyone, that shall be his. You shall inherit according to your tribes and clans. But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land before you, then those whom you allow to remain shall be as thorns in your eyes and barbs in your sides, and they shall trouble you in the land where you settle. And what I planned to do to them I will do to you. Chapter 34.

Numbers.

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Command the children of Israel and say to them: When you have entered the land of Canaan, and it has fallen to you by lot as your possession, you shall mark its boundaries as follows. The southern part shall begin from the wilderness of Zin, which is beside Edom, and its border on the east shall be the Salt Sea. From there it shall turn south of the Ascent of Scorpions, and pass on to Zin, and its southern limit shall be Kadesh-barnea, from which it shall go on to Hazar-addar and pass along to Azmon. From Azmon the border shall turn to the Wadi of Egypt, and its termination shall be at the Great Sea. For the western boundary, you shall have the Great Sea as your border; this shall be your western boundary. For your northern boundary, you shall mark out a line from the Great Sea to Mount Hor, and from Mount Hor to Lebo-hamath, and the limit of the border shall be at Zedad, and the border shall extend to Ziphron, its end being at Hazar-enan; this shall be your northern boundary. You shall draw your eastern boundary from Hazar-enan to Shepham, and the border shall go down from Shepham to Riblah on the east side of Ain; and the border shall go down and reach to the shoulder of the Sea of Chinnereth on the east; and the border shall go down to the Jordan, and its limit shall be the Salt Sea. This shall be your land as defined by its boundaries all around. Moses commanded the children of Israel, saying: This is the land you shall receive by lot, which the Lord commanded to be given to the nine and a half tribes. For the tribe of the sons of Reuben according to their families, and the tribe of the sons of Gad according to their families, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance; the two tribes and the half-tribe have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan at Jericho toward the sunrise.

And the Lord said to Moses: These are the names of the men who shall divide the land for you. Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun, and one leader from every tribe. These are the names of the men: Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh. Of the tribe of Simeon, Samuel the son of Ammihud. Of the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad the son of Chislon. Of the tribe of the children of Dan, Bukki the son of Jogli. Of the children of Joseph: of the tribe of Manasseh, Hanniel the son of Ephod. Of the tribe of Ephraim, Kemuel the son of Shiphtan. Of the tribe of Zebulun, Elizaphan the son of Parnach. Of the tribe of Issachar, the leader Paltiel the son of Azzan. Of the tribe of Asher, Ahihud the son of Shelomi. Of the tribe of Naphtali, Pedahel the son of Ammihud. These are the ones whom the Lord commanded to divide the inheritance for the children of Israel in the land of Canaan. Chapter 35.

And the Lord spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying: Command the children of Israel that they give to the Levites, from their inheritance, cities to dwell in, and open land around the cities shall also be given to the Levites. The cities shall be theirs to dwell in, and their open lands shall be for their cattle and their livestock and all their animals. The open land of the cities that you shall give to the Levites shall extend from the wall of the city outward a thousand cubits all around. And you shall measure outside the city for the east side two thousand cubits, and for the south side two thousand cubits, and for the west side two thousand cubits, and for the north side two thousand cubits, with the city in the middle. This shall belong to them as the open land for their cities. The cities shall be in the middle and the open land on the outside. Among the cities that you give to the Levites, there shall be six cities of refuge, where you shall permit the manslayer to flee; and in addition to these you shall give forty-two cities. All the cities that you give to the Levites shall be forty-eight cities with their open lands. And as for the cities that you shall give from the inheritance of the children of Israel, from those who have more

Numbers.

The more tribes, the more cities; the fewer, the fewer. Each tribe, in proportion to its inheritance, shall give cities to the Levites. The Lord said to Moses: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When you have crossed the Jordan into the land of Canaan, determine which cities shall serve as places of refuge for those who have shed blood unintentionally; so that the kinsman of the slain may not kill the one who fled there, until the case has been judged before the assembly. Of these cities of refuge, three shall be on the far side of the Jordan, and three in the land of Canaan, both for the children of Israel and for strangers and sojourners, so that anyone who has shed blood unintentionally may flee to them. If anyone strikes another with iron and he dies, the striker is a murderer and shall be put to death. If he throws a stone that kills, he shall be punished likewise. If he strikes with a wooden object and the man dies, he shall be avenged by the blood of the striker. The nearest kinsman of the slain shall kill the murderer; as soon as he finds him he shall strike him down. But if someone pushed another without hatred, or threw something at him without lying in wait, or struck him without enmity, and the man died, then the assembly shall judge between the striker and the avenger of blood. The innocent man shall be freed from the avenger's hand and returned by judgment to the city of refuge where he had fled. He shall remain there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with holy oil. If the killer is found outside the boundaries of the city of refuge and is struck down by the avenger of blood, the killer's death shall not be avenged.

For the fugitive was obliged to remain in the city until the death of the high priest. After the high priest's death, the killer may return to his own land. These shall be perpetual statutes and laws for all your generations. No murderer shall be put to death on the testimony of only one witness. You shall not accept a ransom for one who is guilty of murder; he shall surely be put to death. Exiles and fugitives may in no way return to their cities before the death of the high priest, lest you defile the land of your dwelling, which is stained by the blood of the innocent; nor can it be expiated except by the blood of the one who shed it. Thus shall your land be cleansed of defilement. For I am the Lord who dwells among the children of Israel. Chapter 36.

Then the leaders of the families of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, of the clans of the sons of Joseph, came forward and spoke before Moses and before the leaders of Israel, saying: The Lord has commanded our lord to divide the land by lot among the children of Israel, and to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters. But if they marry men from another tribe of Israel, their inheritance will be taken from our ancestral inheritance and added to that of the tribe into which they marry, and so when the jubilee—that is, the fiftieth year of release—comes, their possession will be joined to the inheritance of that tribe, and taken away from the lot of our inheritance. Moses answered the children of Israel, as the Lord commanded him, saying: The tribe of the sons of Joseph has spoken rightly. This is the law that the Lord has ordained concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: Let them marry whom they think best, but only within the family of their father's tribe, so that the inheritance of the children of Israel shall not pass from tribe to tribe. For all men shall take wives from their own tribe.

· Deuteronomy ·

and of her kindred, and all the women of the same tribe shall take husbands, so that the inheritance may remain in the families and not be mixed among tribes, but remain as the Lord has separated them. The daughters of Zelophehad did as had been commanded to them, and Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah were married to the sons of their uncle from the family of Manasseh, who was the son of Joseph, and the possession that had been given to them remained in the tribe and family of their father. These are the commandments and judgments which the Lord commanded through the hand of Moses to the children of Israel in the plains of Moab above the Jordan near Jericho.
Here ends the Book of Numbers. Here begins the book called Deuteronomy.

These are the words which Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan in the wilderness of the plain, opposite the Red Sea, between Paran and Tophel and Laban and Hazeroth, where there is much gold — eleven days journey from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir to Kadesh Barnea. In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Moses spoke to the children of Israel all that the Lord had commanded him to tell them, after he had defeated Sihon the king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan who lived in Ashtaroth and in Edrei, beyond the Jordan in the land of Moab. And Moses undertook to expound the law and say: The Lord our God spoke to us in Horeb, saying: You have stayed long enough on this mountain. Turn and set out, and go to the mountain of the Amorites and to all the neighboring regions, the plains, the mountains, and the lowlands toward the south and along the seacoast, the land of the Canaanites and Lebanon as far as the great river

Euphrates. Behold, he said, I have given it to you. Go in and possess the land which the Lord swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give to them and to their descendants after them. And I said to you at that time: I am not able to bear you alone, because the Lord our God has multiplied you, and today you are as numerous as the stars of heaven. May the Lord God of your fathers add to your number many thousands more and bless you as he has promised. I am not able alone to bear your disputes and your burdens and your contentions. Give me wise and discerning men, whose conduct is proven among your tribes, that I may appoint them as your leaders. Then you answered me: The thing that you have proposed to do is good. So I took the leaders of your tribes, wise and respected men, and appointed them as heads over you, commanders of thousands, and commanders of hundreds, and commanders of fifties, and commanders of tens, who would teach you in all things. And I charged them, saying: Hear them out, and judge what is just. Whether he be a fellow citizen or a stranger, let there be no distinction of persons. For judgment belongs to God. And if anything seems too hard for you, bring it to me and I will hear it. And I commanded you all the things you were to do. Then departing from Horeb, we passed through that terrible and vast wilderness that you saw, by the way of the mountain of the Amorites, as the Lord our God had commanded us. And when we came to Kadesh Barnea, I said to you: You have come to the mountain of the Amorites, which the Lord our God will give to you. See the land which the Lord our God gives to you. Go up and possess it, as the Lord God of your fathers has told you. Do not fear, and do not be dismayed. And you all came near to me and said: Let us send

Deuteronomy

men who would survey the land, and report by which road we should go up, and to which cities. The matter pleased me well, and I sent twelve men from among you, one from each tribe. They went up and entered the hill country, and came as far as the Valley of Eshcol; and having surveyed the land, they took some of its fruit to show its abundance and brought it back to us, saying: "The land which the Lord our God will give us is good." But you would not go up; instead you were rebellious against the command of the Lord your God, and murmured in your tents, saying: "The Lord hates us, and therefore has brought us out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hands of the Amorites and to destroy us. Where are we going? Our brothers have discouraged us, saying: The people are greater and taller than we; the cities are great and walled up to heaven; we have also seen the sons of the Anakim there." Then I said to you: "Do not be terrified or afraid of them. The Lord your God who goes before you, he will fight for you, just as he did for you in Egypt before your eyes, and in the wilderness, as you have seen. The Lord your God carried you, as a man carries his son, throughout all the road that you traveled, until you came to this place." Yet for all this, you did not trust the Lord your God, who went before you on the way to seek out a place for you to camp, showing you by fire in the night and by a cloud in the day the road you should go. When the Lord heard the sound of your words, he was angry and swore: "Not one of these men of this evil generation shall see the good land that I swore to give to your fathers, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh; he shall see it, and to him I will give the land that he has trodden, and to his children."

Because he followed the Lord fully. And the Lord's anger was also kindled against me on your account, saying: "You also shall not enter there; but Joshua the son of Nun, your attendant, he shall enter. Encourage him, for he shall cause Israel to inherit it." Moreover your little ones, who you said would become prey, and your children, who today have no knowledge of good and evil, they shall go in; and to them I will give it, and they shall possess it. But as for you, turn around and set out toward the wilderness in the direction of the Red Sea. Then you answered me: "We have sinned against the Lord. We will go up and fight, just as the Lord our God commanded us." And every one of you equipped himself with weapons and thought it easy to go up into the hill country. The Lord said to me: "Say to them, 'Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not among you; lest you be defeated before your enemies.'" I spoke to you, but you would not listen; you rebelled against the command of the Lord and presumptuously went up into the hill country. Then the Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you and chased you as bees do, and drove you back from Seir to Hormah. And you returned and wept before the Lord, but the Lord did not listen to your voice or give ear to you. So you remained at Kadesh-barnea many days.

Then we turned and journeyed into the wilderness in the direction of the Red Sea, as the Lord told me. And we circled Mount Seir for many days. And the Lord said to me: "You have been circling this mountain long enough. Turn northward, and command the people: You are about to pass through the territory of your brothers, the people of Esau, who live in Seir; and they will be afraid of you. So be very careful: do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of their land, not even enough for the sole of a foot to tread on."

Deuteronomy

because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession. You shall buy food from them with money and eat it; you shall also purchase water from them with money and drink it. The Lord your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has known your journey through this great wilderness. These forty years the Lord your God has been with you, and you have lacked nothing. So when we passed beyond our brothers, the children of Esau who dwell in Seir, through the road of the plain from Elath and from Ezion-geber, we came toward the way of the wilderness of Moab. And the Lord said to me: Do not fight against Moab, nor engage them in battle. For I will not give you any of their land as a possession, because I have given Ar to the children of Lot as a possession. The Emim formerly lived there, a people great and many, and tall as the Anakim; they were also considered to be giants like the Anakim, and the Moabites called them Emim. And in Seir the Horites formerly dwelt, but the children of Esau dispossessed them and destroyed them and settled in their place, just as Israel did to the land of their possession which the Lord gave them. Now rise and cross the brook Zered. So we crossed the brook Zered. The time it took us to come from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the brook Zered was thirty-eight years, until all the generation of fighting men had perished from the camp, as the Lord had sworn to them. For the hand of the Lord was against them, to destroy them from the camp. So when all the fighting men had perished and were dead, the Lord said to me: Today you are to cross the boundary of Moab at Ar, and when you approach the territory of the children of Ammon, do not harass them or contend with them, for I will not give you any of the land of the children of Ammon as a possession, because I have given it to the children of Lot as a possession.

It was also considered the land of giants; giants formerly lived there, whom the Ammonites called Zamzummim, a people great and many, and tall as the Anakim; but the Lord destroyed them before them, and they dispossessed them and settled in their place, just as He had done for the children of Esau who dwell in Seir, when He destroyed the Horites before them. And the Avvim who lived in villages as far as Gaza, the Caphtorim who came from Caphtor destroyed them and settled in their place. Rise up, cross the valley of Arnon. See, I have given into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land; begin to take possession and contend with him in battle. This day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you upon the peoples who are under the whole heaven, who shall hear the report of you and shall tremble and be in anguish because of you. So I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying: Let me pass through your land; I will go by the public road; I will not turn aside to the right or to the left. You shall sell me food for money, that I may eat, and give me water for money, that I may drink. Only let me pass through on foot, just as the children of Esau who dwell in Seir and the Moabites who dwell in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land the Lord our God is giving us. But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass by, for the Lord your God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, that he might give him into your hand, as he is today. And the Lord said to me: See, I have begun to give

Deuteronomy

hand over Sihon and his land: begin to possess it. And Sihon came out against us with all his people to fight at Jahaz: and the Lord our God delivered him to us: and we struck him and his sons and all his people: and we took all his cities at that time, killing the inhabitants, men and women and children. We left nothing except the livestock, which fell to us as plunder, and the spoils of the cities which we took. From Aroer, which is on the bank of the river Arnon, the town which is in the valley, even to Gilead: there was not a village or city that escaped our hand. The Lord our God delivered all to us: except the land of the children of Ammon, which we did not approach: and all things along the river Jabbok, and the cities of the mountains, and all the places from which the Lord our God forbade us. Chapter III. Then we turned and went up the road to Bashan. And Og the king of Bashan came out against us with all his people to fight at Edrei: and the Lord said to me: Fear him not: for he is delivered into your hand with all his people and his land: and you shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon. So the Lord our God delivered into our hands Og also the king of Bashan, and all his people: and we struck them until none was left: laying waste all his cities at one time. There was no town that escaped us. Sixty cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan. All those cities were fortified with very high walls, gates and bars, besides innumerable villages that had no walls. And we destroyed them as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, destroying every city, men and women and children: but the cattle and the spoils of the cities we took for ourselves. And we took at that time the land from the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the river Arnon to mount Hermon, which the Sidonians call Sirion, and the Amorites call Senir: all the cities of the plain, and all Gilead and Bashan to Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan. For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants. His iron bedstead is shown at Rabbath of the children of Ammon: it is nine cubits in length and four cubits in breadth, measured by the cubit of a man's hand. And we possessed the land at that time from Aroer, which is on the bank of the river Arnon, to half mount Gilead: and I gave its cities to Reuben and Gad: and the rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half tribe of Manasseh, all the region of Argob. All Bashan is called the land of giants. Jair the son of Manasseh possessed all the region of Argob to the borders of Geshuri and Maacathi. And he called Bashan after his own name, Havoth-jair, that is, the villages of Jair, unto this day. And I gave Gilead to Machir: and to the tribes of Reuben and Gad I gave the land of Gilead to the river Arnon, half the river and its boundary, to the river Jabbok which is the border of the children of Ammon: and the plain of the wilderness and the Jordan from Kinnereth to the sea of the desert, which is the saltiest sea, at the foot of mount Pisgah to the east. And I commanded you at that time saying: The Lord your God gives you this land as an inheritance: all you able-bodied men shall cross over armed before your brothers the children of Israel, leaving behind your wives and children and livestock. You know that there is much more...

Deuteronomy

after you, and that you may remain for a long time upon the land which the Lord your God will give you. Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan toward the east, so that anyone who kills a neighbor unintentionally, without having been an enemy before, may flee to one of these cities and escape: Bezer in the wilderness, in the flatlands from the tribe of Reuben; and Ramoth in Gilead, which is from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, which is from the tribe of Manasseh. This is the law that Moses set before the children of Israel: these testimonies, ceremonies, and judgments which he spoke to the children of Israel when they came out of Egypt, across the Jordan, in the valley near the plain of Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites who dwelt in Heshbon, whom Moses defeated. The children of Israel also coming out of Egypt possessed his land, and the land of Og king of Bashan, two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan toward the east, from Aroer which is upon the bank of the river Arnon, as far as Mount Senir which is Hermon, all the plain beyond the Jordan toward the east, as far as the sea of the wilderness, and to the foot of Mount Pisgah.

And Moses called all Israel together and said to them: Hear, O Israel, the statutes and judgments which I speak in your ears today. Learn them and fulfill them in deed. The Lord our God made a covenant with us in Horeb. He did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with us, who are all here alive today. Face to face the Lord spoke with us on the mountain out of the midst of fire. I stood between the Lord and you at that time, to declare to you the word of the Lord, for you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain. And he said: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery. You shall have no other gods before me. You shall not make for yourself a carved image or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth. You shall not bow down to them or serve them. For I the Lord your God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me, and showing mercy to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments. You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain, for the Lord will not hold him guiltless who takes his name in vain. Observe the day of the Sabbath, to keep it holy, as the Lord your God commanded you. Six days you shall labor and do all your work. But the seventh day is the Sabbath of the Lord your God: that is the rest of the Lord your God. In it you shall not do any work, you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your ox, nor your donkey, nor any of your livestock, nor the stranger who is within your gates, so that your male servant and female servant may rest as well as you. Remember that you yourself were a servant in Egypt, and that the Lord your God brought you out from there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore the Lord your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day. Honor your father and your mother, as the Lord your God commanded you, so that you may live long, and that it may go well with you in the land which the Lord your God is giving you. You shall not murder, nor commit adultery, nor steal, nor bear false witness against your neighbor. You shall not covet your neighbor's wife, nor his house, nor his field, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor's. These words he spoke

· Deuteronomy ·

And the Lord spoke to you out of the midst of the fire, and of the cloud, and of the darkness, with a great voice, adding nothing more; and he wrote these things on two tablets of stone, which he delivered to me. But you, after you heard the voice out of the midst of the darkness, and saw the mountain burning, came to me, all the princes of the tribes and the elders, and you said: Behold the Lord our God has shown us his majesty and his greatness, and we have heard his voice out of the midst of the fire. This day we have seen that God speaks with man, and man has lived. Why should we die therefore, and why should this exceeding great fire consume us? For if we hear the voice of the Lord our God any more, we shall die. What is all flesh, that it should hear the voice of the living God, who speaks out of the midst of the fire as we have heard, and be able to live? You go nearer and hear all things that the Lord our God shall say to you, and you shall speak to us, and we will hear and do them. And the Lord hearing this said to me: I have heard the voice of the words of this people, which they have spoken to you. They have spoken all things well. Who shall give them to have such a mind, to fear me, and to keep all my commandments at all times, that it may be well with them for ever and with their children? Go and say to them: Return to your tents. But stand here with me, and I will speak to you all my commandments and ceremonies and judgments, which you shall teach them, that they may do them in the land which I shall give them. Keep therefore and do the things which the Lord God has commanded you. You shall not go aside neither to the right hand nor to the left, but you shall walk in the way that the Lord your God has commanded, that you may live and it may be well with you, and your days may be long in the land of your possession. Chapter VI.

These are the precepts and ceremonies and judgments which the Lord your God commanded that I should teach you, that you may do them in the land into which you are crossing to possess it: that you may fear the Lord your God and keep all his commandments and precepts which I command you, and your sons, and your grandsons, all the days of your life, that your days may be prolonged. Hear, O Israel, and observe to do the things which the Lord has commanded you, that it may be well with you, and you may be greatly multiplied, as the Lord the God of your fathers has promised you, a land flowing with milk and honey. Hear, O Israel. The Lord your God is one God. You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, and with your whole soul, and with your whole strength. And these words which I command you this day shall be in your heart, and you shall tell them to your children, and you shall meditate upon them sitting in your house, and walking on your journey, sleeping and rising. And you shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be and shall move between your eyes, and you shall write them on the posts and on the doors of your house. When the Lord your God shall have brought you into the land which he swore to your fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and shall have given you great and goodly cities which you did not build, houses full of riches which you did not set up, cisterns which you did not dig, vineyards and olive yards which you did not plant, and you shall have eaten and be full, take heed diligently lest you forget the Lord who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. You shall fear the Lord your God, and shall serve him only, and you shall swear by his name. You shall not go after the strange gods of all the nations that are round about you, for the Lord your God is a jealous God in the midst of you, lest at any time the wrath of the Lord your God be kindled against you, and take you away from the face of the earth.

Deuteronomy

You shall not put the Lord your God to the test, as you tested him at the place of testing. Keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and his testimonies and ceremonies which he has commanded you. Do what is pleasing and good in the sight of the Lord, that it may go well with you, and that you may enter and possess the excellent land which the Lord swore to your fathers, to drive out all your enemies before you, as he has spoken. When your son asks you tomorrow, saying, "What do these testimonies mean, and the ceremonies and judgments which the Lord our God has commanded us?" you shall say to him: "We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt, and the Lord brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand. He performed great and terrible signs and wonders in Egypt against Pharaoh and all his household, before our eyes. And he brought us out from there, that he might bring us in and give us the land which he swore to our fathers." The Lord commanded us to observe all these statutes, and to fear the Lord our God, that it may go well with us all the days of our life, as it is today. And it will be to our credit if we keep and observe all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he has commanded us. Chapter 7.

When the Lord your God brings you into the land which you are about to enter and possess, and he drives out many nations before you — the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, seven nations more numerous and stronger than you — and when the Lord your God hands them over to you and you defeat them, you shall utterly destroy them. Make no covenant with them and show them no mercy. Do not intermarry with them. Do not give your daughters to their sons, nor take their daughters for your sons, for they would turn your sons away from following me to serve other gods. Then the anger of the Lord would be kindled against you, and he would destroy you quickly. But this is what you shall do with them: tear down their altars, break their sacred pillars, cut down their sacred groves, and burn their graven images in fire; for you are a holy people to the Lord your God. The Lord your God has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, out of all the peoples on the face of the earth. It was not because you were more in number than any other people that the Lord set his love on you and chose you, for you were the fewest of all peoples; but because the Lord loves you, and is keeping the oath which he swore to your fathers. The Lord has brought you out with a mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt. Know therefore that the Lord your God is God, the faithful God who keeps covenant and mercy with those who love him and keep his commandments, to a thousand generations, and who repays those who hate him to their face, by destroying them. He will not delay with those who hate him; he will repay them to their face. Therefore keep the commandments and ceremonies and judgments which I command you today to observe. And if, when you hear these judgments, you keep and observe them, the Lord your God will keep with you the covenant and the mercy which he swore to your fathers. He will love you, bless you, and multiply you. He will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, your grain and your wine and your oil, the increase of your cattle and the young of your flock, in the land which he swore to your fathers to give you. You shall be blessed above all peoples. There shall not be male or female barren among you or among your livestock. And the Lord will take away from you all sickness, and none of the evil diseases of Egypt which you knew will he inflict upon you, but he will lay them upon all who hate you. You shall consume all the peoples that the Lord your God will give over to you. Your eye shall not pity

· Deuteronomy ·

and springs and pools of water: who brought forth streams from the hardest rock and fed you with manna in the wilderness, which your fathers did not know. And after he afflicted and tested you, he had mercy on you at last: lest you should say in your heart, my strength and the power of my hand achieved all this for me. But remember the Lord your God, for he it was who gave you strength to fulfill the covenant which he swore to your fathers, as is evident this day. But if you forget the Lord your God and follow other gods, and worship and adore them, I declare to you this day that you shall utterly perish. As the nations which the Lord destroyed at your coming in, so shall you also perish if you are disobedient to the voice of the Lord your God. ch. v.

Hear, O Israel. You are to cross the Jordan today to dispossess nations greater and mightier than yourself, cities great and fortified up to the heavens, a people great and tall, the sons of the Anakim, whom you yourself have seen and heard: before whom no one is able to stand. Know therefore today that the Lord your God is he who goes before you as a consuming and devouring fire: who shall destroy them and bring them down and scatter them before your face quickly, as he has promised you. Do not say in your heart when the Lord your God has cast them out before you, it is because of my righteousness that the Lord has brought me in to possess this land: for it is because of the wickedness of these nations that he is driving them out before you. It is not for your righteousness nor for the uprightness of your heart that you are going in to possess their land: but because they committed wickedness as you entered, they are to be destroyed: and that the Lord might fulfill the word which he swore with an oath to your fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Know therefore that the Lord your God is not giving you this good land to possess because of your righteousness: for you are a stiff-necked people. Remember and do not forget how you provoked the Lord your God to anger in the wilderness, and from the day you came out of Egypt until you came to this place you have always been contentious against the Lord. Even at Horeb you provoked him: and he was so angry that he was willing to destroy you when I went up the mountain to receive the two stone tablets of the covenant which the Lord had made with you. And I remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights: eating no bread and drinking no water. And the Lord gave me the two stone tablets written by the finger of God: containing all the words which he spoke to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire when the assembly of the people was gathered together. And when the forty days and forty nights were passed, the Lord gave me the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant: and he said to me, Arise, go down from here quickly: for your people whom you brought out of Egypt have quickly turned aside from the way which I showed them: they have made for themselves a cast idol. Furthermore the Lord said to me: I see that this people is stiff-necked. Let me alone that I may destroy them: and blot out their name from under heaven: and I will make of you a nation greater and mightier than they. And when I came down from the burning mountain holding the two tablets of the covenant in both my hands, and I saw that you had sinned against the Lord your God and had made for yourselves a molten calf and had quickly turned aside from the way which the Lord had showed you: I threw the tablets from my hands and broke them before your eyes. And I fell down before the Lord as before, forty days and forty nights, eating no bread and drinking no water, on account of all the sins which you committed against

Deuteronomy

...the Lord, and you provoked him to anger. For I feared his indignation and wrath, with which he was stirred up against you and wanted to destroy you. But the Lord heard me also this time. He was also very angry with Aaron and wanted to destroy him, and I prayed for him likewise. I took the calf, which was your sin, and burned it with fire, and beat it into small pieces, grinding it thoroughly to dust, and cast it into the torrent that came down from the mountain. Also at Massah and at Temptation, and at the Graves of Lust, you provoked the Lord. And when he sent you from Kadesh-Barnea, saying: Go up and possess the land that I have given you, you despised the command of the Lord your God and did not believe him, nor would you listen to his voice; but you were always rebellious from the day that I knew you. And I lay prostrate before the Lord forty days and nights, humbly beseeching him that he would not destroy you, as he threatened: and I prayed and said: Lord God, do not destroy your people and your inheritance, whom you have redeemed in your greatness, whom you brought out of Egypt with a strong hand. Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not look upon the stubbornness of this people, nor upon their wickedness and sin, lest the inhabitants of the land from which you brought us out say: The Lord could not bring them into the land which he promised them, and he hated them, therefore he brought them out to slay them in the wilderness. They are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out with your great strength and with your outstretched arm.

At that time the Lord said to me: Hew for yourself two tablets of stone like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain; and make an ark of wood, and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first ones which you broke, and you shall put them in the ark. So I made an ark of acacia wood. And when I had hewn two tablets of stone like the first, I went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hands. And he wrote on the tablets as before, the ten words which the Lord had spoken to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire, when the congregation was assembled; and the Lord gave them to me. Then I turned and came down from the mountain, and put the tablets in the ark that I had made; and there they are, as the Lord commanded me. The children of Israel journeyed from Beeroth-bene-jaakan to Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son served as priest in his place. From there they journeyed to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land with streams of water. At that time the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to stand before the Lord to minister to him, and to bless in his name to this day. Therefore Levi has no portion or inheritance with his brothers; the Lord himself is his inheritance, as the Lord your God promised him. I myself stayed on the mountain forty days and nights as before; and the Lord heard me that time also, and the Lord was unwilling to destroy you. And the Lord said to me: Arise, go on your journey before the people, that they may go in and possess the land which I swore to their fathers to give them. And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul, and to keep the commandments and statutes of the Lord which I am commanding you today for your good. Behold, to the Lord your God belong the heavens and the highest heavens, the earth and all that is in it. Yet the Lord set his heart on your fathers...

Deuteronomy

The Lord was joined to them and loved them, and after them he chose their descendants, that is you, from all the nations, as is proven today. Therefore circumcise the foreskin of your hearts and stiffen your necks no longer: for the Lord your God, he is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and terrible God, who does not accept persons nor take bribes. He executes judgment for the orphan and the widow, he loves the stranger, and gives him food and clothing. Therefore love the stranger, for you also were strangers in the land of Egypt. You shall fear the Lord your God and serve him alone. You shall hold fast to him and swear by his name. He is your praise and he is your God, who has done for you these great and terrible things which your eyes have seen. Your fathers went down into Egypt with seventy souls, and behold, the Lord your God has made you as numerous as the stars of heaven. Chapter XI.
Therefore love the Lord your God and observe his precepts and ceremonies, his judgments and commandments at all times. Know today what your children do not know, who did not see the discipline of the Lord your God, his greatness and his mighty hand and his outstretched arm: the signs and works he did in the midst of Egypt, against Pharaoh the king and all his land, and against all the army of the Egyptians and their horses and chariots: how the waters of the Red Sea covered them when they were pursuing you, and the Lord destroyed them until this day: and what he did to you in the wilderness until you came to this place: and to Dathan and Abiron, sons of Eliab who was the son of Reuben, whom the earth swallowed up with their houses and tents and all their substance that they had in the midst of Israel. Your eyes have seen all the great works of the Lord that he did, so that you may keep all these commandments which I command you today, and be able to go in and possess the land to which you are going. That you may live long in the land which the Lord swore to your fathers and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey. For the land which you are going in to possess is not like the land of Egypt from which you came out, where after sowing seed you water it with your feet as a garden of herbs: but it is a land of hills and plains, expecting rain from heaven: a land which the Lord your God visits, and his eyes are on it from the beginning of the year to the end of it. If then you obey my commandments which I command you today, to love the Lord your God and serve him with all your heart and with all your soul: he will give rain to your land in due season, the early and the late rain, that you may gather in your grain and your wine and your oil: he will give grass in your fields for your cattle, and that you may eat and be filled. Beware lest your heart be deceived and you turn away and serve strange gods and worship them: and the Lord being angry shut up heaven, that rain come not down, nor the earth yield her fruit, and you perish quickly from the good land which the Lord will give you. Lay up these my words in your hearts and minds, and hang them as a sign on your hands, and place them between your eyes. Teach them to your children, that they may meditate on them. When you sit in your house and walk along the road, and when you lie down and when you rise, you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates: that your days and the days of your children may be multiplied in the land which the Lord swore to your fathers that he would give them, as long as heaven is above the earth. For if you keep the commandments which I command you and do them, to love the Lord your God and walk in all his ways

· Deuteronomy ·

them to him, the Lord Almighty will scatter all these nations before your face, and you shall possess them, for they are greater and stronger than you. Every place your foot treads shall be yours. From the desert and Lebanon, and from the great river Euphrates to the western sea, shall be your borders. No one shall stand against you. The Lord your God shall put the terror and dread of you upon all the land you shall tread, as he has spoken to you. Behold, I set before you today a blessing and a curse: a blessing, if you obey the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you today; and a curse, if you do not obey the commandments of the Lord your God, but turn aside from the way which I show you today, to go after other gods which you have not known. When the Lord your God brings you into the land which you are going to possess, you shall place the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal, which are beyond the Jordan, along the road going toward the sunset, in the land of the Canaanites who dwell in the plain opposite Gilgal, beside the terebinth grove near the valley of Moreh. For you are to cross the Jordan to go in and possess the land which the Lord your God is giving you; you shall possess it and dwell in it. And you shall be careful to observe all the statutes and judgments which I set before you today. Chapter 12.

These are the statutes and judgments which you shall be careful to observe in the land which the Lord God of your fathers is giving you to possess, all the days that you live on the earth. You shall utterly destroy all the places where the nations you are dispossessing served their gods, on the high mountains and on the hills and under every green tree. You shall tear down their altars, and burn their sacred pillars with fire; and you shall cut down their wooden images. You shall destroy the names of those places. You shall not do so to the Lord your God. But you shall seek the place which the Lord your God shall choose from all your tribes to put his name, and there you shall come and bring your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the firstfruits of your hands, and your vows and freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your herds and your flocks. And you shall eat there before the Lord your God, and you shall rejoice in all to which you have put your hand, you and your households, in which the Lord your God has blessed you. You shall not do there as we are doing here today, every man doing whatever seems right to him. For you have not yet come to the rest and the inheritance which the Lord your God is giving you. You shall cross the Jordan, and dwell in the land which the Lord your God is giving you to inherit, and he will give you rest from all your enemies around, and you shall dwell safely. Then there shall be the place which the Lord your God chooses, to make his name dwell there. There you shall bring all that I command you: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the firstfruits of your hands, and all your choice offerings which you vow to the Lord. And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God, you and your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levite who is within your cities, since he has no portion or inheritance among you. Take heed that you do not offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see; but in the place which the Lord shall choose in one of your tribes, there you shall offer your burnt offerings, and there you shall do all that I command you. However, if you desire to eat meat, and you say, "I will eat meat," you may eat as much meat as your heart desires. According to the blessing of the Lord your God which he has given you, in your cities, whether it is unclean

. Deuteronomy .

those who are near or far from the beginning to the end of the land: do not consent to them, nor listen to them, nor shall your eye pity them, to spare them or conceal them, but you shall immediately put them to death. Your hand shall be first upon them, and afterwards the hand of all the people. You shall stone them to death, because they sought to draw you away from the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage: so that all Israel, hearing it, may fear and do no more any such wicked thing. If you hear, in one of the cities which the Lord your God gives you to dwell in, that certain men, children of Belial, have gone out from among you and have turned away the inhabitants of their city, saying: Let us go and serve strange gods which you do not know: inquire carefully and diligently into the truth of the matter; and if you find it to be true and that this abomination has been committed, you shall immediately strike the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, and destroy it and all things that are in it, even the cattle. And all the household goods that are in it you shall gather together in the midst of its streets, and shall burn them with the city itself, so that you consume everything for the Lord your God: and it shall be a heap forever. It shall not be built again: and nothing of that which has been cursed shall cling to your hand: so that the Lord may turn from the wrath of his fury and show you mercy: and multiply you as he swore to your fathers, when you hear the voice of the Lord your God, keeping all his commandments which I command you this day, to do what is pleasing in the sight of the Lord your God. CHAPTER XIV.

You are children of the Lord your God. You shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness between your eyes for the dead: because you are a holy people to the Lord your God, and he chose you to be his own special people from all the nations that are upon the earth. Eat not the things that are unclean. These are the animals you may eat: the ox and the sheep and the goat, the deer and the roe deer, the buffalo and the tragelaphus, the pygarg and the oryx and the camelopard. Every animal that divides the hoof into two parts and chews the cud, you shall eat: but of those that chew the cud but do not divide the hoof, you shall not eat: such as the camel, the hare, and the rabbit. Because they chew the cud but do not divide the hoof, they shall be unclean to you. The swine also, because it divides the hoof but does not chew the cud, shall be unclean. You shall not eat of their flesh, nor touch their carcasses. These you shall eat of all that abide in the waters: eat those that have fins and scales: but those that have no fins and scales, do not eat, because they are unclean. All clean birds you may eat. The unclean you shall not eat: namely, the eagle, and the griffin, and the osprey, and the vulture and the kite according to their kind, and all of the crow kind, and the ostrich and the owl and the larus and the hawk according to their kind, the heron and the charadrius and the ibis and the merganser and the porphyrion and the night raven and the pelican and the plover, each according to their kind, also the hoopoe and the bat: every creeping thing that has wings shall be unclean and shall not be eaten. Everything that is clean, eat. But whatever has died of itself, do not eat of it. Give it to the stranger who is within your gates to eat, or sell it to him: for you are a holy people to the Lord your God. You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk. You shall set apart a tithe of all the fruits of your land that come forth each year: and you shall eat before the Lord your God in the place which he shall choose, that his name may be invoked there: the tithe of your grain

Deuteronomy.

of wine and oil, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks, so that you may learn to fear the Lord your God at all times. But when the journey is too long for you, and the place which the Lord your God has chosen is too far away, and the Lord your God has blessed you there, and you cannot carry all these things there: you shall sell everything and convert it into money, and you shall take the money in your hand and go to the place which the Lord your God has chosen, and you shall spend the money for whatever you desire, whether from the herds or from the flocks. And also wine and strong drink and whatever your soul desires, and you shall eat there before the Lord your God, and you and your household shall rejoice, and the Levite who is within your gates. Take care that you do not abandon him, because he has no portion in your inheritance. In the third year you shall set apart another tithe of all things that grow for you at that time, and you shall lay it up within your gates, and the Levite who has no other portion or inheritance among you shall come, and the stranger and the orphan and the widow who are within your gates, and they shall eat and be satisfied, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.

In the seventh year you shall make a remission, which shall be observed in this manner. Anyone to whom a neighbor, friend, or brother owes something shall not be able to demand repayment, because it is the year of the Lord's remission. From a foreigner and stranger you may exact payment, but from your fellow citizen and kinsman you have no power to demand it back. And there shall be no needy or poor person among you, so that the Lord your God may bless you in the land which he will give you as a possession, if only you listen to the voice of the Lord your God and keep all these commandments which I give you today. He will bless you as he has promised. You will lend to many nations, and you yourself will borrow from none. You will rule over many nations.

And none shall rule over you. If one of your brothers who dwell within the gates of your city in the land which the Lord your God will give you falls into poverty, you shall not harden your heart nor close your hand, but you shall open it to the poor man and lend him what he needs. Take care lest there arise in you a wicked thought, and you say in your heart: the seventh year of remission is near, and you turn your eyes away from your poor brother, refusing to lend him what he asks, lest he cry out against you to the Lord and it become a sin for you. But you shall give to him. And you shall not act cunningly in relieving his needs, so that the Lord your God may bless you at all times and in everything you put your hand to. The poor will never cease from the land of your habitation; therefore I command you to open your hand to your brother who is needy and poor in your land. When your Hebrew brother or sister has been sold to you and has served you for six years, in the seventh year you shall set them free. And when you let them go free, you shall not send them away empty-handed, but you shall give them provisions from your flock, from your threshing floor, and from your winepress, with which the Lord your God has blessed you. Remember that you yourself were a servant in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God redeemed you; therefore I now command you this. But if he says: I do not wish to leave, because he loves you and your household, and is well off with you: then you shall take an awl and pierce his ear at the door of your house, and he shall serve you forever. You shall do the same for your female servant. You shall not be troubled when you let them go free, since they have served you for six years worth a hired worker's wages; so that the Lord your God may bless you in all that you do.

the words of the just. Follow justly what is just, so that you may live and possess the land which the Lord your God will give you. You shall not plant a grove or any tree near the altar of the Lord your God, nor shall you set up or erect a statue, which the Lord your God hates. Chapter XVII.
You shall not sacrifice to the Lord your God an ox or a sheep in which there is a blemish or any defect, for that is an abomination to the Lord your God. If there are found among you within any of your gates, which the Lord your God gives you, a man or a woman who does evil in the sight of the Lord your God and transgresses his covenant, so that they go and serve other gods and worship them, the sun, or the moon, or any of the host of heaven, which I have not commanded, and this is reported to you: then you shall inquire diligently, and if it is true and certain that such an abomination has been committed in Israel, you shall bring out to your gates that man or woman who has done this wicked thing, and you shall stone them with stones. On the testimony of two or three witnesses shall the one who is to die be put to death; he shall not be put to death on the testimony of one witness. The hands of the witnesses shall be first against him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people, so that you shall purge the evil from your midst. If any matter is too difficult for you to judge, between one kind of bloodshed and another, one kind of lawsuit and another, or one kind of assault and another — matters of dispute within your gates — then you shall arise and go up to the place which the Lord your God chooses. And you shall come to the Levitical priests and to the judge who is in office in those days, and you shall inquire of them, and they shall declare to you the decision. You shall do according to what they declare to you from that place which the Lord will choose, and they shall instruct you according to their law. You shall follow their decision, and you shall not turn aside from it to the right hand or to the left. But the man

who acts presumptuously by not obeying the priest who stands to minister there before the Lord your God, or the judge, that man shall die. So you shall purge the evil from Israel, and all the people shall hear and fear, and shall not act presumptuously again. When you come to the land that the Lord your God is giving you, and you possess it and dwell in it and then say, "I will set a king over me, like all the nations that are around me," you shall indeed set a king over you whom the Lord your God will choose. One from among your brothers you shall set as king over you. You may not put a foreigner over you, who is not your brother. And when he sits on the throne of his kingdom, he shall not multiply horses for himself or cause the people to return to Egypt in order to acquire many horses, since the Lord has said to you, "You shall never return that way again." And he shall not acquire many wives for himself, lest his heart turn away, nor shall he acquire for himself excessive silver and gold. And when he sits on the throne of his kingdom, he shall write for himself in a book a copy of this law, taken from that which is in the charge of the Levitical priests. And it shall be with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the Lord his God by keeping all the words of this law and these statutes, and doing them. His heart shall not be lifted up above his brothers, and he shall not turn aside from the commandment, either to the right hand or to the left, so that he may continue long in his kingdom, he and his children, in Israel. Chapter XVIII.

They shall have no inheritance among their brothers; the Lord is their inheritance, as he promised them. And this shall be the priests' due from the people, from those who offer a sacrifice, whether an ox or a sheep: they shall give to the priest the shoulder
