The judges shall investigate thoroughly, and if the witness is a false witness and has accused his brother falsely, then you shall do to him as he intended to do to his brother. So you shall purge the evil from among you; and the rest will hear and be afraid, and will never again do such an evil thing among you. You shall not show pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot. Chapter 20.
When you go out to battle against your enemies and see horses and chariots and an army greater than yours, you shall not be afraid of them; for the Lord your God is with you, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.

When the battle draws near, the priest shall come forward and speak to the people. Hear, O Israel. Today you are going into battle against your enemies: do not let your hearts be faint. Do not fear, do not panic, do not be terrified by them; for the Lord your God goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you. Then the officers shall speak to the army. Who is the man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go back to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man dedicate it. Who is the man who has planted a vineyard and has not yet made its fruit common? Let him go back to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man enjoy its fruit. Who is the man who has betrothed a wife and has not taken her? Let him go back to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her. When the officers have finished speaking to the army, they shall appoint commanders at the head of the army. Who is the man who is fearful and faint-hearted? Let him go back to his house, lest he make his brothers' hearts melt like his own heart. When the officers have finished speaking to the army, they shall appoint commanders of armies at the head of the people. When you draw near to a city to fight against it, offer terms of peace to it. And if it responds to you peaceably and opens to you, then all the people who are found in it shall do forced labor for you and shall serve you. But if it will not make peace with you, and makes war against you, then you shall besiege it. And when the Lord your God gives it into your hand, you shall put all its males to the sword, but the women and the little ones and the livestock and everything else in the city, all its spoil, you shall take as plunder for yourselves. And you shall eat the plunder of your enemies, which the Lord your God has given you. Thus

When you gather olives from your trees: you shall not go over the boughs again; it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow. When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you shall not glean it afterward: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow. And remember that you were a slave in Egypt: therefore I command you to do this thing. Chapter 25.

If there is a dispute between men, and they come to court, and the judges decide between them: they shall justify the righteous and condemn the wicked. And it shall be, if the wicked man deserves to be beaten, the judge shall cause him to lie down and be beaten in his presence. According to his fault a certain number of stripes shall be given him: but not more than forty, lest if he should exceed and beat him above that with many stripes, then your brother should seem vile to you. You shall not muzzle an ox when it treads out the grain. If brothers dwell together and one of them dies without children: the wife of the dead man shall not marry a stranger outside; her brother-in-law shall go in to her, and take her as his wife, and perform the duty of a brother-in-law to her. And the firstborn son she bears shall succeed in the name of his dead brother, that his name may not be blotted out from Israel. But if the man does not wish to take his brother's wife: then his brother's wife shall go up to the gate of the city and speak to the elders, saying: My brother-in-law refuses to raise up a name for his brother in Israel; he will not perform the duty of a brother-in-law to me. Then the elders of the city shall call him and speak to him. And if he stands firm and says, I do not wish to take her: then his brother's wife shall come to him in the presence of the elders, and pull his sandal off his foot, and spit in his face, and say: So shall it be done to the man who will not build up his brother's house. And his name shall be called in Israel the house of the unsandaled. If there is a dispute between them

And Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, saying: Keep all the commandments which I command you this day. When you have crossed the Jordan, set up the stones which I command you today on Mount Ebal, and plaster them with lime; and you shall build there an altar to the Lord your God of stones that no iron tool has touched, of unhewn and unpolished stones; and you shall offer on it burnt offerings to the Lord your God, and shall sacrifice peace offerings, and eat there, and feast before the Lord your God. And you shall write upon the stones all the words of this law plainly and clearly. And Moses and the priests of the tribe of Levi spoke to all Israel, saying: Attend and hear, O Israel. And all the people shall say: Amen. Cursed be he who makes the blind to wander off the road. And all the people shall say: Amen. Cursed be he who perverts the judgment due to the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow. And all the people shall say: Amen. Cursed be he who lies with his mother-in-law. And all the people shall say: Amen. Cursed be he who strikes his neighbor in secret. And all the people shall say: Amen. And all these blessings shall come upon you and overtake you, if you listen to his commandments. Blessed shall you be in the city, and blessed shall you be in the

The Lord shall send upon you famine and hunger and rebuke in all the work that you do, until he destroys you and brings you to ruin quickly, because of your evil deeds in which you have forsaken me. These are the words of the covenant which the Lord commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant which he had made with them at Horeb. Moses summoned all Israel and said to them: You have seen all that the Lord did before your eyes in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land — the great trials which your eyes saw, those great signs and wonders — yet the Lord has not given you a heart to understand or eyes to see or ears to hear, to this day. I have led you forty years through the desert; your clothing has not worn out on you, and your sandals have not worn off your feet. You have not eaten bread, nor have you drunk wine or strong drink, so that you might know that I am the Lord your God. And when you came to this place, Sihon the king of Heshbon and Og the king of Bashan came out against us to battle, and we defeated them and took their land, which we gave as an inheritance to Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh. Therefore keep the words of this covenant and do them, so that you may understand all that you do. You stand today, all of you, before the Lord your God — your leaders and your tribes and your elders and your officers, all the men of Israel, your little ones and your wives, and the stranger who is in your camp, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water — so that you may enter into the covenant of the Lord your God, and into his oath which the Lord your God is making with you today, in order that he may establish you today as his people, and that he may be your God, as he promised you and as he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob. It is not with you alone that I am making this covenant and this oath, but with those who are standing here with us today and also with those who are not here. For you know how we lived in the land of Egypt, and how we passed through the midst of the nations through which you passed, and you have seen their abominations and their idols of wood and stone, silver

Deuteronomy.

For this commandment which I give you today is not too high for you, nor is it far off. It is not in heaven, that you should say, "Who among us can go up to heaven and bring it to us, that we may hear it and do it?" Nor is it beyond the sea, that you should say, "Who among us can cross over the sea and bring it to us, that we may hear it and do it?" But the word is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, so that you can do it. See, I have set before you today life and good, and death and evil: in that I command you to love the Lord your God and to walk in his ways and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his ordinances, so that you may live and multiply, and the Lord your God will bless you in the land which you are entering to possess. But if your heart turns away and you will not hear, and if you are drawn away to worship other gods and serve them, I declare to you today that you shall surely perish; and you shall not live long in the land which you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess. I call heaven and earth to witness against you today, that I have set before you life and good, blessing and curse. Choose life, therefore, that you and your descendants may live; and that you may love the Lord your God, and obey his voice, and hold fast to him: for he is your life and the length of your days, that you may dwell in the land which the Lord swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them. Chapter XXXI.

And Moses spoke and declared all these words to all Israel, and said to them: "I am a hundred and twenty years old today; I can no longer go out and come in. Moreover the Lord has said to me, 'You shall not cross over this Jordan.' The Lord your God himself will cross over before you. He will destroy these nations before you,

and you shall dispossess them. And Joshua will cross over before you, as the Lord has said. And the Lord will do to them as he did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land; he destroyed them. And when the Lord has delivered them over to you, you shall deal with them according to all the commandments which I have commanded you. Be strong and of good courage; do not be afraid or dismayed before them, for it is the Lord your God who goes with you; he will not fail you or forsake you." Then Moses summoned Joshua and said to him in the sight of all Israel: "Be strong and of good courage; for you shall bring this people into the land which the Lord has sworn to their fathers to give them, and you shall put them in possession of it. The Lord himself goes before you; he will be with you, he will not fail you or forsake you. Do not fear or be dismayed." Moses then wrote this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and to all the elders of Israel. And Moses commanded them: "At the end of every seven years, at the feast of booths, when all Israel comes to appear before the Lord your God at the place which he will choose, you shall read this law before all Israel in their hearing. Assemble the people, men and women and little ones, and the sojourner within your gates, that they may hear and learn to fear the Lord your God, and observe all the words of this law; and that their children, who have not known it, may hear and learn to fear the Lord your God, all the days that you live in the land which you are crossing the Jordan to possess." And the Lord said to Moses: "Behold, the days of your death are near. Call Joshua, and stand in the tent of meeting, that I may commission him." So they went...

Moses and Joshua stood in the tabernacle of testimony, and the Lord appeared there in a pillar of cloud, which stood at the entrance of the tabernacle, and the Lord said to Moses: Behold, you will sleep with your fathers, and this people will rise up and fornicate after foreign gods in the land into which they are going and in which they will dwell; there they will forsake me and break the covenant which I made with them. My anger will be kindled against them on that day, and I will forsake them and hide my face from them, and they will be devoured; all evils and afflictions will find them, so that they will say in that day: Truly it is because God is not with me that these evils have found me. But I will hide and conceal my face on that day for all the evils which they have done, because they have followed foreign gods. Now therefore write this song for yourselves and teach it to the children of Israel, that they may know it by heart and recite it with their lips, and it may be a testimony for me against the children of Israel. For I will bring them into the land which I swore to their fathers, flowing with milk and honey. And when they have eaten and are filled and grown fat, they will turn to foreign gods and serve them, and will reject me and break my covenant. And after many evils and afflictions have found them, this song will testify against them, as it will not be forgotten from the mouths of their descendants. For I know their inclinations and what they are planning to do, even before I bring them into the land which I promised. Moses therefore wrote this song and taught it to the children of Israel. And the Lord commanded Joshua the son of Nun, saying: Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the children of Israel into the land which I promised, and I will be with you. After Moses had written the words of this law in a book and completed it, he commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, saying: Take this book and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, that it may be there as a testimony against you. For I know your contentiousness and your very stiff neck. While I was yet alive and going in and out among you, you were always contentious against the Lord; how much more will you be after my death? Gather to me all the elders of your tribes and your teachers, that I may speak these words in their hearing and call heaven and earth to witness against them. For I know that after my death you will act wickedly and quickly turn aside from the way which I have commanded you, and evil will come upon you in the latter days when you do evil in the sight of the Lord, provoking him to anger through the works of your hands. Moses then spoke in the hearing of the entire assembly of Israel the words of this song, until they were finished. Chapter 32.

Give ear, O heavens, and I will speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth. Let my teaching fall like rain, let my speech flow like dew, like showers on the grass and like gentle rain on herbs, for I will proclaim the name of the Lord. Ascribe greatness to our God; the works of God are perfect, and all his ways are justice. He is a faithful God, without any iniquity; just and upright. They have sinned against him, and are not his children because of their blemish. They are a perverse and crooked generation. Is this how you repay the Lord, you foolish and unwise people? Is he not your father who created you, who made you and established you? Remember the days of old; consider the years of many generations. Ask your father and he will tell you, your elders and they will explain to you. When the Most High divided the nations, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the children of Israel. For the Lord's portion is

· Deuteronomy ·

He is his people; Jacob is the portion of his inheritance. He found him in a desert land, in a place of horror and vast wilderness. He led him about and instructed him; he kept him as the apple of his eye. As an eagle that stirs up its nest, hovers over its young, spreads its wings, takes them up, and bears them on its feathers — the Lord alone led him; there was no foreign god with him. He made him ride on the high places of the earth, that he might eat the fruit of the fields. He made him to suck honey out of the rock, and oil out of the flinty rock, butter of the herd and milk of the flock, with the fat of lambs and rams of the sons of Bashan, and goats, with the finest of the wheat; and you drank the pure blood of the grape. But the beloved one grew fat and kicked; he grew fat, thick, and became sleek. Then he forsook God who made him and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation. They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods; with abominations they provoked him to anger. They sacrificed to demons, not to God — to gods whom they did not know, new ones who came recently, whom your fathers did not dread. You neglected the Rock who begot you, and forgot the God who gave you birth. The Lord saw it and spurned them, because of the provocation of his sons and daughters. And he said: I will hide my face from them; I will see what their end will be, for they are a perverse generation, children in whom there is no faithfulness. They have made me jealous with what is no god; they have provoked me to anger with their idols. So I will make them jealous with those who are no people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation. For a fire has been kindled by my anger, and it burns to the depths of the underworld. It devours the earth with its produce and sets on fire the foundations of the mountains. I will heap disasters upon them; I will spend my arrows against them.

They shall be exhausted with hunger, and devoured by plague and bitter destruction; I will send the teeth of beasts against them, with the venom of things that crawl in the dust. Outside, the sword shall bereave them, and inside, terror — both young man and the young woman, the nursing child with the man of gray hair. I said I would scatter them far away; I would make their memory cease from among men — were it not that I feared provocation by the enemy, lest their adversaries should misunderstand, lest they should say: Our hand is triumphant, it was not the Lord who did all this. For they are a nation void of counsel, and there is no understanding in them. If only they were wise, they would understand this; they would discern what their end will be. How could one have chased a thousand, and two have put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them, and the Lord had given them up? For their rock is not as our Rock — even our enemies themselves are judges. For their vine comes from the vine of Sodom, and from the fields of Gomorrah; their grapes are grapes of poison; their clusters are bitter. Their wine is the venom of serpents, the cruel poison of asps. Is not this stored up with me, sealed up in my treasuries? Vengeance is mine, and recompense; their foot will slip in due time. For the day of their disaster is near, and their doom comes swiftly. For the Lord will vindicate his people, and have compassion on his servants. When he sees that their power is gone, and there is none remaining, bond or free. Then he will say: Where are their gods, the rock in whom they took refuge, who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their drink offerings? Let them rise up and help you; let them be your protection. See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god besides me. I kill and I make alive; I wound and I heal; and there is none who can deliver from my hand. For I lift up my hand to heaven and swear: as I live forever —

· Deuteronomy ·

forever. If I sharpen my sword like lightning, and my hand takes hold of judgment, I will render vengeance on my enemies and repay those who hate me. I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh — with the blood of the slain and the captives, from the long-haired heads of the enemy. Rejoice, O nations, with his people, for he will avenge the blood of his servants, and render vengeance to his adversaries, and will be merciful to his land and people. So Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people, he and Joshua the son of Nun. When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel, he said to them: Set your hearts on all the words which I testify among you today, which you shall command your children to observe and do — all the words of this law. For this is not a vain thing for you; because it is your life, and by this thing you shall prolong your days in the land which you cross the Jordan to possess. And the Lord spoke to Moses that very same day, saying: Go up this mountain of the Abarim, that is, of the crossing — Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, across from Jericho, and view the land of Canaan which I give to the children of Israel as a possession. And die on the mountain which you ascend, and be gathered to your people, as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people: because you trespassed against me among the children of Israel at the waters of Meribah-Kadesh in the Wilderness of Zin, because you did not hallow me among the children of Israel. You shall see the land before you, but you shall not enter there, into the land which I am giving to the children of Israel.

And this is the blessing — Chapter 33 — with which Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death. And he said: The Lord came from Sinai, and rose from Seir to us. He shone forth from Mount Paran, and with him were ten thousands of holy ones. In his right hand was a fiery law. He loved the peoples. All his holy ones are in his hand, and they sat down at his feet; everyone shall receive of his words. Moses commanded us a law, the inheritance of the congregation of Jacob. He was king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people were gathered, all the tribes of Israel together. Let Reuben live and not die, and let his men be few. And this is the blessing of Judah. Hear, O Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him to his people. Let his hands be sufficient for him, and be a help against his adversaries. And of Levi he said: Let your Thummim and your Urim belong to your holy man, whom you tested at Massah, and with whom you contended at the waters of Meribah; who said to his father and mother, I do not know you, and who did not acknowledge his brothers and did not know his own children. For they observed your word and kept your covenant. They shall teach Jacob your judgments and Israel your law. They shall put incense before you, and whole burnt offerings on your altar. Bless, Lord, his strength, and accept the work of his hands. Strike through the loins of those who rise against him, and those who hate him, that they rise not again. And of Benjamin he said: The beloved of the Lord shall dwell in safety by him, and the Lord shall cover him all day long, and he shall dwell between his shoulders. And of Joseph he said: Blessed of the Lord is his land, with the precious things of heaven, with the dew, and the deep that lies beneath; and with the precious fruits of the sun and the moon; and with the best things of the ancient mountains, with the precious things of the everlasting hills; and with the precious things of the earth and its fullness. The blessing of him who appeared in the bush shall come upon

·Deuteronomy·

the head of Joseph, and the crown of him who was consecrated among his brothers. His beauty is like that of a firstborn bull; his horns are the horns of a wild ox. With them he shall gore nations, driving them to the ends of the earth. These are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and these are the thousands of Manasseh. And of Zebulun he said: Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar in your tents. They shall summon peoples to the mountain; there they shall offer sacrifices of righteousness, for they shall suck the abundance of the seas and the hidden treasures of the sand. And of Gad he said: Blessed be he who enlarges Gad! He crouches like a lion; he tears the arm and the crown of the head. He chose the best land for himself, for there a commander's portion was reserved; he came with the leaders of the people; he executed the justice of the Lord, and his judgments with Israel. Dan said: Dan is a lion's cub that leaps forth from Bashan. And of Naphtali he said: O Naphtali, satisfied with favor, and full of the blessing of the Lord, possess the sea and the south. And of Asher he said: Blessed above sons is Asher; let him be the favorite of his brothers, and let him dip his foot in oil. Your bars shall be iron and bronze, and as your days, so shall your strength be. There is none like God, O Jeshurun, who rides through the heavens to your help. His majesty is over the skies; beneath are the everlasting arms. He drives out the enemy before you and says, Destroy. Israel lives in safety; the fountain of Jacob alone, in a land of grain and wine; indeed, his heavens drop down dew. Happy are you, O Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the Lord, the shield of your help, and the sword of your triumph! Your enemies shall come fawning to you, and you shall tread upon their backs. Chapter 34.

Then Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, which is opposite Jericho. And the Lord showed him all the land — Gilead as far as Dan, all Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the western sea, the Negeb, and the plain of the valley of Jericho the city of palm trees, as far as Zoar. And the Lord said to him: This is the land of which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, I will give it to your offspring. I have let you see it with your eyes, but you shall not go over there. So Moses the servant of the Lord died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the Lord, and he buried him in the valley in the land of Moab opposite Beth-peor; and no one knows the place of his burial to this day. Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died. His eye was undimmed, and his vigor had not faded. And the people of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days; then the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended. And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him. So the people of Israel obeyed him and did as the Lord had commanded Moses. And there has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face, in all the signs and the wonders that the Lord sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land, and in all the mighty power and all the great deeds of terror that Moses did in the sight of all Israel.

Here ends Deuteronomy.

Prologue

Here begins the prologue of the blessed Jerome, priest, on the Book of Joshua.

At last, having finished the Pentateuch of Moses, as if released from a great burden, we turn our hand to Joshua, son of Nun, whom the Hebrews call Iosue Tennun, that is, Joshua son of Nun; then to the Book of Judges, which they call Sopthim; then to Ruth and Esther, which the same people name in like fashion. We urge the reader to carefully preserve in writing the forest of Hebrew names and the distinctions divided by their members, lest both our labor and his study perish. And above all, as I have often testified, let him know that I am not fashioning new things in reproach of the ancients, as my critics charge, but offering to men even a small portion of wood, which yet may delight them: so that through the Greek editions, which require so great expense and labor, they may obtain our version. And if in reading ancient volumes there is any doubt, comparing these things they may find what they seek. Especially since among the Latins there are as many editions as there are manuscripts, and each person, by his own judgment, has added or removed whatever seemed good to him; and one sees that what is discordant cannot be true. Let the scorpion therefore cease to rise up against us with its bent sting, and let its venomous tongue cease to gnaw at holy work. Accept it if you will, or condemn it if you dislike it — and remember these words: "Your mouth was filled with malice and your tongue devised deceits. You spoke evil against your brother and slandered your mother's son; these things you have done and I was silent. You thought wickedly that I would be like you; but I will rebuke you and set these things before your face." For what benefit is there to listeners or readers, that we labor in sweat while others labor in detraction? Jews grieve that the occasion to mock and ridicule Christians has been taken away, and that church members despise — nay, tear apart — that by which their adversaries are tormented. But if the old translation pleases them — which I also do not dislike, and they think nothing else should be received — why do they read and neglect what has been added or removed under asterisks and obeli? Why has the Church received Daniel according to the translation of Theodotion? Why do they admire Origen and Eusebius of Pamphilus, who differ in all their editions? Or what folly would it be, after someone has stated the truth, to prefer what is false? And from where in the New Testament can assumed testimonies be proven, if they are not found in the Old Testament books? We say these things so that we do not appear to remain silent before slanderers. For the rest, after the holy dominion of Paula, whose life is an example of virtue, and since I could not deny these books to the virgin Eustochia of Christ — as long as the spirit governs these limbs — we have resolved to devote ourselves to their explanation and to repeat a work long since set aside, especially since the admirable and holy man Pammachius urges us to this same task by letter; and we, hastening toward our homeland, yet restrained by death, must hear with deaf ears, as it were.

Here ends the prologue. Here begins the Book of Joshua, Chapter 1.

And it came to pass after the death of Moses, servant of the Lord, that the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, the minister of Moses, and said to him: Moses my servant is dead. Arise and cross this Jordan, you and all this people with you, into the land which I will give to the children of Israel. Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread upon, I will give to you, as I said to Moses. From the desert and Lebanon, even to the great river Euphrates — all the land of the Hittites —

Joshua.

You went out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you destroyed. When we heard these things, our hearts melted and no spirit remained in any man because of you. For the Lord your God is God in heaven above and on earth below. Now therefore swear to me by the Lord that, as I have shown you kindness, so you will also show kindness to my father's house, and give me a true sign that you will save my father and my mother, my brothers and sisters, and all that belongs to them, and deliver our lives from death. The men answered her: Our life for yours unto death, if you do not betray us. And when the Lord has given us the land, we will deal kindly and faithfully with you. Then she let them down by a rope through the window, for her house was on the city wall. And she said to them: Go to the mountain, lest the pursuers meet you, and hide there three days until the pursuers have returned, and afterward you may go your way. The men said to her: We will be guiltless with respect to this oath you have made us swear, unless, when we come into the land, you tie this scarlet cord in the window through which you let us down, and gather into your house your father and mother, your brothers, and all your father's household. If anyone goes out of the doors of your house into the street, his blood shall be on his own head, and we shall be guiltless. But if a hand is laid on anyone who is with you in the house, his blood shall be on our heads if anyone touches him. And if you betray us, we will be guiltless of this oath you have made us swear. And she said: According to your words, so be it.

And she sent them away, and they departed. And she tied the scarlet cord in the window. They went and came to the mountain and stayed there three days until the pursuers returned. The pursuers searched along all the roads and did not find them. The two men then came back down from the mountain and crossed the Jordan and came to Joshua son of Nun and told him everything that had happened to them. And they said: Truly the Lord has given all the land into our hands, and moreover, all the inhabitants of the land are faint-hearted because of us. Chapter III. Then Joshua rose early in the morning and they set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all the children of Israel, and they lodged there three days. After three days the officers went through the camp and commanded the people: When you see the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, carried by the Levitical priests, then you shall set out from your place and follow it. Yet there shall be a distance between you and it, about two thousand cubits in length. Do not come near it, so that you may know the way by which you must go, for you have not passed this way before. And Joshua said to the people: Sanctify yourselves, for tomorrow the Lord will do wonders among you. And Joshua said to the priests: Take up the ark of the covenant and pass on before the people. So they took up the ark of the covenant and went before the people. And the Lord said to Joshua: Today I will begin to exalt you in the sight of all Israel, that they may know that as I was with Moses, so I will be with you. And you shall command the priests who bear the ark of the covenant: When you have come to the edge of the waters of the Jordan, you shall stand still in the Jordan. And Joshua said to the children of Israel: Come here and hear the words of the Lord your God. And again

Joshua.

in the jubilee: and they shall go before the ark of the covenant. Seven times you shall march around the city: and the priests shall blow the trumpets. And when the sound of the trumpet grows long and is prolonged, and it shall ring in your ears, all the people shall shout with a great shout: and the wall of the city shall fall flat, and the people shall go up every man straight before him. So Joshua called the priests and said to them: Take up the ark of the covenant. And let seven other priests carry seven trumpets of jubilee: and go before the ark of the Lord. And he said to the people: Go and march around the city, with the armed men going before the ark of the Lord. And when Joshua had finished speaking to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven trumpets before the Lord went on and blew the trumpets: and the ark of the covenant of the Lord followed them. And the armed men went before the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rearguard followed the ark, while the priests continued to blow the trumpets. And Joshua had commanded the people, saying: You shall not shout, nor let your voice be heard, nor shall any word go out of your mouth, until the day I say to you: Shout! Then you shall shout. So the ark of the Lord went around the city once, and they returned to camp and stayed there. And Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the Lord: and seven priests bearing the seven trumpets of jubilee before the ark of the Lord walked along blowing the trumpets: and the armed men went before them, and the rearguard followed after the ark of the Lord, the priests going on and blowing the trumpets. And they marched around the city once and returned to the camp. So they did six days. On the seventh day they rose early at dawn and marched around the city seven times in the same manner. And when the priests had blown the trumpets on the seventh time, Joshua said to all the people: Shout! For the Lord has given you the city. And the city shall be devoted to the Lord, and all that is in it. Only Rahab the prostitute shall live, with all who are with her in her house. For she hid the messengers whom we sent. But as for you, keep yourselves from the things devoted to destruction, lest you covet them and take any of the devoted things and make the camp of Israel a thing for destruction and bring trouble upon it. But all silver and gold and vessels of bronze and iron are holy to the Lord; they shall go into the treasury of the Lord. So the people shouted, and the priests blew the trumpets. And when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, the people shouted a great shout, and the wall fell down flat, and every man went up into the city straight before him, and they captured the city. Then they devoted all in the city to destruction, both men and women, young and old, oxen, sheep, and donkeys, with the edge of the sword. But to the two men who had spied out the land, Joshua said: Go into the house of the prostitute and bring her out and all who belong to her, as you swore to her. So the young men who had been spies went in and brought out Rahab, and her father and mother and brothers and all who belonged to her. And they brought out all her relatives and put them outside the camp of Israel. And they burned the city with fire, and everything in it. Only the silver and gold and the vessels of bronze and of iron they put into the treasury of the house of the Lord. But Rahab the prostitute and her father's household and all who belonged to her, Joshua saved alive. And she has lived in the midst of Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho. Joshua made an oath at that time, saying: Cursed before the Lord be the man who rises up and rebuilds this city of Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn shall he lay its foundation, and at the cost of his youngest son

Joshua.

Now the children of Israel transgressed the commandment and took from the accursed thing. For Achan the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of the accursed thing. And the anger of the Lord burned against the children of Israel. And Joshua sent men from Jericho against Ai, which is beside Beth-aven, on the east side of Bethel, and spoke to them saying: Go up and spy out the land. And the men went up and spied out Ai. And they returned to Joshua and said: Let not all the people go up, but let about two or three thousand men go up and smite Ai; do not weary all the people there, for they are few. So about three thousand men went up, but they fled before the men of Ai. And the men of Ai struck down about thirty-six of them, and chased them from before the gate even unto Shebarim, and struck them in the going down. And the hearts of the people melted and became like water. And Joshua tore his clothes and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark of the Lord until evening, both he and the elders of Israel; and they put dust upon their heads. And Joshua said: Alas, O Lord God, why did you ever bring this people over the Jordan, to deliver us into the hands of the Amorites, to destroy us? Would that we had been content and remained on the other side of the Jordan! O Lord, what shall I say, when Israel has turned their backs before their enemies? For the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear of it and will surround us and cut off our name from the earth. And what will you do for your great name? And the Lord said to Joshua: Get up!

Why do you lie upon your face? Israel has sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them; they have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen and dissembled, and they have even put it among their own stuff. Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies, but turned their backs before their enemies, because they have become accursed. Neither will I be with you any more, unless you destroy the accursed thing from among you. Get up, sanctify the people, and say to them: Sanctify yourselves for tomorrow. For thus says the Lord God of Israel: There is an accursed thing in the midst of you, O Israel; you cannot stand before your enemies until you take away the accursed thing from among you. In the morning therefore you shall be brought according to your tribes; and it shall be that the tribe which the Lord takes shall come according to families; and the family which the Lord shall take shall come by households; and the household which the Lord shall take shall come man by man. And it shall be that he that is taken with the accursed thing shall be burned with fire, he and all that he has, because he has transgressed the covenant of the Lord and because he has wrought folly in Israel. So Joshua rose up early in the morning and brought Israel by their tribes; and the tribe of Judah was taken. And he brought the family of Judah and he took the family of the Zarhites. And he brought the family of the Zarhites man by man and Zabdi was taken. And he brought his household man by man and Achan the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah of the tribe of Judah, was taken. And Joshua said to Achan: My son, give, I pray, glory to the Lord God of Israel, and make confession to him, and tell me now what you have done; hide nothing from me. And Achan answered Joshua and said: Truly I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel, and this is what I did. When I saw among the spoils a beautiful scarlet robe, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, I coveted them and took them; and they are hidden in the earth in the midst of my tent, and the silver under it. So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran

Joshua.

They found all that was hidden in his tent, along with the silver. They took it from the treasury and brought it to Joshua and all the sons of Israel, and cast it before the Lord. Then Joshua took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons and daughters, and his oxen, and his donkeys, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had, and all Israel with him, and they brought them to the Valley of Achor. And Joshua said: Because you have troubled us, the Lord shall trouble you this day. And all Israel stoned him, and all that he had was consumed by fire. And they raised over him a great heap of stones, which remains to this day. And the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger. And the name of that place was called the Valley of Achor to this day. Chapter VIII.

And the Lord said to Joshua: Do not fear, and do not be dismayed. Take with you all the fighting men, and arise, go up to the city of Ai. Behold, I have given into your hand the king of Ai and his people, his city, and his land. And you shall do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king. The plunder and the livestock you shall take as spoil for yourselves. Set an ambush against the city, behind it. So Joshua arose, and all the fighting men, to go up to Ai. And Joshua chose thirty thousand mighty men of valor and sent them out by night. And he commanded them: Lie in ambush behind the city. Do not go far from the city, and all of you be ready. But I and all the people who are with me will approach the city from the front. And when they come out against us, as they did before, we will flee from them, until we have drawn them away from the city. For they will say: They are fleeing from us as before.

So while we flee from them, you shall rise from the ambush and seize the city, and the Lord your God will deliver it into your hands. And when you have taken it, set the city on fire, and do all things as I have commanded. So he sent them away, and they went to the place of ambush and lay between Bethel and Ai, to the west of Ai. But Joshua spent that night among the people. And Joshua rose early in the morning and mustered the people, and went up with the elders of Israel before the people to Ai, all the fighting men who were with him. And they went up and drew near to the city and encamped on the north side of Ai, with a valley between them and the city. And he took about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of the city. So the people positioned the main force to the north of the city and its rear guard to the west of the city, and Joshua went that night into the middle of the valley. And when the king of Ai saw this, he and all his people hurried and went out early in the morning to meet Israel in battle, toward the desert, not knowing that there was an ambush against him behind the city. And Joshua and all Israel pretended to be beaten before them, and fled in the direction of the wilderness. And all the people who were in Ai were called together to pursue them, and they pursued Joshua and were drawn away from the city. And when they had gone far from the city, and there was not a man left in Ai or Bethel who had not gone out after Israel, and they had left the city open and pursued Israel, the Lord said to Joshua: Raise the javelin that is in your hand toward Ai, for I will give it into your hand. And when Joshua raised the javelin in his hand toward the city, the men in ambush rose quickly from their place and ran

Joshua.

He found the city and they burned it. But the men of the city who were pursuing Joshua, looking back and seeing the smoke of the city rising up to heaven, could no longer flee this way or that, especially since those who had pretended to flee toward the wilderness had turned back most fiercely against their pursuers. When Joshua and all Israel saw that the city was taken and the smoke of the city was rising, they turned back and struck down the men of Ai. For those who had gone out and burned the city, having come out of the city, found themselves in the middle of their enemies striking them on both sides. When the adversaries fell on both sides so that none of that great multitude was saved, they captured the king of the city of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua. When all who had pursued Israel toward the wilderness were killed, falling by the sword in that same place, the children of Israel returned and struck down the city. Those who fell that day, both men and women, were twelve thousand, all the people of Ai. Joshua did not draw back his hand which he had stretched out holding the shield, until all the inhabitants of Ai were slain. But the livestock and the spoil of the city the children of Israel divided among themselves, as the Lord had commanded Joshua. He burned the city and made it an everlasting heap. And he hanged the king of it on a tree until the evening and the going down of the sun. Joshua commanded and they took his body down from the cross and cast it at the entrance of the city gate, and raised over it a great heap of stones which remains to this day. Then Joshua built an altar to the Lord God of Israel on Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded the children of Israel, as it is written in the book

of the law of Moses: an altar of unhewn stones which no iron tool had touched; and they offered burnt offerings upon it to the Lord, and sacrificed peace offerings. And Joshua wrote upon the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he had written before the children of Israel. And all Israel, and their elders and officers and judges, stood on both sides of the ark before the priests the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, both the stranger and the native alike. Half of them were in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded, that they should bless the people of Israel first. Then he read all the words of the law, the blessings and the curses, according to all that is written in the book of the law. There was not a word of all that Moses commanded which Joshua did not read before all the assembly of Israel, including the women and the little ones and the strangers who lived among them. Chapter 9.

When these things were heard, all the kings beyond the Jordan, who lived in the hill country and in the lowlands and all the coast of the great sea, and those who lived near Lebanon — the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites — gathered together to fight against Joshua and Israel with one accord and one purpose. But the inhabitants of Gibeon, hearing all that Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai, acting craftily, took provisions for themselves: worn-out sacks on their donkeys, and wineskins worn out and cracked and mended, and worn-out sandals patched on their feet, evidence of long wear, and old garments on themselves, and all the bread of their provisions was dry and crumbled into pieces. They went to Joshua who was then encamped

Joshua.

At Gilgal he spoke to them, and to all Israel with him. We have come from a distant land, wishing to make peace with you. And the men of Israel answered them and said: Perhaps you dwell in a land that falls to us by lot, and then we could not make a covenant with you. But they said to Joshua: We are your servants. And Joshua said to them: Who are you, and where do you come from? They answered: Your servants have come from a very distant land, in the name of the Lord your God. For we have heard of his might and of all that he did in Egypt, and to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan — to Sihon king of Heshbon and to Og king of Bashan who was in Ashtaroth. So our elders and all the inhabitants of our land spoke to us: Take provisions for the long journey, go to meet them and say: We are your servants; make a covenant with us. Here is our bread: we took it hot when we left our homes to come to you, and now it is dry and has crumbled. These wineskins were new when we filled them, and now they are burst and broken. These garments and sandals we wear, and those on our feet, are worn out from the very long journey and are nearly consumed. They took of their provisions and did not consult the mouth of the Lord. So Joshua made peace with them and entered into a covenant to let them live, and the princes of the congregation swore an oath to them. But after three days, when the covenant was made, they heard that they lived nearby and were to be among them. The children of Israel set out and came to their cities on the third day; their names were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim. And they did not strike them, because the princes of the congregation had sworn to them by the Lord God of Israel.

Then all the congregation murmured against the princes. But the princes answered them: We have sworn to them by the Lord God of Israel, and therefore we cannot touch them. This, however, we will do to them: let them live, so that the wrath of the Lord may not come upon us if we break our oath; but let them live and be cutters of wood and drawers of water for all the congregation. While they were speaking thus, Joshua called the Gibeonites and said to them: Why did you seek to deceive us, saying that you lived far from us, when in fact you dwell among us? Therefore you are cursed, and there shall never fail to be among you servants, cutters of wood and drawers of water for the house of my God. They answered: It was told to us, your servants, that the Lord your God had commanded his servant Moses to give you all the land and to destroy all the inhabitants of it. We feared greatly for our lives because of you, and therefore we did this. And now we are in your hands; do to us whatever seems good and right to you. Joshua did as he said, and delivered them from the hands of the children of Israel, so that they were not killed. And he appointed them on that day to be cutters of wood and drawers of water for all the congregation and for the altar of the Lord, in the place that the Lord would choose, as they are to this day. Chapter 10.

When Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had taken Ai and had destroyed it — just as he had done to Jericho and its king, so he had done to Ai and its king — and that the Gibeonites had gone over to Israel and were among them, he was greatly afraid. For Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities, and greater than Ai, and all its men were mighty warriors. So Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent

Joshua.

To Hoham king of Hebron, and to Piram king of Jarmuth, and to Japhia king of Lachish, and to Debir king of Eglon, saying: Come up to me and help me, that we may fight against Gibeon, because it has surrendered to Joshua and to the children of Israel. Then the five kings of the Amorites assembled together: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon, they and all their armies, and camped around Gibeon and fought against it. But the inhabitants of Gibeon, being besieged, sent to Joshua who was then encamped at Gilgal, and said to him: Do not withdraw your hand from helping your servants. Come up quickly and save us, and bring us aid. For all the kings of the Amorites who dwell in the mountains have gathered against us. So Joshua went up from Gilgal, and all the army of warriors with him, all mighty men. And the Lord said to Joshua: Do not fear them, for I have delivered them into your hands. Not one of them shall be able to resist you. Joshua came upon them suddenly, marching all night from Gilgal. And the Lord threw them into confusion before Israel, and defeated them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and pursued them along the way up to Beth-horon, and struck them as far as Azekah and Makkedah. And as they fled before Israel, while they were on the descent of Beth-horon, the Lord cast great stones from heaven upon them as far as Azekah, and many more died from the hailstones than those whom the children of Israel killed with the sword. Then Joshua spoke to the Lord on the day when the Lord delivered the Amorites before the children of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel: Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and Moon, over the valley of Aijalon. And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the nation took vengeance on their enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? The sun stood still in the middle of the sky, and did not hasten to set for about a whole day. There was no day like that before or after it, when the Lord heeded the voice of a man, and fought for Israel. Then Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal. Now the five kings had fled and hidden themselves in the cave at Makkedah. And it was told Joshua: The five kings have been found, hiding in the cave at Makkedah. And Joshua commanded his men, saying: Roll large stones to the mouth of the cave, and set men by it to guard them. But do not stop yourselves: pursue your enemies, and cut off those at the rear. Do not let them enter their cities, for the Lord your God has delivered them into your hands. And when Joshua and the children of Israel had finished striking them with a very great slaughter, those who escaped went into fortified cities. All the army returned safely to Joshua at Makkedah, and no one dared to move his tongue against any of the children of Israel. Then Joshua commanded: Open the mouth of the cave, and bring those five kings out to me. And they did as commanded, and brought out to him the five kings from the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon. When they had brought them out to him, Joshua called for all the men of Israel, and said to the chiefs of the warriors who had gone with him: Come near, put your feet on the necks of these kings. And they came near and put their feet on their necks. And Joshua said to them: Do not be afraid or dismayed; be strong and courageous. For thus the Lord will do to all your enemies against whom you fight.

Joshua.

upon them, and the Lord delivered them into the hands of Israel. They pursued them and followed them as far as great Sidon and the waters of Misrephoth, and the plain of Mizpeh to the east. And he struck them all down so that none remained. He did as the Lord had commanded him. He hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire. And turning back, he took Hazor at once and struck its king with the sword. For Hazor had formerly held the chief place among all those kingdoms. And he put to death all the souls that dwelled there. He left no remnant of them, but utterly destroyed everything and burned the city itself with fire, together with all the cities around it, and their kings he captured and struck down and killed, as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded. But the rest of Israel did not burn the cities that stood on hills and mounds — only Hazor, the most fortified, did Joshua burn. All the plunder and cattle of these cities the children of Israel divided among themselves, after slaying every person. As the Lord had commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and Joshua fulfilled all things. He did not pass over any of the commandments, not so much as one word that the Lord had commanded Moses. So Joshua took the whole land, the mountain country and the south, and the land of Goshen, and the lowlands, and the western plain, and the mountain of Israel and its lowlands, and the part of the mountain that goes up to Seir as far as Baal-gad by the plain of Lebanon under Mount Hermon. All their kings he captured, struck, and slew. For a long time Joshua waged war against these kings. There was no city that surrendered itself to the children of Israel, except the Hivites who dwelt in Gibeon — all the rest they took by battle. For it was the Lord's doing to harden their hearts, so that they would fight against Israel and perish, receiving no mercy, and be destroyed, as the Lord had commanded Moses. At that time Joshua came and cut off the Anakim from the hill country of Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah and Israel; Joshua utterly destroyed them with their cities. No Anakim were left in the land of the children of Israel; only in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod did some remain. So Joshua took the whole land, just as the Lord had spoken to Moses, and he gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to their tribal divisions. And the land rested from war.

Chapter XII

These are the kings whom the children of Israel struck and whose land they possessed beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise, from the torrent Arnon to Mount Hermon, and all the eastern plain. Sihon king of the Amorites who dwelt in Heshbon ruled from Aroer, which is situated on the bank of the torrent Arnon, and from the middle of the valley, and half of Gilead, to the torrent Jabbok, which is the border of the children of Ammon; and from the desert as far as the Sea of Chinnereth to the east, and as far as the sea of the desert, which is the Salt Sea, eastward by the road that goes to Beth-jeshimoth, and to the south under the slopes of Pisgah. The territory of Og king of Bashan, of the remnant of the Rephaim, who dwelt at Ashtaroth and Edrei, and ruled over Mount Hermon and Salecah and all Bashan, as far as the borders of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and half of Gilead, the border of Sihon king of Heshbon. Moses the servant of the Lord and the children of Israel struck them down; and Moses gave their land as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the children of Israel struck beyond the Jordan

Joshua.

To the western region of Baal-gad in the plain of Lebanon as far as Mount Lebanon, whose slope ascends toward Seir. Joshua therefore distributed to the tribes of Israel their individual portions, both in the mountains and in the plains and the open fields. In Ashtaroth and in the wilderness and in the south were the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. The king of Jericho, one. The king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one. The king of Jerusalem, one. The king of Hebron, one. The king of Jarmuth, one. The king of Lachish, one. The king of Eglon, one. The king of Gezer, one. The king of Debir, one. The king of Geder, one. The king of Hormah, one. The king of Arad, one. The king of Libnah, one. The king of Adullam, one. The king of Makkedah, one. The king of Bethel, one. The king of Tappuah, one. The king of Hepher, one. The king of Aphek, one. The king of Sharon, one. The king of Madon, one. The king of Hazor, one. The king of Shimron, one. The king of Achshaph, one. The king of Taanach, one. The king of Megiddo, one. The king of Kedesh, one. The king of Jokneam of Carmel, one. The king of Dor and the province of Dor, one. The king of the nations of Gilgal, one. The king of Tirzah, one. All the kings, thirty-one. Chapter 13.
Now Joshua was old and advanced in years, and the Lord said to him: You have grown old and are advanced in years, and a very large land remains to be possessed, which has not yet been divided by lot: namely all of Philistia and all of Geshur, from the Shihor River, which flows before Egypt, as far as the border of Ekron to the north — which is counted as Canaanite territory — the five rulers of the Philistines: the Gazites, the Ashdodites, the Ashkelonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites. To the south are all the Canaanite lands and Mearah that belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, to the border of the Amorites, and the region of Gebal and all of Lebanon toward the east, from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to the entrance of Hamath, with all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon

to Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians. I myself will drive them out before the people of Israel. Only divide the land for Israel as I have commanded you. Now therefore, divide this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh. The other half of Manasseh, together with Reuben and Gad, have already received the territory which Moses gave them beyond the Jordan to the east, as Moses the servant of the Lord assigned to them: from Aroer on the bank of the river Arnon and the town in the middle of the valley, and all the plateau of Medeba as far as Dibon, and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the Ammonites; and Gilead, and the region of the Geshurites and Maachathites, and all of Mount Hermon, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah; all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei — he alone was left of the remnant of the Rephaim — Moses struck him down and destroyed him. Yet the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maachathites, but Geshur and Maachath have lived among Israel to this day. To the tribe of Levi he gave no inheritance; the sacrifices and offerings of the Lord God of Israel are their inheritance, as he promised them. Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Reuben according to their clans. Their territory was from Aroer, which is on the bank of the river Arnon, and the town in the middle of the valley, and all the plateau by Medeba; Heshbon and all its cities that are in the plateau: Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-shahar on the hill of the valley, Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah, Beth-jeshimoth — all the cities of the plateau, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck down along with the leaders of Midian.

Joshua

and Rekem and Zur and Hur and Reba, princes of Seon, inhabitants of the land; and Balaam the son of Beor, the soothsayer, they killed with the sword along with the others they slew. And the Jordan River became the boundary of the children of Reuben. This is the possession of the Reubenites by their families, with their cities and villages. Moses also gave to the tribe of Gad and to his sons by their families their possession, of which this is the division. The border of Jazer, and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon, as far as Aroer which is opposite Rabbah; and from Heshbon to Ramoth-Mizpeh and Betonim and Mahanaim to the borders of Debir. In the valley, Beth-haran and Beth-nimrah and Succoth and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon. The Jordan also is its boundary to the farthest part of the sea of Chinnereth, beyond the Jordan eastward. This is the possession of the children of Gad by their families, with their cities and their villages. Moses also gave to the half tribe of Manasseh and his sons by their families their possession, of which this is the beginning. Mahanah, all of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Og king of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair which are in Bashan, sixty cities; and half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, to the children of Machir the son of Manasseh, to half of the children of Machir by their families. These possessions Moses distributed in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan near Jericho, toward the east. But to the tribe of Levi he gave no possession, because the LORD God of Israel is their possession, as he said to them. Chapter XIV.

This is what the children of Israel inherited in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun and the heads of the families distributed to them by the tribes of Israel,

dividing everything by lot as the LORD had commanded through Moses, for the nine tribes and half a tribe. For Moses had given the possession of the two tribes and the half tribe beyond the Jordan; but to the Levites he had given no portion among them, for the children of Joseph had grown into two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim; and the Levites received no portion of the land except cities to dwell in and their suburbs for their livestock and herds. As the LORD commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did and divided the land. Then the children of Judah came to Joshua in Gilgal, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite spoke to him, saying: You know what the LORD said to Moses the man of God about you and me at Kadesh-barnea. I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land, and I brought back an honest report to him. But my brothers who went up with me made the hearts of the people melt; yet I wholly followed the LORD my God. And Moses swore on that day, saying: The land on which your foot has trodden shall be your possession and your children's forever, because you have wholly followed the LORD my God. And the LORD has kept me alive as he promised until this present day. I am now eighty-five years old; I am still as strong today as I was on the day that Moses sent me; my strength now is as my strength was then, for war and for going out and coming in. Give me therefore this mountain which the LORD promised, you also heard it, where the Anakim are and where there are great and fortified cities; perhaps the LORD will be with me

Joshua.

I could destroy them, as he promised me. And Joshua blessed him, and gave Hebron to Caleb the son of Jephunneh as an inheritance: and Hebron became the possession of Caleb the son of Jephunneh unto this day, because he wholly followed the Lord God of Israel. The name of Hebron before was called Kirjath-arba; which Arba was a great man among the Anakim. And the land had rest from war. Chapter 15.

This then was the lot of the tribe of the children of Judah by their families: even to the border of Edom southward, and to the wilderness of Zin at the uttermost part of the south. Their south border was from the shore of the Salt Sea, from the bay that looks southward: and it went out to the south side to the ascent of Akrabbim, and passed along to Zin, and ascended up on the south side to Kadesh-barnea, and passed along to Hezron, and went up to Adar, and fetched a compass to Karkaa: from thence it passed toward Azmon, and went out unto the river of Egypt; and the goings out of that border were at the sea. This shall be your south coast. And the east border was the Salt Sea, even unto the end of Jordan. And their border in the north quarter was from the bay of the sea at the uttermost part of Jordan: and the border went up to Beth-hogla, and passed along by the north of Beth-arabah; and the border went up to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben: and the border went up toward Debir from the valley of Achor, and so northward, looking toward Gilgal, that is before the going up to Adummim, which is on the south side of the river: and the border passed toward the waters of En-shemesh, and the goings out thereof were at En-rogel: and the border went up by the valley of the son of Hinnom unto the south side of the Jebusite; the same is Jerusalem: and the border went up to the top of the mountain that lies before the valley of Hinnom westward, which is at the end of the valley of the giants northward: and the border was drawn from the top of the hill unto the fountain of the water of Nephtoah:

and went out to the towns of mount Ephron; and the border was drawn to Baalah, which is Kirjath-jearim: that is, the city of forests: and the border compassed from Baalah westward unto mount Seir, and passed along unto the side of mount Jearim, which is Chesalon, on the north side, and went down to Beth-shemesh, and passed on to Timnah: and the border went out unto the side of Ekron northward: and the border was drawn to Shicron, and passed along to mount Baalah, and went out unto Jabneel; and the goings out of the border were at the sea. And the west border was to the great sea. This is the coast of the children of Judah round about according to their families. And unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh he gave a part among the children of Judah, according to the commandment of the Lord to Joshua, even the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron. And Caleb drove thence the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak. And he went up thence to the inhabitants of Debir: and the name of Debir before was Kirjath-sepher, which is the city of letters. And Caleb said: He that smiteth Kirjath-sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife. And Othniel the son of Kenaz, the younger brother of Caleb, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife. And it came to pass, as she came unto him, that he moved her to ask of her father a field: and she alighted from off her ass; and Caleb said unto her, What wouldst thou? And she answered: Give me a blessing; for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And Caleb gave her the upper springs and the nether springs. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families. And the uttermost cities of the tribe of the children of Judah toward the coast of Edom southward were: Kabzeel, and Eder, and Jagur, and Kinah, and Dimonah, and Adadah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Ithnan, Ziph, and Telem, and Bealoth, and Hazor-hadattah, and Kerioth, and Hezron, which is Hazor: Amam, and Shema, and Moladah, and Hazar-gaddah, and Heshmon, and Beth-pelet, and

Joshua

Atesual and Beersheba, Baziothia, Abala and Humesem, and Heltholad, and Agul, and Zarma, and Sicelech, Medemena, Seusenna, Lebaoth, and Selim, and Ahen-Canon: all the cities twenty-nine and their villages. In the plains were Estaol and Sara and Alsena and Azone and Engannim and Thapha, Enaym, Ierimoth, Adulam, Sotho, and Azetha, and Sarim, and Adithaym, and Gedera, and Giderothayim: fourteen cities and their villages. Sanan, Adasa, Magdalgad, Delean and Maspha, Iedel, Lachis, Baschat and Eglon, Tebbon and Lemnas, Teethis and Gideroth, and Bethdagon, and Neama, and Maceda: sixteen cities and their villages. Labana, Ether and Asan, Iepta, and Esua, and Nesibstteyla, Achzib, Marela: nine cities and their villages. Accaron with its towns and villages. From Accaron as far as the sea, all that lies toward Azotus and its villages. Azotus with its towns and villages, Gaza with its towns and villages as far as the river of Egypt, and the Great Sea is its border. And in the mountain, Samir, Iether and Socho, and Edenna, Cariathsethna (this is Dabir), Anab and Histhemo and Anym, Gosen, Olon and Gylo: eleven cities and their villages. Arab, Roma and Slaan, Ianum, Iechabua, Aseca, Achnatha, and Chariath-Arbe (this is Hebron), and Sior: nine cities and their villages. Maon, Chermel, Ziph, and Loche, Israel, and Iucadam, and Zanoe, Accaym, Gabaa and Thamna: ten cities and their villages. Elul, Bethslu and Itedor, Mareth, Bethanoth and Betchecer: six cities and their villages. Cariathbaal (this is Cariathiarim, city of forests), and Arebba: two cities and their villages. In the desert, Bersaraba, Meddyn and Sacha and Nebsan: the cities of salt and Engaddi, cities altogether and their villages. In all, one hundred and fifteen. But the children of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem; and the Jebusites lived with the children of Judah in Jerusalem unto this day.

Chapter 16.
The lot also fell to the children of Joseph from the Jordan by Jericho and its waters on the east, the wilderness that goes up from Jericho to the mountain of Bethel, and it goes out from Bethel to Luz, and passes along the border of Archiatharoth, and it goes down westward to the border of Iesleci, as far as the borders of lower Bethoron, and of Gazer; and the regions thereof reach to the Great Sea. So the children of Joseph — Manasseh and Ephraim — took possession. And the border of the children of Ephraim was set according to their families; and the boundary of their possession on the east was Ataroth-addar as far as upper Bethoron, and it goes out to the sea. Machmecraft on the north, and it circles around the borders to the east at Thanaselo, and it passes from the brook of Tanoe, and goes down from Tanoe to Atharoth and Noaratha, and reaches to Jericho, and goes out to the Jordan from Taphua, and its boundary reaches to the sea in the valley of Hacundineti; and its exits are at the saltiest sea. This is the possession of the tribe of the children of Ephraim according to their families; the cities set apart for the children of Ephraim in the midst of the possession of the children of Manasseh, and their villages. And the children of Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanite who lived in Gazer; but the Canaanite lived in the midst of Ephraim unto this day, as a tributary.

Chapter 17.
The lot also fell to the tribe of Manasseh, for he is the firstborn of Joseph. Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead, was a man of war, and had possession of Gilead and Bashan. And the remaining children of Manasseh according to their families — to the children of Abiezer and the children of Heloch —

Joshua.

and to the sons of Helrihel, and to the sons of Lecher, and to the sons of Epher, and to the sons of Semida. These are the sons of Manasseh, the sons of Joseph, by their families. But Zelophehad, the son of Epher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons but only daughters, and these are their names: Mahlah, and Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah. And they came before Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun and the leaders and said: The Lord commanded by the hand of Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers. And he gave them, according to the command of the Lord, an inheritance among their father's brothers. And there fell ten portions to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan beyond the Jordan. For the daughters of Manasseh inherited a possession among his sons. And the land of Gilead fell to the rest of the sons of Manasseh. And the border of Manasseh was from Asher, to Michmethath, which faces Shechem, and goes to the right to the inhabitants of the spring of Tappuah. For the land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, which is on the border of the sons of Manasseh, belonging to the sons of Ephraim. And the border goes down to the valley of reeds, to the south of the river of the city of Ephraim, which is in the midst of the cities of Manasseh. The border of Manasseh is on the north side of the river, and its end goes to the sea, so that the possession of Ephraim is to the south and to the north is Manasseh, and both are bounded by the sea, and they join together in the tribe of Asher on the north and in the tribe of Issachar on the east. And the inheritance of Manasseh in Issachar and in Asher was Beth-shean and its villages, and Ibleam with its villages, and the inhabitants of Dor with its towns, and the inhabitants of Endor with its villages, and likewise the inhabitants of Taanach with its villages, and the inhabitants of Megiddo with its villages, and the third part of the city

of Nopheth. But the sons of Manasseh could not drive out those cities, and the Canaanite began to dwell in that land. But after the sons of Israel had grown strong, they made the Canaanites subject and made them tributaries, but did not drive them out. And the sons of Joseph spoke to Joshua and said: Why have you given me only one lot and one portion for an inheritance, since I am a great people and the Lord has blessed me? And Joshua said to them: If you are a great people, go up to the forest and clear a place for yourselves in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you. And the sons of Joseph said: We cannot go up to the hill country, for the Canaanites who live in the plain have iron chariots, both those in Beth-shean and its villages and those in the valley of Jezreel. And Joshua said to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh: You are a numerous people and of great power; you shall not have one lot only, but you shall go up to the forest and clear it, and its farthest borders shall be yours, for you shall drive out the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots and are very strong. Here ends Chapter XVIII.

And all the sons of Israel assembled at Shiloh, and they set up the tabernacle of testimony there, and the land was subdued before them. But there remained among the sons of Israel seven tribes who had not yet received their inheritance. And Joshua said to them: How long will you be slack to go in and possess the land which the Lord, the God of your fathers, has given you? Choose three men from each tribe, and I will send them out to go through the land and describe it according to each one's inheritance, and bring the description back to me. Divide the land into seven

Joshua.

portions: let Judah remain within its borders on the south side, and the house of Joseph on the north; between these, divide the land into seven parts, and come to me here, that I may cast lots for you before the Lord your God, for there is no portion among you for the Levites, but the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance. Gad and Reuben and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their possessions beyond the Jordan on the east side, which Moses the servant of the Lord gave them. So when the men had risen up to go and survey the land, Joshua commanded them, saying: Go through the land and survey it, and come back to me, so that I may cast lots for you here before the Lord in Shiloh. So they went and surveyed the land, dividing it into seven parts and recording it in a book; and they came back to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh. And he cast lots before the Lord in Shiloh, and divided the land among the children of Israel into seven parts. And the first lot came up for the children of Benjamin, by their families, to possess the land between the children of Judah and the children of Joseph.
