Their border on the north side was from the Jordan, running along the side of Jericho toward the north, and going up through the hill country westward, ending at the wilderness of Beth-aven; passing along to Luz, toward the south — that is, Bethel — and descending to Ataroth-addar, on the mountain that lies south of Lower Beth-horon; and the border turns and goes around on the west side southward from the mountain that lies before Beth-horon southward, and its extremity is at Kiriath-baal — which is also called Kiriath-jearim — a city of the children of Judah. This is the west side. On the south side, from the edge of Kiriath-jearim the border goes out toward the sea and comes to the spring of the waters of

Nephtoah. Then it goes down to the edge of the mountain that lies before the valley of the son of Hinnom, which is in the north end of the valley of Rephaim; and it descends into the valley of Hinnom — that is, the valley of the son of Hinnom — along the side of the Jebusite on the south, and it comes down to En-rogel, passing along to the north side to En-shemesh — that is, the Fountain of the Sun — and goes out to the cairns that are opposite the ascent of Adummim; and it descends to the stone of Bohan son of Reuben; and it passes along the north side to the Arabah; and it goes down to the Arabah and passes along northward to Beth-hoglah; and the border ends at the north bay of the Salt Sea, at the south end of the Jordan. This is the southern border. The Jordan forms the eastern border. This is the inheritance of the children of Benjamin, by its borders all around, according to their families. And the cities of this tribe were: Jericho and Beth-hoglah and the valley of Keziz, and Beth-arabah and Zemaraim and Bethel, and Avim and Parah and Ophrah, and Chephar-ammoni and Ophni and Geba — twelve cities with their villages. Gibeon and Ramah and Beeroth, and Mizpeh and Chephirah and Mozah, and Rekem and Irpeel and Taralah, and Zelah, Eleph, and the Jebusite — that is, Jerusalem — Gibeah and Kiriath — fourteen cities with their villages. This is the inheritance of the children of Benjamin according to their families. Chapter nineteen.

And the second lot came out for the children of Simeon according to their families: and their inheritance was in the midst of the inheritance of the children of Judah. Beer-sheba and Sheba and Moladah, and Hazar-shual and Balah and Ezem and Eltolad, and Bethul and Hormah, and Ziklag and Beth-marcaboth and Hazar-susah, and Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen — thirteen cities with their villages. Ain and Rimmon and Ether and Ashan — four cities

Joshua.

and its villages. All the towns surrounding these cities as far as Baal-gad by the border of Hamath to the south. There were seventeen cities in all. This is the inheritance of the sons of Simeon according to their clans, within the portion of the sons of Judah, because the share of Judah was too large for them; so the sons of Simeon received their inheritance in the midst of Judah's inheritance. The third lot fell to the sons of Zebulun according to their clans: the boundary of their possession extended as far as Sarid. Going up westward to Maralah and touching Dabbesheth, then the stream that is east of Jokneam; then turning from Sarid eastward toward the sunrise to the border of Chisloth-tabor and going to Daberath and up to Japhia; from there it passes along on the east toward the sunrise to Gath-hepher and to Eth-kazin, and going to Rimmon, which curves to Neah; then the boundary turns about on the north to Hannathon, and it ends at the valley of Iphtahel; and Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem: twelve cities with their villages. This is the inheritance of the sons of Zebulun according to their clans, these cities with their villages. The fourth lot came out for Issachar, for the sons of Issachar according to their clans. Their territory included Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-gannim, En-haddah, and Beth-pazzez; and the boundary touches Tabor, Shahazimah, and Beth-shemesh, and their boundary ends at the Jordan: sixteen cities with their villages. This is the possession of the sons of Issachar according to their clans, the cities and their villages. The fifth lot fell to the tribe of the sons of Asher according to their clans. Their boundary included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph, Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal; and it reaches to Carmel on the west and to Shihor-libnath; then it turns toward the east to

Beth-dagon, and reaches to Zebulun and to the valley of Iphtahel northward to Beth-emek and Neiel, going to Cabul on the left, and Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Great Sidon. Then the boundary turns to Ramah and to the fortified city of Tyre; then the boundary turns to Hosah, and it ends at the sea by the region of Achzib, Ummah, Aphek and Rehob: twenty-two cities with their villages. This is the possession of the sons of Asher according to their clans, these cities with their villages. The sixth lot came out for the sons of Naphtali, for the sons of Naphtali according to their clans. Their boundary extended from Heleph, from the oak in Zaanannim, and Adami-nekeb and Jabneel as far as Lakkum, and it ended at the Jordan; then the boundary turns westward to Aznoth-tabor and proceeds from there to Hukkok, reaching to Zebulun on the south and touching Asher on the west and Judah at the Jordan toward the sunrise. The fortified cities are Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Chinnereth, Adamah, Ramah, Hazor, Kedesh, Edrei, En-hazor, Yiron, Migdal-el, Horem, Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh: nineteen cities with their villages. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali according to their clans, the cities with their villages. The seventh lot came out for the tribe of the sons of Dan according to their clans. The territory of their inheritance included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir-shemesh (that is, City of the Sun), Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah, Elon, Timnah, Ekron, Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath, Jehud, Bene-berak, Gath-rimmon, and Me-jarkon and Rakkon, with the territory over against Joppa. And the border of the sons of Dan went out beyond them; for the sons of Dan went up and fought against Leshem, and captured it and struck it with the edge of the sword and possessed it and settled in it; and they called Leshem, Dan, after

Joshua.

This is the possession of the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families, their cities and their villages. When they had finished dividing the land by lot among the tribes, the children of Israel gave to Joshua the son of Nun a possession in the midst of them, according to the commandment of the Lord, the city which he asked for, Timnath-serah in mount Ephraim. And he built the city and dwelt in it. These are the possessions which Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun and the heads of the families and of the tribes of the children of Israel divided by lot in Shiloh before the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and they made an end of dividing the country. Chapter 20.

And the Lord spoke to Joshua, saying: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: Set apart cities of refuge, of which I spoke to you by the hand of Moses, that whoever kills a person accidentally and unawares may flee there, and may escape the wrath of the avenger of blood. When he has fled to one of these cities, he shall stand at the entrance of the gate of the city and speak to the elders of that city what he has done, and they shall take him into the city and give him a place that he may dwell among them. And when the avenger of blood pursues him, they shall not deliver the slayer into his hand, because he struck his neighbor unawares and had not hated him before. And he shall dwell in that city until he stands before the congregation in judgment, until the death of the high priest who shall be in those days. Then the manslayer shall return and come to his own city and his own house, from the city from which he fled. And they appointed Kedesh in Galilee in mount Naphtali, and Shechem in mount Ephraim, and Kirjath-arba which is Hebron in mount Judah: and on the other side of Jordan by Jericho eastward they assigned Joshua...

...which is situated in the plain wilderness, of the tribe of Reuben: and Ramoth in Gilead of the tribe of Gad: and Golan in Bashan of the tribe of Manasseh. These cities were appointed for all the children of Israel and for the stranger that sojourned among them, that whoever killed any person unawares might flee there, and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stood before the congregation. Chapter 21.

Then the heads of the families of the Levites came to Eleazar the priest and to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the heads of the families of the tribes of the children of Israel, and they spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan and said: The Lord commanded by the hand of Moses to give us cities to dwell in, with their common lands for our livestock. And the children of Israel gave to the Levites out of their inheritance, according to the commandment of the Lord, these cities and their common lands. And the lot came out for the families of the Kohathites, the children of Aaron the priest, from the tribe of Judah and the tribe of Simeon and the tribe of Benjamin, thirteen cities: and the rest of the children of Kohath, that is the Levites who remained, had by lot from the tribes of Ephraim and Dan and the half tribe of Manasseh ten cities. And to the children of Gershon the lot came out to receive from the tribes of Issachar and Asher and Naphtali and the half tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities in number. And to the children of Merari according to their families from the tribes of Reuben and Gad and Zebulun, twelve cities. And the children of Israel gave to the Levites cities with their common lands as the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses, by lot from each tribe. From the tribes of the children of Judah and of Simeon, Joshua gave cities which are named here for the children of Aaron of the families of the Kohathites of the Levites, for the first lot fell to them: Kirjath-arba, the father of Anak, which is called Hebron, in mount...

Joshua.

Judah, and its surrounding pasture lands. The fields and villages thereof he had given to Caleb son of Jephunneh to possess. So to the sons of Aaron the priest he gave Hebron as a city of refuge with its pasture lands, and Libnah with its pasture lands, and Jattir and Eshtemoa and Holon and Debir and Ain and Juttah and Beth-shemesh with their pasture lands — nine cities from those two tribes. And from the tribe of Benjamin: Gibeon and Geba and Anathoth and Almon with their pasture lands — four cities. All the cities of the sons of Aaron the priest together were thirteen with their pasture lands. The remainder went by families of the sons of Kohath of the Levites, and this was their possession. From the tribe of Ephraim: the cities of refuge, Shechem with its pasture lands in the hill country of Ephraim, and Gezer and Kibzaim and Beth-horon with their pasture lands — four cities. From the tribe of Dan: Elteke and Gibbethon and Aijalon and Gath-rimmon with their pasture lands — four cities. From the half-tribe of Manasseh: Taanach and Gath-rimmon with their pasture lands — two cities. All the cities given to the sons of Kohath of the lower rank were ten with their pasture lands. To the sons of Gershon of the Levites from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan and Beeshterah with their pasture lands — two cities. From the tribe of Issachar: Kishion and Daberath and Jarmuth and En-gannim with their pasture lands — four cities. From the tribe of Asher: Mishal and Abdon and Helkath and Rehob with their pasture lands — four cities. From the tribe of Naphtali: the cities of refuge, Kedesh in Galilee and Hammoth-dor and Kartan with their pasture lands — three cities. All the cities of the families of Gershon were thirteen with their pasture lands.

To the sons of Merari the Levites by their families were given from the tribe of Zebulun: Jokneam and Kartah and Dimnah and Nahalal — four cities with their pasture lands. From the tribe of Gad: the city of refuge Ramoth in Gilead, and Mahanaim and Heshbon and Jazer — four cities with their pasture lands. From the tribe of Reuben, beyond the Jordan opposite Jericho: the cities of refuge, Bezer in the wilderness, and Mephaath and Jahaz and Kedemoth and Mephaath — four cities with their pasture lands. All the cities of the sons of Merari by their families and clans were twelve. So all the cities of the Levites within the possession of the children of Israel were forty-eight in all, with their pasture lands, each distributed by family. And the Lord God of Israel gave to all the land which he had sworn to their fathers, and they took possession of it and dwelt in it. And he gave them rest on every side according to all that he had sworn to their fathers, and not one of all their enemies withstood them, for the Lord delivered all their enemies into their hands. Not one word of all the good promises which the Lord had made to the house of Israel failed; all came to pass. Chapter 22.

At that time Joshua called the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and said to them: You have done all that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you, and have obeyed me in all things; you have not abandoned your brothers these many days down to this present day, and you have kept the commandment of the Lord your God. Because therefore the Lord your God has given rest and peace to your brothers as he promised, return now and go to your tents and to the land of your possession which Moses the servant of the Lord gave you beyond the Jordan — only take diligent care and fulfill the commandment

Joshua.

and the law which Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you: that you love the Lord your God, and walk in all his ways, and observe his commandments, and cleave to him, and serve him with all your heart and with all your soul. And Joshua blessed them and dismissed them, and they returned to their tents. Now to the half tribe of Manasseh, Moses had given a possession in Bashan: and therefore to the other half, Joshua gave a portion among their brethren on the west side of the Jordan. And when Joshua dismissed them to their tents and blessed them, he said to them: Return to your homes with great substance and riches, with silver and gold, brass and iron, and abundance of clothing. Divide the spoils of your enemies with your brethren. And the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh returned, and departed from the children of Israel from Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan, to go into the country of Gilead, to the land of their possession, which they had obtained according to the commandment of the Lord by the hand of Moses. And when they were come to the banks of the Jordan, in the land of Canaan, they built an altar there by the Jordan, an altar of great size. And when the children of Israel heard of it, and certain messengers had brought them word that the children of Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh had built an altar in the land of Canaan upon the banks of the Jordan, over against the children of Israel: all the congregation of Israel assembled at Shiloh, to go up and fight against them. And in the meantime they sent to the land of Gilead, Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, and ten princes with him, one from each tribe. Who came to the children of Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh, in the land of Gilead, and said to them: Thus says the whole congregation of the Lord: What is this transgression? Why have you forsaken the Lord God of Israel, building a sacrilegious altar, and departing from his worship? Is it a small thing to you that you sinned with Baal-peor, and the stain of that crime remains in us to this day, and many of the people have fallen? And you have this day forsaken the Lord, and tomorrow his wrath will be kindled against all of Israel. But if you think the land of your possession is unclean, cross over to the land where the tabernacle of the Lord dwells, and dwell among us: only do not depart from the Lord and from our fellowship, by building an altar other than the altar of the Lord our God. Did not Achan the son of Zerah transgress the commandment of the Lord, and his wrath lay upon all the congregation of Israel? And he was but one man, and would that he alone had perished in his sin. Then the children of Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh answered the leaders of the delegation of Israel: The Lord God of gods, the Lord God of gods, he knows, and Israel shall understand: if it was in rebellion or transgression that we built this altar, let the Lord not save us but punish us. And if we did it with the intention of placing burnt offerings and sacrifices and peace offerings upon it, let him himself require it and judge: and it was not with that intention that we acted, but rather for fear that in time to come your children might say to our children: What have you to do with the Lord God of Israel? The Lord has placed the Jordan as a boundary between us and you, O children of Reuben and children of Gad; you have no part in the Lord. And so your children might turn away our children from fearing the Lord. Therefore we said: Let us build ourselves an altar, not for burnt offerings, nor for sacrifices, but as a witness between us and you and our descendants after us, that we may serve the Lord: and that our priests may come before him to offer burnt offerings and sacrifices and peace offerings.

Joshua.

...offerings: lest your children say to our children tomorrow, "You have no part in the Lord." But if they wish to say so, they shall answer them: "Behold the altar of the Lord which our fathers made — not for burnt offerings nor for sacrifice, but as a witness between us and you." Far be it from us that we should turn away from the Lord and forsake his footsteps, by returning to build an altar for burnt offerings, sacrifices, and oblations besides the altar of the Lord our God, which stands before his tabernacle. When Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the assembly who were with him heard this, they were satisfied; and the words of the children of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh pleased them greatly. And Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest, said to them: "Now we know that the Lord is with us, because you have not committed this trespass against the Lord, and you have delivered the children of Israel from the hand of the Lord." And he returned with the leaders from the children of Reuben and Gad from the land of Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the children of Israel, and reported to them. The report pleased all the children of Israel; and they praised God, and no longer talked of going up against them in battle to destroy the land they possessed. And the children of Reuben and the children of Gad called the altar: "A witness between us that the Lord is God." Chapter XXII.

A long time after the Lord had given peace to Israel, subduing all the surrounding nations, Joshua, now old and advanced in years, called all Israel — their elders, their leaders, their judges, and their officers — and said to them: "I am old and advanced in years. You have seen all that the Lord your God has done to all these nations before you, how the Lord your God has fought for you." And he allotted to you by lot all the land, from the east side of the Jordan to the great sea. Many nations still remain; the Lord your God will drive them out and remove them from before you, and you shall possess their land, just as he promised you. Therefore be very strong to keep and to do all that is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, turning aside from it neither to the right hand nor to the left; lest you go among these nations that remain among you, and swear by the names of their gods, and serve them, and bow down to them; but hold fast to the Lord your God as you have done to this day. Then the Lord will drive out before you great and strong nations; no one shall be able to stand before you. One of you puts to flight a thousand, for the Lord your God fights for you, just as he promised. Be very careful, therefore, to love the Lord your God. For if you turn back and cling to the remnant of these nations that remain among you, and make marriages with them, and associate with them and they with you, know for certain that the Lord your God will no longer drive out these nations before you; but they shall be a snare and a trap for you, a whip on your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from off this good land which the Lord your God has given you. And behold, this day I am going the way of all the earth, and you know in your hearts and souls, with all your whole being, that not one word has failed of all the good things that the Lord your God promised concerning you; all have come to pass for you, not one of them has failed. But just as all the good things have come upon you which the Lord your God promised you, so the Lord will bring upon you all the evil things, until he has destroyed you from off this good land which the Lord your God has given you, because...

Joshua.

You will transgress the covenant of the Lord your God which he made with you, and you will serve foreign gods and worship them. Quickly and swiftly the anger of the Lord will rise against you, and you will be removed from this good land which he has given you. Chapter 24.

And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem, and called the elders and the leaders and the judges and the officers. And they stood in the presence of God, and he spoke to them thus: Thus says the Lord God of Israel. From the beginning, your fathers dwelt beyond the river — Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor — and they served foreign gods. And I took your father Abraham from the region of Mesopotamia, and brought him into the land of Canaan. And I multiplied his descendants and gave him Isaac; and to Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. And to Esau I gave Mount Seir to possess; but Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt. And I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt with many signs and wonders; and I brought you and your fathers out of Egypt and you came to the sea; and the Egyptians pursued your fathers with chariots and horsemen as far as the Red Sea. And the children of Israel cried to the Lord; and he put darkness between you and the Egyptians, and brought the sea upon them and covered them. Your eyes saw all that I did in Egypt; and you dwelt in the wilderness a long time. And I brought you into the land of the Amorites who dwelt beyond the Jordan. And when they fought against you, I delivered them into your hands; and you possessed their land and destroyed them. And Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel. And he sent and called Balaam the son of Beor to curse you; but I would not listen to him, but on the contrary I blessed you through him:

and I delivered you from his hand. And you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho; and the men of that city fought against you — the Amorites and the Perizzites and the Canaanites and the Hittites and the Girgashites and the Hivites and the Jebusites — and I delivered them into your hands. And I sent hornets before you and drove them from their places — the two kings of the Amorites — not by your sword or your bow; and I gave you a land on which you did not toil, and cities which you did not build, that you might dwell in them; vineyards and olive groves which you did not plant. Now therefore fear the Lord and serve him with a whole and sincere heart; and put away the gods which your fathers served in Mesopotamia and in Egypt, and serve the Lord. But if it seem evil to you to serve the Lord, you have the choice today whom you wish to serve most: whether the gods whom your fathers served in Mesopotamia, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. But as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord. And the people answered and said: Far be it from us that we should forsake the Lord and serve foreign gods. The Lord our God himself brought us and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, and performed before our eyes those great signs, and preserved us in all the way through which we traveled, and among all the peoples through whom we passed; and the Lord drove out before us all the nations, the Amorites who inhabited the land which we entered. We will therefore serve the Lord, for he is our God. And Joshua said to the people: You will not be able to serve the Lord, for he is a holy and mighty God, jealous, and he will not overlook your sins and transgressions. If you forsake the Lord and serve foreign gods, he will turn and afflict you and destroy you, after he has done you good. And he said

Judges

These things said to Joshua, not in such a way as you have spoken to them, but they shall serve the Lord. And Joshua said to the people: You are witnesses that you yourselves have chosen the Lord to serve him. And they answered: Witnesses. Now therefore put away the strange gods that are among you, and incline your hearts to the Lord God of Israel. And the people said to Joshua: We will serve the Lord our God, and we will be obedient to his commandments. So Joshua on that day made a covenant with the people, and set before them commandments and ordinances in Shechem. And he wrote all these things in the book of the law of the Lord: and he took a great stone, and set it under the oak that was in the sanctuary of the Lord. And he said to all the people: Behold this stone shall be a testimony unto you, that you have heard all the words of the Lord, lest hereafter you deny it and lie to the Lord your God. And Joshua sent the people away, every one to his own possession. And after these things Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died, being a hundred and ten years old. And they buried him in the borders of his possession at Timnath-heres, in mount Ephraim, on the north side of mount Gaash. And Israel served the Lord all the days of Joshua, and of the elders who lived a long time after Joshua, and who had known all the works of the Lord that he had done for Israel. Also the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel had brought out of Egypt, they buried in Shechem, in the parcel of the field which Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred young goats: and it was in the possession of the children of Joseph. And Eleazar the son of Aaron died, and they buried him in Gibeah of Phinehas his son, which was given him in mount Ephraim.
Here ends Joshua, and begins the book of Judges which we call by that name. Chapter 1.

After the death of Joshua the children of Israel consulted the Lord, saying: Who shall go up before us against the Canaanites, and shall be the leader of the war? And the Lord said: Judah shall go up. Behold I have delivered the land into his hand. And Judah said to Simeon his brother: Come up with me into my lot, and fight against the Canaanites, that I may likewise go with you into your lot. And Simeon went with him. And Judah went up, and the Lord delivered the Canaanite and the Perizzite into their hands, and they defeated ten thousand men in Bezek. And they found Adoni-bezek in Bezek, and fought against him, and they defeated the Canaanites and the Perizzites. And Adoni-bezek fled; and they pursued after him, and caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his great toes. And Adoni-bezek said: Seventy kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered their food under my table: as I have done, so God has repaid me. And they brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there. And the children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire. And afterward the children of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites that dwelt in the mountains, and in the south, and in the plains. And Judah went against the Canaanites that dwelt in Hebron, whose name in former times was Kirjath-arba, and they defeated Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai. And departing from there, he went to the inhabitants of Debir, whose ancient name was Kirjath-sepher, that is, the city of letters. And Caleb said: He that takes Kirjath-sepher and lays it waste, I will give him Achsah my daughter to wife. And Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, took it, and he gave him

Judges.

his daughter as his wife. As they were traveling, her husband urged her to ask her father for a field. When she sighed as she sat on her donkey, Caleb said to her, "What is the matter?" She answered, "Give me a blessing; since you have given me dry land, give me also springs of water." So Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs. The children of Hobab the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law, went up from the city of palms with the children of Judah into the wilderness of their inheritance, which lies in the south of Arad, and dwelt with them. And Judah went with his brother Simeon, and they struck together the Canaanites who inhabited Zephath, and utterly destroyed it. And the name of the city was called Hormah, that is, Anathema. Also Judah took Gaza with its borders, and Ashkelon, and Ekron with their borders. And the Lord was with Judah, and he possessed the hill country; but he could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron. And they gave Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had said, who drove out from it the three sons of Anak. But the children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites who inhabited Jerusalem; and the Jebusites dwelt with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem until this day. Also the house of Joseph went up to Bethel, and the Lord was with them. For when they besieged the city, which was formerly called Luz, they saw a man coming out of the city, and they said to him, "Show us the entrance to the city, and we will show you mercy." And when he had shown them the city, they struck it with the edge of the sword; but they let that man and all his family go. And he went into the land of the Hittites, and built a city there, and called its name Luz, which is its name to this day. Manasseh also did not drive out Beth-shean and

Taanach with their villages, nor the inhabitants of Dor, nor Ibleam, nor Megiddo with their villages; but the Canaanites continued to dwell in that land. And after Israel grew strong, they put the Canaanites to tribute, but did not utterly drive them out. Neither did Ephraim drive out the Canaanites who dwelt in Gezer, but the Canaanites dwelt among them in Gezer. Zebulun did not drive out the inhabitants of Kitron or Nahalol, but the Canaanites dwelt among them, and became subject to forced labor. Asher did not drive out the inhabitants of Acco or Sidon, nor Ahlab, nor Achzib, nor Helbah, nor Aphik, nor Rehob; and the Asherites dwelt among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land; for they did not drive them out. Naphtali did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh or Beth-anath, but dwelt among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land; nevertheless the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath became subject to forced labor for them. And the Amorites pressed the children of Dan back into the hill country, for they would not allow them to come down to the valley; and the Amorites persisted in dwelling in Mount Heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim. But the hand of the house of Joseph prevailed, and they became subject to forced labor. And the border of the Amorites ran from the ascent of Akrabbim, from the rock, and upward. Chapter II. And the angel of the Lord went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said: "I brought you up out of Egypt and brought you into the land which I swore to give to your fathers. I said, 'I will never break my covenant with you; and you shall make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land; you shall break down their altars.' But you have not obeyed my voice. What is this you have done? Therefore I will not drive them out before you; they shall become thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare to you." When the angel of the Lord spoke these words to all the children of Israel, the people lifted up their voices and wept.

Judges

And the name of that place was called the Place of Weeping, or of Tears; and they sacrificed there to the Lord. Then Joshua dismissed the people, and the children of Israel went each to their own inheritance to possess it, and they served the Lord all the days of Joshua, and of the elders who lived a long time after him, and who had known all the works of the Lord that he had done for Israel. And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died, being a hundred and ten years old, and they buried him in the borders of his possession at Timnath-heres, in the mountain of Ephraim, on the north side of mount Gaash. And all that generation also were gathered to their fathers, and there arose another generation after them who did not know the Lord, nor the works which he had done for Israel. And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and served Baal, and forsook the Lord God of their fathers who had brought them out of the land of Egypt, and followed other gods, the gods of the peoples who were round about them, and bowed down to them, and provoked the Lord to anger, forsaking him and serving Baal and the Ashtaroth. And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of plunderers who spoiled them, and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, so that they could no longer stand before their enemies; wherever they went out, the hand of the Lord was against them for evil, as the Lord had spoken and as the Lord had sworn to them; and they were greatly distressed. Then the Lord raised up judges who saved them out of the hand of those who plundered them; and yet they would not listen to their judges, but played the harlot after other gods and bowed down to them. They soon turned aside from the way in which their fathers had walked, who had obeyed the commandments of the Lord, and they did not do so. Whenever the Lord raised up judges for them, the Lord was with the judge and saved them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge; for the Lord was moved to pity by their groaning because of those who afflicted and oppressed them. And after the judge died, they turned back and behaved worse than their fathers, going after other gods, serving them and bowing down to them; they did not drop any of their practices or their stubborn ways. The anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel, and he said: Because this nation has transgressed my covenant which I commanded their fathers, and has not obeyed my voice, I also will not hereafter drive out before them any of the nations which Joshua left when he died; that through them I may test Israel, whether they will keep the way of the Lord to walk therein, as their fathers did keep it, or not. So the Lord left those nations, without driving them out quickly; and he did not deliver them into the hand of Joshua.

Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to test Israel by them, that is, all in Israel who had no experience of any war in Canaan, so that the generations of the children of Israel might know war and be taught to fight, at least those who formerly knew nothing of it: the five lords of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites, and the Sidonians, and the Hivites who dwelt on Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon to the entrance of Hamath. They were for the testing of Israel, to know whether Israel would obey the commandments of the Lord, which he commanded their fathers by Moses. So the children of Israel dwelt among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites; and they took their daughters to be their wives, and their own daughters they gave to their sons; and they served their gods. And the children of Israel did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, and forgot the Lord their God, and served the Baals and the Asheroth. Therefore the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia; and the children of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim eight years. Then the children of Israel cried to the Lord, who

Judges.

He raised up for them a savior and delivered them: namely Othniel the son of Kenaz, the younger brother of Caleb; and the spirit of the Lord was in him and he judged Israel. He went out to battle, and the Lord delivered into his hands Cushan-rishathaim, king of Syria, and he overcame him. And the land rested for forty years, and Othniel the son of Kenaz died. But the children of Israel again did evil in the sight of the Lord, who strengthened against them Eglon the king of Moab, because they had done evil in his sight. And he joined to himself the children of Ammon and Amalek, and went and struck Israel, and possessed the city of palm trees. And the children of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab for eighteen years. And then they cried out to the Lord, who raised up for them a savior named Ehud, the son of Gera, the son of Benjamin, a man who was left-handed. And the children of Israel sent by him a present to Eglon the king of Moab. He made for himself a two-edged sword, having in the middle a hilt of the length of a palm's breadth; and he girded it under his garment on his right thigh. And he presented the gift to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man. And when he had presented the gift, he accompanied the people who had come with him, and returning from the idols that were at Gilgal, he said to the king: I have a secret word to say to you, O king. And he commanded silence. And all who were around him having gone out, Ehud went in to him. He was sitting alone in a summer parlor. And Ehud said: I have a word from God to you. He immediately rose from his throne. And Ehud put forth his left hand, and took the dagger from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly so forcefully that the hilt followed the blade into the wound, and was enclosed by the very fat. So that he did not draw out the sword, but left it in the body just as he had struck; and through the natural passages the bowels gushed out. And Ehud, locking the doors of the parlor most carefully, and fastening them, went out by a postern door. And the servants of the king coming in saw the doors of the parlor locked, and said: Perhaps he is relieving himself in his summer room. And waiting a long while until they were ashamed, and seeing that no one opened the door, they took the key and opening it, they found their lord lying dead upon the ground. But Ehud escaped while they were confused, and passed by the place of the idols from which he had returned. And he came to Seirath, and immediately sounded the trumpet in mount Ephraim; and the children of Israel went down with him, he himself leading them. And he said to them: Follow me, for the Lord has delivered our enemies the Moabites into our hands. And they went down after him and seized the fords of Jordan that led to Moab, and they suffered no one to pass over. But they slew of the Moabites at that time about ten thousand men, all strong and valiant; none of them could escape. So Moab was humbled that day under the hand of Israel, and the land rested eighty years. After him was Shamgar the son of Anath, who slew of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox goad; and he also defended Israel. IV.

And the children of Israel again did evil in the sight of the Lord after the death of Ehud. And the Lord delivered them into the hands of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; and the captain of his army was Sisera, who dwelt in Harosheth of the Gentiles. And the children of Israel cried to the Lord: for he had nine hundred chariots of iron, and for twenty years had mightily oppressed them. Now Deborah, the wife of Lapidoth, was a prophetess who judged Israel at that time, and she sat

Judges.

The earth was moved, and the heavens also dropped water. The mountains melted before the Lord, even Sinai before the Lord God of Israel. In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were deserted, and travelers went by roundabout paths. The strong men ceased in Israel until I, Deborah, arose, arose as a mother in Israel. God chose new warfare, and he himself overthrew the gates of the enemy. Was there a shield or spear seen among forty thousand in Israel? My heart is with the princes of Israel. You who willingly offered yourselves among the people, bless the Lord. You who ride on white donkeys, who sit in judgment and walk by the way, speak. In the places where they divided the spoils, the hosts of the enemy were smothered: there let them rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord, the righteous acts toward the villages in Israel. Then the people of the Lord went down to the gates. Arise, arise, Deborah: arise, speak a song. Arise, Barak, and capture your captives, son of Abinoam. Then the survivors came down to the nobles. The Lord made me have dominion over the mighty. Out of Ephraim their root was against Amalek; after you, Benjamin, among your peoples. Out of Machir came down governors, and out of Zebulun those who handle the marshal's staff. The princes of Issachar were with Deborah, and Barak was sent into the valley under his command, rushing forward. For the divisions of Reuben there were great thoughts of heart. Why did you sit among the sheepfolds, to hear the pipings for the flocks? For the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart. Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan, and Dan remained in ships. Asher sat still at the seacoast and stayed by his inlets. Zebulun and Naphtali

offered their lives to death in the high places of the field. The kings came and fought; then the kings of Canaan fought in Taanach by the waters of Megiddo; they took no gain of silver. From heaven the stars fought; from their courses they fought against Sisera. The torrent of Kishon swept them away, the ancient torrent, the torrent Kishon. March on, my soul, with might! Then the hoofbeats of horses thundered: the galloping of his steeds. Curse Meroz, said the angel of the Lord, curse its inhabitants bitterly, because they did not come to the help of the Lord, to the help of the Lord against the mighty. Most blessed among women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite; blessed shall she be among women in the tent. He asked for water, and she gave him milk; she brought out curds in a noble's bowl. She put her hand to the tent peg and her right hand to the workmen's mallet; she struck Sisera and crushed his head; she shattered and pierced his temple. Between her feet he sank, he fell, he lay still; between her feet he sank and fell. Where he sank, there he fell dead. Out of the window she peered, the mother of Sisera wailed through the lattice: Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why tarry the hoofbeats of his chariots? Her wisest princesses answer, indeed, she answers herself: Have they not found and divided the spoil? A damsel or two for every man; plunder of dyed stuffs for Sisera, plunder of embroidered work for the neck as spoil. So let all your enemies perish, O Lord! But let those who love him be like the sun as it rises in its might. And the land had rest for forty years. Chapter VI.
The children of Israel did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord gave them

. Judges .

And you shall take the second bull and offer a burnt offering with the wood of the grove that you shall cut down. Then Gideon took ten men from his servants and did as the Lord had commanded him. But because he feared his father's household and the men of the city, he did not do it by day, but did it by night. When the men of the city arose early in the morning, they saw that the altar of Baal was broken down, and the grove cut down beside it, and the second bull was offered upon the altar that had been built. And they said to one another: Who has done this? When they inquired and sought to find who had done it, they were told: Gideon the son of Joash has done this. Then the men of the city said to Joash: Bring out your son, that he may die, because he has broken down the altar of Baal and cut down the grove. Joash replied to all who stood against him: Will you plead for Baal? Will you save him? Whoever will plead for him, let him be put to death while it is yet morning. If he is a god, let him plead for himself, because someone has broken down his altar. Therefore on that day Gideon was called Jerubbaal, because Joash said: Let Baal plead against him, who has thrown down his altar. Then all the Midianites and Amalekites and the children of the east gathered together, and they crossed over and camped in the valley of Jezreel. But the Spirit of the Lord came upon Gideon, and he blew a trumpet, and the house of Abiezer rallied behind him. And he sent messengers throughout all Manasseh, who also rallied behind him. And he sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they came up to meet them. Then Gideon said to the Lord: If you will save Israel by my hand as you have said, I will place a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there is dew only on the fleece and all the ground is dry, then I shall know that you will save Israel by my hand as you have said. And it was so. When he arose early the next morning, he wrung the fleece and squeezed dew from it,

filling a bowl with water. Then Gideon said to God: Do not let your anger burn against me, and let me speak just once more. Let me test once more with the fleece: let it now be dry only on the fleece, and on all the ground let there be dew. And God did so that night: it was dry on the fleece only, and there was dew on all the ground. Chapter 7: Then Jerubbaal, who is Gideon, rose early with all his people and camped beside the spring of Harod. And the camp of Midian was to the north of them, in the valley beside the hill of Moreh. The Lord said to Gideon: The people who are with you are too many for me to give the Midianites into their hands, lest Israel boast about themselves against me, saying: My own hand has saved me. Now therefore go, proclaim in the hearing of the people, saying: Whoever is fearful and afraid, let him return and depart. And twenty-two thousand of the people returned, and ten thousand remained. And the Lord said to Gideon: The people are still too many. Bring them down to the water, and I will test them for you there. And whoever I say to you shall go with you, shall go; and whoever I say shall not go, shall not go. So he brought the people down to the water. And the Lord said to Gideon: Everyone who laps the water with his tongue as a dog laps, you shall set apart; and everyone who kneels down to drink shall be set apart. The number of those who lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, was three hundred men; but all the rest of the people knelt down to drink water. And the Lord said to Gideon: By the three hundred men who lapped I will save you, and deliver the Midianites into your hand. Let all the others go every man to his place. So they took provisions and their trumpets in their hands, and he sent all the rest of Israel away,

Judges.

He commanded them to their tents, and he himself engaged in the battle with the picked men. The camp of Midian was below in the valley. That same night the Lord said to him: Rise up and go down into the camp, for I have delivered them into your hand. But if you are afraid to go alone, let your servant Purah go down with you. And when you hear what they are saying, your hands will be strengthened, and you will go down more confidently against the camp of the enemy. He went down himself with his servant Purah to the edge of the camp where the armed men were keeping watch. Now Midian and Amalek and all the peoples of the east lay in the valley like a swarm of locusts, and their camels were without number, as the sand on the seashore. When Gideon arrived, a man was telling his neighbor a dream, and he related what he had seen. I dreamed a dream, and it seemed to me that a loaf of barley bread rolled into the camp of Midian and came to a tent, struck it and turned it upside down, leveling it to the ground. He to whom he spoke answered: This is nothing other than the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel. God has delivered Midian and all the camp into his hand. When Gideon heard the account of the dream and its interpretation, he worshiped, and returned to the camp of Israel and said: Arise, for the Lord has delivered the camp of Midian into your hands. He divided the three hundred men into three companies, and gave each man a trumpet and an empty jar with a torch inside the jar. And he said to them: Do as I do. I will go to the edge of the camp, and whatever I do, do likewise. When I blow the trumpet, you also blow your trumpets all around the camp and shout: For the Lord and for Gideon!

So Gideon and the hundred men who were with him came to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just when the guards had been posted. They blew the trumpets and smashed the jars they were holding. The three companies blew their trumpets and broke their jars, holding the torches in their left hands and the trumpets in their right hands for blowing, and they cried: A sword for the Lord and for Gideon! Each man stood in his place around the camp, and all the men in the camp ran, crying out and fleeing. When the three hundred trumpets were blown, the Lord set every man's sword against his neighbor throughout the entire camp, and the army fled as far as Beth-shittah and as far as Abel-meholah near Tabbath. The men of Israel from Naphtali and Asher and all Manasseh were called out and they pursued Midian. And God gave the victory to Israel that day. Gideon sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying: Come down against the Midianites and capture the waters ahead of them as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan. So all the men of Ephraim were called out, and they seized the waters as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan. They captured the two princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; they killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb they killed at the winepress of Zeeb. They pursued Midian and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon across the Jordan.

Then the men of Ephraim said to him: What is this you have done to us, not calling us when you went to fight against Midian? And they argued with him fiercely. He answered them: What have I done now compared to what you have done? Is not the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better? The Lord delivered into your hands the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb. What

Judges.

"What have you done to me that is like what I have done?" When he had said this, their anger against him subsided. And when Gideon came to the Jordan, he crossed over with the three hundred men who were with him, though they were exhausted and could not pursue. He said to the men of Succoth, "Please give loaves of bread to the people who follow me, for they are exhausted, and I am pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, kings of Midian." But the princes of Succoth answered, "Are Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hands, that we should give bread to your army?" He said, "Very well, when the Lord has given Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will thresh your flesh with the thorns and briers of the wilderness." And from there he went up to Penuel, and spoke similarly to the men there; and the men of Penuel answered him as the men of Succoth had answered. He said to the men of Penuel, "When I return victorious, I will tear down this tower." Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their forces, about fifteen thousand men, all who were left of all the army of the people of the East; for there had fallen one hundred and twenty thousand men who drew the sword. So Gideon went up by the route of the tent dwellers east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and attacked the army when it felt secure. And Zebah and Zalmunna fled; and he pursued them and captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and he threw all the army into a panic. Then Gideon the son of Joash returned from the battle by the ascent of Heres. And he caught a young man from the men of Succoth and questioned him; and he listed for him the officials and elders of Succoth, seventy-seven men. Then he came to the men of Succoth and said, "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying,

'Are Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hands, that we should give bread to your exhausted men?'" So he took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he disciplined the men of Succoth. He also pulled down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city. Then he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, "What kind of men were they whom you killed at Tabor?" They answered, "They were like you; each one resembled the son of a king." He said, "They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As the Lord lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you." So he said to Jether his firstborn, "Rise and kill them." But the young man did not draw his sword, for he was afraid, because he was still a youth. Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Rise yourself and fall upon us; for as the man is, so is his strength." Gideon arose and killed Zebah and Zalmunna; and he took the crescent ornaments that were on the necks of their camels. Then the men of Israel said to Gideon, "Rule over us, you and your son and your grandson also; for you have saved us from the hand of Midian." Gideon said to them, "I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you; the Lord will rule over you." Gideon said to them, "Let me make one request of you; give me every man the earrings from his spoil." For they had golden earrings, because they were Ishmaelites. They answered, "We will willingly give them." And they spread a garment, and every man threw in the earrings of his spoil. The weight of the golden earrings that he requested was one thousand seven hundred shekels of gold, besides the crescent ornaments and the pendants and the purple garments worn by the kings of Midian, and besides the collars that were around the necks of their camels. And Gideon made an ephod of it and put it in his city

Judges.

ephra. And all Israel fornicated with it: and it became a snare to Gideon and to all his house. And Midian was humbled before the children of Israel, and they could no longer lift up their heads: and the land was quiet for forty years, while Gideon held authority. Then Jerubbaal the son of Joash went and dwelt in his own house. And he had seventy sons who were born of him, for he had many wives. And his concubine who was in Shechem bore him a son also, whose name he called Abimelech. And Gideon the son of Joash died in a good old age, and was buried in the tomb of Joash his father at Ophrah of the family of Ezri. But after Gideon was dead, the children of Israel turned again, and went whoring after Baalim. And they made Baal-berith their god, and did not remember the Lord their God, who had delivered them out of the hands of all their enemies on every side: neither did they show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal Gideon, according to all the goodness which he had shown unto Israel. Chapter 10.

And Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem unto his mother's brothers, and spoke with them and with all the family of the house of his mother's father, saying: Speak, I pray you, in the ears of all the men of Shechem, whether is better for you, that all seventy sons of Jerubbaal should reign over you, or that one man should reign over you? Remember also that I am your bone and your flesh. And his mother's brothers spoke of him in the ears of all the men of Shechem all these words: and their hearts inclined to follow Abimelech, for they said: He is our brother. And they gave him seventy pieces of silver out of the house of Baal-berith, with which Abimelech hired worthless and reckless fellows, who followed him. And he went unto his father's house at

Ophrah, and killed his brothers the sons of Jerubbaal, seventy persons, upon one stone: but Jotham the youngest son of Jerubbaal was left, for he hid himself. And all the men of Shechem gathered together, and all the house of Millo, and went and made Abimelech king, by the oak of the pillar that was in Shechem. When they told it to Jotham, he went and stood on the top of mount Gerizim, and lifted up his voice, and cried, and said unto them: Hearken unto me, you men of Shechem, that God may hearken unto you. The trees went forth on a time to anoint a king over them. And they said unto the olive tree: Reign thou over us. But the olive tree said unto them: Should I leave my fatness, with which by me they honor God and man, and go to be promoted over the trees? And the trees said to the fig tree: Come thou, and reign over us. But the fig tree said unto them: Should I forsake my sweetness and my good fruit, and go to be promoted over the trees? Then said the trees unto the vine: Come thou, and reign over us. And the vine said unto them: Should I leave my wine, which cheers God and man, and go to be promoted over the trees? Then said all the trees unto the bramble: Come thou, and reign over us. And the bramble said unto the trees: If in truth you anoint me king over you, then come and put your trust in my shadow: and if not, let fire come out of the bramble and devour the cedars of Lebanon. Now therefore, if you have done truly and sincerely in making Abimelech king, and if you have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house, and have done unto him according to the deserving of his hands — for my father fought for you and risked his life, and delivered you out of the hand of Midian — and you have risen up against my father's house this day, and have killed his sons, seventy persons upon one

Judges.

...and you have made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the inhabitants of Shechem, because he is your brother. If then you have acted rightly and without fault toward Jerubbaal and his house, rejoice this day in Abimelech, and may he likewise rejoice in you. But if not, let fire come out from him and consume the inhabitants of Shechem and the town of Millo; and let fire come out from the men of Shechem and from the town of Millo and devour Abimelech. When he had said this, he fled and went to Beer, and he lived there, out of fear of his brother Abimelech. Abimelech ruled over Israel for three years. Then God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem, and the men of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech, so that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal and their blood might come upon Abimelech their brother, who had killed them, and upon the men of Shechem who had strengthened his hands to kill his brothers. The men of Shechem set ambushes against him on the mountaintops, and they robbed all who passed by them along that way. Abimelech was told of this. Now Gaal son of Ebed came with his kinsmen and moved into Shechem; and the men of Shechem put confidence in him. They went out into the field and gathered the grapes from their vineyards, trod them, and held a festival, and went into the temple of their god; and they ate and drank and cursed Abimelech. Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who is Abimelech, and who are we of Shechem, that we should serve him? Did he not serve the son of Jerubbaal?" He appointed Zebul as his officer over the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem. Why then should we serve Abimelech? "Oh that this people were under my command! Then I would remove Abimelech." Word was sent to Abimelech: "Gather your army and come."

Now Zebul the ruler of the city heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, and his anger was kindled. He sent messengers to Abimelech secretly, saying, "Gaal son of Ebed and his kinsmen have come to Shechem, and they are stirring up the city against you. Now therefore, go up by night, you and the troops that are with you, and lie in wait in the fields. Then early in the morning, as soon as the sun is up, rise early and rush upon the city. When he and the troops that are with him come out against you, do to him whatever you can." So Abimelech and all the troops he had with him rose up by night and laid an ambush against Shechem in four companies. When Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood in the entrance of the gate of the city, Abimelech and the troops he had with him rose from the ambush. When Gaal saw them, he said to Zebul, "Look, a crowd is coming down from the mountaintops!" Zebul said to him, "You are seeing the shadow of the mountains as if they were men." Gaal spoke again and said, "Look, a crowd is coming down from the center of the land, and one company is coming from the direction of the Oak of the Diviners." Then Zebul said to him, "Where is your boast now, you who said, 'Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him?' Are these not the troops you scorned? Go out now and fight with them." So Gaal went out at the head of the men of Shechem and fought with Abimelech. Abimelech chased him, and he fled before him, and many fell wounded, up to the entrance of the gate. Then Abimelech withdrew to Arumah; and Zebul drove out Gaal and his kinsmen, so that they could not live on in Shechem. On the following day the troops went out into the fields, and Abimelech was told. He took his troops and divided them into three companies, and lay in wait in the fields; and when he looked and saw the people coming out of the city, he rose against them and attacked...

Judges.

But the towers of the palaces were being pursued through the countryside. Moreover Abimelech attacked the city all that day, and when he had taken it, killing its inhabitants, he destroyed it so that salt was scattered over it. When those who dwelt in the tower of Shechem heard this, they entered the temple of their god Berith, where they had made a covenant, and from which that place had received its name, which was very well fortified. Abimelech also, hearing that the men of the tower of Shechem had gathered together, went up to Mount Zalmon with all his forces: and taking an axe, he cut down a bough from a tree, and laying it on his shoulder, said to his companions: What you see me do, do quickly. They therefore vied with one another in cutting down branches from the trees and followed their leader. And surrounding the stronghold they set it on fire, so that a thousand men and women were killed by smoke and flame, the inhabitants of the tower of Shechem. Then Abimelech, departing from there, came to the city of Thebez, which he surrounded and besieged with his army. But there was in the middle of the city a high tower, to which both men and women had fled together, and all the leaders of the city, and having shut the gate fast, they stood on the roof of the tower to defend it. And Abimelech, approaching near the tower, fought bravely, and drawing close to the gate, tried to set fire to it. And behold, a certain woman cast a piece of millstone upon the head of Abimelech, and broke his skull. Then he quickly called his armor-bearer and said to him: Draw your sword and kill me, lest it be said that I was killed by a woman. He did as he was ordered and killed him. And when he was dead, all the men of Israel who were with him returned to their homes. And God repaid the evil that Abimelech had done against his father by killing seventy of his brothers.

Also the Shechemites received what they deserved, and upon them came the curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal. r. r.

After Abimelech there arose a ruler in Israel, Tola the son of Puah, uncle of Abimelech, a man of Issachar, who lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim; and he judged Israel twenty-three years, and he died and was buried in Shamir. After him arose Jair the Gileadite, who judged Israel twenty-two years; he had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty cities in the land of Gilead, which are called the villages of Jair to this day. And Jair died and was buried in Kamon. But the people of Israel again did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, and served the Baals and the Ashtaroth and the gods of Syria and the gods of Sidon and the gods of Moab and the gods of the Ammonites and the gods of the Philistines: and they forsook the Lord and did not serve him. And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the Ammonites; and they afflicted and oppressed the people of Israel eighteen years, all the people of Israel who were beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead. And the Ammonites crossed the Jordan to fight also against Judah and against Benjamin and against Ephraim, so that Israel was greatly distressed. And the people of Israel cried to the Lord, saying: We have sinned against you, because we have forsaken the Lord our God, and have served the Baals. And the Lord said: Where are your gods now? Let them deliver you in the time of your distress. Did not the Egyptians and the Amorites and the Ammonites and the Philistines and the Sidonians and also Amalek and Canaan oppress you, and when you cried to me, did I not deliver you from their hand? Yet you have forsaken me and served other gods: therefore I will save you no more. Go and cry to the gods you have chosen;

Judges.

the gods you chose. Let them deliver you in your time of distress." And the children of Israel said to the Lord: "We have sinned. Do to us whatever pleases you, only deliver us now." And saying this, they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the Lord God, who was moved by their miseries. Then the children of Ammon gathered and encamped in Gilead. And the children of Israel assembled and encamped at Mizpah. And the princes of Gilead said to one another: "Whoever shall be the first to begin the fight against the children of Ammon, he shall be the leader of all who dwell in Gilead." Chapter 11.

Now there was at that time Jephthah of Gilead, a mighty man of valor and a warrior, the son of a harlot woman, who was born of Gilead. And Gilead had a wife from whom he had sons; and when the wife's sons were grown, they drove out Jephthah, saying: "You cannot be an heir in our father's house, for you are the son of another woman." So Jephthah fled from them and dwelt in the land of Tob. And worthless men gathered to him as followers, and went out with him. And in those days the children of Ammon made war against Israel. When they did so, the elders of Gilead went to fetch Jephthah from the land of Tob, and they said to him: "Come and be our commander, that we may fight against the children of Ammon." But he said to them: "Are you not the ones who hated me and drove me out from my father's house? Why have you come to me now when you are in trouble?" And the princes of Gilead said to Jephthah: "For this reason we have come to you, that you may go with us and fight against the children of Ammon, and you shall be the head of all who dwell in Gilead." And Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead: "If you truly bring me back to fight against the children of Ammon, and the Lord delivers them before me, shall I be your head?" And they answered him: "The Lord is witness between us; we will surely do as you say." So Jephthah went with the princes of Gilead, and the people made him their head and commander. And Jephthah spoke all his words before the Lord at Mizpah. Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the children of Ammon, saying: "What do you have against me, that you have come to me to fight against my land?" And the king of the children of Ammon answered the messengers of Jephthah: "Because Israel took away my land when they came up out of Egypt, from the Arnon as far as the Jabbok and the Jordan. Now therefore restore those lands peaceably." But Jephthah again sent messengers to the king of the children of Ammon, saying: "Thus says Jephthah: Israel did not take away the land of Moab or the land of the children of Ammon, but when they came up from Egypt, Israel went through the wilderness to the Red Sea and came to Kadesh. Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying: 'Please let me pass through your land.' But the king of Edom would not listen. And they also sent to the king of Moab, but he would not consent either. So Israel stayed at Kadesh and traveled around the land of Edom and the land of Moab, and came to the east side of the land of Moab, and they camped on the other side of the Arnon, and did not enter the territory of Moab, for the Arnon was the boundary of Moab. Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, and said to him: 'Please let us pass through your land to our place.' But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory; instead he gathered all his people together and went out against him.

Judges.

in Japhia, and strongly resisted. And the Lord delivered him into the hand of Israel with all his army, and they defeated him: and they possessed all the land of the Amorite who dwelt in that region, and all its borders from Arnon to Jabbok, and from the wilderness to the Jordan. The Lord God of Israel therefore drove out the Amorite from before his people Israel. And do you now wish to possess his land? Are not those things which your god Chemosh possessed rightfully yours? But what the Lord our God has conquered shall belong to us. Unless perhaps you are better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, or can you show that he ever contended against Israel, or fought against them, when they dwelt in Heshbon and its villages, and in Aroer and its towns, and in all the cities along the Jordan, for three hundred years? Why have you not during all that time tried to recover them? Therefore I am not sinning against you, but you are doing me wrong by making war against me. Let the Lord, the judge, decide this day between Israel and the children of Ammon. But the king of the children of Ammon would not listen to the words of Jephthah which he had sent by the messengers. Therefore the Spirit of the Lord came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh, and through Mizpah of Gilead, and from Mizpah of Gilead he passed on to the children of Ammon, and made a vow to the Lord, saying: If you will deliver the children of Ammon into my hands, whoever comes forth first from the doors of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the children of Ammon, shall be offered as a burnt offering to the Lord. And Jephthah passed over to the children of Ammon to fight against them, and the Lord delivered them into his hands, and he struck them from Aroer until you come to Minnith, twenty cities, and to Abel-keramim, with a very great slaughter;

and the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel. And Jephthah returned to Mizpah to his house, and behold his daughter came out to meet him with timbrels and dances: she was his only child, for he had no other son or daughter. When he saw her, he tore his garments and said: Alas, my daughter, you have brought me very low, and you have become the cause of great trouble to me; for I have opened my mouth to the Lord, and I cannot take back what I have said. And she said to him: My father, you have opened your mouth to the Lord; do to me whatever you have promised, since the victory has been given you over your enemies. And she said to her father: Grant me this one request: let me go for two months through the mountains, and let me bewail my virginity with my companions. And he said: Go. And he sent her away for two months. And she went with her companions and mourned her virginity upon the mountains. And when two months were passed, she returned to her father, and he did to her as he had vowed. And she had not known any man. And it became a custom in Israel, that after the circuit of the year the daughters of Israel gathered to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite for four days. Chapter 12.

And there arose a great dispute in Ephraim. For the men who had crossed over to the north said to Jephthah: Why did you go to fight against the children of Ammon and did not call us to go with you? We will burn your house down over you. And he answered them: I and my people were in great strife with the children of Ammon; and I called you, but you would not deliver me out of their hands. And when I saw that you would not save me, I took my life in my hands, and passed over against the children of Ammon, and the Lord delivered them into my hands. Why then have you risen up against me to fight? And Jephthah gathered together all the men of Gilead

Judges.

The men of Gilead fought against Ephraim. And the men of Gilead struck down the Ephraimites, because they had said: Gilead is a fugitive from Ephraim and dwells in the midst of Ephraim and Manasseh. And the Gileadites seized the fords of the Jordan, by which Ephraim would return. And when any of the fugitives from Ephraim came there and said: Let me cross over, the men of Gilead said to him: Are you an Ephraimite? If he said No, they told him: Then say Shibboleth, which is interpreted as an ear of grain. But he said Sibboleth, being unable to pronounce the same letter for an ear of grain. And they immediately seized him and killed him at the crossing of the Jordan. At that time forty-two thousand of Ephraim fell. And Jephthah the Gileadite judged Israel six years: and he died and was buried in his city of Gilead. After him Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel, who had thirty sons and as many daughters: he sent his daughters out to husbands, and brought in thirty daughters-in-law for his sons, bringing them into his house. He judged Israel seven years, and he died and was buried in Bethlehem. After him Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel for ten years, and he died and was buried in Zebulun. After him Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel, who had forty sons and thirty grandsons riding on seventy ass colts: and he judged Israel eight years, and he died and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim on Mount Amalek. Chapter XIII. And the children of Israel again did evil in the sight of the Lord, and he delivered them into the hands of the Philistines for forty years. Now there was a certain man of Zorah, of the tribe of Dan, whose name was Manoah, and his wife was barren: and an angel of the Lord appeared to her and said to her: You are barren and without children, but you shall conceive and bear a son. Beware therefore that you drink no wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing: for you shall conceive and bear a son, upon whose head no razor shall come. For the child shall be a Nazirite of God from his mother's womb: and he shall begin to deliver Israel from the hand of the Philistines. And she came to her husband and said to him: A man of God came to me, having the appearance of an angel, very awesome. When I asked him who he was and where he came from, and by what name he was called, he would not tell me: but he said this: Behold, you shall conceive and bear a son. Beware that you drink no wine or strong drink, and eat nothing unclean. For the child shall be a Nazirite of God from his mother's womb unto the day of his death. Then Manoah prayed to the Lord and said: I beseech you, O Lord, let the man of God whom you sent come again to us, and teach us what we must do for the child that shall be born. And the Lord heard the prayer of Manoah: and the angel of the Lord appeared again to his wife as she sat in the field. But Manoah her husband was not with her. And when she saw the angel, she hurried and ran to her husband, and announced to him saying: Behold, the man has appeared to me whom I saw before. And he arose and followed his wife: and he came to the man and said to him: Are you the one who spoke to the woman? And he answered: I am. Then Manoah said: When your word comes to pass, what must the child do, and what must he observe? And the angel of the Lord said to Manoah: From all that I spoke to your wife let her abstain: and let her not eat anything that comes from the vine, nor drink wine or strong drink: let her touch nothing

Judges.

entreat him earnestly and that he fulfill and keep what he has commanded. And Manoah said to the angel of the Lord: I pray you to consent to my request, and I will offer you a kid of the goats. And the angel answered him: If you press me, I will not eat of your bread; but if you would offer a holocaust, offer it to the Lord. And Manoah did not know that he was an angel of God. And he said to him: What is your name, so that if your word comes to pass, we may honor you? And he answered him: Why do you ask my name, which is wonderful? So Manoah took a kid of the goats and libations, and put them upon the rock, offering to the Lord who works wonders. But he and his wife were watching. And when the flame from the altar went up toward heaven, the angel of the Lord ascended in the flame. When Manoah and his wife saw this, they fell face down on the ground: and the angel of the Lord appeared to them no more. And Manoah understood at once that it was an angel of the Lord, and said to his wife: We shall surely die, because we have seen God. But his wife answered him: If the Lord had meant to kill us, he would not have accepted a holocaust and libations from our hands, nor would he have shown us all these things, nor would he have told us the things that are to come. So she bore a son and called his name Samson. And the child grew, and the Lord blessed him: and the spirit of the Lord began to go with him in the camp of Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol. Chapter 14.

Then Samson went down to Timnath, and seeing there a woman of the daughters of the Philistines, he came up and told his father and mother, saying: I saw a woman in Timnath of the daughters of the Philistines; I ask you to take her for my wife. But his father and mother said to him: Is there no woman among the daughters of your brethren, or among all my people, that you want to take a wife from the Philistines, who are uncircumcised?

And Samson said to his father: Take this woman for me, for she has pleased my eyes. Now his parents did not know that the thing was done by the Lord, and that he was seeking an occasion against the Philistines. For at that time the Philistines had dominion over Israel. Then Samson went down to Timnath with his father and mother. And when they were come to the vineyards of the town, a young lion came roaring toward him. And the spirit of the Lord came upon Samson, and he tore the lion apart as he would a kid, having nothing in his hand; and he did not tell his father or mother what he had done. And he went down and spoke to the woman who had pleased his eyes. And after some days, returning to take her, he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion. And behold, there was a swarm of bees in the mouth of the lion, and a honeycomb. And when he had taken some of it in his hands, he ate it as he walked, and coming to his father and mother, he gave them some of it, and they ate: but he did not tell them that he had taken the honey from the body of the lion. So his father went down to the woman, and Samson made a feast there, for young men used to do so. And when the citizens of that place saw him, they brought him thirty companions to be with him. And Samson said to them: I will propose to you a riddle; if you can solve it for me within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing.
