Saul also went home to Gibeah, and with him went men of valor whose hearts God had touched. But certain worthless men said: How can this man save us? And they despised him and brought him no gifts. But he held his peace.

Then, about a month later, Nahash the Ammonite came up and besieged Jabesh-gilead. And all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash: Make a treaty with us, and we will serve you. And Nahash the Ammonite said to them: On this condition I will make a treaty with you, that I gouge out all your right eyes, and thus bring disgrace on all Israel. And the elders of Jabesh said to him: Give us seven days respite that we may send messengers through all the territory of Israel. Then, if there is no one to save us, we will give ourselves up to you. When the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul, they spoke these words in the hearing of the people, and all the people wept aloud. Now Saul was coming from the field behind his oxen, and Saul said: What is wrong with the people, that they are weeping? So they told him the news of the men of Jabesh. And the Spirit of God came upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger was greatly kindled. He took a yoke of oxen and cut them in pieces and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying: Whoever does not come out after Saul and Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen! Then the dread of the Lord fell upon the people, and they came out as one man. And he mustered them at Bezek. The men of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand. And they said to the messengers

Kings.

And Samuel cried out to the Lord, and the Lord sent thunder and rain that day. And all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel. And all the people said to Samuel: Pray for us to the Lord your God, that we may not die. For we have added to all our sins this evil, to ask for a king. And Samuel said to the people: Do not be afraid. You have done all this evil; yet do not turn aside from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart. And do not turn aside after empty things which cannot profit you or deliver you, for they are empty. For the Lord will not forsake his people, for his great name's sake, because it has pleased the Lord to make you his people. Moreover, as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you; and I will teach you the good and the right way. Only fear the Lord and serve him in truth with all your heart, for consider how great things he has done for you. But if you persist in wickedness, both you and your king shall be swept away.

Saul was one year old when he began to reign. [Chapter 13]
Saul reigned when he began, and after two years he reigned over Israel. And Saul chose three thousand men of Israel; two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in mount Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. And the rest of the people he sent home, every man to his tent. And Jonathan smote the garrison of the Philistines that was in Gibeah. And when the Philistines heard it, Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying: Let the Hebrews hear. And all Israel heard it said that Saul had smitten the garrison of the Philistines, and that Israel was held in abomination by the Philistines. And the people were gathered after Saul to Gilgal. And the Philistines assembled to fight against Israel, thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand

which is on the sea shore in multitude. And they came up and camped in Michmash, to the east of Beth-aven. When the men of Israel saw that they were in trouble — for the people were distressed — the people hid themselves in caves, and in thickets, and in rocks, and in high places, and in pits. And some of the Hebrews crossed over the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. And while Saul was still in Gilgal, all the people followed him trembling. And he waited seven days, according to the set time that Samuel had appointed; but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him. And Saul said: Bring here the burnt offering to me and the peace offerings. And he offered the burnt offering. And as soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, Samuel came. And Saul went out to meet him, to greet him. And Samuel said: What have you done? And Saul said: Because I saw that the people scattered from me, and that you did not come within the days appointed, and that the Philistines gathered themselves together at Michmash, I said: Now the Philistines will come down upon me to Gilgal, and I have not made supplication to the Lord. I felt compelled, and offered the burnt offering. And Samuel said to Saul: You have done foolishly. You have not kept the commandment of the Lord your God which he commanded you. For if you had, the Lord would have established your kingdom over Israel forever. But now your kingdom shall not continue. The Lord has sought for himself a man after his own heart, and the Lord has commanded him to be ruler over his people, because you have not kept what the Lord commanded you. And Samuel arose and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people that were present with him, about six hundred men. And Saul and Jonathan his son, and the people

· first ·

The young men who had been with them were at Gibeah of Benjamin. Now the Philistines had set up camp at Michmash. And three raiding parties went out from the camp of the Philistines. One company turned toward the road to Ophrah, toward the land of Shual. Another went by the road to Beth-horon. The third turned toward the road along the border overlooking the valley of Zeboim toward the desert. Now there was no blacksmith to be found throughout all the land of Israel, for the Philistines had taken care that the Hebrews could not make swords or spears. So all the Israelites went down to the Philistines to sharpen each man's plowshare, mattock, axe, and sickle. The edges of the plowshares, the mattocks, the forks, and the axes were blunted, and the goads needed to be reset. So on the day of battle neither sword nor spear was found in the hands of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan, except for Saul and his son Jonathan. The garrison of the Philistines had marched out to pass through to Michmash. Chapter fourteen.

One day Jonathan, the son of Saul, said to the young man who bore his armor: Come, let us go over to the Philistine garrison that is on the other side. But he did not tell his father. Saul was staying on the outskirts of Gibeah under the pomegranate tree that was in Migron, and the people with him were about six hundred men. And Ahijah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod's brother, the son of Phinehas, who had been born to Eli, the priest of the Lord at Shiloh, was wearing an ephod. But the people did not know that Jonathan had gone. In the pass through which Jonathan sought to cross over to the Philistine garrison, there was a rocky crag on each side, one on one side and one on the other. The name of the one was Bozez and the name of the other Seneh. One crag rose sharply to the north in front of Michmash, and the other to the south in front of Gibeah. Jonathan said to the young man who bore his armor: Come, let us cross over to the garrison of these uncircumcised. Perhaps the Lord will act for us, for nothing can hinder the Lord from saving by many or by few. His armor-bearer said to him: Do all that is in your heart. I am with you, wherever you go. Then Jonathan said: Behold, we will cross over to these men, and we will reveal ourselves to them. If they say to us, Wait until we come to you, then we will stand still in our place and not go up. But if they say, Come up to us, then we will go up, for the Lord has given them into our hand. This shall be the sign to us. Both of them showed themselves to the garrison of the Philistines. And the Philistines said: Look, Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they have hidden themselves. And the men of the garrison called out to Jonathan and his armor-bearer and said: Come up to us, and we will show you something. And Jonathan said to his armor-bearer: Come up after me, for the Lord has given them into the hands of Israel. Then Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, and his armor-bearer after him. And they fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer killed them after him. In that first slaughter Jonathan and his armor-bearer killed about twenty men within about half an acre of land. And there was a panic in the camp, in the field, and among all the garrison; even the raiders trembled. The earth quaked, and it became a very great panic. And the watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked on.

. Kings .

And behold, the panic spread: and they fled here and there. And Saul said to the one who was with him: Look and see who has gone from us. And when they had searched, it was found that Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there. And Saul said to Ahijah: Bring the ark of the Lord. For the ark of God was there on that day with the children of Israel. And while Saul was speaking to the priest, the tumult in the camp of the Philistines grew louder and louder. And Saul said to the priest: Withdraw your hand. And Saul and all the people who were with him cried out, and they came to the place of battle. And behold, every man's sword was turned against his fellow: and there was a very great slaughter. Moreover the Hebrews who had been with the Philistines yesterday and the day before, and had gone up with them into the camp, they also turned to be with the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan. Also all the men of Israel who had hidden themselves in mount Ephraim, when they heard that the Philistines fled, they joined themselves to them in the battle. And there were with Saul about ten thousand men: and the Lord saved Israel on that day. And the battle passed beyond Beth-aven. And the men of Israel were joined together on that day. And Saul put the people under oath, saying: Cursed be the man who eats any food until evening, until I have avenged myself on my enemies. So none of the people tasted any food. And all the people came into the forest, and there was honey on the ground. And Jonathan entered the forest and extended the end of the staff he had in his hand and dipped it in a honeycomb. And he turned his hand to his mouth, and his eyes were enlightened.

And one of the people answered and said: Your father strictly charged the people with an oath, saying: Cursed be the man who eats food today. And the people were faint. Then Jonathan said: My father has troubled the land. See how my eyes have been brightened because I tasted a little of this honey: how much more if the people had eaten freely of the spoil of their enemies which they found? Would not the slaughter among the Philistines have been greater? And they struck the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon. And the people were very faint. And the people flew upon the spoil and took sheep and oxen and calves and slew them on the ground: and the people ate with the blood. And they told Saul, saying: The people are sinning against the Lord, eating with the blood. And he said: You have transgressed: roll a great stone to me now. And Saul said: Disperse yourselves among the people and tell them that every man bring his ox and his sheep and slay them here, and eat; and you shall not sin against the Lord in eating with the blood. So every one of the people brought his ox with him that night and slew them there. And Saul built an altar to the Lord: and that was the first altar he built to the Lord. And Saul said: Let us go down after the Philistines by night and spoil them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man of them. And the people said: Do whatever seems good to you. Then the priest said: Let us draw near here to God. And Saul inquired of God: Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will you deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he did not answer him that day. And Saul said: Draw near here all the leaders of the people, and know and see how this sin has occurred today. As the Lord lives, who saves Israel, even if it is in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die—

retraction he would die. To which no one contradicted him in anything. And he said to all Israel: Separate yourselves on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side. And all the people answered Saul: Do what seems good to you. And he said to the Lord God of Israel: Lord God of Israel, give a clear answer; why have you not answered your servant today? If the iniquity be in me, or in Jonathan my son, give a sign; or if this iniquity be in your people, give holiness. And Jonathan and Saul were taken, but the people escaped. And Saul said: Cast lots between me and Jonathan my son. And Jonathan was taken. And Saul said to Jonathan: Tell me what you have done. And Jonathan told him and said: I tasted a little honey with the end of the rod that was in my hand, and behold I must die. And Saul said: God do so and more also, for you shall surely die, Jonathan. And the people said to Saul: Shall Jonathan die, who has wrought this great salvation in Israel? This must not be. As the Lord lives, not one hair of his head shall fall to the ground, for he has worked with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not. And Saul went up from following the Philistines, and the Philistines went to their own place. And Saul having secured the kingdom over Israel, fought against all his enemies on every side: against Moab and the children of Ammon and Edom, and the kings of Zobah and the Philistines; and wherever he turned he was victorious. And gathering an army he defeated Amalek, and delivered Israel from the hand of those who plundered them. Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan and Ishui and Melchisua; and the names of his two daughters, the name of the firstborn was Merab, and the name of the younger Michal; and the name of Saul's wife was Ahinoam the daughter of

Ahimaaz. And the name of the captain of his host was Abner the son of Ner, uncle to Saul. For Kish was the father of Saul, and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel. And there was hard war against the Philistines all the days of Saul; and whenever Saul saw any strong man, or any valiant man, he took him unto himself. Chapter XV.
And Samuel said to Saul: The Lord sent me to anoint you king over his people Israel. Now therefore listen to the voice of the Lord. Thus says the Lord of hosts: I have reckoned up what Amalek did to Israel, how he resisted him in the way when he came up from Egypt. Now therefore go and strike Amalek, and utterly destroy all that he has. Do not spare him, and do not covet anything of his, but kill both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and donkey. And Saul commanded the people and numbered them as lambs: two hundred thousand foot soldiers, and ten thousand men of Judah. And when Saul had come to the city of Amalek, he laid ambushes in the torrent. And Saul said to the Kenites: Go, depart, get down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them; for you showed kindness to all the children of Israel when they came up out of Egypt. So the Kenites departed from among the Amalekites. And Saul smote the Amalekites from Havilah until you come to Shur, which is east of Egypt. And he took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive. But all the people he put to the sword. And Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep and of the cattle, and the garments and the rams, and all that was good, and would not utterly destroy them; but everything that was vile and worthless, that they destroyed utterly. And the word of the Lord came to Samuel saying: It repents me that I have set up Saul to be king, for he has forsaken me and has not performed my words. And Samuel was grieved

. Kings .

And Samuel cried out to the Lord all night. And when Samuel rose early to go to Saul in the morning, it was told Samuel that Saul had come to Carmel, and had erected a triumphal arch for himself, and had turned and passed on, and gone down to Gilgal. And Samuel came to Saul, and Saul was offering a burnt offering to the Lord of the first fruits of the spoils which he had brought from Amalek. And when Samuel had come to Saul, Saul said to him: Blessed are you to the Lord. I have fulfilled the word of the Lord. And Samuel said: What then is this noise of the flocks which sounds in my ears, and of the herds which I hear? And Saul said: They have brought them from Amalek, for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the herds, to sacrifice to the Lord your God, and the rest we have killed. And Samuel said to Saul: Allow me, and I will tell you what the Lord has said to me this night. And he said: Speak. And Samuel said: When you were little in your own eyes, were you not made the head of the tribes of Israel? And the Lord anointed you king over Israel, and the Lord sent you on a journey, and said: Go, and kill the sinners of Amalek, and you shall fight against them until you have destroyed them. Why then did you not listen to the voice of the Lord, but turned to the spoils, and did evil in the sight of the Lord? And Saul said to Samuel: Indeed I did listen to the voice of the Lord, and I walked in the way by which the Lord sent me, and I brought back Agag the king of Amalek, and I have destroyed Amalek. But the people took of the spoils, sheep and oxen, the first fruits of those things that were slain, to offer sacrifice to the Lord their God in Gilgal. And Samuel said: Does the Lord desire burnt offerings and victims, and not rather that the voice of the Lord should be obeyed? For obedience is better than sacrifices, and to listen to him is better than to offer the fat of rams: because it is like the sin of divination to rebel, and like the crime of idolatry to refuse to obey.

Therefore, because you have rejected the word of the Lord, the Lord has also rejected you from being king. And Saul said to Samuel: I have sinned, because I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord and your words, fearing the people, and obeying their voice. But now bear my sin, I pray you, and return with me, that I may adore the Lord. And Samuel said to Saul: I will not return with you, because you have rejected the word of the Lord, and the Lord has rejected you from being king over Israel. And Samuel turned to go away, but he caught hold of the skirt of his mantle, and it tore. And Samuel said to him: The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel from you this day, and has given it to your neighbor who is better than you. And moreover the Conqueror of Israel will not spare, and will not be moved to repentance; for he is not a man, that he should repent. Then he said: I have sinned; but honor me now before the elders of my people and before Israel, and return with me, that I may worship the Lord your God. And Samuel turned back after Saul, and Saul worshipped the Lord. And Samuel said: Bring me Agag the king of Amalek. And Agag was brought to him, very fat and trembling. And Agag said: Is bitter death really here? And Samuel said: As your sword has made women childless, so your mother shall be childless among women. And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal. Then Samuel departed to Ramah, and Saul went up to his house in Gibeah. And Samuel saw Saul no more until the day of his death; nevertheless Samuel mourned for Saul, because the Lord repented that he had made Saul king over Israel. Chapter XVI.

And the Lord said to Samuel: How long will you mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil, and come, that I may send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have provided myself a king among his sons. And Samuel said:

Kings

The weight of his coat of mail was five thousand shekels of bronze, and he had bronze greaves on his legs, and a bronze shield hung between his shoulders. The shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam, and the iron head of his spear weighed six hundred shekels of iron, and his shield-bearer went before him. He cried out against the ranks of Israel and said to them: Why have you come out ready for battle? Am I not a Philistine, and are you not servants of Saul? Choose a man for yourselves and let him come down to fight me in single combat. If he is able to fight me and kill me, then we will be your servants; but if I prevail against him and kill him, then you shall be our servants and serve us. And the Philistine said: I have defied the ranks of Israel this day. Give me a man, that we may fight together. When Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, they were dismayed and greatly afraid.

Now David was the son of an Ephrathite man from Bethlehem in Judah, whose name was Jesse, and he had eight sons. In the days of Saul, this man was old and advanced in years. The three eldest sons of Jesse had followed Saul to the battle. And the names of his three sons who went to the battle were: Eliab the firstborn, and the second Abinadab, and the third Shammah. David was the youngest. The three eldest followed Saul, but David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father's flock at Bethlehem. The Philistine came forward morning and evening and presented himself for forty days.

Then Jesse said to his son David: Take now for your brothers an ephah of this parched grain and these ten loaves of bread, and run to the camp to your brothers; and bring these ten cheeses to the commander of their thousand. See how your brothers fare, and take note of those with whom they are assigned. Now Saul and they and all the men of Israel were in the valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.

So David rose early in the morning, and left the flock with a keeper, and took the provisions and went, as Jesse had commanded him. He came to the encampment as the army was going out to the battle line, shouting the war cry. Israel and the Philistines drew up their battle lines facing each other. David left his baggage in the care of the keeper of the supplies, ran to the battle line, and came and greeted his brothers. While he talked with them, the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, came up out of the ranks of the Philistines and spoke the same words as before. And David heard him.

All the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him and were greatly afraid. The men of Israel said: Have you seen this man who has come up? Surely he has come up to defy Israel. The king will enrich with great riches the man who kills him, and will give him his daughter and make his father's house free in Israel.

And David said to the men who stood by him: What shall be done for the man who kills this Philistine and takes away the reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God? The people told him the same thing again. Now Eliab, his eldest brother, heard when he spoke to the men, and Eliab's anger was kindled against David. He said: Why have you come down? And with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your presumption and the evil of your heart, for you have come down to see the battle. David said: What have I done? Is there not a reason? And he turned away from him to another and spoke in the same way.

First [book]

And the words which David spoke were heard and reported before Saul. And when he had been brought to him, David spoke to him. Let no man's heart be troubled because of him. I your servant will go and fight against this Philistine. And Saul said to David: You are not able to withstand this Philistine, nor to fight against him, for you are but a youth, and he has been a warrior from his youth. And David said to Saul: Your servant kept his father's flock, and there came a lion or a bear, and took a ram out of the midst of the flock. And I pursued them and struck them, and delivered it out of their mouth. And they rose up against me, and I caught them by the throat, and I choked and killed them. For both a lion and a bear have I slain, I your servant. This uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them. Now I will go and take away the reproach of the people. For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, who has dared to curse the army of the living God? And David said: The Lord who delivered me from the paw of the lion and from the paw of the bear, he will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said to David: Go, and the Lord be with you. And Saul clothed David with his own garments, and put a helmet of bronze upon his head, and clothed him with a coat of mail. And David girded his sword over his garments, and began to try whether he could walk in the armor, for he was not accustomed to it. And David said to Saul: I cannot walk in these, for I am not used to them. And he put them off. And he took his staff in his hand, which he always had with him, and chose himself five smooth stones from the brook, and put them in a shepherd's bag which he had with him, and with his sling in his hand he advanced toward the Philistine. And the Philistine came on, drawing near to David, and his armor-bearer

went before him. And when the Philistine looked and saw David, he despised him. For he was a young man, ruddy and of a fair countenance. And the Philistine said to David: Am I a dog, that you come to me with a staff? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods. And he said to David: Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the air and to the beasts of the field. Then David said to the Philistine: You come to me with a sword and with a spear and with a shield, but I come to you in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied this day. And the Lord will deliver you into my hand, and I will strike you and take your head from you. And I will give the bodies of the camp of the Philistines this day to the birds of the air and to the wild beasts of the earth, that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel. And all this assembly shall know that the Lord does not save with sword and spear, for the battle is the Lord's, and he will deliver you into our hands. And when the Philistine arose and came and drew near to meet David, David hastened and ran toward the battle line to meet the Philistine. And he put his hand into his bag and took out a stone and slung it, and struck the Philistine on his forehead. And the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground. So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and struck the Philistine and killed him. There was no sword in the hand of David. But David ran and stood over the Philistine and took his sword and drew it out of its sheath and killed him, and cut off his head with it. And when the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they fled. And the men of Israel and Judah rose up with a shout and pursued the Philistines as far as the valley and to the gates of Ekron. And the slain of the Philistines fell along the road to Shaaraim, even to Gath and

. Kings .

...as far as Ekron. And the children of Israel, returning after they had pursued the Philistines, plundered their camp. And David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem, but he put his armor in his tent. Now when Saul had seen David going out against the Philistine, he said to Abner, the captain of the army: "Of what family is this young man descended?" And Abner said: "As your soul lives, O king, I do not know." And the king said: "Ask whose son this young man is." And when David returned, having slain the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul, with the head of the Philistine in his hand. And Saul said to him: "Young man, of what family are you?" And David said: "I am the son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite."

And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking to Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul. And Saul took him that day and would not let him return to his father's house. Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul. And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was upon him and gave it to David, and his garments, even to his sword and to his bow and to his belt. And David went out wherever Saul sent him, and he behaved wisely; and Saul set him over the men of war, and he was accepted in the sight of all the people, and also in the sight of Saul's servants. Now it came to pass as they came, when David was returning from the slaughter of the Philistine, and when he brought the head to Jerusalem, that the women came out of all the cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet king Saul, with tambourines, with joy, and with instruments of music. And the women answered one another as they played, and said: "Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands." And Saul was very angry, and this saying displeased him.

And he said: "They have attributed ten thousands to David, and to me they have attributed only thousands; what more can he have but the kingdom?" And Saul viewed David with suspicion from that day forward. And on the next day an evil spirit from God came upon Saul, and he prophesied in the midst of his house. And David played with his hand, as at other times. And Saul held a spear, and he cast it, thinking he would pin David to the wall. But David avoided his presence twice. And Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was with him, and had departed from Saul. Therefore Saul removed him from him and made him a captain over a thousand; and he went out and came in before the people. And David behaved wisely in all his ways, and the Lord was with him. And when Saul saw that he was very wise, he was afraid of him. But all Israel and Judah loved David, for he went out and came in before them. And Saul said to David: "Behold, my older daughter Merab, I will give her to you as a wife; only be a valiant man for me and fight the Lord's battles." For Saul thought: "Let not my hand be upon him, but let the hand of the Philistines be upon him." And David said to Saul: "Who am I? And what is my life, or my father's family in Israel, that I should be son-in-law to the king?" But it came to pass at the time when Merab, Saul's daughter, should have been given to David, that she was given to Adriel the Meholathite as a wife. Now Michal, Saul's other daughter, loved David; and they told Saul, and the thing pleased him. And Saul said: "I will give her to him, that she may be a snare to him, and that the hand of the Philistines may be against him." And Saul said to David: "You shall be my son-in-law today in one of these two things." And Saul commanded his servants: "Speak to David secretly, saying: 'Behold, the king delights in you, and all his servants love you; now therefore be the king's son-in-law.'" And they spoke

· First ·                                                                                                                    140·

all these words were spoken in the hearing of Saul's servants. And David said: Does it seem to you a small thing to be the king's son-in-law? I am a poor man and of little means. And Saul's servants reported to him, saying: David spoke such words as these. And Saul said: Say these things to David: The king desires no dowry except a hundred foreskins of the Philistines, for revenge on the king's enemies. Now Saul planned to hand David over to the Philistines. When his servants reported these words to David, it pleased David to become the king's son-in-law. After a few days David set out and went with his men and struck down two hundred Philistines, and he brought their foreskins and counted them out before the king, so that he might be the king's son-in-law. Saul then gave him his daughter Michal as a wife. And Saul saw and understood that the Lord was with David. And Michal, the daughter of Saul, loved him. And Saul began to fear David even more. And Saul became David's enemy for all his days. The princes of the Philistines went out, and from the beginning of their campaigns David conducted himself more wisely than all of Saul's men, and his name became very famous. Chapter XIX.

And Saul spoke to his son Jonathan and to all his servants, that they should kill David. But Jonathan, Saul's son, loved David greatly. And Jonathan told David, saying: Saul my father is seeking to kill you. Therefore watch yourself in the morning, and stay hidden. I will go out and stand beside my father in the field wherever he may be, and I will speak to my father about you, and whatever I see I will tell you. And Jonathan spoke well of David to Saul his father, and said to him: Let not the king sin against his servant David, for he has not sinned against you, and his deeds have been very good toward you. He put his life in his own hand and struck down the Philistine, and the Lord brought about a great victory for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced. Why then would you sin against innocent blood by killing David, who is without fault? When Saul heard this, he was appeased, and he swore: As the Lord lives, he shall not be put to death. So Jonathan called David and told him all these things. And Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence as he had been before. But war broke out again, and David went out and fought against the Philistines, and he struck them with a great blow, and they fled before him. But an evil spirit from the Lord came upon Saul. He was sitting in his house with his spear in hand, while David was playing music. And Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear. But David stepped aside from before Saul, and the spear struck the wall, and David fled and escaped that night. Saul then sent his officers to David's house to watch him, so they might kill him in the morning. But Michal, David's wife, told him: If you do not save your life tonight, tomorrow you will be dead. So she let him down through the window, and he fled and escaped and was saved. Then Michal took a household idol and laid it on the bed, and placed a covering of goat's hair at its head, and covered it with clothes. When Saul sent messengers to seize David, she said he was sick. And Saul sent messengers again to see David, saying: Bring him to me in his bed so that he may be killed. And when the messengers came in, they found the idol on the bed with the goat's hair cover at its head. And Saul said to Michal: Why

. Kings .

"Thus you have mocked me and let my enemy escape?" And Michal answered Saul, "Because he said to me, 'Let me go, or I will kill you.'" So David fled and was safe. And he came to Samuel at Ramah and told him all that Saul had done to him. And they went, he and Samuel, and stayed in Naioth. And it was told to Saul, saying, "Behold, David is at Naioth in Ramah." So Saul sent messengers to take David. And when they saw the company of prophets prophesying, with Samuel standing as head over them, the Spirit of God came upon the messengers of Saul, and they also prophesied. When this was told to Saul, he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. And again Saul sent a third group of messengers, and they also prophesied. Then Saul himself went to Ramah and came to the great cistern that is in Sechu. And he asked, saying, "Where are Samuel and David?" And one said, "Behold, they are at Naioth in Ramah." And he went to Naioth in Ramah. And the Spirit of God came upon him also, and he went on, and prophesied until he came to Naioth in Ramah. And he too stripped off his clothes, and he also prophesied before Samuel, and lay naked all that day and night. Therefore they say, "Is Saul also among the prophets?" Chapter 20.
David fled from Naioth in Ramah and came and spoke before Jonathan, "What have I done? What is my iniquity, and what is my sin before your father, that he seeks my life?" And he said to him, "Far from it! You shall not die. Behold, my father does nothing either great or small without revealing it to me. Why would my father hide this from me? It is not so." But David swore moreover, and said, "Your father knows well that I have found favor in your sight, and he thinks, 'Let not Jonathan know this, lest he be grieved.' But truly, as the Lord lives and as your soul lives, there is but one step between me and death." Then Jonathan said to David, "Whatever you say, I will do for it for you." And David said to Jonathan, "Behold, tomorrow is the new moon, and I should sit with the king at dinner. But let me go, that I may hide in the field until the third evening. If your father misses me at all, then say, 'David earnestly asked leave of me to run to Bethlehem his city, for there is a yearly sacrifice there for all the clan.' If he says, 'It is well,' your servant will be safe. But if he is angry, know that harm is determined by him. Therefore deal kindly with your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of the Lord with you. But if there is iniquity in me, kill me yourself, for why should you bring me to your father?" And Jonathan said, "Far be it from me! For if I knew that harm was determined by my father to come upon you, would I not tell you?" Then David said to Jonathan, "Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?" And Jonathan said to David, "Come, let us go out into the field." And when they had gone out into the field, Jonathan said to David, "O Lord, the God of Israel! When I have sounded out my father about this time tomorrow, or the third day, and if it is well with David, and I do not send to you and make it known to you, may the Lord do so to Jonathan and more also. But if my father intends to do you harm, I will make it known to you and send you away, that you may go in peace. And may the Lord be with you as he has been with my father. And if

"I have lived, you have shown me the kindnesses of the Lord; but if I die, do not cut off your kindness from my house forever. And if I do not act — when the Lord has cut off every one of David's enemies from the face of the earth — let Jonathan be cut off from the house of David, and may the Lord require it from the hand of David's enemies." So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, and Jonathan caused David to swear again, because he loved him, for he loved him as he loved his own soul. And Jonathan said to him, "Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed, because your seat will be empty. Stay until the day after tomorrow, and come to the place where you hid on the day of the deed, and sit by the stone called Ezel. I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, as though I were shooting at a mark. I will then send the boy, saying, 'Go find the arrows.' If I say to the boy, 'Look, the arrows are on this side of you, pick them up,' then come, for there is peace for you and nothing wrong, as the Lord lives. But if I say to the youth, 'Look, the arrows are beyond you,' go, for the Lord has sent you away. As for the matter you and I have spoken of, may the Lord be between you and me forever."

So David hid himself in the field. When the new moon came, the king sat down to eat bread. The king sat in his customary seat by the wall, and Jonathan sat opposite him, and Abner sat beside Saul; but David's place was empty. Saul said nothing that day, for he thought, "Something has happened to him; he is not clean, he has not been purified." But on the second day, the day after the new moon, David's place was empty again. Saul said to Jonathan his son, "Why has the son of Jesse not come to the meal, either yesterday or today?"

Jonathan answered Saul, "David earnestly asked me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, 'Let me go, for our family is holding a sacrifice in the city, and my brother has summoned me. Now if I have found favor in your eyes, let me get away and see my brothers.'" That is why he has not come to the king's table. Then Saul's anger was kindled against Jonathan, and he said to him, "You son of a perverse and rebellious woman! Don't I know that you have chosen the son of Jesse to your own shame, and to the shame of your mother's nakedness? For as long as the son of Jesse lives on the earth, neither you nor your kingdom will be established. Now send and fetch him to me, for he shall surely die."

Jonathan answered his father Saul, "Why should he be put to death? What has he done?" But Saul hurled his spear at him to strike him. So Jonathan knew that his father was determined to put David to death. Jonathan rose from the table in fierce anger and ate no food the second day of the month, for he was grieved for David, because his father had shamed him.

In the morning Jonathan went out into the field at the time appointed with David, and a small boy was with him. He said to his boy, "Run and find the arrows that I shoot." As the boy ran, he shot an arrow beyond him. When the boy came to the place of the arrow that Jonathan had shot, Jonathan called after the boy, "Is not the arrow beyond you?" And Jonathan called after the boy, "Hurry, be quick, do not stop!" Jonathan's boy gathered up the arrows and came to his master, but the boy knew nothing; only Jonathan and David knew the matter. Jonathan gave his weapons to his boy and said to him, "Go and carry them to the city." And when the boy had gone —

· Kings ·

When the boy had gone, David rose from the place that faced south, and falling on his face to the ground, bowed three times. And kissing each other they wept together, but David more so. And Jonathan said to David: Go in peace. As for the things which we two have sworn in the name of the Lord, saying: The Lord be between me and thee, and between my seed and thy seed forever. And David arose and departed, and Jonathan also went into the city. Chapter XXI.

And David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. And Ahimelech was astonished at David's coming, and said to him: Why are you alone, and no man with you? And David said to Ahimelech the priest: The king has commanded me a business, and said to me: Let no man know the thing for which thou art sent by me, and what manner of commands I have given thee: for I have appointed my servants to such and such a place. Now therefore if thou have any thing at hand, though it were but five loaves of bread, give me, or whatever thou canst find. And the priest answering David, said to him: I have no common bread at hand, but only holy bread, if the young men, especially the women, have been kept from. And David answered the priest and said to him: Truly, as to the matter of women, we have kept ourselves from yesterday and the day before, when we came out, and the vessels of the young men were holy. And this way is defiled, but it shall also be sanctified this day in the vessels. So the priest gave him hallowed bread: for there was no bread there, but only the loaves of proposition, which had been taken away from before the Lord, that hot loaves might be set up. Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day within the tabernacle of the Lord, and his name was Doeg the Edomite, the chiefest of the herdsmen of Saul. And he kept the mules of Saul. And David said to Ahimelech: If thou have here at hand a spear or a sword, give it to me; for I brought not my sword nor my arms with me, for the king's business required haste. And the priest said: Behold here the sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom thou didst kill in the valley of Terebinth, wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod: if thou wilt take this, take it, for there is no other but this here. And David said: There is none like that: give it me. And David arose and fled that day from the face of Saul, and came to Achish king of Gath. And the servants of Achish said to him, when they saw David: Is not this David the king of the land? Did they not sing to him in their dances saying: Saul slew his thousands, and David his ten thousands? And David laid up these words in his heart, and was very much afraid of Achish king of Gath. And he changed his countenance before them, and slipped down between their hands: and he stumbled against the doors of the gate, and his spittle ran down upon his beard. And Achish said to his servants: You saw the man was mad: why have you brought him to me? Do we need madmen, that you have brought in this fellow to be mad in my presence? Should this fellow come into my house? Chapter XXII.

David therefore departed from thence, and fled to the cave of Adullam. And when his brethren and all his father's house heard it, they went down to him thither. And all that were in distress, and oppressed with debt, and discontented, gathered together to him, and he became their captain: and there were with him about four hundred men. And David went from thence to Mizpeh of Moab: and he said to the king of Moab: Let my father and my mother, I beseech thee, remain with you till I know what God will do for me. And he left them before the king of Moab: and they abode with him all the days that David was in the hold. And the prophet Gad said

. first.

to David. "Do not stay in the stronghold. Go and depart into the land of Judah." And David departed and came to the forest of Hareth. And Saul heard that David had appeared, and the men who were with him. Now Saul was staying in Gibeah, and he was in the grove which is in Ramah, holding a spear, and all his servants were standing around him. And he said to his servants who stood about him: "Hear me, you sons of Benjamin. Will the son of Jesse give all of you fields and vineyards, and make you all commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds? For you have all conspired against me, and there is no one who informs me when my son has made a covenant with the son of Jesse. Not one of you is sorry for me, nor tells me, since my son has stirred up my servant against me to lie in wait, as he does today." Then Doeg the Edomite, who stood by the servants of Saul, answered and said: "I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub the priest. And he consulted the Lord for him, and gave him provisions, and also gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine." Then the king sent to call Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father's house, the priests who were at Nob. And they all came to the king. And Saul said to Ahimelech: "Hear me, son of Ahitub." He answered: "Here I am, my lord." And Saul said to him: "Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, in that you have given him bread and a sword, and have inquired of God for him, so that he should rise against me and lie in wait, as he does today?" Then Ahimelech answered the king and said: "And who among all your servants is so faithful as David, who is also the king's son-in-law, and is honored in your house? Did I just begin to inquire of God for him today? Far be it from me. Let not the king impute anything against his servant."

He said nothing of all this matter, more or less. Then the king said: "You shall surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father's house." And the king said to the guards who stood about him: "Turn and kill the priests of the Lord, because their hand also is with David, and because they knew when he fled and did not tell me." But the servants of the king would not put out their hands to strike the priests of the Lord. And the king said to Doeg: "You turn and strike the priests." And Doeg the Edomite turned and struck the priests, and he killed on that day eighty-five persons who wore a linen ephod. And Nob, the city of the priests, he struck with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and infants, oxen and donkeys and sheep, with the edge of the sword. And one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped and fled after David. And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the Lord. And David said to Abiathar: "I knew that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul. I have caused the death of all the persons of your father's house. Stay with me, and do not fear, for he who seeks my life seeks your life. You shall be safe with me." Chapter XXIII.

Then they told David: "Behold, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah and are robbing the threshing floors." David inquired of the Lord, saying: "Shall I go and attack these Philistines?" And the Lord said to David: "Go and attack the Philistines and save Keilah." But David's men said to him: "Behold, we are afraid here in Judah; how much more then if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?" Then David inquired of the Lord again. And he answered him and said: "Arise, go down to Keilah, for I will

· Kings ·

"I will deliver the Philistines into your hand." So David and his men went to Keilah and fought against the Philistines and drove away their livestock and struck them with a great blow, and David saved the inhabitants of Keilah. Now at the time when Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, he had brought down the ephod with him. It was reported to Saul that David had come to Keilah. And Saul said, "God has delivered him into my hands, for he has shut himself in by entering a city that has gates and bars." And Saul summoned all the people to go down to Keilah to besiege David and his men. When David learned that Saul was plotting evil against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod." And David said, "O Lord God of Israel, your servant has surely heard that Saul seeks to come to Keilah to destroy the city on my account. Will the men of Keilah deliver me into his hands? Will Saul come down as your servant has heard? O Lord God of Israel, tell your servant." And the Lord said, "He will come down." Then David asked again, "Will the men of Keilah deliver me and my men into the hands of Saul?" And the Lord said, "They will deliver you." Then David and his men, about six hundred, arose and departed from Keilah and wandered wherever they could. When Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah, he abandoned the expedition. David remained in the strongholds in the wilderness, and stayed in the hill country of the wilderness of Ziph. Saul sought him every day, but God did not deliver him into his hands. David saw that Saul had come out to seek his life. David was in the wilderness of Ziph in a wood, and Jonathan, Saul's son, arose and went to David in the wood and strengthened his hand in God and said to him:

"Do not be afraid, for the hand of Saul my father shall not find you. You shall reign over Israel, and I shall be next to you. Even Saul my father knows this." And the two of them made a covenant before the Lord. David remained in the wood, and Jonathan went home. Then the Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah, saying, "David is hiding among us in the strongholds of the wood, on the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south of the wasteland. Now come down, O king, whenever you desire to come down; and our part shall be to deliver him into the king's hand." Saul said, "May you be blessed by the Lord, for you have had compassion on me. Go now and make further preparation: find out and see the place where his foot is, and who has seen him there, for I am told he is very cunning. Look and learn all the hiding places where he hides, and come back to me with sure information, and I will go with you. And if he is in the land, I will search him out among all the thousands of Judah." They arose and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. Now David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah to the south of Jeshimon. And Saul and his men went to seek him. David was told, and he went down to the rock and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. When Saul heard this, he pursued David into the wilderness of Maon. Saul was going on one side of the mountain, and David and his men were on the other side of the mountain. David was hurrying to get away from Saul, while Saul and his men were closing in on David and his men to capture them. But a messenger came to Saul, saying, "Hurry and come, for the Philistines have invaded the land." So Saul turned back from pursuing

. first .

And David went out to meet the Philistines. For this reason they called that place the Rock of Division. Chapter 24.
David therefore went up from there and dwelt in the strongholds of En-gedi. When Saul returned after pursuing the Philistines, they told him, saying: Behold, David is in the wilderness of En-gedi. Then Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel, and went to seek David and his men upon the most rugged rocks, which are accessible only to wild goats. And he came to the sheepfolds along the way, where there was a cave; and Saul went in to relieve himself. Now David and his men were sitting in the innermost parts of the cave. And the men of David said to him: Behold, this is the day of which the Lord said to you: I will deliver your enemy into your hand, that you may do to him as it shall seem good in your eyes. Then David arose and cut off the skirt of Saul's robe silently. After this, David's heart struck him, because he had cut off the skirt of Saul's robe. And he said to his men: The Lord forbid that I should do this thing to my master, the Lord's anointed, to put forth my hand against him, seeing he is the anointed of the Lord. As the Lord lives, unless the Lord shall strike him, or his day shall come to die, or he shall go down into battle and perish: the Lord be merciful to me, that I put not forth my hand against the Lord's anointed. So David restrained his servants with these words and did not permit them to rise against Saul. Then Saul rose from the cave and went on his way. David also arose afterward and went out of the cave and cried after Saul, saying: My lord the king. And Saul looked behind him: and David bowing himself to the ground, worshipped. And he said to Saul: Why do you listen to the words of men who say that David seeks your harm? Behold, this day

your eyes have seen how that the Lord delivered you into my hand in the cave: and someone urged me to kill you, but my eye spared you; and I said: I will not put forth my hand against my lord, for he is the Lord's anointed. Moreover, my father, see and recognize the skirt of your robe in my hand: for when I cut off the skirt of your robe, I did not kill you. Know and see that there is no evil or transgression in my hand, and I have not sinned against you; yet you hunt my soul to take it. The Lord judge between me and you, and the Lord avenge me on you: but my hand shall not be against you, as the ancient proverb says: From the wicked comes wickedness. But my hand shall not be against you. After whom does the king of Israel come out? Whom do you pursue? A dead dog? A single flea? The Lord therefore be judge and decide between me and you: and see and judge my cause, and deliver me out of your hand. When David had made an end of speaking these words to Saul, Saul said: Is this your voice, my son David? And Saul lifted up his voice and wept. And he said to David: You are more righteous than I: for you have rewarded me with good, whereas I have rewarded you with evil. And you have shown this day what good you have done to me: how the Lord delivered me into your hand, and you have not killed me. For who when he has found his enemy, will let him go away safely? So the Lord reward you with good for what you have done to me this day. And now I know that you shall surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in your hand. Swear to me therefore by the Lord, that you will not destroy my descendants after me, nor blot out my name from my father's house. And David swore to Saul. And Saul went home; and David and his men went up to stronger positions.

. Kings .

Now Samuel died, and all Israel assembled and mourned for him greatly, and they buried him in his house at Ramah. Then David arose and went down to the wilderness of Paran.

There was a man in the wilderness of Maon whose property was in Carmel, and the man was very great; he had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats. And it came about that he was shearing his sheep in Carmel. The name of the man was Nabal, and the name of his wife was Abigail. She was a woman of good understanding and beautiful in appearance, but the man was harsh and evil in his dealings. He was of the house of Caleb.

When David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep, he sent ten young men, and David said to the young men, "Go up to Carmel, visit Nabal, and greet him in my name. Say to him: Peace be to you, peace to your house, and peace to all that you have. I have heard that you are shearing. Now your shepherds have been with us; we did not harm them, nor was anything missing from their flock all the days they were in Carmel. Ask your young men and they will tell you. Therefore let my young men find favor in your eyes, for we come on a good day. Please give whatever you can to your servants and to your son David."

When David's young men came, they spoke all these words to Nabal in David's name, and then waited. But Nabal answered David's servants and said, "Who is David? Who is the son of Jesse? There are many servants nowadays who are breaking away from their masters. Shall I then take my bread and my water and my meat that I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give it to men who come from I do not know where?" So David's young men turned away and came back, and told him all these words.

And they reported to him all the words that Nabal had spoken. Then David said to his men, "Every man strap on his sword." And every man strapped on his sword, and David also strapped on his sword. About four hundred men went up with David, while two hundred stayed with the supplies.

Now Abigail, Nabal's wife, was told by one of the young men, "David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, but he scorned them. Yet the men were very good to us; we were not harmed, and we did not miss anything all the days we went about with them in the fields. They were a wall to us both by night and by day, all the days we were with them keeping the sheep. Now therefore consider what you will do, for evil is determined against our master and against all his household. He is such a worthless man that no one can speak to him."

Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five sheep already dressed, five measures of roasted grain, one hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred fig cakes, and loaded them on donkeys. She said to her young men, "Go on before me; I am coming after you." But she did not tell her husband Nabal.

As she came down on her donkey into a mountain ravine, David and his men were coming down toward her, and she met them. David had said, "Surely in vain I have protected all that belongs to this man in the wilderness, so that nothing of his was missing. He has repaid me evil for good. May God do so to the enemies of David and more also, if by morning I leave even one male of all who belong to him."

When Abigail saw David, she hurried and dismounted from her donkey, and fell before David on her face.

. first .

She fell on her face to the ground and bowed before him, and fell at his feet, and said: Upon me, my lord, be this iniquity. Let your handmaid speak, I pray, in your ears, and hear the words of your servant. Let not my lord the king set his heart upon this wicked man Nabal, for his name matches him — Fool is his name, and folly is with him. But I, your handmaid, did not see my lord's servants whom you sent. Now therefore, my lord, as the Lord lives and as your soul lives, who has kept you from coming into bloodshed and saving your own hand — now let your enemies be as Nabal, and those who seek evil against my lord. And now accept this blessing which your handmaid has brought to my lord, and let it be given to the young men who follow my lord. And take away the iniquity of your handmaid. For the Lord will certainly make my lord a sure house, because my lord fights the battles of the Lord, and evil has not been found in you all your days. And if a man rises to pursue you and to seek your life, the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life with the Lord your God. But the souls of your enemies he shall sling out as from the hollow of a sling. And when the Lord has done for you all the good things he has spoken concerning you, and has appointed you ruler over Israel, this shall be no grief to my lord, nor offense of heart, that you shed innocent blood or that my lord avenge himself. And when the Lord has dealt well with my lord, remember your handmaid. And David said to Abigail: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel who sent you this day to meet me, and blessed be your speech, and blessed be you, who have kept me this day from coming to shed blood and from avenging myself with my own hand. For in very deed, as the Lord God of Israel lives, who has kept me from hurting you, unless you had hastened and come to meet me, there would not have been left to Nabal by the morning light any male. So David received from her hand what she had brought him, and said to her: Go in peace to your house; I have listened to your words and have granted your request. And Abigail came to Nabal, and behold, he was holding a feast in his house like the feast of a king, and Nabal's heart was merry within him, for he was very drunk; so she told him nothing at all until the morning light. And in the morning, when the wine had gone out of Nabal, his wife told him these things. And his heart died within him, and he became like a stone. And about ten days later, the Lord struck Nabal, and he died. And when David heard that Nabal was dead, he said: Blessed be the Lord who has avenged the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and has kept his servant from evil; and the Lord has returned the wickedness of Nabal upon his own head. And David sent and spoke to Abigail, to take her as his wife. And the servants of David came to Abigail at Carmel, and spoke to her, saying: David has sent us to you to take you as his wife. And she rose and bowed with her face to the ground, and said: Behold, your handmaid is a servant to wash the feet of the servants of my lord. And Abigail rose quickly and mounted a donkey, and five of her maids attended her; and she followed the messengers of David, and became his wife. David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel, and both of them became his wives. But Saul had given Michal his daughter, David's wife, to Palti the son of Laish, who was from Gallim. Chapter 26.

Then the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, saying: Behold, David is hiding...

Kings.

He was on the hill of Hachilah, which faces the wilderness. And Saul rose and went down to the desert of Ziph, and with him three thousand chosen men of Israel, to seek David in the desert of Ziph. And Saul encamped in the hill of Hachilah, which faces the wilderness by the way. But David dwelt in the desert. When he saw that Saul had come after him into the desert, he sent out spies and learned that he had certainly come there. And David rose and came to the place where Saul was camped. And when David saw the place where Saul lay, and Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host, and Saul lying within the camp and the rest of the people round about him, David said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, saying: Who will go down with me to Saul in the camp? And Abishai said: I will go down with you. So David and Abishai went to the people by night, and they found Saul lying asleep within the camp, with his spear stuck in the ground at his head; and Abner and the people lay round about him. Then Abishai said to David: God has given your enemy into your hand this day. Now therefore let me strike him with the spear to the ground with one stroke, and I will not need to strike him a second time. But David said to Abishai: Do not destroy him, for who can put forth his hand against the Lord's anointed and be guiltless? And David said: As the Lord lives, the Lord shall strike him, or his day shall come to die, or he shall go down into battle and perish. The Lord forbid that I should put forth my hand against the Lord's anointed. But take now the spear that is at his head and the cruse of water, and let us go. So David took the spear and the cruse of water from beside Saul's head, and they departed; and no man saw it, nor knew it, nor did any awake, for they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from the Lord had fallen upon them. And when David had crossed over to the other side and stood on the top of the mountain far off, with a great distance between them, David called out to the people and to Abner the son of Ner, saying: Do you not answer, Abner? And Abner answered and said: Who are you who calls out to the king? And David said to Abner: Are you not a man? And who is like you in Israel? Why then have you not guarded your lord the king? For one of the people came in to destroy the king your lord. This thing is not good that you have done. As the Lord lives, you are worthy to die, because you have not kept watch over your lord, the Lord's anointed. And now see where the king's spear is, and the cruse of water that was at his head. And Saul recognized David's voice and said: Is this your voice, my son David? And David said: It is my voice, my lord, O king. And he said: Why does my lord pursue his servant? What have I done, or what evil is in my hand? Now therefore, I pray you, let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the Lord has stirred you up against me, let him accept an offering; but if it is the sons of men, they are cursed before the Lord, who have driven me out this day so that I should have no share in the inheritance of the Lord, saying: Go, serve other gods. And now let not my blood fall to the earth before the Lord, for the king of Israel has come out to seek a flea, as when one hunts a partridge in the mountains. And Saul said: I have sinned. Return, my son David, for I will do you no more harm, because my life was precious in your eyes this day. Behold, I have acted foolishly and have made a very great mistake. And David answered and said: Here is the king's spear; let one of the young men come over and take it. The Lord rewards every man according to his righteousness and his faithfulness. For the Lord delivered you into my hand today, but I would not put forth my hand

my soul in the Lord. And just as my life was magnified today in your eyes, so let my soul be magnified in the eyes of the Lord, and let him deliver me from all distress. Then Saul said to David: Blessed are you, my son David, and you will surely do great things and prevail. Chapter 27. And David said in his heart: One day I shall fall into the hand of Saul. It is better that I escape into the land of the Philistines, so that Saul may despair of seeking me in all the borders of Israel, and I may escape out of his hand. So David arose and went, he and the six hundred men with him, to Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath. And David dwelt with Achish at Gath, he and his men, each with his household; David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite. And it was told Saul that David had fled to Gath, and he sought no more for him. Then David said to Achish: If I have found favor in your eyes, let a place be given me in one of the cities of the region, that I may dwell there; for why should your servant dwell in the royal city with you? So Achish gave him Ziklag that day; therefore Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day. The time that David dwelt in the country of the Philistines was four full months. And David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites; for these were the inhabitants of the land from of old, as you go to Shur, as far as the land of Egypt. And David smote the land, and left neither man nor woman alive, and took away the sheep, the oxen, the donkeys, the camels, and the clothing, and came back to Achish. And Achish would ask: Where have you raided today? And David would say: Against the Negeb of Judah, and against the Negeb of the Jerahmeelites, and against the Negeb of the Kenites. But David saved neither man nor woman alive to bring them to Gath, saying: Lest they tell about us. This was David's practice all the while he dwelt in the country of the Philistines. And Achish trusted David, thinking: He has made himself utterly abhorrent to his people Israel; therefore he shall be my servant forever. Chapter 28. In those days the Philistines gathered their forces for war, to fight against Israel. And Achish said to David: Know for certain that you and your men are to go out with me in the army. And David said to Achish: Very well, you shall know what your servant can do. And Achish said to David: Then I will make you my bodyguard for life. Now Samuel had died, and all Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, his own city. And Saul had put the mediums and the wizards out of the land. The Philistines assembled and came and encamped at Shunem. And Saul gathered all Israel, and they encamped at Gilboa. When Saul saw the army of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly. And when Saul inquired of the Lord, the Lord did not answer him, either by dreams, or by the priests, or by the prophets. Then Saul said to his servants: Seek out for me a woman who is a medium, that I may go to her and inquire of her. And his servants said to him: Behold, there is a medium at En-dor. So Saul disguised himself and put on other garments, and went, he and two men with him; and they came to the woman by night. And he said: Divine for me by a spirit, and bring up for me whomever I shall name to you. The woman said to him: Surely you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off

. Kings .

How he had driven out soothsayers and diviners from the land. Why then do you lay a snare for my life, to bring about my death? And Saul swore to her by the Lord, saying: As the Lord lives, no harm shall come to you for this thing. And the woman said to him: Whom shall I bring up for you? And he said: Bring up Samuel for me. But when the woman saw Samuel, she cried out with a loud voice and said to Saul: Why have you deceived me? For you are Saul. And the king said to her: Do not be afraid. What did you see? And the woman said to Saul: I saw gods coming up out of the earth. And he said to her: What form is he of? And she said: An old man comes up, and he is covered with a mantle. And Saul perceived that it was Samuel, and he bowed with his face to the ground and worshiped. And Samuel said to Saul: Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up? And Saul said: I am greatly distressed. For the Philistines fight against me, and God has departed from me, and answers me no more, neither by prophets nor by dreams. Therefore I have called you, that you may make known to me what I shall do. And Samuel said: Why do you ask me, seeing that the Lord has departed from you and become your enemy? The Lord has done to you as he spoke by my hand, and has torn the kingdom out of your hand and given it to your neighbor David, because you did not obey the voice of the Lord and did not carry out his fierce wrath against Amalek. Therefore the Lord has done this thing to you this day. And the Lord will give Israel also with you into the hand of the Philistines. Tomorrow you and your sons shall be with me, and the Lord will give the army of Israel also into the hand of the Philistines. Then Saul fell immediately full length upon the ground, for he was terrified because of Samuel's words. And there was no strength in him, for he had eaten nothing all that day. And the woman came to Saul and she was troubled. And she said to him: Behold, your handmaid has obeyed your voice, and I have risked my life

and heeded the words that you spoke to me. Now therefore, you also listen to your handmaid: let me set a morsel of bread before you, that you may eat and have strength for your journey. But he refused and said: I will not eat. But his servants, together with the woman, urged him, and he listened to their voice. So he arose from the earth and sat upon the bed. Now the woman had a fatted calf in the house, and she quickly killed it, and she took flour and kneaded it and baked unleavened bread, and she put it before Saul and before his servants. And when they had eaten, they rose and went away that night. Chapter 29.

Now the Philistines gathered all their forces at Aphek, and Israel encamped by the spring that is in Jezreel. As the lords of the Philistines were passing on by hundreds and thousands, and David and his men were passing on in the rear with Achish, the commanders of the Philistines said: What are these Hebrews doing here? And Achish said to the commanders of the Philistines: Is this not David, the servant of Saul, king of Israel, who has been with me now for days and years, and since he deserted to me I have found no fault in him to this day? But the commanders of the Philistines were angry with him and said to him: Send the man back, that he may return to his place where you have assigned him. He must not go down with us into battle, lest in the battle he become an adversary to us. For how could this fellow reconcile himself to his lord? Would it not be with the heads of the men here? Is not this David, of whom they sing to one another in dances: Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands? Then Achish called David and said to him: As the Lord lives, you have been honest, and to me it seems right that you go out and come in with me in the campaign.

· first ·

And I have found no evil in you from the day you came to me until this day, but you do not please the lords. Return therefore and go in peace, and do not offend the eyes of the lords of the Philistines. And David said to Achish: But what have I done, and what have you found in your servant from the day that I was before you until this day, that I may not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king? And Achish answered and said to David: I know that you are good in my sight, as an angel of God: but the princes of the Philistines have said, He shall not go up with us to the battle. Rise therefore in the morning, you and the servants of your lord who came with you, and when you are up early and have light, depart. So David and his men rose up early to depart in the morning to return to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.

And it came to pass, when David and his men were come to Ziklag on the third day, that the Amalekites had invaded the south, and Ziklag, and smitten Ziklag, and burned it with fire; and had taken captive the women that were therein, from the least to the greatest; they slew not any, but carried them off and went their way. So David and his men came to the city, and behold, it was burned with fire; and their wives, and their sons, and their daughters, were taken captive. Then David and the people that were with him lifted up their voices and wept, until they had no more strength to weep. And David's two wives were taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite. And David was greatly distressed; for the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and his daughters. But David encouraged himself in the Lord his God; and he said

to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech: Bring me the ephod. And Abiathar brought the ephod to David. And David inquired of the Lord, saying: Shall I pursue after this troop? Shall I overtake them? And the Lord answered him: Pursue, for you shall surely overtake them, and shall without fail recover all. So David went, he and the six hundred men that were with him, and came to the brook Besor, where those that were left behind stayed; and some were too faint to cross the brook Besor. And they found an Egyptian in the field, and brought him to David, and gave him bread, and he ate, and they gave him water to drink. And they gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins. And when he had eaten his spirit came back to him, for he had eaten no bread nor drunk water for three days and three nights. And David said to him: To whom do you belong, and from where do you come, and where are you going? He said: I am a young man of Egypt, servant of an Amalekite. My master left me because I fell sick three days ago. For we made an invasion upon the south of the Cherethites, and upon the coast of Judah, and upon the south of Caleb, and we burned Ziklag with fire. And David said to him: Can you lead me to this troop? And he said: Swear to me by God that you will not kill me, nor deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will lead you to this troop. And he swore to him. And when he had led him there, behold, they were spread abroad upon the face of all the earth, eating and drinking and celebrating, because of all the great spoil that they had taken out of the land of the Philistines and out of the land of Judah. And David smote them from twilight even unto the evening of the next day, and there escaped not a man of them, save four hundred

. Second .

And they burned their bones and buried them in the grove of Jabesh, and they fasted seven days. Here ends the First Book of Kings. Here begins the Second Book of Kings. Chapter One.

It came to pass after the death of Saul, that David had returned from the slaughter of Amalek and stayed in Ziklag two days. And on the third day, behold, a man came from Saul's camp with his clothes torn and earth upon his head. And when he came to David, he fell to the ground and bowed down. And David said to him: Where do you come from? And he said to him: I have escaped from the camp of Israel. And David said to him: What has happened? Tell me. He said: The people fled from the battle, and many of the people fell and died. And Saul and Jonathan his son also perished. And David said to the young man who told him: How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead? The young man who told him said: By chance I came upon Mount Gilboa, and Saul was leaning upon his spear, and the chariots and horsemen were closing in on him. Turning and seeing me, he called to me. When I answered him: Here I am, he said to me: Who are you? And I answered him: I am an Amalekite. And he said to me: Stand over me and kill me, for anguish has seized me, yet my life still lingers in me. So I stood over him and killed him, for I knew that he could not survive after he fell. And I took the crown that was on his head and the bracelet from his arm, and I have brought them here to you, my lord. Then David took hold of his own garments and tore them, and all the men who were with him did likewise; and they mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and for Jonathan his son and for the people of the Lord and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword. And David said to the young man who had brought him the news: Where do you come from? He answered: I am the son of a resident alien, an Amalekite. And David said to him: Why were you not afraid to put out your hand to destroy the Lord's anointed? And David called one of his young men and said: Go, strike him down. And he struck him so that he died. And David said to him: Your blood be upon your own head, for your own mouth has testified against you, saying: I have killed the Lord's anointed. And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son, and he commanded that the sons of Judah be taught this lament, as it is written in the Book of the Upright.
