He said: Consider this for those who have died: your heights have been wounded. Israel, your enemies are upon your mountains. How have the mighty fallen! Tell it not in Gath, nor proclaim it in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult. O mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew, no rain upon you, nor fields of first-fruits, for there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, as though he had not been anointed with oil. The bow of Jonathan did not turn back, and the sword of Saul did not return empty. Saul and Jonathan, beloved and beautiful in their lives, and in their deaths they were not divided. Swifter than eagles, stronger than lions. O daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet and fine things, who adorned your garments with golden ornaments. How have the mighty fallen in battle! Jonathan lies slain upon your heights. I grieve for you, my brother Jonathan; you were exceedingly dear to me. Your love for me was wonderful, surpassing the love of women. As a mother loves her only child, so I loved you. How have the mighty fallen

Kings (2 Samuel), Chapter 2

After these things David consulted the Lord, saying: "Shall I go up into one of the cities of Judah?" And the Lord said to him: "Go up." And David said: "Where shall I go up?" And he answered: "To Hebron." So David went up there, and his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and David brought up the men who were with him, each with his household, and they settled in the towns of Hebron. And the men of Judah came and anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David that the men of Jabesh-gilead had buried Saul. David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead and said to them: "Blessed are you by the Lord, for you showed this kindness to Saul your lord and buried him. And now may the Lord show kindness and faithfulness to you; and I also will reward you because you have done this thing. Let your hands be strong and be valiant, for Saul your lord is dead, and the house of Judah has anointed me king over them."

But Abner son of Ner, commander of Saul's army, took Ish-bosheth son of Saul and brought him over to Mahanaim; and he made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel. Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David. And the time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

Abner son of Ner went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon with the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul; and Joab son of Zeruiah and the servants of David went out and met them by the pool of Gibeon. And when they had come together, they sat down, one group on one side of the pool and the other on the other side. And Abner said to Joab: "Let the young men arise and compete before us." And Joab said: "Let them arise." So they arose and crossed over by number: twelve for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David. And each man seized his opponent by the head and thrust his sword into his opponent's side; so they fell down together. Therefore that place was called the Field of Strong Men, which is in Gibeon. And the battle was very fierce that day, and Abner and the men of Israel were beaten before the servants of David.

And there were three sons of Zeruiah there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Now Asahel was as fleet of foot as a wild gazelle. Asahel pursued Abner and did not turn to the right or to the left from following him. Then Abner looked behind him and said: "Are you Asahel?" And he answered: "I am." And Abner said to him: "Turn aside to your right hand or to your left, and seize one of the young men and take his armor for yourself." But Asahel would not turn away from following him. And Abner said again to Asahel: "Turn aside from following me; why should I strike you to the ground? How then could I face your brother Joab?" But he refused to turn aside. Therefore Abner struck him in the belly with the butt end of the spear, so that the spear came out behind him; and he fell there and died on the spot. And everyone who came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died, stood still. But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner, and as the sun was going down they came to the hill of Ammah, which lies before Giah on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon. And the Benjaminites gathered around Abner and formed a single band and took their stand on top of a hill. And Abner called out—

. Second .

Abner said to Joab: and said, "Shall your sword devour endlessly? Do you not know how dangerous desperation is? How long will you not tell the people to stop pursuing their brothers?" And Joab said, "As the Lord lives, if you had spoken in the morning, the people would have given up pursuing their brother." Then Joab blew the trumpet, and all the army stood still and pursued Israel no more, neither did they fight anymore. And Abner and his men went through the plain of Moab all that night and crossed the Jordan, and having gone through all of Bithron, they came to Mahanaim. And Joab returned, leaving Abner, and gathered all the people; and there were missing of David's servants nineteen men and Asahel. But David's servants had struck down of Benjamin, and of Abner's men, three hundred and sixty men who died. And they took Asahel and buried him in the tomb of his father in Bethlehem. And Joab and his men went all night, and they arrived at Hebron at the break of day.

Now there was a long war between the house of David and the house of Saul. And David grew stronger and stronger, while the house of Saul became weaker and weaker. And sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelite; and his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; and the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital; and the sixth, Ithream, of Eglah David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron. While there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner the son of Ner was strengthening his hold on the house of Saul. Now Saul had a concubine whose name was Rizpah the daughter of Aiah; and Ish-bosheth said to Abner, "Why have you gone in to

my father's concubine?" Then Abner was very angry over the words of Ish-bosheth and said, "Am I a dog's head from Judah? This day I am showing loyalty to the house of Saul your father, to his brothers, and to his friends, and have not delivered you into the hand of David; and yet you charge me today with a fault concerning this woman. God do so to Abner and more also, if I do not do for David as the Lord has sworn to him — to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan to Beersheba." And Ish-bosheth could not answer Abner another word, because he feared him. And Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, "Whose is the land?" and that they should say, "Make your covenant with me, and my hand shall be with you to bring all Israel over to you." And David said, "Good, I will make a covenant with you. But one thing I require of you: you shall not see my face unless you first bring Michal, Saul's daughter, when you come to see me." Then David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, saying, "Give me my wife Michal, to whom I was betrothed for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines." And Ish-bosheth sent and took her from her husband Paltiel the son of Laish. And her husband went with her, weeping as he went, as far as Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, "Go, return." And he returned. Then Abner conferred with the elders of Israel, saying, "For some time past you have been seeking David as king over you. Now then do it; for the Lord has spoken of David, saying, 'By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and from the hand of all their enemies.'" Abner also spoke to Benjamin; and Abner went to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel and to all the house of Benjamin. And Abner came to David at Hebron with twenty men. And

Kings.

David made a feast for Abner and the men who had come with him. And Abner said to David: I will rise and gather all Israel to you, my lord the king, and make a covenant with you, so that you may reign over all that your heart desires. So when David had sent Abner away and he had gone in peace, immediately the servants of David and Joab came from a raid, bringing a great amount of plunder. Now Abner was not with David in Hebron, for he had already sent him away and he had departed in peace; and Joab and all the army that was with him had come afterward. When Joab was told by those who reported to him: Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he dismissed him, and he went away in peace. Then Joab went to the king and said: What have you done? Behold, Abner came to you. Why did you send him away so that he departed? Do you not know Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive you, and to learn your comings and goings, and to know everything you are doing? So Joab left David and sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the well of Sirah, without David knowing it. When Abner had returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the middle of the gate to speak with him privately, and there he struck him in the belly and he died, in revenge for the blood of Asahel his brother. When David heard that the deed was already done, he said: I and my kingdom are innocent before God forever of the blood of Abner the son of Ner. May it fall upon the head of Joab and upon all his father's house, and may there never be lacking from the house of Joab one who suffers from a discharge, or who is a leper, or who leans on a staff, or who falls by the sword, or who lacks bread. So Joab and Abishai his brother killed Abner, because he had killed Asahel their brother at Gibeon in battle. Then David said to Joab and to all the people who were with him: Tear your garments and put on sackcloth and mourn before

Abner. And King David followed the bier. And when they had buried Abner in Hebron, the king lifted up his voice and wept at the grave of Abner, and all the people wept. And the king lamented over Abner and said: Should Abner die as a fool dies? Your hands were not bound, your feet were not put in fetters; as one falls before the wicked, so you fell. And all the people wept again over him. Then all the people came to persuade David to eat while it was still day; but David swore, saying: God do so to me and more also, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun goes down. And all the people took notice, and it pleased them, as everything the king did pleased all the people. And all the people and all Israel understood that day that it was not the king's will to kill Abner the son of Ner. And the king said to his servants: Do you not know that a prince and a great man has fallen this day in Israel? And I was this day weak, though anointed king. These men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too harsh for me. May the Lord repay the evildoer according to his wickedness. Chapter 4.

When Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul, heard that Abner had died in Hebron, his hands grew feeble, and all Israel was troubled. Now there were two men who were captains of raiding bands, belonging to the son of Saul; the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin. For Beeroth also was counted as part of Benjamin. And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and have been sojourners there to this day. And Jonathan, the son of Saul, had a son who was lame in his feet. He was five years old when the news came from Jezreel about Saul and Jonathan. And his nurse took him up and fled; and as she made haste to flee, he fell:

· Kings ·

And he was lame and was called Mephibosheth. Then the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, came and entered the house of Ishbosheth during the heat of the day, while he was taking his midday rest. The doorkeeper of the house had been cleaning wheat and had become drowsy and fallen asleep. So Rechab and his brother Baanah slipped inside the house and found him lying on his bed in his bedroom, and they struck him and killed him and cut off his head. Then they took his head and traveled all night through the Arabah, and brought the head of Ishbosheth to David at Hebron. They said to the king, "Here is the head of Ishbosheth son of Saul, your enemy, who sought your life. The Lord has avenged my lord the king this day against Saul and his offspring." David answered Rechab and his brother Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, "As the Lord lives, who has redeemed my life from every adversity, when someone told me, 'Saul is dead,' thinking he was bringing good news, I seized him and killed him at Ziklag, which was the reward I gave him for his news. How much more, when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his own house on his bed, shall I not now require his blood from your hand and destroy you from the earth?" And David commanded his servants, and they killed them and cut off their hands and feet and hanged them beside the pool at Hebron. But they took the head of Ishbosheth and buried it in the tomb of Abner at Hebron. Chapter 5.

Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, "We are your bone and flesh. In times past, when Saul was king over us, it was you who led Israel out and brought them in. And the Lord said to you, 'You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall be ruler over Israel.'"

So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the Lord, and they anointed David king over Israel. David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years. At Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and at Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah. The king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land. And the Jebusites said to David, "You will not come in here, but the blind and the lame will ward you off," meaning that David could not come in there. Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion, that is, the city of David. And David had said on that day, "Whoever would strike the Jebusites, let him get up through the water shaft to attack the lame and the blind, who are hated by David's soul." Therefore it is said, "The blind and the lame shall not come into the house." And David lived in the stronghold and called it the city of David. And David built the city all around from the Millo inward. And David became greater and greater, for the Lord, the God of hosts, was with him. And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar trees, also carpenters and masons, and they built David a house. And David knew that the Lord had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel. And David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, after he came from Hebron, and more sons and daughters were born to David. And these are the names of those who were born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet. When the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to search for David.

Kings

When David heard this, he went down to the stronghold. And the Philistines came and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim. And David inquired of the Lord, saying: Shall I go up against the Philistines, and wilt thou deliver them into my hand? And the Lord said to David: Go up, for I will surely deliver the Philistines into your hand. And David came to Baal-perazim, and smote them there, and said: The Lord has divided my enemies before me, as water is divided. Therefore the name of that place was called Baal-perazim. And they left their idols there, and David and his men took them. And the Philistines came up yet again and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim. And David inquired of the Lord again. He answered: You shall not go up directly against them, but circle around behind them and come upon them opposite the balsam trees. And when you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then act, for the Lord will have gone out before you to strike down the army of the Philistines. David did as the Lord commanded him, and smote the Philistines from Geba all the way to Gezer.

Chapter 6. And David again gathered all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand. And David arose and went with all the people who were with him from the men of Judah to bring up the ark of God, over which the name of the Lord of hosts, who sits enthroned on the cherubim, is called. And they placed the ark of God on a new cart and brought it out of the house of Abinadab which was in Gibeah. And Uzzah and Ahio, sons of Abinadab, were driving the new cart. When they brought it out of the house of Abinadab in Gibeah, with Ahio going before the ark, David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the Lord with all kinds of instruments made of wood,

and with harps, with lyres, with tambourines, with flutes, and with cymbals. And when they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out to the ark of God and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled and nearly overturned it. And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzzah, and God struck him down there for his irreverence, and he died there beside the ark of God. And David was distressed because the Lord had broken out against Uzzah; and that place is called Perez-uzzah to this day. And David was afraid of the Lord that day, saying: How can the ark of the Lord come to me? And he was not willing to take the ark of the Lord into the city of David, but David took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. And the ark of the Lord remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months, and the Lord blessed Obed-edom and all his household. And it was told King David: The Lord has blessed the household of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him, because of the ark of God. So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom to the city of David with rejoicing; and there were with David seven choirs and a sacrificial animal. And when those who bore the ark of the Lord had gone six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened animal; and David danced before the Lord with all his might. David was wearing a linen ephod. And David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the Lord with shouting and with the sound of the trumpet. As the ark of the Lord came into the city of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out of the window, and saw King David leaping and dancing before the Lord, and she despised him in her heart. And they brought in the ark of the Lord and set it in its place inside the tent that David had pitched for it; and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the Lord. And when

he had completed the offerings of burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the Lord of hosts. And he distributed among all the people of Israel, both men and women, to each one a loaf of bread, a portion of roasted meat, and a cake of raisins. Then all the people departed, each to their own home. And David returned to bless his household. But Michal, the daughter of Saul, came out to meet David, and said: How glorious was the king of Israel today, uncovering himself before the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovers himself! And David said to Michal: It was before the Lord, who chose me above your father and all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the Lord, over Israel. Therefore I will celebrate before the Lord. And I will be more vile than this, and I will be humble in my own sight, but with the maidservants of whom you have spoken, with them I shall be honored. Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.

Chapter VII. Now it came to pass when the king dwelt in his house, and the Lord had given him rest from all his enemies round about, that he said to Nathan the prophet: See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of God dwells within curtains. And Nathan said to the king: Go, do all that is in your heart, for the Lord is with you. But it came to pass that night that the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying: Go and tell my servant David, Thus says the Lord: Shall you build me a house for me to dwell in? For I have not dwelt in a house since the time that I brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt, even to this day, but have walked in a tent and in a tabernacle. In all the places where I have walked with all the children of Israel, did I speak a word to any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, saying, Why have you not built me a house of cedar? Now therefore thus shall you say to my servant David: Thus says the Lord of hosts: I took you from the pasture, from following the flocks, to be ruler over my people, over Israel. And I was with you wherever you went, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you, and have made you a great name, like unto the names of the great ones that are on the earth. And I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place; and shall be moved no more, neither shall the children of wickedness afflict them any more, as before, even from the days that I commanded judges over my people Israel. And I will give you rest from all your enemies. Moreover the Lord tells you that the Lord will make you a house. And when your days are fulfilled, and you shall sleep with your fathers, I will raise up your seed after you, which shall proceed out of your body, and I will establish his kingdom. He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever. I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men. But my mercy shall not depart from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I put away from before me. And your house and your kingdom shall be established forever before me: and your throne shall be established forever. According to all these words and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak to David. Then David the king went in and sat before the Lord, and he said: Who am I, O Lord God? And what is my house, that you have brought me this far? And yet this was a small thing in your sight, O Lord God; but you have spoken also of your servant's house for a great while to come. And is this the manner of man, O Lord God? What can David say more to you? For you know your servant, O Lord God. For your word's sake, and according to your own heart, have you done all these great things.

Kings.

These great things, that you might make them known to your servant. Therefore you are magnified, O Lord God, for there is none like you, nor is there any God besides you, in all that we have heard with our ears. And what nation on earth is like your people Israel, whom God went to redeem for himself as a people, and to make a name for himself, and to do great and terrible things for them, before your people whom you redeemed for yourself from Egypt, driving out nations and their gods? For you established your people Israel as your own people forever, and you, O Lord God, have become their God. And now, O Lord God, the word that you have spoken concerning your servant and concerning his house, confirm it forever, and do as you have spoken, that your name may be magnified forever, so that it may be said, "The Lord of hosts is God over Israel," and the house of your servant David will be established before the Lord, because you, O Lord of hosts, God of Israel, have revealed this to your servant, saying, "I will build you a house." Therefore your servant has found it in his heart to pray this prayer to you. And now, O Lord God, you are God, and your words are true, and you have spoken these good things to your servant. Begin now, and bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever before you; for you, O Lord God, have spoken, and with your blessing the house of your servant shall be blessed forever. Chapter 8.

Afterward David defeated the Philistines and subdued them, and David took the tribute from the hand of the Philistines. He also defeated Moab, and he measured them with a line, making them lie down on the ground. He measured two lengths of line to put to death, and one length to keep alive. And Moab became servants to David and brought tribute. David also defeated Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to restore his control at the Euphrates River. David captured from him one thousand seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers, and David hamstrung all the chariot horses, but kept enough for a hundred chariots. When Syria of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand men of Syria, and David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus, and Syria became servants to David and brought tribute. The Lord gave victory to David wherever he went. David took the shields of gold that were carried by the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem. From Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took a great amount of bronze, from which Solomon made the bronze sea and the pillars and the vessels of bronze. When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the whole army of Hadadezer, Tou sent his son Joram to King David to greet him and to congratulate him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and defeated him. For Hadadezer had often been at war with Tou. And Joram brought with him articles of silver, articles of gold, and articles of bronze, which King David dedicated to the Lord, together with the silver and gold that he dedicated from all the nations he had subdued — from Syria, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, Amalek, and from the spoils of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah. David made a name for himself when he returned from striking down eighteen thousand Syrians in the Valley of Salt, and he garrisoned Edom and all the Edomites became servants to David. The Lord gave victory to David wherever he went. David reigned over all Israel, and David administered justice and equity to all his people. Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder, and Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of

Abiathar were the priests, and Seraiah was the scribe; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites. And David's sons were priests. And David said: Is there anyone still remaining of the house of Saul, that I may show him kindness for Jonathan's sake? Now there was a servant of the house of Saul whose name was Ziba. And when they had called him to the king, the king said to him: Are you Ziba? And he answered: I am your servant. And the king said: Is there not still someone of the house of Saul, that I may show the kindness of God to him? And Ziba said to the king: There remains yet a son of Jonathan, who is lame in his feet. Where is he? said the king. And Ziba said to the king: Behold, he is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar. Then when Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he fell on his face and did reverence. And David said: Mephibosheth. And he answered: Here is your servant. And David said to him: Do not fear, for I will surely show you kindness for Jonathan your father's sake, and will restore to you all the land of Saul your father, and you shall eat bread at my table always. And he bowed down and said: Who am I, your servant, that you should look upon such a dead dog as I am? Then the king called Ziba, Saul's servant, and said to him: All that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to your master's son. You therefore shall till the land for him, you and your sons and your servants, and you shall bring in the produce, that your master's son may have food to eat. But Mephibosheth your master's son shall eat bread always at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants. And Ziba said to the king: According to all that my lord the king has commanded his servant, so shall your servant do. So Mephibosheth ate at David's table, like one of the king's sons. And Mephibosheth had a young son whose name was Micha. And all who dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants to Mephibosheth. So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem, because he ate always at the king's table; and he was lame in both his feet. Chapter 10. And it came to pass after this that the king of the Ammonites died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place. And David said: I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father showed kindness to me. So David sent his servants to console him concerning his father. And when David's servants came into the land of the Ammonites, the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun their lord: Do you think that David is honoring your father in sending comforters to you? Has David not rather sent his servants to you to search the city and to spy it out and to overthrow it? So Hanun took David's servants and shaved off half their beards and cut off their garments in the middle, as far as their buttocks, and sent them away. When this was told to David, he sent to meet them, for the men were greatly ashamed. And David said: Stay at Jericho until your beards have grown, and then return. And when the Ammonites saw that they had made themselves odious to David, they sent and hired the Syrians of Rehob and the Syrians of Zoba, twenty thousand foot soldiers, and from the king of Maacah a thousand men, and from Istob twelve thousand men. And when David heard of it, he sent Joab and all the army of mighty warriors. And the Ammonites came out and drew up their battle line at the entrance of the gate; and the Syrians of Zoba and of Rehob and the men of Istob and Maacah were by themselves in the open field. When Joab saw that the battle was set against him both in front and in the rear, he chose some of the best men of Israel and arrayed them against the Syrians; and the rest of the people he put in the care of Abishai his brother, who arrayed them against the Ammonites. And he said: If the Syrians are too strong for me,

· Kings ·

be to me as a help; but if the sons of Ammon prevail against you, I will come and help you. Be strong and let us fight for our people and for the cities of our God. And the Lord will do what is good in his sight. So Joab and the people who were with him drew near to battle against the Syrians, and they fled before him. And when the sons of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled, they also fled before Abishai and entered the city. So Joab returned from the sons of Ammon and came to Jerusalem. When the Syrians saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they gathered themselves together. And Hadadezer sent and brought out the Syrians who were beyond the river, and their army came with Shobach the commander of the army of Hadadezer leading them. When it was told to David, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and came to Helam. And the Syrians set themselves in array against David and fought with him. Then the Syrians fled before Israel, and David killed seven hundred chariot fighters and forty thousand horsemen, and struck Shobach the commander of their army, who died there. And when all the kings who were servants of Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with Israel and served them. So the Syrians feared to help the sons of Ammon anymore. Chapter 11.

It came to pass in the spring of the year, at the time when kings go out to battle, that David sent Joab and his servants with him and all Israel, and they devastated the sons of Ammon and besieged Rabbah. But David remained in Jerusalem. One evening David arose from his bed and walked about on the roof of the king's house, and from the roof he saw a woman bathing,

and the woman was very beautiful. So the king sent and inquired about the woman. And it was told him that she was Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite. Then David sent messengers and took her. And when she came to him, he lay with her. She was purified from her uncleanness, and she returned to her house, having conceived. Then she sent and told David, saying: I am with child. So David sent word to Joab, saying: Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David. When Uriah came to David, David asked how Joab was doing and how the people were doing and how the war was going. Then David said to Uriah: Go down to your house and wash your feet. So Uriah left the king's house, and a gift of food from the king was sent after him. But Uriah slept at the door of the king's house with all the servants of his lord, and did not go down to his own house. And when they told David, saying: Uriah did not go down to his house, David said to Uriah: Have you not come from a journey? Why did you not go down to your house? And Uriah said to David: The ark and Israel and Judah dwell in tents, and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord are encamped in the open field. Shall I then go to my house to eat and drink and lie with my wife? As you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do this thing. Then David said to Uriah: Remain here today also, and tomorrow I will let you go. So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next, and David invited him and he ate before him and drank, and he made him drunk. And Uriah went out in the evening to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, and he did not go down to his house. In the morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah, writing in the letter:

. Kings .

All this: and in the sight of the sun. And David said to Nathan: I have sinned against the Lord. And Nathan said to David: The Lord also has taken away your sin. You shall not die. Nevertheless, because you have given occasion to the enemies of the Lord to blaspheme, for this word the child that is born to you shall surely die. And Nathan returned to his house. And the Lord struck the child that Uriah's wife bore to David, and it was very sick. David therefore besought God for the child: and David fasted, and going in, lay all night upon the ground. And the elders of his house came to him, to make him rise from the ground: but he would not, neither did he eat food with them. And it came to pass on the seventh day that the child died: and the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead. For they said: Behold, when the child was yet alive, we spoke to him and he would not hear our voice: how much more will he afflict himself if we tell him that the child is dead? But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: and David said to his servants: Is the child dead? They answered him: He is dead. Then David rose from the ground, and washed and anointed himself, and changed his clothes: and he went into the house of the Lord and worshipped: and then he came to his own house, and he asked them to set bread before him, and he ate. Then his servants said to him: What thing is this that you have done? You fasted and wept for the child while it was alive: but when the child was dead, you rose and ate bread. And he said: While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who knows whether the Lord may give him to me, and the child may live? But now that he is dead, why should I fast? Shall I be able to bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me.

And David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and went in to her and lay with her. And she bore a son, and he called his name Solomon: and the Lord loved him. And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he called his name Jedidiah, because the Lord loved him. And Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city. And Joab sent messengers to David, saying: I have fought against Rabbah, and the city of waters is about to be taken. Now therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city and take it: lest I take the city and it be called after my name. So David gathered all the people together, and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and took it. And he took the crown of Milcom from off his head, the weight of which was a talent of gold, with precious stones: and it was set on David's head. And he brought forth the spoil of the city, a very great amount, and brought out the people who were in it and set them to work with saws and iron picks and axes. And thus he did to all the cities of the children of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem. Chapter XIII.

And it came to pass after this, that Amnon the son of David loved Tamar, the beautiful sister of Absalom the son of David: and Amnon was so distressed that he fell sick on account of his sister Tamar; for she was a virgin, and it seemed hard to Amnon to do anything to her. But Amnon had a friend whose name was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David's brother: and Jonadab was a very cunning man. And he said to him: Why are you, being the king's son, so lean from day to day? Will you not tell me? And Amnon said to him: I love Tamar, the sister of my brother Absalom. And Jonadab said to him:

Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick; when your father comes to visit you, say to him: Let my sister Tamar come to me and give me food and prepare some nourishment, that I may eat from her hand. So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill. And when the king came to visit him, Amnon said to the king: I pray you, let my sister Tamar come and make two little cakes in my sight, that I may take nourishment from her hand. So David sent word to Tamar at home, saying: Go to your brother Amnon's house and prepare food for him. And Tamar went to the house of her brother Amnon, who was lying down. She took flour and kneaded it, and made cakes in his sight, and cooked them; she then took what she had cooked and poured it out, and set it before him, but he refused to eat. And Amnon said: Send everyone away from me. When everyone had left, Amnon said to Tamar: Bring the food into the inner room, that I may eat from your hand. And Tamar took the cakes she had made and brought them to her brother Amnon in the inner room. When she offered him the food, he seized her and said: Come lie with me, my sister. She answered him: No, my brother, do not force me; this must not be done in Israel. Do not commit this outrage. I would not be able to bear my shame, and you would be like one of the fools in Israel. Rather, speak to the king; he will not refuse me to you. But he would not listen to her; being stronger than her, he forced her and lay with her. Then Amnon felt intense hatred for her, far greater than the love he had felt for her before. And Amnon said to her: Get up and go. She replied: This wrong in sending me away is greater than the other you did to me. But he would not listen to her.

He called the young man who waited on him and said: Throw this woman out of my presence and bolt the door after her. Now she was wearing a long robe, for this is how the king's daughters who were virgins used to dress. His servant put her out and bolted the door after her. Tamar put ashes on her head and tore the long robe she was wearing; she put her hands on her head and went away, weeping as she walked. Her brother Absalom said to her: Has your brother Amnon been with you? Be quiet for now, sister; he is your brother. Do not take this matter to heart. So Tamar, desolate, remained in her brother Absalom's house. When King David heard all this, he was very angry, but he would not punish his son Amnon, because he loved him, since he was his firstborn. Absalom said nothing to Amnon, either good or bad; yet Absalom hated Amnon because he had violated his sister Tamar. Two years later, when Absalom's shearers were at Baal-hazor, which is near Ephraim, Absalom invited all the king's sons. He went to the king and said: My shearers are at work; let the king and his servants come with your servant. The king said to Absalom: No, my son, we should not all go, for we would be a burden to you. Though Absalom pressed him, he would not go but gave him his blessing. Then Absalom said: If you will not come, please let my brother Amnon come with us. The king said to him: It is not necessary for him to go with you. But Absalom pressed the king, and he sent with him Amnon and all the king's sons. Absalom had prepared a feast like a royal banquet. And Absalom commanded his servants: Watch when Amnon is merry with wine; and when I say to you:

. Kings .

Strike him and kill him; do not be afraid. For I am the one who commands you. Be strong and be valiant men. So Absalom's servants did to Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king's sons arose and each mounted his mule and fled. While they were still on their way, a rumor reached David saying: Absalom has struck down all the king's sons, and not one of them remains. Then King David arose and tore his garments and lay on the ground, and all his servants who stood about him tore their garments. But Jonadab, son of Shimeah, David's brother, spoke up and said: Let not my lord the king suppose that all the young men, the king's sons, have been killed. Amnon alone is dead, for by Absalom's design this has been set since the day he violated his sister Tamar. Now therefore let not my lord the king take the matter to heart by saying that all the king's sons are dead, for Amnon alone is dead. And Absalom fled. The young man who kept watch looked up and saw a great crowd coming down the road from the hillside. And Jonadab said to the king: Look, the king's sons are coming, just as your servant said. And when he had finished speaking, the king's sons arrived and lifted up their voices and wept. And the king and all his servants wept very bitterly. But Absalom fled and went to Talmai the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And David mourned for his son Amnon many days. And Absalom, having fled and come to Geshur, remained there three years. And King David ceased to pursue Absalom, because he was comforted concerning Amnon's death. Chapter XIV.

And Joab the son of Zeruiah, perceiving that the king's heart was turned toward Absalom, sent to Tekoa and brought from there a wise woman,

and said to her: Pretend to be in mourning and put on mourning garments and do not anoint yourself with oil, so that you may seem like a woman who has been long mourning for the dead. Go in to the king and speak to him in this manner. And Joab put the words in her mouth. So when the woman of Tekoa came to the king, she fell on her face to the ground and did obeisance and said: Save me, O king. And the king said to her: What is your trouble? She answered: Alas, I am a widow; my husband is dead. And your handmaid had two sons, and the two of them quarreled with each other in the field, and there was no one to separate them, and one struck the other and killed him. And now the whole family has risen against your handmaid, saying: Give up the one who struck his brother, that we may put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed, and so destroy the heir also. Thus they would quench my coal that is left, and leave my husband neither name nor remnant upon the earth. Then the king said to the woman: Go to your house, and I will give orders concerning you. And the woman of Tekoa said to the king: On me be the guilt, my lord the king, and on my father's house; but let the king and his throne be guiltless. The king said: Whoever says anything to you, bring him to me, and he shall never touch you again. Then she said: Let the king remember the Lord your God, so that the avenger of blood may destroy no more, lest they destroy my son. He said: As the Lord lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground. Then the woman said: Let your handmaid speak a word to my lord the king. He said: Speak. And the woman said: Why then have you devised such a thing against the people of God? For in giving this decision the king convicts himself in that the king does not bring his banished one home again. We must all die; we are like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again. And God does not wish to destroy

[Chapter heading: Second Books of Kings]

She held back her soul, thinking lest the one who had been cast out should perish. "Now therefore I have come to speak to my lord the king this word, with his servant present." And she said, "Let your handmaid speak." "Speak to the king: so that the king may do the word of his handmaid. And the king heard, to deliver his handmaid from the hand of all who would destroy me and my son together from the inheritance of God. Let your handmaid say: let the word of my lord the king be as a sacrifice." For as the angel of God, so is my lord the king: that he is moved neither by blessing nor by cursing. May the Lord your God also be with you. And the king laughed and said to the woman, "Do not hide from me what I ask you." The woman said, "Let my lord the king speak." And the king said, "Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?" The woman answered and said, "By the life of your soul, my lord the king, one cannot turn to the right hand or to the left from anything that my lord the king has spoken. For your servant Joab himself commanded me, and he himself put all these words in the mouth of your handmaid, to present the matter in this form. Your servant Joab commanded this. But you, my lord the king, are wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are upon earth." And the king said to Joab, "Behold, I have done the thing; go therefore, bring back the young man Absalom." And Joab fell to the ground on his face, and bowed himself, and blessed the king: and Joab said, "Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your sight, my lord the king, in that the king has fulfilled the request of his servant." So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem. And the king said, "Let him return to his own house, and let him not see my face." So Absalom returned to his own house, and saw not the king's face. But in all Israel there was none so praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him. And when he shaved his head — for it was at every year's end that he shaved it, because it grew heavy on him — he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels, by the king's weight. And to Absalom were born three sons, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar, a woman of beautiful form. And Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem, and did not see the king's face. Therefore Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king; but he would not come to him. And when he sent again the second time, and he would not come, he said to his servants, "See, Joab's field is near mine, and he has barley there; go and set it on fire." And Absalom's servants set the field on fire. Then Joab arose and came to Absalom at his house, and said, "Why have your servants set my field on fire?" And Absalom answered Joab, "Behold, I sent word to you saying, Come here, that I may send you to the king, to ask, Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me to still be there. Now therefore let me see the king's face; and if there is iniquity in me, let him kill me." So Joab came to the king and told him. And Absalom was called, and he came to the king, and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king: and the king kissed Absalom.

Chapter XV.
After this, Absalom prepared himself chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him. And Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate: and whenever any man who had a lawsuit came to the king for judgment, Absalom called to him and said, "What city are you from?" And he would answer and say, "From one of the

· Kings ·

of this tribe I am your servant. Absalom answered him. Your words seem good and right to me, but there is no one appointed by the king to hear you. And Absalom would say: Who will make me judge over the land, so that all who have a dispute might come to me and I would judge them justly? And when someone came near to greet him, he would stretch out his hand and take hold of him and kiss him. He did this to all of Israel who came to the king for judgment, and so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

After forty years, Absalom said to King David: Let me go and fulfill the vow I made to the Lord in Hebron. For your servant made a vow when I was in Geshur in Aram, saying: If the Lord brings me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the Lord. King David said to him: Go in peace. So he arose and went to Hebron. Then Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel saying: As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then say: Absalom is king in Hebron. Now two hundred men from Jerusalem went with Absalom, invited as guests, going in their simplicity and knowing nothing of the matter. And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, from his city of Giloh, while he was offering sacrifices. The conspiracy grew strong, and the people with Absalom kept increasing. A messenger came to David saying: The hearts of all Israel have gone after Absalom. And David said to his servants who were with him in Jerusalem: Rise and let us flee, for otherwise there will be no escape for us from Absalom. Hurry to leave, lest he come quickly and overtake us, and bring disaster upon us and strike the city with the edge of the sword. The king's servants said to him: Whatever my lord the king decides, your servants are ready to do.

So the king went out, and all his household on foot. The king left ten concubines to keep the house. And the king went out, and all Israel with him on foot, and they stopped at the last house. All his servants passed by him, along with all the Cherethites and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who had followed him from Gath, passing on before the king. Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite: Why are you also coming with us? Go back and stay with the king, for you are a foreigner and also an exile from your own place. You came only yesterday, and shall I today make you wander about with us, since I go wherever I must go? Return, and take your brothers back with you, and may the Lord show you steadfast love and faithfulness, for you have shown loyalty. But Ittai answered the king: As the Lord lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king shall be, whether in death or life, even there also will your servant be. And David said to Ittai: Go then, pass on. So Ittai the Gittite passed on, with all his men and all the little ones who were with him, and all the rest of the people. And everyone wept aloud as all the people passed by, and the king crossed the brook Kidron, and all the people crossed toward the way of the wilderness.

Zadok also came, and with him all the Levites, carrying the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God. And Abiathar went up until all the people had finished passing out of the city. The king said to Zadok: Carry the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the Lord, he will bring me back and let me see it and his dwelling place. But if he says: I have no delight in you — here I am, let him do to me what seems good to him. The king also said to Zadok the priest: Look, go back to the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz your son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar — your two sons shall be with you.

Behold, I will hide myself in the open fields of the desert until word comes from you to inform me. So Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark of God back to Jerusalem and stayed there. But David went up the slope of the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went, with his head covered and his feet bare. And all the people with him covered their heads and went up weeping. Then David was told that Ahithophel was among the conspirators with Absalom. And David said: O Lord, I pray you, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness. And when David came to the top of the mountain where he was about to worship God, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his garment torn and earth upon his head. And David said to him: If you come with me, you will be a burden to me. But if you return to the city and say to Absalom: I am your servant, O king; as I was your father's servant before, so I will now be your servant — then you may defeat the counsel of Ahithophel for me. You have there with you Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and every word you hear in the king's house you shall report to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. There are with them their two sons, Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar, and through them you shall send me every word you hear. So Hushai, David's friend, came into the city, and Absalom entered Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him. Chapter 16.
When David had passed a little beyond the summit of the mountain, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth came to meet him with a pair of donkeys saddled, bearing two hundred loaves of bread, one hundred clusters of raisins, one hundred cakes of figs, and a skin of wine. And the king said to Ziba: What do you mean by these things? Ziba answered: The donkeys are for the king's household to ride on, the bread and figs are for the young men to eat, and the wine is for those who grow faint in the wilderness to drink. The king said: And where is your master's son? Ziba answered: He has remained in Jerusalem, saying, Today the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my father. The king said to Ziba: All that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours. And Ziba said: I bow before you; let me find favor in your sight, my lord the king. When King David came to Bahurim, behold, a man of the family of the house of Saul came out, whose name was Shimei the son of Gera, and as he came he cursed continually, throwing stones at David and at all the servants of King David. All the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left. And Shimei said as he cursed: Get out, get out, you man of blood, you worthless man! The Lord has repaid you for all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and the Lord has given the kingdom into the hand of your son Absalom. See, your evil is upon you, for you are a man of blood. Then Abishai the son of Zeruiah said to the king: Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and take off his head. But the king said: What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? Let him curse, for the Lord has told him to curse David. Who then shall say, Why have you done so? And the king said to Abishai and to all his servants: Behold, my own son seeks my life; how much more now may this Benjaminite! Leave him alone, and let him curse, for the Lord has commanded him. It may be that the Lord will look on my affliction, and that the Lord will repay me with good for this cursing of me today. So David and his men went along the road, while Shimei went along the hillside opposite him, cursing as he went and throwing stones at him and flinging dust.

Jedus [Header]

lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that are with him. Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying by the spring of Rogel. A maidservant went and told them, and they went to carry the news to king David, for they could not be seen entering the city. But a young boy saw them and told Absalom. They however went quickly and entered the house of a certain man in Bahurim, who had a well in his courtyard, and they went down into it. And a woman took and spread a covering over the mouth of the well, as if drying groats, and so the matter was hidden. When Absalom's servants came to the woman at the house and asked, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" the woman answered them, "They have crossed over the brook of water." And when they had sought them and could not find them, they returned to Jerusalem. Then after they had departed, the two came up out of the well and went and told king David, saying, "Arise and cross quickly over the river, for Ahithophel has given such and such counsel against you." So David arose, and all the people with him, and they crossed the Jordan before daybreak, until not one remained who had not crossed the river. Now Ahithophel, seeing that his counsel was not followed, saddled his donkey and arose and went to his house, to his own city. And having set his house in order, he hanged himself and died, and was buried in the tomb of his father. And David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom crossed the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him. And Amasa was appointed by Absalom over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra the Israelite, who had gone in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah who was Joab's mother. And Israel and Absalom encamped in the land of Gilead. And when David came to Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash

from Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel from Lodebar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim, brought beds and basins and earthen vessels, and wheat and barley and flour and parched grain, and beans and lentils and roasted grain, and honey and butter and sheep and fat calves, and offered them to David and to the people with him to eat, for they said the people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness. Chapter 18. And David numbered the people who were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them. And David divided the people into three groups: one third under the command of Joab, one third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and one third under the command of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the people, "I will also go out with you myself." But the people said, "You shall not go out. For if we flee, they will not care about us. Even if half of us die, they will not care about us. But you are worth ten thousand of us. Therefore it is better that you stay in the city to support us." Then the king said to them, "Whatever seems best to you I will do." So the king stood beside the gate, while all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands. And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai saying, "Deal gently for my sake with the young man Absalom." And all the people heard when the king commanded all the captains concerning Absalom. So the people went out into the field against Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim. And the people of Israel were defeated there before the servants of David, and there was a great slaughter that day of twenty thousand men. For the battle spread over the face of all the country, and the forest devoured more people that day than the sword devoured. And Absalom happened to meet the servants of David. Absalom was riding on a mule, and as the mule went under the thick boughs

Kings.

his head caught fast in the oak, and he was left hanging between heaven and earth, while the mule that was under him went away. A certain man saw it and told Joab, saying: I saw Absalom hanging in an oak. And Joab said to the man who had told him: If you saw it, why did you not stab him to the ground? And I would have given you ten pieces of silver and one belt. He answered Joab: Even if you were to weigh out a thousand pieces of silver into my hands, I would not lay my hand on the king's son. For in our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, saying: Take care of the young man Absalom. And if I had acted boldly against my own life, nothing could have been hidden from the king, and you would have stood apart. And Joab said: I will not waste time with you like this. He took three spears in his hand and thrust them into the heart of Absalom, while he was still alive in the oak. And ten young men, armor-bearers of Joab, ran up and struck Absalom and killed him. Then Joab sounded the trumpet, and the troops turned back from pursuing Israel, for Joab restrained them, wanting to spare the multitude. They took Absalom and cast him into a great pit in the forest, and raised over him a very great heap of stones. And all Israel fled, each to his own tent. Now Absalom, while he was still alive, had set up for himself a pillar which is in the King's Valley; for he said: I have no son to keep my name in remembrance. He called the pillar after his own name, and it is called Absalom's Monument to this day. Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said: Let me now run and carry news to the king, for the Lord has delivered him from the hand of his enemies. Joab said to him: You shall not carry news today; you may carry news another day, but today you shall carry no news, because the king's son is dead. Then Joab said to the Cushite: Go, tell the king what you have seen. The Cushite bowed before Joab and ran.

Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said again to Joab: Come what may, let me also run after the Cushite. Joab said: Why will you run, my son, seeing that you have no news ready? But he said: Come what may, I will run. So he said to him: Run. Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain, and outran the Cushite. Now David was sitting between the two gates, and the watchman went up to the roof over the gate by the wall, and when he lifted up his eyes and looked, he saw a man running alone. The watchman called out and told the king. The king said: If he is alone, there is news in his mouth. As he came nearer and nearer, the watchman saw another man running, and he called to the gatekeeper: See, another man running alone! The king said: He also brings news. The watchman said: The running of the first is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok. And the king said: He is a good man and comes with good news. Then Ahimaaz called out to the king: All is well! He bowed before the king with his face to the ground and said: Blessed be the Lord your God, who has delivered up the men who raised their hand against my lord the king! The king said: Is it well with the young man Absalom? Ahimaaz answered: When Joab sent the king's servant, and me your servant, I saw a great tumult, but I do not know what it was. The king said: Turn aside and stand here. So he turned aside and stood still. And the Cushite came, and the Cushite said: Good news for my lord the king! For the Lord has delivered you this day from the hand of all who rose up against you. The king said to the Cushite: Is it well with the young man Absalom? The Cushite answered: May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up against you for evil be like that young man. And the king was deeply moved...

. Kings .

You sons of Zeruiah, why do you become adversaries to me today? Should any man be put to death in Israel today? Do I not know that today I am king over Israel? And the king said to Shimei, You shall not die. And he swore to him. Mephibosheth, the son of Saul, came down to meet the king, unwashed feet and unshaven beard, and his clothes unwashed from the day the king left until the day he returned in peace. When he came to meet the king, the king said to him, Why did you not come with me, Mephibosheth? And he answered, My lord the king, my servant deceived me. For he said, I will saddle a donkey for me, that I may ride upon it and go with the king, for I am lame. Moreover he has slandered your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king is as an angel of God, do therefore what is good in your sight. For all of my father's house were nothing but men deserving death before my lord the king; yet you set your servant among those who eat at your own table. What right have I therefore to cry any more to the king? So the king said to him, Why do you speak any more of your matters? I have decided: you and Ziba shall divide the land. And Mephibosheth said to the king, Let him take it all, since my lord the king has come back to his house in peace. Now Barzillai the Gileadite, a very old man, came down from Rogelim and brought the king over the Jordan, to escort him across. Now Barzillai was a very aged man, eighty years old, and he had provided the king with supplies while he stayed at Mahanaim, for he was a very wealthy man. And the king said to Barzillai, Come with me, and I will provide for you in Jerusalem. But Barzillai said to the king, How many years do I have left to live, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem? I am today eighty years old. Can I discern between good and bad? Can your servant taste what I eat or drink? Can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? Why then should your servant be a further burden to my lord the king? Your servant will go a little way across the Jordan with the king. But let your servant return, that I may die in my own city by the grave of my father and my mother. But here is your servant Chimham; let him go with my lord the king, and do for him what seems good to you. And the king answered, Chimham shall go with me, and I will do for him what seems good to you, and whatever you ask of me I will do for you. And all the people crossed the Jordan, and the king crossed over, and the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his own place. Then the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him. And all the people of Judah had escorted the king over, and also half the people of Israel. And behold, all the men of Israel came to the king and said to him, Why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen you away and brought the king and his household over the Jordan, along with all David's men? And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, Because the king is closely related to us. Why then are you angry over this matter? Have we eaten at all at the king's expense, or has any gift been given us? And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah and said, We have ten shares in the king, and in David also we have more than you. Why then did you despise us? Were we not the first to speak of bringing back our king? Yet your words were harder than ours. And there happened to be there a man of Belial, whose name was Sheba the son of Bichri, a Benjaminite, and he blew a trumpet and said, We have no part in David, nor do we have an inheritance in the son of Jesse. Every man to his tents, O Israel. So all the men of Israel departed from David and followed Sheba the son of Bichri.

And all of the tribe of Sheba son of Bichri followed him; but the men of Judah stayed close to their king from the Jordan all the way to Jerusalem. When the king came to his house in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubine women whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in a house under guard, and provided food for them. But he did not go in to them, and they were shut up until the day of their death, living as widows.

The king said to Amasa: Summon the men of Judah for me within three days, and you be present here. So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he stayed longer than the set time which David had appointed him. And David said to Abishai: Now Sheba the son of Bichri shall do us more harm than Absalom did. Take your lord's servants and pursue him, lest he find himself fortified cities and escape from us. So the men who followed Joab went out, along with the Cherethites and the Pelethites and all the mighty men, and they went out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri. When they were at the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa came before them. Now Joab was dressed in a close-fitting military garment, and over it he had strapped a sword at his hip in its sheath, and as he went it fell out. And Joab said to Amasa: Are you well, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand as if to kiss him. But Amasa did not notice the sword that was in Joab's hand. And Joab struck him with it in the stomach and his bowels poured out on the ground; and he died, and Joab did not strike him a second time. Then Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri. Meanwhile one of Joab's young men stood by Amasa and said: Whoever favors Joab and whoever is for David, let him follow Joab. But Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the road.

When a certain man saw that all the people stopped, he moved Amasa from the road to a field and threw a garment over him, because he saw that everyone who came upon him would stop. When he was removed from the road, all the men passed on after Joab to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri. And Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel and Beth-maachah, and all the Berites gathered together and followed him. And Joab's forces came and besieged him in Abel of Beth-maachah, and they cast up a siege mound against the city, and it stood in the outer rampart; and all the people who were with Joab were battering the wall to throw it down. Then a wise woman called from the city: Hear, hear! Tell Joab: Come here that I may speak with you. And when he had come to her, the woman said: Are you Joab? He answered: I am. Then she said to him: Hear the words of your servant. And he answered: I hear. Then she spoke, saying: In the old days they used to say: Let them ask counsel at Abel, and so they settled matters. I am among those who are peaceable and faithful in Israel; you seek to destroy a city and a mother in Israel. Why would you swallow up the inheritance of the Lord? And Joab answered: Far be it from me, far be it from me that I should swallow up or destroy. That is not the matter. But a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, has lifted up his hand against King David. Give up him alone, and I will withdraw from the city. The woman said to Joab: His head shall be thrown over the wall to you. So the woman went in her wisdom to all the people, and they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri and threw it to Joab. And he blew the trumpet and they all withdrew from the city, each to his home. And Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king. Now Joab was over all the army of Israel; and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and

Kings

Adoram was over the tribute; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder; Sheva was scribe; Zadok and Abiathar were priests; and Ira the Jairite was also a priest of David. Chapter 21...

Now there was a famine in the days of David for three years, year after year. And David sought the face of the Lord, and the Lord said: "It is for Saul, and for his bloody house, because he put to death the Gibeonites." So the king called the Gibeonites and spoke to them. Now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites. The children of Israel had sworn to them, but Saul had sought to slay them in his zeal for the children of Israel and Judah. David therefore said to the Gibeonites, "What shall I do for you? And with what shall I make atonement, so that you may bless the inheritance of the Lord?" The Gibeonites said to him, "It is not a matter of silver or gold between us and Saul or his house; neither is it for us to put any man to death in Israel." And he said, "What do you say that I shall do for you?" They answered the king, "The man who consumed us and who plotted against us, so that we have been destroyed from remaining in any of the territories of Israel — let seven of his sons be given to us, and we will hang them before the Lord in Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the Lord." And the king said, "I will give them." But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of the Lord's oath that was between David and Jonathan the son of Saul. So the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bore to Saul: Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she brought up for Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite. And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them on the hill before the Lord. And the seven of them fell together and were put to death in the days of the first harvest, at the beginning of the barley harvest.

Then Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it for herself on the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water poured on them from the heavens. She did not allow the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the wild animals by night. And David was told what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done. And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh-gilead, who had stolen them from the public square of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hanged them on the day the Philistines killed Saul in Gilboa. And he brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son; and they gathered the bones of those who had been hanged, and buried them with the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the land of Benjamin, in Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father. And after that God heeded the supplication for the land. Now again there was war between the Philistines and Israel, and David went down together with his servants, and they fought against the Philistines. And David grew faint, and Ishbi-benob, who was one of the descendants of the giant, the weight of whose spear was three hundred shekels of bronze, and who was armed with a new sword, thought to have killed David. But Abishai the son of Zeruiah came to his aid, and attacked the Philistine and killed him. Then the men of David swore to him, saying, "You shall not go out with us to battle anymore, lest you quench the lamp of Israel." After this there was again a battle with the Philistines at Gob. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph, who was one of the descendants of the giants. And there was again war with the Philistines at Gob, and Elhanan the son of Jair of Bethlehem struck down Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver's beam. And there was again war at Gath, where there was a man of great stature who had six fingers on each hand, and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in number, and he also was descended from the giants.

Kings.

me. My enemies you have given into my hand; those who hated me you have scattered. They cry out, but there is none to save them; to the Lord they cry, but he does not answer them. I will beat them as fine as the dust of the earth; like the mud of the streets I will crush and stamp them down. You will deliver me from the contradictions of my people; you will keep me as the head of the nations. A people I did not know shall serve me; foreign sons will resist me, but at the hearing of the ear they will obey me. Foreign sons have faded away and have drawn back in their distress. The Lord lives, and blessed is my God, and the mighty God of my salvation shall be exalted. God who gives me vengeance and brings peoples under me. Who leads me out from my enemies and lifts me up from those who resist me; from the unjust man you will free me, therefore you will keep me as head of the nations, and I will sing to your name. He who magnifies the salvation of his king and shows mercy to his anointed, to David and to his seed forever. Chapter 23.

Now these are the last words of David. David the son of Jesse said; the man to whom it was established concerning the Christ of the God of Jacob, the excellent psalmist of Israel, said: The Spirit of the Lord spoke through me, and his word was upon my tongue. The God of Israel said to me; the strong one of Israel spoke. He that rules over men justly, that rules in the fear of God. He shall be as the light of morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds; as the tender grass springs from the earth through clear shining after rain. Though my house is not so with God, yet he has made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things and sure. For this is all my salvation and all my desire, though he makes it not to grow. But the ungodly shall be as thorns thrust away, for they cannot be taken with hands. And whoever shall touch them must be armed with iron and the staff of a spear, and they shall be utterly burned with fire where they stand. These are the mighty men of

David. David sitting in the seat, the wisest prince among three. He himself is like a tender worm of wood, who with a single attack destroyed eight hundred. After him was Eleazar the son of his uncle, among the three mighty men who were with David, when they defied the Philistines who were gathered there to battle. And when the men of Israel had gone away, he stood and struck the Philistines until his hand grew weary, and his hand clung to the sword. And the Lord brought about a great victory that day; and the people returned after him only to take spoil. After him was Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite. And the Philistines were gathered together into a garrison, and there was a piece of ground full of lentils. And the people fled from the Philistines; but he stood in the midst of the field and defended it, and struck the Philistines; and the Lord brought about a great victory. And before this, three of the thirty chief men went down and came to David in the harvest time to the cave of Adullam; and the troop of the Philistines pitched in the valley of the giants. And David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then in Bethlehem. And David longed and said: O that someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem, which is by the gate! And the three mighty men broke through the host of the Philistines and drew water from the well of Bethlehem that was by the gate, and took it and brought it to David. But he would not drink of it, but poured it out to the Lord, saying: Far be it from me, O Lord, that I should do this. Is this not the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives? Therefore he would not drink it. These things did the three mighty men. Abishai also, the brother of Joab the son of Zeruiah, was chief among three. He lifted up his spear against three hundred, whom he slew, and had a name among the three. He was more honored than the three: therefore he was their captain.

. second .

was a prince: but he did not attain to the first three. And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, a valiant man of great deeds from Kabzeel. He struck down two lion-like men of Moab: and he went down and struck a lion in the middle of a pit on a day of snow. He also slew an Egyptian, a man of great stature, who had a spear in his hand. He went down to him with a staff, and wrested the spear out of the Egyptian's hand, and killed him with his own spear. These things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada. He was renowned among the thirty, but he did not attain to the first three. And David set him over his guard. Asahel the brother of Joab was among the thirty: Elhanan the son of his uncle of Bethlehem. Shammah the Harodite. Elika the Harodite. Helez the Paltite. Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. Abiezer the Anathothite. Mebunnai the Hushathite. Zalmon the Ahohite. Maharai the Netophathite. Heleb the son of Baanah, also a Netophathite.
