Amasai son of Telcana, son of Joel, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah, son of Tahath, son of Asir, son of Abiasaph, son of Korah, son of Izhar, son of Levi, son of Israel; and his brother Asaph, who stood at his right hand — Asaph son of Berachiah, son of Shimea, son of Michael, son of Baaseiah, son of Malchijah, son of Ethni, son of Zerah, son of Adaiah, son of Ethan, son of Zimmah, son of Shimei, son of Jahath, son of Gershom, son of Levi. The sons of Merari, their brothers, were on the left: Ethan son of Kishi, son of Abdi, son of Malluch, son of Hashabiah, son of Amaziah, son of Hilkiah, son of Amasai, son of Bani, son of Shemer, son of Mahli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi. Their brothers the Levites were appointed to all the service of the tabernacle of the house of the Lord. But Aaron and his sons offered sacrifices upon the altar of burnt offering and upon the altar of incense, for all the work of the most holy place, and to make atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded. These are the sons of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son, Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son, Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son, Zadok his son, Ahimaaz his son. These are the dwelling places by their settlements within their boundaries, belonging to the sons of Aaron of the families of the Kohathites, for theirs was the first lot. They gave them Hebron in the land of Judah and its surrounding pasturelands, but the fields of the city and its villages they gave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh. And to the sons of Aaron they gave the cities of refuge: Hebron, Libnah with its pasturelands, Jattir, Eshtemoa with its pasturelands, Hilen and Debir with their pasturelands, Ashan, and Beth-shemesh with their pasturelands. And from the tribe of Benjamin: Geba with its pasturelands, Alemeth with its pasturelands, and Anathoth with its pasturelands. All their cities throughout their families were thirteen. To the remaining sons of Kohath were given by lot ten cities from the half-tribe of Manasseh. To the sons of Gershom, according to their families, thirteen cities from the tribe of Issachar, from the tribe of Asher, from the tribe of Naphtali, and from the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan. To the sons of Merari according to their families, twelve cities by lot from the tribe of Reuben, from the tribe of Gad, and from the tribe of Zebulun. The people of Israel gave the Levites the cities and their pasturelands. They gave by lot from the tribe of the people of Judah, from the tribe of the people of Simeon, and from the tribe of the people of Benjamin these cities which are mentioned by name, and which belonged to the families of the Kohathites. They were cities within the territory of the tribe of Ephraim. They gave them Shechem, the city of refuge for the manslayer, with its pasturelands in the hill country of Ephraim, Gezer with its pasturelands, Jokmeam with its pasturelands, Beth-horon likewise, and Aijalon with its pasturelands, and Gath-rimmon in the same manner. From the half-tribe of Manasseh: Aner with its pasturelands, and Bileam with its pasturelands, for the rest of the families of the sons of Kohath. To the sons of Gershom from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan with its pasturelands, and Ashtaroth with its pasturelands. From the tribe of Issachar: Kedesh with its pasturelands, Daberath with its pasturelands, Ramoth with its pasturelands, and Anem with its pasturelands. From the tribe of Asher: Mashal with its pasturelands, Abdon likewise, Hukok with its pasturelands, and Rehob with its pasturelands.

. First.

Furthermore, from the tribe of Naphtali, cities in Galilee and its suburbs: Amon with its suburbs, and Kariathaim and its suburbs. To the remaining sons of Merari, from the tribe of Zebulun: Rimmono and its suburbs, and Tabor with its suburbs. Also across the Jordan, opposite Jericho, on the eastern side of the Jordan, from the tribe of Reuben: Bezer in the wilderness with its suburbs, and Jahaz with its suburbs, and Kedemoth with its suburbs, and Mephaath with its suburbs. Also from the tribe of Gad: Ramoth in Gilead and its suburbs, and Mahanaim with its suburbs, and Heshbon with its suburbs, and Jazer with its suburbs. Chapter VII.

The sons of Issachar: Tola and Puah, Jashub and Shimron, four. The sons of Tola: Uzzi and Rephaiah, and Jeriel and Jahmai, and Jibsam, and Samuel, heads of their father's houses. Of the family of Tola, mighty warriors, numbered in the days of David: twenty-two thousand and seven hundred. The sons of Uzzi: Izrahiah, of whom were born Michael and Obadiah and Joel and Isshiah, five, all of them chief men; and with them, by their generations, after the house of their fathers, were bands of soldiers for war, thirty-six thousand men; for they had many wives and sons. And their brothers among all the families of Issachar, mighty warriors, were eighty-seven thousand in all enrolled. The sons of Benjamin: Bela and Becher and Jediael, three. The sons of Bela: Ezbon and Uzzi and Uzziel and Jerimoth and Iri, five; heads of families, mighty warriors. Their number was twenty-two thousand and thirty-four. The sons of Becher: Zemirah and Joash and Eliezer and Elioenai and Omri and Jerimoth and Abijah and Anathoth and Alemeth. All these were sons of Becher; and they were enrolled by genealogy, as heads of their fathers' houses,

mighty warriors for battle: twenty thousand and two hundred. The sons of Jediael: Bilhan. And the sons of Bilhan: Jeush and Benjamin and Ehud and Chenaanah and Zethan and Tarshish and Ahishahar. All these were sons of Jediael, heads of their fathers' houses, mighty warriors, seventeen thousand and two hundred, fit for service in war. Shuppim and Huppim were the sons of Ir; and Hushim, the son of Aher. The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel and Guni, and Jezer and Shallum, the sons of Bilhah. The son of Manasseh: Asriel, whom his concubine the Aramean bore; she bore Machir the father of Gilead. And Machir took a wife for his sons Huppim and Shuppim, whose sister's name was Maachah; and the name of the second was Zelophehad; and Zelophehad had daughters. And Maachah the wife of Machir bore a son, and she called his name Peresh; and the name of his brother was Sheresh; and his sons were Ulam and Rekem. The son of Ulam: Bedan. These were the sons of Gilead the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh. And his sister Hammolecheth bore Ishhod and Abiezer and Mahlah. And the sons of Shemida were Ahian and Shechem and Likhi and Aniam. The sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah, and Bered his son, and Tahath his son, and Eladah his son, and Tahath his son, and Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son, and Ezer and Elead. The men of Gath who were born in the land slew them, because they came down to take their livestock. And Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him. Then he went in to his wife, and she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Beriah, because disaster had befallen his house. His daughter was Sheerah, who built both Lower and Upper Beth-horon, and Uzzen-sheerah. And his son was Rephah, and Resheph, and Telah,

from whom was born Tahath, who fathered Ladan. His son was Ammihud, who fathered Elishama, from whom came Nun, who took Joshua as his son. The possession and habitation of the sons of Ephraim was Bethel with its towns, and to the east Naaran, to the west side Gaza and its towns, Shechem also with its towns as far as Aiah with its towns; and next to the sons of Manasseh, Beth-shean and its towns, Taanach and its towns, Megiddo and its towns, Dor and its towns. In these dwelt the sons of Joseph, the sons of Israel. The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and Serah their sister. And the sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel, who is the father of Birzaith. Heber fathered Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and Shua their sister. The sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These are the sons of Japhlet. The sons of Shomer: Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram. And the sons of Helem his brother: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal. The sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah, Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera. The sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara. And the sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia. All these were the sons of Asher, heads of the ancestral houses, chosen, mighty warriors, chiefs among the princes. Their number enrolled for military service was twenty-six thousand men.

Benjamin fathered Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, Aharah the third, Nohah the fourth, and Rapha the fifth. And the sons of Bela were Addar, Gera, Abihud, Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah, Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram. These are the sons of Ehud — they were heads of ancestral houses of the inhabitants of Geba, and they were carried into exile to Manahath. And Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera — he carried them into exile — and he fathered Uzza and Ahihud. And Shaharaim fathered children in the country of Moab after he had sent away Hushim and Baara his wives. He fathered by Hodesh his wife: Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam, Jeuz, Sachia, and Mirmah. These were his sons, heads of ancestral houses. And Methushael fathered Ahitob and Elpaal. The sons of Elpaal: Eber, Misham, and Shemed, who built Ono and Lod with its towns. And Beriah and Shema were heads of ancestral houses of the inhabitants of Aijalon, who put to flight the inhabitants of Gath. And Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth, Zebadiah, Arod, Eder, Michael, Ishpah, and Joha were sons of Beriah. And Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber, Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab were the sons of Elpaal. And Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi, Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel, Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath were the sons of Shimei. And Ishpan, Eber, Eliel, Abdon, Zichri, Hanan, Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah, Iphdeiah, and Penuel were the sons of Shashak. And Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah, Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri were the sons of Jeroham. These were the heads of ancestral houses, according to their generations, chiefs. These lived in Jerusalem. In Gibeon lived the father of Gibeon, and the name of his wife was Maacah. His firstborn son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio, Zecher, and Mikloth. And Mikloth fathered Shimeah. They also lived opposite their kinsmen in Jerusalem, with their brothers. Ner fathered Kish, and Kish fathered Saul. And Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal. The son of Jonathan was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal fathered Micah. The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz. And Ahaz fathered Jadah, and Jadah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. And Zimri fathered Moza, and Moza fathered Binea, whose son was Rapha.

from whom Elasa begat Azel. Now Azel had six sons, whose names are these: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These are all the sons of Azel. And the sons of Eshek his brother: Ulam his firstborn, Jehush the second, and Eliphelet the third. And the sons of Ulam were mighty men of valor, archers, and had many sons and grandsons, a hundred and fifty. All these were of the sons of Benjamin. So all Israel was reckoned by genealogies — one hundred [thousand].
And the sum of them was written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah, and they were carried away to Babylon for their transgression. Now those who dwelt in their own possessions in their cities of Israel were the priests, the Levites, and the Nethinim. And in Jerusalem dwelt of the children of Judah and of the children of Benjamin. Of the children of Ephraim and Manasseh: Uthai the son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani. Of the children of Perez, the son of Judah, and of the Shilonites: Asaiah the firstborn and his sons. Of the sons of Zerah: Jeuel and their brethren, six hundred and ninety. Of the children of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hasenuah, and Ibneiah the son of Jeroham, and Elah the son of Uzzi, the son of Michri, and Meshullam the son of Shephatiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah, and their brethren according to their generations, nine hundred and fifty-six. All these men were chief men of their fathers' houses. And of the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin, and Azariah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the ruler of the house of God. And Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pashur, the son of Malchijah, and Maasiai the son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer: and their brethren, heads of their fathers' houses, one thousand seven hundred and sixty, very able men

for the work of the service of the house of God. And of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, and the sons of Azrikam of the sons of Merari. And Bakbakkar, the carpenter, and Galal, and Mattaniah the son of Micah, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph, and Obadiah the son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun, and Berechiah the son of Asa, the son of Elkanah, who dwelt in the villages of the Netophathites. And the gatekeepers: Shallum, and Akkub, and Talmon, and Ahiman, and their brother Shallum was the chief — who until then had waited at the king's gate to the east; these were the gatekeepers for the camp of the children of Levi. And Shallum the son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his brethren of his father's house, the Korahites, were over the work of the service, keepers of the thresholds of the tabernacle, and their fathers had been over the camp of the Lord, keepers of the entry. And Phinehas the son of Eleazar was ruler over them in time past, and the Lord was with him. And Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah was gatekeeper at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. All these, chosen to be gatekeepers at the thresholds, were two hundred and twelve; and they were reckoned by genealogy in their villages, whom David and Samuel the seer established in their office of trust — both them and their sons — over the gates of the house of the Lord and of the tabernacle, according to their ability. By the four winds were the gatekeepers: toward the east, toward the west, toward the north, and toward the south. And their brethren, who were in their villages, came in every seven days from time to time with them. For these four chief gatekeepers were entrusted with the whole number of gatekeepers; and they were over the chambers and over the treasuries of the house of God. And they lodged round about the house of God, because their duty required it, and they had the oversight of the opening of it every morning. And certain of them had charge of the vessels of the ministry; for by number were the vessels brought in and taken out.

They were responsible for it. Of those who had charge of the vessels of the sanctuary, they provided fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense, and spices. The sons of the priests prepared ointments from spices. And Mattithiah, a Levite and firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, was in charge of baking the flat cakes. Among the sons of Kohath, their kinsmen were in charge of preparing the showbread every Sabbath. These are the leaders of the singers, by families of the Levites, who dwelt in the chambers of the temple, free from other service, for they were occupied in their duties day and night. These were the heads of the Levites, chiefs in their family, who lived in Jerusalem. In Gibeon there dwelt the father of Gibeon, Jeiel, and his wife's name was Maacah. His firstborn son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab, Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth. Mikloth fathered Shimeam. These also dwelt alongside their kinsmen in Jerusalem, opposite their relatives. Ner fathered Kish, and Kish fathered Saul. And Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal. The son of Jonathan was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal fathered Micah. The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz. Ahaz fathered Jarah, and Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri fathered Moza, and Moza fathered Binea, whose son Raphaiah fathered Elasah, from whom Azel descended. Azel had six sons, whose names were: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.

Chapter 10. The Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa. The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons, and they killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul. The battle was fierce against Saul, and the archers found him and wounded him with their arrows. Then Saul said to his armor-bearer: "Draw your sword and run me through, lest these uncircumcised come and abuse me." But his armor-bearer would not, for he was greatly afraid. So Saul took his own sword and fell upon it. When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell upon his sword and died. So Saul died, and his three sons died, and all his house died together. When all the men of Israel who were in the valley saw that they had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their cities and fled here and there; and the Philistines came and settled in them. The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa. They stripped him, cut off his head, and took his armor; then they sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to carry the good news to their idols and to the people. They put his armor in the temple of their gods, and fastened his body to the temple of Dagon. When all the men of Jabesh-gilead heard everything that the Philistines had done to Saul, all the valiant men arose and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons and brought them to Jabesh and buried their bones under the oak tree in Jabesh, and they fasted seven days. So Saul died for his unfaithfulness: because he broke faith with the Lord and did not keep his commandment, and also because he consulted a medium and did not seek guidance from the Lord; therefore the Lord put him to death and turned the kingdom over to David the son of Jesse. Chapter 11.

· first ·

All Israel gathered together to David at Hebron, saying: We are your bone and your flesh. Yesterday also and the day before, when Saul was king, it was you who led Israel in and out. And the Lord your God said to you: You shall feed my people Israel, and you shall be prince over them. So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and David made a covenant with them before the Lord. And they anointed David king over Israel, according to the word of the Lord which he had spoken by the hand of Samuel. And David and all Israel went to Jerusalem, which is Jebus, where the Jebusites were, the inhabitants of the land. And the inhabitants of Jebus said to David: You shall not come in here. Nevertheless David took the castle of Zion, which is the city of David. And David said: Whoever shall smite the Jebusite first shall be chief and captain. And Joab the son of Zeruiah went up first, and became chief. And David dwelt in the castle, and therefore it was called the city of David. And he built the city round about, from Millo even round about. And Joab repaired the rest of the city. And David went on and grew great, and the Lord of hosts was with him. These are the chief of the mighty men of David, who helped him to become king over all Israel, according to the word of the Lord to Israel. And this is the number of the mighty men of David: Jashobeam the son of a Hachmonite, the chief of the thirty. He lifted up his spear against three hundred, whom he slew at one time. And after him was Eleazar the son of Dodo, the Ahohite, who was one of the three mighty men. He was with David at Pasdammim, when the Philistines were gathered there to battle. And there was a plot of ground full of barley, and the people fled from before the Philistines. These men

stood in the middle of the field and defended it, and slew the Philistines; and the Lord saved them by a great victory. And three of the thirty chief men went down to the rock to David, into the cave of Adullam, when the host of the Philistines encamped in the valley of Rephaim. And David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was at Bethlehem. And David longed, and said: Oh that one would give me water to drink of the well of Bethlehem, that is at the gate! And the three broke through the host of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem, that was by the gate, and took it, and brought it to David: but David would not drink it, but poured it out to the Lord, saying: God forbid that I should do this; shall I drink the blood of these men who went in jeopardy of their lives? For at the risk of their lives they brought it. Therefore he would not drink it. These things did the three mighty men. And Abishai, the brother of Joab, was chief of the three; and he lifted up his spear against three hundred and slew them; and he had a name among the three. Of the three he was the most honorable, and he became their captain; but he attained not to the first three. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man, who had done many acts in Kabzeel; he slew two lion-like men of Moab. He went down also and slew a lion in a pit in time of snow. And he slew an Egyptian, a man of great stature, five cubits high; and in the Egyptian's hand was a spear like a weaver's beam; and he went down to him with a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian's hand, and slew him with his own spear. These things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and had a name among the three mighty men. He was more honorable than the thirty, but he attained not to the first three. And David set him

David to his own ear. Now the most valiant men of the army: Asahel the brother of Joab, and Elhanan the son of his uncle from Bethlehem: Shammoth the Harodite: Helez the Pelonite: Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite: Abiezer the Anathothite: Sibbecai the Hushathite: Ilai the Ahohite: Maharai the Netophathite: Heled the son of Baanah the Netophathite: Ithai the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the sons of Benjamin: Benaiah the Pirathonite: Hurai of the brooks of Gaash: Abiel the Arbathite: Azmaveth the Baharumite: Eliahba the Shaalbonite: the sons of Hashem the Gizonite: Jonathan the son of Shageh: Ahiam the son of Sacar the Ararite: Eliphal the son of Ur: Hepher the Mecherathite: Ahijah the Pelonite: Hezro the Carmelite: Naarai the son of Ezbai: Joel the brother of Nathan: Mibhar the son of Hagri: Zelek the Ammonite: Naharai the Berothite, the armorbearer of Joab the son of Zeruiah: Ira the Ithrite: Gareb the Ithrite: Uriah the Hittite: Zabad the son of Ahlai: Adina the son of Shiza the Reubenite, a captain of the Reubenites, and thirty with him: Hanan the son of Maachah: and Joshaphat the Mithnite: Uzzia the Ashtarothite: Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hothan the Aroerite: Jediael the son of Shimri, and Joha his brother, the Tizite: Eliel the Mahavite, and Jeribai, and Joshaviah, the sons of Elnaam: and Ithmah the Moabite: Eliel, and Obed, and Jasiel the Mesobaite.

Chapter XII. These also came to David to Ziklag, while he was still hiding from Saul the son of Kish: and they were among the mighty men, helpers of the war. They were armed with bows, and could use both the right hand and the left in hurling stones and shooting arrows. Of the brethren of Saul of Benjamin: the chief was Ahiezer, then Joash, the sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite: and Jeziel, and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth: and Berachah, and Jehu the Anathothite: and Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the thirty, and over the thirty: and Jeremiah, and Jahaziel, and Johanan, and Jozabad the Gederathite: and Eluzai, and Jerimoth:

and Bealiah, and Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite: Elkanah, and Isshiah, and Azareel, and Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korhites: and Joelah, and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham of Gedor. And of the Gadites there separated themselves unto David into the hold in the wilderness, mighty men of valor, men trained for war, that could handle shield and spear: whose faces were like the faces of lions, and they were as swift as the roes upon the mountains. Ezer the first, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third, Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth, Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh, Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth, Jeremiah the tenth, Machbanai the eleventh. These were of the sons of Gad, captains of the host. The least was worth a hundred, and the greatest a thousand. These are they that went over Jordan in the first month, when it had overflowed all its banks; and they put to flight all them of the valleys, both toward the east, and toward the west. And there came of the children of Benjamin and Judah to the hold unto David. And David went out to meet them, and answered and said unto them, If you have come peaceably unto me to help me, my heart shall be knit unto you: but if you have come to betray me to my enemies, seeing there is no wrong in my hands, the God of our fathers look thereon, and rebuke it. Then the Spirit came upon Abishai the chief among the thirty, and he said, We are yours, O David, and on your side, you son of Jesse: peace, peace be unto you, and peace be to your helpers; for your God helps you. Then David received them, and made them captains of the band. And of Manasseh there went over some to David, when he came with the Philistines against Saul to battle: but they helped them not: for the lords of the Philistines upon advisement sent him away, saying, He will fall to his master Saul at the risk of our heads.

their lord Saul. So when he returned to Ziklag, there came over to him from Manasseh, Adnah, and Jozabad, and Jediael, and Michael, and Jozabad, and Elihu, and Zillethai, captains of thousands that were of Manasseh. And they helped David against the band of rovers, for they were all mighty men of valor, and were captains in the host. For at that time day by day there came to David to help him, until it was a great host, like the host of God. And these are the numbers of the bands that were ready armed to the war, and came to David to Hebron, to turn the kingdom of Saul to him, according to the word of the Lord. The children of Judah that bare shield and spear were six thousand and eight hundred, ready armed to the war. Of the children of Simeon, mighty men of valor for the war, seven thousand and one hundred. Of the children of Levi four thousand and six hundred. And Jehoiada was the leader of the Aaronites, and with him were three thousand and seven hundred. And Zadok, a young man mighty of valor, and of his father's house twenty and two captains. And of the children of Benjamin, the kindred of Saul, three thousand: for hitherto the greatest part of them had kept the ward of the house of Saul. And of the children of Ephraim twenty thousand and eight hundred, mighty men of valor, famous throughout the house of their fathers. And of the half tribe of Manasseh eighteen thousand, who were expressed by name, to come and make David king. And of the children of Issachar, which were men that had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do, the heads of them were two hundred. And all their brethren were at their commandment. Of Zebulun, such as went forth to battle, expert in war, with all instruments of war, fifty thousand, which could keep rank: they were not of double heart. And of Naphtali a thousand captains, and with them with shield and spear thirty and seven thousand. And of Dan expert in war twenty and eight thousand and six hundred. And of Asher, such as went forth to battle, expert in war, forty thousand. And on the other side of Jordan, of the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and of the half tribe of Manasseh, with all manner of instruments of war for the battle, an hundred and twenty thousand. All these men of war, that could keep rank, came with a perfect heart to Hebron, to make David king over all Israel: and all the rest also of Israel were of one heart to make David king. And there they were with David three days, eating and drinking: for their brethren had prepared for them. Moreover they that were nigh them, even unto Issachar and Zebulun and Naphtali, brought bread on asses, and on camels, and on mules, and on oxen, and meat, meal, cakes of figs, and bunches of raisins, and wine, and oil, and oxen, and sheep abundantly: for there was joy in Israel. Chapter XIII. And David consulted with the captains of thousands and hundreds, and with every leader. And David said unto all the congregation of Israel, If it seem good unto you, and that it be of the Lord our God, let us send abroad unto our brethren every where, that are left in all the land of Israel, and with them also to the priests and Levites which are in their cities and suburbs, that they may gather themselves unto us. And let us bring again the ark of our God to us: for we enquired not at it in the days of Saul. And all the congregation said that they would do so: for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people. So David gathered all Israel together, from Shihor of Egypt even unto the entering of Hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kirjath-jearim. And David went up, and all Israel, to Baalah, that is, to Kirjath-jearim, which belonged to Judah.

Paralipomenon (Chronicles)

...to bring from there the ark of the Lord God who sits upon the cherubim, upon whom his name is called. And they set the ark of God upon a new cart from the house of Abinadab. And Oza and his brothers drove the cart. And David and all Israel played before God with all their might, with songs and with harps, psalteries, timbrels, cymbals, and trumpets. And when they had come to the threshing floor of Chidon, Oza put forth his hand to hold up the ark, for the ox had stumbled and shaken it a little. And the Lord was angry with Oza, and struck him because he had touched the ark; and he died there before the Lord. And David was grieved because the Lord had struck Oza, and he called that place the Division of Oza, to this day. And David feared God that day, saying: How shall I bring the ark of God to me? And for this reason he did not bring it to himself into the city of David, but he turned it aside into the house of Obededom the Gittite. And the ark of God remained in the house of Obededom three months, and the Lord blessed his house and all that he had.

And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar trees, and workmen in stone and timber, to build him a house. And David perceived that the Lord had confirmed him king over Israel, and that his kingdom was exalted over his people Israel. And David took more wives in Jerusalem, and he fathered more sons and daughters. Now these are the names of those who were born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua and Shobab, Nathan and Solomon, and Ibhar and Elishua and Elphalet, and Nogah and Nepheg and Japhia, and Elishama and Beeliada and Eliphalet. When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David. And when David heard of it, he went out against them. The Philistines came and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim. And David inquired of the Lord, saying: Shall I go up against the Philistines, and will you deliver them into my hand? And the Lord said to him: Go up, and I will deliver them into your hand. And when they had gone up to Baalperazim, David struck them there, and said: God has divided my enemies by my hand, like the dividing of waters; therefore the name of that place was called Baalperazim. And they left their gods there, and David gave order that they be burned. The Philistines again made a raid, and were spread in the valley. And David inquired again of God, and God said to him: Do not go up after them; turn away from them and come upon them over against the pear trees. And when you shall hear the sound of one moving in the tops of the pear trees, then you shall go out to battle, for God has gone forth before you to strike the army of the Philistines. And David did as God commanded him, and struck the army of the Philistines from Gibeon to Gezer. And the fame of David went out into all lands, and the Lord brought the fear of him upon all nations.

And he built houses for himself in the city of David, and prepared a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it. Then David said: No one may carry the ark of God except the Levites, whom the Lord has chosen to carry it and to minister to him forever. And David gathered all Israel to Jerusalem, to bring the ark of God to the place which he had prepared for it; and also the sons of Aaron and the Levites. Of the sons of Caath: Uriel the chief, and his brothers two hundred and twenty. Of the sons of Merari: Asaiah the chief, and his brothers two hundred and twenty. Of the sons of Gershon: Joel the chief...

Paralipomenon (Chronicles)

You have bestowed so many benefits upon him, and you began to bless the house of your servant, that it might continue always before you. For you, O Lord, have blessed it, and it shall be blessed forever.

After these things it came to pass that David struck the Philistines and humbled them, and took Gath and its villages out of the hand of the Philistines. And he struck Moab, and the Moabites became servants of David, bringing tribute. At that time David also struck Hadadezer, king of Zobah of the region of Hamath, when he went to extend his dominion to the river Euphrates. And David took from him a thousand chariots, and seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. He also hamstrung all the chariot horses, keeping back enough for a hundred chariots. And when the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck twenty-two thousand of them. And he put garrisons in Syria of Damascus, so that Syria also served David and brought tribute. And the Lord preserved David wherever he went. And David took the golden shields that the servants of Hadadezer carried, and brought them to Jerusalem. Also from Tibhath and from Cun, cities of Hadadezer, David took very much bronze, with which Solomon made the bronze sea, the pillars, and the bronze vessels. When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the army of Hadadezer king of Zobah, he sent Hadoram his son to King David, to greet him and to congratulate him for having fought and conquered Hadadezer, for Tou had been at war with Hadadezer. And all the vessels of gold and silver and bronze, David King consecrated to the Lord, along with the silver and gold that he had taken from all the nations: from Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and Amalek. Abishai the son of Zeruiah also struck the Edomites

in the Valley of Salt, eighteen thousand of them, and he put garrisons in Edom, so that all the Edomites became servants of David. And the Lord preserved David wherever he went. So David reigned over all Israel, and he administered judgment and justice to all his people. Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder. Zadok the son of Ahitub and Abimelech the son of Abiathar were priests; Shavsha was secretary. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites. And David's sons were the chief officials at the king's side.

Now it came to pass after this that Nahash the king of the Ammonites died, and his son Hanun reigned in his place. And David said, "I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, for his father showed kindness to me." So David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. And when David's servants came to the land of the Ammonites to comfort Hanun, the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun, "Do you think that David is honoring your father because he has sent comforters to you? Have you not considered that his servants have come to you to search and to overthrow and to spy out the land?" So Hanun took David's servants, shaved them, cut off their garments at the hips, and sent them away. When they told David about the men, he sent messengers to meet them, for the men were greatly ashamed. And the king said, "Stay at Jericho until your beards grow, and then return." When the Ammonites saw that they had made themselves odious to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Mesopotamia, Syria, and Maacah, and from Zobah. And they hired thirty-two thousand chariots,

. first .

and king Maacah with his own men. When they had come, they encamped in the region of Medeba. And the children of Ammon also gathered from their cities and came to battle. When David heard of it, he sent Joab and all the army of mighty men. And the children of Ammon went out and set the battle in array before the gate of the city. But the kings who had come to his aid stood apart in the field. So Joab, seeing that the battle was set against him both in front and behind, chose out some of the best men of all Israel and went against the Syrians. The rest of the people he gave into the hand of Abishai his brother, and they went against the children of Ammon. He said: If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you shall help me; but if the children of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will help you. Be of good courage and let us be strong for our people and for the cities of our God. And let the Lord do what seems good in his sight. So Joab and the people with him went before the Syrians to battle, and they fled before him. And when the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled, they likewise fled before Abishai his brother and entered the city. So Joab returned to Jerusalem. But when the Syrians saw that they had been defeated before Israel, they sent messengers and brought out the Syrians that were beyond the river. Sophat, the commander of the army of Hadadezer, was their leader. And when it was told David, he gathered all Israel and crossed over the Jordan and came against them and set the battle in array against them. But the Syrians fled before Israel, and David killed of the Syrians seven thousand charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers, and also killed Sophat the commander of the army. And when the servants of Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with David and served him. And the Syrians would no longer

give help to the children of Ammon. Chapter XX.

Now it came to pass at the turn of the year, at the time when kings go out to battle, that Joab led out the army and ravaged the land of the children of Ammon. He came and besieged Rabbah. But David remained at Jerusalem when Joab attacked Rabbah and destroyed it. And David took the crown of Milcom from his head and found in it a talent of gold weight, and the most precious gems; and it was set upon David's head, and he also brought out very much plunder of the city. And he brought out the people who were in it and set them to work with saws and iron picks and axes. Thus David dealt with all the cities of the children of Ammon, and then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem. After this there arose war with the Philistines at Gezer, in which Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Sippai, who was one of the descendants of the giants; and they were subdued. And there was war again with the Philistines, in which Elhanan the son of Jair the Bethlehemite killed the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver's beam. And there was again war at Gath, where there was a man of great stature who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in number; and he also was descended from the giants. He defied Israel, and Jonathan the son of Shimea, David's brother, struck him down. These were descended from the giants in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

Then Satan rose up against Israel Chapter XXI

and incited David to number Israel. So David said to Joab and to the commanders of the people: Go, number Israel from Beersheba to Dan, and bring me a report that I may know the number. But Joab answered: May the Lord increase the people

· Paralipomenon (Chronicles) ·

Are not all of them, O Lord, my lord's servants? Why does my lord require this, so that it should be imputed as a sin to Israel? But the king's word prevailed. So Joab departed and went throughout all Israel, and returned to Jerusalem. And David received the number of the people, which was found to be in all Israel one million one hundred thousand men who drew the sword. And of Judah four hundred and seventy thousand fighting men. But Levi and Benjamin he did not number, because the king's command was abhorrent to him. And God was displeased with this thing, and he struck Israel. And David said to God: I have sinned greatly in doing this. I beseech you, take away the iniquity of your servant, for I have acted very foolishly. And the Lord spoke to Gad, David's seer, saying: Go and speak to David, and say to him: Thus says the Lord. I offer you three choices; choose one of them, that I may do it to you. And when Gad came to David, he said to him: Thus says the Lord. Choose: either three years of famine, or three months of fleeing before your enemies and being unable to escape their sword, or three days of the sword of the Lord and pestilence in the land and the angel of the Lord destroying throughout all the territory of Israel. Now then, consider what answer I shall return to him who sent me. And David said to Gad: I am in great distress; but let me fall into the hand of the Lord, for his mercy is very great; but let me not fall into the hand of man. So the Lord sent pestilence upon Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell. And God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it. Sufficient —

now, let your hand be stayed. And the angel of the Lord stood by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. And David lifted up his eyes and saw the angel of the Lord standing between earth and heaven, with a drawn sword in his hand, stretched out over Jerusalem. Then David and the elders fell on their faces, clothed in sackcloth. And David said to God: Was it not I who gave the command to count the people? It is I who have sinned and done great evil; but these sheep, what have they done? O Lord my God, let your hand be against me and against my father's house, but do not let your people be plagued. Then the angel of the Lord commanded Gad to tell David that David should go up and erect an altar to the Lord on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. So David went up at the word of Gad, which he had spoken in the name of the Lord. Now Ornan turned and saw the angel, and his four sons who were with him hid themselves. Now Ornan was threshing wheat. And as David came to Ornan, Ornan looked and saw David, and went out from the threshing floor and bowed before David with his face to the ground. And David said to Ornan: Give me the place of your threshing floor, that I may build on it an altar to the Lord — give it to me at its full price — so that the plague may be averted from the people. And Ornan said to David: Take it, and let my lord the king do what seems good to him; see, I give the oxen for burnt offerings and the threshing sledges for the wood and the wheat for the grain offering — I give it all. But King David said to Ornan: No, I will buy it for the full price; I will not take for the Lord what is yours, nor offer burnt offerings that cost me nothing. So David paid Ornan for the site six hundred shekels of gold by weight. And David built there an altar to the Lord and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

And he called upon God, and God answered him with fire from heaven upon the altar of burnt offering. And the Lord commanded the angel, and he put his sword back into its sheath. Then David, seeing that the Lord had heard him at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, made offerings there. But the tabernacle of the Lord which Moses had made in the desert, and the altar of burnt offerings, were at that time on the high place at Gibeon, and David could not go there to seek God, for he was greatly terrified by the sword of the angel of the Lord. Chapter 22.

And David said: This is the house of God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel. And he commanded that all the foreigners in the land of Israel be gathered, and he set stonecutters among them to hew and polish stones for building the house of God. He also prepared iron in great quantity for the nails of the doors and for the joints and hinges, and an immeasurable amount of bronze. Timber in abundance, cedar wood beyond reckoning, was brought to David by the Sidonians and Tyrians. And David said: My son Solomon is still young and tender. The house that is to be built for the Lord must be of such grandeur that it will be renowned in all lands. I will therefore make preparation for it. So before his death David made all the preparations. Then he called Solomon his son and commanded him to build a house for the Lord God of Israel. And David said to Solomon: My son, it was my desire to build a house to the name of the Lord my God. But the word of the Lord came to me, saying: You have shed much blood and have waged many wars; therefore you shall not build a house to my name, for you have shed so much blood before me. But a son shall be born to you; he shall be a man of peace. And I will give him rest from all his enemies round about.

For his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quiet to Israel in all his days. He shall build a house to my name, and he shall be my son and I will be his father; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever. Now therefore, my son, the Lord be with you, and may you prosper and build the house of the Lord your God, as he has spoken concerning you. May the Lord give you wisdom and understanding, that you may govern Israel and keep the law of the Lord your God. Then you shall prosper, if you keep the commandments and ordinances which the Lord commanded Moses for Israel. Be strong and courageous; do not be afraid or dismayed. Behold, in my poverty I have prepared for the house of the Lord a hundred thousand talents of gold, a thousand thousand talents of silver, and bronze and iron beyond weighing, for there is so much. I have also prepared timber and stone for all the needs. You have many craftsmen: stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and skilled workers in every craft, in gold, silver, bronze, and iron, beyond number. Rise therefore and work, and the Lord be with you. David also commanded all the leaders of Israel to help Solomon his son, saying: Is not the Lord your God with you? Has he not given you rest on every side? For he has delivered the enemies of the land into my hands, and the land is subdued before the Lord and before his people. Now therefore devote your hearts and souls to seeking the Lord your God. Arise and build the sanctuary of the Lord God, so that the ark of the covenant of the Lord and the holy vessels of God may be brought into the house that is to be built for the name of the Lord. Chapter 23.

· Paralipomenon (Chronicles) ·

Then David, old and full of days, made Solomon his son king over Israel, and gathered together all the princes of Israel, and the priests and Levites. The Levites were numbered from twenty years old and upward, and there were found thirty-eight thousand men. Of these, twenty-four thousand were chosen and appointed to oversee the work of the house of the Lord; six thousand were officers and judges; four thousand were gatekeepers, and four thousand praised the Lord with instruments which David had made for giving praise. And David distributed them into divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Of the sons of Gershon: Ladan and Shimei. The sons of Ladan: the chief was Jehiel, then Zethan and Joel, three. The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran, three. These were the heads of the families of Ladan. And the sons of Shimei: Lahath, Ziza, Jeush, and Beriah, four. Lahath was the first and Ziza the second. But Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, and therefore they were counted as one family and one household. The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, four. The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. And Aaron was set apart to minister in the holy of holies, he and his sons forever, and to burn incense before the Lord according to his rite, and to bless his name forever. The sons of Moses the man of God were also numbered among the tribe of Levi. The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer. The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the first. And the sons of Eliezer were: Rehabiah the first, and Eliezer had no other sons. But the sons of Rehabiah were very many. Of the sons of Izhar: Shelomith the first. Of the sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekameam the fourth. Of the sons of Uzziel: Micah the first, Isshiah the second. The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli:

Eleazar and Kish. But Eleazar died and had no sons, only daughters; and the sons of Kish, their kinsmen, took them as wives. The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth, three. These are the sons of Levi according to their families and their fathers' houses, the chiefs according to their divisions, by the number of their names individually, who did the work of the service of the house of the Lord from twenty years old and upward. For David said: The Lord God of Israel has given rest to his people and has made his dwelling in Jerusalem forever. The Levites shall no longer carry the tabernacle and all its vessels for its service. So according to the last commands of David, the Levites were numbered from twenty years old and upward, and they were placed under the hand of the sons of Aaron for the service of the house of the Lord, in the courts and in the chambers, and in the purification of all holy things, and in the work of the service of the house of God. The priests were over the bread of the Presence and the offerings of fine flour, and the unleavened wafers, and the pan-cakes, and the frying, and for all weight and measure. And the Levites were to stand every morning to give thanks and praise to the Lord, and likewise in the evening, and at every offering of burnt offerings to the Lord on sabbaths, new moons, and feasts, by number according to the ordinance concerning them, continually before the Lord. And they shall keep the charge of the tent of meeting and the charge of the sanctuary, and shall attend to the sons of Aaron their brothers, for the service of the house of the Lord. Chapter XXIV.

Now these were the divisions of the sons of Aaron. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. But Nadab and Abihu died before their father and had no children, so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests. And David with Zadok of the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar divided them according to

their turns and their ministry: and there were found many more sons of Eleazar among the chief men than sons of Ithamar. And he divided them, that is, the sons of Eleazar, as rulers of the house, sixteen in number, and of the sons of Ithamar, by their families, eight. And he divided them both by lot, the one to the other; for there were governors of the sanctuary, and governors of the house of God, both from the sons of Eleazar and from the sons of Ithamar. And Shemaiah the son of Nethaneel the scribe, a Levite, wrote them before the king and the princes, and Zadok the priest and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the heads of the families of the priests and Levites, one father's house being taken for Eleazar, and one for Ithamar. Now the first lot fell to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah, the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim, the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin, the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah, the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah, the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim, the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab, the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer, the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Aphses, the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezekel, the twenty-first to Jachin, the twenty-second to Gamul, the twenty-third to Delaiah, the twenty-fourth to Maaziah. These were their appointments for their ministry to come into the house of the Lord according to their ordinance under the hand of Aaron their father, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded him. And of the rest of the sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shubael; and of the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah. Concerning Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah the first. Of the Izharites: Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath. And the sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekameam the fourth. Of the sons of Uzziel: Michah; of the sons of Michah, Shamir. The brother of Michah: Isshiah; of the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah. The sons of Merari:

Mahli and Mushi; the sons of Jaaziah: Beno. And the sons of Merari by Jaaziah: Beno and Shoham and Zaccur and Ibri. Of Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons. Concerning Kish: the sons of Kish; Jerahmeel. Also the sons of Mushi: Mahli and Eder and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites after the house of their fathers. These also cast lots over against their brethren the sons of Aaron in the presence of David the king, and Zadok and Ahimelech, and the chief of the fathers of the priests and Levites, both the chief fathers and also the younger of his brethren alike.

Moreover David and the captains of the army separated to the service the sons of Asaph and of Heman and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals, and the number of the workmen according to their service was. Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur and Joseph and Nethaniah and Asarelah, the sons of Asaph under the hand of Asaph, who prophesied according to the order of the king. Of Jeduthun: the sons of Jeduthun, Gedaliah and Zeri and Jeshaiah and Hashabiah and Mattithiah, under the hand of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with a harp, to give thanks and to praise the Lord. Of Heman: the sons of Heman; Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel and Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti and Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir and Mahazioth. All these were the sons of Heman the king's seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn. And God gave to Heman fourteen sons and three daughters. All these were under the hands of their father for song in the house of the Lord, with cymbals, psalteries, and harps, for the service of the house of God, according to the king's order to Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman. So the number of them, with their brethren that were instructed in the songs of the Lord, all that were cunning, was two hundred fourscore and eight. And they cast lots for their offices, the small as well as the great, the teacher as well as the scholar.

Paralipomenon (Chronicles).

...these were lesser, both alike. The first lot fell to Joseph, who was of Asaph; the second to Gedaliah, to him and his sons and his brothers, twelve; the third to Zaccur, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the fourth to Izri, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the fifth to Nethaniah, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the sixth to Bukkiah, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the seventh to Jesharelah, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the eighth to Jeshaiah, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the ninth to Mattaniah, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the tenth to Shimei, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the eleventh to Azarel, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the twelfth to Hashabiah, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the thirteenth to Shubael, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the fourteenth to Mattithiah, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the fifteenth to Jeremoth, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the sixteenth to Hananiah, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the seventeenth to Joshbekashah, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the eighteenth to Hanani, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the nineteenth to Mallothi, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the twentieth to Eliathah, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the twenty-first to Hothir, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the twenty-second to Giddalti, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the twenty-third to Mahazioth, to his sons and his brothers, twelve; the twenty-fourth to Romamti-ezer, to his sons and his brothers, twelve. Now the divisions of the gatekeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah the son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph. The sons of Meshelemiah: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth, Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Eliehoenai the seventh. The sons of Obed-edom: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sachar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth, Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peullethai the eighth; for God blessed him. Also to Shemaiah his son were sons born who ruled over their father's house, for they were mighty men of valor. The sons of Shemaiah: Othni, and Rephael, and Obed, Elzabad, whose brothers were strong men — Elihu also, and Semachiah. All these of the sons of Obed-edom; they and their sons and their brothers, able men in strength for the service, sixty-two of Obed-edom. Meshelemiah's sons and brothers, eighteen strong men. Also Hosah, of the sons of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief (for though he was not the firstborn, his father made him chief), Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth. All the sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen. These were the divisions of the gatekeepers, so that the chief gatekeepers, like their brothers, should always minister in the house of the Lord. They cast lots equally, small and great alike, by their families, for every gate. The lot for the east gate fell to Shelemiah. Then for Zechariah his son, a prudent counselor, they cast lots, and his lot came out for the north. To Obed-edom and his sons fell the south, where the house of the council of elders was. Shuppim and Hosah were to the west, by the gate of Shallecheth, on the ascending road, guard opposite guard. To the east were six Levites, to the north four per day, to the south four per day, and to the storehouse two and two. In the chambers of the gatekeepers to the west were four on the road and two at the chambers. These are the divisions of the gatekeepers of the sons of Korah and Merari. And Ahijah was over the treasuries of the house of the Lord.

This Shelomith and his brothers were over all the treasuries of the dedicated things which David the king and the heads of families, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the captains of the army, had dedicated, from battles and from the spoils of war, which they had consecrated to maintain the house of the Lord. And all that Samuel the seer and Saul the son of Kish and Abner the son of Ner and Joab the son of Zeruiah had dedicated — all dedicated things were in the care of Shelomith and his brothers. Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed for outside duties over Israel, as officers and judges. Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, men of valor, one thousand seven hundred, had the oversight of Israel westward of the Jordan for all the work of the Lord and for the service of the king. As for the Hebronites, Jerijah was the chief, according to the generations of his families. In the fortieth year of the reign of David, a search was made and men of great valor were found at Jazer of Gilead; and his brothers, two thousand seven hundred men of valor, heads of families, whom David the king appointed over the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, for every matter pertaining to God and the king.

The sons of Israel according to their number, the heads of families, the commanders of thousands and hundreds and their officers who served the king in all matters of the monthly divisions — each division numbering twenty-four thousand. Over the first division for the first month was Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel, and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
Of the sons of Perez, he was chief of all the commanders for the first month. The second month's division was under Dodai the Ahohite; in the fourth, Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him; and in his division were twenty-four thousand. The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; and in his division were twenty-four thousand. The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, of the sons of Ephraim; and in his division were twenty-four thousand. The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbechai the Hushathite, of the family of Zerah; and in his division were twenty-four thousand. The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, of the sons of Benjamin; and in his division were twenty-four thousand. The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, of the family of Zerah; and in his division were twenty-four thousand. The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the sons of Ephraim; and in his division were twenty-four thousand. The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, of the family of Othniel; and in his division were twenty-four thousand.

Families. Over the tribes of Israel the rulers were: over the Reubenites, Eliezer the son of Zichri; over the Simeonites, Shephatiah the son of Maachah; over the Levites, Hashabiah the son of Kemuel; over the Aaronites, Zadok; over Judah, Elihu, the brother of David; over Issachar, Omri the son of Michael; over Zebulun, Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah; over Naphtali, Jerimoth the son of Azriel; over the children of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Azaziah; over the half tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Pedaiah; and over the half tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo the son of Zechariah; over Benjamin, Jaasiel the son of Abner; over Dan, Azarel the son of Jeroham. These were the princes of the children of Israel. But David did not number those who were twenty years old and under, because the Lord had said he would multiply Israel like the stars of heaven. Joab the son of Zeruiah had begun to number them but did not finish, because wrath had fallen upon Israel on account of this; and therefore the number was not recorded in the chronicles of King David. Over the treasuries of the king was Azmaveth the son of Adiel; and over the storehouses in the cities, in the villages and in the towers was Jonathan the son of Uzziah. Over those who did the work of the field for tilling of the ground was Ezri the son of Chelub; over the vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite; over the produce of the vineyards for the wine cellars was Zabdi the Shiphmite. Over the olive trees and the sycamore trees in the lowlands was Baal-hanan the Gederite; and over the cellars of oil was Joash. Over the herds that fed in Sharon was Shitrai the Sharonite; and over the herds in the valleys was Shaphat the son of Adlai. Over the camels was Obil the Ishmaelite; and over the donkeys was Jehdeiah the Meronothite; over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite. All these were the stewards of King David's property. Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counselor, a wise and learned man; and Jehiel the son of Hachmoni was with the king's sons.

Ahithophel also was the king's counselor, and Hushai the Archite was the king's friend. After Ahithophel was Jehoiada the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar. The commander of the king's army was Joab. Chapter XXVIII.

And David assembled all the princes of Israel, the leaders of the tribes and the commanders of the divisions that served the king, and the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, and the stewards over all the property and possessions of the king and of his sons, together with the officers and the mighty men, all the valiant warriors, to Jerusalem. Then David the king stood up and said: Hear me, my brothers and my people. I had it in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the Lord and for the footstool of our God, and I had made preparations to build it. But God said to me: You shall not build a house for my name, because you are a man of war and have shed blood. Yet the Lord God of Israel chose me from all the house of my father to be king over Israel forever; for he chose Judah to be the leader, and of the house of Judah the house of my father; and among the sons of my father he was pleased to make me king over all Israel. And of all my sons — for the Lord has given me many sons — he has chosen Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel. And he said to me: It is Solomon your son who shall build my house and my courts. For I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father; and I will establish his kingdom forever, if he continues resolute in keeping my commandments and my ordinances, as he is today. Now therefore, in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of the Lord, and in the hearing of our God, observe and seek out all the commandments of the Lord our God, that you may possess this good land and leave it as an inheritance to your children after you forever. And you, Solomon my son,

First

Know the God of your father, and serve him with a perfect heart and a willing mind. For the Lord searches all hearts and understands every thought of the mind. If you seek him, you will find him; but if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever. Now therefore, since the Lord has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary, be strong and do it. And David gave Solomon his son the plan of the porch and of the temple, and its treasuries, and its upper rooms, and its inner chambers, and the room for the mercy seat; and the plan of all that he had in mind for the courts of the house of the Lord, all the surrounding chambers, the treasuries of the house of God, and the treasuries for dedicated gifts; the divisions of the priests and the Levites, and all the work of the service of the house of the Lord; for all the vessels for the service in the house of the Lord, the weight of gold for all vessels of each use, the weight of silver for all vessels of each use; the weight of the golden lampstands and their lamps, the weight of gold for each lampstand and its lamps; and likewise silver by weight for each silver lampstand and its lamps; and the weight of gold for each table for the showbread, and likewise silver for the silver tables; and for the forks, the basins, and the cups of pure gold; for the golden bowls by weight for each bowl; and likewise for silver bowls, by weight for each bowl; for the altar of incense made of refined gold, and its weight; also his plan for the golden chariot of the cherubim that spread their wings and covered the ark of the covenant of the Lord. All this, said David, the Lord made me understand in writing by his hand upon me, all the works of this plan.

And David said to Solomon his son: Be strong and courageous and do it. Do not be afraid or dismayed, for the Lord God, my God, is with you. He will not leave you or forsake you, until all the work for the service of the house of the Lord is finished. And behold, the divisions of the priests and the Levites for all the service of the house of God are ready to help you in all the work, and also every willing craftsman for any kind of service; and the leaders and all the people will be entirely at your command. Chapter XXIX.

And David the king spoke to all the assembly: Solomon my son, whom alone God has chosen, is young and inexperienced, and the work is great, for the palace will not be for man but for the Lord God. So I have provided with all my might for the house of my God: gold for the things of gold, silver for the things of silver, bronze for the things of bronze, iron for the things of iron, and wood for the things of wood; onyx stones, stones for setting, stones of antimony, and stones of various colors; and all precious stones and marble stones in abundance. Moreover, in addition to all that I have provided for the holy house, I have a treasure of my own of gold and silver, and because of my devotion to the house of my God I give it to the house of my God: three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, for overlaying the walls of the house; for gold for the things of gold, and silver for the things of silver, and for all the work done by craftsmen. Who then will offer willingly, consecrating himself today to the Lord? Then the leaders of fathers' houses made their freewill offerings, as did also the leaders of the tribes of Israel, and the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officers over the king's work. They gave for the service of the house of God five thousand talents of gold, ten thousand darics, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, a hundred thousand talents of iron. And whoever had precious stones

· Paralipomenon (Chronicles) ·

They gave to the treasuries of the house of the Lord by the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite. And the people rejoiced when they voluntarily offered their vows, because with a whole heart they offered them to the Lord. And David the king also rejoiced with great joy, and he blessed the Lord before all the multitude, and said: Blessed are you, O Lord God of Israel our father, from everlasting to everlasting. Yours, O Lord, is greatness and power and glory and victory, and to you is praise. All things that are in heaven and in earth are yours. Yours, O Lord, is the kingdom, and you are above all princes. Riches are yours, and glory is yours; you rule over all. In your hand is strength and power; in your hand is greatness and the empire of all things. Now therefore our God, we give thanks to you, and we praise your glorious name. Who am I and what is my people, that we should be able to promise all these things to you? All things are yours, and we have given you what we received from your hand. For we are sojourners before you and strangers, as were all our fathers. Our days upon the earth are as a shadow, and there is no stay. O Lord our God, all this store that we have prepared to build a house to your holy name, is from your hand, and all is yours. I know, my God, that you test hearts and love simplicity; therefore I, in the simplicity of my heart, have joyfully offered all these things; and I have seen with great joy your people who are gathered here offering their gifts to you. O Lord God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Israel our fathers, keep forever this will of their hearts, and let this mind remain always in the devotion of you. And grant to Solomon my son a perfect heart, that he may keep your commandments, your testimonies and your ceremonies,

and do all things, and build the temple for which I have made provision. And David commanded all the assembly: Bless the Lord our God. And all the assembly blessed the Lord God of their fathers, and they bowed down and worshipped God, and then the king. And they sacrificed victims to the Lord, and offered holocausts the next day: a thousand bullocks, a thousand rams, a thousand lambs, with their libations, and every rite most abundantly for all Israel. And they ate and drank before the Lord that day with great joy, and they anointed Solomon the son of David a second time. And they anointed him to the Lord as ruler, and Zadok as high priest. And Solomon sat on the throne of the Lord as king in place of David his father, and all were pleased with him; and all Israel obeyed him. And all the princes and the mighty men, and all the sons of king David gave their hand and submitted to Solomon the king. And the Lord magnified Solomon over all Israel, and gave him the glory of a kingdom such as no king of Israel had before him. Thus David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel, and the days that he reigned over Israel were forty years. In Hebron he reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem thirty years; and he died in a good old age, full of days, riches and glory; and Solomon his son reigned in his place. Now the acts of king David, first and last, are written in the book of Samuel the seer, and in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the book of Gad the seer, and of all his reign and his might, and the times that passed under him, whether in Israel or in all the kingdoms of the countries.
Here ends the first book of Paralipomenon.
Here begins the second: Chapter one.

Paralipomenon (Chronicles)

For our God is above all gods. But who is able to build him a worthy house? If heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain him, how much less am I able to build him a house? But this much I can do: to burn incense before him. Send me therefore a skilled man who knows how to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, purple and crimson and violet, and who knows how to engrave, to work alongside the craftsmen whom I have with me in Judea and Jerusalem, whom David my father appointed. Also send me cedar wood and juniper and pine from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut timber in Lebanon. My servants shall work with yours, to prepare timber in abundance for me. The house which I desire to build is great and magnificent. I will give as food for your servants who cut the timber: twenty thousand measures of wheat, twenty thousand measures of barley, and twenty thousand measures of oil. Hiram king of Tyre answered in a letter which he sent to Solomon: Because the Lord loves his people, he has made you king over them. And he added: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who gave King David a wise, learned, intelligent and prudent son, to build a house for the Lord and a palace for himself. I am sending you a skilled and learned man, Hiram my master, the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, whose father was a Tyrian, who knows how to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, stone and wood, purple and violet, fine linen and crimson, and who knows how to engrave any kind of engraving and to devise whatever may be necessary, together with your craftsmen and the craftsmen of my lord David your father.

So now, the wheat and barley and oil and wine which you promised, my lord, send to your servants. We will cut as much timber from Lebanon as you need, and we will bring it to you by sea on rafts to Joppa, and it will be for you to transport it to Jerusalem. Solomon then numbered all the foreigners who were in the land of Israel, after the census which David his father had taken of them, and there were found to be fifty-three thousand six hundred. He set seventy thousand of them to bear burdens, and eighty thousand to hew stone in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred as overseers of the people's work. Chapter III.

Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, which had been shown to David his father, in the place which David had prepared in the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. He began to build in the second month of the fourth year of his reign. These are the foundations which Solomon laid for the building of the house of God: the length in cubits after the first measure was sixty cubits, and the breadth twenty cubits. The porch which was in front stretched along the breadth of the house, twenty cubits, and the height was a hundred and twenty cubits. He overlaid it within with pure gold. He covered the larger house with planks of fir wood, and overlaid them with fine gold, and engraved on them palm trees and chain-like patterns. He also paved the floor of the temple with precious stone of great beauty. The gold was of the finest quality, with which he covered the house, its beams, its doorposts, its walls and its doors, and he carved cherubim on the walls. He also made the house

. Second Kings (or Chronicles) .

of the holy of holies, in length according to the width of the house, twenty cubits, and likewise twenty cubits in width. And he covered it with pure gold, as with talents fashioned, and he made golden nails, so that each nail weighed fifty shekels. The upper rooms he also covered with gold. He also made in the house of the holy of holies two cherubim of carved work and covered them with gold. The wings of the cherubim were spread twenty cubits: so that one wing was five cubits long and touched the wall of the house, and the other wing five cubits long touched the wing of the other cherub. Likewise the other cherub's wing was five cubits and touched the wall, and its other wing of five cubits joined to the wing of the other cherub. So the wings of both cherubim spread twenty cubits. They stood upright on their feet, and their faces were turned toward the outer house. He also made a veil of violet, purple, scarlet, and fine linen, and wove cherubim into it. Before the doors of the temple he made two columns, which were thirty-five cubits high. And their capitals, which were five cubits, as well as small chain-work above the oracle, and he set them upon the tops of the columns. He also made a hundred pomegranates which he interspersed among the chainwork. These columns he set up in the porch of the temple: one on the right and the other on the left. The one on the right he called Jachin and the one on the left he called Boaz. Chapter 4.
He also made a bronze altar, twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide and ten cubits high. He also made a molten sea of bronze, ten cubits from brim to brim, round in shape, five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits measured its circumference. Beneath it was the likeness of oxen. And for ten cubits, certain ornaments on the outside circled around it in two rows, surrounding the sea. The oxen were cast, and the sea was set upon twelve oxen: three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east, with the sea resting upon them. The hindquarters of the oxen were toward the inside. The thickness of it was a handbreadth, and its brim was shaped like the brim of a cup, or a lily blossom; it held three thousand measures. He also made ten basins and placed five on the right and five on the left, so that they could wash in them everything that was offered for burnt offerings. But the priests washed in the sea. He also made ten golden lampstands according to the design that had been ordered, and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left. He also made ten tables and set them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left. He also made a hundred golden bowls. He also built a court for the priests and a great hall, and doors for the hall which he overlaid with bronze. The sea he set on the right side toward the east, toward the south. Hiram also made the pots, the shovels, and the bowls, and completed all the work that King Solomon assigned him in the house of God: namely, two columns and their capitals and the network that covered the capitals on top of the pillars; the pomegranates and the two networks, so that two rows of pomegranates were attached to each network to cover the capitals upon the pillars. He also made bases and basins, which he placed upon them.

· Chronicles ·

basins: one sea with twelve oxen beneath it and lavers and bowls and basins. All the vessels that Hiram made for Solomon in the house of the Lord were of burnished bronze. In the plain of Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredath. And the number of the vessels was so great that the weight of the bronze was not determined. And Solomon made all the vessels for the house of God: the golden altar and the tables upon which the showbread was set.
