Likewise the lampstands with their lamps, to burn before the oracle, of purest gold. And certain flowers and lamps and golden tongs, all were made of the purest gold. The bowls also, and censers and basins and small mortars, all of purest gold. And he engraved the doors of the inner temple, that is, of the holy of holies, and the outer doors of the temple, of gold. Thus was completed all the work that Solomon made for the house of the Lord. Chapter V.
Then Solomon brought in all the things that David his father had dedicated, the silver and the gold, and all the vessels, and placed them in the treasuries of the house of the Lord. After this he assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, and the princes of the families of the children of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which is Zion. And all the men of Israel assembled to king Solomon on the feast day in the seventh month. And when all the elders of Israel were come, the Levites took up the ark and carried it, and brought it and all the furnishings of the tabernacle. Now the priests and the Levites carried the vessels of the sanctuary that were in the tabernacle. And king Solomon and all the congregation of Israel that were assembled before the ark, sacrificed sheep and oxen without number. So great was the multitude of the victims.

And the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the Lord to its place, that is, to the oracle of the temple, into the holy of holies, under the wings of the cherubim: so that the cherubim spread out their wings over the place where the ark was, and covered the ark itself and its staves. Now the staves by which the ark was carried were so long that their ends could be seen before the oracle. But if anyone were slightly outside, they could not see them. And the ark was there to this present day. There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets which Moses had placed there at Horeb, when the Lord made a covenant with the children of Israel when they came out of Egypt. And when the priests came out of the sanctuary — for all the priests who could be found were sanctified, and the divisions by courses and ministry were not yet established among them — both the Levites and the singers, that is, those who were under Asaph, and those under Heman, and those under Jeduthun, with their sons and brothers, clothed in fine linen, with cymbals and psalteries and harps, stood at the east end of the altar; and with them were one hundred and twenty priests sounding trumpets. So all these together, with trumpets and voice and cymbals and organs and instruments of various kinds, raised their voices on high, and the sound was heard far off, so that when they began to praise the Lord and to say: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever — the house of God was filled with a cloud, so that the priests could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud. For the glory of the Lord had filled the house of God. Chapter VI.
Then Solomon said: The Lord has promised that he would dwell in a dark cloud; but I have built a house for his name, that he might dwell there forever. And the king turned his face and blessed all the congregation

to the multitude of Israel. For all the assembly stood attentive, and he said: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who has fulfilled with his hand what he spoke with his mouth to my father David, saying: From the day that I brought my people out of the land of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel in which a house might be built for my name, nor did I choose any man to be a ruler over my people Israel: but I have chosen Jerusalem that my name might be there, and I have chosen David to be over my people Israel. And whereas it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the Lord God of Israel: the Lord said to him: Whereas it was your intention to build a house for my name, you did well indeed to have this intention: but you shall not build the house; rather your son, who shall come forth from your loins, he shall build the house to my name. The Lord therefore has fulfilled his word which he spoke: and I have risen up in the place of David my father, and I sit upon the throne of Israel, as the Lord promised, and have built a house to the name of the Lord God of Israel: and I have placed in it the ark in which is the covenant of the Lord that he made with the children of Israel. And he stood before the altar of the Lord in the sight of all the assembly of Israel, and spread forth his hands. For Solomon had made a bronze scaffold and had placed it in the midst of the temple: it was five cubits long, and five cubits broad, and three cubits high. And he stood upon it, and then kneeling down over against all the multitude of Israel, he lifted up his hands toward heaven and said: O Lord God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven or on earth, who keep covenant and mercy with your servants who walk before you with all their heart: who have fulfilled to your servant David my father

whatever you promised him, and what you spoke with your mouth, you have also accomplished with your hand, as this present day shows. Now therefore, O Lord God of Israel, fulfill to your servant David my father whatever you have spoken to him, saying: There shall not be taken away from you a man in my sight who shall sit upon the throne of Israel: yet so that your sons take heed to their ways, and walk in my law, as you have walked before me. And now Lord God of Israel, let your word be established which you have spoken to your servant David. Is it then to be thought that God should indeed dwell with men on earth? If heaven and the heavens of heavens cannot contain you, how much less this house which I have built? But to this end only it is made, that you may regard the prayer of your servant and his supplication, O Lord my God: and may hear the prayers and supplications which your servant pours forth before you: that your eyes may be open upon this house day and night, upon the place wherein you have promised that your name should be called upon: that you would hear the prayer which your servant prays in it: that you would hear the supplications of your servant and of your people Israel. Whosoever shall pray in this place, hear from your dwelling place, that is, from heaven. If any man sin against his neighbor, and come prepared to swear against him, and bind himself with a curse before your altar in this house: then hear from heaven, and judge your servants: so as to recompense the wicked by making his way fall upon his own head, and to vindicate the just, rewarding him according to his own justice. If your people Israel be overcome by their enemies, for they will sin against you: and being converted shall do penance and beseech your name, and pray to you in this place: then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land which you gave to them and to their fathers.

and one hundred and twenty thousand rams. And the king and all the people dedicated the house of God. The priests stood in their offices, and the Levites with the instruments of music of the Lord, which David the king had made to praise the Lord, for his mercy endures forever, singing the psalms of David with their hands. The priests also sounded trumpets before them, and all Israel stood. And Solomon sanctified the middle of the court before the temple of the Lord, for he had offered there the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar which Solomon had made was not able to receive the burnt offerings and the meat offerings and the fat. And Solomon kept the feast at that time seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great congregation, from the entrance of Hamath to the river of Egypt. And in the eighth day they made a solemn assembly, for they had celebrated the dedication of the altar seven days. So Solomon finished the house of the Lord, and the king's house, and all that came into Solomon's heart to make in the house of the Lord and in his own house, and he prospered. And the Lord appeared to him by night and said: I have heard your prayer and have chosen this place for myself as a house of sacrifice. If I shut up heaven and there be no rain, or if I command the locusts to devour the land, or if I send pestilence among my people; if my people, who are called by my name, shall humble themselves and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land. Now my eyes shall be open and my ears attentive to the prayer that is made in this place. For I have chosen and sanctified this house, that my name may be there forever, and my eyes and my heart shall be there perpetually. And as for you, if you will walk before me as David your father walked, and do according to all that I have commanded you, and shall observe my statutes and my judgments; then will I establish the throne of your kingdom, as I covenanted with David your father, saying: You shall not lack a man to be ruler in Israel. But if you turn away and forsake my statutes and my commandments which I have set before you, and shall go and serve other gods and worship them; then will I pluck them up by the roots out of my land which I have given them, and this house which I have sanctified for my name will I cast out of my sight, and will make it a proverb and a byword among all nations. And everyone that passes by it shall be astonished and say: Why has the Lord done this to this land and to this house? And it shall be answered: Because they forsook the Lord God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and laid hold on other gods and worshipped them and served them; therefore he has brought all this evil upon them. Chapter VIII. And it came to pass at the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the house of the Lord and his own house, that the cities which Hiram had given to Solomon, Solomon built them and caused the children of Israel to dwell there. And Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and prevailed against it. And he built Tadmor in the wilderness, and all the store cities which he built in Hamath. Also he built upper Beth-horon and lower Beth-horon, fortified cities with walls, gates, and bars. And Baalath, and all the fortified cities that Solomon had:

· Paralipomenon ·

and all the chariot cities and the cities of horsemen. Everything that Solomon desired and planned, he built in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout all the land under his rule. All the people who remained of the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, who were not of the stock of Israel, of their children and descendants whom the children of Israel had not destroyed, Solomon made into tributaries down to this day. But of the children of Israel Solomon put none to serve in the king's works; for they were men of war and his chief captains and the commanders of his chariots and horsemen. And all the chief officers of king Solomon's army were two hundred and fifty, who taught the people. And Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharaoh out of the city of David into the house he had built for her. For he said: My wife shall not dwell in the house of David king of Israel, for it is holy, because the ark of the Lord has entered into it. Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to the Lord upon the altar of the Lord which he had built before the porch, that he might offer thereon daily according to the commandment of Moses, on the sabbaths, on the new moons, and on the feast days, three times a year — that is, on the feast of unleavened bread, on the feast of weeks, and on the feast of tabernacles. And he appointed, according to the order of David his father, the offices of the priests in their ministries, and the Levites in their order, to praise and minister before the priests according to the duty of every day, and the gatekeepers in their divisions at gate after gate. For so had David the man of God commanded. Neither the priests nor the Levites departed from the king's commandments in any matter he had commanded. And Solomon had all the expenses prepared in the treasuries from the day he founded

the house of the Lord until the day he finished it. Then Solomon went to Eziongeber and to Elath on the shore of the Red Sea, which is in the land of Edom. And Hiram sent him, by the hands of his servants, ships and servants skilled in the sea; and they went with Solomon's servants to Ophir, and they brought from there four hundred and fifty talents of gold and brought it to king Solomon. III. v.

And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she came to test him with riddles in Jerusalem, with great wealth and camels bearing spices, and very much gold, and precious stones. And when she had come to Solomon, she spoke to him all that was in her heart. And Solomon explained to her all that she proposed, and there was nothing hidden from him which he did not make plain to her. And when she had seen the wisdom of Solomon, and the house he had built, and the food of his table and the lodgings of his servants, and the offices of his ministers and their garments, his cupbearers also and their garments, and the sacrifices he offered in the house of the Lord, she was overcome with amazement and there was no more spirit in her. And she said to the king: The report that I heard in my own land about your virtue and wisdom is true. I did not believe those who told me, until I came and my own eyes saw it, and I found that not even half of your wisdom had been reported to me. You have surpassed your fame by your virtue. Happy are your men and happy are your servants, who stand before you always and hear your wisdom. Blessed be the Lord your God, who has been pleased to set you on his throne as king for the Lord your God. Because your God loves Israel and wishes to preserve them forever, therefore he has set you over them as king, to do judgment and justice. And she gave to the king

SECOND

talents of gold and very great quantities of spices, and precious stones. Never again were there such spices as those which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon. And also the servants of Hiram with the servants of Solomon brought gold from Ophir, and thyine wood, and precious stones. From the thyine wood the king made steps in the house of the Lord and in the king's house, and harps and psalteries for the singers. No such thyine wood had ever been seen before in the land of Judah. And King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all that she desired and asked, and more than she had brought to him. So she turned and departed to her own land with her servants. Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold, besides that which merchants and traders brought, and all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the country who brought gold and silver to Solomon. King Solomon made two hundred shields of hammered gold, six hundred shekels of gold going into each shield, and three hundred shields of hammered gold, three hundred shekels of gold going into each. The king put them in the house of the Forest of Lebanon. The king also made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with the finest gold. The throne had six steps, and a footstool of gold, and two armrests on each side of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests, while twelve lions stood on the six steps, one on each end of each step. Nothing like it had ever been made in any kingdom. All King Solomon's drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the Forest of Lebanon were of pure gold. Silver was not considered as anything in the days of Solomon. For the king's ships went to Tarshish with Hiram's servants once every three years, bringing back gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks. So King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom. All the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his mind. And they brought every one of them his tribute: vessels of silver and gold, garments, weapons, spices, horses, and mules, year by year. Solomon also had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen. He stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem. He exercised dominion over all the kings from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt. The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stone, and cedar as plentiful as the sycamore of the lowlands. Horses were imported from Egypt for Solomon and from all lands. The rest of the acts of Solomon, from first to last, are they not written in the records of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam the son of Nebat? Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years. Solomon slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David his father; and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.

And Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king. When Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard of it, he returned from Egypt, for he had fled from Solomon. They sent and called him; and Jeroboam and all Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying: Your father made our yoke heavy. Now therefore lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke on us, and we will serve you. He said to them...

· Paralipomenon (Chronicles) ·

You have laid a heavy burden of service upon us: lighten it somewhat, and we will serve you. He said: Come back to me in three days. And when the people had departed, he took counsel with the elders who had stood before his father Solomon while he still lived, saying: What counsel do you give me to answer the people? And they said to him: If you show kindness to this people and speak gentle words to them, they will serve you forever. But he left the counsel of the old men and took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him and were in his retinue. And he said to them: What do you think I should answer to this man who said to me: lighten the yoke your father laid upon us? And those young men who had been raised with him in luxury answered: Thus shall you say to the people who told you that your father made our yoke heavy: You shall make it lighter for us. Thus you shall say to them: My little finger is thicker than my father's loins. My father laid a heavy yoke on you; I will make it even heavier. My father beat you with whips; I will beat you with scorpions. So Jeroboam and all the people came back to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had commanded. And the king answered them harshly, having forsaken the counsel of the elders, and spoke according to the will of the young men. My father made your yoke heavy; I will make it heavier still. My father beat you with whips; I will beat you with scorpions. And he did not listen to the people's plea. For it was the will of God, that he might fulfill the word which he had spoken by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat. And all the people, when the king spoke harsher words, said to him: We have no part in David, nor inheritance

in the son of Jesse. Return to your tents, O Israel. And as for you, David, look now to your own house. And Israel departed to their tents. But over the children of Israel who dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned. Then king Rehoboam sent Aduram, who was over the tribute, and the children of Israel stoned him to death. And king Rehoboam made haste to get into his chariot and fled to Jerusalem. And Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day. Now when all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they sent and called him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel: and none followed the house of David but the tribe of Judah alone. Chapter XI.

And when Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, he assembled all the house of Judah and Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight against Israel and bring the kingdom back to himself. But the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying: Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin, saying: Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up nor fight against your brothers; let every man return to his house, for this thing is done by my will. And when they heard the word of the Lord, they returned and did not march against Jeroboam. And Rehoboam dwelt in Jerusalem and built fortified cities in Judah: and he built Bethlehem and Etam and Tekoa, and Beth-zur and Soco and Adullam, and Gath and Mareshah and Ziph, and Adoraim and Lachish and Azekah, and Zorah and Aijalon and Hebron, which are in Judah and Benjamin, fortified cities. And when he had enclosed them with walls, he placed in

Secundus [Second]

...the princes had storehouses for food, that is for oil and wine. And in every city he made armories for shields and spears, and fortified them with great diligence, and he ruled over Judah and Benjamin. And the priests and Levites who were throughout all Israel came to him from all their territories, leaving their suburbs and their possessions, and they came to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off, so that they could not serve as priests to the Lord; and he appointed for himself priests for the high places and for demons and for the calves which he had made. And from all the tribes of Israel, those who had set their hearts to seek the Lord God of Israel came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the Lord, the God of their fathers; and they strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and confirmed Rehoboam the son of Solomon for three years, for they walked in the way of David and Solomon for three years. And Rehoboam took for himself as wife Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David, and Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse; and she bore him sons: Jeush and Shemariah and Zaham. And after her he took Maachah the daughter of Absalom; and she bore him Abijah and Attai and Ziza and Shelomith. And Rehoboam loved Maachah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and concubines; for he had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters. And he appointed Abijah the son of Maachah as chief above all his brothers, for he intended to make him king, because he was wiser and more powerful than all his sons; and in all the territories of Judah and Benjamin and in all the fortified cities he provided them with abundant food, and sought many wives.

Chapter 12. And when the kingdom of Rehoboam was established and strong, he abandoned the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him. And in the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had sinned against the Lord, with twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen; and there was no counting the people who came with him from Egypt — Lubim and Sukkiim and Ethiopians. And he took the fortified cities of Judah and came as far as Jerusalem. Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the princes of Judah, who had gathered at Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said to them: Thus says the Lord: You have abandoned me, therefore I have abandoned you into the hand of Shishak. Then the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said: The Lord is righteous. And when the Lord saw that they humbled themselves, the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, saying: They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy them, but I will grant them a little deliverance, and my wrath shall not be poured out upon Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak. Nevertheless they shall be his servants, so that they may know my service and the service of the kingdoms of the countries. So Shishak king of Egypt departed from Jerusalem, taking with him the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king's house; he took everything, including the golden shields that Solomon had made; and King Rehoboam made bronze ones in their place and committed them to the care of the captains of the guard who kept the door of the king's house. And whenever the king entered the house of the Lord, the guards came and carried them and then brought them back to the guardroom. And because they had humbled themselves, the wrath of the Lord turned away from them and did not destroy them utterly; for in Judah good things were found. So King Rehoboam was strengthened in Jerusalem...

· Chronicles ·

And he reigned. He was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the Lord had chosen to establish his name there, out of all the tribes of Israel. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonitess. And he did evil, and did not prepare his heart to seek the Lord. The first and last deeds of Rehoboam are written in the books of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, carefully preserved. And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days. And Rehoboam slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Abijah his son reigned in his place. Chapter XIII.
In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah began to reign over Judah. He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Michaiah, daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam. And when Abijah joined battle, having the most valiant men, and four hundred thousand chosen men, Jeroboam drew up against him eight hundred thousand men, who were also chosen and most skilled in battle. Then Abijah stood upon Mount Zemaraim, which is in Ephraim, and said: Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel. Do you not know that the Lord God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David forever, to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt? Yet Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his lord. And worthless men and sons of Belial gathered to him, and they prevailed against Rehoboam the son of Solomon. For Rehoboam was young and faint-hearted and could not resist them. And now you say that you can resist the kingdom of the Lord, which he holds through the sons of David?

And you have with you a great multitude, and the golden calves which Jeroboam made for you as gods. And you have cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and you have made for yourselves priests like all the peoples of the lands. Whoever comes and consecrates himself with a bull and seven rams becomes a priest of those who are no gods. But as for us, the Lord is our God, and we have not forsaken him. The priests who serve the Lord are sons of Aaron, and the Levites attend to their order: they offer burnt offerings to the Lord every day, morning and evening, and incense prepared according to the prescription of the law, and the bread of the Presence is set on the pure table. And we have the golden lampstand and its lamps, to light them every evening. We keep the commandments of the Lord our God, which you have forsaken. Therefore, God is our leader in our army, and his priests with their trumpets sound the call against you. O sons of Israel, do not fight against the Lord God of your fathers, for you will not succeed. But even as he spoke, Jeroboam was setting an ambush behind them. And while he stood facing the enemy, he surrounded Judah with an ambush. When Judah looked back, they saw the battle was both before and behind them; and they cried out to the Lord, and the priests blew the trumpets, and all the men of Judah raised a battle cry. And behold, as they cried out, God struck Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah, and the sons of Israel fled before Judah, and God delivered them into their hands. And Abijah and his army struck them with a great slaughter, and five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell slain. Thus the sons of Israel were humbled at that time, and most grievously

. Second .

The children of Judah were strengthened, because they had relied upon the Lord God of their fathers. And Abijah pursued Jeroboam who was fleeing, and took his cities: Bethel and its villages, Jeshanah and its villages, and Ephron and its villages. And Jeroboam was not able to resist any longer in the days of Abijah. And the Lord struck him and he died. But Abijah, having strengthened his rule, took fourteen wives, and begot twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters. The rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways and his deeds, are written most carefully in the book of the prophet Iddo. Chapter XIV.

So Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David. And Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days the land was quiet for ten years. And Asa did what was good and right in the sight of his God, and took away the foreign altars and the high places, and broke down the sacred pillars, and cut down the wooden images. And he commanded Judah to seek the Lord God of their fathers, and to observe the law and the commandment. And he removed the high places and the incense altars from all the cities of Judah, and the kingdom was quiet under him. He also built fortified cities in Judah, for the land had rest, and he had no war in those years, because the Lord had given him peace. And he said to Judah: "Let us build these cities and surround them with walls and towers, gates and bars, while the land is yet before us; because we have sought the Lord our God, and he has given us rest on every side." So they built and prospered. Asa had an army of three hundred thousand from Judah who carried shields and spears, and from Benjamin two hundred and eighty thousand who carried shields and drew bows; all of these were mighty men. And he went out against

Zerah the Ethiopian with his army of a million men and three hundred chariots, and came as far as Mareshah. Then Asa went out to meet him, and they set the battle in array in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah. And Asa cried to the Lord his God, and said: "Lord, there is no difference with you whether you help the few or the many. Help us, O Lord our God, for we rest on you, and in your name we go against this multitude. O Lord, you are our God; let not man prevail against you." So the Lord struck the Ethiopians before Asa and before Judah, and the Ethiopians fled. And Asa and the people that were with him pursued them as far as Gerar. And the Ethiopians were overthrown until none of them remained alive, for they were destroyed before the Lord and before his army. And they carried away very much spoil, and they attacked all the cities around Gerar, for the fear of the Lord came upon them. And they plundered all the cities, for there was much plunder in them. They also attacked the encampments of the herdsmen, and carried away sheep and camels in abundance, and returned to Jerusalem. Chapter XV.

And the Spirit of God came upon Azariah the son of Oded, and he went out to meet Asa, and said to him: "Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin: The Lord is with you while you are with him. If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will forsake you. For many days Israel has been without the true God, without a teaching priest, and without the law. But when in their distress they turned to the Lord God of Israel and sought him, he was found by them. In those times there was no peace to him who went out, nor to him who came in, but great disturbances were upon all the inhabitants of the lands. And nation was destroyed by nation, and city by city

. Paralipomenon (Chronicles) .

For the Lord will throw them into confusion in all their distress. So be strong and do not let your hands grow weak, for your work will be rewarded. When Asa heard these words — that is, the prophecy of Azariah son of Oded the prophet — he took courage and removed the idols from all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and from the cities he had taken in the hill country of Ephraim, and he repaired the altar of the Lord that stood before the vestibule of the Lord. Then he gathered all of Judah and Benjamin, and those from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who resided with them, for great numbers had come over to him from Israel when they saw that the Lord his God was with him. They came together at Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa. They sacrificed to the Lord on that day from the spoil they had brought: seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep. They entered into a covenant to seek the Lord, the God of their ancestors, with all their heart and soul. Whoever would not seek the Lord, the God of Israel, should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman. They took an oath to the Lord with a loud voice and with shouting and with trumpets and with horns. All Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart and had sought him wholeheartedly, and he was found by them. The Lord gave them rest on every side. He also removed Maacah, the mother of King Asa, from being queen mother because she had made an abominable image for Asherah. Asa cut down her image, crushed it, and burned it at the brook Kidron. But the high places were not taken away from Israel. Nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect all his days. He brought into the house of God the silver and gold and the various vessels that he and his father had dedicated. And there was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa. Chapter 16.

In the thirty-sixth year of the reign of Asa, Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah and built Ramah, so that no one could go out or come in to Asa king of Judah. Then Asa took silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the Lord and the king's house and sent them to Ben-hadad the king of Syria who lived in Damascus, saying: There is a covenant between me and you. My father and your father had a treaty together; I am sending you silver and gold; now break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel so that he will withdraw from me. Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, and they struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali. When Baasha heard of it, he stopped building Ramah and let his work cease. Then King Asa took all Judah, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timber with which Baasha had been building, and with them he built Geba and Mizpah. At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him: Because you relied on the king of Syria and did not rely on the Lord your God, the army of the king of Syria has escaped you. Were not the Ethiopians and the Libyans a huge army with very many chariots and horsemen? Yet because you relied on the Lord, he gave them into your hand. For the eyes of the Lord run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to give strong support to those whose heart is fully committed to him. You have done foolishly in this, for from now on you will have wars. Then Asa was angry with the seer and put him in prison. And Asa was greatly

. Second .

For the Lord had been angered at this, and struck down many of them at that time. Now the first and last acts of Asa are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel. Asa also fell sick in the thirty-ninth year of his reign with a very severe disease of the feet, and even in his illness he did not seek the Lord, but rather put his trust in the skill of physicians. And he slept with his fathers, and died in the forty-first year of his reign; and they buried him in his own tomb which he had hewn for himself in the city of David. And they laid him on a bier filled with aromatics and various kinds of spices prepared by the perfumers' art, and they made a very great burning for him. Chapter 17.
And Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place, and prevailed against Israel. And he placed forces in all the cities of Judah that were walled, and set garrisons in the land of Judah, and in the cities of Ephraim which Asa his father had taken. And the Lord was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the first ways of David his father, and did not seek the Baals, but sought the God of his father, and walked in his commandments, and not after the doings of Israel. Therefore the Lord established the kingdom in his hand, and all Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, and he had great riches and honor. And when his heart was lifted up in the ways of the Lord, he also removed the high places and the groves from Judah. Also in the third year of his reign he sent out his princes, Benhail and Obadiah and Zechariah and Nathanael and Michaiah, to teach in the cities of Judah; and with them the Levites, Shemaiah and Nethaniah and Zebadiah and Asahel and Shemiramoth and Jehonathan and Adonijah and Tobijah and Tobadonijah, Levites; and with them Elishama and Joram,

priests. And they taught throughout Judah, having the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about through all the cities of Judah and taught the people. And the fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were around Judah, so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat. Also some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat gifts and tribute in silver. The Arabians also brought him flocks, seven thousand seven hundred rams, and seven thousand seven hundred male goats. And Jehoshaphat grew ever greater and built in Judah fortresses and store cities. He carried on great works in the cities of Judah. And he had men of war, mighty men of valor, in Jerusalem. And this was their number according to their fathers' houses: Of Judah, the commanders of thousands: Adnah the commander, and with him three hundred thousand mighty men of valor. Next to him was Jehohanan the commander, and with him two hundred and eighty thousand. Next to him was Amasiah the son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself to the Lord, and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of valor. And from Benjamin: Eliada, a mighty man of valor, and with him two hundred thousand armed with bow and shield. Next to him was Jehozabad, and with him a hundred and eighty thousand ready for war. These were those who served the king, besides those whom the king had put in the fortified cities throughout all Judah. Chapter 18.
Now Jehoshaphat had great riches and honor, and allied himself with Ahab by marriage. And after some years he went down to Ahab in Samaria. And Ahab slaughtered many sheep and oxen for him and for the people with him, and persuaded him to go up with him to Ramoth-gilead. And Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: Come with me to Ramoth-gilead. And he answered him,

. Paralipomenon (Chronicles) .

He answered: As I am, so are you; my people as your people; and we will be with you in the war. And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel: Inquire, I beseech you, this day the word of the Lord. Then the king of Israel gathered together the prophets, about four hundred men, and said to them: Shall we go to Ramoth Gilead to fight, or shall we forbear? They answered: Go up, and God will deliver it into the hand of the king. But Jehoshaphat said: Is there not here a prophet of the Lord, that we may inquire also of him? And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: There is one man by whom we may inquire of the Lord: but I hate him, for he never prophesies good for me, but always evil. He is Micaiah the son of Imlah. And Jehoshaphat said: Let not the king say so. So the king of Israel called one of the eunuchs and said: Bring quickly Micaiah the son of Imlah. Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting each on his throne, clothed in royal robes; and they sat in the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria: and all the prophets prophesied before them. And Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made himself horns of iron and said: Thus says the Lord: With these you shall push Syria until they are consumed. And all the prophets prophesied in the same manner, saying: Go up to Ramoth Gilead and prosper, for the Lord will deliver it into the hands of the king. And the messenger who went to call Micaiah said to him: Behold, the words of the prophets with one mouth declare good to the king; let your word therefore be like one of theirs, and speak favorably. And Micaiah said: As the Lord lives, whatever my God says, that I will speak. So he came to the king. And the king said to him: Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth Gilead to fight, or shall I forbear? And he answered: Go up and all will go well, and they will be delivered into your hands.

Then the king said: How many times shall I adjure you that you tell me nothing but what is true in the name of the Lord? And he said: I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains like sheep without a shepherd. And the Lord said: These have no master; let every man return to his house in peace. Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good for me, but evil? And Micaiah said: Therefore hear the word of the Lord. I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing on his right hand and on his left. And the Lord said: Who will persuade Ahab king of Israel to go up and fall at Ramoth Gilead? And one spoke in this manner and another in that manner. Then there came out a spirit and stood before the Lord and said: I will persuade him. The Lord said to him: By what means? And he answered: I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And the Lord said: You shall persuade him, and you shall also prevail; go out and do so. Now therefore behold, the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these your prophets; and the Lord has spoken evil against you. Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said: Which way did the spirit of the Lord pass from me to speak to you? And Micaiah said: You will see on that day when you go into an inner chamber to hide. Then the king of Israel commanded, saying: Take Micaiah and carry him to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son, and say: Thus says the king: Put this man in prison and feed him with bread of affliction and water of affliction until I return in peace. And Micaiah said: If you return in peace, the Lord has not spoken by me.

. Second .

spoken in me. And he said: Hear, all of you. So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead: and the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, I will change my dress and go into battle: but you put on your own robes. So the king of Israel changed his dress and came to battle. Now the king of Syria had commanded the captains of his chariots, saying: Fight neither with small nor great, but only against the king of Israel. When the captains of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, they said: It is the king of Israel: and they surrounded him to fight. But he cried to the Lord, and the Lord helped him: and turned them away from him. For when the captains of the chariots saw that he was not the king of Israel, they left off pursuing him. But a certain man drew his bow at a venture and struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor. And he said to the charioteer: Turn your hand and carry me out of the battle, for I am wounded. And the battle ended that day. The king of Israel stood in his chariot against the Syrians until evening, and he died at sunset. Chapter 19.

And Jehoshaphat the king of Judah returned safely to his house in Jerusalem. And Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him and said to him: You help the ungodly, and make friends of those that hate the Lord, and therefore you did deserve indeed the wrath of the Lord: but good works are found in you, in that you have taken away the groves out of the land of Judah, and have prepared your heart to seek the Lord God of your fathers. So Jehoshaphat dwelt in Jerusalem: and he went out again among the people from Beersheba to mount Ephraim, and brought them back to the Lord God of their fathers: and he appointed judges in the land in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city, and princes

to see and declare to the judges what to do. For it is not in the name of men that you exercise judgment, but in the name of the Lord: and whatever you shall judge will redound to you. Let the fear of the Lord be with you and do everything with diligence. For there is no iniquity with the Lord our God, nor respect of persons, nor desire of gifts. In Jerusalem also Jehoshaphat appointed Levites and priests and heads of families of Israel for the judgment and causes of the Lord for the inhabitants thereof: and he commanded them, saying: Thus shall you do in the fear of the Lord faithfully and with a whole heart. Every cause that shall come to you of your brethren that dwell in their cities between kindred and kindred, wherever question is of law, of commandment, of ceremonies and of justifications, show them that they may not sin against the Lord, lest wrath come upon you and upon your brethren. Thus doing, you shall not sin. But Amariah the priest your high priest shall preside in those things that pertain to God: and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, who is the ruler in the house of Judah, shall be over those works that pertain to the king's office. You have also Levites as officers before you: take courage and act diligently: and the Lord shall be with the good. Chapter 20.

After these things, the children of Moab and the children of Ammon and with them some of the Ammonites came against Jehoshaphat to fight against him. And there came messengers and told Jehoshaphat, saying: A great multitude has come against you from beyond the sea, from Syria: and behold they are in Hazazon-tamar, which is Engedi. And Jehoshaphat, seized with fear, gave himself wholly to seeking the Lord: and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah. And Judah was gathered together to implore the Lord: but also all from

Second.

217.

the furnishings, garments, and very precious vessels, and they plundered them, so that all could not be carried away, nor could the spoils be taken away in three days, so great was the quantity of plunder. On the fourth day they assembled in the valley of Benediction. For because they had blessed the Lord there, they called that place the valley of Benediction, even to the present day. And all the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem returned, and Jehoshaphat at their head, back to Jerusalem with great joy, because the Lord had given them gladness over their enemies. And they entered Jerusalem with psalteries and harps and trumpets into the house of the Lord. And the fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands, when they heard that the Lord had fought against the enemies of Israel; and the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was at peace, and his God gave him rest on all sides. So Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah, and he was thirty-five years old when he began to reign. He reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Azubah, daughter of Shilhi; and he walked in the way of his father Asa, and did not turn aside from it, doing what was pleasing in the sight of the Lord. Nevertheless the high places were not removed, and the people had not yet directed their hearts to the Lord God of their fathers. Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, first and last, are written in the book of Jehu the son of Hanani, which is inserted in the book of the Kings of Israel. After this Jehoshaphat king of Judah allied himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, whose works were most wicked; and he was partner with him to make ships to go to Tarshish, and they made the fleet at Ezion-geber. But Eliezer the son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying: Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the Lord has destroyed your works; and the ships were wrecked and could not go to Tarshish.
And Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers, and was buried

in the city of David; and Jehoram his son reigned in his place. He had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, and Jehiel, and Zechariah, and Azariah, and Michael, and Shephatiah. All these were the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Judah. And their father gave them great gifts of silver and of gold and of precious things, with fortified cities in Judah; but the kingdom he gave to Jehoram, because he was the firstborn. And Jehoram rose up over the kingdom of his father; and when he had established himself, he killed all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the princes of Israel. Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem; and he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab, for the daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did evil in the sight of the Lord. Yet the Lord would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant he had made with him, and because he had promised to give a lamp to him and to his sons for all time. In those days Edom revolted from under the dominion of Judah, and set up a king over themselves. And Jehoram passed over with his princes and all his cavalry with him; and he rose up by night and struck Edom who had surrounded him, and all the captains of the cavalry. Yet Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah to this day. At that same time Libnah also revolted from under his hand, because he had forsaken the Lord God of his fathers. Moreover he built high places in the cities of Judah, and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit fornication and led Judah astray. And there came to him a letter from Elijah the prophet, in which was written: Thus says the Lord God of David your father: Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your father, nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah, but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and have caused Judah and the inhabitants

Paralipomenon (Chronicles)

Jerusalem, imitating the fornication of the house of Ahab; moreover you have killed your brothers, your father's sons, who were better than yourself. Behold, the Lord will strike you with a great plague, along with your people, your wives, and your children, and all your possessions. And you yourself will suffer a severe illness of the bowels, until your vital organs come out day by day through the disease. Then the Lord stirred up against Joram the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabians, who border on the Ethiopians, and they came up into the land of Judah and laid it waste. They carried off all the substance found in the king's house, and likewise his sons and his wives; so that no son was left to him except Jehoahaz, who was the youngest. And above all these things the Lord struck him with an incurable disease of the bowels. As days passed and time rolled on, after the course of two years, his bowels fell out with the disease, and he died of a lingering illness. And his people did not make a burning for him, as they had done for his fathers. He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He walked not uprightly, and they buried him in the city of David, but not in the sepulchers of the kings. Chapter 22.

The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, his youngest son, king in his place, for the company of men who had come with the Arabians into the camp had killed all the older ones. So Ahaziah, son of Joram king of Judah, reigned; Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem; and the name of his mother was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri. He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother counseled him to do wickedly. He did evil in the sight of the Lord, like the house of Ahab, for they were his counselors after the death of his father, to his destruction. He also followed their counsel, and he went with Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead, and the Syrians wounded Joram. He returned to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds which he had received at Ramah. For he had received many wounds in the said land. So Ahaziah the son of Joram king of Judah went down to see Joram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, for he was sick. Now it was ordained by God that the coming of Ahaziah to Joram should lead to his downfall. When he came, he went out with Joram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the Lord had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab. And when Jehu was executing judgment upon the house of Ahab, he found the princes of Judah and the sons of the brothers of Ahaziah, who served Ahaziah, and he killed them. And he searched for Ahaziah, and they caught him hiding in Samaria, and they brought him to Jehu and killed him; and they buried him, because he was the son of Jehoshaphat, who had sought the Lord with all his heart. And there was no one left of the house of Ahaziah who was able to hold the kingdom. Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and killed all the royal family of the house of Joram. But Jehosheba, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being killed, and put him and his nurse in a bedroom. So Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest — for she was the sister of Ahaziah — hid him from Athaliah, so that she did not kill him. He remained hidden with them in the house of God six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land. Chapter 23.

. Second .

Now in the seventh year, Jehoiada took courage and assembled the captains of hundreds: Azariah the son of Jeroham, and Ishmael the son of Johanan, and Azariah the son of Obed, and Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri, and made a covenant with them. And they went about through Judah and gathered the Levites out of all the cities of Judah, and the chief men of the fathers of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem. And all the assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. And Jehoiada said to them: This is the thing that you shall do. A third part of you, coming on the sabbath, of the priests and Levites, shall be porters at the gates; and a third part shall be at the king's house; and a third part at the gate of the foundation. But all the rest of the people shall be in the courts of the house of the Lord. And let no one enter the house of the Lord except the priests and those who minister among the Levites. Let them alone enter, because they are holy; but let all the rest of the people keep the watch of the Lord. And the Levites shall surround the king, every man with his weapons in his hand; and whoever enters the temple shall be killed; and be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out. So the Levites and all Judah did according to all that Jehoiada the priest had commanded, and they took every man his men, those who were to come in on the sabbath, and those who were to go out on the sabbath; for Jehoiada the priest did not dismiss the divisions. And Jehoiada the priest gave to the captains the spears and shields and bucklers that had been King David's, which were in the house of God. And he set all the people as a guard for the king, every man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the temple to the left side of the temple, along the altar and the temple round about the king.

Then they brought out the king's son, and put upon him the crown, and gave him the law, and made him king. And Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and said: God save the king. Now when Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came into the house of the Lord. And she looked, and behold, the king stood at his pillar at the entrance, and the captains and the trumpeters were beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoiced and sounded with trumpets, and the singers with instruments of music, leading the praises. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and said: Treason, treason! But Jehoiada the priest went out to the captains of hundreds who were set over the host, and said to them: Take her outside the precincts of the temple, and whoever follows her, let him be put to death with the sword; for the priest had said: Let her not be slain in the house of the Lord. So they laid hands on her, and when she had come to the entering of the horse gate of the king's house, they slew her there. And Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and all the people and the king, that they should be the Lord's people. Then all the people went into the house of Baal and destroyed it, and broke down his altars and his images, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. And Jehoiada appointed the offices of the house of the Lord under the hand of the priests and Levites, whom David had assigned over the house of the Lord, to offer burnt offerings to the Lord, as it is written in the law of Moses, with rejoicing and with singing, according to the order of David. And he set the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the Lord, that no one who was in any way unclean should enter. And he took the captains of hundreds, and the mighty men of valor, and the rulers of the people, and all the people of the land, and they brought down the king from the house of the Lord, and caused him to enter

Chronicles

Through the upper gate into the king's house, they placed him on the royal throne. And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. And Athaliah was killed by the sword. Chapter 23.
Joash was seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba. And he did what was good in the sight of the Lord all the days of Jehoiada the priest. Jehoiada took for him two wives, by whom he had sons and daughters. After this, Joash decided to restore the house of the Lord, and he gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them: Go out to the cities of Judah and gather money from all Israel for the yearly repair of the temple of your God; do this promptly. But the Levites were slow to act. The king called Jehoiada the chief and said to him: Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the tax that Moses the servant of the Lord laid on the congregation of Israel for the tabernacle of testimony? For Athaliah, that wicked woman, and her sons had broken up the house of God and had used all the dedicated things of the house of the Lord for the Baals. So the king commanded, and they made a chest and set it outside at the gate of the house of the Lord. And a proclamation was made throughout Judah and Jerusalem to bring to the Lord the tax that Moses the servant of God had laid on Israel in the wilderness; and all the princes and all the people rejoiced, and they brought their tax and cast it into the chest. Whenever the chest was brought to the king's officials by the Levites, and when they saw that there was much money in it, the king's secretary and the chief priest's officer would come and empty the chest and carry it back to its place. Thus they did day after day, and gathered money in abundance, which the king and Jehoiada gave to those who did the work of the house of the Lord. They hired masons and carpenters to restore the house of the Lord, and also workers in iron and bronze to repair the house of the Lord. The craftsmen worked diligently, and the repair work progressed under their hands, and they restored the house of God to its proper condition and strengthened it. When they had finished, they brought the rest of the money before the king and Jehoiada, and with it were made vessels for the house of the Lord: vessels for the service and for burnt offerings, ladles and vessels of gold and silver. And they offered burnt offerings in the house of the Lord continually all the days of Jehoiada. But Jehoiada grew old and full of days and died; he was one hundred and thirty years old when he died. And they buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel and toward God and His house. After the death of Jehoiada, the princes of Judah came and paid homage to the king. Then the king listened to them. And they abandoned the house of the Lord God of their fathers and served the wooden images and the idols; and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem because of their trespass. Yet He sent prophets to them, to bring them back to the Lord, and they testified against them but they would not listen. Then the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, and he stood before the people and said to them: Thus says God: Why do you transgress the commandments of the Lord, so that you cannot prosper? Because you have forsaken the Lord, He has also forsaken you. But they conspired against him and stoned him at the king's command

Secundus 4

in the court of the house of the Lord. And Joash the king did not remember the kindness that Jehoiada his father had shown him, but killed his son. And when he was dying, he said: "May the Lord see and avenge." When a year had passed, the army of Syria came up against him, and they came into Judah and Jerusalem and killed all the princes of the people, and sent all the plunder to the king of Damascus. And indeed, though the army of Syria had come with a small number of men, the Lord delivered into their hands a very great army, because they had forsaken the Lord God of their fathers. And they executed judgments against Joash, and when they departed they left him in great suffering. His servants rose up against him to avenge the blood of Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, and they slew him on his bed, and he died; and they buried him in the city of David, but not in the tombs of the kings. Those who conspired against him were Zabad the son of Shimeath the Ammonitess, and Jehozabad the son of Shimrith the Moabitess. Now his sons, and the large amount of money that was collected, and the restoration of the house of God, are written more carefully in the book of the kings. And Amaziah his son reigned in his place. [Chapter 25]

Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem. And he did what was right in the sight of the Lord, yet not with a perfect heart. And when he saw that his kingdom was firmly established, he killed the servants who had killed the king his father. But he did not put their children to death, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses, where the Lord commanded: "The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, nor the children for the fathers, but each man shall die for his own sin." Then Amaziah gathered Judah together and

arranged them by families, with commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds throughout all Judah and Benjamin; and he mustered those from twenty years old and upward, and found them to be three hundred thousand choice men able to go to war, who could handle spear and shield. He also hired one hundred thousand mighty warriors from Israel for one hundred talents of silver. But a man of God came to him and said: "O king, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the Lord is not with Israel — not with any of the children of Ephraim. But if you go, be strong for the battle; God will make you fall before the enemy, for God has power to help and to overthrow." And Amaziah said to the man of God: "But what shall we do about the hundred talents which I have given to the troops of Israel?" And the man of God answered: "The Lord is able to give you much more than this." So Amaziah discharged the army that had come to him from Ephraim, to return to their own place. And they were furious with Judah, and returned home in great anger. But Amaziah strengthened himself and led his people out, and went to the Valley of Salt and struck down ten thousand of the sons of Seir. And another ten thousand men the people of Judah took alive, brought them to the top of a cliff, and threw them down from the top of the cliff, so that they were all dashed to pieces. But the soldiers of the army which Amaziah had dismissed, not allowing them to go with him to battle, raided the cities of Judah from Samaria to Beth-horon, killed three thousand people in them, and took much plunder. Now after Amaziah came from the slaughter of the Edomites, he brought the gods of the sons of Seir and set them up as his gods, and worshipped them and burned incense to them. Therefore the anger of the Lord burned against Amaziah, and He sent a prophet to him, who said: "Why have you sought the gods of a people that could not deliver their own people

· Paralipomenon (Chronicles) ·

people from your hand? And while he was saying these things, he answered him. Are you a counselor to the king? Be quiet, lest you be killed. And the prophet departing said: I know that God has determined to destroy you, because you have done this evil and moreover have not listened to my counsel. So Amaziah king of Judah, having taken evil counsel, sent to Joash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu king of Israel, saying: Come, let us see one another face to face. But he sent back messengers saying: The thistle that is in Lebanon sent to the cedar that is in Lebanon, saying: Give your daughter to my son as wife. And the beasts that were in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle. You said: I have struck Edom, and therefore your heart is lifted up in pride. Stay at home. Why do you provoke evil against yourself, that you should fall, and Judah with you? Amaziah would not listen, for it was the will of God that he should be delivered into the hands of enemies, because of Edom. So Joash king of Israel came up, and they looked one another in the face. And Amaziah king of Judah was at Bethshemesh of Judah. And Judah was defeated before Israel and fled to their tents. Moreover Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash son of Ochoziah, at Bethshemesh, and brought him to Jerusalem, and broke down its wall from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits. And all the gold and silver, and all the vessels found in the house of God and with Obededom, and the treasures of the royal house, along with the sons of hostages, he brought to Samaria. Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel fifteen years. The rest of the acts of Amaziah, the first and the last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel. After he turned away from the Lord,

they plotted against him in Jerusalem. When he fled to Lachish, they sent after him and killed him there; and they brought him back on horses and buried him with his fathers in the city of David. Chapter 26.

All the people of Judah took his son Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah. He built Elath and restored it to Judah after the king slept with his fathers. Uzziah was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem. And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Amaziah his father had done; and he sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God. As long as he sought the Lord, God made him prosper. He went out and made war against the Philistines and broke down the wall of Gath and the wall of Jabneh and the wall of Ashdod. And he built cities in the region of Ashdod and among the Philistines; and God helped him against the Philistines and against the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal, and against the Ammonites. The Ammonites paid tribute to Uzziah, and his fame spread as far as the borders of Egypt, for he grew very strong. Moreover Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate, and at the other corners of the wall, and fortified them. He also built towers in the wilderness and dug many cisterns, for he had much livestock, both in the lowlands and in the plain. He had farmers and vinedressers in the mountains and in Carmel, for he loved farming. Uzziah also had an army ready for battle, which went out to war by companies, according to the number of their muster as prepared by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer, under the direction of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders. All

Second

The number of the chiefs by families of valiant men was six hundred thousand; and under them the whole army was three hundred and seven thousand five hundred, who were fit for war and fought for the king against his enemies. Uzziah prepared for them, that is, for the whole army, shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and slings for casting stones. He made in Jerusalem engines of war of various kinds, which he placed in the towers and at the corners of the walls, to shoot arrows and great stones. His fame spread far and wide, because the Lord helped him and strengthened him. But when he had become strong, his heart was lifted up to his own destruction, and he transgressed against the Lord his God: for he went into the temple of the Lord to burn incense upon the altar of incense. And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him fourscore priests of the Lord, valiant men. They withstood the king and said: It is not your office, Uzziah, to burn incense to the Lord, but that of the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated for this ministry. Go out of the sanctuary; do not despise this, for it shall not be counted as glory to you before the Lord God. Then Uzziah was angry, and held in his hand the censer to burn incense; and while he was in a rage against the priests, leprosy broke out on his forehead before the priests in the house of the Lord, beside the altar of incense. And Azariah the chief priest and all the priests looked at him, and behold, he was leprous on his forehead, and they drove him out quickly from there. He himself also hastened to go out, because the Lord had struck him. Uzziah the king was a leper to the day of his death, and dwelt in a separate house, being excluded from the house of the Lord. And Jotham his son was over the king's house, governing the people of the land. Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, first and last, Isaiah the prophet, son of Amos, wrote. And Uzziah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of burial that belonged to the kings, for they said, he was a leper; and Jotham his son reigned in his stead. Chapter 27.

Jotham was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerushah the daughter of Zadok. He did what was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father Uzziah had done; however he did not enter into the temple of the Lord, and the people still acted corruptly. He built the upper gate of the house of the Lord, and on the wall of Ophel he built much. He also built cities in the mountains of Judah, and in the forests he built fortresses and towers. He fought with the king of the children of Ammon and prevailed against him. The children of Ammon gave him in that year a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand measures of wheat, and ten thousand of barley. This the children of Ammon rendered him both the second and third year. Jotham became mighty, because he ordered his ways before the Lord his God. Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all his wars and his conduct, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. And Jotham slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and Ahaz his son reigned in his stead. Chapter 28.

Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the sight of the Lord, as David his father had done; but he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and moreover he cast images for Baal. He himself burned incense

Paralipomenon [Chronicles].

He burned incense in the valley of Hinnom and passed his sons through fire according to the customs of the nations whom the Lord had driven out before the children of Israel. He sacrificed and burned incense on the high places and on the hills and under every leafy tree. And the Lord his God delivered him into the hand of the king of Syria, who struck him with a great plague and carried away many from his territory and brought them to Damascus. He was also delivered into the hand of the king of Israel, who struck him with a great slaughter. For Pekah son of Remaliah killed one hundred and twenty thousand men of Judah in one day, all of them warriors, because they had forsaken the Lord God of their fathers. At the same time Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king's son and Azrikam the governor of the house and Elkanah who was second to the king. The children of Israel carried away captive from their brothers two hundred thousand women, boys and girls, together with a vast amount of plunder, and brought it all to Samaria. At that time there was a prophet of the Lord named Oded, who went out to meet the army returning to Samaria and said to them: Behold, because the Lord God of your fathers was angry with Judah, he delivered them into your hands, and you have killed them with a cruelty that has reached up to heaven. And now you intend to subject the children of Judah and Jerusalem as your male and female slaves, which is something you ought not to do. For you yourselves have sinned against the Lord your God. But listen to my counsel and return the captives you have taken from your brothers, because the great wrath of the Lord hangs over you. Then certain leaders of the children of Ephraim stood up: Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Ezekiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai, against those who were coming from the war, and said to them: You shall not bring the captives here, lest we sin against the Lord. Why do you wish to add

to our sins and to heap up our offenses? For it is already a great sin, and the fierce wrath of the Lord hangs over Israel. So the warriors left the captives and the spoils before the princes and all the assembly. And the men who were mentioned by name rose up and took the captives, and from the spoils they clothed all who were naked among them. They dressed them and gave them sandals, and gave them food and drink, and anointed them, and carried on donkeys all who were feeble, and brought them to Jericho, the city of palms, to their brothers. Then they returned to Samaria. At that time King Ahaz sent to the king of the Assyrians asking for help. The Edomites came and attacked Judah and carried off prisoners. The Philistines also spread out across the lowland cities and into the south of Judah and captured Beth-shemesh, and Aijalon, and Gederoth, and Socho with its villages, and Timnah with its villages, and Gimzo with its villages, and they settled there. For the Lord had humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Judah, since he had abandoned the Lord and brought disgrace. So Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came against him and afflicted him and devastated him without any resistance. And Ahaz, having stripped the house of the Lord and the houses of the king and the princes, gave tribute to the king of Assyria, but it did him no good. Moreover, in his time of distress he increased his contempt of the Lord. King Ahaz himself sacrificed to the gods of Damascus who had struck him, saying: The gods of the kings of Syria help them, and I will offer sacrifices to them so that they may help me. But they were the ruin of him and of all Israel. And when Ahaz had plundered all...

. Second .

He shut the doors of the temple of God, broke its vessels, and made himself altars in every corner of Jerusalem. In every city of Judah he erected altars to burn incense, provoking the Lord, the God of his fathers, to anger. The rest of his acts and all his deeds, first and last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel. Ahaz slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of Jerusalem, but he was not brought into the tombs of the kings of Israel. And Hezekiah his son reigned in his place, in the twenty-fifth year. So Hezekiah began to reign when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abijah, the daughter of Zechariah. He did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that David his father had done. In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of the Lord and repaired them. He brought in the priests and the Levites and gathered them in the eastern square and said to them: Hear me, Levites! Sanctify yourselves and sanctify the house of the Lord, the God of your fathers, and carry out the filth from the sanctuary. Our fathers have sinned and done evil in the sight of the Lord our God; they have forsaken him and turned their faces away from the dwelling of the Lord our God and turned their backs; they have shut the doors of the vestibule and put out the lamps; they have not burned incense nor offered burnt offerings in the sanctuary of the God of Israel. Therefore the wrath of the Lord came upon Judah and Jerusalem, and he made them an object of terror and horror and hissing, as you can see with your own eyes. For our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and daughters and wives have been taken captive because of this wickedness. Now therefore it pleases me that we enter into a covenant with the Lord, the God of Israel, that he may turn away his fierce anger from us. My children, do not be negligent. The Lord has chosen you to stand before him and to serve him, to worship him and to burn incense to him. Then the Levites arose: Mahath the son of Amasai, and Joel the son of Azariah, of the sons of Kohath; and of the sons of Merari: Kish the son of Abdi and Azariah the son of Jehallelel; and of the sons of Gershon: Joah the son of Zimmah and Eden the son of Joah; and of the sons of Elizaphan: Shimri and Jeuel; and of the sons of Asaph: Zechariah and Mattaniah; and of the sons of Heman: Jehuel and Shimei; and of the sons of Jeduthun: Shemaiah and Uzziel. They gathered their brothers and sanctified themselves, and went in according to the command of the king and the order of the Lord to cleanse the house of the Lord. The priests went into the inner part of the house of the Lord to cleanse it, and they brought out all the unclean things that they found in the temple of the Lord into the court of the house of the Lord; and the Levites took them and carried them out to the Kidron Valley. They began to sanctify on the first day of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the vestibule of the temple of the Lord; they sanctified the house of the Lord in eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished. Then they went in to Hezekiah the king and said: We have cleansed all the house of the Lord, the altar of burnt offering and all its vessels, and the table of showbread with all its vessels, and all the furnishings of the temple that King Ahaz had defiled during his reign when he broke faith; and behold, they are all before the altar of the Lord. And Hezekiah the king rose early, gathered the rulers of the city, and went up to the house of the Lord. They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats for a sin offering

· Paralipomenon (Chronicles) ·
