for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, for Judah. And he spoke to the priests, the sons of Aaron, to offer them upon the altar of the Lord. So they slaughtered the bulls, and the priests received the blood and poured it upon the altar. They also slaughtered the rams, and poured their blood upon the altar. And they slaughtered the lambs and poured the blood upon the altar. Then they brought the goats for a sin offering before the king and all the assembly. And they laid their hands upon them, and the priests slaughtered them and sprinkled their blood upon the altar as an atonement for all Israel. For the king had commanded that the burnt offering should be made for all Israel as a sin offering. He stationed the Levites in the house of the Lord with cymbals, harps, and lyres, according to the arrangement of David and of Gad the king's seer and Nathan the prophet; for the commandment was from the Lord through his prophets. The Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets. And Hezekiah commanded that the burnt offerings be offered upon the altar. And when the burnt offerings began, the song of the Lord began also, with the trumpets and with the instruments of David king of Israel. And all the assembly worshipped, while the singers sang and the trumpeters sounded, until the burnt offering was finished. When the offering was finished, the king and all who were present with him bowed and worshipped. And Hezekiah the king and the princes commanded the Levites to praise the Lord with the words of David and of Asaph the seer. And they sang praises with gladness, and they bowed their heads and worshipped. Then Hezekiah said: Now you have consecrated yourselves to the Lord; come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of the Lord. And all the assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings and burnt offerings with a willing heart.

Now the number of the burnt offerings which the assembly brought was this: seventy bulls, one hundred rams, two hundred lambs; and six hundred bulls and three thousand sheep were consecrated to the Lord. But the priests were too few and could not skin all the burnt offerings, so their brothers the Levites helped them until the work was done and the priests had sanctified themselves. For the Levites were more upright in heart to sanctify themselves than the priests. So there were very many burnt offerings, with the fat of the peace offerings and the drink offerings for the burnt offering. Thus the service of the house of the Lord was restored. And Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced because of what God had done for the people, for the thing had come about suddenly. Chapter 30.

Hezekiah sent word to all Israel and Judah, and wrote letters also to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to the house of the Lord at Jerusalem to keep the Passover to the Lord, the God of Israel. For the king and his princes and all the assembly in Jerusalem had decided to keep the Passover in the second month, since they could not keep it at its proper time because the priests had not sanctified themselves in sufficient number, nor had the people assembled at Jerusalem. The plan seemed right to the king and all the assembly. So they decided to send a proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, that the people should come and keep the Passover to the Lord, the God of Israel, at Jerusalem, for they had not kept it in great numbers as prescribed. So the couriers went throughout all Israel and Judah with letters from the king and his princes, as the king had commanded, saying: O people of Israel, return to the Lord, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, that he may turn again to the remnant of you who have escaped from the hand of the kings of Assyria. Do not be like your fathers and your brothers who were unfaithful to the Lord God of their fathers,

And he delivered them to destruction, so that they themselves would perish. Do not harden your necks as your fathers did. Submit yourselves to the Lord and come to his sanctuary which he has sanctified forever. Serve the Lord God of your fathers, and he will turn away from you the wrath of his fury. For if you return to the Lord, your brothers and your children will find mercy before their masters who led them into captivity, and they will return to this land. For the Lord your God is merciful and compassionate, and he will not turn his face away from you if you return to him. So the runners went swiftly from city to city through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh as far as Zebulun, while the people mocked and ridiculed them. However, some men of Asher and Manasseh and Zebulun, humbling themselves, came to Jerusalem. In Judah also the hand of the Lord was at work, giving them one heart to carry out the command of the king and the princes, the word of the Lord. A great multitude gathered in Jerusalem to celebrate the feast of Unleavened Bread in the second month. They arose and tore down the altars that were in Jerusalem, and everything on which incense was burned to idols they threw into the Kidron brook. They sacrificed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and the Levites, being now sanctified, offered burnt offerings in the house of the Lord. They stood in their place according to the order of Moses, the man of God. The priests received the blood from the hands of the Levites, because the great multitude was not sanctified, and therefore the Levites killed the Passover for those who were not able to sanctify themselves to the Lord. A large portion of the people from Ephraim and Manasseh and Issachar and Zebulun who had not sanctified themselves ate the Passover not as it was written, and Hezekiah prayed for them, saying: The Lord who is good will be merciful to all who seek the Lord God of their fathers with all their heart, and he will not impute it to them that they were not sanctified. The Lord listened and was appeased. The children of Israel who were found in Jerusalem celebrated the feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great joy, praising the Lord day by day, both the Levites and the priests, with instruments suited to their ministry. And Hezekiah spoke to the heart of all the Levites who had good understanding in the service of the Lord, and they ate throughout the seven days of the festival, offering peace offerings and praising the Lord God of their fathers. The whole assembly agreed to celebrate another seven days, and they did so with great joy. For Hezekiah king of Judah provided for the assembly a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep. The princes gave to the people a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep. A great number of priests sanctified themselves, and the whole multitude of Judah, both priests and Levites, and all the assembly that came from Israel, as well as strangers from the land of Israel and those dwelling in Judah, rejoiced. There was great celebration in Jerusalem, the like of which had not been seen there since the days of Solomon son of David king of Israel. The priests and the Levites arose and blessed the people, and their voice was heard, and their prayer came to his holy dwelling place. Chapter 31. When all this was duly celebrated, all Israel who were present in the cities of Judah went out and broke the idols and cut down the sacred groves, tore down the high places and demolished the altars, not only throughout Judah and Benjamin, but also in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they had utterly destroyed them all. Then all the children of Israel returned

· Chronicles ·

All the children of Israel returned to their possessions and cities. And Hezekiah appointed the divisions of priests and Levites according to their divisions, each one in his own office, both priests and Levites, for burnt offerings and for peace offerings, to minister, to give thanks, and to sing praises in the gates of the courts of the Lord. He also appointed the king's portion from his own wealth for burnt offerings — morning and evening, and on sabbaths, new moons, and set feasts, as it is written in the law of Moses. And he commanded the people who lived in Jerusalem to give the portion to the priests and the Levites, that they might be free to observe the law of the Lord. As soon as the commandment spread abroad, the children of Israel brought in abundance the firstfruits of grain, wine, oil, honey, and of all the produce of the field, and brought in abundantly the tithe of all things. And the children of Israel and Judah who lived in the cities of Judah also brought in the tithe of cattle and sheep, and the tithe of holy things that had been consecrated to the Lord their God, and they piled them up in heaps. In the third month they began to lay the heaps, and in the seventh month they finished. When Hezekiah and the princes came and saw the heaps, they blessed the Lord and his people Israel. Then Hezekiah asked the priests and the Levites concerning the heaps. And Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok, answered him and said: Since the people began to bring their offerings into the house of the Lord, we have eaten and had enough, and there is a great store left, for the Lord has blessed his people, and what is left is this great store you see. Then Hezekiah commanded them to prepare storerooms in the house of the Lord, and when they had done so, they faithfully brought in the offerings, the tithes, and the dedicated things. The overseer of these things was Conaniah the Levite, and Shimei his brother was second,

and after him Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah, appointed by Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by the appointment of Hezekiah the king and Azariah the ruler of the house of God, to whom all things pertained. And Kore the son of Imnah the Levite, the keeper of the east gate, was over the freewill offerings of God, to distribute the oblations of the Lord, and the most holy things. And under him were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah, in the cities of the priests, to distribute faithfully to their brothers the portions, both small and great, to males from three years old and upward, to everyone who entered the house of the Lord each day for his service, for their offices according to their divisions. The priests were distributed by family, and the Levites from twenty years old and upward, in their appointments and by their divisions, to every household of their wives and children, male and female, faithfully with all that had been consecrated. And for the sons of Aaron, the priests, who were in the fields of the common-lands of their cities, in every city, there were men designated to distribute portions to every male among the priests and among the Levites. Thus Hezekiah did throughout all Judah, and he did what was good and right and faithful before the Lord his God. In everything that he undertook for the service of the house of God, in accordance with the law and the commandments, seeking his God with his whole heart, he prospered. Chapter 32.

After these things and these acts of faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and invaded Judah and besieged the fortified cities, intending to capture them. When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and that the full force of war

· Chronicles ·

Judah. He was exalted after these things before all the nations. In those days Hezekiah was sick unto death, and he prayed to the Lord. And the Lord heard him and gave him a sign; but he did not render according to the benefit he had received, for his heart was lifted up. Therefore wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem. And he humbled himself afterward, because his heart had been lifted up, both he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so the wrath of the Lord did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah. Now Hezekiah was very wealthy and honored, and he accumulated great treasures of silver and gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and all manner of desirable vessels; storehouses also for the produce of grain, wine, and oil; stalls for all kinds of livestock, and flocks in abundance, and cities. For God had given him very great wealth. This same Hezekiah also stopped the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon, and directed them down to the west side of the city of David. Hezekiah prospered in all his works. However, concerning the ambassadors of the princes of Babylon, who were sent to him to inquire about the wonder that had occurred in the land, God left him alone to test him, that He might know all that was in his heart. Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his goodness are written in the vision of Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel. So Hezekiah rested with his fathers, and they buried him above the tombs of the sons of David. And all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem honored him at his death. Then Manasseh his son reigned in his place. Chapter 33.
Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.

But he did evil in the sight of the Lord, according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord had cast out before the children of Israel. For he went back and rebuilt the high places which Hezekiah his father had broken down; he raised up altars for the Baals, and made wooden images; and he worshiped all the host of heaven and served them. He also built altars in the house of the Lord, of which the Lord had said, "In Jerusalem shall My name be forever." And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord; and he caused his sons to pass through the fire in the Valley of Ben Hinnom. He practiced soothsaying, used witchcraft and sorcery, and consulted mediums and spiritists. He did much evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke Him to anger. He even set a carved image, the idol which he had made, in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put My name forever; and I will not again remove the foot of Israel from the land which I have appointed for your fathers, only if they are careful to do all that I have commanded them, according to the whole law and the statutes and the ordinances given by Moses." So Manasseh seduced Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to do more evil than the nations whom the Lord had destroyed before the children of Israel. And the Lord spoke to Manasseh and his people, but they would not listen. Therefore the Lord brought upon them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria, who took Manasseh captive, bound him with bronze fetters, and carried him off to Babylon. Now when he was in affliction, he implored the Lord his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers. He prayed to Him, and God received his entreaty, heard his supplication, and brought him back to Jerusalem into his kingdom; and

(second column heading) Second [book? / part?]

Manasseh recognized that the Lord himself was God. After these things he built a wall outside the city of David, to the west of Gihon, in the valley, from the entrance of the Fish Gate as far as Ophel, and he raised it to a great height. He appointed military commanders in all the fortified cities of Judah, and removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the Lord, and all the altars that he had built on the mountain of the house of the Lord and in Jerusalem, and he cast them outside the city. He also restored the altar of the Lord and offered upon it sacrifices of peace offerings and of praise, and commanded Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel. Nevertheless the people still sacrificed at the high places to the Lord their God. Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the Lord God of Israel, are written in the records of the kings of Israel. His prayer also, and how God received his entreaty, and all his sin and trespass, and the places where he built high places and set up wooden images and carved images before he humbled himself: these are written in the records of the Hozai. So Manasseh slept with his fathers and they buried him in his house; and Amon his son reigned in his place. Amon was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. He did evil in the sight of the Lord as Manasseh his father had done; and Amon sacrificed to all the carved images which his father Manasseh had made and served them, and did not humble himself before the Lord as his father Manasseh had humbled himself; but this same Amon trespassed more and more. And his servants conspired against him and killed him in his own house; but the people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place.

Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. He did what was right in the sight of the Lord and walked in the ways of his father David; he did not turn aside to the right or to the left. In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still a boy, he began to seek the God of his father David; and in the twelfth year he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the wooden images, and the carved and molded images. They broke down the altars of the Baals before him, and he cut down the incense altars that were high above them, and the wooden images and the carved images he broke in pieces and made dust of them and scattered it on the graves of those who had sacrificed to them. He also burned the bones of the priests on their altars, and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem. And in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, as far as Naphtali, he broke everything down. When he had broken down the altars and the wooden images, beaten the carved images into powder, and cut down all the incense altars throughout all the land of Israel, he returned to Jerusalem. In the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had purged the land and the temple, he sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah and Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah the son of Joahaz the recorder, to repair the house of the Lord his God. When they came to Hilkiah the high priest, they delivered the money that was brought into the house of God, which the Levites who kept the doors had gathered from the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim and from all the remnant of Israel, from all Judah and Benjamin and the inhabitants of Jerusalem. And they put it in the hand of the workmen who had the oversight of the house of the Lord; and they gave it to the workmen who worked in the house of the Lord, to repair and restore the temple. They gave it to the craftsmen and builders to buy hewn stone and timber for beams and for flooring of the buildings which the kings of Judah had destroyed.

Judah. Who faithfully did all things. Now the overseers of the workers were Jakab and Abdias of the sons of Merari, Zacharias and Mosolla of the sons of Caath, who pressed on the work; all the Levites who were skilled in playing instruments. Over those who carried the burdens to the various uses were scribes and masters of the Levite gatekeepers. And when they brought out the money that had been brought into the temple of the Lord, Hilkiah the priest found the book of the law of the Lord given by the hand of Moses, and he said to Shaphan the scribe: I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord. And he gave it to him. And he brought the volume to the king, and told him, saying: All things that you committed to the hand of your servants have been completed. They have melted down the silver that was found in the house of the Lord, and it has been given to the overseers of the craftsmen and to those who work at various tasks. Furthermore Hilkiah the priest gave me this book. And when it had been read in the presence of the king, and he had heard the words of the law, he tore his garments, and commanded Hilkiah and Aidan the son of Shaphan, and Abdon the son of Micha, and Shaphan the scribe, and Alsai the servant of the king, saying: Go and consult the Lord for me and for the remnant of Israel and Judah, concerning all the words of this book that has been found. For great is the wrath of the Lord that has poured out upon us, because our fathers have not kept the word of the Lord, to do all things that are written in this volume. Then Hilkiah and those who had been sent by the king went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Sellum the son of Thecuath, the son of Hasra, keeper of the wardrobe, who dwelt in Jerusalem in the second part, and they spoke to her the words we have related. And she answered them: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Tell the man who sent you to me. Thus says the Lord: Behold I will bring evils upon this place and upon the inhabitants thereof, and all the curses that are written in the book which they have read before the king of Judah, because they have forsaken me and have sacrificed to strange gods, to provoke me to anger by all the works of their hands; therefore my wrath shall pour out upon this place and shall not be quenched. But to the king of Judah who sent you to inquire of the Lord, thus shall you say: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Because you have heard the words of the volume, and your heart was moved, and you humbled yourself before God at the things that are spoken against this place and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and reverencing my face, you tore your garments and wept before me: I also have heard you, says the Lord. For now I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be brought to your tomb in peace, and your eyes shall not see all the evil that I will bring upon this place and upon the inhabitants thereof. They brought back therefore to the king all that she had said. And he called together all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem, and went up to the house of the Lord, and all the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests and the Levites and all the people from the least to the greatest. And when he had read in their hearing in the house of the Lord all the words of the volume, the king standing at his tribunal made a covenant before the Lord to walk after him and to keep his commandments and testimonies and justifications with his whole heart and with his whole soul, and to do the things that were written in that volume which he had read. He also adjured all who were found in Jerusalem and Benjamin, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem did according to the covenant of the Lord God of their fathers. And Josiah took away all the abominations from all the countries of the children of Israel, and made all who were left in Israel serve the Lord their God. All his days they did not depart from the Lord God of their fathers. Chapter XXXV.

Pasipon.

which God commanded me to hasten toward. Cease acting against God, who is with me, lest he kill you. Josiah refused to turn back but prepared for battle against him, and would not heed the words that Necho spoke from God's mouth; but he came to fight in the plain of Megiddo. And when he was wounded there by archers, he said to his servants: Take me away from the battle, for I am grievously wounded. His servants moved him from one chariot to another that followed after him, as was the royal custom, and brought him to Jerusalem. He died and was buried in the tombs of his fathers, and all Judah and Jerusalem mourned for him, especially Jeremiah, whose singers and songstresses still repeat lamentations over Josiah to this day, as a law established in Israel. Behold, it is written in the book of Lamentations. The rest of the acts of Josiah, and his mercies according to what is written in the law of the Lord, and his deeds, first and last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel. Chapter 36.

Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah and made him king in Jerusalem in his father's place. Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. The king of Egypt removed him when he came to Jerusalem, and condemned the land to a hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold. He appointed his brother Eliakim king over Judah and Jerusalem and changed his name to Jehoiakim. And Necho took Jehoahaz his brother and brought him to Egypt. Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; and he did evil in the sight of the Lord his God. Against him Nebuchadnezzar king of Chaldea came up and bound him in chains and brought him to Babylon, and also carried away some of the vessels of the house of the Lord and put them in his palace. Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim and the abominations he committed, and what was found against him,

are recorded in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel. His son Jehoiachin reigned in his place. Jehoiachin was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem, and he did evil in the sight of the Lord. And when the year had run its course, King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him to Babylon, with the precious vessels of the house of the Lord, and made his uncle Zedekiah king over Judah and Jerusalem. Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. He did evil in the eyes of the Lord his God, and did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke to him from the mouth of the Lord. He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God; he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against turning to the Lord God of Israel. Moreover all the leading priests and the people transgressed more and more, following all the abominations of the nations, and polluted the house of the Lord which he had made holy in Jerusalem. And the Lord God of their fathers sent persistently to them by his messengers, rising up early and sending, because he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place. But they kept mocking the messengers of God, despising his words and scoffing at his prophets, until the wrath of the Lord rose against his people, until there was no remedy. Therefore he brought against them the king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and had no compassion on young man or virgin, old man or aged; he gave them all into his hand, and all the vessels of the house of God, great and small, and the treasures of the temple and of the king

· Preamble ·

And he brought the leaders to Babylon. The enemies burned the house of God and tore down the wall of Jerusalem. They burned all the towers, and whatever was precious they demolished. If anyone had escaped the sword, he was led to Babylon and served the king and his sons, until the king of Persia came to power and the word of the Lord spoken through Jeremiah was fulfilled, and the land had observed its sabbaths. For all the days of its desolation it kept sabbath, until seventy years were completed. Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom and also put it in writing, saying: Thus says Cyrus king of Persia: The Lord, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has charged me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever is among you of all his people, may the Lord his God be with him. Let him go up. Here ends the book of Chronicles. The Prayer of Manasseh king of Judah, when he was held captive in Babylon.

O Lord God Almighty, the God of our fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and of their righteous offspring; who made heaven and earth with all their glory; who bound the sea by the word of your command; who shut up the abyss and sealed it with your terrible and glorious name; whom all things fear and tremble before the face of your power; for the majesty of your glory cannot be borne, and the wrath of your threatening toward sinners is irresistible; yet your promised mercy is immeasurable and unsearchable; for you are the Lord Most High, of great compassion, long-suffering and very merciful, and you relent at human suffering. You, O Lord, according to your great goodness promised repentance and forgiveness to those who sinned against you; and in the multitude of your mercies you appointed repentance for sinners, so that they might be saved. You therefore, O Lord, God of the righteous, did not appoint repentance for the righteous, for Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, those who did not sin against you;

but I have sinned beyond the number of the sand of the sea. My transgressions are multiplied, and I am not worthy to behold and see the height of heaven, for the multitude of my iniquities. I am bent down by many iron bonds, so that I cannot lift up my head, and there is no relief for me; for I have provoked your wrath and done evil before you, setting up abominations and multiplying offenses. And now I bend the knee of my heart, beseeching your goodness. I have sinned, O Lord, I have sinned, and I acknowledge my transgressions. I earnestly beseech you, forgive me, O Lord, forgive me; do not destroy me together with my iniquities; do not be angry with me forever or lay up evil for me, but deliver me, though I am unworthy, according to your great mercy; and I will praise you continually all the days of my life; for all the powers of heaven sing your praise, and yours is the glory forever and ever. Amen. Here ends the Prayer of Manasseh king of Judah. Here begins the Preface of St. Jerome to the Book of Ezra.

Whether it is more difficult to do what you have commanded or to refuse, I have not yet decided. For to yield to your imperious demands is burdensome, and the weight of the task imposed presses upon the neck so that one must stoop under the load before lifting it. Added to this are the efforts of my detractors, who think that everything I write is to be criticized. And sometimes, against their own conscience, they publicly tear apart what they secretly read, compelling me to cry out: O Lord, deliver my soul from lying lips and from a deceitful tongue. It is now three years that you continually write and write back asking me to translate the books of Ezra and Esther from Hebrew for you, as though you did not have Greek and Latin volumes; or as if whatever is translated by us ought not at once to be approved by all. It is in vain, as someone said, to struggle, and to seek nothing but hatred through one's efforts — that is the act of a madman.

· Prologue ·

Therefore I beseech you, my lord and dearest Rogaianus: that, content with a private reading, you do not bring these books out in public, nor press them upon the fastidious, and that you avoid those who are accustomed to judge others and yet know how to do nothing themselves. Those among you whom our work does not displease, let them use this as a model: being warned that the Hebrew names, of which there is a great abundance in this volume, should be written out distinctly and at proper intervals. For it profits nothing to have corrected a book unless the diligence of the correction is preserved by the copyists. Let no one be troubled that only one book has been issued by us, nor let anyone be delighted by the fictions of the third and fourth books of the Apocrypha: since even among the Hebrews the words of Ezra and Nehemiah are gathered into a single volume, and those things which are not found among them — nor among the twenty-two scribes — are to be cast far aside. And if anyone brings against you the Seventy Translators as an authority — whose exemplars the very variety of copies, torn and overturned, demonstrates — and it cannot at any point be asserted with certainty what the correct reading is: send him to the Gospels, where many things are cited from the Old Testament that are not found in the Septuagint translators: such as "He shall be called a Nazarene," and "Out of Egypt I called my son," and "They shall look upon him whom they have pierced," and others — if we were to rebuild in a fuller work — seek from him where these are written. And if he cannot produce them, let you read from those exemplars which, having recently been published by us, the tongues of detractors daily wound. But to come to the point: what I am about to bring forward is certainly most equitable. I have published something which is not in the Greek, or is otherwise rendered there; am I to be called an interpreter? Let them ask the Hebrews: and let them either grant or deny credit to the original authors of my translation. Moreover it is one thing if, with eyes closed,

they wish to speak evil of what they see: and they do not imitate the zeal and goodwill of the Greeks, who after the Seventy Translators, now that the Gospel of Christ was shining forth, examined the Jewish and Ebionite interpreters of the Old Law — namely Aquila, Symmachus, and Theodotion — with curiosity, and through Origen's work dedicated them in the churches in the Hexapla: how much more should the Latins be grateful, that something resulting from Greece itself might be borrowed from them? First, because it is a matter of great expense and infinite difficulty to be able to have all the exemplars; and then even those who have them, being ignorant of the Hebrew tongue, will err all the more, not knowing which of the various readings is correct. This did not happen even to a certain most wise man recently among the Greeks: so that he sometimes, abandoning the sense of Scripture, followed the error of some individual interpreter. But we, who have at least a small knowledge of the Hebrew tongue, and to whom the Latin language is not at all lacking, can better judge of other things and bring forth in our own tongue what we ourselves understand. Therefore, though Sibylla and Victor and Symon may at times be indignant, my modest eloquence will never be silenced in aiding my own people: even a small tongue shall stammer. Let those who wish read it; those who do not wish may cast it aside. I will be urged on more by your charity to study than deterred by the detraction and hatred of those others. Here ends the Prologue. Here begins the first Book of Ezra. Chapter One.
In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, that the word of the Lord spoken by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians, and he caused a proclamation to go forth throughout all his kingdom, also in writing, saying: Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians: The Lord God of heaven has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has commanded me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judea. Who among you is of all his people? The Lord his God be with him.

· Ezra ·

Accub, son of Atsita, son of Jobai: one hundred and twenty-nine. The Nethinim. The sons of Fia, son of Asupha, son of Tebbaoth, son of Ceros, son of Liaa, son of Phadon, son of Lebana, son of Azaba, son of Accub, son of Agab, son of Selmai, son of Anan, son of Gadoel, son of Gaer, son of Raahia, son of Rasin, son of Nechoda, son of Gazem, son of Aza, son of Phasea, son of Lesee, son of Asenaa, son of Munim, son of Nephusim, son of Bechue, son of Acupha, son of Azur, son of Besluth, son of Maida, son of Arla, son of Bercos, son of Lisara, son of Thema, son of Nasia, son of Athupha. The servants of Solomon: the sons of Sotei, son of Sophereth, son of Pharuda, son of Iala, son of Dercon, son of Geddel, son of Saphata, son of Athil, son of Phpcereth, who were of Aselbaim: the sons of Amun. All the Nethinim and the sons of the servants of Solomon were three hundred and ninety-two. And these were those who went up from Thelmala, Thelarla, Cherub, Don, and Mer, but could not show their fathers' houses or their descent, whether they were of Israel. The sons of Dalaia, the sons of Tobia, the sons of Nechoda: six hundred and fifty-two. And of the sons of the priests: the sons of Tobia, the sons of Acros, the sons of Berzellai, who had taken a wife from the daughters of Berzellai the Galaadite, and was called by their name. These sought their genealogical record but did not find it, and they were excluded from the priesthood. And Athersacha told them that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest should arise learned and skilled. The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty, besides their male and female servants who were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; and among them were two hundred male and female singers. Their horses were seven hundred and thirty-six; their mules, two hundred and forty-five; their camels, four hundred and thirty-five; their donkeys, six thousand seven hundred and twenty. And some of the heads of families,

when they came to the temple of the Lord which is in Jerusalem, offered freely to the house of God to restore it in its place. According to their ability they gave to the treasury of the work: sixty-one thousand gold darics, and five thousand silver minas, and one hundred priestly garments. So the priests and the Levites and some of the people, and the singers and the gatekeepers and the Nethinim, lived in their towns; and all Israel in their towns. Chapter III.

When the seventh month came, and the children of Israel were in their towns, the people gathered as one man in Jerusalem. Then Jeshua the son of Jozadak arose, with his fellow priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel with his kinsmen, and they built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the Law of Moses the man of God. They set the altar in its place, for fear was on them because of the peoples of the lands, and they offered burnt offerings on it to the Lord, morning and evening. And they kept the Feast of Tabernacles, as it is written, and offered the daily burnt offerings by number according to the rule, as each day required, and after that the regular burnt offerings, the offerings at the new moon and at all the appointed feasts of the Lord that were consecrated, and the offerings of everyone who made a freewill offering to the Lord. From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the Lord, though the foundation of the temple of the Lord was not yet laid. And they gave money to the masons and the carpenters, and food, drink, and oil to the Sidonians and the Tyrians to bring cedar trees from Lebanon to the sea, to Joppa, according to the grant that they had from Cyrus king of Persia. Now in the second year of their coming to the house of God at Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and

. first .

The golden and silver vessels of the temple of God which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple that was in Jerusalem and had carried away to the temple of Babylon — Cyrus the king brought them forth from the temple of Babylon, and they were given to Sheshbazzar by name, whom he had appointed as governor, saying to him: Take these vessels, go, and place them in the temple that is in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be built in its place. Then accordingly Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house of God in Jerusalem, and from that time until now it has been in building and is not yet completed. Now therefore, if it seems good to the king, let search be made in the royal library which is in Babylon, to find out whether a decree was issued by Cyrus the king that the house of God in Jerusalem should be built, and let the king's decision concerning this matter be sent to us. Chapter VI.
Then Darius the king commanded, and they searched in the library of the books that were stored in Babylon; and there was found at Ecbatana, which is a castle in the province of Media, a scroll, and written therein was a record as follows: In the first year of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king decreed that the house of God which is in Jerusalem should be built, in the place where sacrifices are offered; and that its foundations should be laid, its height sixty cubits and its width sixty cubits, with three courses of great stones and one course of new timber. And the expenses shall be paid from the royal house. Also the golden and silver vessels of the house of God which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the temple in Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, shall be restored and brought back to the temple in Jerusalem, each to its place; and you shall put them in the house of God. Now therefore, Tattenai, governor of the region beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai, and your associates the officials who are beyond the River, keep away from there; let the work on this house of God alone; let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews rebuild this house of God in its place.

Moreover, a decree is issued by me as to what you shall do for these elders of the Jews for the rebuilding of this house of God: the cost is to be paid to these men from the royal revenue, the taxes of the region beyond the River, and with all diligence. And whatever is needed — young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine, and oil, as the priests in Jerusalem require — let it be given to them day by day without fail, so that they may offer pleasing sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons. Also I issue a decree that whoever alters this edict, a timber shall be pulled from his house and he shall be impaled on it, and his house shall be made a dunghill for this. And may the God who has caused his name to dwell there overthrow any king or people who stretches out a hand to alter or destroy this house of God which is in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued this decree; let it be carried out with all diligence. Then Tattenai, the governor of the region beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates carried out with all diligence what Darius the king had ordered. And the elders of the Jews built and prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo. They finished their building by decree of the God of Israel and by decree of Cyrus and Darius and Artaxerxes king of Persia; and this house was finished on the third day of the month of Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king. And the people of Israel, the priests and the Levites, and the rest of the returned exiles, celebrated the dedication of this house of God with joy. They offered at the dedication of this house of God one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs;

· first ·

one hundred measures of wine, one hundred measures of oil, and salt without measure. Whatever pertains to the ritual of the God of heaven, let it be diligently provided in the house of the God of heaven, lest he grow angry against the kingdom of the king and his sons. We also make known to you, concerning all the priests and Levites, singers, doorkeepers, temple servants, and ministers of the house of this God, that you shall have no authority to impose tribute, tax, or toll upon them. And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God which is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges to judge all the people who are beyond the river, that is, all those who know the law of your God; and those who do not know it, you shall teach freely. And whoever does not observe the law of your God and the law of the king, let judgment be strictly executed upon him, whether unto death, or unto exile, or unto confiscation of goods, or unto imprisonment. Blessed be the Lord God of our fathers, who has put such things in the heart of the king, to glorify the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem, and has inclined his mercy toward me before the king and his counselors and all the king's mighty princes. And I, strengthened by the hand of the Lord my God which was upon me, gathered out of Israel chief men to go up with me. Eight in number.

These then are the heads of families and the genealogy of those who went up with me in the reign of Artaxerxes king of Babylon. Of the sons of Phinehas: Gershon. Of the sons of Ithamar: Daniel. Of the sons of David: Hattush. Of the sons of Shecaniah and of the sons of Parosh: Zechariah, and with him were numbered one hundred and fifty men. Of the sons of Pahath-moab: Eliehoenai the son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred men. Of the sons of Shecaniah: the son of Jahaziel, and with him three hundred men. Of the sons of Adin: Ebed the son of Jonathan, and with him fifty men. Of the sons of

Elam: Isaiah the son of Athaliah, and with him seventy men. Of the sons of Shephatiah: Zebadiah the son of Michael, and with him eighty men. Of the sons of Joab: Obadiah the son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred and eighteen men. Of the sons of Shelomith: the son of Josiphiah, and with him one hundred and sixty men. Of the sons of Bebai: Zechariah the son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight men. Of the sons of Azgad: Johanan the son of Hakkatan, and with him one hundred and ten men. Of the sons of Adonikam, who were the last, and these are their names: Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, and with them sixty men. Of the sons of Bigvai: Uthai and Zaccur, and with them seventy men. I gathered them together at the river that runs to Ahava, and we camped there three days. I searched among the people and among the priests and found there none of the sons of Levi. So I sent for Eliezer and Ariel and Shemaiah and Elnathan and Jarib and another Elnathan and Nathan and Zechariah and Meshullam, chief men, and also for Joiarib and Elnathan, men of understanding. And I sent them to Iddo, who is the leader at Casiphia, and I told them what to say to Iddo and to his brothers the temple servants at Casiphia, that they should bring to us ministers for the house of our God. And by the good hand of our God upon us, they brought us a man of great learning, of the sons of Mahli the son of Levi, the son of Israel, namely Sherebiah, with his sons and brothers, eighteen; and Hashabiah, and with him Isaiah of the sons of Merari, with his brothers and their sons, twenty. And of the temple servants whom David and the princes had appointed for the service of the Levites, two hundred and twenty temple servants, all of whom were designated by name. Then I proclaimed a fast there, by the river Ahava, that we might humble ourselves before the Lord our God, and seek from him a safe journey for ourselves and for our children.

Ezra

of all our substance. For I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to defend us against the enemy on the road, because we had said to the king: The hand of our God is upon all who seek him in goodness, and his power and his wrath are against all who forsake him. So we fasted and prayed to our God for this, and he granted us success. Then I separated from among the chief priests twelve men, Sherebiah and Hashabiah, and with them ten of their brethren. And I weighed out to them the silver and the gold and the consecrated vessels of the house of our God, which the king and his counselors and his princes had offered, and all the Israelites who were present. I weighed into their hands three hundred and fifty talents of silver, a hundred silver vessels, a hundred talents of gold, twenty golden bowls worth a thousand darics, and two vessels of fine polished bronze. And I said to them: You are holy to the Lord, and the vessels are holy, and the silver and gold are a freewill offering to the Lord God of your fathers. Watch and keep them until you weigh them before the chief priests and the Levites and the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel in Jerusalem, in the chambers of the house of the Lord. So the priests and the Levites received the weight of the silver and gold and the vessels, to bring them to Jerusalem to the house of our God. Then we departed from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month to go to Jerusalem. And the hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us from the hand of the enemy and those who lay in wait along the way. And we came to Jerusalem and stayed there three days. On the fourth day the silver and the gold and the vessels were weighed in the house of our God into the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest, and with him Eleazar the son of Phinehas, and with them Jozabad the son of Jeshua and Noadiah

the son of Binnui, the Levite, by number and by weight, and all the weight was recorded at that time. Also those who had come from captivity, the returned exiles, offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, twelve male goats as a sin offering — all this was a burnt offering to the Lord. They also delivered the king's orders to the king's satraps and to the governors beyond the river, and they aided the people and the house of God. Chapter 7.

Now when these things had been completed, the princes came to me saying: The people of Israel and the priests and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands and their abominations, namely the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites. For they have taken some of their daughters for themselves and for their sons, and have mingled the holy race with the peoples of the lands. And the hand of the princes and rulers has been chief in this unfaithfulness. When I heard this matter, I tore my garment and my robe and pulled hair from my head and beard, and sat down appalled. Then all who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered to me because of the unfaithfulness of the returned exiles, and I sat appalled until the evening offering. At the evening offering I arose from my fasting, and with my garment and robe torn I fell upon my knees and spread out my hands to the Lord my God and said: O my God, I am ashamed and blush to lift my face to you, for our iniquities have risen higher than our heads and our guilt has mounted up to the heavens from the days of our fathers. And we ourselves have sinned grievously to this day, and in our iniquities

· Ezra ·

Ezra the priest said to them: "You have transgressed and have taken foreign wives, adding to the guilt of Israel. And now make confession to the Lord, the God of your fathers, and do his will, and separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from foreign wives." And all the assembly answered with a loud voice: "As you have said, so it is our duty to do. But the people are many, and it is a time of rain, and we are not able to stand outside; nor is it a work of one day or two, for we have greatly sinned in this matter. Let rulers be appointed over the whole assembly, and let all those in our cities who have taken foreign wives come at appointed times, and with them the elders and judges of each city, until the fierce wrath of our God over this matter is turned away from us." Only Jonathan the son of Asahel and Jahzeiah the son of Tikvah stood against this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levites supported them. And the returned exiles acted accordingly. Ezra the priest selected men who were heads of families, all of them by name, and they sat down on the first day of the tenth month to examine the matter. And by the first day of the first month they had dealt with all the men who had taken foreign wives. Among the sons of the priests who had taken foreign wives were found: of the sons of Jeshua the son of Jozadak and his brothers: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah. They pledged themselves to put away their wives, and being guilty, they offered a ram of the flock for their guilt. Of the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah. Of the sons of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah. Of the sons of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah. Of the Levites:

Jozabad, Shimei, and Kelaiah (that is, Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer. Of the singers: Eliashib. Of the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri. Of Israel, of the sons of Parosh: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah. Of the sons of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah. Of the sons of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza. Of the sons of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athalai. Of the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Jeremoth. Of the sons of Pahath-moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh. Of the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon, Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah. Of the sons of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei. Of the sons of Bani: Maadai, Amram, Uel, Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluhi, Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Mattenai, Jaasu, Bani, Binnui, Shimei, Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah, Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai, Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah, Shallum, Amariah, Joseph. Of the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah. All these had taken foreign wives, and some of the women had borne children. Here ends the first book of Ezra. Here begins the book of Nehemiah, which is:

The words of Nehemiah, son of Hacaliah. In the month of Chislev, in the twentieth year, while I was in the citadel of Susa, Hanani, one of my brothers, came with certain men from Judah. And I asked them concerning the Jews who had survived the exile, and concerning

Jerusalem. And they said to me: The remnant that are left of the captivity there in the province are in great affliction and reproach: the wall of Jerusalem also is broken down, and the gates thereof are burnt with fire. And it came to pass, when I heard these words, that I sat down and wept, and mourned certain days, and fasted, and prayed before the God of heaven. And I said: I beseech thee, O Lord God of heaven, strong, great, and terrible, who keepest covenant and mercy with those that love thee and observe thy commandments: Let thine ear now be attentive, and thine eyes open, that thou mayest hear the prayer of thy servant. I pray before thee now, day and night, for the children of Israel thy servants, and confess the sins of the children of Israel, which we have sinned against thee: both I and my father's house have sinned. We have dealt very corruptly against thee, and have not kept the commandments, nor the statutes, nor the judgments, which thou commandedst thy servant Moses. Remember, I beseech thee, the word that thou commandedst thy servant Moses, saying: If ye transgress, I will scatter you abroad among the nations: But if ye turn unto me, and keep my commandments, and do them; though there were of you cast out unto the uttermost part of the heaven, yet will I gather them from thence, and will bring them unto the place that I have chosen to set my name there. Now these are thy servants and thy people, whom thou hast redeemed by thy great power, and by thy strong hand. O Lord, I beseech thee, let now thine ear be attentive to the prayer of thy servant, and to the prayer of thy servants, who desire to fear thy name: and prosper, I pray thee, thy servant this day, and grant him mercy in the sight of this man. For I was the king's cupbearer. Chapter II. And it came to pass in the month Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, that wine was before him: and I took up the wine, and gave it unto the king. Now I had not been beforetime sad in his presence. Wherefore the king said unto me: Why is thy countenance sad, seeing thou art not sick? This is nothing else but sorrow of heart. Then I was very sore afraid. And I said unto the king: Let the king live for ever: why should not my countenance be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers' sepulchres, lieth waste, and the gates thereof are consumed with fire? Then the king said unto me: For what dost thou make request? So I prayed to the God of heaven. And I said unto the king: If it please the king, and if thy servant have found favour in thy sight, that thou wouldest send me unto Judah, unto the city of my fathers' sepulchres, that I may build it. And the king said unto me, the queen also sitting by him: For how long shall thy journey be? And when wilt thou return? So it pleased the king to send me; and I set him a time. Moreover I said unto the king: If it please the king, let letters be given me to the governors beyond the river, that they may convey me over till I come into Judah; And a letter unto Asaph the keeper of the king's forest, that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the palace which appertained to the house, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that I shall enter into. And the king granted me, according to the good hand of my God upon me. Then I came to the governors beyond the river, and gave them the king's letters. Now the king had sent captains of the army and horsemen with me. When Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel. So I came to Jerusalem, and was there three days. And I arose in the night, I and some few men with me; neither told I any man what my God had put in my heart to do at Jerusalem: neither was there any beast with me, save the beast that I rode upon. And I went out by night by the gate of the valley, even before the dragon well, and to the dung port, and viewed the walls of Jerusalem, which were broken down, and the gates thereof were consumed with fire. And

· Ezra ·

I went to the Fountain Gate and to the King's Pool, but there was no room for the animal I was riding to pass. So I went up by the valley in the night, examining the wall, and then turned back and entered through the Valley Gate, and so returned. The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing, and I had told nothing yet to the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the officials, or the rest who were to do the work. Then I said to them: You know the distress we are in, how Jerusalem lies in ruins and its gates are burned with fire. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so that we may no longer be a disgrace. And I told them of the hand of my God that had been upon me for good, and also of the words that the king had spoken to me. And they said: Let us rise up and build. So they strengthened their hands for the good work. But when Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the Ammonite servant, and Geshem the Arab heard of it, they mocked and despised us, and said: What is this thing you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king? Then I replied to them and said: The God of heaven will make us prosper, and we his servants will arise and build; but you have no portion or right or memorial in Jerusalem. Chapter 3.
Then Eliashib the high priest arose with his fellow priests, and they built the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set up its doors, and they consecrated it as far as the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Tower of Hananel. And next to him the men of Jericho built, and next to them Zaccur the son of Imri built. The sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate; they laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars. And next to them Meremoth the son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz repaired. And next to him Meshullam the son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel repaired.

And next to him Zadok the son of Baana repaired. And next to them the Tekoites repaired, but their nobles did not put their necks to the work of their Lord. The Old Gate was repaired by Joiada the son of Paseah and Meshullam the son of Besodeiah; they laid its beams and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars. And next to them repaired Melatiah the Gibeonite, and Jadon the Meronothite, the men of Gibeon and Mizpah, for the seat of the governor who was beyond the River. Next to him repaired Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths. Next to him repaired Hananiah, one of the perfumers, and they restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall. Next to him repaired Rephaiah the son of Hur, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem. Next to him repaired Jedaiah the son of Harumaph, opposite his house. And next to him repaired Hattush the son of Hashabneiah. Malchijah the son of Harim and Hasshub the son of Pahath-moab repaired another section and the Tower of the Ovens. And next to him repaired Shallum the son of Hallohesh, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, he and his daughters. Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate; they rebuilt it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars, and also a thousand cubits of the wall, as far as the Dung Gate. Malchijah the son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-haccherem, repaired the Dung Gate; he rebuilt it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars. And Shallum the son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate; he rebuilt it and covered it and set up its doors, its bolts and its bars, and the wall of the Pool of Shelah of the king's garden, as far as the stairs that go down from the City of David. After him Nehemiah the son of Azbuk, ruler of half the district of Beth-zur, repaired to a point opposite the tombs of David, and to the pool that had been made with great effort

. Ezra .

Our enemies. Let them not know until we come into their midst and kill them, and cause the work to stop. And it came to pass that when the Jews who lived near them came, they said to us ten times, from all the places where they had come to us: stand in the place behind the wall around it, in order with your swords and spears and bows. And I looked and arose and said to the nobles and the rulers and to the rest of the people: Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and terrible, and fight for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives and your houses. And it came to pass when our enemies heard that it was made known to us, that God had brought their counsel to nothing. And we all returned to the wall, every one to his work. And it came to pass from that day forth, that half of my servants worked in the labor, and the other half held spears, shields, bows and armor; and the rulers were behind all the house of Judah, who were building the wall, and those who bore burdens and those who loaded. Every one with one hand worked at the task, and with the other held a sword. And every one who was building had his sword girded at his side. And the trumpeters were next to me. And I said to the nobles and to the rulers and to the rest of the people: The work is great and wide, and we are separated on the wall far from one another. In whatever place you hear the sound of the trumpet, rally to us there. Our God will fight for us, and we ourselves will work. And half of them held spears from the rise of dawn until the stars came out. Also at that time I said to them: Let every one with his servant stay within Jerusalem, and they shall be a guard for us by night and a labor force by day.

So neither I nor my brothers nor my servants nor the guards who followed me took off our clothes. Each kept his weapon in his hand. Chapter 5.

And there arose a great cry of the people and their wives against their Jewish brothers. Some said: We, our sons and our daughters, are many; let us get grain that we may eat and live. Some said: We are mortgaging our fields, our vineyards and our houses to get grain because of the famine. And others said: We have borrowed money for the king's tax on our fields and our vineyards. Now our flesh is as the flesh of our brothers, our children as their children. Yet we are forcing our sons and daughters to be servants, and some of our daughters have already been enslaved; and we are powerless to help, for other men have our fields and our vineyards. I was very angry when I heard their cry and these words. I took counsel with myself, and I contended with the nobles and the rulers. I said to them: You are each taking interest from your own brothers. And I held a great assembly against them and said to them: We, as far as we were able, have bought back our Jewish brothers who were sold to the nations; but you even sell your brothers, and they are sold to us. They were silent and could find nothing to say. And I said: What you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God, so that the taunts of the nations our enemies will not reproach us? And I myself and my brothers and my servants are lending them money and grain. Let us stop this taking of interest. Return to them this very day their fields, their vineyards,

Jeshua: nine hundred and seventy-four. The children of Immer: one thousand and fifty-two. The children of Pashur: one thousand two hundred and forty-seven. The children of Harim: one thousand and seventeen. Levites. The children of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the children of Hodaviah: seventy-four. Singers. The children of Asaph: one hundred and forty-eight. Gatekeepers. The children of Shallum, the children of Ater, the children of Talmon, the children of Akkub, the children of Hatita, the children of Shobai: one hundred and thirty-eight. The Nethinim. The children of Ziha, the children of Hasupha, the children of Tabbaoth, the children of Keros, the children of Siaha, the children of Padon, the children of Lebana, the children of Hagaba, the children of Shalmai, the children of Hanan, the children of Giddel, the children of Gahar, the children of Reaiah, the children of Rezin, the children of Nekoda, the children of Gazzam, the children of Uzza, the children of Paseah, the children of Besai, the children of Meunim, the children of Nephishesim, the children of Bakbuk, the children of Hakupha, the children of Harhur, the children of Bazlith, the children of Mehida, the children of Harsha, the children of Barkos, the children of Sisera, the children of Temah, the children of Neziah, the children of Hatipha, the children of the servants of Solomon: the children of Sotai, the children of Sophereth, the children of Perida, the children of Jaala, the children of Darkon, the children of Giddel, the children of Shephatiah, the children of Hattil, the children of Pochereth of Zebaim, the son of Amon. All the Nethinim and the children of Solomon's servants were three hundred and ninety-two. These are those who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer, but they could not prove their fathers' houses or their descent, whether they were of Israel. The children of Delaiah, the children of Tobiah, the children of Nekoda: six hundred and forty-two. And of the priests: the children of Hobaiah, the children of Hakkoz, the children of Barzillai, who had taken a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name. These sought their registration among those enrolled in the genealogies, but it was not found there, so they were excluded from the priesthood. The governor told them that they were not to partake of the most holy food until a priest stood up with Urim and Thummim. The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty, besides

their male and female servants, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; and they had two hundred and forty-five singing men and women. Their horses: seven hundred and thirty-six; their mules: two hundred and forty-five; their camels: four hundred and thirty-five; their donkeys: six thousand seven hundred and twenty. Some of the heads of families contributed to the work. The governor gave to the treasury one thousand gold darics, fifty bowls, and five hundred and thirty priestly garments. And some of the heads of families gave to the treasury for the work twenty thousand gold darics and two thousand two hundred silver minas. And the rest of the people gave twenty thousand gold darics, two thousand silver minas, and sixty-seven priestly garments. So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the Nethinim, and all Israel lived in their towns. Chapter VIII.

And when the seventh month came, the children of Israel were in their towns. And all the people gathered as one man into the square before the Water Gate, and they told Ezra the scribe to bring the Book of the Law of Moses that the Lord had commanded Israel. So Ezra the priest brought the Law before the assembly, both men and women and all who could understand what they heard, on the first day of the seventh month. And he read from it facing the square before the Water Gate from early morning until midday, in the presence of the men and the women and those who could understand. And the ears of all the people were attentive to the Book of the Law. And Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform that they had made for the purpose, and beside him stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, and Uriah, and Hilkiah, and Maaseiah on his right hand, and

· Ezra ·

to the left: Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam. Ezra opened the book before all the people, for he stood above all the people. And when he opened it, all the people stood. And Ezra blessed the Lord God with a great voice. And all the people answered, Amen, Amen, lifting up their hands. And they bowed down and worshipped the Lord with their faces to the ground. Now Jeshua, and Bani, and Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodijah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, the Levites, caused the people to understand the law, while the people stood in their place. And they read in the book of the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading. Then Nehemiah, who was the governor, and Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who taught the people, said to all the people: This day is holy to the Lord your God. Do not mourn or weep. For all the people wept when they heard the words of the law. Then he said to them: Go, eat rich food, and drink sweet wine, and send portions to those for whom nothing is prepared, for this day is holy to our Lord. And do not be sorrowful, for the joy of the Lord is your strength. The Levites silenced all the people, saying: Be quiet, for this day is holy; do not grieve. And all the people went to eat and drink and to send portions and to make great celebration, because they had understood the words that had been declared to them. And on the second day the heads of families of all the people, the priests and the Levites, gathered to Ezra the scribe, to study the words of the law. And they found written in the law that the Lord had commanded through Moses that the children of Israel should dwell in booths during the feast of the seventh month, and that they should proclaim and publish it in all their cities and in Jerusalem, saying: Go out to the mountain and bring branches of olive,

and branches of beautiful trees, branches of myrtle, and palm fronds, and branches of thick trees, that they might make booths as it is written. And the people went out and brought them. And they made for themselves booths, every one on his roof, and in their courts, and in the courts of the house of God, and in the square of the Water Gate, and in the square of the Gate of Ephraim. And so the whole congregation of those who had returned from captivity made booths and dwelt in booths. For the children of Israel had not done so since the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day. And there was very great gladness. Also he read from the book of the law of God day by day, from the first day to the last day. And they kept the feast seven days, and on the eighth day there was a solemn assembly, according to the rite. Now on the twenty-fourth day of this month the children of Israel were assembled with fasting and in sackcloth, with dust upon them. And the seed of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners, and stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers. And they stood up in their place and read in the book of the law of the Lord their God for a quarter of the day, and for another quarter they confessed and worshipped the Lord their God. Then the Levites stood on the raised platform: Jeshua and Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, Chenani; and they cried with a loud voice to the Lord their God. And the Levites, Jeshua and Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabniah, Sherebiah, Hodijah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah, said: Stand up and bless the Lord your God from everlasting to everlasting. And let them bless your glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise. You are the Lord, you alone; you have made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their host, the earth and all that is on it, the seas and all that is in them. And you preserve all of them, and the host of heaven worships you. You are the Lord God who chose Abram

· Ezra ·

You abandoned them into the hand of their enemies, and their enemies possessed them. Yet when they cried out to you, you heard from heaven, and according to your great mercies you delivered them many times. You warned them to return to your law, but they acted arrogantly and did not obey your commandments, they sinned against your ordinances, which if a person keeps them, he will live by them. They turned a stubborn shoulder, stiffened their neck, and would not obey. You bore with them for many years, and warned them by your Spirit through your prophets; yet they would not listen. Therefore you gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands. Nevertheless, in your great mercies you did not make an end of them or forsake them, for you are a gracious and merciful God. Now therefore, our God, the great, the mighty, and the awesome God, who keeps covenant and steadfast love, do not let all the hardship seem little to you that has come upon us, our kings, our princes, our priests, our prophets, our ancestors, and all your people, since the time of the kings of Assyria until this day. You have been just in all that has come upon us, for you have dealt faithfully, and we have acted wickedly. Our kings, our princes, our priests, and our ancestors have not kept your law or heeded your commandments and your warnings that you gave them. Even in their own kingdom, amid the great goodness you gave them, and in the large and rich land you set before them, they did not serve you or turn from their evil works. Here we are today, slaves; and the land you gave to our ancestors to enjoy its fruit and its good gifts, we are slaves in it. Its rich yield goes to the kings whom you have set over us because of our sins. They have power also over our bodies and over our livestock at their pleasure, and we are in great distress. Because of all this we make a firm covenant in writing, and our princes, our Levites, and our priests set their seal to it. Chapter 10.

Those who sealed it were: Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah, Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah, Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah, Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch, Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah, Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch, Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin, Maaziah, Bilgai, Shemaiah — these were the priests. And the Levites: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel, and their associates: Shecaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan, Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah, Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah, Hodiah, Bani, Beninu. The leaders of the people: Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani, Bunni, Azgad, Bebai, Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin, Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur, Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai, Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai, Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir, Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua, Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah, Hosea, Hananiah, Hasshub, Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek, Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah, Ahijah, Hanan, Anan, Malluch, Harim, Baanah, and the rest of the people. The priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and all who have separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to follow the law of God, their wives, their sons, their daughters, all who have knowledge and understanding, join with their kin, their nobles, and enter into a curse and an oath to walk in God's law that was given by Moses the servant of God, and to observe and do all the commandments of the Lord our God and his ordinances and his statutes. We will not give our daughters to the peoples of the land or take their daughters for our sons. As for the peoples of the land who bring merchandise or any grain on the Sabbath day to sell, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on a holy day. And we will forgo

. Second.

In the seventh year, with the renewal of the hand of each. And we established over ourselves commandments: that we would give a third part each year to the work of the house of our God: to the showbread, and to the perpetual sacrifice, and to the perpetual burnt offering on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, on the solemn feasts, and on the holy days, and for sin, that atonement might be made for Israel: and for all the work of the house of our God. We also cast lots among the priests, the Levites, and the people, for the offering of wood, to bring it into the house of our God, by the houses of our fathers, at set times year by year, to burn upon the altar of the Lord our God, as it is written in the law of Moses. And we would bring the firstfruits of our ground, and the firstfruits of all fruit of every tree, year by year, into the house of the Lord: also the firstborn of our sons, and of our cattle, as it is written in the law, and the firstlings of our herds and of our flocks; that we would bring them to the house of our God, to the priests that minister in the house of our God. And that we would bring the firstfruits of our dough, and our offerings, and the fruit of all manner of trees, of wine and of oil, to the priests, to the chambers of the house of our God; and the tithes of our ground to the Levites, for the Levites might take the tithes in all the cities of our work. And a priest, the son of Aaron, shall be with the Levites, when the Levites take tithes: and the Levites shall bring up the tithe of the tithes unto the house of our God, to the chambers, into the treasure house. For the children of Israel and the children of Levi shall bring the offering of the grain, of new wine, and of oil, to the chambers, where the vessels of the sanctuary are, and the priests that minister, and the doorkeepers and the singers: and we will not forsake the house of our God. Chapter XI.
Now the leaders dwelt in Jerusalem: but the rest of the people cast lots to bring one in ten to dwell in Jerusalem the holy city, and nine parts to dwell in the other cities.

And the people blessed all the men who willingly offered themselves to dwell at Jerusalem. Now these are the chiefs of the province that dwelt in Jerusalem: but in the cities of Judah every one dwelt in his own possession in their cities: Israel, the priests, and the Levites, and the Nethinims, and the children of Solomon's servants. And in Jerusalem dwelt of the children of Judah, and of the children of Benjamin. Of the children of Judah: Athaiah the son of Uzziah, the son of Zechariah, the son of Amariah, the son of Shephatiah, the son of Mahalaleel. Of the children of Phares: Maaseiah the son of Baruch, the son of Col-hozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, the son of Shiloni. All the sons of Phares that dwelt at Jerusalem were four hundred and sixty-eight valiant men. And these are the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Isaiah.
