And after him Gabbai and Sallai: nine hundred and twenty-eight. And Joel the son of Zichri was their overseer: and Judah the son of Senuah was second over the city. Of the priests: Jedaiah the son of Joiarib, Jachin, Seraiah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitob, was the ruler of the house of God. And their brethren that did the work of the temple were eight hundred and twenty-two. And Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pelaliah, the son of Amzi, the son of Zechariah, the son of Pashur, the son of Malchijah, and his brethren, chief men: two hundred and forty-two. And Amashai the son of Azareel, the son of Ahzai, the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer, and their brethren, mighty men of valor: a hundred and twenty-eight. And their overseer was Zabdiel the son of one of the great men. And of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hashub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Bunni: and Shabbethai and Jozabad, of the chiefs of the Levites, who had oversight of the outward business of the house of God.

. Second .

Now the sons of the singers were gathered from the settlements around Jerusalem, and from the villages of the Netophathites, and from the house of Gilgal, and from the regions of Geba and Azmaveth, for the singers had built villages for themselves around Jerusalem. And the priests and Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gates and the wall. Then I brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall, and appointed two great choirs giving thanks. They went to the right along the wall toward the Dung Gate. And after them went Hoshaiah and half of the leaders of Judah, and Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam, Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah. And from the sons of the priests with trumpets: Zechariah the son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Michaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph; and his brothers Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God; and Ezra the scribe went before them. At the Fountain Gate they went straight up by the stairs of the City of David, on the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, and up to the Water Gate on the east. The second choir of those giving thanks went the other way, and I followed it with half of the people on the wall, past the Tower of the Ovens, and as far as the Broad Wall, and above the Gate of Ephraim, and above the Old Gate, and above the Fish Gate, and the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate; and they came to a halt at the Gate of the Guard. So both choirs of those giving thanks stood in the house of God, and I and half of the officials with me.

And the wives and children also rejoiced, so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard from afar. On that day men were appointed over the storerooms for the treasuries, for the contributions, the firstfruits, and the tithes, to gather into them from the fields of the towns the portions required by the law for the priests and for the Levites, for Judah rejoiced over the priests and the Levites who ministered. And they performed the service of their God and the service of purification, as did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the command of David and his son Solomon. For in the days of David and Asaph, long ago, there were directors of the singers, and there were songs of praise and thanksgiving to God. And all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah gave the daily portions for the singers and the gatekeepers; and they consecrated the Levites, and the Levites consecrated the sons of Aaron. Chapter XIII.

On that day they read from the book of Moses in the hearing of the people. And it was found written in it that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God, because they had not met the children of Israel with bread and water, but had hired Balaam against them to curse them; however, our God turned the curse into a blessing. Now when they had heard the law, they separated from Israel all those of foreign descent. And before this, Eliashib the priest, who had been appointed over the storerooms of the house of our God, and who was related to Tobiah, had prepared for him a large storeroom, where previously they had stored the grain offerings, the frankincense, the vessels, the tithes of grain, wine, and oil, which were given to the Levites, the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the contributions for the priests. But during all this time I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had returned to the king. And at the end of that time I asked leave of the king and came to Jerusalem. And I discovered the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, in preparing him a chamber in the courts of

· Esdras ·

...the Lord said, and it seemed very evil to me. And I cast out the household goods of Tobiah from the storeroom, and gave orders, and they cleansed the storerooms. And I brought back there the vessels of the house of God, the offerings and the incense. And I found that the portions of the Levites had not been given to them, and that the Levites and singers who did the work had fled each to his own region. And I contended with the rulers and said: Why is the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them together and set them in their stations. Then all Judah brought the tithes of grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses. And we appointed as treasurers over the storehouses Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites; and next to them were Hanan the son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, for they were counted faithful, and their duty was to distribute to their brethren. Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and do not blot out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God and for its services. In those days I saw in Judah people treading winepresses on the Sabbath, and bringing in heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys, and also wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of burdens, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. And I warned them on the day when they sold provisions. Men of Tyre also lived there, who brought in fish and all kinds of wares and sold them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah, and in Jerusalem. Then I contended with the nobles of Judah and said to them: What is this evil thing that you are doing, profaning the Sabbath day? Did not your fathers act in this way, and did not our God bring all this disaster on us and on this city? Yet you are bringing more wrath upon Israel by profaning the Sabbath. When the gates of Jerusalem began to grow dark before the Sabbath, I commanded that the doors should be shut and ordered that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath. And some of my servants I set at the gates, so that no burden could be brought in on the Sabbath day. Then the merchants and sellers of all wares spent the night outside Jerusalem once or twice.

And I warned them and said to them: Why do you spend the night before the wall? If you do this again, I will lay hands on you. From that time on they did not come on the Sabbath. And I commanded the Levites that they should purify themselves and come and guard the gates, to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember this also in my favor, O my God, and spare me according to the greatness of your steadfast love. In those days also I saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. And half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and they could not speak the language of Judah, but only the language of each people. And I confronted them and cursed them and beat some of them and pulled out their hair, and made them swear by God, saying: You shall not give your daughters to their sons, or take their daughters for your sons or for yourselves. Did not Solomon king of Israel sin on account of such women? Among the many nations there was no king like him, and he was beloved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel. Nevertheless, foreign women made even him to sin. Shall we then listen to you and do all this great evil and act treacherously against our God by marrying foreign women? And one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite; therefore I chased him from me. Remember them, O my God, because they have desecrated the priesthood, the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites. Thus I cleansed them of everything foreign, and I established the duties of the priests and Levites, each in his work, and for the offering of wood at appointed times, and for the first fruits. Remember me, O my God, for good. Amen. Here ends the book of Nehemiah, which is the second book of Esdras.

Here begins the third book of Esdras.

· Third Esdras ·

Chapter One
Josias kept the passover in Jerusalem unto the Lord, and offered the passover the fourteenth day of the first month, having set the priests according to their daily courses, being arrayed in long garments, in the temple of the Lord. And he spoke unto the Levites, the holy ministers of Israel, that they should hallow themselves unto the Lord, to set the holy ark of the Lord in the house that king Solomon the son of David had built. He said: You shall no more bear the ark upon your shoulders. Now therefore serve the Lord your God, and take care of his people Israel, and prepare yourselves by your families and kindreds, in conformity with the writing of David king of Israel, and according to the magnificence of Solomon his son: stand in the temple according to the groupings of the families of you that are the Levites, who minister in the presence of your brethren the children of Israel. Offer the passover in order, and prepare the sacrifices for your brethren, and keep the passover according to the commandment of the Lord, which was given to Moses. And Josias gave to the people that were present sheep, and lambs, and kids of the goats: thirty thousand, and three thousand calves. These were given out of the king's allowance, as he promised, to the priests for the passover, two thousand oxen, and one hundred calves. And Jechnias and Jeneia, and Nathanael his brothers, and Asabias, and Oziel, and Coraba for the passover gave five thousand sheep, and five hundred calves. When these things were done honorably, the priests and the Levites stood with the unleavened bread by their tribes. And according to the groupings of the heads of families, they offered to the Lord, according to what is written in the book of Moses. And they roasted the passover with fire, as required, and the other sacrifices they boiled in copper pots and cauldrons with good care. And they brought them to all those that were of the people; and afterward they prepared for themselves and for the priests. For the priests offered the fat until nightfall; and the Levites prepared for themselves and for their brethren the sons of Aaron. The singers, the sons of Asaph, were in their order, according to the commandment of David, and Asaph, and Zacharias, and Jeddinus, who was appointed by the king; and the doorkeepers were at every gate, so that none should turn aside from his appointed duty. Their brethren prepared for them. So all the things that belonged to the sacrifice of the Lord were accomplished that day. They kept the passover and offered the sacrifices upon the altar of the Lord, according to the commandment of king Josias. And the children of Israel that were present kept the passover at that time, and the feast of unleavened bread seven days. And such a passover had not been kept in Israel since the time of the prophet Samuel; and none of the kings of Israel had kept such a passover as Josias kept, with the priests, and the Levites, and the Jews, and all Israel that were dwelling in Jerusalem. In the eighteenth year of the reign of Josias was this passover kept. And the works of Josias were upright before his Lord with a heart full of godliness. And the things of his times are written in former times, of those who sinned and acted wickedly against the Lord before all other nations, and those who did not seek the words of the Lord concerning Israel. And after all these acts of Josias, it came to pass that Pharao the king of Egypt came to make war at Carchemish upon Euphrates, and Josias went out against him. But the king of Egypt sent to him, saying: What have I to do with you, O king of Judah? I am not sent against you from the Lord God. My war is upon Euphrates. Come down not against me. And Josias did not turn back his chariot, but undertook to fight with him, not heeding the words of the prophet from the mouth of the Lord; and he joined battle with him in the plain of Megiddo. And the princes came down to king Josias. And the king said to his servants: Take me away from the battle, for I am grievously wounded.

. Third .

Lord of all the earth, the Lord God of Israel, has made known to me that he wishes to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judea. Whoever there is among you of his people, may his Lord God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem. And as many as dwell in any place around, let the men of his place help him with silver and gold, with goods and livestock, and with offerings willingly made for the house of God which is in Jerusalem. And the heads of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, and the priests and Levites, whom God had stirred up to go up to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, arose; and all those around them aided them with silver and gold, with goods and livestock, and with many precious things willingly offered. And many whose spirit God had moved. And King Cyrus brought forth the sacred vessels of the Lord which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken from Jerusalem and placed in the temple of his idol. And Cyrus king of Persia brought them out and gave them to Mithredath the treasurer. These were counted out to Sheshbazzar the prince of Judah. And their number was this: thirty gold basins, two thousand four hundred silver basins, thirty gold bowls, thirty silver bowls, two thousand four hundred other vessels, and a thousand other vessels. All the vessels of gold and silver numbered four thousand five hundred and sixty. And Sheshbazzar took all these along with those who came up from the captivity of Babylon to Jerusalem. Now in the reign of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of their colleagues wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia. The letter was written in Aramaic script. Rehum the commander and Shimshai the secretary wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes, along with the rest of their colleagues, the judges and officials in the regions beyond the River. Now let it be known to the king that the Jews who came up from you to us have come to Jerusalem and are rebuilding the rebellious and evil city; they are finishing its walls and repairing its foundations. Now let it be known to the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls finished, they will not pay tribute, tax, or toll, and the royal revenue will be harmed. Now because we eat the salt of the palace, it is not proper for us to witness the king's dishonor. Therefore we send and inform the king, so that a search may be made in your fathers' records. You will find in the records that this city is a rebellious city, hurtful to kings and provinces, and that sedition was stirred up in it from of old. That is why this city was laid waste. We inform the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls finished, you will then have no possession in the province beyond the River. Then the king sent a reply to Rehum the commander and Shimshai the secretary and the rest of their colleagues who were living in Samaria and in the rest of the province beyond the River. The letter which you sent to us has been plainly read before me. And I commanded, and a search has been made, and it is found that this city from of old has risen up against kings, and that rebellion and sedition have been stirred up in it; and that mighty kings have ruled over Jerusalem, who have ruled over all the province beyond the River, and that tribute, tax, and toll were paid to them. Make a decree that these men be made to cease, and that this city be not rebuilt, until a decree is made by me; and beware of being negligent about this, so that damage does not grow to the hurt of the kings.

Chapter 4

Then when the copy of the letter of King Artaxerxes was read before Rehum and Shimshai the secretary and their colleagues, they went in haste to Jerusalem to the Jews and stopped them by force. Then the work on the house of God in Jerusalem ceased.

· Esdras ·

...until the second year of the reign of Darius, king of Persia. King Darius also made a great feast for all his household servants, and for all his officers of Media and Persia, and for all the nobles and governors, and for the prefects under him from India even unto Ethiopia, over a hundred and twenty-seven provinces. And when they had eaten and drunk and were satisfied, Darius the king went to his bedchamber and fell asleep and then woke up. Then those three young men of the bodyguard who kept watch over the body of the king said to one another: Let each of us state what one thing is strongest, and to whichever one's saying seems wisest, Darius the king will give great gifts: to be clothed in purple, to drink from gold vessels, to sleep on gold, and to ride in a chariot with a gold bridle, and a turban of fine linen, and a chain about his neck; and he shall sit second to Darius for his wisdom, and shall be called a kinsman of Darius. Then they each wrote their own saying and sealed it and put it under the pillow of King Darius, and said: When the king rises, we will give him our writings, and whichever of the three the king and the three princes of Persia shall judge that his word is wisest, to him the victory shall be given as written. One wrote: Wine is strong. Another wrote: The king is stronger. The third wrote: Women are strongest, but above all things truth conquers. And when the king arose, they took their writings and gave them to him, and he read them. And sending, he called all the officials of the Persians and Medes, and the nobles and governors and prefects, and they sat in council; and the writings were read before them. And he said: Call the young men, and they shall explain their words. And they were called and came in. And he said to them: Declare to us concerning what is written. And the first who had spoken of the strength of wine began and said: How powerful is wine over all men who drink it!

It weakens the mind. Likewise it makes the mind of the king and of the orphan vain. And likewise of servant and free man, of poor and rich; it turns every mind to pleasure and joy, and one remembers neither sorrow nor debt; it makes all hearts feel noble, and one remembers neither king nor magistrate, and makes one speak of everything boldly. And they do not remember, when they have drunk, the friendship and brotherhood they had; but shortly after they take up swords, and when they are overcome by wine and rise up they do not remember what they have done. O men, is not wine the strongest? Who then thinks to rule it? And he was silent after this saying. Chapter IIII.

And the next one began to speak, who had said concerning the strength of the king: O men, are not men the strongest, who rule over land and sea and all that is in them? But the king surpasses all, and he dominates them, and whatever he commands them, they do. And if he sends them against warriors, they go and tear down mountains and walls and towers. They kill and are killed, and the king's word they do not disobey. For if they are victorious they bring to the king everything whatsoever they have plundered. Likewise all the others, as many as do not serve as soldiers nor fight but till the land — they also bring tribute to the king when they are summoned. And he alone, if he says "kill," they kill; if he says "come," they come; if he says "strike," they strike; if he says "lay waste," they lay waste; if he says "build," they build; if he says "cut down," they cut down; if he says "plant," they plant. And all the people and the forces obey him; and beyond this he himself reclines and eats and drinks and sleeps. But others keep watch around him, and no one is able to go away individually and do his own work, but they are obedient to his word in everything. O men, how shall the king not be the mightiest, since he has such authority? And he fell silent. The third, who had spoken of women and...

· the third ·

in truth — this is Zerubbabel, who began to speak.
Men, the king is great, and many men there are: but wine surpasses them. Who then is it that rules over them? Is it not women? Women bore the king, and all those who rule over sea and land; and they were born of women, and they nurtured those who planted the vineyards from which wine comes. And they make the robes of all men, and they bring glory to men; and men cannot be separated from women. If men have gathered gold and silver and every beautiful thing, and then they see a woman fair in appearance and beauty, they leave all these things and gape at her with open mouth, and are drawn to her more than to gold or silver or any precious thing. A man leaves his own father who raised him, and his own country, and cleaves to his wife. And with his wife he lays down his soul, and remembers neither his father nor his mother nor his country. And from this you should know that women rule over you. Do you not grieve? And a man takes his sword and goes out to rob and steal and to sail the sea and rivers; he faces lions and walks in darkness, and when he has stolen and plundered and robbed, he brings it to his beloved. And yet a man loves his wife more than his father or his mother. Many men have lost their minds because of women, and have become slaves because of them; many have perished and stumbled and sinned because of women. And now, do you not believe me that the king is great in his power, seeing that all regions long to touch him? Yet I saw the king's concubine, the daughter of Bartacus, sitting at the right hand of the king, and she took the crown from his head and placed it on herself, and with her left hand she slapped the king in the face. And on top of all this he gazed at her with open mouth, and if she turned away to smile at him:

he smiled back at her; and if she showed anger toward him, he flattered her until she was reconciled to him. O men, why are not women then mighty, seeing that they do such things? Then the king and his nobles looked at one another. And he began to speak of truth. O men, are not women strong? Great is the earth, and high is the heaven, and swift is the sun in its course, for it turns about in the circuit of the heavens and returns to its place in one day. Is not he great who does these things? But truth is great and stronger than all things. All the earth calls upon truth, and heaven blesses it; all works tremble and quake before it, and there is no unrighteousness in it. Wine is unrighteous, the king is unrighteous, women are unrighteous, all the sons of men are unrighteous, all their works are unrighteous, and there is no truth in them; they shall perish in their unrighteousness. But truth endures and is forever strong, and lives and prevails world without end. With her there is no partiality or preference, but she does what is right to all, to the unjust and to the wicked alike, and all men approve of her judgments. And there is no unrighteousness in her judgment; but the strength, the kingdom, the power, and the majesty of all ages is hers. Blessed be the God of truth. And he stopped speaking. And all the people cried out and said: Great is truth and it prevails. Then the king said to him: Ask what you will, beyond what is written, and I will give it to you, for you have been found wiser; and you shall sit next to me and be called my kinsman. Then he said to the king: Remember the vow which you vowed to build Jerusalem, on the day when you received the kingdom, and to send back all the vessels taken from Jerusalem which Cyrus set apart when he destroyed Babylon, and vowed to send them back. And you vowed to build the temple which the Edomites burned when

· Ezra ·

was ruled in Judea by the Chaldeans. And now this is what I ask of the Lord, and what I request: this is the greatness I ask of you, that you fulfill the vow which you vowed to the King of heaven with your own mouth. Then King Darius arose and kissed him, and wrote a letter to all the governors, prefects, and nobles, that they should escort him and those who were going up with him to build Jerusalem. And to all the rulers who were in Syria, Phoenicia, and Lebanon he wrote letters, that they should bring cedar wood from Lebanon to Jerusalem, to build the city with it. And he wrote to all the Jews who were going up from his kingdom to Judea for their freedom, that no official or magistrate or governor should appear at their gates, and that all the regions they had held should be free to them; and the Edomites should give up the strongholds they held in Judea; and for the building of the temple, twenty talents should be given each year until the temple should be rebuilt, for the burnt offerings to be offered daily as they had been commanded; and ten other talents to be given each year; and to all those who came from Babylon to the city, they should be free, both themselves and their children, and all the priests. He also wrote down the quantities and the sacred vestments which were to be given; and to the Levites he prescribed their duties until the day when the Lord's house should be completed and Jerusalem rebuilt; and to all those dwelling in the city he wrote to give them wages and stipends. And he dismissed all the vessels which Cyrus had set apart from Babylon, and everything that Cyrus had commanded to be done, he also commanded to be done and sent to Jerusalem. And when that young man came out, raising his face toward Jerusalem, he blessed the king and said: From you comes victory, and from you comes wisdom and glory. And I am yours. Blessed are you, who have given me wisdom; to you I give thanks, O Lord God of our fathers. And he took the letters and went to Babylon. And he came and announced to his brothers all who were in Babylon, and they blessed the God of their fathers, who had given them relief and refreshment, that they might go up and build Jerusalem and the temple where his name was called upon; and they rejoiced with music and gladness for seven days. (fol. v.)

After these things, heads of families were chosen to go up, according to their tribes and their clans, with their wives and their sons and daughters and their menservants and maidservants and their cattle. And King Darius sent with them a thousand horsemen until they had brought them back to Jerusalem in peace, with music and drums and flutes, and all their fellow countrymen were making merry; and he had them all go up together. These are the names of the men who went up by their districts, by their tribes and the divisions of their rule. The priests: the sons of Phinehas, the sons of Aaron; Jeshua the son of Jozadak; Joachim the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, of the house of David; from the lineage of Perez, of the tribe of Judah; who, in the reign of Darius, built magnificent walls in the first month of Nisan, in the first year of his reign. These are they who came up from Judea from the captivity of the exile: for they had been carried into exile by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to Babylon, and returned to Jerusalem. And each ruled his own city among those who came up with Zerubbabel, and Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mizpar, Bigvai, Rehum, Baanah: these were the leaders; and the number of the men of the people of Israel: the sons of Parosh, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two. And those appointed over the districts came to the temple of the Lord that was in Jerusalem, to renew and restore the temple in its place according to their ability, and to bring into the temple the treasury of sacred things — twelve thousand gold minas and priestly robes. And the priests and the Levites dwelt there, and those who came out from among the people in Jerusalem and in the region, and the singers and the gatekeepers and all Israel in their districts. When the seventh month came, and the children of Israel were each in their own places, the people gathered as one in the court that was before the eastern gate. And Jeshua the son of Jozadak stood up, and his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and his brothers, and they prepared the altar to offer burnt offerings upon it, as it is written in the book of Moses, the man of God. And there came to them from the other nations of the land, and they set up the altar in its place, though all the peoples of the land were against them, and they offered burnt offerings and holocausts to the Lord morning by morning. And they kept the Feast of Tabernacles, and the solemn day as commanded in the law, and sacrifices daily as was required, and after these the appointed offerings, and the sabbaths, and the new moons, and all the solemn feast days of sanctification. And all who made vows to the Lord, from the new moon of the seventh month, began to offer sacrifices to the Lord, though the temple of the Lord was not yet built. And they gave money to the stonecutters and craftsmen, and food and drink with joy. And they gave carts to the Sidonians and Tyrians to bring cedar logs from Lebanon to the port of Joppa, according to the decree written for them by Cyrus king of Persia. In the second year of their coming to the temple of God in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Jeshua the son of Jozadak began, along with their brothers the priests and the Levites and all who had come from captivity to Jerusalem, and they laid the foundation of the temple of God.

In the second month of the second year, when they had come to Judea and Jerusalem. And they appointed the Levites from twenty years of age over the work of the Lord. And Jeshua stood up with his sons and his brothers, all the Levites, breathing together and serving as executors of the law, performing work in the house of the Lord. And the priests stood with their robes and trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, praising the Lord and blessing him according to David king of Israel. And they sang a song to the Lord, for his goodness and his honor are holy above all Israel. And all the trumpets sounded, and they cried out with a great voice, praising the Lord at the raising up of the house of the Lord. And there came priests and Levites and leaders by districts, elders who had seen the former house, and at the founding of this one they wept with great lamentation, while many others blew trumpets with great joy, so that the sound could not be distinguished from the sound of the joyful shouting of the people. For the crowd of trumpeters was making a magnificent sound, so that it could be heard far away. And the enemies of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin heard and came to learn what the sound of the trumpets meant. And they learned that those who had returned from captivity were building a temple to the Lord God of Israel. And they came to Zerubbabel and Jeshua and the leaders of the districts and said to them: We will build with you. For we likewise have sought the Lord your God, and we have offered sacrifices to him since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us here. But Zerubbabel and Jeshua and the leaders of the districts of Israel said to them: It is not for us and you together to build a house to our God. For we alone will build to the Lord God of Israel, according to what Cyrus king of Persia commanded us. Then the peoples of the lands who surrounded Judea, raising up opposition to the building work and laying snares, hindered them from building, and by threats and aggressions prevented them from completing the building throughout the whole lifetime of the king, and impeded the construction.

Ezra

In that same place. And I also commanded that they should build it entirely and prosper, so that they may help those who are of the captivity of the Jews, until the temple of the house of the Lord is completed; and from the tribute of the region of Syria and Phoenicia, the quantity should be given diligently to these men for the sacrifice of the Lord — to Zerubbabel, for bulls and rams and lambs; likewise also wheat and salt and wine and oil, steadily year by year, as the priests who are in Jerusalem have declared to be consumed daily without any delay, so that libations may be offered to the Most High God for the king and his sons, and that they may pray for their lives. And let it be declared that whoever shall transgress any of these things that are written, or shall despise them, a beam shall be taken from their own house and they shall be hanged upon it, and their goods shall be forfeited to the king. Therefore may the Lord, whose name is invoked there, destroy every king and nation that shall stretch out their hand to hinder or to harm the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have decreed this to be done most diligently. Chapter VII.

Then Sisinnes, the governor of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, and Sathrabuzanes, and their companions, following those things which had been decreed by Darius the king, assisted most diligently in the holy works, working together with the elders of the Jews and the leaders of Syria; and the holy works prospered, with Haggai and Zechariah the prophets encouraging them. And they completed everything by the commandment of the Lord God of Israel, and by the counsel of Cyrus and Darius and Artaxerxes, kings of Persia. And the house was finished on the twenty-third day of the month Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of Darius. And the children of Israel — the priests and the Levites and the rest who were of the captivity who had been added — did according to what is written in the book of Moses. And they offered at

the dedication of the temple of the Lord a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; and twelve male goats for the sin of all Israel, according to the number of the tribes of Israel. And the priests and the Levites stood in their divisions for the works of God in Jerusalem, according to the book of Moses; and the doorkeepers at each gate. And the children of Israel who were of the captivity kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, when the priests and Levites were sanctified together. Not all the children of the captivity were sanctified together; but the Levites were all sanctified together. And they slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the children of the captivity, and for their brothers the priests, and for themselves. And the children of Israel who were of the captivity, all those who had separated themselves from the abominations of the nations of the land, seeking the Lord, ate of it, and celebrated the feast of unleavened bread seven days, feasting before the Lord; because the Lord had turned the counsel of the king of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in the works of the Lord God of Israel. And after these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, there came up Ezra son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah, son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub, son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Bukki, son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest. This Ezra came up from Babylon, being a scribe and skilled in the law of Moses which was given by the Lord God of Israel, to teach and to practice it. And the king granted him glory, for he had found favor in all dignity and honor before him. And there came up with him to Jerusalem some of the children of Israel, priests and Levites, sacred singers of the temple, doorkeepers, and servants of the temple. In the seventh year of the reign of Artaxerxes, in the fifth month — this being the seventh year of his reign — those who had gathered from Babylon arrived on the fifth day of the month.

Jerusalem, according to his command, and with the prosperity of the journey given to them by the Lord. For in these things Ezra maintained great discipline, so that he would not omit anything that was in the law of the Lord and his commandments, and by teaching all Israel righteousness and judgment. And those who were scribes of King Artaxerxes came forward and delivered the letter that had come from King Artaxerxes to Ezra the priest and reader of the law of the Lord, a copy of which is given below. Chapter VIII.

King Artaxerxes to Ezra the priest and reader of the law of the Lord, greetings. Being more generous in my beneficences, I have commanded those who desire from the Jewish people of their own free will, and from the priests and Levites who are in my kingdom, to accompany you to Jerusalem. If any therefore wish to go with you, let them gather and depart as it has pleased me and my counselors and friends: to visit those things that are done according to the law in Judea and Jerusalem, observing as you have in the law of the Lord, bringing gifts to the Lord God of Israel, which I and my friends of Jerusalem have vowed. And all the gold and silver that shall be found in the region of Babylon, let it be brought to the Lord in Jerusalem, together with what has been donated for that people in the temple of the Lord which is in Jerusalem: so that this gold and silver may be gathered for bulls and rams, and for lambs and kids, and whatever is fitting with these, that they may offer sacrifices to the Lord upon the altar of the Lord which is in Jerusalem. And whatever you wish to do with your brothers with gold and silver, carry out according to your will and according to the commandment of the Lord your God; and the sacred vessels that have been given to you for the service of the house of the Lord your God which is in Jerusalem, and whatever else shall occur to you for the service of the temple of your God, you shall give from the royal treasury.

When you wish to do with your brothers with gold and silver, carry it out according to the will of the Lord. And I, King Artaxerxes, have commanded the keepers of the treasuries of Syria and Phoenicia: that whatever Ezra the priest and reader of the law of the Lord shall write, it shall be diligently given to him up to one hundred talents of silver, and likewise of gold, and up to one hundred measures of wheat, and one hundred jars of wine, and other things in abundance without limit. Let all things be done according to the law of the Most High God, lest perhaps wrath arise in the kingdom of the king and his sons. And to you it is said: that upon all the priests and Levites and sacred singers and temple servants and scribes of the temple, no tribute or any other imposition shall be laid, nor shall anyone have power to impose anything upon them. And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of God, appoint judges and arbiters throughout all Syria and Phoenicia, and let all those who do not know the law of your God be taught; and as many as have transgressed the law, let them be diligently punished: whether by death, or by torture, or by monetary fine, or by exile. And Ezra the scribe said: Blessed is the Lord God of our fathers, who has put this will into the heart of the king to glorify his house which is in Jerusalem, and has honored me in the sight of the king and his counselors and friends and all his nobles. And I, being of firm mind, gathered the men of Israel to ascend with me. And these are set down according to their families and their leading men, those who came up with me from Babylon in the reign of Artaxerxes. Of the sons of Phares: Gershon. Of the sons of Shemaiah: Amen. Of the sons of David: Acus the son of Fredie. Of the sons of Phares: and Zacharias, and with him were reckoned one hundred and fifty men.

· Ezra ·

Of the sons of the leader of Moab, Zara-et: with him two hundred and fifty men. Of the sons of Zaccai, Jechonias Zccheli: with him two hundred and fifty men. Of the sons of Sala, Maastas Gotholias: with him seventy men. Of the sons of Saphania, Zarias Nichelei: with him eighty men. Of the sons of Job, Abdias Jeheli: with him two hundred and twelve men. Of the sons of Bani, Salimoth son of Josaphia: with him a hundred and sixty men. Of the sons of Beer, Zacharias Beber: with him two hundred and eight men. Of the sons of Ezrad, Johannes Arechan: with him a hundred and ten men. Of the sons of Adonicham, the last: and these were the names of them, Eliaphalam son of Gebel and Semeias: with him seventy men. And I gathered them to the river called Thia and Mechan: there we stayed three days and I reviewed them. And of the sons of the priests and Levites I found none there. And I sent to Eleazar and Eccolom and Masiuan and Maloban and Enathan and Samea and Ioribu, Nathan, Enuagan, Zacharianu and Mosollamum: these as leaders and guides. And I told them to go to Luddeus who was near the treasury. And I instructed them to tell Luddeus and his brothers and those who were in the treasury: to send us those who would serve as priests in the house of the Lord our God. And they brought to us, by the mighty hand of the Lord our God, men of the sons of Mooli, son of Levi, son of Israel — Sebedian and his sons and brothers who were eighteen — Albiam and Amin — of the sons of the Chanaanites and their sons, twenty men. And of those who served in the temple, whom David and the princes had appointed for the service of the Levites in the temple — two hundred and ninety. All these names are recorded in the scriptures. And I proclaimed a fast there in the sight of the Lord: that we might seek from him a safe journey for us and for those with us, and for our children and our cattle, against dangers. For I was ashamed to ask the king for foot soldiers and horsemen as an escort for protection against our enemies. For we had told the king: the power of the Lord will be with those who seek him with all their heart. And so we fasted and prayed to our Lord God for this purpose: and we obtained what we sought from our God. And I set apart twelve of the leading men of the priests and of the temple: Sededian and Asaman and with them ten of their brothers. And I weighed out for them silver and gold and the sacred vessels of the house of our God: which the king and his counselors and princes and all Israel had donated. And when I had weighed it out, I delivered silver of a hundred and fifty talents and a hundred silver vessels of a talent each and a hundred talents of gold: and twenty golden bowls and twelve magnificent vessels of fine polished bronze, gleaming like gold. And I said to them: You are holy to the Lord, and the vessels are holy, and the gold and silver are a votive offering to the Lord God of our fathers. Watch and keep them until you deliver them to the chief priests and Levites and the heads of the families of Israel in Jerusalem: in the treasury of the house of our God. And the priests and Levites received the gold and silver and vessels and brought them to Jerusalem into the temple of the Lord. And we set out from the river on the twelfth day of the first month: and we arrived in Jerusalem. And when the third day had come: on the fourth day the gold and silver were weighed out in the house of the Lord our God — to Marimoth son of Jori the priest: and with him was Eleazar son of Phinees, and with them were Josadus son of Jesu and Mediaserbanu son of the Levite: by number and

And all was weighed at the same time. Those who came back from captivity offered a sacrifice to the Lord of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-two lambs, twelve male goats as a sin offering, and twelve cows for a peace offering — all as a sacrifice to the Lord. They read out the decrees of the royal king to the satraps and the governors of Coelesyria and Phoenicia, and they honored the people and the temple of the Lord. When all these things were accomplished, those appointed to me came and said: The people of Israel, the princes, the priests, and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands, nor from the uncleanness of the Gentiles — the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Edomites. For they have taken their daughters for themselves and for their sons, and the holy seed has been mixed with the alien peoples of the land, and the leaders and officials have been foremost in this transgression from the very beginning of the reign. And as soon as I heard this, I tore my garments and my sacred robe, and pulled out the hair from my head and my beard, and sat down in grief and mourning. And all who were moved by the word of the Lord God of Israel gathered to me on account of this transgression, and I sat in sadness until the evening sacrifice. Then I rose from my fasting, with my garments and sacred robe still torn, and knelt down and stretched out my hands to the Lord, saying: O Lord, I am ashamed and confounded before your face. For our sins have multiplied above our heads, and our iniquities have piled up to heaven, since the days of our fathers even to this day. And because of our sins and those of our fathers, we have been handed over, along with our brothers and our priests, to the kings of the earth, to the sword, to captivity, and to plundering with confusion, even to this day. And now, O Lord our God, how much mercy has reached us through you — to leave us a root and a name in the place of your sanctuary, to uncover our light in the house of the Lord our God, to give us food in all the time of our servitude. Even while we were serving, we were not forsaken by the Lord our God, but he showed us favor, granting us grace before the kings of Persia to give us food, and to glorify the temple of the Lord our God, and to rebuild the desolate places of Zion, and to give us a firm standing in Judea and Jerusalem. And now, Lord, what shall we say, having these things? For we have transgressed your commandments, which you gave by your servants the prophets, saying: The land which you enter to possess as an inheritance is a land polluted by the uncleanness of the peoples of the land, and they have filled it with their impurity from one end to the other. Now therefore do not give your daughters to their sons, nor take their daughters for your sons, and do not seek to make peace with them at any time, so that you may be strong and eat the good of the land and leave it as an inheritance to your children forever. And all that has come upon us is because of our evil deeds and our great sins. For you gave us such a root, and yet we have turned again to transgress your laws, to mingle ourselves with the uncleanness of the peoples of these lands. Were you not angry with us to destroy us, until there should be no root or name left for us? O Lord God of Israel, you are truthful. For a root remains even to this day. Behold, we are now before you in our iniquities. For because of these things we can no longer stand before you. And while worshipping —

Ezra

Ezra wept and prostrated himself before the temple, and gathered before him from Jerusalem a great crowd of men and women, young men and young women. The weeping was great throughout the whole assembly. And Shechaniah son of Jehiel, of the sons of Israel, said to Ezra: We have sinned against the Lord in that we have taken foreign wives from the peoples of the land. Yet even now there is hope for Israel. Therefore let us make a covenant with our God to put away all these wives and their children, according to the counsel of the Lord and of those who tremble at the commandment of our God. Let it be done according to the law. Rise up, for it is your responsibility, and we are with you. Be strong and act. Then Ezra rose and made the leading priests and Levites and all Israel swear to do according to this word. Chapter 9.

Then Ezra rose from before the house of God and went into the chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib, and lodged there. He ate no bread and drank no water, for he mourned over the faithlessness of the exiles. And a proclamation was made throughout Judah and Jerusalem to all the returned exiles to assemble in Jerusalem, and that whoever did not come within two or three days, by the decision of the officials and elders all his property would be forfeited and he himself would be excluded from the congregation of the exiles. Then all the men of Judah and Benjamin assembled at Jerusalem within the three days. This was the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month. All the people sat in the open square before the house of God, trembling because of this matter and because of the heavy rain. Then Ezra the priest stood up and said to them: You have broken faith and taken foreign wives, adding to the guilt of Israel. Now then make confession to the Lord God of your fathers.

And the whole assembly answered with a loud voice: It is so! We must do as you say. But the people are many, and it is a time of heavy rain; we cannot stand in the open. Nor is this a work of one or two days, for we have greatly transgressed in this matter. Let our officials stand for the whole assembly, and let all in our cities who have taken foreign wives come at appointed times, with the elders and judges of each city, until the fierce wrath of our God over this matter is turned from us. Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah opposed this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite supported them. Then the returned exiles did so. Ezra the priest selected men who were heads of fathers' houses, according to their houses, every one of them designated by name. On the first day of the tenth month they sat down to examine the matter; and by the first day of the first month they had come to the end of all the men who had married foreign women. And among the sons of the priests who had married foreign women were found: of the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers: Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah, and they pledged themselves to put away their wives, and their guilt offering was a ram of the flock for their guilt. Of the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah. Of the sons of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah. Of the sons of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah. Of the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah, Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer. Of the singers: [continues]

And all the people gathered together as one in the square that is before the eastern gate of the sacred city. And he read it in the square before the sacred gate from first light until

evening, before the men and women. And all the people gave their attention to the law. And Ezra the priest and reader of the law stood upon a wooden platform which had been made for that purpose. And standing beside him were Mathathias, Samuel, Ananias, Azarias, Urias, Ezechias, and Balsamus on his right hand, and on his left Saldeus, Misael, Malachias, Abusthas, Sabusnabadias, and Zacharias. And Ezra took up the book before all the people, for he presided in glory in the sight of them all. And when he had finished reading the law, all rose up, and Ezra blessed the Lord God most high, the God of Sabaoth, the Almighty. And all the people answered, Amen. And lifting up their hands, they fell to the ground and worshipped the Lord. And Jeshua, Bannus, Sarabias, Jadinus, Acubs, Sabbatheus, Calithes, Azarias, Toradus, Ananias, and the sons of the Levites, who were teaching the law of the Lord, and reading the law of the Lord throughout the multitude, and explaining to each one those who understood the reading. And he said to the chiefs, to Ezra the priest and reader, and to the Levites who were teaching the multitude, saying: This day is holy to the Lord. And all the people wept when they heard the law. Go now and eat of the richest foods and drink of the sweetest drinks, and send portions to those who have nothing. For this day is holy to the Lord, and do not be sorrowful. For the Lord will glorify you. And the Levites proclaimed to all the people in public, saying: This day is holy. Do not be sorrowful. And all the people went to eat and drink and to make merry, and to send gifts to those who had nothing, so that they might celebrate. For they were greatly uplifted by the words with which they had been instructed. And all assembled in Jerusalem to celebrate with joy, according to the covenant of the Lord God of Israel.
Here ends the third book of Ezra.

Chapter One.
Esdras the prophet, second son of Sarei, son of Azarci, son of Elchi, son of Sadanias, son of Sadoch, son of Achitob, son of Archias, son of Phinees, son of Heli, son of Ameas, son of Ahrei, son of Marimoch, son of Aznas, son of Ozias, son of Borieth, son of Abissel, son of Phinees, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, of the tribe of Levi: who was a captive in the land of the Medes, in the reign of King Artaxerxes. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Go and declare to my people their crimes, and to their children the iniquities which they have committed against me; so that the children may declare to the children of their parents that their sins have multiplied. For they have forgotten me and sacrificed to foreign gods. Did I not bring you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery? But they provoked me and despised my counsels. Cut off the hair of your head and cast all evils upon them, because they have not obeyed my law. The people are undisciplined. How long shall I endure them, upon whom I have bestowed such great benefits? I overthrew many kings for their sake; I struck down Pharaoh with his servants and all his army. I destroyed all nations before them; in the east I scattered the two cities of Tyre and Sidon; I killed all their enemies. Speak to them therefore, saying: Thus says the Lord. I indeed led you through the sea and made safe roads for you. I gave you Moses and Aaron as leaders and priests; I gave you light through a pillar of fire, and I performed great wonders for you. Yet you have forgotten me, says the Lord. Thus says the Lord Almighty. I provided for you a pillar in the wood; I gave you camps as a refuge, and there you murmured;

and you did not triumph in my name over the defeat of your enemies, but even now you continue to murmur. Where are the benefits that I gave you? Was it not in the desert when you cried out to me in hunger, saying: Why have you brought us into this desert to kill us? It would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in this desert. I pitied your groaning and gave you manna for food. You ate the bread of angels. Did I not split the rock when you were thirsty, and water flowed in abundance? Because of the heat I covered you with the leaves of trees. I divided fertile lands among you; I drove out the Canaanites, the Perizzites, and the Philistines before you. What more shall I do for you, says the Lord? Thus says the Lord Almighty. When you were in the desert, by the river of the Amorites, thirsty and blaspheming my name, I did not punish you with fire for your blasphemies; instead I threw a piece of wood into the water and made the stream sweet. What shall I do with you, O Jacob? You of Judah would not obey. I will turn to other nations and give them my name so that they may keep my statutes. Because you have forsaken me, I also will forsake you. When you beg me for mercy, I will have no mercy; when you call upon me, I will not hear you. For you have defiled your hands with blood, and your feet are swift to commit murder. It is not as though you have forsaken me, says the Lord; you have forsaken yourselves. Thus says the Lord Almighty. Did I not entreat you as a father does his sons, and as a mother her daughters, and as a nurse her little children, so that you would be my people and I would be your God? I gathered you as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings. But now what shall I do with you? I will cast you away from my face. When you bring me offerings, I will turn my face away from you.

. Esdras .

from you. For I have rejected your feast days and new moons and circumcisions. I sent my servants the prophets to you, whom you received and killed, and tore apart their bodies, whose blood I will require, says the Lord. Thus says the Lord Almighty: Your house is desolate. I will cast you out like dry stubble, and your children will not make petition, because they have neglected my commandment and have done what is evil before me. I will deliver your houses to a people that is coming, who will believe without having heard me, to whom I showed no signs; they will do what I commanded. The prophets they did not see, yet they will call to mind their iniquities. I call to witness the grace of the people that is coming, whose children rejoice with gladness, though they see me not with fleshly eyes, yet believe in spirit what I have said. And now, brother, behold the glory and see the people coming from the east, to whom I will give as leaders Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and Hosea, and Amos, and Micah, and Joel, and Obadiah, and Jonah, and Nahum, and Habakkuk, Zephaniah, Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi, who are also called the angel of the Lord.

And the Lord says: I called — [chapter 2] — I led this people out of bondage, to whom I gave commandments through my servants the prophets, whom they refused to hear, but made my ordinances void. The mother who bore them says to them: Go, my children, for I am a widow and forsaken. I would have brought you up with gladness, but I lost you with mourning and sorrow, because you sinned before the Lord your God, and did what was evil in my sight. Now what shall I do for you? I am a widow and forsaken. Go, my children, and ask mercy of the Lord. I call upon the Father as witness over those children who refused to keep my covenant, so that you may bring them to confusion and their mother to plunder, that their offspring may cease. Let them be scattered among the nations, let them be blotted from the earth, for they have despised my covenant.

Woe to you, Assyria, who hide the unrighteous among you. O God, remember what you did to Sodom and Gomorrah, whose land lies in clods of pitch and heaps of ashes. So will I do to those who have not heard me, says the Lord Almighty.

Thus says the Lord to Ezra: Declare to my people that I will give them the kingdom of Jerusalem, which I was going to give to Israel. And I will take to myself their glory, and give them the everlasting tabernacles which I had prepared for them. The tree of life shall be for them as a fragrant ointment; they shall neither labor nor be weary. Go and receive it. Pray for yourselves that your days may be few, that they may be shortened. The kingdom is already prepared for you. Watch. Call heaven and earth to witness: I put away evil and created good, for I live, says the Lord. Mother, embrace your children, bring them up with gladness, as a dove confirms her feet — for I have chosen you, says the Lord. And I will raise the dead from their places, and bring them out from their tombs, for I have recognized my name in Israel. Fear not, mother of children, for I have chosen you, says the Lord. I will send to your aid my servants Isaiah and Jeremiah, at whose word I have sanctified and prepared for you twelve trees laden with various fruits, and as many springs flowing with milk and honey, and seven mighty mountains on which roses and lilies grow: with these I will fill your children with joy.

Do justice to the widow, judge for the orphan, give to the needy, defend the fatherless, clothe the naked, care for the broken and the weak, do not mock the lame, watch over the maimed, and admit to the sight of my glory those who are blind. Keep the aged and the young within your walls; where you find the dead, commit them to the grave with a sign, and I will give you the first place in my resurrection.

Rest and be still, my people, for your rest shall come. Nurse —
