Nourish your sons well, strengthen their feet. Of the servants I gave you, none shall perish. For I will require them by your number. Do not grow weary. For when the days of pressure and anguish come, others will weep and be sorrowful, but you shall be joyful and abundant. The nations will be zealous, yet nothing will prevail against you, says the Lord. My hands will guide you, so that your sons will not see hell. Rejoice, mother, with your children, for I will exalt you, says the Lord. Remember your sleeping sons, for I will lead them out from the ends of the earth, and I will show them mercy, for I am merciful, says the Lord Almighty. Embrace your children until I come and proclaim mercy to them, for my springs overflow and my grace shall not fail. I, Ezra, received a commission from the Lord on Mount Horeb, to go to Israel. But when I came to them, they rejected me and refused the commandment of the Lord. Therefore I say to you, O nations: hear and understand. Await your shepherd; he will give you the rest of eternal life, for he who is to come at the end of the age is near. Be ready for the rewards of the kingdom, for eternal light will shine upon you forever. Flee the shadow of this age. Receive the joy of your glory. I solemnly declare to you the Savior: accept him who is commended to the Lord and rejoice; give thanks to him who has called you to the heavenly kingdom. Rise and stand, and see the number of those who are sealed at the feast of the Lord. Those who have passed from the shadow of this world have received splendid robes from the Lord. Receive, O Zion, your number, and close the roll of your elect who have fulfilled the law of the Lord. The number of your sons whom you desired is complete. Pray to the sovereignty of the Lord that he may sanctify your people who have been called from the beginning. I, Ezra, saw on Mount Zion a great multitude which I could not number, and they all praised the Lord with songs. And in their midst was a young man of great stature, taller than all the rest, and he placed crowns on each of their heads, and was exalted higher. I was held in wonder. Then I asked the angel and said: Who are these, O Lord? He answered and said to me: These are they who have put off the mortal garment and have put on the immortal, and they have confessed the name of God. Now they are crowned and receive palms. I said to the angel: Who is that young man who places crowns on them and puts palms in their hands? He answered and said to me: He is the Son of God, whom they confessed in the world. Then I began to glorify those who had stood bravely for the name of the Lord. Then the angel said to me: Go, declare to my people what wonders you have seen of the Lord God. Chapter III.

In the thirtieth year after the ruin of the city, I was in Babylon, and I lay troubled upon my bed. And my thoughts rose up in my heart, for I had seen the desolation of Zion and the abundance of those who lived in Babylon. And my spirit was greatly troubled. And I began to speak to the Most High words full of fear. And I said: O Lord and Master, did you not speak from the beginning when you planted the earth — and that alone — and commanded the dust, and gave Adam a dead body? Yet even then it was the work of your hands, and you breathed into him the breath of life, and he was made alive before you, and you led him into the paradise which your right hand had planted before the earth appeared. And you commanded him to love your way, but he transgressed it, and immediately you appointed death for him and for his descendants; and from him were born nations, tribes, peoples, and clans without number. And he walked

· Esdras ·

Every nation went about in its own will, and they did wondrous things before you, and despised your commandments. And again, in due time, you brought the flood upon those inhabiting the world, and you destroyed them. And it came to pass that death came upon each of them as it came upon Adam, so the flood came upon these. Yet you left one of them, Noah, with his household, and from him came all the righteous. And it came to pass, when those who dwelt upon the earth began to multiply, they multiplied sons and peoples and many nations, and they began again to be more ungodly than those before them. And it came to pass, when they committed iniquity before you, you chose for yourself one from among them, whose name was Abraham. And you loved him, and to him alone you showed your will. And you made with him an everlasting covenant, and promised him that you would never forsake his seed. And you gave him Isaac, and to Isaac you gave Jacob and Esau. And you set apart Jacob for yourself, but Esau you put aside. And Jacob became a great multitude. And it came to pass, when you led his seed out of Egypt, you brought them to Mount Sinai. And you bowed the heavens and shook the earth, and moved the whole world, and made the depths tremble, and troubled the age, and your glory passed through the four gates of fire and earthquake and wind and cold, that you might give the law to the seed of Jacob and the commandment to the generation of Israel. Yet you did not take away from them their evil heart, so that your law might bring forth fruit in them. For the first Adam, bearing an evil heart, transgressed and was overcome, and so too all who were born of him. And the weakness remained, and the law was in the heart of the people together with the evil root, and what was good departed, and the evil remained. And the times passed and the years came to an end, and you raised up for yourself a servant named David, and you said to him to build a city for your name and to offer there incense and oblations.

And it came to pass for many years: those who dwelt in the city sinned in all things, doing as Adam and all his generations had done. For they also walked with an evil heart. And you delivered your city into the hands of your enemies. Then I said: Are those who dwell in Babylon doing better? And for this reason will you punish Zion? When I came here and saw the iniquities that are without number, and many transgressors, my soul was troubled in this thirtieth year, and my heart failed me, for I saw how you endure those who sin and spare those who act wickedly, and you have destroyed your own people and preserved your enemies, and you gave no sign. I cannot remember how this way is to be forsaken. Does Babylon do better than Zion? Or has any other nation known you, besides Israel? Or what tribes have believed your covenants as Jacob has? Yet their reward has not appeared, nor has their labor borne fruit. For I have passed among the nations and seen them in abundance, though they are unmindful of your commandments. Weigh now our iniquities and those of the inhabitants of the world in the balance, and no name shall be found but Israel's. Or when have those who inhabit the earth not sinned in your sight? Or what nation has so observed your commandments? You will find individuals among us who have kept your commandments, but among the nations you will find none. Chapter four.

And the angel who was sent to me, whose name was Uriel, answered and said to me: Your understanding has greatly exceeded the understanding of this age, and you think to comprehend the way of the Most High. And I said: Yes, my lord. And he answered me and said: I have been sent to show you three ways and to set before you three comparisons, of which, if you can explain one of them to me,

· Fifth ·

these things: and I will show you the way you desire to see, and I will teach you from where comes the evil heart. And I said: Speak, my Lord. And he said to me: Go, weigh for me the heaviness of fire, or measure for me a blast of wind, or call back for me the day that has passed. And I answered and said: Who among those born could do this, that you ask me concerning these things? And he said to me: If I were to ask you saying: how many dwellings are in the heart of the sea, or how many springs are at the beginning of the deep, or how many passages are above the firmament, or which are the exits of paradise — you would perhaps say to me: I have not descended into the deep, nor have I yet gone down into hell, nor have I ever ascended into heaven. But now I have only asked you about fire and wind and the day through which you have passed, and from which you cannot be separated: and you have not answered me concerning them. And he said to me: You cannot understand the things that are your own, which have grown up with you. And how then can your vessel comprehend the way of the Most High, and in a world already outwardly corrupted understand the corruption manifest in my sight? And I said to him: It would have been better for us not to exist at all, than to live in impiety and to suffer, and not to understand for what reason. And he answered me and said: I went out into a forest of trees of the field, and they took counsel among themselves and said: Come, let us go and make war against the sea, that it may retreat before us, and we may make for ourselves other forests. And likewise the waves of the sea also took counsel and said: Come, let us go up and subdue the forests even of the plain, that there also we may make for ourselves another territory. But the plan of the forest came to nothing, for fire came and consumed it. Likewise the plan of the waves of the sea: for the sand stood firm and stopped them. If you were a judge between them,

whom would you begin to justify, or whom to condemn? And I answered and said: Truly both have taken a vain thought. For the earth is given to the forest, and to the sea is appointed a place to carry its floods. And he answered me and said: You have judged rightly. But why have you not judged so in your own case? For just as the earth is given to the forest, and the sea to its waves: so also those who dwell upon the earth can only understand the things of the earth, and those above the heavens the things of the height of the heavens. And I answered and said: I beseech you, O Lord, give me understanding. For I did not wish to ask about the things above you, but about those things which pass through us every day: why Israel has been given as a reproach to the nations whom you loved; why the people you loved has been given to godless tribes; and the law of our fathers is brought to destruction; and the written statutes are nowhere to be found; and we have passed away from the world like locusts, and our life is astonishment and fear: and we are not worthy to obtain mercy. But what will he do for his name which is called upon us? It is about these things that I have asked. And he answered me and said: If you search diligently you shall often marvel. For the world hastens to pass away, and cannot contain what has been promised in the future times to the righteous, because this world is full of injustice and infirmities. But concerning what you ask me, I will tell you. The evil has been sown, but its destruction has not yet come. If therefore that which has been sown is not turned back, and if the place where the evil was sown does not pass away: the good shall not come where it was sown. For a grain of evil seed was sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness it has produced until now, and shall produce until the threshing floor comes. Consider therefore in yourself how great a grain of evil

. Esdras .

of the seed, as much as the field of wickedness has produced: when it will have been time to sow, the ears of grain of which there is no number will begin to make a great field. And I answered and said: How long, and when will these things happen? Why are our years so few and evil? And he answered me and said: Do not hurry to be above the Most High. For you hurry in vain to be above him. For your excess is great. Have not the souls of the righteous asked about these things in their chambers, saying: How long are we to remain here? And when will the fruit of the threshing floor of our reward come? And Jeremiel the archangel answered them and said: When the number of seeds is completed in you, for he who weighed the age in the balance and measured the times by measure, and numbered the times by number, shall not move nor stir until that said measure is fulfilled. And I answered and said: O Lord and Master, yet we all are also full of ungodliness. And lest perhaps for our sake the floor of the righteous should not be filled, because of the sins of those who dwell on earth. And he answered me and said: Go ask a woman who is with child, when she has completed her nine months, whether her womb can still hold the birth within her. And I said: It cannot, Lord. And he said to me: In the underworld, the chambers of souls are like the womb. For just as a woman in travail makes haste to escape the necessity of the birth, so also these places hasten to return those things that were committed to them. From the beginning the things you desire to see shall be shown to you. And I answered and said: If I have found favor in your sight, and if it is possible, and if I am sufficient, show me whether there is more to come than has passed, or whether more has passed than is to come. What is past I know, but what is future I do not know. And he said to me: Stand on the right side, and I shall show you

the interpretation of a likeness. And I stood and watched, and behold, a burning furnace passed before me. And it came to pass when the flame had gone by, I looked, and behold, there remained only the smoke. After this a cloud full of water passed before me, and poured down a heavy and violent rain; and when the violent rainstorm had passed, the drops remained therein. And he said to me: Consider this for yourself. As the rain is more than the drops, and as the fire is more than the smoke, so the measure that passed was greater. But the drops and the smoke remained. And I prayed and said: Do you think that I shall live until those days? And who will be alive in those days? He answered me and said: Concerning the signs about which you ask me, I can tell you in part; but as for your life, I was not sent to tell you, and furthermore I do not know. Chapter 5.

But concerning the signs: Behold, the days will come when those who dwell on earth shall be seized with great panic, and the way of truth shall be hidden, and the land shall be barren of faith, and iniquity shall be increased beyond what you yourself see, and beyond what you have heard of formerly. And the land that you now see ruling shall become a desolate wasteland. But if the Most High grants you to live, you will see after the third trumpet: the sun shall suddenly shine at night, and the moon shall appear three times in a day; and blood shall drip from wood, and the stone shall utter its voice; the peoples shall be troubled, and a ruler shall reign whom those on earth do not expect; the birds shall migrate together; and the sea of Sodom shall cast up fish; and it shall make a sound in the night which many have not known, and all shall hear its voice. There shall be chaos in many places, and fire shall break out frequently, and wild beasts shall roam abroad; women shall give birth to monsters; and in the sweet waters salt shall be found; and friends shall attack one another;

and then sense and understanding will be hidden away and stored in its treasury, and it will be sought by many and not found; and injustice and lack of restraint will increase upon the earth. And the neighboring region will ask its own: "Did justice ever justify the just?" And it will deny it. And it will be in that time: people will hope, yet not be governed; they will labor, yet their ways will not be directed. These are the signs I am permitted to tell you. And if you pray again and weep as you do now, and fast for seven days, you will hear still greater things than these. And I awoke, and my body shuddered greatly, and my soul labored to the point of failing. But the angel who had spoken in me came and strengthened me and set me on my feet. And it came to pass on the second night: Salathiel, the leader of the people, came to me and said: Where were you? And why is your face so sad? Or do you not know that Israel has been entrusted to you in the region of their captivity? Rise then and eat bread, and do not forsake us as a shepherd forsakes his flock in the hands of wicked wolves. And I said to him: Go away from me and do not come near me. And he heard what I said and departed from me. And I fasted seven days, wailing and weeping, as the angel Uriel had commanded me. And it came to pass after seven days: the thoughts of my heart again greatly troubled me. And my soul recovered its spiritual understanding, and I began again to speak words before the Most High. And I said: O Lord and Master, of all the forests of the earth and all their trees, you chose for yourself one vine; and of all the lands of the world, you chose for yourself one region; and of all the flowers of the world, you chose for yourself one lily; and of all the depths of the sea, you filled for yourself one river; and of all the cities that have been built, you sanctified Zion for yourself; and of all the birds that were created, you named for yourself one dove; and of all the flocks that were made, you provided for yourself one sheep; and of all the multitude of peoples, you acquired for yourself one people; and to this one, whom you have loved, you gave the Law proven above all others. And now, O Lord, why did you hand over the one to the many? And you prepared one root above the others, and you scattered your only one among the many. And those who opposed your promises trampled him down, because they did not believe your covenants. And if you truly hate your people, they should be punished by your own hands. When I had finished speaking, the angel who had come to me on the previous night was sent to me, and he said to me: Listen to me and I will instruct you; pay attention to me and I will tell you more. And I said: Speak, my Lord. And he said to me: You are greatly distraught in mind over Israel. Do you love him more than his Maker does? And I said to him: No, my Lord; but I spoke out of grief. My thoughts torment me every hour as I seek to comprehend the path of the Most High and to search out part of his judgment. And he said to me: You cannot. And I said: Why, O Lord? For what purpose was I born, or why was my mother's womb not my tomb, so that I would not have seen the travail of Jacob and the exhaustion of the people of Israel? And he said to me: Count for me those who have not yet come, and gather for me the scattered flowers; and open for me the closed storehouses; and bring forth for me the winds shut up in them. Show me the image of a voice; and then I will show you the labor that you ask to see. And I said: O Lord and Master, who is there that is able to

· Esdras ·

These things no one can know except one who does not dwell among men. But I am foolish — how then shall I be able to speak of the things you have asked me? And he said to me: Just as you cannot accomplish one of the things that have been said, so neither will you be able to find the judgment I have promised, or the end of the mercy I have promised to the people. And I said: But behold, Lord — you who are here for those who are at the end — what shall those do who came before me? Or we ourselves, or those who come after us? And he said to me: I will liken my judgment to a crown: just as lateness does not overtake the last, so neither does swiftness overtake the first. And I answered and said: Could you not have made those who were made, and those who are yet to be, all at once, so that you might show your judgment more swiftly? And he answered me and said: The creature cannot hasten beyond the Creator, nor can the world sustain at once those who are yet to be created in it. And I said: How did you say to your servant that you, giving life, gave life to the creature you made, all at once, and the creature sustained it — it was able — and now it cannot contain those presently living all at once? And he said to me: Ask the womb of a woman, and say to her: If you give birth, why only in time? Ask her then to produce ten at once. And I said: She cannot do so, but only according to her time. And he said to me: Even so have I given the womb of the earth to those who are sown upon it, each in their time. For just as an infant does not bring forth what has been sown, so I have ordered the age I created. And I asked and said: Since you have now shown me the way, I will speak before you. For our mother, of whom you spoke to me — she is still young; let her now approach old age. And he answered me and said: Ask her who gives birth, and she will tell you. Say to her: Why are those you have borne now not like those born before — smaller in stature? And she will say to you: Those born in the vigor of youth are one kind, and those born when the womb fails in old age are another. Consider therefore, you also, that you are of smaller stature than those who came before you, and those after you will be smaller still — as creatures already aging, passing beyond the strength of youth. And I said: I pray, Lord, if I have found favor in your sight, show your servant through whom you will visit your creation. Chapter 6.

And he said to me: In the beginning of the earth, before the boundaries of the age were established, and before the winds blew in their courses, and before the voices of thunder sounded, and before the flashes of lightning shone, and before the foundations of paradise were laid, and before the beautiful flowers were seen, and before the powers were established, and before the innumerable hosts of the angels were gathered, and before the heights of the air were raised up, and before the measures of the firmament were named, and before the fires burned in Zion, and before the full years were reckoned, and before those who now sin were separated, and before those who stored up faith were marked — I thought upon all these things, and they were made through me alone and through no other; through me and not through another. And I answered and said: What will be the separation of the times? Or when will the end of the first age come, and the beginning of the next? And he said to me: From Abraham to Isaac, when they were born — from Jacob and Esau — the hand of Jacob held the heel of Esau from the beginning. The end of this age is Esau, and the beginning of the next is Jacob. The hand of man is between the heel and the hand. Seek nothing else beyond this. And I answered and said: O Lord Creator, if I have found favor in your sight, I pray that you show your servant the signs of the end.

which parts you showed me going before at night. And he answered and said to me: Rise upon your feet and hear a most full sound of voice. And it shall be as a movement: and the place upon which you stand shall not be moved. Therefore when it speaks, do not be afraid: because the word concerns the end and the foundations of the earth; at which speech the earth trembles and is moved. For it says that its end must needs be changed. And it came to pass when I had heard, I rose upon my feet and hearkened; and behold a voice spoke, and the sound thereof was like the sound of many waters. And it said: Behold, the days come, and it shall be when the time draws nigh that those who dwell on earth shall be visited: and when the hour comes that those who have done injustice shall be punished, and when the humiliation of Zion shall be fulfilled, and when the world that is to pass away shall be sealed, then I will show these signs: The books shall be opened before the face of the firmament, and all shall see together; and children of a year old shall speak with their voices; and pregnant women shall bring forth untimely children of three and four months, and these shall live and leap. And suddenly shall the sown places appear unsown, and the full storehouses shall suddenly be found empty; and the trumpet shall sound, and when all hear it suddenly they shall be terrified. And it shall come to pass at that time that friends shall make war upon friends as enemies, and the earth shall be afraid with its inhabitants. And the springs of fountains shall stand still, and for the space of three hours they shall not flow. And whosoever remains of all those things I have foretold to you shall be saved, and shall see my salvation and the end of your world. And those who have received it shall see those men who were taken up, who from their birth have not tasted death; and the heart of the inhabitants shall be changed, and turned into a different spirit. For evil shall be blotted out and deceit shall be extinguished. But faith shall flourish and corruption shall be overcome; and truth shall be revealed, which has been without fruit for so many years. And it came to pass when he spoke with me, behold I looked little by little upon him as he gazed upon me, and he said to me these things: Come here, I will show you the nights that are to come. If therefore you shall ask again, and shall fast again seven days, I will tell you greater things than these by day, such as I have heard. For your voice has been heard before the Most High; for the Mighty One has seen your right way, and also the purity which you have had from your youth: and therefore he has sent me to show you all these things, and to say to you: Be confident and fear not, and do not hasten to think vain things in the former times, that you may not hasten in the last times. And it came to pass after this I wept again, and fasted seven days in like manner, that I might fulfill the three weeks which had been told me. And on the eighth night my heart was troubled within me again, and I began to speak before the Most High. For my spirit was greatly set on fire and my soul was in distress, and I said: O Lord, you did speak from the beginning of creation, even on the first day, saying: Let the heaven and earth be made; and your word was a perfect work. And then was the spirit, and darkness and silence were on every side; the sound of man's voice was not yet from you. Then you commanded that a ray of light should be brought forth from your treasures, that your works might then appear. Upon the second day you made the spirit of the firmament, and commanded it to part asunder and to make a division between the waters, that one part might go upward and the other remain beneath. And on the third day you commanded the waters to be gathered together in the seventh part of the earth; six parts you dried up and kept them to the end, that of these some might be planted by God and tilled. For your word went forth and at once the work was done; and it happened suddenly.

· Esdras ·

The fruit of industry is immense, and the pleasure of desire takes many forms; there are flowers of unchanging color, and fragrances of scent beyond investigation. And on the third day these things were made. But on the fourth day you commanded the splendor of the sun to come into being, the light of the moon, and the arrangement of the stars; and you commanded them to serve the human being yet to be formed. On the fifth day you commanded the seventh part, where the waters were gathered, to bring forth living creatures, and birds and fish; and so it came to pass. The water, mute and without soul, produced living creatures at God's nod, so that the nations might recount your wonders. And then you kept two living beings: you called the name of the first Enoch, and the name of the second Leviathan, and you separated them from one another. For the seventh part, where the waters were gathered, could not contain them both. And to Enoch you gave one part, which was dried up on the third day, so that it might be inhabited; where there are a thousand mountains. But to Leviathan you gave the seventh part of moisture, and you kept it so that it might serve as a devourer, at your will, whenever you wish. On the sixth day you commanded the earth to bring forth before you livestock and beasts and reptiles; and over these you set Adam as ruler over all that you had made, and from him we all descend, as many as you have chosen. And all these things I have spoken before you, O Lord, because for our sake you created the world. As for the remaining nations who have descended from Adam, you said they are nothing, and that they are like spittle, and their abundance you have compared to a drop from a bucket. And now, O Lord, behold, these nations which have been counted as nothing have begun to rule over us and devour us; but we, your people, whom you have called your firstborn, your only begotten, your zealous defender, have been delivered into their hands. And if the world was created for our sake, why do we not possess the inheritance along with the age? How long shall this be so?

Chapter 7.
And it came to pass, when I had finished speaking these words, the angel who had been sent to me on the first nights was sent to me again, and he said to me: Rise, Esdras, and hear the words that I have come to speak to you. And I said: Speak, my God. And he said to me: The sea is set in a broad place so that it might be deep and vast; but its entrance is set in a narrow place, so as to be like a river. Who, wishing to enter the sea and to see it or to command it, could do so without first passing through the narrows? Is there another example? A city is built and set in a plain, and is full of all good things. But its entrance is narrow and set on a steep place, so that on the right side there is fire, and on the left side deep water; and there is only one single path between them, set between the fire and the water, so that only a man's footstep can fit upon the path. If then that city is given to a man as an inheritance, but he has never crossed the perilous passage before, how shall he receive his inheritance? And I said: So it is, Lord. And he said to me: Such is also the portion of Israel. For it was for their sake that I made the world; and when Adam transgressed my statutes, what was done was judged. And the entrances of this present world were made narrow and sorrowful and toilsome; they are few and evil and full of dangers, and full of great labor and hardship; but the entrances of the greater world are broad and secure, and bear the fruit of immortality. Therefore if those who live in this cramped and vain life do not enter through the narrow gate, they cannot receive the things that are stored up. Now therefore why are you troubled along with those who are corruptible, and why do you stir yourself along with those who are mortal? And why have you not taken to heart what is to come?

· Fourth ·                                                                                                        252.

But as for what is present, I answered and said: O Lord, you have indeed ordained in your law that the righteous shall inherit these things, and that the wicked shall perish. The righteous shall endure hardship, hoping for spacious things, but the ungodly who have acted wickedly, and suffered narrow things, shall not see the spacious ones. And he said to me: There is no judge above God, nor anyone understanding above the Most High. For many nations shall perish, because they have neglected what has been set before them as the law of God. For God purified the ancient ones when they came: what they should do to live, and what they should observe so as not to be punished. But the ungodly were not obedient, and they contradicted him, and established for themselves vain thoughts, and appointed for themselves deceits of wickedness, and declared that the Most High does not exist — and did not know his ways, and despised his law, and rejected his ordinances, and did not accomplish his works. Therefore, Ezra, empty things for the empty, and full things for the full. Behold, the time is coming, and when it comes there shall be the signs I foretold to you. The bride shall appear, and she appearing shall show what is now hidden on earth; and everyone who is delivered from the evils I have foretold shall see my wonders. For my son Jesus shall be revealed together with those who are with him, and those left shall rejoice for four hundred years. And after those years my son the Messiah shall die, and all who draw human breath, and the world shall turn to ancient silence for seven days as it was at the beginning of creation, so that no one shall remain, and after seven days the age which is not yet awake shall be roused, and the corruptible shall perish. And the earth shall give back what sleeps in it, and the dust what dwells in it in silence, and the chambers shall give back the souls committed to them. And the Most High shall be revealed upon the seat of judgment, and mercy shall pass away; long-suffering shall be withdrawn, and judgment alone shall remain; truth shall stand, and faithfulness shall prevail. And work shall follow, and the reward shall be shown; righteousness shall keep watch, and unrighteousness shall not rule. Then I said: Abraham first prayed for the people of Sodom, and Moses for the fathers who sinned in the desert, and after him Joshua for Israel in the days of Achan and Samuel, and David for the plague, and Solomon for those who were to come into the sanctuary, and Elijah for those who received rain, and for the dead man that he might live, and Hezekiah for the people in the days of Sennacherib, and many for many. If therefore now, when corruptibility has grown and unrighteousness has multiplied, the righteous prayed for the ungodly — why then cannot it be so now? And he answered and said to me: This present age is not the end; the glory of God abides within it frequently; therefore they prayed for the weak. But the Day of Judgment shall be the end of this age and the beginning of the immortal age to come, in which corruptibility has passed away, intemperance has been cut off, unbelief has been destroyed, and righteousness has grown and truth has dawned. Therefore no one shall be able to save one who is destroyed, nor shall anyone harm one who has conquered. I answered and said: This is my first and last word: it would have been better if the earth had not produced Adam, or else, when it had produced him, had restrained him from sinning. For what does it profit all who live in this present age in sorrow, and yet after death hope for punishment? O what have you done, Adam? For when you sinned, the fall was not yours alone, but ours who are descended from you. What does it profit us that we are promised an immortal age, when we have done deadly deeds? And since an everlasting hope has been declared to us, but we most wretchedly in vain...

with your own intellect, and you will mortify him as your creature, and you will quicken him as your own work. If then you destroy him who was formed with such great labors, it is easily arranged by your will that what was made might be preserved. And now, O Lord, I will speak: you know more about every man than I do; and concerning your own servant, for whom I grieve, and concerning your inheritance, over whom I mourn, and concerning Israel, for whom I am sad, and concerning Jacob, for whom I sorrow — therefore I begin to pray before you for myself and for them, for I see our sins of those who dwell on earth. But I have heard the swiftness of the Judge who is to come. Therefore hear my voice and understand my speech, and I will speak before you. The beginning of words was before anything was created. And I said: O Lord, who inhabit eternity, whose eyes are lifted up on high and in the air, whose throne is beyond measure and whose glory is incomprehensible; before whom stands the host of angels with trembling, at whose command the wind and fire are turned; whose word is true and whose utterances are enduring; whose command is strong and whose disposition is terrible; whose glance dries up the abyss and whose wrath causes the mountains to melt away; and truth testifies. Hear the prayer of your servant, and receive in your ears the petition of your creature. While I live I will speak, and while I have understanding I will answer. Do not look upon the sins of your own people, but upon those who have served you in truth. Do not attend to the wicked pursuits of the nations, but to those who have kept your testimonies with suffering. Do not consider those who before your sight have lived falsely, but remember those who have known your fear of their own will. Do not wish to destroy those who have lived like cattle, but look upon those who have gloriously taught your law. Do not be troubled by those who were judged inferior, but love those who have always trusted in your justice and glory.

For we and our fathers have languished with such diseases, but you because of us sinners will be called merciful. For if you desire to have mercy on us, you will be called merciful, since we do not have works of righteousness. For the righteous, who have many good works stored up, shall receive their reward from their own works. What is man, that you should be angered over him who is corruptible, so that you should love him so? In truth there is no one from the nations who has not acted wickedly, or among those who confess who has not sinned. For in this your justice and your goodness will be announced, O Lord, when you have mercy on those who have no store of good works. And he answered me and said: You have spoken some things rightly, and according to your words so it shall be. For I will not think about the fashioning of those who have sinned before death, before judgment, before perdition; but I will rejoice over the fashioning of the righteous, and I will remember also their pilgrimage and their salvation and the receiving of their reward. So as I have spoken, so it is. For just as a farmer sows many seeds on the ground and plants many plants, but not all that was sown is saved in season, nor do all things that were planted take root — so also those who are sown in the world will not all be saved. And I answered and said: If I have found favor, let me speak. How is it with the seed of the farmer, if it does not come up, or if it does not receive your rain in season, or if it has been corrupted by too much rain — so likewise is it with man who is formed by your hands; you are called his image, because you are made like him, and for whose sake you have fashioned all things, and you have made him like the seed of the farmer. Do not be angry with us, but spare your own, and have mercy on your inheritance. And to your creature...

miseries. And he answered me and said: What things are present for those who are present, and future things for those who are to come. For much still remains for you, that you might love my creation above me: but I have drawn near to you frequently, and to the just, but never to the unjust. And in this also you are wonderful before the Most High: that you humbled yourself as is fitting, and did not judge yourself to be among the just and most glorious. Therefore the miseries are wondrous and miserable for those who inhabit the world in the last times: because they have walked in great pride. But understand for yourself: and inquire about those like you about glory. For paradise is opened to you: the tree of life is planted: the future age is prepared: abundance is prepared: a city is built: rest is established: goodness is perfected: and wisdom is perfected. The root of evil is sealed from you: weakness and the snare are hidden from you: and corruption has fled into hell, into oblivion. Sorrows have passed away: and in the end the treasure of immortality is revealed. Therefore do not continue to inquire about the multitude of those who perish. For they themselves, having received freedom, despised the Most High: and scorned his law: and forsook his ways. And moreover they trampled down his righteous ones: and said in their hearts that there is no God: even knowing that they must die. As therefore these things shall receive you which are foretold: so also thirst and torment which are prepared for them. For he did not wish man to perish. But they who were created have themselves defiled the name of him who made them: and were ungrateful to him who prepared life for them. Therefore my judgment now draws near. These things I have not shown to all, but only to you and to a few like you. And I answered and said: Behold, O Lord, you have now shown me the multitude of signs which you will begin to perform in the last times:

but you have not shown me at what time. And he answered me and said: Measure the time carefully within yourself: and when you see that a certain part of the signs which have been foretold has passed, then you shall understand that it is the time in which the Most High will begin to visit the age which he made. And when you see in the world disturbances in places and tumults of peoples: then you shall understand that the Most High has spoken of these things from the days that were before you from the beginning. For just as everything that is made in the world has a beginning as well as an end, and the end is manifest: so also the times of the Most High have manifest beginnings in signs and wonders, and conclusions in deeds and signs. And everyone who shall be saved and shall be able to escape by his works and by the faith in which you have believed shall be preserved from the said perils: and shall see my salvation in my land and within my borders, which I have sanctified for myself from eternity. And then those who have now abused my ways shall marvel: and those who have cast them aside with contempt shall dwell in torments. For those who did not acknowledge me while living, though they received benefits, and who despised my law while they still had freedom: and while the place of repentance was still open to them did not understand but spurned it: these must come to know it after death in torment. Therefore do not inquire further about how the impious shall be tormented: but inquire rather how the just shall be saved: and whose is the age and for whose sake it was made and when. And I answered and said: I have said before and I say now and will say again: for those who perish are more than those who shall be saved: as a wave is greater than a drop. And he answered me and said: Such as the field, such also the seed:

· Fifth ·

What flowers, such is the coloring and such is the maker's craft; what farmer, such is the cultivation of the age. And now, when I was preparing these things for those who now exist, before the age in which they would dwell came to be, no one contradicted me. For then each one, and now the Creator, with the world prepared and with sustenance never failing and the law beyond searching out, the ways of men were corrupted. And I considered the age, and behold there was danger because of the thoughts that had come into it. And I saw and spared greatly, and kept for myself a grape from the cluster, and a planting from a great tribe. Let the multitude therefore perish that was born in vain, but let my grape and my planting be preserved, for I brought them to perfection with great labor. But you, if you still remain seven more days — yet you shall not fast during them — you shall go into a field of flowers where no house is built, and you shall eat only of the flowers of the field; you shall taste no meat and drink no wine, but only flowers. Pray to the Most High without ceasing, and I will come and speak with you. And I went out as he told me, into the field called Ardat, and I sat there among the flowers. And I ate of the herbs of the field, and the food thereof satisfied me. And after seven days I was again lying upon the grass, and my heart was troubled again as before. And my mouth was opened and I began to speak before the Most High and said: O Lord, you who revealed yourself to our fathers in the desert when they were going out of Egypt, into a land uncultivated and unfruitful — and you spoke, saying: Hear me, O Israel, and give ear to my words, O seed of Jacob. For behold, I sow my law in you, and it shall bring forth fruit in you, and you shall be glorified in it forever. But our fathers who received the law did not keep it,

and your statutes they did not observe; and the fruit of the law was not produced, for it could not be, since it was yours; yet those who received it perished because they did not keep what had been sown in them. And behold, the custom is: when the earth receives seed, or the sea a vessel, or any vessel a liquid or food — when that in which it was sown or placed is destroyed, that which was sown or placed in it likewise perishes, and what received it does not remain with us. But for us it has not been so. We who have received the law have sinned and perished, and the heart that received it; yet the law has not perished but remains in its own working. And when I was speaking these things in my heart, I looked up with my eyes and saw a woman on the right side. And behold, she was mourning and weeping with a loud voice, and was deeply grieved in spirit, and her garments were torn, and there was ashes upon her head. Then I dismissed the thoughts in which I had been occupied, and turned to her and said to her: Why do you weep, and why are you grieved in spirit? And she said to me: Leave me, my lord, that I may weep for myself, and add to my grief, for I am very bitter in spirit and deeply humbled. And I said to her: What has happened to you? Tell me. And she said to me: I your servant was barren and had no child, though I had a husband for thirty years. And every hour and every day and all thirty years I prayed to the Most High, night and day. And after thirty years God heard me your handmaid, and saw my humiliation and attended to my distress, and gave me a son. And I rejoiced greatly over him, I and my husband and all our neighbors, and we gave great honor to the Mighty One. And I nursed him with great toil, and when he had grown

· Esdras ·

When he had grown up and had come to take a wife: and it came to pass on the day of the wedding feast, when my son had entered his wedding chamber, he fell down and died; and we overturned all the lamps. And all my fellow citizens rose up to comfort me, and I rested until the second day at night. And when all of them had quieted down to comfort me, so that I might rest, I arose in the night and fled and came to this field as you see, and I intend no longer to return to the city, but to remain here, and neither to eat nor to drink, but to mourn and fast without ceasing until I die. And I left off the words I was speaking, and answered her with anger and said: You are foolish above all women; do you not see our grief and what has befallen us? For Zion, our mother, is sorrowful in all things, deeply humbled and greatly mourning; and now while all of us mourn and are sad, because all of us are to be comforted, you grieve for one son alone. Ask the earth itself, and it will tell you that it is she who ought to mourn for so many who have grown upon her. And from her all were born from the beginning and others will come. And behold, nearly all now walk to destruction, and the multitude of them is consumed. Who then ought to mourn more — she who has lost so great a multitude, or you who grieve for one alone? But if you say to me that your grief is not like the earth's grief — because you have lost the fruit of your womb, whom you bore with travail and brought forth with pain — yet the earth, after the manner of the earth, and those who live in her multitude: how has it come about? And I say to you: just as you labored in bringing forth, so also does the earth give her fruit to mankind, from the beginning, to him who made her. Now, therefore, keep your sorrow within yourself and bear with courage what has befallen you. For if you acknowledge the judgment of God and accept his counsel, in due time you will receive comfort and be praised thereby. Go therefore into the city to your husband. And she said to me: I will not do so, neither will I go into the city, but here I will die. And I continued to speak with her and said: Do not do this thing, but be persuaded and let reason prevail. For how many are the calamities of Zion? Be comforted on account of the grief of Jerusalem. You see how our sanctuary is laid waste, our altar thrown down, our temple destroyed, our psalteries humbled, our hymns silenced, our rejoicing dissolved, the light of our candlestick put out, the ark of our covenant plundered, our holy things defiled, the name that was called upon us profaned, our children suffered disgrace, our priests burned, our Levites gone into captivity, our virgins defiled, our women ravished, our righteous men carried away, our little ones destroyed, our young men enslaved, and our strong men made feeble. And what is more than all else, the seal of Zion has lost her glory, for she has been given into the hands of those who hate us. You therefore shake off your great sorrow and put away your multitude of griefs, so that the Almighty may be merciful to you again and the Most High may give you rest, relief from your toils. And it came to pass, while I was speaking with her, that her face suddenly shone brightly, and her appearance became radiant like lightning, so that I was greatly afraid of her and wondered what this might be. And behold, she suddenly let out a loud cry full of terror, so that the earth shook at the sound of the woman. And I looked, and the woman was no longer visible to me, but there was a city being built...

· Fifth ·

255.

was being built and the place was shown with great foundations: and I was afraid and cried out with a loud voice: and I said, Where is the angel Uriel, who came to me at the beginning? For he it was who brought me into this great ecstasy of mind. And my end has come in corruption, and my prayer into reproach: and while I was speaking these things, behold he came to me and looked at me. And behold I was laid as one dead, and my understanding was taken away from me. And he took my right hand and strengthened me and set me on my feet. And he said to me: What is the matter with you, and why is your understanding troubled, and why is the sense of your heart disturbed? And I said: Because you have forsaken me. For I did according to your directions, and I went out into the field, and behold I saw and still see what I cannot tell. And he said to me: Stand up like a man, and I will instruct you. And I said: Speak, my Lord, to me. Do not forsake me, lest I die in vain: for I have seen what I did not know, and I hear what I do not understand. Or is my sense deceived, and my soul dreaming? Now therefore I beseech you: show your servant concerning this departure. And he answered me and said: Hear me, and I will inform you, and tell you the things of which you are afraid: for the Most High has revealed many secrets to you. He has seen your right way, because you have sorrowed continually for your people, and mourned greatly for Zion. This therefore is the interpretation of the vision which appeared to you a little while ago. You saw a woman mourning, and you began to comfort her; and of the sorrows of the woman you saw no more, but there appeared to you a city being built; and the woman who appeared to you told you of the fall of her son. This is the interpretation: The woman whom you saw, she is Zion; and whereas she told you that she had been barren thirty years: those are the thirty years during which there was as yet no offering made in her. And it came to pass after thirty years that Solomon built the city and offered offerings: it was then that she who had been barren bore a son. And whereas she told you that she nurtured him with labor: that was the dwelling in Jerusalem. And whereas she said to you that her son coming into his bridal chamber died: and that calamity befell her: this was the fall that came upon Jerusalem. And behold you saw her likeness: and because she mourned for her son, you began to comfort her; of these things which have happened, these were to be revealed to you. And now the Most High sees that you are sincerely grieved, and that you suffer with your whole heart for her: he has shown you the brightness of her glory, and the beauty of her comeliness. Therefore I told you to remain in the field where no house was built: for I knew that the Most High was beginning to show you these things; therefore I told you to come into the field where no foundation of any building was. For the work of the building of men could not stand in a place where the city of the Most High was beginning to be shown. Therefore do not fear, and let not your heart be troubled, but go in and see the splendor and greatness of the building, as much as your eyes are able to see: and afterward you will hear as much as your ears can hear. For you are blessed above many, and are called with the Most High as but few have been. And you shall remain here tonight and the next night: and the Most High shall show you those visions of what the Most High will do to those who dwell upon the earth in the last days. And I slept that night and the next, as he had told me. Chapter XI. And I saw a dream: and behold there came up from the sea an eagle that had twelve

. Esdras .

ale of the wings: and three heads. And I saw: and behold it spread its wings over all the earth: and all the winds of heaven blew upon it and gathered around it. And I saw: and from its feathers there grew contrary feathers: and it produced small and modest little feathers. For its heads were at rest: and the middle head was greater than the others: but it rested with them. And I saw: and behold the eagle flew on its wings: and reigned over the earth and over those who dwell in it. And I saw that all things under heaven were subject to it: and no one spoke against it: nor any one of the creatures that are upon the earth. And I saw: and behold the eagle rose up upon its talons: and sent its voice to its wings saying. Do not all wake at once: sleep every one in his own place: and watch in turn. But the heads were last. And I saw: and behold the voice did not come from its heads: but from the middle of its body. And I counted its contrary feathers: and behold there were eight. And I saw: and behold from the right side one rose up first: and reigned over all the earth. And when it reigned: its end came: and it disappeared: and the next rose up and reigned. It held power for a long time. And when it reigned: its end came so that it disappeared like the one before: and behold a voice was sent to it saying. Hear, you who have held the earth for so long. I announce this to you before you cease to appear. No one after you shall hold your time: nor even half of it. And the third raised itself: and held the rule like the ones before: and it also disappeared. And so it happened to all the others, each holding rule in turn: and then none appearing again. And I saw: and behold in time the following wings rose up from the right side to take hold of the rule: and these were among those that held: but nevertheless

they immediately disappeared: for some of them also rose up: but did not hold the rule. And I saw after this: and behold the twelve wings and two little feathers did not appear: and nothing remained in the body of the eagle except two resting heads and six little feathers. And I saw: and behold of six feathers two were divided: and they remained under the head that is on the right side. For four remained in their place. And I saw: and behold these sub-wings thought to raise themselves up: and to hold the rule. And I saw: and one was raised up: but immediately disappeared. And it vanished more quickly than the ones before. And I saw: and behold the two that remained by themselves thought to reign also: and while they were thinking this: behold one of the resting heads, which was the middle one, awoke. For there were two heads greater. And I saw that two heads were complete beside it: and behold a head turned aside with those who were with it: and devoured the two sub-wings that thought to reign. But this head crushed all the earth: and dominated over those who dwell on the earth with great oppression: and held power over the whole world above all the wings that had been. And I saw after this: and behold the middle head suddenly disappeared: and likewise the wings. And two heads remained: and they likewise reigned over the earth: and over those who dwell in it. And I saw: and behold the head on the right side devoured the one on the left. And I heard a voice saying to me. Look before you: and consider what you see. And I saw: and behold like a lion roused from the forest roaring: and I saw that it sent the voice of a man to the eagle. And it spoke saying. Hear you: and I will speak to you: and the Most High says to you. Are you not the one that has prevailed over the four animals which I had made to reign in my world so that through them might come

the end of the ages. And the fourth came and subdued all the animals that had passed, and held dominion with them in great terror, and inhabited the whole world with toil and sorrow, and dwelt for so many ages in the earth with deceit. And you judged the earth not with truth. You afflicted the meek, and injured those who were at peace, and loved liars, and destroyed the dwellings of those who brought forth fruit, and cast down the walls of those who had done you no harm. And your insolence rose up to the Most High, and your arrogance to the Mighty One. And the Most High looked upon your arrogant times, and behold, they are ended, and your abominations are fulfilled. Therefore you shall no more appear, O eagle, nor your dreadful wings, nor your wicked feathers, nor your evil heads, nor your most harmful talons, nor your whole vain body, that the whole earth may be refreshed and freed from your violence, and may hope for the judgment and mercy of him who made it.

And it came to pass that while the lion was speaking these words to the eagle, I looked and behold, the remaining head had vanished, and the four wings which had passed over to support it were gone, to reign; and the kingdom was small and full of tumult. And I looked and behold, it appeared no more, and the whole body of the eagle was burned, and I was greatly astonished. And I awoke from the tumult and confusion of my mind and from great fear, and I said to my spirit: Behold, you have brought this upon me, in that you search out the ways of the Most High. Behold, I am still weary in spirit and very faint in soul, and there is but little strength in me, for I was much afraid this night. Therefore I will now pray to the Most High, that he may strengthen me to the end. And I said: O Lord and Master, if I have found grace before your eyes, and if I am justified before you above many others, and if indeed my prayer has ascended before your face, strengthen me

and show to your servant the interpretation and distinction of this terrible vision, so that you may fully comfort my soul. For you have judged me worthy to show me the last times. And he said to me: This is the interpretation of this vision. The eagle which you saw coming up from the sea is the kingdom which was seen in the vision of Daniel your brother. But it was not interpreted to him as I now interpret it to you. Behold, the days are coming when a kingdom shall arise upon the earth, and it shall be more terrible than all the kingdoms that were before it. And twelve kings shall reign in it, one after another. And the second shall begin to reign, and shall hold power longer than any of the twelve. This is the interpretation of the twelve wings you saw. And the voice which you heard speaking not from the heads but from the middle of the body: this is the interpretation. After the time of that kingdom great contentions shall arise, and it shall be in danger of falling, yet shall not fall, but shall be restored again to its former state. And the eight subordinate wings you saw: this is the interpretation. Eight kings shall arise in it whose times shall be short and their years swift, and two of them shall perish. As the middle time approaches, four shall be kept until their time is near its end; but two shall remain until the end. And the three heads you saw at rest: this is the interpretation. In the last days the Most High shall raise up three kingdoms, and shall renew many things in them, and they shall have dominion over the earth and over those who dwell therein, with much toil above all who were before them. Therefore they are called the heads of the eagle. For these are they who shall recapitulate its wickedness and bring its last deeds to completion. And when you saw

· Esdras ·

The greater head not appearing: this is its interpretation. Because their time has come and their rest shall die, yet with torments. For two who persevered: the sword shall devour them. For one sword shall devour him who is with it, yet in the last days this sword shall cut down. And you who saw the two pinions passing over the head which is on the right side: this is its interpretation. These are they whom the Most High has gathered at his end: this is a kingdom full of exile and trouble. Just as you saw and the lion that you saw arising from the forest, roaring and speaking to the eagle and accusing it of its injustices through all its words, as you heard: this is the Ancient One whom the Most High has kept to the end against them and their impieties, and he shall rebuke them and shall cast before them their contempts. He shall set them living before the judgment, and when he has rebuked them he shall correct them. For the remnant of my people shall be delivered with mercy, those who have been saved within my borders, and he shall gladden them until the end, the day of judgment, of which I have spoken to you from the beginning. This is the dream that you saw, and these are its interpretations. You therefore alone were worthy to know this secret of the Most High. Therefore write all these things in a book that you have seen, and place them in a hidden place, and you shall teach them to the wise among your people, whose hearts you know are able to receive and keep these secrets. But wait here yet another seven days, so that whatever the Most High wishes to show you may be shown to you. And he departed from me. And it came to pass, when all the people heard that the seven days had passed and I had not returned to the city, they all gathered together from the least to the greatest and came to me, and said to me: What have we sinned against you, or what injustice have we done to you,

that you have forsaken us and sit in this place? For you are the only one remaining to us among all, like a cluster of grapes from the vineyard, and like a lamp in a dark place, and like a harbor and a ship saved from the storm. Are not the evils that have come upon us sufficient? If therefore you forsake us, how much better it would have been for us had we also been burned in the burning of Zion! For we are no better than those who died there. And they wept with a loud voice. And I answered them and said: Take courage, O Israel, and do not grieve, O house of Jacob. For your remembrance is before the Most High, and the Mighty One has not forgotten you in your tribulation. For I have not forsaken you, nor have I departed from you, but I came to this place to pray for the desolation of Zion and to seek mercy for the humiliation of your sanctuary. Now therefore go, each of you to your own house, and I will come to you after these days. And the people went as I told them, truly. But I sat in the field seven days as he commanded me, and I ate only of the flowers of the field and herbs; such was my food in those days. CHAPTER XIII.

And it came to pass after seven days that I dreamed a dream in the night. And behold, a wind arose from the sea and stirred up all its waves. And I looked, and behold, that man grew strong with thousands alongside him, and he turned his face to look, and everything beneath his gaze trembled, and a voice went out from his mouth, and all who heard his voice melted as wax melts when it feels the fire. And I looked after this, and behold, there was gathered together a multitude of men without number from the four winds to make war against the man who had come up from the sea. And I looked, and behold, he carved out for himself a great mountain:

And it flew over him. And I sought to see the region or place from which the mountain had been cut, but I could not. And after these things I saw, and behold all those who had gathered to him to fight against him were very afraid, and yet they dared to fight. And behold, when he saw the onset of the multitude coming, he did not raise his hand, nor did he hold a sword, nor any warlike weapon: but only as I saw, he sent forth from his mouth as it were a blast of fire, and from his lips a flaming breath, and from his tongue he cast forth sparks and tempests: and all these were mingled together, the blast of fire and the flaming breath and the great tempest, and fell upon the oncoming multitude which was ready to fight, and burned them all up: so that suddenly nothing was to be seen of the innumerable multitude, but only dust and the smell of smoke. When I saw this I was amazed. Afterward I saw the same man come down from the mountain and call to himself another multitude which was peaceable: and there came to him the faces of many men, some of whom were joyful, and some sad, and some were bound, and some were bringing others as offerings. Then I fainted from great fear, and I awoke and said: You have shown these wonders from the beginning and have deemed me worthy to receive my prayer; and now show me also the interpretation of this dream. For as I consider in my mind, woe to those who shall be left in those days — and much more woe to those who are not left. For those who are not left shall be sorrowful, knowing what things are laid up in the last days, which shall happen to them and those who are left. But still it is easier for those who enter into these dangers to come like a cloud, and not to see what shall happen in the last time. And he answered me and said: The interpretation of the vision I will tell you, and I will also open to you the things you have spoken of. Since you have spoken of those who are left, this is the interpretation: He who shall bring the peril at that time shall himself guard those in peril. And those who have fallen into danger are those who have works and faith toward the Almighty. Know therefore that those who are left are more blessed than those who have died. These are the interpretations of the vision. Because you saw a man coming up from the heart of the sea: this is he whom the Most High has been keeping for many ages, who shall himself deliver his creation; and he shall direct those who are left behind. And because you saw that out of his mouth there came as it were a blast of wind, and fire, and storm; and because he held neither sword nor any warlike weapon, yet destroyed the multitude that had come to fight him: this is the interpretation. Behold, the days are coming when the Most High will begin to deliver those who are on the earth, and there shall come bewilderment of mind upon those who dwell on the earth. And they shall plan to war against one another, city against city, place against place, people against people, and kingdom against kingdom. And when these things come to pass and the signs occur which I showed you before, then shall my Son be revealed, whom you saw as a man ascending. And it shall be that when all the nations hear his voice, every man shall leave his own land and the warfare that he has against another, and an innumerable multitude shall gather together, as you saw, desiring to come and fight against him. But he shall stand on the top of Mount Zion. And Zion shall come and shall be shown to all men, prepared and built, as you saw the mountain cut out without hands. And my Son shall rebuke...

Esdras

Because the nations have found the iniquities of those who drew near to the tempest, on account of the evil thoughts and torments with which they will begin to be tormented, who are likened to flame: and he shall destroy them without effort through the law that is compared to fire. And because you saw him gathering to himself another peaceable multitude: these are the ten tribes who were taken captive from their own land in the days of King Josiah, whom Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, took captive, and carried them beyond the river, and they were brought into another land. But they took counsel among themselves that they would leave the multitude of the nations, and go into a further country where no human race had ever dwelt, so that there they might keep their statutes, which they had not kept in their own country. And they went in by the narrow passages of the river Euphrates. For the Most High then performed wonders for them, and held back the channels of the river until they had passed over. Through that region there was a great journey of a year and a half; and the same region is called Arzareth. There they dwelt until the last time; and now when they begin to come again, the Most High will hold back the springs of the river again, so that they may be able to cross over. Therefore you saw the multitude gathered together in peace. But those who are left of your people, who are found within my holy borders — these are they who shall be saved. Chapter XIV.

And it came to pass on the third day, and I was sitting under an oak. And behold, a voice came out of a bush near me and said, Esdras, Esdras. And I said, Here am I, Lord. And I stood up upon my feet. And he said to me, I revealed myself in a bush and spoke to Moses, when my people were in bondage in Egypt; and I sent him and led my people out of Egypt; and I brought him up to Mount Sinai, and kept him with me many days; and I told him many wondrous things, and showed him the secrets of the times and the end, and commanded him, saying: These things you shall declare openly, and these you shall keep secret. And now I say to you: lay up in your heart the signs that I have shown you, and the dreams that you have seen, and the interpretations which you have heard. For you shall be taken away from among men, and from now on you shall remain with those like you, until the times are ended. For the age has lost its youth, and the times begin to grow old. For the age is divided into twelve parts, and ten parts of it are already past, and half of the tenth part. Now therefore, set your house in order, and reprove your people, comfort the lowly among them, and renounce now corruption, and let go the mortal.

thoughts, and let human burdens weigh you down no longer, remembering your weak nature; set aside the most troubling concerns, and make haste to depart from these times. For the evils you have now seen befall will bring yet worse things to come. For as the world grows weaker with age, so will the evils multiply upon its inhabitants. The age has prolonged itself in lies, and falsehood has drawn near. For what you saw in the vision is now hastening to come to pass. And I answered and said before you, O Lord: Behold, I will go as you have commanded me, and I will rebuke the people who are now present. But who will warn those yet to be born? The world is set in darkness, and those who dwell in it are without light. For your law has been burned, and therefore no one knows what you have done or what will begin. If I have found favor in your sight, send your Holy Spirit into me, and I will write all that has happened in the world from the beginning — all that was written in your law — so that people might find the path, and those who wish to live in the last times may live. He answered me and said: Go, gather the people and tell them not to seek you for forty days. But you, prepare for yourself many writing tablets, and take with you Dabriah, Selniah, Echaniah, and Asiel — five men skilled at writing swiftly. Come here, and I will light in your heart the lamp of understanding, which shall not be extinguished until you have finished what you are about to write. And when you have done so, some things you shall publish openly, and some you shall deliver secretly to the wise. Tomorrow at this hour you shall begin to write. I went forth as he commanded me, gathered all the people, and said: Hear these words, O Israel. Our fathers from the beginning sojourned in Egypt and were delivered from there; they received the law of life which they did not keep — and you after them have likewise transgressed it. The land of Zion was given to you as an inheritance, and your fathers and you yourselves acted in wickedness, and you did not walk in the ways that the Most High commanded. Therefore the righteous Judge, being what he is, took away in due time what he had given. And now you are here, while your brothers are already within. If therefore you rule over your own minds and discipline your hearts, you shall be preserved alive and after death shall obtain mercy. For judgment comes after death, when we live again; then the names of the righteous shall be made known and the deeds of the wicked shall be revealed. Let no one come to me now, nor seek me for forty days. I took the five men as he commanded me, and we went into the field and remained there. On the next day a voice called to me saying: Ezra, open your mouth and drink what I give you. I opened my mouth and behold, a full cup was held out to me. It was full like water, but its color was like fire. I took it and drank, and when I had drunk, my heart poured forth understanding and wisdom grew in my breast. My spirit retained its memory, and my mouth was opened and was no longer shut. The Most High gave understanding to the five men, and they wrote what was spoken, in characters they did not know, taking turns during the night. By day I spoke and by night I was not silent. In forty days, two hundred and four books were written. And when the forty days were ended, the Most High spoke to me, saying: Make public the twenty-four books you wrote first, so that both the worthy and the unworthy may read them; but keep the seventy that were last, to hand on to the wise among your people. For in them is the spring of understanding and the fountain of wisdom.
