And I spoke thus. Chapter 15.
Speak in the ears of my people the words of the prophecy which I will put in your mouth, says the Lord, and have them written down, for they are faithful and true. Do not fear the thoughts that arise against you, nor be troubled by the unbelief of those who say such things, for all unbelievers shall perish in their unbelief.
Behold, says the Lord, I bring upon the earth: evils, the sword, famine, death, and destruction, because iniquity has spread over the whole earth, and their wicked deeds are fulfilled. Therefore the Lord says: I will no longer be silent about the impieties of those who act irreligiously, nor will I endure those who practice wickedness. Behold, the blood of the innocent and the just cries out to me, and the souls of the righteous cry out unceasingly. I will surely avenge them, says the Lord, and I will receive to myself all the innocent blood from them. Behold, my people are being led like a flock to slaughter; I will no longer allow them to dwell in the land of Egypt, but I will bring them out with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. And I will strike them with a first plague as before, and I will corrupt all their land. Egypt shall mourn, and its foundations, with plague and chastisement which God shall bring upon it. Those who till the land shall grieve, for their seeds shall fail from blight, hail, and a terrible storm. Woe to the world and to those who dwell in it, for the sword draws near and their destruction is at hand. Nation shall rise against nation for battle, and they shall clash with one another. There shall be upheaval among people; some, growing stronger, shall care nothing for their king or rulers; the ways of those who work shall come to nothing. A man shall desire to enter a city and shall not be able. Because of their pride, the cities shall be thrown into turmoil; men shall fear one another. A man shall have no mercy on his neighbor to save them, for their enemies shall come with the sword to take their possessions because of famine and great tribulation.
Behold, says God, I call together all the kings of the earth from the rising of the sun, from the south, from the east, and from Lebanon, to turn against one another and repay what they have given, just as they have done to my chosen ones to this day; so I will do and repay them. Thus says the Lord God: My decrees shall not spare the sinners, and my sword shall not cease over those who shed innocent blood on the earth. A fire went forth from his wrath and consumed the foundations of the earth, and sinners like straw kindled with fire. Woe to those who sin and do not keep my commandments, says the Lord; I will not spare them. Depart, children, from power; do not examine my sanctuary, for the Lord knows all who transgress against him. Therefore he has delivered them to death and slaughter. Now evils have come upon the whole earth, and you shall remain in them. God will not deliver you, because you have sinned against him.
Behold a vision, and terrible is the sight from the east. And there shall come forth nations of Arab dragons in their chariots, and their number rushes over the land like the wind, so that all who hear them tremble with fear; they shall rage like wild boars from the forest and shall come with great might and stand in battle against them, and shall lay waste a portion of the land of Assyria. Then the dragons, remembering their origin, shall gather together in great strength to pursue them. These shall be thrown into confusion and weep before their power, and turn their feet to flight; and one from the territory of Assyria shall besiege them, and take one of them, and there shall be fear and trembling in their army, and strife among their kings. Behold, clouds from

from the east and from the north as far as the south: and their appearance shall be dreadful and full of fury and violence. And they shall strike one against another, and they shall strike the stars together upon the earth and those stars. And there shall be blood from the sword as far as the belly, and the smoke of man as far as the camel's bedding. And there shall be great fear and trembling upon them: and those who see that wrath shall tremble, and trembling shall seize them. And after these things, great clouds shall rise from the south and from the north, and another portion from the west. And mighty winds from the east shall prevail and push them back, and the cloud which was stirred up in wrath, and the star shall violate the eastern and western wind. And the great and mighty clouds, full of wrath, shall move over all the earth and its inhabitants: and they shall pour out upon every high and prominent place a terrible fire, with hail and flying coals, and dark waters, so that they may fill all the ravines and all the rivers with an abundance of dark waters. And the cities shall be destroyed and walls and mountains and hills and the trees of the forests, and the hay of the meadows and their grain. And standing armies shall march up to Babylon and ravage her: they shall come to her and surround her, and shall pour all their wrath upon her. And the dust and smoke shall rise to heaven, and all who are around shall mourn for her, and those who remain under her shall grieve for those who were destroyed. And you, who are another in the hope of Babylon, and her glory: woe to you, miserable one, because you have likened yourself and adorned your daughters in fornication, to please and to glory before your lovers, who always desired to fornicate with you. You have imitated the abominable one in all her works and in her ordinances: therefore God says: I will send upon you evils, widowhood, poverty, famine, and the sword and pestilence to devastate your houses

from violence and death and the glory of your virtue. The flower shall dry up when the heat that was sent upon you returns: you shall be weakened like a poor woman, struck and chastened by the miserable, so that your lovers and keepers cannot receive you. Did I not thus zealously pursue you, says the Lord, unless you had killed my chosen ones in all wrath, exalting the striking of hands, and speaking over their death while they were drunk: and offering the beauty of your face as the price of fornication in your bosom: therefore you shall receive retribution. As you have done to my chosen ones, says the Lord, so shall the Lord do to you, and deliver you to evil. And your own people shall perish by famine, and you yourself shall fall in ruins, and your cities shall be destroyed, and all your people shall fall by the sword in the field. And those who are in the mountains shall perish of hunger, and they shall eat their own flesh and drink blood for want of bread. You shall come through the seas and receive evils again. And passing through they shall beat down the hateful city and destroy a portion of your land, and they shall wipe out a part of your glory, and returning from their captivity. And you shall be to them as stubble, and they shall be as fire to you, and they shall devour you and your cities and your land and your mountains, and all your forests and timber they shall burn with fire. They shall lead your sons into captivity, and take your tribute as plunder, and they shall destroy the glory of your face.

Woe to you, Babylon and Asia, chapter 16.
Woe to you, Egypt and Syria. Gird yourselves with sackcloth and ashes, and mourn for your sons and grieve, for your destruction has drawn near. A sword has been sent against you: and who is there to turn it aside? Fire has been sent against you: and who is there to quench it? Evils have been sent against you: and who is there to drive them away? Can anyone drive away a hungry lion in the forest, or quench

fire in stubble — as soon as it finds something to burn, it bursts into flame. Can anyone drive back an arrow shot by a strong archer? The Lord God sends evils: who can drive them back? See, his fire and his wrath — and who is there to put it out? He will thunder, and who will not fear? He will roar, and who will not be terrified? The Lord threatens, and who will not be utterly cast down before his face? The earth trembled and its foundations; the sea swells from the deep, and its waves are thrown into turmoil, and its fish tremble before the face of the Lord and before the glory of his power. His right arm, which bends the bow, is strong; his arrows are sharp, shot from him, and they will not fail when they begin to be sent to the ends of the earth. Behold, evils are sent out and they will not return until they come upon the earth. Fire is kindled and will not be quenched until it consumes the foundations of the earth. Just as an arrow shot by a mighty archer does not return, so the evils that are sent upon the earth will not return. Woe to me, woe to me! Who will deliver me in those days? The beginning of sorrows and great groaning; the beginning of famine and great death; the beginning of wars and the powers will tremble; the beginning of evils, and all will quake. What shall I do when these evils come? Behold, famine and plague and tribulation and anguish — these scourges are sent as chastisement, and in all these things they will not turn from their iniquities, nor will they keep the memory of the scourges. Behold, there will be a cheapness of grain upon the earth, so that they will think peace has been given to them — and then evils will spring up upon the earth: the sword, famine, and great confusion. For the many who inhabit the earth will perish by famine, and the sword will destroy those who survive the famine; the dead will be cast out like dung, and there will be no one to console them. For the land will be left

desolate and its cities will fall. No one will be left to cultivate the land or to sow it. The trees will give their fruit, and who will harvest them? The grapes will ripen, and who will tread them? For there will be great desolation in every place. For a man will long to see another human being or to hear his voice. For out of a city ten will be left, and two from the field who had hidden themselves in dense forests and clefts of rocks — just as in an olive grove three or four olives are left on each tree, or as in a harvested vineyard a cluster is left by those who carefully glean the vineyard — so in those days three or four will be left by those who search through the houses with the sword. The land will be left desolate, its fields will be laid waste, its roads and all its paths will be overgrown with thorns, because no one will pass through them. Virgins will mourn because they have no bridegrooms; women will mourn because they have no husbands; their daughters will mourn because they have no one to help them. Their bridegrooms will be consumed in war, and their husbands will perish of famine. Hear these things, O servants of the Lord, and know them. Behold, the word of the Lord — receive it; do not disbelieve what the Lord says. Behold, the evils draw near and do not delay. Just as a pregnant woman in the ninth month, when the hour of her delivery is near, feels the pains circling her womb two or three hours before — and the infant comes forth from the womb without delay by even one moment — so the evils will not delay in coming upon the earth, and the world will groan, and pains will surround it. Hear, O my people, the word of the Lord. Prepare yourselves for battle, and in these evils be like strangers upon the earth. Let the one who sells be as one who flees, and the one who buys as one who will lose what he gains.

Here begins the Prologue to the Book of Tobias.

. Tobias .

Jerome, a priest, sends greetings in the Lord to the bishops Chromatius and Heliodorus. I never cease to marvel at your persistent demands. For you require that I translate into Latin the book of Tobit, written in the Chaldean language — a book which the Hebrews exclude from their canon of divine scriptures, placing it among those works they call the Hagiographa. I have done what I could, more to satisfy your wish than my own inclination. For the Hebrews criticize our studies and accuse us of translating things contrary to their canon for Latin ears. But thinking it better to displease the judgment of the Pharisees than to disobey the commands of bishops, I undertook the task as best I could. And since the Chaldean language is closely related to Hebrew, finding a man most skilled in both tongues, I took up the labor of a single day, and whatever he rendered to me in Hebrew words, I in turn conveyed to a secretary I had summoned, translating it into Latin. By your prayers I shall be repaid for this work, once I learn that what you saw fit to command has pleased you. Here ends the Prologue. Here begins the Book of Tobias. Chapter I.

Tobias was of the tribe and city of Naphtali, which is in upper Galilee, above Naalon, past the road that leads westward, having the city of Sepphoris on the left. When he was taken captive in the days of Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, even in captivity he did not forsake the path of truth, but shared all that he could daily with his brothers who were of his tribe. And though he was the youngest of all in the tribe of Naphtali, he did nothing childish in his conduct. Moreover, when all went to the golden calves which Jeroboam king of Israel had made, he alone fled their company and went to Jerusalem to the temple of the Lord, and there he worshiped the Lord God of Israel, faithfully offering all his firstfruits and tithes, so that in the third year he ministered all the tithe to the strangers and newcomers. These things and similar ones the young boy observed according to the law of God. And when he had grown to be a man, he took a wife named Anna from his own tribe, and by her he had a son, giving him his own name, and from childhood he taught him to fear God and to refrain from all sin. So when he had come in captivity with his wife and son to the city of Nineveh, with his whole tribe, and when all were eating of the food of the Gentiles, he kept his soul undefiled and never polluted himself with their food. And because he remembered the Lord with his whole heart, God gave him favor in the sight of Shalmaneser the king, who gave him the freedom to go wherever he wished and to do whatever he desired. He therefore went to all those who were in captivity and gave them wholesome counsel. When he came to Rages, a city of Media, and had with him ten talents of silver from the king's gifts, and saw among his large kindred one Gabael, who was in need and was of his tribe, he gave him the said sum of silver under a bond. But after a long time, when Shalmaneser the king had died and Sennacherib his son reigned in his place, and held the children of Israel as his subjects before him, Tobias went about among all his own kindred and comforted them and distributed to each as much as he could from his resources. He fed the hungry, clothed the naked, and carefully provided burial for the dead and the slain. And when

. Tobias .

We have walked according to your precepts and have not walked sincerely before you. And now, O Lord, do with me according to your will: and command my spirit to be received in peace. For it is better for me to die than to live. On that same day it happened that Sara, the daughter of Raguel, in the city of Rages among the Medes, also heard a reproach from one of her father's maidservants: because she had been given to seven husbands, and a demon named Asmodeus had killed them as soon as they had gone in to her. Therefore, when she rebuked the girl on account of her fault, she answered her saying: May we never see son or daughter of yours upon the earth, you killer of your husbands. Will you kill me also, as you have already killed seven? At these words she went up to a higher room of her house, and for three days and three nights she neither ate nor drank, but continuing in prayer with tears she besought God that he would deliver her from this reproach. On the third day, when she had finished her prayer, blessing the Lord she said: Blessed is your name, O God of our fathers: who when you are angry will show mercy, and in the time of tribulation forgive the sins of those who call upon you. To you I turn my face, to you I direct my eyes. I pray you, O Lord, that you loose me from the bond of this reproach, or else take me away from the earth. You know, O Lord, that I never coveted a husband, and have kept my soul clean from all desire. Never have I joined myself with them that play, neither have I made myself partaker with those who walk in lightness. But a husband I consented to take, with your fear, not with my lust. And either I was unworthy of them, or they perhaps were not worthy of me: because perhaps you have kept me for another man. For it is not in man's power to govern his own will. But this every one is sure of who worships you: that his life, if it be under trial, shall be crowned: if it be under tribulation, it shall be delivered: and if it be under correction, it shall be allowed to come to your mercy. For you are not delighted in our being lost: because after a storm you make a calm, and after tears and weeping you pour in joyfulness. Be your name, O God of Israel, blessed for ever. In that time the prayers of them both were heard in the sight of the glory of the most high God: and the holy angel of the Lord, Raphael, was sent to heal them both, whose prayers at one time were rehearsed in the sight of the Lord. Chapter 4.
Therefore when Tobias thought that his prayer was heard so that he might die, he called to him Tobias his son, and said to him: Hear, my son, the words of my mouth, and lay them as a foundation in your heart. When God shall take my soul, bury my body: and you shall honor your mother all the days of her life. For you must be mindful what and how great perils she suffered for you in her womb. And when she also shall have ended the time of her life, bury her by me. And all the days of your life have God in your mind: and take heed you never consent to sin, and neglect the commandments of the Lord our God. Give alms out of your substance, and turn not away your face from any poor person: for so it shall come to pass that the face of the Lord shall not be turned from you. According to your ability be merciful. If you have much, give abundantly: if you have little, take care even so to bestow willingly a little. For thus you lay up to yourself a good reward for the time of necessity: because alms deliver from

· Tobias ·

from sin and from death it sets free: and it will not suffer the soul to go into darkness. Almsgiving will be a great confidence before the most high God for all who practice it. Take heed, my son, to keep yourself from all fornication: and besides your wife, never endure to know a sin. Let not pride dominate in your mind or in your word: for in it all ruin had its beginning. Whoever has done any service for you: immediately pay him his wages: and let the pay of your hired servant remain with you not at all. Whatever you hate to be done to you, see that you do not do to another at any time. Eat your bread with the hungry and the poor: and cover the naked with your garments. Lay your bread and your wine upon the burial of a just man: and do not eat and drink from it with sinners. Always seek counsel from a wise man. Bless God at all times: and ask of him that your ways may be directed: and that all your counsels may abide in him. I tell you also, my son, that I gave ten talents of silver to Gabael at Rages, a city of the Medes, when I was but a boy: and I have a note of his hand with me. Inquire therefore how you may go to him and receive from him the aforesaid sum of money: and restore to him his note. Fear not, my son: we lead a poor life indeed: but we shall have many good things if we fear God: and depart from all sin: and do that which is good. Chapter 5.
Then Tobias answered his father and said: All things whatsoever you have commanded me, I will do, father. But how I shall recover this money I do not know. He knows not me: I know not him. I will give him no token: and I have never known the road by which to go there. Then his father answered him and said:

I have a note of his hand indeed with me: which when you shall show him, he will straightway pay. But go now and find some fit man to accompany you for your wages: that you may receive it while I still live: and bring it back to me. Then Tobias going out found a young man standing, girded and ready, as it were prepared to walk. And not knowing that he was an angel of God, he saluted him, and said: From where are you, good young man? And he answered: From the children of Israel. And Tobias said to him: Do you know the way that leads to the country of the Medes? And he answered: I know it: and I have often traveled all the roads through it: and I have stayed with Gabael our brother who lives at Rages, a city of the Medes, which is situated on the mountain of Ecbatana. And Tobias said to him: Wait for me, I beseech you: until I tell these things to my father. Then Tobias going in told all these things to his father. At which his father, wondering, requested that he would come in to him. And going in he saluted him and said: Joy be to you always. And Tobias said: What joy can be to me, who sit in darkness and see not the light of heaven? The young man said to him: Be of good courage: your cure from God is at hand. Then Tobias said to him: Can you bring my son to Gabael at Rages, a city of the Medes? And when you return I will pay you your wages. And the angel said to him: I will lead him and bring him back to you. And Tobias said to him: I beg you: tell me: of what family or what tribe are you? And the angel Raphael said to him: Do you seek the family of one hired to serve, or the hired servant himself who will go with your son? But lest I give you concern: I am Azarias, the son of the great Ananias. And Tobias answered: You are of a great family. But do not be angry that I wished

. Tobias .

to know your family. And the angel said to him: I will lead him safely, and safely return your son to you. And Tobias answered and said: Go in peace, and may the Lord be with you on your journey, and may His angel accompany you. Then, when everything that was to be carried on the road was prepared, Tobias said farewell to his father and his mother, and both went off together. And when they had set out, his mother began to weep and say: You have taken away the staff of our old age, and sent him from us. Would that the money had never existed, for which you sent him. Our poverty was sufficient for us, since we counted it as riches that we saw our son. And Tobias said to her: Do not weep. Our son will arrive safely, and return to us safely, and your eyes shall see him. For I believe that the good angel of God accompanies him, and will direct everything that happens around him well, so that he returns to us with joy. At these words his mother stopped weeping and was silent. Chapter 6.

So Tobias set out, and the dog followed him, and he stayed at the first lodging by the river Tigris. And he went out to wash his feet, and behold, a huge fish came up to devour him. Tobias, in fear, cried out with a loud voice saying: Lord, it attacks me! And the angel said to him: Take it by the gill and draw it to you. And when he had done so, he pulled it onto dry land, and it began to thrash before his feet. Then the angel said to him: Gut this fish, and take its heart, gall, and liver, and set them aside for yourself. For these things are useful and necessary for medicines. When he had done so, he roasted the flesh of the fish, and they carried it with them on the road; the rest they salted, enough to last until they arrived at the city of Rages of the Medes. Then Tobias questioned

the angel and said to him: I beg you, Azarias brother, tell me what remedy these things which you told me to keep from the fish will provide. And the angel answered and said to him: If you place a portion of its heart upon coals, its smoke will drive away every kind of demon, whether from man or from woman, so that it will no longer approach them. And Tobias said to him: Where do you wish us to stay? And the angel answered: Here is a man named Raguel, a close relative of your tribe, and he has a daughter named Sara; but he has no other son or daughter besides her. All his substance is owed to you, and you ought to take her as your wife. Ask her of her father, and he will give her to you as a wife. Then Tobias answered and said: I have heard that she has been given to seven husbands, and they all died; but I have also heard that a demon killed them. I fear therefore lest the same happen to me, and since I am the only child of my parents, I should bring their old age down to the grave in sorrow. And the angel Raphael said to him: Listen to me, and I will show you who those are over whom the demon has power. Those who receive marriage in such a way that they shut out God from themselves and from their minds, and give themselves over to their lust like the horse and mule which have no understanding — over them the demon has power. But when you have received her, go into the bedroom and for three days keep yourself continent from her, and devote yourselves to nothing but prayers. On that night, burn the liver of the fish, and the demon will be driven away. On the second night, you will be admitted into the company of the holy patriarchs. On the third night, you will obtain a blessing, that healthy children may be born to you. And when the third night has passed, you will take the virgin with

driven by fear of the Lord and love of children rather than by lust, that in the seed of Abraham you may obtain a blessing upon your children. Chapter 7.
They came therefore to Raguel, and Raguel received them with joy. And Raguel looked at Tobias, and said to Anna his wife: How like is this young man to my cousin! And when he had said this, he asked them: Where are you from, young men, our brothers? And they said: We are of the tribe of Naphtali, captives in Nineveh. And Raguel said to them: Do you know Tobias my brother? And they said: We know him. And when he was speaking many good things about him, the angel said to Raguel: Tobias, of whom you inquire, is the father of this young man. And Raguel sprang up and kissed him with tears and wept upon his neck, and said: A blessing be upon you, my son, for you are the son of a good and virtuous man. And Anna his wife and Sara their daughter wept. And after they had spoken, Raguel commanded a ram to be killed and a supper to be prepared. And when he urged them to sit down to eat, Tobias said: I will not eat nor drink here today unless you first grant my request and promise to give me Sara your daughter. When Raguel heard this he was afraid, knowing what had happened to the seven men who had gone in to her, and he began to fear lest the same might happen to this one also. And when he hesitated and gave no answer to the request, the angel said to him: Do not be afraid to give her to this man, for to him who fears God is your daughter's due, and therefore another could not have her. Then Raguel said: I have no doubt that God has accepted my tears and prayers. And I believe that therefore he has made you come to me, so that she might be joined to one of her own kindred according to the law of Moses. Now do not doubt that I will give her to you. And taking the right hand of his daughter, he placed it in the right hand of Tobias, saying: The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob be with you, and may he join you together and fulfill his blessing in you. And taking a document they made a record of the marriage. And after this they feasted and blessed God. And Raguel called his wife Anna and told her to prepare another room, and she brought Sara in there, and she wept. And he said to her: Be of good courage, my daughter. The Lord of heaven give you joy instead of the grief you have suffered. Chapter 8.
After they had supped they brought the young man in to her. And Tobias, remembering the words of the angel, took out of his bag a part of the liver and laid it on the burning coals. Then the angel Raphael seized the demon and bound him in the desert of upper Egypt. Then Tobias exhorted the virgin and said to her: Sara, arise and let us pray to God today and tomorrow and the day after tomorrow, for during these three nights we are joined to God, and when the third night is past we shall be in our own marriage. For we are children of the saints, and we must not be joined together like the heathens who do not know God. And they both arose and prayed earnestly together that health might be given to them. And Tobias said: Lord God of our fathers, may the heavens and the earth and the seas and the springs and the rivers and all your creatures that are in them bless you. You made Adam from the slime of the earth and gave him Eve as a helper. And now, Lord, you know that it is not for lust that I take my sister as my wife, but only for the love of posterity in which your name may be blessed forever and ever. And Sara said: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us, and let us grow old together

· Tobias ·

likewise rejoiced. And it came to pass that about the time of the crowing of the cocks, Raguel ordered his servants to go with him and dig a grave. For he said, lest what happened to the other seven men who had gone in to her should happen to him as well. When they had prepared the grave, Raguel returned to his wife and said to her: Send one of the maids to see if he is dead, so that I may bury him before it grows light. So she sent one of her handmaids, who went into the chamber and found them both safe and sound, sleeping together. The maid returned and brought the good news. And Raguel and his wife Anna blessed God, saying: We bless you, O Lord God of Israel, because it has not happened to us as we feared. For you have shown us your mercy and shut out from us our enemy who persecuted us. You have had mercy on two only children. Make them, O Lord, give you fuller blessings, and offer to you the sacrifice of your praise and of their health, that all nations may know that you alone are God in all the earth. And straightway Raguel commanded his servants to fill up the grave they had dug before it was light. And he told his wife to make ready a feast, and prepare everything that travelers needed for the journey. He also had two fat cows and four rams killed, and ordered a banquet prepared for all his neighbors and friends. And Raguel adjured Tobias to stay with him for two weeks. Of all that he possessed, Raguel gave half to Tobias, and drew up a document stating that the remaining half should come to Tobias after Raguel's death. Chapter IX.
Then Tobias called the angel to him, whom he thought to be a man, and said to him: Brother Azarias, I beg you to hear my words. Even if I gave myself to you as a servant, I would not be worthy of your care. Yet I beseech you to take animals or servants and go to Gabael in Rages, a city of the Medes, return to him his note, and receive from him the money, and ask him to come to my wedding. For my father counts the days, and if I delay one day more, his soul will be very sorrowful. And surely you see how Raguel has adjured me, whose oath I cannot despise. Then Raphael, taking four of Raguel's servants and two camels, went to Rages the city of the Medes. Finding Gabael, he gave him the note, and received all the money. And he told him everything concerning Tobias, son of Tobit, and asked him to come with him to the wedding. When he entered Raguel's house, he found Tobias at table, and they leapt up and kissed each other. And Gabael wept and blessed God, saying: May the God of Israel bless you, for you are the son of a very good and just man, one who fears God and gives alms. And may a blessing be said over your wife and over your parents, and may you see your children and your children's children to the third and fourth generation, and may your seed be blessed by the God of Israel, who reigns forever and ever. When all said amen, they went to the feast, and they celebrated the wedding banquet with the fear of the Lord. Chapter X.
Now when Tobias delayed on account of the wedding, his father Tobit was worried and said: Why do you think my son delays, or why is he detained there? Do you think Gabael is dead

.Tobias.

and no one returned the money to him. And he began to be very sad, both he and Anna his wife; and they both wept together, because on the appointed day their son did not return to them. His mother wept with unceasing tears, and said: "Woe is me, my son, why did we send you away, the light of our eyes, the staff of our old age, the comfort of our life, the hope of our posterity — having all things at once in you alone, we should not have let you go from us." To her Tobias said: "Be quiet and do not be troubled; our son is safe, and the man with whom we sent him is trustworthy enough." But she could in no way be comforted, but daily ran out and looked around, going about all the roads by which there seemed to be hope of his return, so that she might see him coming from afar if possible. Meanwhile Raguel said to his son-in-law: "Stay here, and I will send a messenger of good news about you to Tobit your father." But Tobias said to him: "I know that my father and my mother are counting the days, and their spirits are failing within them." So when Raguel had urged Tobias much with many words, and he would in no way listen to him, he handed over to him Sara and half of all his substance — male servants, maidservants, cattle, camels, cows, and a great sum of money — and sent him away safe and joyful, saying: "May the holy angel of the Lord be on your journey, and bring you through safe, and may you find all things well with your parents, and may my eyes see your children before I die." And the parents took their daughter, kissed her, and let her go, admonishing her to honor her parents-in-law, to love her husband, to govern the household, to manage the home, and to show herself irreproachable. r. xl

And as they were returning, they came to Charra, which is in the middle of the journey toward Nineveh, on the eleventh day. And the angel said: "Brother Tobias, you know how you left your father. If it pleases you, let us go ahead, and let the family follow at a leisurely pace with your wife and the animals." And when this plan pleased them so that they should go, Raphael said to Tobias: "Take with you some of the gall of the fish, for it will be necessary." And Tobias took some of that gall and they departed. Now Anna sat daily by the road on the brow of a hill, from which she could look far away. And while she was watching from that same place for his coming, she saw him from afar and immediately recognized her son coming; and she ran and told her husband, saying: "Behold, your son is coming!" And Raphael said to Tobias: "When you enter your house, immediately worship the Lord your God, and giving thanks to him, go to your father and kiss him. Then straightway anoint his eyes with this gall of the fish which you carry with you. For know that his eyes shall presently be opened, and your father shall see the light, and shall rejoice at the sight of you." Then the dog, which had been with them on the journey, ran ahead, and coming as if bringing news, showed his joy by wagging his tail. And Tobit, his father, rising up, began to run stumbling with his feet; and giving his hand to a servant, he went to meet his son. And he received him and kissed him with his wife, and they both began to weep for joy. And when they had worshipped God and given thanks, they sat down together. Then Tobias, taking the gall of the fish, anointed his father's eyes. And he waited about half an hour, and a film began to come from his eyes like the membrane of an egg. And Tobias took hold of it and pulled it from his eyes, and immediately his sight was restored.

· Tobias ·

He received it. And they glorified God — he himself and his wife, and all who knew him. And Tobias said: "I bless you, O Lord God of Israel, because you have chastised me and you have saved me." And behold, I see my son Tobias. Sara also, the wife of his son, came in after seven days, with all the family and the cattle safe, and the camels, and much money of his wife; and also the money which he had received from Gabael. And he told his parents all the benefits of God, which he had done to him by the man who had led him. And Achior and Nabath, cousins of Tobias, came rejoicing to Tobias, and congratulating him for all the good things which God had shown concerning him. And for seven days they feasted with him with great joy.

Chapter 12.
Then Tobias called to him his son and said to him: "What can we give to this holy man who has come with you?" Tobias answered his father and said: "Father, what reward shall we give him? Or what can be worthy of his benefits? He led me and brought me back safe; he received the money from Gabael; he caused me to have my wife; and he drove the demon away from her; he gave joy to her parents; he saved me from being devoured by the fish; he made you see the light of heaven; and through him we have been filled with all good things. What can we give him worthy of these things? But I ask you, father, to ask him if perhaps he will deign to accept half of all the things that have been brought." And calling him, both the father and the son together, they took him aside and began to ask him to be pleased to accept half of all things they had brought.

Then he said to them privately: "Bless the God of heaven, and before all the living confess to him, because he has shown his mercy to you. For it is good to hide the secret of a king, but it is honorable to reveal and confess the works of God. Prayer is good with fasting and almsgiving, more than to lay up treasures of gold; for almsgiving delivers from death, and it is that which purges away sins and makes one find eternal life. But those who commit sin and iniquity are enemies to their own soul. I will therefore show you the truth, and I will not hide the secret word from you. When you prayed with tears, and buried the dead, and left your dinner, and hid the dead by day in your house and buried them by night, I offered your prayer to the Lord. And because you were acceptable to God, it was necessary that temptation should prove you. And now the Lord has sent me to heal you, and to deliver Sara, your son's wife, from the devil. For I am the angel Raphael, one of the seven who stand before the Lord. And when they had heard these things, they were troubled and being seized with fear they fell upon the ground on their faces. And the angel said to them: "Peace be to you; fear not. For when I was with you, I was there by the will of God; bless him and sing praises to him. I seemed indeed to eat and drink with you; but I use an invisible meat and drink, which cannot be seen by men. It is time therefore that I return to him who sent me; but bless God and publish all his wondrous works." And when he had said these things, he was taken from their sight, and they could see him no more. Then they lying prostrate for three hours upon their faces, blessed God; and rising up, they told all his wonderful works.

Chapter 14.
Then Tobias the elder opening his mouth, blessed the Lord and said:

· Tobias ·

You are great, O Lord, forever, and your kingdom endures for all ages; for you both scourge and save; you lead down to the underworld and bring back again, and there is no one who can escape your hand. Give thanks to the Lord, O children of Israel, and praise him before the nations, because he has scattered you among them who did not know him, so that you might declare his wonderful works and make them know that there is no other God all-powerful but he. He has chastised us for our iniquities, and he will save us for his mercy. Look then at what he has done with you, and with fear and trembling give him thanks; exalt the King of ages in your works. As for me, in the land of my captivity I will give him thanks, because he has shown his majesty toward a sinful nation. Therefore be converted, O sinners, and do justice before God, believing that he will show his mercy to you. As for me and my soul, we will rejoice in him. Bless the Lord, all his elect, and celebrate days of joy and give thanks to him. O Jerusalem, city of God, the Lord has chastised you for the works of your hands. Give thanks to the Lord for your good things, and bless the God of ages, so that he may rebuild his tabernacle in you, and call back to you all the captives, and you may rejoice for all ages of ages. You will shine with a glorious light, and all the ends of the earth will worship you. Nations from afar will come to you, and bearing gifts will adore the Lord in you, and will hold your land as holy. They will call upon his great name in you. Cursed will be all who despise you, and condemned will be all who blaspheme you; blessed will be all who build you up. But you will rejoice in your children, because they will all be blessed and gathered together to the Lord. Blessed are all who love you and who rejoice in your peace.

My soul, bless the Lord, because he has delivered Jerusalem, his city. Blessed if there remain survivors of my seed to see the glory of Jerusalem. The gates of Jerusalem will be built with sapphire and emerald, and all its walls with precious stone; the towers of Jerusalem will be built with gold, and their battlements with pure gold. The streets of Jerusalem will be paved with white and pure stone, and Alleluia will be sung through its lanes. Blessed be the Lord who has exalted it, and may his kingdom be over it forever and ever. Amen. Chapter 14.

And so the words of Tobias were ended. And after Tobias was restored to his sight, he lived forty-two years, and saw the children of his grandchildren. And when he had completed one hundred and two years, he was buried honorably in Nineveh. For fifty-six years he lost the sight of his eyes, and after that he recovered it. The rest of his life was in joy, and with good advancement in the fear of God he departed in peace. And at the hour of his death he called to him his son Tobias, and his seven sons, the children of his grandchildren, and said to them: The destruction of Nineveh is at hand. For the word of the Lord will not fail, and our brothers who are scattered from the land of Israel will return to it. All its deserted land will be repopulated, and the house of God which was burned there will be rebuilt again, and all who fear God will return there. And the nations will leave their idols and come to Jerusalem, and will dwell in it, and all the kings of the earth will rejoice in it, adoring the King of Israel. Hear therefore, my children, your father. Serve the Lord in truth, and seek to do what pleases him. And command your children to do justice and almsgiving, that they may be mindful of God and bless him at all times in truth and with their whole

· Judith ·

In his own strength. Now therefore, my children, hear me: and do not remain here. But on whatever day you bury your mother, go from her grave and direct your steps so that you may leave this place. For I see that her iniquity will bring her to an end. And it came to pass that after the death of his mother, Tobias left Nineveh with his wife and children and his son, and returned to his father-in-law. He found them both in good health in their old age, and he cared for them. And he closed their eyes, and he received all the inheritance of the house of Raguel, and he saw the fifth generation of his children and his children's children. And having completed ninety-nine years in the fear of the Lord, he was buried with joy. And all his kindred and all his generation lived in good life and in holy conversation at the end, so that they were acceptable both to God and to men, and to all who dwelt on the earth. Here ends the book of Tobias. Here begins the prologue to the book of Judith.

Among the Hebrews, the book of Judith is read among the Hagiographa, whose authority is considered less suitable for confirming matters that come into dispute. It is reckoned among the histories, written in the Chaldean tongue. But we have reckoned this book among the holy scriptures, following the judgment of those men — indeed their authority — and occupied with the works that pressed upon me most urgently; I have produced this edition translating more by sense than word for word from the Chaldean. I found a most corrupt variety among many manuscripts: I have expressed in Latin only what I could recover with the meaning intact from the Chaldean words. Receive Judith, a widow and example of chastity, and celebrate her with the praises of triumph proclaimed before her,

declaring it abroad with praises. For He gave this not only as an example for women but also for men, for the rewarder of her chastity granted her such virtue that she conquered the unconquerable among all men and surpassed the unsurpassable.
Here begins the book of Judith. Chapter the first.

Arphaxad, king of the Medes, had therefore subjugated many peoples under his rule, and he himself built a most powerful city which he called Ecbatana. And he made its walls of squared stones, seventy cubits high and thirty cubits wide; and he set its towers at a height of one hundred cubits. On each of its four sides they extended twenty feet in breadth, and he set its gates at the height of the towers. And he gloried as though mighty in the power of his army and in the glory of his chariots. Now in the twelfth year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Assyrians, who reigned in the great city of Nineveh, made war against Arphaxad, and defeated him in the great plain which is called Ragau, near the Euphrates and the Tigris and the Yadason in the plain of Erioch, king of the Elicians. Then the kingdom of Nebuchadnezzar was exalted and his heart was lifted up. And he sent to all who dwelt in Cilicia and Damascus and Lebanon, and to the nations that are in Carmel and Cedar and the inhabitants of Galilee in the great plain of Esdraelon, and to all who were in Samaria and beyond the river Jordan as far as Jerusalem, and all the land of Jesse, as far as the mountains of Ethiopia. To all these Nebuchadnezzar king of the Assyrians sent messengers; but they all with one mind refused him and sent his messengers back empty and without honor.

Judith.

They had cast away. Then Nebuchadnezzar, king, enraged against all that land, swore by his kingdom and his throne that he would avenge himself for all these things. Chapter II.

In the thirteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar the king, on the twenty-second day of the first month, the word came in the house of Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Assyrians, that he should take revenge. And he called all his elders and all the commanders of his warriors, and he shared with them the secret counsel of his mind. And he declared that his thought was to bring all the earth under his rule. When this speech pleased everyone, Nebuchadnezzar the king called Holofernes, the chief general of his army, and said to him: Go out against all the kingdoms of the west, and especially against those who have despised my authority. Your eye shall spare no kingdom, and every fortified city you shall subdue for me. Then Holofernes called together the officers and commanders of the military strength of the Assyrians, and he mustered fighting men on foot, two hundred and twenty thousand, and twelve thousand mounted archers. And he caused all his expedition to advance before him with an innumerable multitude of camels, with supplies sufficient for the armies in abundance, and herds of oxen and flocks of sheep beyond counting. He arranged for grain to be prepared along all his route. He took also very much gold and silver from the king's house. And he set out, he and all the army, with chariots and horsemen and archers, who covered the face of the earth like locusts. When he had passed through the borders of Assyria, he came to the great mountains of Ange, which are on the left side of Cilicia, and he scaled all their fortresses and overcame all their defenses. He broke through the most renowned city,

and plundered all the sons of Tharsis and the sons of Ishmael who were opposite the desert, and to the south of the land of Cellon. And he crossed the Euphrates and came into Mesopotamia, and he broke down all the high cities that were there, from the stream of Mambre until one comes to the sea; and he seized its boundaries from Cilicia as far as the borders of Japheth, which are toward the south. And he brought away all the sons of Midian and plundered all their wealth, and all who resisted him he slew with the edge of the sword. And after these things he went down into the plains of Damascus in the days of harvest, and he burned all their fields and caused all their trees and their vineyards to be cut down, and the fear of him fell upon all the inhabitants of the land. Chapter III.

Then the kings and rulers of all the cities and provinces — of Syria, that is, and Mesopotamia, and Syria Sobal, and Libya, and Cilicia — sent their ambassadors to Holofernes, saying: Let your indignation toward us cease. For it is better that we live and serve Nebuchadnezzar the great king and be subject to you, than that we die and by our own destruction suffer the losses of servitude. All our cities and all our possessions, all the hills and mountains and plains, the herds of oxen and flocks of sheep and the horses and camels and all our wealth and the households of our families are before your sight. Let all things be under your law. We and our children are your servants. Come to us as a peaceful lord and use our service as it shall please you. Then he came down from the mountains with a great force of horsemen and gained possession of every city and every inhabitant of the land. And from all the cities he took for himself strong and able men for war. And such a great terror

Judith.

Who is the king of their army? Why, above all peoples who dwell in the east, have they scorned me, and not come out to meet us to receive us in peace? Then Achior, the leader of all the sons of Ammon, answered and said: If you deign to hear, my lord, I will speak the truth in your presence concerning this people who dwell in the mountains, and no false word shall come from my mouth. This people is of Chaldean descent. They first dwelt in Mesopotamia, because they were unwilling to follow the gods of their fathers who were in the land of the Chaldeans. Departing from the religious customs of their fathers, which involved a multitude of gods, they worshipped one God of heaven, who commanded them to leave that place and to dwell in the land of Canaan. When a famine spread over all the land, they went down to Egypt, where, for four hundred years, they multiplied so greatly that their army could not be counted. When the king of Egypt oppressed them, putting them to work making bricks for his cities, they cried out to their Lord, and he struck the whole land of Egypt with various plagues. When the Egyptians drove them out, and the plague ceased from them, and they wanted to recapture them and bring them back to their service, the God of heaven opened the sea before those who fled, so that on both sides the waters stood firm like walls, and these people walked on dry ground through the bottom of the sea. When an innumerable host of Egyptians pursued them, they were so covered by the waters that not one remained to tell what had happened to future generations. After leaving the Red Sea, they wandered through the desert of Sinai, where no man had ever been able to live, nor could the son of man dwell. There bitter springs were made sweet for them to drink, and for forty years

they received their food from heaven. Wherever they went, without bow and arrow, without shield and sword, their God fought for them and prevailed. And there was no one who could triumph over this people, except when they departed from the worship of the Lord their God. But as often as they worshipped any god other than their own, they were given over to plunder, to the sword, and to shame. And as often as they repented of having departed from the worship of their God, the God of heaven gave them strength to resist. Thus they overthrew the king of Canaan, and the Jebusites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, the Hittites, and the Amorites, and all the powerful men of Heshbon; and they took possession of their lands and their cities. And as long as they did not sin in the sight of their God, all went well with them, for their God hates iniquity. For even in the years before this, when they had departed from the way that God had given them to walk in, they were destroyed in battles by many nations, and many of them were led away captive into a foreign land. But recently they have returned to the Lord their God, gathering from the dispersion in which they had been scattered; and they have come up into all these mountains and possess Jerusalem again, where their sanctuary is. Now therefore, my lord, inquire whether there is any iniquity of this people before their God: then we can go up against them, because their God will surely deliver them into your hand, and they will be brought under the yoke of your power. But if there is no offense of this people before their God, we cannot resist them, because their God will defend them, and we shall be a reproach to all the earth. And it came to pass, when Achior had ceased speaking these words, that all the nobles of Holofernes were angry, and they intended to kill him, saying to one another: Who is this man who says that the sons of Israel can resist king Nebuchadnezzar and his armies, men who

Judith.

unarmed and without courage, and without skill in the art of war? So that Achior may know that he deceives us — we shall go up into the mountains, and when their strongest men have fallen, then he himself shall be cut down with the same sword along with them; so that all nations may know that Nabuchodonosor is the god of the earth, and there is no other besides him. Chapter 6.
And it came to pass, when they had ceased speaking, that Holofernes, greatly enraged, said to Achior: Because you have prophesied to us, saying that the people of Israel are defended by their God — to show you that there is no god but Nabuchodonosor: when we shall have slain them all as one man, then you also shall die with them by the sword of the Assyrians, and all Israel shall perish with them in ruin; and you shall know that Nabuchodonosor is lord of the whole earth. Then the sword of my army shall pass through your sides, and you shall fall pierced among the wounded of Israel, and you shall breathe no more until you are destroyed with them. But if you believe your prophecy to be true, let not your countenance fall, nor let the pallor that has covered your face depart from you — if you think these words of mine cannot be fulfilled. But so that you may know that you shall share their fate at the same time — behold, from this hour you shall be counted among them, so that when they have received the worthy punishment of my sword, you also shall undergo the same vengeance. Then Holofernes commanded his servants to take Achior and lead him to Bethulia, and deliver him into the hands of the children of Israel. And his servants, taking him, went through the plain; but when they drew near to the mountains, the slingers came out against them. Then they turned aside from the side of the mountain, and bound Achior to a tree by his hands and feet; and having bound him with cords they left him there, and returned to their lord.

Now the children of Israel, coming down from Bethulia, came to him. And loosing him, they brought him to Bethulia, and set him in the midst of the people, asking him what had happened, and why the Assyrians had left him bound. In those days the rulers there were Ozias the son of Micha, of the tribe of Simeon, and Charmi who is also called Gothoniel. In the midst of the elders, and in the sight of all, Achior told everything he had said — how he had been questioned by Holofernes, and how, because of those words, Holofernes had wished to put him to death; and how Holofernes, angered for this reason, had handed him over so that the Lord would conquer the children of Israel — because he had said that God of heaven was their defender. Then when Achior had related all these things, all the people fell upon their faces adoring the Lord, and with common lamentation and one voice they poured out their prayers to the Lord, saying: O Lord, God of heaven and earth, behold their pride, and look upon our lowliness, and regard the face of your holy ones; and show that you do not forsake those who trust in you, and that you humble those who presume in themselves, and who glory in their own strength. When the weeping was finished, and the people's prayer throughout the day was completed, they consoled Achior, saying: The God of our fathers, whose power you have proclaimed, shall himself repay you this reward, that you may rather see their destruction. And when the Lord our God shall give this freedom to his servants, let God be also with you in our midst, as it has pleased him, so that with all of us he may deal well with you. Then Ozias, when the council was ended, received him into his house, and made a great supper. And calling all the elders together, they refreshed themselves when the fast was ended. And afterward

Judith.

All the people were called together and prayed through the whole night within the church, seeking help from the God of Israel. Chapter 7.
But Holofernes on the next day commanded his armies to go up against Bethulia. His foot soldiers numbered one hundred and twenty thousand, and his cavalry twenty-two thousand, besides the contingents of those men he had taken captive, and who had been brought from the princes and the cities of all the youth. All prepared themselves together for battle against the children of Israel, and they came through the pass of the mountain up to the summit that looks over Dothaim, from the place called Belmaul to Chelmon, which is opposite Esdraelon. The children of Israel, when they saw the great multitude, prostrated themselves upon the ground, putting ashes upon their heads, praying with one accord that God would show his mercy upon his people. Then taking up their weapons of war, they positioned themselves at the narrow passes of the roads which wind through the mountains, and kept watch over them all day and night. But Holofernes, while circling around, discovered that the spring which supplied their aqueduct flowed from the south outside the city, and he ordered the aqueduct to be cut off. Nevertheless there were springs not far from the walls, from which they were seen to secretly draw water, more for refreshment than for drinking. But the sons of Ammon and Moab came to Holofernes saying: The sons of Israel cannot be overcome by spear or arrow; the mountains defend them, and the steep hills fortify them. Therefore, that you may overcome them without engaging in battle, set guards at the springs so that they cannot draw water from them, and you will slay them without a sword, or else, worn out, they will surrender their city, which they think cannot be taken because it is situated in the mountains.

These words pleased Holofernes and his officers, and he stationed a hundred men around each spring. When this watch had continued for twenty days, the cisterns and all water supplies failed all the inhabitants of Bethulia, so that there was not enough within the city to satisfy even one person for a single day, for water was being rationed to them daily. Then all the men, women, young people, and children gathered before Ozias, and with one voice they cried out: Let God judge between us and you, for you have done us evil by refusing to make peace with the Assyrians; and because of this, God has sold us into their hands. There is now no one to help us, while we perish before their eyes through thirst and utter ruin. Now call together all who are in the city, that we may willingly surrender to the forces of Holofernes. It is better for us to be taken captive and yet bless the living Lord, than to die and be a reproach to all mankind, when we see our wives and children dying before our eyes. We call today heaven and earth and the God of our fathers to witness, who takes vengeance upon us according to our sins: deliver now the city into the hands of Holofernes' army, that our end may be swift by the sword rather than drawn out by the agony of thirst. When they had said these things, there was great weeping and lamentation throughout the whole congregation, and for many hours they cried out with one voice to God, saying: We have sinned with our fathers; we have acted unjustly; we have committed iniquity. Since you are merciful, have pity on us; punish our sins with your own chastisement, but do not deliver those who trust in you into the hands of those who do not know you, lest they say among the nations:

· Judith ·

Where is their God? And when they had grown weary and exhausted by these outcries and lamentations, Ozias arose, his face wet with tears, and said: "Take heart, brothers; let us wait these five more days for the mercy of the Lord. Perhaps He will restrain His indignation and give glory to His own name. But if after five days no help has come, we will do what you have said." Chapter VIII.

Now it came to pass, when Judith, a widow, heard these words — she was the daughter of Merari, son of Ydoe, son of Joseph, son of Ozia, son of Elai, son of Iamnoz, son of Gedeon, son of Rafoim, son of Achirob, son of Melchie, son of Enam, son of Nathanie, son of Salathiel, son of Symeon, son of Ruben — and her husband had been Manasses, who died during the barley harvest: for while he stood supervising the binding of sheaves in the field, the heat came upon his head and he died in Bethulia his own city, and was buried there with his ancestors. Judith had remained as his widow for three years and some months. She had made for herself a private room in the upper part of the house, where she stayed shut in with her maids; she wore sackcloth about her loins and fasted all the days of her life, except the Sabbaths and new moons and the feasts of the house of Israel. She was very beautiful in appearance, and her husband had left her great riches and a numerous household, and herds of cattle and flocks of sheep. She was highly regarded by all, for she feared the Lord greatly, and there was no one who spoke an ill word about her. When she heard, therefore, that Ozias had promised that he would surrender the city to the Assyrians after five days, she sent for the elders Chabri and Charmi. And they came to her, and she said to them: "What is this word

by which Ozias has consented to hand over the city to the Assyrians, if within five days no help comes to you? Who are you to put the Lord to the test? This is not a word that calls forth mercy, but rather one that provokes wrath and kindles fury. You have set a time limit for the mercies of the Lord, and you have appointed a day for Him according to your own pleasure. But since the Lord is patient, let us repent in this very matter and with tears beg His indulgence. For God does not threaten as a man does, nor will He be inflamed with anger as the son of man. Therefore let us humble our souls before Him, and serving Him in a contrite spirit, let us say weeping to the Lord, that according to His will He may deal mercifully with us; that just as our hearts were troubled by their pride, so also we may glory in our own humility, because we have not followed the sins of our ancestors who forsook their God and worshipped foreign gods — for which crime they were given over to the sword, to plunder, and to shame before their enemies. But we know no other God but Him. Let us hope humbly for His consolation, and He will require our blood from the afflictions of our enemies, and He will humble all the nations that rise up against us, and He will bring them to dishonor — the Lord our God. And now, brothers, since you are elders among the people, and the souls of them all depend upon you, lift up their hearts by your words, so that they may be mindful that our ancestors were tested, in order to prove whether they truly worshipped their God. They ought to remember how our father Abraham was put to the test, and through many tribulations was proven and made the friend of God. So too Isaac, so too Jacob, so too Moses, and

Judith

All those who pleased God passed through many tribulations as faithful ones. But those who did not endure temptations with fear of the Lord and in patience, and who brought forth their own murmurings for a long time, were destroyed by the destroyer and perished by serpents. Let us therefore not take vengeance for ourselves on account of what we suffer, but counting these very punishments as lesser than our sins, let us believe that these scourges of the Lord have come upon us as upon servants who are being corrected for amendment, not for destruction. And Ozias and the elders said to her: All that you have spoken is true, and there is nothing to be found fault with in your words. Now therefore pray for us, since you are a holy woman and one fearing the Lord. And Judith said to them: As you know what I have proposed to speak, so what I have resolved to do, pray that God may make firm my plan. Stand at the gate this night, and I will go out with my handmaid, and pray that within the five days as you have said, the Lord may look upon his people Israel. But do not inquire into my act until I bring you word. And Ozias the prince of Judah said to her: Go in peace, and may the Lord be with you to take vengeance on our enemies. And returning, they went away. Chapter V.
When they had departed, Judith entered her oratory, and putting on haircloth, she placed ashes on her head, and prostrating herself before the Lord, she cried out to the Lord saying: O Lord God of my father Simeon, who gave him a sword to take revenge on the strangers who had loosened the belt of a virgin to her confusion, and uncovered her thigh to her shame, and polluted her womb, and you gave their wives as prey and their daughters into captivity, and all their spoils to be divided among your servants who were zealous for your honor: help me, I beseech you, O Lord my God, a widow. For you did the things of old, and devised one thing after another, and what you willed came to pass. For all your ways are prepared, and in your providence you have placed your judgments. Look upon the camp of the Assyrians now, as you deigned to look upon the camp of the Egyptians, when they pursued armed after your servants, trusting in their chariots and in their horsemen and in a multitude of warriors. But you looked upon their camp, and darkness wearied them. The deep held their feet fast, and the waters covered them. So may it be with these also, O Lord, who trust in their multitude and in their chariots and in their pikes and in their arrows and glory in their lances, and do not know that you yourself are our God who crushes wars from the beginning, and the Lord is your name. Lift up your arm as from the beginning, and cast down their power by your power. Let their power fall in your wrath, who promise themselves to violate your sanctuary and to defile the tabernacle of your name and to cast down with the sword the horn of your altar. Bring it to pass, O Lord, that his pride may be cut off with his own sword. Let him be caught in the net of his own eyes in my regard, and strike him by the graces of my lips. Give me constancy in my mind that I may despise him, and courage that I may overthrow him. For this will be a glorious monument to your name, when he falls by the hand of a woman. For your strength, O Lord, is not in numbers, nor is your pleasure in the strength of horses, nor from the beginning have the proud been acceptable to you. But the prayer of the humble and the meek has always pleased you. O God of the heavens, creator of the waters, and Lord of the whole creation, hear me a wretched woman, praying to you and trusting in your mercy.

· Judith ·

Remember, O Lord, your covenant, and put a word in my mouth and strengthen the counsel of my heart, so that your house may remain in your sanctification, and all nations may know that you are God and there is no other besides you. Chapter 10.

And it came to pass that when she had ceased crying out to the Lord, she rose from the place where she had lain prostrate before the Lord. And she called her maid Abra, and going down into her house she put off her sackcloth, and laid aside the garments of her widowhood, and she washed her body, and anointed herself with rich ointment, and dressed her hair, and put a tiara upon her head, and clothed herself with the garments of her gladness. And she put sandals on her feet, and took her bracelets and lilies and earrings and rings, and adorned herself with all her ornaments. And the Lord also gave her more beauty, because all this dressing up was not for lust but for virtue, and therefore the Lord increased her beauty so that she appeared incomparable in the eyes of all. She then gave to her maid a bottle of wine and a vessel of oil, and parched grain and dried figs and bread and cheese, and went on her way. And when they came to the gate of the city, they found Uzziah waiting there, with the elders of the city. And when they saw her, they were astonished with great wonder at her beauty. Yet they asked her nothing, but let her pass, saying: The God of our fathers give you grace and strengthen all the counsel of your heart with his power, and let Jerusalem glory in you, and your name be in the number of the holy and just. And all who were there answered with one voice: So be it, so be it. And Judith praying to the Lord, passed through the gates, she and her maid. And it came to pass, when she came down the mountain about the break of day, that the Assyrian scouts met her and stopped her, saying: Where do you come from, and where are you going? She answered: I am a daughter of the Hebrews, and I have fled from them because I knew that they were about to be given to you as prey, since they despised you and would not deliver themselves up, so that they might find mercy in your sight. For this reason I thought to myself: I will go to the presence of the prince Holofernes, to reveal to him their secrets, and to show him by what approach he can overcome them, so that not a man of his army shall fall. And when the men heard her words, they regarded her face, and their eyes were astonished, for they marveled greatly at her beauty. And they said to her: You have saved your life by your good sense in coming down thus to our lord. Know that when you stand before him, he will treat you well and you will be most pleasing to his heart. And they led her to the tent of Holofernes, announcing her arrival. And when she had come before his face, Holofernes was immediately captivated by his eyes upon her. And his attendants said to him: Who could despise the people of the Hebrews, who have such beautiful women? Is it not worth fighting against them for their sakes? And so Judith, seeing Holofernes sitting under a canopy woven of purple and gold and emeralds and precious stones, and when she had looked upon his face, she bowed down to him, prostrating herself to the ground, and the servants of Holofernes raised her up, at the order of their lord. Chapter 11.

Then Holofernes said to her: Take courage and have no fear in your heart, for I have never harmed anyone who chose to serve Nebuchadnezzar the king. And as for your people, if they had not despised me...

· Judith ·

me: I would not have raised my spear against you. Now therefore tell me for what reason you have left them, and why it has pleased you to come to us. And Judith said to him: Hear the words of your handmaid; for if you follow the words of your handmaid, God will bring this thing to a perfect conclusion with you. For as Nebuchadnezzar king of the earth lives, and as his power lives which is in you for the chastening of all straying souls — for not only do men serve him through you, but also the beasts of the field obey him — the industry of your mind is proclaimed to all nations, and it is known to all peoples that you alone are great and powerful in his whole kingdom, and your discipline is preached in all the provinces. Nor is it hidden what Achior said, nor is it unknown what you ordered to be done to him. For it is established that our God is so offended by the sins of the people that he has commanded through his prophets to deliver them up for their sins. And since the children of Israel know they have offended their God, your dread is upon them. Moreover, famine has overtaken them, and for lack of water they are now counted among the dead. Finally, they have determined to kill their cattle and drink their blood, and to use the holy things of their Lord which God has commanded shall not be touched — the grain, the wine, and the oil. Since they intend to do these things, they are determined to consume what they ought not even to touch with their hands. Therefore, since they do these things, it is certain they shall be given over to destruction. And I your handmaid, knowing this, have fled from them; and the Lord has sent me to announce these very things to you. For I your handmaid worship God even now in your presence, and your handmaid will go out and I will pray to God: and he will tell me when he will repay them for their sins, and coming back I will tell you, so that I may lead you through the midst of Jerusalem. And you shall have all Israel like sheep that have no shepherd.

And not even one person shall be hidden from you, because these things have been told to me through the providence of God. And because he is angry with them, I have been sent to announce these very things to you. All these words pleased Holofernes and his servants, and they marveled at her wisdom, and they said one to another: There is no such woman upon the earth in appearance, in beauty, and in the sense of her words. And Holofernes said to her: God has done well who sent you before your people, that you might give them into our hands. And since your promise is good: if your God does this for me, he shall also be my God, and you shall be great in the house of Nebuchadnezzar, and your name shall be renowned throughout all the earth. CHAPTER XII.
Then he commanded that she should be brought in where his treasures were stored, and ordered that she should stay there, and he appointed what should be given to her from his own table. Judith answered him and said: I cannot eat of these things which you command to be given to me, lest it become an offense to me. But I will eat of what I have brought with me. Holofernes said to her: But if what you have brought with you runs out, what shall we do for you? Judith said: As your soul lives, my lord, your handmaid shall not use up all these things before God does by my hand what I have purposed. And his servants led her into the tent where he had commanded, and she requested that when she went in, she might be given liberty to go out at night and before dawn to pray, and to beseech the Lord. And he commanded his chamberlains that she should be permitted to go in and out as she pleased and to worship her God for three days. And she went out at night into the valley of Bethulia and bathed herself in a spring of water. And as she came up she prayed to the Lord God of Israel that he would direct her way for the deliverance of his people. And returning clean

Judith.

She remained in the tent until she received her food in the evening. And on the fourth day, Holofernes made a feast for his servants, and said to Vagao the eunuch: "Go and persuade that Hebrew woman to come willingly to live with me. For it is a disgrace among the Assyrians if a woman scorns a man, by letting him go without having her." Then Vagao went in to Judith and said: "Let not the good maiden be afraid to go in to my lord, that she may be honoured before his face, and eat with him and drink wine in gladness." Judith answered him: "Who am I to contradict my lord? Whatever shall seem good in his eyes, I will do with all diligence. And whatever shall please him, that shall be best for me all the days of my life." And she arose and adorned herself with her garments, and went in and stood before his face. And the heart of Holofernes was smitten, for he was burning with desire for her. And Holofernes said to her: "Drink now and recline in gladness, for you have found favour with me." Judith said: "I will drink, my lord, for my soul is magnified this day above all the days of my life." And she took and ate and drank before him what her maid had prepared. And Holofernes was made merry on her account, and drank a very great quantity of wine, more than he had ever drunk in his life. Chapter XIII.

And when it was evening, his servants made haste to depart, and Vagao shut the chamber door and went away. And they were all heavy with wine. And Judith was alone in the chamber. But Holofernes lay on his bed, fast asleep, being exceedingly drunk. And Judith said to her maid to stand before the chamber door and watch. And Judith stood before the bed praying with tears and moving her lips in silence,

saying: "Strengthen me, O Lord God of Israel, and in this hour look upon the works of my hands, that as you promised you may raise up Jerusalem your city; and that believing that through you this work was able to be done, I may bring it to pass." And when she had said this, she went to the post of the bed which was at Holofernes' head and took down his sword that hung upon it. And when she had drawn it, she took him by the hair of his head and said: "Strengthen me, O Lord God, in this hour." And she struck twice upon his neck and cut off his head, and took down his canopy from the posts and rolled away his headless body. And after a little while she went out and delivered the head of Holofernes to her maid, and bade her put it in her bag. And they two went out according to their custom, as it were to prayer, and they passed through the camp, and going around the valley they came to the gate of the city. And Judith said from afar to the watchmen on the walls: "Open the gates, for God is with us, who has shown his power in Israel." And when the men had heard her voice, they called the elders of the city. And they all ran to meet her, from the least to the greatest, for they had not expected her to return. And they lit lights and gathered round about her. She then went up to a higher place and commanded silence. And when all were quiet, Judith said: "Praise the Lord our God, who has not forsaken those who hope in him; and through me his handmaid he has fulfilled his mercy which he promised to the house of Israel; and this night he has slain the enemy of his people by my hand." And bringing forth the head of Holofernes out of the bag, she showed it to them, saying: "Behold the head of Holofernes, the general of the army of the Assyrians. And behold his canopy, wherein he lay in his drunkenness, where by the hand of a woman

Judith.

Our Lord God has struck him down. The Lord lives, for his angel has guarded me — going out from here, staying there, and returning here — and the Lord did not allow his handmaid to be defiled, but brought me back to you without the pollution of sin, rejoicing in his victory, in my escape, and in your deliverance.
