Trouble terrifies him, and anguish surrounds him like a king prepared for battle. He has stretched out his hand against God and strengthened himself against the Almighty. He has run against him with a stiff neck, armed with a thick shield. Fatness covers his face, and from his sides fat hangs.

He has dwelt in desolate cities, in abandoned houses that are reduced to rubble. He will not be rich, nor will his substance endure, nor will he take root in the earth. He will not escape from darkness. Flame will wither his branches, and the breath of his mouth will carry him away. He will not trust in vain, deceived by error, that he can be redeemed for any price. Before his days are complete, he will perish, and his hands will wither. He will be stripped like a vine in its first blossom, like an olive tree that sheds its flower. For the congregation of the hypocrite is barren, and fire will devour the tents of those who readily accept bribes. He has conceived sorrow and brought forth iniquity, and his womb prepares deceit. Chapter XVI.

Then Job answered and said: I have heard such things many times. You are all troublesome comforters. Shall your wordy speeches never end? Or what ails you that you keep on speaking? I also could speak as you do — if only your soul were in my soul's place. I could heap up words against you and shake my head at you. I could strengthen you with my words, and the moving of my lips would restrain your grief. But what shall I do? If I speak, my pain is not relieved; and if I hold back, it does not leave me. Now he has worn me out, and all my members are reduced to nothing. My gauntness rises up to testify against me, and a false witness speaks against my face in contradiction. He has gathered his anger against me and threatened me, gnashing at me with his teeth; my enemy has fixed his terrible eyes on me. They have opened their mouths wide against me and struck my cheek in scorn, and they have joined together against me. God has given me over to the ungodly, and into the hands of the wicked he has cast me.

Job

He has delivered me. I, who was once wealthy, am suddenly brought low: he has seized me by the neck and shaken me to pieces, and set me up as his target. His archers surround me; he pierces my kidneys without mercy and pours out my gall on the ground. He breaks me with breach upon breach; he runs upon me like a warrior. I have sewed sackcloth over my skin and buried my horn in the dust. My face is red with weeping, and on my eyelids is the shadow of death, although there is no violence in my hands and my prayer is pure. O earth, cover not my blood, and let my cry have no resting place. Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and he who vouches for me is on high. My friends scoff at me, but my eye pours out tears to God, that he would argue for a man with God, as a man argues with his neighbor. For when a few years are past, I shall go the way from which I shall not return. Chapter XVII.

My spirit is broken, my days are extinguished, the grave is ready for me. I have not sinned, yet my eye remains in bitterness. Give me a pledge; be surety for me with yourself; who else is there that will strike hands with me? For you have closed their minds to understanding; therefore you will not let them triumph. He who informs against his friends to get a share of their property — the eyes of his children will fail. He has made me a byword of the peoples, and I am one before whom men spit in the face. My eye has grown dim from grief, and all my members are like a shadow. Upright men are appalled at this, and the innocent stirs himself up against the godless. Yet the righteous holds to his way, and he who has clean hands grows stronger and stronger. But come on again, all of you, and I shall not find a wise man among you. My days are past, my plans are broken off, the desires of my heart.

They turn night into day; the light, they say, is near to the darkness. If I hope for Sheol as my house, if I make my bed in the dark, if I say to the pit, "You are my father," and to the worm, "My mother," or "My sister," where then is my hope? Who will see my hope? Will it go down to the bars of Sheol? Shall we descend together into the dust? Chapter XVIII.

Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said: How long will you hunt for words? Consider, and afterwards we will speak. Why are we counted as cattle? Why are we stupid in your sight? You who tear yourself in your anger, shall the earth be forsaken for you? Or shall the rock be removed out of its place? The light of the wicked shall be put out, and the spark of his fire shall not shine. The light shall be dark in his tent, and his lamp above him shall be put out. His strong steps shall be shortened, and his own counsel shall cast him down. For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he walks on a pitfall. A trap seizes him by the heel; a snare lays hold of him. A rope is hidden for him in the ground, a trap for him in the path. Terrors frighten him on every side, and chase him at his heels. His strength shall be hunger-bitten, and calamity shall be ready for his stumbling. It shall devour the members of his skin; the firstborn of death shall devour his members. He is torn from the tent in which he trusted and is brought to the king of terrors. In his tent dwells that which is none of his; sulfur is scattered over his habitation. His roots dry up beneath, and his branches wither above. His memory perishes from the earth, and he has no name in the street. He is thrust from light into darkness, and driven out of the world.

·Job·

His bread in his belly will be turned into the gall of asps within him. The riches he swallowed, God will cast out of his belly and drag them from him. He will suck the head of asps, and the viper's tongue will kill him. Let him not see the streams of rivers, the floods of honey and butter. He has consumed all things, yet he shall not be satisfied. According to the multitude of his inventions, so also shall he suffer: for he has oppressed and forsaken the poor, has seized a house he did not build, and there shall be no fullness for his belly. When he has filled himself, he shall be straitened, he shall burn, and every sorrow shall come upon him. Would that his belly might be filled so that God might send the fury of his wrath upon him, and rain down his battles upon him. He shall flee from weapons of iron, and the bow of brass shall strike him through. The sword is drawn and comes out of its sheath, glittering in his bitterness. Terrors shall come upon him on every side. Darkness is laid up for his treasures. A fire not kindled shall devour him; what is left in his tent shall be consumed. The heavens shall reveal his iniquity, and the earth shall rise up against him. The destruction of his house shall be made manifest: it shall be swept away in the day of God's wrath. This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the heritage appointed to him by the Lord. Chapter 21.

Then Job answered and said: Hear, I pray, my words, and do penance. Bear with me and I will speak; and after I have spoken, mock on if you will. Is my dispute against man, that I should not justly be impatient? Look at me and be astonished, and lay your hand upon your mouth. And when I remember, I am troubled, and horror seizes my flesh. Why do the wicked live, are advanced and strengthened with riches?

Their offspring continues in their sight; their kinsfolk and descendants before their eyes. Their houses are secure and peaceable, and the rod of God is not upon them. Their cattle have conceived and not miscarried; their cow has calved and not been deprived of her young. Their little ones go out like a flock, and their children dance and play. They take the timbrel and the harp and rejoice at the sound of the organ. They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment they go down to the grave. They have said to God: Depart from us, we desire not the knowledge of your ways. Who is the Almighty, that we should serve him? And what does it profit us if we pray to him? Yet the counsel of the wicked is far from me, for their prosperity is not in their own hands. How often is the lamp of the wicked put out, and a flood comes upon them? God will distribute the sorrows of his fury. They shall be as chaff before the wind, and as ashes which the whirlwind scatters. God shall lay up the sorrow of the father for his children; and when he repays, then he shall know. His eyes shall see his own destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty. For what does he care for his house after him, when the number of his months is cut short? Can anyone teach God knowledge, who judges those that are high? One man dies strong and hale and prosperous, with rich and fat sides and his bones full of marrow. But another dies in bitterness of soul, without any riches; yet they shall both sleep together in the dust, and worms shall cover them. Surely I know your thoughts and your unjust judgments against me. For you say: Where is the house of the prince, and where are the tents of the wicked? Ask any of the travelers, and you shall understand that the wicked man is kept for the day of destruction, and they are led to the day of wrath.

Job.

Who will argue His ways before Him, and who will make Him answer for what He has done? He will be led to the grave, and he will keep watch over a heap of the dead. He was sweet to the clods of clay, and he draws every man after him, and before him are innumerable ones. How then do you comfort me in vain, since your answer has been shown to contradict the truth? Chapter 22.

Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said: Can a man be compared to God, even one who may have been perfect in knowledge? What does it profit God if you are righteous, or what does He gain if you make your conduct blameless? Does He fear you and bring you to judgment, and is it not because of your great wickedness and your endless iniquities? For you have taken pledges from your brothers without cause, and you have stripped the naked of their clothing. You gave no water to the weary, and you withheld bread from the hungry. By the strength of your arm you possessed the land, and you who were mighty held it. You sent widows away empty-handed and crushed the strength of the fatherless. Therefore snares surround you, and sudden fear troubles you. You thought you would not see darkness, and that a flood of waters would not overwhelm you. Do you not think that God is higher than heaven and that He is exalted above the highest stars? And you say: What does God know? He judges as through a dark cloud. The clouds are His hiding place; He does not watch over us, and He walks about the vault of heaven. Will you keep to the old path that wicked men have trodden, who were carried off before their time, and whose foundation was swept away by a river? They said to God: Depart from us, and counted the Almighty as nothing, though He had filled their houses with good things. The counsel of the wicked is far from me. The righteous will see it and rejoice, and the innocent will mock them.

Is not their prosperity cut off, and has fire not devoured what remained of them? Come to terms with Him and be at peace; in this way good will come to you. Receive instruction from His mouth and lay up His words in your heart. If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored; if you put wickedness far from your dwelling, then you will lay gold in the dust and gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks, and the Almighty will be your gold and your silver. Then you will delight yourself in the Almighty and lift up your face to God. You will make your prayer to Him, and He will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows. You will decide on a matter and it will be established for you, and light will shine on your ways. When men are brought low you will say there is lifting up, and God saves the humble. He will deliver even the one who is not innocent; he will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands. Chapter 23.

Then Job answered and said: Even today my complaint is bitter; His hand is heavy despite my groaning. Oh, that I knew where I might find Him, that I might come even to His seat! I would lay my case before Him and fill my mouth with arguments, that I might know what He would answer me and understand what He would say to me. Would He contend with me in the greatness of His power? No, He would pay attention to me. There an upright man could argue with Him, and I would be acquitted forever by my judge. If I go to the east, He is not there; if I go to the west, I cannot perceive Him. On the left hand when He is working, I do not behold Him; He turns to the right hand, but I cannot see Him. But He knows the way that I take; when He has tried me, I shall come out like gold. My foot has held fast to His steps; I have kept His way and have not turned aside. I have not departed from the commandment of His lips; I have treasured the words of His mouth more than my portion of food. But He alone is:

Job

Before him nothing is hidden. He stretches out the north over the void and hangs the earth upon nothing. He binds the waters in his clouds, so that they do not burst downward together. He covers the face of his throne and spreads his cloud over it. He has set a boundary between the waters until light and darkness end. The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his rebuke. By his power the seas were suddenly gathered, and by his understanding he struck down the proud. By his breath the heavens were made fair; his hand pierced the fleeing serpent. Behold, these are but the fringes of his ways, and how small a whisper do we hear of him! Who can understand the thunder of his full power? Chapter XXVII.

And Job continued his discourse and said: As God lives, who has taken away my right, and the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter — as long as there is breath in me and the breath of God in my nostrils, my lips will not speak wickedness, nor my tongue utter deceit. Far be it from me to say that you are right; until I die I will not put away my integrity. I hold fast to my righteousness and will not let it go; my heart does not reproach me for any of my days. Let my enemy be as the wicked, and my adversary as the unrighteous. For what is the hope of the godless when he cuts them off, when God takes away his life? Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him? Can he delight himself in the Almighty and call upon God at all times? I will teach you about the hand of God and what is with the Almighty I will not conceal. Behold, all of you have seen it yourselves; why then have you become altogether vain? This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the heritage that oppressors receive from the Almighty. If his children are multiplied, it is for the sword; and his offspring are not satisfied with bread. Those who survive him are buried in death, and his widows do not weep. Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up clothing like clay — he may pile it up, but the righteous will wear it, and the innocent will divide the silver. He builds his house like a moth's cocoon, like a booth that a watchman makes. He lies down rich and will do so no more; when he opens his eyes, it is gone. Terrors overtake him like a flood; in the night a storm sweeps him away. The east wind carries him off, and he is gone, sweeping him out of his place. It hurls itself against him without pity; he flees headlong from its power. Men clap their hands at him and hiss him out of his place. Chapter XXVIII.

Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place where gold is refined. Iron is taken out of the earth, and copper is smelted from ore. Man puts an end to darkness; he searches out to the farthest limit the ore in gloom and deep darkness. He opens shafts in a valley away from where anyone lives; they are forgotten by travelers; they hang in the air, far away from mankind, they swing to and fro. As for the earth, out of it comes bread, but underneath it is turned up as by fire. Its stones are the place of sapphires, and it has dust of gold. That path no bird of prey knows, and the falcon's eye has not seen it. The proud beasts have not trodden it; the lion has not passed over it. Man puts his hand to the flinty rock and overturns mountains by the roots. He cuts out channels in the rocks, and his eye sees every precious thing. He dams up the streams so that they do not trickle, and the thing that is hidden he brings out to light. But where shall wisdom be found? And where is the place of understanding? Man does not know its worth, nor

Job.

It is not found in the land of the living. The abyss says it is not in me; and the sea says it is not with me. Gold cannot be given in exchange for it, nor can silver be weighed as its price. It cannot be compared with the dyed colors of India, nor with the most precious sardius stone or sapphire. Gold and glass cannot equal it, nor can vessels of fine gold be exchanged for it. The heights and eminences of gold shall not be remembered in comparison with it. Wisdom is drawn from hidden places. The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, nor shall it be compared with the purest dyes. Where then does wisdom come from, and where is the place of understanding? It is hidden from the eyes of all the living; the birds of the air know nothing of it. Destruction and death have said: We have heard its fame with our ears. God understands its way, and he knows its place. For he looks to the ends of the earth, and sees everything under the heavens. He made a weight for the wind, and weighed the waters by measure. When he made a law for the rain, and a path for the thunderstorm, then he saw it and declared it; he prepared it and searched it out. And he said to man: Behold, the fear of the Lord is wisdom, and to depart from evil is understanding. Chapter 29.

And Job continued his discourse and said: Who will grant me that I might be as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me? When his lamp shone over my head, and by his light I walked through darkness. As I was in the days of my youth, when God was secretly present in my tent. When the Almighty was yet with me, and my children were around me. When my steps were washed with butter, and the rock poured out streams of oil for me. When I went out to the gate of the city, and prepared my seat in the street,

the young men saw me and hid themselves; and the elders rose up and stood. The princes ceased speaking, and laid their hand upon their mouth. The voice of the nobles was hushed, and their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth. The ear that heard me called me blessed, and the eye that saw me gave witness to me: because I delivered the poor man who cried out, and the fatherless who had no helper. The blessing of him who was ready to perish came upon me, and I comforted the heart of the widow. I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; my justice was like a robe and a crown. I was eyes to the blind, and feet to the lame. I was a father to the poor, and the cause of him whom I did not know I searched out most diligently. I broke the jaws of the wicked man, and plucked the prey out of his teeth. And I said: I shall die in my nest, and shall multiply my days as the palm tree. My root is spread out to the waters, and dew shall remain in my harvest. My glory shall always be renewed, and my bow in my hand shall be restored. Those who heard me waited in silence for my counsel; and after my words they spoke no more. My speech dropped upon them as the rain, and they opened their mouth wide as for the spring rain. If I laughed on them, they believed it not; and the light of my countenance fell not to the ground. If I wished to go to them, I sat first. And when I sat as a king with his army around him, yet I was a comforter of those who mourned. Chapter 30.

But now the younger men mock me, whose fathers I would have disdained to put with the dogs of my flock. The strength of whose hands was to me as nothing; and they were thought unworthy of life itself. Barren with want and hunger, who gnawed in the wilderness, wretched with calamity and misery.

· Job ·

They gnawed on herbs and the bark of trees: and the root of the juniper was their food. Those who gathered such things from the valleys: when they found them, ran to them with clamoring. They dwelt in desert torrents, and in caverns of the earth, or upon gravel. They who rejoiced among such things: and counted it a delight to be under the briers. The children of fools and base men, who were not even known in the land. Now I am turned into their song, and am become their byword. They abhor me and flee far from me: and spare not to spit in my face. For he has opened his quiver and afflicted me: and has put a bridle in my mouth. On the right hand of my rising calamities arose at once. They have overturned my feet and have overwhelmed me with their paths as with waves. They have destroyed my ways: they have lain in wait against me and have prevailed: there was no helper. They rushed in upon me as through a wide breach: they rolled themselves upon me in my misery. I am brought to nothing. You have taken away my desire as the wind: and my prosperity has passed away as a cloud. Now my soul fades within me: and the days of affliction have taken hold upon me. In the night my bone is pierced with sorrows: and they that feed upon me do not sleep. With the multitude of them my garment is consumed: and they have girded me about as with the collar of my coat. I am compared to dirt and am likened to embers and ashes. I cry to you and you do not hear me: I stand up and you do not regard me. You are changed to be cruel to me: and in the hardness of your hand you are against me. You have lifted me up and set me as it were upon the wind: and you have mightily dashed me. I know that you will deliver me to death, where a house is appointed for every one that lives. Yet you do not stretch forth your hand to consume them: and if they fall down you will save. I wept heretofore for him that was afflicted: and my soul had compassion on the poor. I expected good things and evil has come upon me: I waited for light and darkness broke out. My inner parts have boiled without any rest: the days of affliction have prevented me. I went mourning without indignation: I rose up and cried in the crowd. I was the brother of dragons and companion of ostriches. My skin is grown black upon me: and my bones are dried up with heat. My harp is turned to mourning: and my organ into the voice of those that weep. Chapter XXXI.

I made a covenant with my eyes, that I would not so much as think upon a virgin. For what part would God from above have in me: and what inheritance the Almighty from on high? Is not destruction to the wicked: and aversion to those that work iniquity? Does he not consider my ways: and number all my steps? If I have walked in vanity and my foot has hastened to deceit: let him weigh me in a just balance and let God know my simplicity. If my step has turned out of the way: and if my heart has followed my eyes and if a spot has cleaved to my hands: let me sow and another eat: and let my offspring be rooted out. If my heart has been deceived upon a woman: and if I have laid wait at my friend's door: let my wife be the harlot of another: and let other men be bent over her. For this is a heinous crime and a most grievous iniquity: it is a fire that devours unto destruction: and rooting out all things. If I have despised to submit to judgment with my manservant and my maidservant: when they had a controversy against me. For what shall I do when God rises to judge: and when he shall examine, what shall I answer him? Did not he that made me in the womb make him also: and did not one form us both? If I have denied

Job

Furthermore, they have taken away speech from you. Since therefore I have spoken repeatedly and they have not replied, they stood and did not answer further: I also will answer my part, and I will show my knowledge. I am full of words, and the spirit of my belly constrains me. Behold, my belly is like new wine without a vent, which bursts new vessels. I will speak and breathe a little: I will open my lips and answer. I will not accept the person of man, nor will I compare God to man. For I do not know how long I shall last, and whether after a short time my maker will take me away. Chapter 33.
Therefore, Job, hear my speeches, and hearken to all my words. Behold, I have opened my mouth; my tongue shall speak in my throat. My words come from my upright heart, and my lips shall speak pure knowledge. The Spirit of God made me, and the breath of the Almighty gave me life. If you can, answer me, and stand before my face. Behold, God made me as well as you: I also was formed out of clay. Surely you should not be frightened by me, neither should my speech be heavy upon you. You have spoken in my hearing, and I have heard the voice of your words. I am clean and without transgression; I am innocent and there is no iniquity in me. Behold, he finds occasions against me, he counts me as his enemy. He puts my feet in the stocks and watches all my paths. Behold, in this you are not just; I will answer you that God is greater than man. Why do you contend against him? For he gives not account of any of his matters. For God speaks once, and he does not repeat it a second time. In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls upon men, and they slumber in their beds: then he opens the ears of men

and instructs them with discipline: that he may withdraw man from his purpose, and deliver him from pride; keeping back his soul from corruption, and his life from perishing by the sword. He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and all his bones are made strong. So that his life abhors bread, and his soul dainty meat. His flesh is consumed away that it cannot be seen, and his bones that were not seen stick out. His soul draws near unto the grave, and his life to the destroyers. If there be an angel with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to show unto man what is right for him: then he is gracious unto him and says: Deliver him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom. His flesh shall be fresher than a child's; he shall return to the days of his youth. He shall pray unto God, and he will be favorable unto him; and he shall see his face with joy, and he will restore to man his righteousness. He looks upon men and says: I have sinned and perverted what was right, and it was not repaid to me. He has redeemed my soul from going into the pit, and my life shall see the light. Lo, all these things God works twice, even three times with a man: to bring back his soul from the pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of the living. Take heed, Job, and listen to me: hold your peace, and I will speak. If you have anything to say, answer me: speak, for I desire you to be justified. But if you have nothing, then listen to me: hold your peace, and I will teach you wisdom. Chapter 34.
So Elihu continued and said: Hear my words, O you wise men; and give ear to me, you who have knowledge. For the ear tests words, as the mouth tastes food. Let us choose for ourselves what is right; let us know among ourselves what is good. For Job has said: I am righteous, and God has taken away my right. In judging me he has called me a liar; and my wound is incurable without transgression.

Job.

my [prayer] without any sin. Who is the man like Job, who drinks up scoffing like water, who walks along with workers of iniquity and goes with wicked men? For he has said: Man is not pleasing to God, even if he runs to him. Therefore, you men of understanding, hear me. Far be it from God to do wickedness, and from the Almighty to do wrong. For he will repay man for his work, and cause every man to find according to his ways. Truly, God will not condemn without cause, nor will the Almighty pervert justice. Who appointed another over the earth, or who set the whole world in place? If he should set his heart toward him, he would gather to himself his spirit and his breath. All flesh would perish together, and man would return to dust. If you have understanding, hear this; listen to the sound of my words. Can one who hates justice be healed? And how can you condemn one who is so righteous? Who says to a king: You are a scoundrel, who calls rulers wicked; who shows no partiality to princes, nor regards the rich more than the poor. Suddenly they die, and in the middle of the night the people are troubled, and they pass away; the mighty are taken away without hand. For his eyes are upon the ways of man, and he sees all his steps. There is no darkness or shadow of death where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves. For it is not for man to set an appointed time with God, to come before him in judgment. He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their place. For he knows their works, and he overturns them in the night, so that they are destroyed. He strikes them down as wicked men in the sight of others. Because they turned away from him, and would not consider any of his ways, so that they caused the cry of the poor to come before him;

and he would hear the voice of the poor. When he grants peace, who then can make trouble? When he hides his face, who then can see him? Whether it be done against a nation, or against a man only: that the hypocrite should not reign, lest the people be ensnared. Since then I have spoken to God, I will not hinder you. If I have erred, teach me. If I have spoken iniquity, I will say no more. Should God repay it on your terms, because you reject it? For you must choose, and not I; therefore speak what you know. Men of understanding will say to me, every wise man who hears me. Job speaks without knowledge, and his words are without wisdom. My desire is that Job may be tried to the end, because his answers are like those of wicked men. For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against God. Chapter 35.
Then Elihu spoke again and said: Do you think this is right, when you say, My righteousness is more than God's? For you said, What advantage will it be to you, and what profit shall I have, if I am cleansed from my sin? I will answer you, and your companions with you. Look unto the heavens and see; and behold the clouds which are higher than you. If you sin, what do you do against him? Or if your transgressions are multiplied, what do you do to him? If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand? Your wickedness may hurt a man as you are, and your righteousness may profit a son of man. By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out; they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty. But no one says, Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night, who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of heaven? There they cry out, but he does not answer

Job.

Because of the pride of evil men. Therefore God does not hear in vain, and the Almighty considers the causes of each. Even though you say he does not consider it, judgment is before him, and you wait for him. For now he does not bring his anger, nor does he greatly punish wickedness. Therefore Job opens his mouth in vain, and multiplies words without knowledge. Chapter 36.

Elihu also continued speaking and said: Bear with me a little while, and I will show you. For I still have something to say on God's behalf. I will repeat my knowledge from the beginning, and I will prove my maker to be just. For truly my words are without falsehood, and perfect knowledge will be made known to you. Behold, God does not cast away the mighty, for he himself is mighty; but he does not save the wicked, and he gives judgment to the poor. He does not withdraw his eyes from the just, and he places kings on the throne forever, and they are exalted there. And if they are in chains and are bound with the cords of poverty, he will show them their works and their transgressions, because they have been violent. He will open their ear to correction, and speak that they may turn from iniquity. If they hear and obey, they shall complete their days in good, and their years in glory. But if they do not hear, they shall perish by the sword and die in foolishness. Hypocrites and crafty men provoke the wrath of God; they shall not cry when he binds them. Their soul shall die in the storm, and their life among the effeminate. He will deliver the poor from their distress, and will open their ear in affliction. Therefore he will bring you out of the narrow mouth into a broad place, and that which is set under it will have no foundation. Your table will be full of fatness. Your cause has been judged as that of the wicked: cause and judgment you shall recover. Let not anger overcome you so that you oppress anyone, nor let the multitude of gifts bend you. Set aside your greatness without tribulation, and all the mighty in strength. Do not prolong the night, so that people may rise up for them. Take care not to turn to iniquity, for you have begun to follow this after misery. Behold, God is exalted in his strength, and there is none like him among lawmakers. Who can search out his ways, or who can say to him: You have done wrong? Remember that you do not know his work, of which men have sung. All men see him; every man beholds him from afar. Behold, God is great, exceeding our knowledge. The number of his years is inestimable. He draws up the drops of rain, and pours out showers like floods, which flow from the clouds, passing over all things. If he wishes to spread the clouds like a tent, and to lighten with his light from above, he will also cover the foundations of the sea. For by these things he judges the peoples, and gives food to the multitude of mortals. He covers the light in his hands, and commands it to come again. He tells his friend concerning it, that it is his possession, and that he may ascend to it. Chapter 37.

At this my heart trembled, and was moved out of its place. Hear the thunder of his voice, and the sound that proceeds from his mouth. He considers it under all the heavens, and his light reaches to the ends of the earth. After it a voice shall roar; he shall thunder with the voice of his majesty, and he will not restrain them when his voice is heard. God shall thunder wonderfully with his voice, he who does great and inscrutable things. He commands the snow to fall upon the earth, and the winter rain and the showers of his strength. He seals up the hand of all men, so that every man may know his work. The beast goes into its den, and stays in its lair. Out of the interior comes the whirlwind, and cold from the north.

Job.

When God breathes, ice forms; and again the waters spread out very broadly. The clouds pour down rain, and the clouds scatter their light. They circle around everywhere, wherever the will of the one guiding them leads them, over all the face of the world: whether in one tribe or in their own land, or in whatever place of his mercy he has commanded them to be found. Hear this, Job: stand and consider the wonders of God. Do you know when God commanded the rains, and made the light of the clouds shine? Do you know the broad paths of the clouds and perfect knowledge? Are not your garments warm when the south wind blows over the earth? Did you, together with him, spread out the skies, which are cast firm as molten bronze? Show us what we shall say to him. We are wrapped in darkness. Who shall tell him what I speak? Even if a man speaks, he shall be swallowed up; for now they cannot see the light. The air thickens into clouds, and the wind passing sweeps them away. Gold comes from the north, and awesome praise comes from God. We cannot find him worthy enough. He is great in strength, in judgment, and in justice; and cannot be fully told. Therefore men fear him, and none who think themselves wise dare to contemplate him. Chapter 38.

Then the Lord answered Job out of the whirlwind and said: Who is this who wraps up counsel in words without knowledge? Gird yourself like a man; I will question you and you shall answer me. Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell me, if you have understanding. Who set its measurements, if you know; or who stretched a measuring line over it? Upon what were its bases set? Or who laid its cornerstone, when the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

Who shut up the sea with doors when it burst out as if from the womb, when I made a cloud its garment and thick darkness its swaddling band? I set boundaries for it, placed bars and doors, and said: "You shall come this far and no further; here your proud waves shall stop." Have you commanded the morning since your days began, and caused the dawn to know its place, that it might take hold of the ends of the earth and shake the wicked out of it? It is changed like clay under a seal, and stands out like a garment. Their light is withheld from the wicked, and the arm of pride is broken. Have you entered into the springs of the sea, or walked in the depths of the abyss? Have the gates of death been revealed to you, and have you seen the gates of deep darkness? Have you comprehended the breadth of the earth? Tell me, if you know all this: where is the way where light dwells, and where is the place of darkness, that you might take them each to their own bounds and understand the paths of their dwelling? Did you know then that you would be born, and do you know the number of your days? Have you entered into the treasuries of the snow, or have you seen the treasuries of hail, which I have reserved for the time of trouble, for the day of battle and war? By what way is the light distributed, and the heat scattered over the earth? Who has given the mighty rain its course, and the way of the thunderstorm, that it should rain on the earth where no man is, in the desert where no mortal dwells, to satisfy the waste and desolate land and make tender grass spring up? Who is the father of rain, and who has begotten the drops of dew? Out of whose womb came the ice, and who has given birth to the frost of heaven? The waters are hardened like stone, and the surface of the deep is frozen. Can you bind the sweet influences of the Pleiades, or

Then the Lord answered Job out of the whirlwind and said: Gird up your loins like a man; I will question you and you shall answer me. Will you make my judgment void, and condemn me so that you may be justified? And do you have an arm like God, and can you thunder with a voice like his? Deck yourself now with majesty and excellence, and clothe yourself in glory and beauty. Cast abroad the rage of your wrath, and look on everyone that is proud and abase him. Look on everyone that is proud and bring him low, and tread down the wicked in their place. Hide them in the dust together, and bind their faces in secret. Then I will also confess to you that your own right hand can save you. Behold now Behemoth, which I made along with you; he eats grass like an ox. His strength is in his loins, and his force is in the navel of his belly. He moves his tail like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are knit together. His bones are like tubes of brass; his limbs are like bars of iron. He is the chief of the ways of God. He who made him has furnished him with his sword; the beasts of the field play nearby; he lies under the lotus plants, in the covert of reeds and fens. The shade covers him with their shadow; the willows of the brook surround him. Behold, he will drink up a river and not marvel; he trusts that he can draw up the Jordan into his mouth. He takes it with his eyes; his nose pierces through snares. Can you draw out Leviathan with a hook, or snare his tongue with a cord? Can you put a hook into his nose, or bore his jaw through with a thorn? Will he make many supplications to you, or will he speak softly to you? Will he make a covenant with you, to be taken as a servant forever? Will you play with him as with a bird, or tie him for your maidens? Will traders haggle over him?
Will they divide him among the merchants? Can you fill his skin with harpoons, or his head with fish spears? Lay your hand upon him; remember the battle — you will not do it again! Behold, the hope of him is in vain; shall not one be cast down even at the sight of him? Chapter 41.
I will not stir him up like one who is cruel. Who then is able to stand before me? Who has given me anything beforehand, that I should repay him? Whatever is under the whole heaven is mine. I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, nor his power, nor his graceful proportion. Who can strip off his outer garment? Who can penetrate his double coat of mail? Who can open the doors of his face? His teeth are terrible round about. His scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal. One is so near to another that no air can come between them. They are joined one to another; they stick together and cannot be separated. His sneezing flashes forth light, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the dawn. Out of his mouth go burning lights; sparks of fire leap out. Out of his nostrils goes smoke, as from a boiling pot and burning rushes. His breath sets coals on fire, and a flame goes out of his mouth. In his neck remains strength, and sorrow dances before him. The folds of his flesh are joined together; they are firm on him and cannot be moved. His heart is as hard as a stone, and as hard as a piece of the lower millstone. When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid; because of his crashings they are beside themselves. Though the sword reach him, it cannot avail; neither the spear, the dart, nor the javelin. He counts iron as straw, and bronze as rotten wood. No arrow can make him flee; slingstones are turned to stubble for him. He regards a club as a piece of straw; he laughs at the rattling of a javelin. The rays of the sun are spread beneath him; he spreads gold upon the mud.

It will make the deep sea boil like a pot of ointments; it makes the sea to shine in its wake, as if it were white-haired. There is no power upon earth that can be compared to him: who was made to fear no one. He sees everything that is high: he is king over all the children of pride. Chapter 40.

Then Job answered the Lord and said: I know that you can do all things, and no thought is hidden from you. Who is this that hides counsel without knowledge? Therefore I have spoken foolishly, things that exceeded my understanding. Hear me and I will speak: I will question you, and you answer me. I have heard you with my ears, and now my eye sees you. Therefore I reprehend myself, and do penance in dust and ashes. After the Lord had spoken these words to Job, he said to Eliphaz the Temanite: My wrath is kindled against you and your two friends: because you have not spoken the things that are right before me, as my servant Job has. Take therefore seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer a holocaust for yourselves. And Job my servant shall pray for you: his face I will accept, that folly be not imputed to you: for you have not spoken right things before me, as my servant Job has. So Eliphaz the Temanite, and Baldad the Suhite, and Sophar the Naamathite went, and did as the Lord had spoken to them, and the Lord accepted the face of Job. The Lord also was turned at the penance of Job, when he prayed for his friends. And the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before. And all his brethren came to him, and all his sisters, and all that had known him before, and they ate bread with him in his house. And the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. And he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she-asses. And he had seven sons and three daughters. And he called the name of the first Day, and the name of the second Cassia, and the name of the third Cornistibii. And there were not found in all the earth women so beautiful as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren. And Job lived after this a hundred and forty years, and he saw his children, and his children's children, unto the fourth generation, and he died an old man and full of days.
Here ends the Book of Job. Here begins the Prologue of the Blessed Jerome, priest, to the Psalter.

When I was at Rome, I revised the Psalter and corrected it, as best I could, in accordance with the Septuagint, though the correction was somewhat hasty. But since you, Paula and Eustochium, find that through the errors of copyists this text has become corrupted, and that the old mistakes prevail more than the new corrections, you compel me, as if tilling a field already exhausted, to root out with crooked furrows the thorns of long-standing error, saying it is proper that what sprouts most abundantly should be cut back most vigorously. Therefore I advise you in my usual preface, both those upon whom this labor falls, and those who wish to have copies of this kind: that what I have carefully corrected should be transcribed with care and diligence. Let each person mark for himself either a horizontal line or shining marks — that is, obeli or asterisks: and wherever he sees a mark extending from it to two points impressed, let him know that in the Seventy translators this passage has more; but where he finds the likeness of a star:

From the Hebrew books let it be known that everything up to the two points follows the edition of the translation alone, which in simplicity of expression does not differ from the Seventy translators. This therefore, both for you and for the studious reader, I have no doubt I have done, though I know there will be many who will prefer to disdain and look down upon fine things rather than learn them, and to drink from a muddy stream rather than from the purest. Here ends the Prologue. Here begins the Book of Hymns, or Soliloquies. I.

Blessed is the man who has not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners, nor sat in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the Lord, and in his law he meditates day and night. He shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that brings forth its fruit in its season; whose leaf also shall not wither, and whatever he does shall prosper. The ungodly are not so, but are like the chaff which the wind drives away. Therefore the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous. For the Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the ungodly shall perish. A Psalm of David. II.

Why do the nations rage, and the people imagine vain things? The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the Lord and against his anointed. Let us break their bonds asunder, and cast away their cords from us. He who sits in the heavens shall laugh; the Lord shall hold them in derision. Then shall he speak to them in his wrath, and vex them in his fierce displeasure. Yet I have set my king upon Zion, my holy hill, declaring the decree. The Lord has said to me: You are my son; today I have begotten you. Ask of me, and I shall give you the nations for your inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for your possession. You shall rule them with a rod of iron; you shall dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel. Now therefore be wise, O kings; be instructed, you judges of the earth. Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice with trembling. Embrace discipline, lest the Lord be angry and you perish from the right way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed are all who trust in him. A Psalm of David when he fled from Absalom his son. III.

Lord, how many are those who trouble me; many rise up against me. Many say of my soul: there is no salvation for him in his God. But you, O Lord, are my shield, my glory, and the lifter of my head. I cried to the Lord with my voice, and he heard me from his holy hill. I lay down and slept; I awoke, for the Lord sustained me. I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people who have set themselves against me on every side. Arise, O Lord; save me, O my God. For you have struck all my enemies on the cheekbone; you have broken the teeth of the ungodly. Salvation belongs to the Lord; your blessing is upon your people. In the end, among the songs. A Psalm of David. IV.

When I called, the God of my righteousness heard me; you have relieved me in my distress. Have mercy on me, and hear my prayer. O sons of men, how long will you be heavy of heart? Why do you love vanity and seek falsehood? Know that the Lord has set apart his holy one for himself; the Lord will hear me when I call to him. Be angry and do not sin; commune with your own heart upon your bed and be still. Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the Lord. Many say: who will show us any good?

Your countenance, O Lord, has been signed upon us as a light; you have put gladness in my heart. From the time that their grain and wine and oil increased. In peace, in the selfsame, I will sleep and take my rest. For you, O Lord, have singularly settled me in hope. For the end, for her who obtains the inheritance. A title.

Give ear, O Lord, to my words: understand my cry. Hearken to the voice of my prayer, O my King and my God. For to you will I pray, O Lord: in the morning you shall hear my voice. In the morning I will stand before you and will see: because you are not a God that wills iniquity. Neither shall the wicked dwell near you: nor shall the unjust abide before your eyes. You hate all the workers of iniquity: you will destroy all that speak a lie. The bloody and the deceitful man the Lord will abhor: but as for me, in the multitude of your mercy, I will come into your house: I will worship toward your holy temple, in your fear. O Lord, lead me in your justice: guide my way in your sight, because of my enemies. For there is no truth in their mouth: their heart is vain. Their throat is an open sepulchre: they dealt deceitfully with their tongues; judge them, O God. Let them fall from their devices: according to the multitude of their wickedness cast them out, for they have provoked you, O Lord. And let all them be glad that hope in you: they shall rejoice for ever and you shall dwell among them. And all they that love your name shall glory in you: for you will bless the just. O Lord, you have crowned us as with a shield of your good will. For the end, in verses for the eighth. A psalm of David. VI.

O Lord, rebuke me not in your indignation: nor chastise me in your wrath.

Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am weak: heal me, O Lord, for my bones are troubled. And my soul is troubled exceedingly: but you, O Lord, how long? Turn to me, O Lord, and deliver my soul: save me for your mercy's sake. For there is no one in death who is mindful of you: and who shall confess to you in hell? I have labored in my groanings: every night I will wash my bed, I will water my couch with my tears. My eye is troubled through indignation: I have grown old amongst all my enemies. Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity: for the Lord has heard the voice of my weeping. The Lord has heard my supplication: the Lord has received my prayer. Let all my enemies be ashamed and be very much troubled: let them be turned back and be ashamed very speedily. For the end, a psalm of David which he sang to the Lord concerning the words of Chusi the son of Gemini.

O Lord my God, in you have I put my trust: save me from all them that persecute me and deliver me. Lest at any time he seize my soul like a lion, while there is no one to redeem, nor to save. O Lord my God, if I have done this thing: if there be iniquity in my hands. If I have rendered to them that repaid me evils, let me deservedly fall empty before my enemies. Let the enemy pursue my soul and take it: and tread down my life on the earth and bring down my glory to the dust. Rise up, O Lord, in your anger: and be exalted in the borders of my enemies. And arise, O Lord my God, in the commandment which you have commanded: and a congregation of people shall surround you. And for their sakes return on high: the Lord judges the people. Judge me, O Lord, according to my justice: and according to my innocence upon me. The wickedness of sinners shall be brought to naught: and you shall direct the just.

He who troubles me will rejoice if I am moved: but I have hoped in your mercy. My heart will rejoice in your salvation: I will sing to the Lord who has bestowed good things upon me: and I will sing praise to the name of the Lord most high. End of Psalm of David. 13.

The fool has said in his heart: there is no God. They are corrupt and have become abominable in their pursuits: there is none who does good, not even one. The Lord looked down from heaven upon the children of men: to see if there is any who understands or seeks God. All have turned aside, they have together become unprofitable: there is none who does good, not even one. Their throat is an open sepulchre: they dealt deceitfully with their tongues: the poison of asps is under their lips. Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness: their feet are swift to shed blood. Destruction and misery are in their ways: and the way of peace they have not known: there is no fear of God before their eyes. Will not all those who work iniquity know: who devour my people as they eat bread? They have not called upon the Lord: there they trembled in fear, where there was no fear. For the Lord is in the just generation: you have confounded the counsel of the poor: but the Lord is his hope. Who will give out of Zion the salvation of Israel? When the Lord shall have turned away the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice and Israel shall be glad. End of Psalm of David. 14.

Lord, who shall dwell in your tabernacle: or who shall rest in your holy mountain? He who walks without blemish: and works justice. He who speaks truth in his heart: who has not used deceit in his tongue. He has not done evil to his neighbour: and has not taken up a reproach against his neighbours. In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing: but he glorifies those who fear the Lord. He who swears to his neighbour and does not deceive: who has not lent his money at usury: and has not accepted bribes against the innocent. He who does these things: shall not be moved forever. Title inscription, Psalm of David. 15.

Preserve me, O Lord, for I have hoped in you: I have said to the Lord, you are my God: for you have no need of my goods. To the saints who are in his land: he has made all my desires wonderful in them. Their infirmities were multiplied: afterwards they made haste. I will not gather their assemblies of blood: nor will I be mindful of their names through my lips. The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup: it is you who will restore my inheritance to me. The lines have fallen for me in a goodly place: for my inheritance is goodly to me. I will bless the Lord who has given me understanding: and moreover until night my reins have instructed me. I set the Lord always in my sight: for he is at my right hand, that I be not moved. Therefore my heart was glad and my tongue rejoiced: moreover my flesh also shall rest in hope. For you will not abandon my soul in hell: nor will you allow your holy one to see corruption. You have made known to me the ways of life: you will fill me with joy with your countenance: at your right hand are delights even to the end.

Hear, O Lord, of justice: Prayer of David. 17.

Attend to my prayer. Hear my prayer with your ears: not from deceitful lips. Let my judgment come forth from your countenance: let your eyes behold equity. You have proved my heart and visited it by night: you have tried me by fire and iniquity was not found in me. That my mouth may not speak the works of men: for the sake of the words of your lips I have kept

Make my paths straight. Perfect my steps in your paths: so that my footsteps may not be moved. I have cried out to you, O God, for you will hear me: incline your ear to me and hear my words. Show forth your wonderful mercies: you who save those who trust in you. Keep me as the apple of your eye. Under the shadow of your wings protect me from the face of the wicked who afflict me. My enemies have surrounded my soul: they have enclosed themselves in their own fat: their mouth has spoken proudly. They have cast me out and now surround me: they have set their eyes to cast me down to the earth. They have taken me like a lion ready for prey: and like a young lion dwelling in secret places. Rise up, O Lord, prevent him and cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked: your sword from the enemies of your hand. O Lord, divide them from the few of the earth in their life: their belly is filled from your hidden stores. They are full of children: and they have left the rest of their substance to their little ones. But as for me, I will appear before your sight in justice: I shall be satisfied when your glory shall appear. At the end of the servant of the Lord David, the words of the canticle which he spoke to the Lord on the day that the Lord delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul. And he said:

I will love you, O Lord, my strength: the Lord is my firmament and my refuge and my deliverer. My God is my helper: and in him will I put my trust. My protector and the horn of my salvation: and my support. I will call upon the Lord who is worthy to be praised: and I shall be saved from my enemies. The sorrows of death surrounded me: and the torrents of iniquity troubled me. The sorrows of hell encompassed me: and the snares of death prevented me. In my affliction I called upon the Lord: and I cried to my God. And he heard my voice from his holy temple: and my cry before him came into his ears. The earth shook and trembled: the foundations of the mountains were troubled and were moved: because he was angry with them. There went up a smoke in his wrath: and a fire flamed from his face: coals were kindled by it. He bowed the heavens and came down: and darkness was under his feet. And he ascended upon the cherubim and flew: he flew upon the wings of the winds. And he made darkness his covert, his tabernacle round about him: dark waters in the clouds of the air. Before his brightness that was before him the clouds passed: hail and coals of fire. And the Lord thundered from heaven: and the Most High gave his voice: hail and coals of fire. And he sent forth his arrows and scattered them: he multiplied lightnings and troubled them. Then the fountains of waters appeared: and the foundations of the world were discovered. At your rebuke, O Lord: at the blast of the breath of your anger. He sent from on high and took me: and received me out of many waters. He delivered me from my strongest enemies and from those who hated me: for they were too strong for me. They prevented me in the day of my affliction: and the Lord became my protector. And he brought me forth into a large place: he saved me because he was pleased with me. And the Lord will reward me according to my justice: and according to the cleanness of my hands he will reward me. Because I have kept the ways of the Lord: and have not wickedly departed from my God. For all his judgments are in my sight: and his justices I have not put away from me. And I shall be spotless with him: and shall keep myself from my iniquity. And the Lord will reward me according to my justice: and according to the cleanness of my hands before his eyes.

that the words of my mouth may be pleasing, and the meditation of my heart always in your sight. O Lord, my helper and my redeemer. At the end, a psalm of David. XIX.

May the Lord hear you in the day of tribulation; may the name of the God of Jacob protect you. May he send you help from the sanctuary and defend you from Zion. May he remember all your offerings and find your burnt sacrifice acceptable. May he grant you according to your own heart and confirm all your plans. We shall rejoice in your salvation and be magnified in the name of our God. May the Lord fulfill all your petitions. Now I know that the Lord has saved his anointed. He will hear him from his holy heaven; the salvation of his right hand is in great power. Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we will call upon the name of the Lord our God. They are bound and have fallen, but we have risen and stand upright. O Lord, save the king and hear us on the day we call upon you. At the end, a psalm of David. XX.

O Lord, the king shall rejoice in your strength and shall greatly exult in your salvation. You have given him his heart's desire and have not denied the request of his lips. For you have come before him with the blessings of sweetness; you have placed on his head a crown of precious stone. He asked life of you and you gave it to him, length of days forever and ever. Great is his glory in your salvation; you will lay glory and great beauty upon him. For you will make him a blessing forever and ever; you will make him joyful with gladness through your presence. For the king trusts in the Lord, and through the mercy of the Most High he shall not be moved. Let your hand be upon all your enemies; let your right hand find out all those who hate you. You shall make them as a fiery oven in the time of your presence; the Lord shall trouble them in his wrath and fire shall devour them. You shall destroy their fruit from the earth and their seed from among the children of men. For they intended evil against you; they devised plans which they were not able to establish. For you shall make them turn their back; you shall make ready your arrows against their faces. Be exalted, O Lord, in your own strength; we will sing and praise your power. At the end, a psalm of David for the morning prayer. XXI.

O God, my God, look upon me; why have you forsaken me? Far from my salvation are the words of my sins. O my God, I shall cry to you by day and you will not hear, and by night, and it will not be folly for me. But you dwell in the holy place, the praise of Israel. In you our fathers trusted; they trusted and you delivered them. They cried to you and were saved; they trusted in you and were not confounded. But I am a worm and no man, the reproach of men and the outcast of the people. All those who saw me laughed me to scorn; they spoke with their lips and wagged their heads. He trusted in the Lord, let him deliver him; let him save him, since he delights in him. For you are the one who drew me out of the womb; my hope from my mother's breasts. I was cast upon you from the womb; you are my God from my mother's belly; do not depart from me. For tribulation is near and there is none to help. Many calves have surrounded me; fat bulls have besieged me. They have opened their mouths against me like a ravening and roaring lion. I am poured out like water, and all my bones are scattered. My heart has become like melting wax in the midst of my bowels. My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue cleaves to my jaws, and you have brought me down to the dust of death. For many dogs have surrounded me; the council of the malignant

He has surrounded me. They have dug holes through my hands and my feet; they have counted all my bones. They themselves have looked and stared at me; they divided my garments among them, and cast lots upon my robe. But you, O Lord, do not remain far away; come to my aid. Rescue my soul from the sword, my only life from the power of the dog. Save me from the mouth of the lion, and from the horns of the wild oxen my lowliness. I will declare your name to my brethren; in the midst of the assembly I will praise you. You who fear the Lord, praise him; all you offspring of Jacob, glorify him. Let all the offspring of Israel fear him, for he has not despised nor scorned the supplication of the poor. Nor has he turned his face away from me; but when I cried out to him, he heard me. My praise is with you in the great assembly; I will fulfill my vows before those who fear him. The poor shall eat and be satisfied; those who seek the Lord shall praise him; their hearts shall live forever. All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the Lord; all the families of the nations shall worship before him. For the kingdom belongs to the Lord, and he rules over the nations. All the prosperous of the earth have eaten and worshiped; all who go down to the dust shall fall before him. And my soul shall live for him; my descendants shall serve him. A generation to come shall be told of the Lord, and they shall proclaim his righteousness to a people yet to be born, what he has done. Psalm of David.

The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. In a place of pasture he has settled me. He has led me beside restful waters; he has restored my soul. He has guided me along the paths of righteousness for the sake of his name. Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no
evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they have comforted me. You have prepared a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You have anointed my head with oil; my cup overflows, how glorious it is. And your mercy shall follow me all the days of my life. And that I may dwell in the house of the Lord for length of days.
A Psalm of David, for the first day of the week. The twenty-third.

The earth is the Lord's and the fullness thereof; the world and all who dwell in it. For he himself founded it upon the seas, and established it upon the rivers. Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord, or who shall stand in his holy place? Those with innocent hands and a pure heart, who have not lifted up their soul to vanity, nor sworn deceitfully to their neighbor. They shall receive a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from God their savior. This is the generation of those who seek him, who seek the face of the God of Jacob. Lift up your heads, O gates, be lifted up, O eternal doors, and the King of glory shall come in. Who is this King of glory? The Lord, strong and mighty, the Lord, mighty in battle. Lift up your heads, O gates, be lifted up, O eternal doors, and the King of glory shall come in. Who is this King of glory? The Lord of hosts, he is the King of glory. At the end of Psalm of David.

To you, O Lord, I lift up my soul; my God, in you I trust, let me not be put to shame. Let not my enemies mock me; indeed, all who wait upon you shall not be confounded. Let all who act wickedly be put to shame and left empty. Show me your ways, O Lord; teach me your paths. Guide me in your truth and teach me, for you are the God of my salvation; for you I wait all the day long. Remember your mercies, O Lord, and your lovingkindnesses,

...those things that are from of old. Remember not the sins of my youth and my ignorances: be mindful of me according to your mercy, for your goodness' sake, O Lord. The Lord is sweet and righteous: therefore he will give a law to those who fall short in the way. He will guide the meek in judgment: he will teach the meek his ways. All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth: to those who seek his covenant and his testimonies. For your name's sake, O Lord, you will pardon my sin: for it is great. Who is the man that fears the Lord? He has appointed him a law for the way he has chosen. His soul shall dwell in good things: and his seed shall inherit the land. The Lord is a firmament to those who fear him: and his covenant shall be made manifest to them. My eyes are always toward the Lord: for he shall pluck my feet out of the snare. Look upon me and have mercy on me: for I am alone and poor. The troubles of my heart are multiplied: deliver me from my necessities. See my lowliness and my labor: and forgive all my sins. Look upon my enemies, for they are multiplied: and have hated me with unjust hatred. Keep my soul and deliver me: I shall not be ashamed, for I have hoped in you. The innocent and the upright have adhered to me: because I have waited for you. Deliver Israel, O God: from all his tribulations. Psalm of David. 25.
Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence: and trusting in the Lord I shall not be weakened. Examine me, O Lord, and prove me: try my reins and my heart. For your mercy is before my eyes: and I am well pleased with your truth. I have not sat with the council of vanity: neither will I go in with the doers of unjust things. I have hated the assembly of the malignant: and with the wicked I will not sit. I will wash my hands among the innocent:

and will encompass your altar, O Lord. That I may hear the voice of your praise: and tell of all your wondrous works. Lord, I have loved the beauty of your house: and the place where your glory dwells. Take not away my soul with the wicked, O God: nor my life with men of blood. In whose hands are iniquities: their right hand is filled with gifts. But as for me, I have walked in my innocence: redeem me and have mercy on me. My foot has stood on the right path: in the assemblies I will bless you, O Lord. At the end, a Psalm of David, before it is completed. 26.
The Lord is my light and my salvation: whom shall I fear? The Lord is the protector of my life: of whom shall I be afraid? While the wicked draw near against me to eat my flesh: my enemies that trouble me have themselves been weakened and have fallen. If armies in camp should stand together against me: my heart shall not fear. If a battle should rise up against me: in this I will be confident. One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life. That I may see the delight of the Lord: and may visit his temple. For he has hidden me in his tabernacle in the day of evils: he has protected me in the secret place of his tent. He has exalted me upon a rock: and now he has lifted up my head above my enemies. I have gone round and have offered up in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation: I will sing and recite a psalm to the Lord. Hear, O Lord, my voice with which I have cried to you: have mercy on me and hear me. My heart has said to you: my face has sought you: your face, O Lord, will I still seek. Turn not away your face from me: decline not in your wrath from your servant. Be my helper, forsake me not: and do not...

Do not despise me, O God my savior. For my father and my mother have left me: but the Lord has taken me up. Set a law for me, O Lord, in your way: and direct me in a right path because of my enemies. Do not give me over to the desires of those who trouble me: for false witnesses have risen up against me, and iniquity has lied to itself. I believe that I shall see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living. Wait for the Lord, act manfully: and let your heart take courage, and wait for the Lord. Psalm of David. XXVII.

To you, O Lord, will I cry, O my God, be not silent to me: lest if you are silent to me, I become like those who go down into the pit. Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication when I pray to you: when I lift up my hands toward your holy temple. Do not drag me away together with sinners: and with those who work iniquity destroy me not. Who speak peace to their neighbors: but evils are in their hearts. Give them according to their works: and according to the wickedness of their devices. According to the works of their hands give to them: render to them their reward. Because they have not understood the works of the Lord and the operation of his hands: you shall destroy them and shall not build them up. Blessed be the Lord: for he has heard the voice of my supplication. The Lord is my helper and my protector: and in him my heart has trusted and I have been helped. And my flesh has flourished again: and with my whole heart I will give praise to him. The Lord is the strength of his people: and the protector of the salvation of his anointed. Save your people, O Lord, and bless your inheritance: and rule them and lift them up forever. Psalm of David at the dedication of the tabernacle. XXVII.

Bring to the Lord, O you sons of God: bring to the Lord the young of rams. Bring to the Lord glory and honor: bring to the Lord glory

to his name: adore the Lord in his holy court. The voice of the Lord is upon the waters: the God of majesty has thundered: the Lord is upon many waters. The voice of the Lord is in power: the voice of the Lord in magnificence. The voice of the Lord breaks the cedars: and the Lord shall break the cedars of Lebanon: and shall reduce them to pieces like a calf of Lebanon: and the beloved one shall be like the son of unicorns. The voice of the Lord divides the flame of fire: the voice of the Lord shakes the desert: and the Lord shall shake the desert of Cades. The voice of the Lord prepares the stags: and he will reveal the dense forests: and in his temple all shall speak his glory. The Lord makes the flood to dwell: and the Lord shall sit king forever. The Lord will give strength to his people: the Lord will bless his people with peace. A Psalm at the dedication of the house of David. XXIX.

I will extol you, O Lord, for you have upheld me: and have not made my enemies to rejoice over me. O Lord my God, I have cried to you: and you have healed me. Lord, you have brought out my soul from the underworld: you have saved me from those going down into the pit. Sing to the Lord, O you his saints: and give praise to the memory of his holiness. For wrath is in his indignation: and life in his good will. In the evening weeping shall have place: and in the morning gladness. And in my abundance I said: I shall not be moved forever. O Lord, in your favor you gave strength to my beauty. You turned away your face from me: and I became troubled. To you, O Lord, will I cry: and I will make supplication to my God. What profit is there in my blood, when I go down to corruption? Shall dust confess to you: or declare your truth? The Lord heard and had mercy on me: the Lord became my helper. You have turned my mourning into joy for me: you have cut my sackcloth

and you have surrounded me with joy. Let my glory sing to you and not be silent: Lord my God, I will give thanks to you forever. [Psalm heading: A psalm of David, for the thirtieth.]

In you, O Lord, I take refuge, let me never be put to shame: in your justice deliver me. Turn your ear to me: make haste to rescue me. Be for me a rock of refuge, a stronghold to save me. For you are my strength and my refuge: and for your name's sake you will lead me and nourish me. You will bring me out of the snare they have hidden for me: for you are my protector. Into your hands I commend my spirit: you have redeemed me, O Lord God of truth. You hate those who observe vanities: but I have trusted in the Lord. I will rejoice and be glad in your mercy. For you have looked upon my lowliness: you have saved my soul from distress. You have not shut me in the hands of the enemy: you have set my feet in a wide place. Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am in distress: my eye is troubled by wrath, my soul and my body too. For my life is spent with sorrow: and my years with sighing. My strength has failed because of my poverty: and my bones are troubled. I have become a reproach to all my enemies and very much to my neighbors: and a fear to my acquaintances. Those who saw me outside fled from me: I am forgotten in their heart like a dead man. I am become like a lost vessel: for I have heard the reproach of many who dwell round about. While they gathered together against me: they plotted to take away my life. But I have trusted in you, O Lord: I said, You are my God: my times are in your hands. Deliver me from the hands of my enemies: and from those who persecute me.

Let your face shine upon your servant: save me in your mercy: Lord, let me not be confounded, for I have called upon you. Let the wicked be ashamed and brought down to hell: let lying lips be made silent. Which speak iniquity against the just: in pride and abuse. How great is the multitude of your sweetness, O Lord: which you have hidden for those who fear you. You have perfected it for those who hope in you: in the sight of the sons of men. You hide them in the secret of your face: from the disturbance of men. You protect them in your tabernacle: from the contradiction of tongues. Blessed be the Lord: for he has shown his wonderful mercy to me in a fortified city. But I said in the excess of my mind: I am cast away from before your eyes. Therefore you heard the voice of my prayer: when I cried to you. Love the Lord, all you his saints: for the Lord will require truth: and will repay abundantly those who act proudly. Be brave and let your heart be strengthened: all you who hope in the Lord. Understanding. Psalm 31.

Blessed are those whose transgressions are forgiven: and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord has not imputed sin: and in whose spirit there is no deceit. Because I was silent my bones grew old: while I cried out all the day. For day and night your hand was heavy upon me: I was turned in my anguish while a thorn was driven in. I acknowledged my sin to you: and my injustice I did not hide. I said I will confess against myself my injustice to the Lord: and you forgave the wickedness of my sin. For this shall every holy one pray to you: in a fitting time. Yet in a flood of many waters: they shall not come near to him. You are my refuge from

from the tribulation that surrounded me: my exultation, rescue me from those surrounding me.
I will give you understanding and instruct you: in the way you shall go I will guide you, keeping my eyes upon you. Do not become like the horse or the mule, which have no understanding. Restrain their jaws with bit and bridle, lest they come near to you. Many are the scourges of the sinner: but mercy shall encompass him who hopes in the Lord. Be glad in the Lord and rejoice, you righteous: and glory, all you upright of heart. At the end of Psalm of the Lord, 32.

Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous: praise befits the upright. Give thanks to the Lord on the harp: sing to him with the psaltery of ten strings. Sing to him a new song: play skillfully with a joyful sound. For the word of the Lord is right: and all his works are done in faithfulness. He loves righteousness and justice: the earth is full of the goodness of the Lord. By the word of the Lord the heavens were made: and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth. He gathers the waters of the sea as a heap: he lays up the deep in storehouses. Let all the earth fear the Lord: let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of him. For he spoke, and it was done: he commanded, and it stood fast. The Lord brings the counsel of the nations to nothing: he frustrates the plans of the peoples and the plans of princes. The counsel of the Lord stands forever: the thoughts of his heart to all generations. Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord: the people he has chosen as his heritage. The Lord looks down from heaven: he sees all the children of men. From his prepared dwelling place: he looks upon all who inhabit the earth. He who fashions the hearts of them all: who observes all their deeds. A king is not saved by a great army: and a giant is not

saved by his great strength. A horse is a vain hope for safety: and by its great power it cannot save. Behold, the eye of the Lord is on those who fear him: and on those who hope in his mercy. To deliver their souls from death: and to keep them alive in famine. Our soul waits for the Lord: for he is our help and shield.
