Clouds and darkness are round about him: justice and judgment are the establishment of his throne. A fire shall go before him and shall burn his enemies round about. His lightnings have shone forth to the world: the earth saw and trembled. The mountains melted like wax at the presence of the Lord: at the presence of the Lord of all the earth. The heavens declared his justice: and all people saw his glory. Let them be all confounded that adore graven things, and that glory in their idols. Adore him, all you his angels: Sion heard and was glad. And the daughters of Juda rejoiced, because of thy judgments, O Lord. For thou art the Lord the most high above all the earth: thou art exalted exceedingly above all gods. You that love the Lord, hate evil: the Lord preserveth the souls of his saints, he will deliver them out of the hand of the sinner. Light is risen to the just, and joy to the right of heart. Rejoice, ye just, in the Lord: and give praise to the remembrance of his holiness. Psalm 98. Sing to the Lord a new canticle: because he hath done wonderful things. His right hand hath wrought for him salvation, and his arm is holy. The Lord hath made known his salvation: he hath revealed his justice in the sight of the Gentiles. He hath remembered his mercy and his truth toward the house of Israel. All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God. Sing joyfully to God, all the earth: make melody, rejoice and sing. Sing praise to the Lord on the harp, on the harp and with the voice of a psalm: with long trumpets and sound of cornet. Make joyful noise before the Lord our King: let the sea be moved and the fullness thereof: the world and they that dwell therein. The rivers

They shall clap their hands together; the mountains shall exult before the Lord, who comes to judge the earth. He shall judge the world in righteousness, and the peoples with equity. Psalm of the Lord, 98.

The Lord reigns; let the peoples tremble: he sits enthroned upon the cherubim; let the earth quake. The Lord is great in Zion; he is exalted above all the peoples. Let them praise your great and awesome name; holy it is, and the honor of the king loves justice. You have established equity; you have executed justice and righteousness in Jacob. Exalt the Lord our God and worship at his footstool; holy is he. Moses and Aaron were among his priests, and Samuel was among those who called upon his name. They called upon the Lord and he answered them; he spoke to them in the pillar of cloud. They kept his testimonies and the commandment that he gave them. O Lord our God, you answered them; you were a forgiving God to them, yet an avenger of their wrongdoings. Exalt the Lord our God and worship at his holy mountain; for the Lord our God is holy. Psalm of praise, 99.

Make a joyful noise to the Lord, all the earth; serve the Lord with gladness. Enter his presence with exultation. Know that the Lord himself is God; he made us and not we ourselves. We are his people and the sheep of his pasture; enter his gates with thanksgiving, his courts with hymns; give thanks to him. Praise his name, for the Lord is gracious; his mercy is everlasting, and his truth endures to all generations. Psalm of David, 100.

I will sing of mercy and justice; to you, O Lord, I will sing praise. I will ponder the way that is blameless; when will you come to me? I will walk in the integrity of my heart within my house. I will not set before my eyes anything that is base; I hate those who do crooked things. No perverse heart shall cling to me; I will know nothing of evil. Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, that one I will destroy. Whoever has haughty eyes and an arrogant heart, I will not endure. I look to the faithful of the land to dwell with me; whoever walks in the way that is blameless shall minister to me. No one who practices deceit shall dwell in my house; no one who utters lies shall continue before my eyes. Morning by morning I will destroy all the wicked of the land, to cut off all evildoers from the city of the Lord. A prayer of one afflicted, when he is faint and pours out his complaint before the Lord. Psalm 101.

O Lord, hear my prayer; let my cry come to you. Do not hide your face from me in the day of my distress; incline your ear to me. In the day when I call, answer me speedily. For my days pass away like smoke, and my bones burn like a furnace. I am stricken like grass and withered; I forget to eat my bread. Because of my loud groaning, my bones cling to my flesh. I am like a pelican of the wilderness; I am like an owl of the waste places. I lie awake; I am like a lonely sparrow on a rooftop. All day my enemies taunt me; those who deride me use my name for a curse. For I eat ashes like bread, and mingle tears with my drink. Because of your indignation and anger, you have taken me up and thrown me down. My days are like an evening shadow; I wither away like grass. But you, O Lord, are enthroned forever; your name endures to all generations. You will arise and have pity on Zion; it is the time to favor her; the appointed time has come. For your servants hold her stones dear.

He freed him and made him lord of his household, and ruler over all his possessions. That he might instruct his princes as himself, and teach his elders wisdom. And Israel entered into Egypt, and Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham. And he increased his people greatly, and made them stronger than their enemies. He turned their heart to hate his people, and to deal craftily with his servants. He sent Moses his servant, and Aaron whom he had chosen. He set among them the words of his signs and wonders in the land of Ham. He sent darkness and made it dark: and he did not disobey his words. He turned their waters into blood, and killed their fish. Their land brought forth frogs in abundance, even in the chambers of their kings. He spoke and there came swarms of flies and lice in all their borders. He gave them hail for rain, and flaming fire in their land. And he struck their vines also and their fig trees, and broke the trees of their borders. He spoke and the locusts came, and caterpillars without number. And they ate up all the grass in their land, and devoured the fruit of their ground. He struck also all the firstborn in their land, the chief of all their strength. He brought them forth also with silver and gold, and there was not one feeble person among their tribes. Egypt was glad when they departed, for the fear of them had fallen upon them. He spread a cloud for a covering, and fire to give light in the night. They asked and he brought quails, and satisfied them with the bread of heaven. He opened the rock and the waters gushed out; they ran in the dry places like a river. For he remembered his holy promise, and Abraham his servant. And he brought forth his people with joy, and his chosen with gladness. And gave them the lands of the nations, and they inherited the labor of the peoples. That they might observe his statutes and keep his laws. Alleluia.

Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endures forever. Who can utter the mighty acts of the Lord: who can show forth all his praise. Blessed are they that keep judgment, and do righteousness at all times. Remember us, O Lord, in the favor that you bear toward your people: visit us with your salvation. That we may see the goodness of your chosen, that we may rejoice in the gladness of your nation: that we may glory with your inheritance. We have sinned with our fathers: we have committed iniquity, we have done wickedly. Our fathers in Egypt did not understand your wonders: they did not remember the multitude of your mercies. But they provoked him at the sea, even at the Red Sea: but he saved them for his name's sake, that he might make his power known. He rebuked the Red Sea also, and it dried up: so he led them through the depths, as through the wilderness. And he saved them from the hand of him that hated them, and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy. And the waters covered their enemies: there was not one of them left. Then they believed his words: they sang his praise. But they soon forgot his works: they did not wait for his counsel. But they lusted exceedingly in the wilderness, and tempted God in the desert. And he gave them their request: but sent leanness into their soul. They angered Moses also in the camp, and Aaron the holy one of the Lord. The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram. And a fire was kindled in their company: the flame burned up the wicked. They made a calf in Horeb, and worshiped the molten image. And they changed their glory into the likeness of an ox that eats grass. They forgot God their savior, who had done great things.

They were humbled. Every food was abominable to their soul: and they drew near to the gates of death. And they cried to the Lord in their trouble: and he delivered them out of their distresses. He sent his word and healed them: and rescued them from their destruction. Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercy: and his wonderful works to the children of men. And let them offer the sacrifice of praise: and declare his works with rejoicing. They that go down to the sea in ships: doing business in great waters. These men saw the works of the Lord: and his wonders in the deep. He commanded and there arose a stormy wind: and the waves thereof were lifted up. They mount up to the heavens and descend to the depths: their soul melts away in their distress. They reeled and staggered like drunken men: and all their skill was swallowed up. And they cried to the Lord in their affliction: and he delivered them out of their distresses. And he turned the storm into a calm: and the waves thereof were still. And they rejoiced because they were quiet: and he brought them to the haven they wished for. Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercy: and his wonderful works to the children of men. Let them exalt him in the assembly of the people: and praise him in the council of the elders. He turned rivers into a wilderness: and water-springs into dry ground. A fruitful land into barrenness: because of the wickedness of those who dwelt therein. He turned a wilderness into pools of water: and dry ground into water-springs. And he caused the hungry to dwell there: and they established a city for habitation. And they sowed fields and planted vineyards: and gathered in the fruits of their increase. And he blessed them and they multiplied greatly: and he did not let their cattle decrease. Yet they were diminished and brought low: through oppression, affliction, and sorrow. Contempt was poured upon princes: and he caused them to wander in a pathless wilderness.

Yet he raised the poor out of misery: and made their families like flocks. The righteous shall see it and rejoice: and all iniquity shall stop its mouth. Whoever is wise will observe these things: and they will understand the loving-kindness of the Lord. Alleluia. A song of praise, a Psalm of David.

My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready: I will sing and give praise, even with my glory. Awake, psaltery and harp: I will awaken the dawn. I will give thanks to you, O Lord, among the peoples: and I will sing praises to you among the nations. For your mercy is great above the heavens: and your truth reaches to the clouds. Be exalted, O God, above the heavens: and your glory above all the earth; that your beloved may be delivered. Save with your right hand and answer me: God has spoken in his holiness. I will rejoice, I will divide Shechem: and measure out the valley of Succoth. Gilead is mine; Manasseh is mine: and Ephraim is the strength of my head. Judah is my lawgiver; Moab is my washpot. Over Edom I will cast my shoe: the Philistines have become my friends. Who will bring me into the fortified city: who will lead me to Edom? Is it not you, O God, who had cast us off: and will you not go forth, O God, with our armies? Give us help from trouble: for the help of man is vain. Through God we shall do valiantly: for he shall tread down our enemies. To the end, a Psalm of the Lord.

O God of my praise, do not keep silent: for the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful are opened against me. They have spoken against me with a lying tongue: and they surrounded me with words of hatred and fought against me without cause. In return for my love they have opposed me: but I gave myself to prayer. And they have rewarded me evil for good: and hatred for my love. Set a wicked man over him:

and let the devil stand at his right hand. When he is judged, let him come out condemned: and let his prayer be turned to sin. Let his days be few: and let another take his office. Let his children be fatherless: and his wife a widow. Let his children wander about and beg: and let them be cast out of their dwellings. Let the usurer search out all his substance: and let strangers plunder his labors. Let there be none to help him: nor any to have pity on his fatherless children. Let his posterity be cut off: in one generation let his name be blotted out. Let the iniquity of his fathers be remembered before the Lord: and let not the sin of his mother be blotted out. Let them be before the Lord continually: and let the memory of them perish from the earth: because he remembered not to show mercy. And he loved cursing and it shall come upon him: and he desired not blessing and it shall be far from him. And he put on cursing like a garment: and it entered into his bowels like water, and like oil into his bones. Let it be to him as a garment which covers him: and as a girdle with which he is always girded. This is the work of those who slander me before the Lord: and who speak evils against my soul. But you, O Lord my Lord, do with me for your name's sake: because your mercy is sweet. Deliver me, for I am poor and needy: and my heart is troubled within me. I am taken away like a shadow when it declines: and I am tossed about as locusts. My knees are weakened through fasting: and my flesh has been changed for want of oil. And I became a reproach to them: they saw me and they shook their heads. Help me, O Lord my God: save me according to your mercy. And let them know that this is your hand: and that you, O Lord, have done it. They will curse and you will bless: let those who rise up against me be confounded, but your servant shall rejoice. Let those who slander me be clothed with shame: and let them be covered with their confusion as with a double cloak. I will give great thanks to the Lord with my mouth: and in the midst of many I will praise him. Because he has stood at the right hand of the poor: to save my soul from persecutors. Psalm 109.

The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand. Until I make your enemies your footstool. The Lord will send forth the scepter of your power out of Zion: rule in the midst of your enemies. With you is the beginning in the day of your strength, in the splendor of the saints: from the womb before the daystar I begot you. The Lord has sworn and he will not repent: you are a priest forever according to the order of Melchisedech. The Lord at your right hand has broken kings in the day of his wrath. He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: he shall crush the heads in the land of many. He shall drink of the torrent in the way: therefore shall he lift up his head.

I will give thanks to you, O Lord. Alleluia.
With my whole heart: in the council of the just and in the congregation. Great are the works of the Lord: sought out according to all his wills. His work is praise and magnificence: and his justice remains forever and ever. He has made a remembrance of his wonderful works, being a merciful and gracious Lord: he has given food to those who fear him. He will be mindful forever of his covenant: he will show his people the power of his works. That he may give them the inheritance of the nations: the works of his hands are truth and judgment. All his commandments are faithful: confirmed forever and ever: made in truth and equity. He has sent redemption to his people: he has commanded his covenant forever. Holy and terrible is his name: the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. And good understanding to all

your justifications. Then I shall not be confounded, when I shall look into all your commandments. I will give you praise with uprightness of heart, when I have learned the judgments of your justice. I will keep your justifications: do not utterly forsake me. Beth. By what does a young man correct his way? By observing your words. With my whole heart I have sought you: let me not stray from your commandments. I have hidden your words in my heart, that I may not sin against you. Blessed are you, O Lord: teach me your justifications. With my lips I have pronounced all the judgments of your mouth. I have been delighted in the way of your testimonies, as in all riches. I will meditate on your commandments: and I will consider your ways. I will think of your justifications: I will not forget your words. Gimel.

Give reward to your servant, keep me alive and I will keep your words. Open my eyes: and I will consider the wondrous things of your law. I am a sojourner on the earth: hide not your commandments from me. My soul has coveted to long for your justifications at all times. You have rebuked the proud: they are cursed who decline from your commandments. Remove from me reproach and contempt: because I have sought your testimonies. For princes sat and spoke against me: but your servant was exercised in your justifications. For your testimonies are my meditation: and your justifications are my counsel. Daleth.

My soul has cleaved to the pavement: quicken me according to your word. I have declared my ways and you have heard me: teach me your justifications. Make me to understand the way of your justifications: and I shall be exercised in your wondrous works. My soul has slumbered through heaviness: strengthen me in your words. Remove from me the way of iniquity:

and have mercy on me according to your law. I have chosen the way of truth: your judgments I have not forgotten. I have stuck to your testimonies, O Lord: put me not to shame. I ran the way of your commandments, when you enlarged my heart. He.

Set before me, O Lord, the law of your justifications: and I will always seek it. Give me understanding and I will search your law: and I will keep it with my whole heart. Lead me into the path of your commandments: for this same I have desired. Incline my heart into your testimonies: and not to covetousness. Turn away my eyes that they may not behold vanity: quicken me in your way. Establish your word to your servant, in your fear. Turn away my reproach which I have apprehended: for your judgments are delightful. Behold I have longed after your precepts: quicken me in your justice. Vau.

Let your mercy come also upon me, O Lord: your salvation according to your word. So shall I answer them that reproach me in any thing: for I have trusted in your words. And take not the word of truth utterly out of my mouth: for in your words, I have hoped exceedingly. So shall I always keep your law: for ever and ever. And I walked at large: because I have sought your commandments. And I spoke of your testimonies before kings: and I was not ashamed. I meditated also on your commandments, which I loved. And I lifted up my hands to your commandments, which I loved: and I was exercised in your justifications.

Be mindful of your word to your servant, Zain, in which you have given me hope. This has comforted me in my humiliation: because your word has enlivened me. The proud did iniquitously altogether: but I declined not from your law. I remembered your judgments of old, O Lord: and I was comforted. A fainting has taken hold of me, because of the wicked who forsake your law.

Your law. How sweet to me were your statutes in the place of my pilgrimage. I remembered your name, O Lord, in the night, and I kept your law. This happened to me because I sought your statutes. You are my portion, O Lord; I have said that I would keep your law. I entreated your face with my whole heart; have mercy on me according to your word. I thought on my ways, and turned my feet to your testimonies. I was ready and was not troubled, that I might keep your commandments. The cords of the wicked have wound around me, but I have not forgotten your law. At midnight I rose to give praise to you, for the judgments of your justifications. I am a partaker with all who fear you, and keep your commandments. The earth, O Lord, is full of your mercy; teach me your justifications. Teth. You have done well with your servant, O Lord, according to your word. Teach me goodness and discipline and knowledge; for I have believed in your commandments. Before I was humbled I offended; therefore I have kept your word. You are good, and in your goodness teach me your justifications. The iniquity of the proud has been multiplied over me; but I will seek your commandments with my whole heart. Their heart has been curdled like milk; but I have meditated on your law. It is good for me that you have humbled me, that I may learn your justifications. The law of your mouth is good to me, above thousands of gold and silver. Ioth. Your hands have made me and formed me; give me understanding that I may learn your commandments. They that fear you shall see me, and shall be glad, because I have greatly hoped in your words. I know, O Lord, that your judgments are equity, and in your truth you have humbled me. Let your mercy be for my comfort, according to your word to your servant.

Let your mercies come to me and I shall live, for your law is my meditation. Let the proud be ashamed because they have done unjust things against me; but I will meditate on your commandments. Let those who fear you turn to me, and those who know your testimonies. Let my heart be undefiled in your justifications, that I may not be confounded. My soul has fainted for your salvation; and I have greatly hoped in your word. My eyes have failed for your word, saying: when will you console me? For I am become like a bottle in the frost; I have not forgotten your justifications. How many are the days of your servant; when will you execute judgment on those who persecute me? The wicked have told me fables, but not as your law. All your commandments are truth; they have persecuted me unjustly, do you help me. They had almost made an end of me upon earth; but I have not forsaken your commandments. According to your mercy quicken me; and I shall keep the testimonies of your mouth. Lameth. Forever, O Lord, your word remains in heaven. Your truth to all generations; you have founded the earth and it endures. By your ordinance the day persists; for all things serve you. Unless your law had been my meditation, I should then perhaps have perished in my humiliation. I will never forget your justifications; for by them you have given me life. I am yours, save me; for I have sought your justifications. The wicked have waited for me to destroy me; but I have understood your testimonies. I have seen an end of all perfection; your commandment is exceeding broad. Mem. How have I loved your law, O Lord; it is my meditation all the day. Through your commandment you have made me wiser than my enemies; for it is ever with me. I have understood more than all my teachers:

Because your testimonies are my meditation.
I have understood more than the elders, because I have sought your commandments. I have restrained my feet from every evil way, so that I might keep your word. I have not declined from your judgments, because you have set the law before me. How sweet are your words to my mouth, sweeter than honey to my lips. Through your commandments I have gained understanding; therefore I have hated every way of iniquity. Nun.
Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my paths. I have sworn and determined to keep the judgments of your justice. I have been humbled exceedingly, O Lord; give me life according to your word. The willing offerings of my mouth make acceptable, O Lord, and teach me your judgments. My soul is continually in my hands, and I have not forgotten your law. The wicked have laid a snare for me, but I have not strayed from your commandments. I have claimed your testimonies as a heritage forever, because they are the joy of my heart. I have inclined my heart to perform your justifications forever, because of the reward. I have hated the wicked because of them; but I have loved your law. Samech.
You are my helper and my protector, and in your word I have hoped. Depart from me, you malicious ones, and I will search the commandments of my God. Uphold me according to your word, that I may live, and let me not be confounded in my expectation. Help me and I shall be saved, and I will meditate on your justifications continually. You have despised all those who fall away from your judgments, for their thought is unjust. I have accounted all the sinners of the earth as transgressors; therefore I have loved your testimonies. Pierce my flesh with your fear, for I am afraid of your judgments. Ain.
I have done judgment and justice; deliver me not to those who slander me. Take up your servant for good; let not the proud ones calumniate me. My eyes have failed for your salvation, and for the word of your justice. Deal with your servant according to your mercy, and teach me your justifications. I am your servant; give me understanding, that I may know your testimonies. It is time, O Lord, to act, for they have broken your law. Therefore I have loved your commandments above gold and topaz. Therefore I was directed toward all your commandments; I hated every way of iniquity.
Wonderful are your testimonies; Phe. Therefore my soul has searched them. The declaration of your words gives light and understanding to the little ones. I opened my mouth and drew in breath, because I longed for your commandments. Look upon me and have mercy on me, according to the judgment of those who love your name. Direct my steps according to your word, and let no iniquity have dominion over me. Redeem me from the calumnies of men, so that I may keep your commandments. Make your face shine upon your servant, and teach me your justifications. My eyes have poured out streams of water, because they have not kept your law. Sade.
You are just, O Lord, and your judgment is right. You have commanded justice as your testimonies, and your truth exceedingly. My zeal has made me pine away, because my enemies have forgotten your words. Your word is exceedingly refined, and your servant has loved it. I am young and despised, yet I have not forgotten your justifications. Your justice is justice forever, and your law is truth. Trouble and anguish have found me; your commandments are my meditation. Your testimonies are equity forever; give me understanding and I shall live. Coph.
I cried with my whole heart; hear me, O Lord; I will seek your justifications. I cried to you; save me, that I may keep your commandments. I rose before dawn and cried out; I hoped in your words. My eyes have been awake before morning, that I might meditate on

seats in judgment: seats above the house of David.
Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: and abundance for those who love you. Let peace be within your strength: and abundance within your towers. For the sake of my brothers and neighbors: I spoke peace concerning you. For the sake of the house of the Lord our God: I sought good things for you. A canticle of ascents.
To you I have lifted up my eyes: O Lord. You who dwell in the heavens. Behold, as the eyes of servants: are on the hands of their masters. And as the eyes of the handmaid are on the hands of her mistress: so are our eyes on the Lord our God, until he has mercy on us. Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: for we are greatly filled with contempt. For our soul is greatly filled: with the scorn of the abundant and the contempt of the proud. A canticle of ascents.
Had not the Lord been among us, let Israel now say: had not the Lord been among us. When men rose up against us: perhaps they would have swallowed us alive. When their fury was kindled against us: perhaps the waters would have overwhelmed us. The torrent passed over our soul: perhaps our soul would have passed through the unbearable waters. Blessed be the Lord: who has not given us as a prey to their teeth. Our soul is like a sparrow escaped: from the snare of the hunters. The snare is broken: and we are freed. Our help is in the name of the Lord: who made heaven and earth. A canticle of ascents.
Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion: they shall not be moved forever, they who dwell in Jerusalem. Mountains are round about them: and the Lord is round about his people, from henceforth and forever. For the Lord will not leave the rod of sinners over the lot of the just: lest the just put forth their hands to iniquity. Do good, O Lord: to the good and to the upright in heart. But those who turn aside into obligations, the Lord shall lead away with the workers of iniquity: peace upon Israel. A canticle of ascents.

When the Lord brought back the captivity of Zion: we became like those who are comforted. Then our mouth was filled with joy: and our tongue with exultation. Then said they among the nations: the Lord has done great things for them. The Lord has done great things for us: we are made joyful. Turn again our captivity, O Lord: as a stream in the south. Those who sow in tears: shall reap in joy. Going they went and wept: casting their seeds. But coming they shall come with exultation: carrying their sheaves. A canticle of ascents for Solomon.
Unless the Lord builds the house: they labor in vain who build it. Unless the Lord guards the city: he watches in vain who guards it. It is vain for you to rise before dawn: rise after you have sat down, you who eat the bread of sorrow. When he gives sleep to his beloved: behold the inheritance of the Lord — children are a reward of the womb. Like arrows in the hand of the mighty: so are the children of those who have been cast out. Blessed is the man who has filled his desire with them: he shall not be confounded when he speaks with his enemies in the gate. A canticle of ascents.
Blessed are all who fear the Lord: who walk in his ways. For you shall eat the labor of your hands: blessed are you and it shall be well with you. Your wife as a fruitful vine: on the sides of your house. Your children like olive shoots: round about your table. Behold, thus shall the man be blessed: who fears the Lord. May the Lord bless you from Zion: and may you see the good things of Jerusalem all the days of your life. And may you see your children's children: peace upon Israel. A canticle of ascents.
Often have they fought against me from my youth: let Israel now say. Often have they fought against me from my youth: but they could not prevail against me. Upon my back sinners have wrought: they have lengthened...

their fathers. Arise, O Lord, to your resting place: you and the ark of your sanctification. Let your priests be clothed with justice: and your holy ones rejoice. For the sake of David your servant: do not turn away the face of your anointed. The Lord swore to David in truth and will not deceive him: of the fruit of your body I will set upon your throne. If your sons keep my covenant: and these my testimonies which I shall teach them. Their sons also forever: shall sit upon your throne. For the Lord has chosen Zion: he has chosen it for his dwelling. This is my rest forever and ever: here I will dwell, for I have chosen it. I will abundantly bless her widow: I will satisfy her poor with bread. I will clothe her priests with salvation: and her holy ones shall rejoice greatly. There I will bring forth a horn for David: I have prepared a lamp for my anointed. I will clothe his enemies with confusion: but upon himself my sanctification shall flourish.

Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity. Like precious ointment upon the head: that ran down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron. Which ran down to the skirt of his garment: as the dew of Hermon that descends upon the mountain of Zion. For there the Lord commanded blessing: and life forevermore.

Behold, bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord: who stand in the house of the Lord. In the nights, lift up your hands to the holy places: and bless the Lord. May the Lord bless you from Zion: who made heaven and earth. Alleluia.

Praise the name of the Lord: praise him, O servants of the Lord. You who stand in the house of the Lord: in the courts of the house of our God. Praise the Lord, for the Lord is good: sing to his name, for it is sweet. For the Lord has chosen Jacob for himself: Israel for his own possession. For I know that the Lord is great: and our God is above all gods. Whatsoever...

your holy one. On whatever day I call upon you, hear me: you will multiply the strength in my soul. Let all the kings of the earth praise you, O Lord, for they have heard the words of your mouth. And let them sing in the ways of the Lord, for great is the glory of the Lord. For the Lord is high, yet he regards the humble: and the proud he knows from afar. If I walk in the midst of tribulation, you will give me life: against the anger of my enemies you have stretched out your hand, and your right hand has saved me. The Lord will repay on my behalf: O Lord, your mercy endures forever: do not forsake the works of your hands. For the end, a psalm of David. 138.

O Lord, you have searched me and known me: you have known my sitting down and my rising up. You have understood my thoughts from afar: you have searched out my path and my lying down. And you have foreseen all my ways: for there is not a word in my tongue. Behold, O Lord, you have known all things, the last and the first: you have formed me and have laid your hand upon me. Your knowledge has become wonderful to me: it is high, and I cannot attain to it. Where shall I go from your spirit? And where shall I flee from your face? If I ascend into heaven, you are there: if I descend into hell, you are present. If I take my wings in the early morning and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea: even there shall your hand lead me: and your right hand shall hold me. And I said: perhaps darkness shall cover me: and night shall be my light in my pleasures. For darkness shall not be dark to you: and night shall be light as the day: as its darkness, so also its light. For you have possessed my reins: you received me from my mother's womb. I will praise you, for you are fearfully magnified: wonderful are your works, and my soul knows this right well. My bone is not hidden from you, which you have made in secret,

in secret: and my substance in the lower parts of the earth. Your eyes did see my imperfect being, and in your book all shall be written: days shall be formed, and no one in them. But to me your friends, O God, are made exceedingly honorable: their rule is greatly strengthened. I will count them, and they shall be more in number than the sand: I rose up and am still with you. If you will kill the wicked, O God: you men of blood, depart from me. For you say against your thought: they shall receive your cities in vain. Do I not hate them, O Lord, that hate you: and pine away because of your enemies? I hate them with perfect hatred: and they are become enemies to me. Prove me, O God, and know my heart: examine me, and know my paths. And see if there be in me the way of iniquity: and lead me in the eternal way. For the end, a psalm of David. 139.

Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: rescue me from the unjust man. Who have devised iniquities in their hearts: all the day long they designed battles. They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent: the venom of asps is under their lips. Keep me, O Lord, from the hand of the wicked: and from unjust men deliver me. Who have proposed to supplant my steps: the proud have hidden a snare for me. And they have stretched out cords for a snare: they have laid for me a stumbling block by the wayside. I said to the Lord: you are my God: hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication. O Lord, Lord, the strength of my salvation: you have overshadowed my head in the day of battle. Give me not up, O Lord, from my desire to the wicked: they have plotted against me: do not forsake me, lest they should triumph. The head of them compassing me about: the labor of their lips shall overwhelm them. Burning coals shall fall upon them: you shall cast them into the fire, in miseries they shall not be able to stand. A man full of tongue shall not be established in the earth: evil shall catch the unjust man

He will seize them to their destruction, for I know that the Lord will render justice to the poor and vengeance to the needy. Surely the righteous shall give thanks to your name, and the upright shall dwell in your presence. Psalm 140.

Lord, I have cried to you, hear me: give ear to my voice when I cry to you. Let my prayer be directed as incense in your sight: the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice. Set a guard, O Lord, over my mouth: and a door round about my lips. Incline not my heart to evil words: to make excuses in sins. With men that work iniquity: and I will not communicate with the choicest of them. The just man shall correct me in mercy and shall reprove me: but let not the oil of the sinner anoint my head. For my prayer also shall still be against the things with which they are well pleased: their judges falling upon the rock have been swallowed. They shall hear my words, for they have prevailed: as when the thickness of the earth is broken up upon the ground. Our bones are scattered by the side of hell: for to you, O Lord, Lord, are my eyes; in you have I put my trust, take not away my soul. Keep me from the snare which they have laid for me: and from the stumbling blocks of the workers of iniquity. The wicked shall fall in his net: I am alone until I pass. A prayer when he was in the cave.

I cried to the Lord with my voice: with my voice I made supplication to the Lord. In his sight I pour out my prayer: and before him I declare my trouble. When my spirit failed me: then you knew my paths. In this way wherein I walked: they have hidden a snare for me. I looked on my right hand and beheld: and there was no one that would know me. Flight has perished from me: and there is no one who has regard for my soul. I cried to you, O Lord:

I said: You are my hope, my portion in the land of the living. Attend to my supplication: for I am brought very low. Deliver me from my persecutors: for they are stronger than I. Bring my soul out of prison: that I may praise your name. The just wait for me: until you reward me. A Psalm of David when his son Absalom pursued him.

Lord, hear my prayer: give ear to my supplications in your faithfulness: hear me in your justice. And enter not into judgment with your servant: for no living man shall be justified in your sight. For the enemy has persecuted my soul: he has brought down my life to the earth. He has made me dwell in darkness as those who have been long dead: and my spirit is in anguish within me, my heart within me is troubled. I remembered the days of old: I meditated on all your works, I thought upon the works of your hands. I stretched forth my hands to you: my soul is as earth without water unto you. Hear me speedily, O Lord: my spirit has failed. Turn not away your face from me: lest I be like those who go down into the pit. Cause me to hear your mercy in the morning: for in you have I hoped. Make me know the way wherein I should walk: for I have lifted up my soul to you. Deliver me from my enemies, O Lord, to you I flee: teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Your good spirit shall lead me into the right land: for your name's sake, O Lord, you will quicken me in your justice. You will bring my soul out of trouble: and in your mercy you will destroy my enemies. And you will cut off all those who afflict my soul: for I am your servant.
A Psalm of David against Goliath.

Blessed be the Lord my God, who teaches my hands for battle and my fingers for war. My mercy and my refuge, my support and my deliverer, my protector in whom I trusted, who subdues peoples under me. Lord, what is man that you are mindful of him, or the son of man that you take account of him? Man is made like vanity; his days pass like a shadow. Lord, bow your heavens and come down; touch the mountains and they shall smoke. Send forth lightning and scatter them; shoot your arrows and throw them into confusion. Stretch out your hand from on high; deliver me and rescue me from many waters, from the hand of foreign children, whose mouths speak vanity and whose right hand is a right hand of falsehood. O God, I will sing to you a new song; upon a psaltery of ten strings I will sing praises to you. You who give salvation to kings, who redeemed your servant David from the evil sword. Rescue me and deliver me from the hand of foreign children, whose mouths speak vanity, and whose right hand is a right hand of falsehood. Their sons are like new plants; their daughters adorned, beautified like the image of a temple. Their storehouses full, overflowing with this and that. Their flocks fruitful, abounding in their fields; their cattle fat. There is no breach of wall, no going away, no cry in their streets. They called blessed the people for whom these things are so; blessed is the people whose God is the Lord.

I will exalt you, O God my King, and I will bless your name forever and ever. Every day I will bless you and praise your name forever and ever. Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised, and his greatness is unsearchable. Generation after generation shall praise your works, and shall declare your power. They shall speak of the glorious splendor of your holiness, and shall tell of your wondrous works. And they shall speak of the power of your awesome deeds, and tell of your greatness. They shall pour forth the memory of your abundant goodness, and shall sing of your righteousness. The Lord is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love. The Lord is good to all, and his mercy is over all that he has made. All your works shall give thanks to you, O Lord, and all your saints shall bless you. They shall speak of the glory of your kingdom, and tell of your power. To make known to the sons of men your power, and the glorious splendor of your kingdom. Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and your dominion endures throughout all generations. The Lord is faithful in all his words and holy in all his works. The Lord upholds all who are falling and raises up all who are bowed down. The eyes of all look to you, O Lord, and you give them their food in due season. You open your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing. The Lord is righteous in all his ways and holy in all his works. The Lord is near to all who call on him, to all who call on him in truth. He fulfills the desire of those who fear him; he hears their cry and saves them. The Lord preserves all who love him, but all the wicked he will destroy. My mouth will speak the praise of the Lord, and let all flesh bless his holy name forever and ever. Alleluia.

Praise the Lord, O my soul! I will praise the Lord as long as I live; I will sing praises to my God while I have being. Put not your trust in princes, in the sons of men, in

...and he will exalt the meek unto salvation.
The saints shall exult in glory; they shall rejoice in their beds. The praises of God shall be in their throats, and two-edged swords in their hands, to execute vengeance upon the nations and punishments upon the peoples; to bind their kings with chains and their nobles with fetters of iron; to execute upon them the judgment that is written: this glory belongs to all his saints. Alleluia.   Psalm 150.
Praise the Lord in his holy places; praise him in the firmament of his power.
Praise him for his mighty acts; praise him according to the multitude of his greatness.
Praise him with the sound of the trumpet; praise him with psaltery and harp.
Praise him with timbrel and choir; praise him with strings and organs.
Praise him with well-sounding cymbals; praise him with cymbals of jubilation: let every spirit praise the Lord. Alleluia.   Here ends the Psalter.

Prologue                                                    Proverbs

Here begins the prologue of Saint Jerome to the Book of Proverbs of Solomon
May a letter join those whom the priesthood joins; indeed, may the page not divide those whom the love of Christ unites. You wrote commentaries on Hosea, Amos, Zechariah, and Malachi, which we have distributed. You wrote, if health had permitted. Mutius provides the comfort of expenses, sustaining our secretaries and copyists, so that you might have the best of my talent dedicated to you. And behold, a frequent crowd lurks around, as though it were fair for me to labor for others while you go hungry, or that I should be obligated to anyone besides you in accounts of giving and receiving. Therefore, worn down by a long illness, lest I be silent this year and be of less service to you, I have dedicated three days' work to your name: namely the interpretation of the three books of Solomon — what the Hebrews call "Malloth," which the common edition calls Proverbs; "Coeleth," which in Greek is Ecclesiastes and in Latin we can call the Preacher; and "Sirasirin," which translates into our language as Song of Songs. There is also the book of Panarctos, of Jesus son of Sirach, and another by a pseudographer, which is inscribed as the Wisdom of Solomon. Of these, I found the former in Hebrew — not as Ecclesiasticus among the Latins, but as Proverbs of the wise. To it were added Ecclesiastes and Song of Songs, so that in the likeness of Solomon it might match not only in the number of books but also in subject matter. The second is not found among the Hebrews anywhere, because its style itself breathes Greek eloquence, and some ancient writers affirm it to be the work of Philo the Jew. Therefore, just as the Church reads the books of Judith, Tobias, and the Maccabees, but does not receive them among the canonical scriptures, so too let these two volumes be read for the edification of the people, but not to confirm the authority of ecclesiastical doctrine.

If anyone prefers the edition of the Seventy interpreters, he has it, corrected by us long ago. For we do not coin new things in such a way as to destroy the old. And yet when one has read most carefully, let him know that our translation has added more sharpness; but taken immediately from the press, most carefully emended, it has preserved its own flavor. Here begins the Proverbs of Solomon, Chapter 1.

The Proverbs of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel: to know wisdom and instruction; to understand the words of prudence; and to receive the instruction of doctrine, justice, judgment, and equity; to give prudence to the simple, to the young man knowledge and understanding. A wise man shall hear and shall be wiser; and a man of understanding shall possess sound counsel. He shall understand a parable and the interpretation, the words of the wise and their mysterious sayings. The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. Fools despise wisdom and instruction. Hear, my son, the instruction of your father, and forsake not the law of your mother: that grace may be added to your head, and a chain of gold about your neck. My son, if sinners entice you, do not consent to them. If they say: Come with us, let us lie in wait for blood, let us hide snares for the innocent without cause; let us swallow him up alive like the grave, and whole, like one who goes down to the pit; we shall find all precious substance, we shall fill our houses with spoils; cast in your lot among us, let there be one purse for us all: my son, walk not with them, restrain your foot from their paths. For their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed blood. For the net is spread in vain in the sight of any bird. And they themselves lie in wait for their own blood, and

Proverbs.

They plot frauds against their own souls. The soul of all the greedy seizes the possessions of those it owns. Wisdom cries out in the open; in the streets she raises her voice. At the head of the crowds she calls out; at the gates of the city she utters her words, saying: How long, you simple ones, will you love childishness, and fools desire what is harmful to them, and the imprudent hate knowledge? Turn back to my correction. Behold, I will bring forth my spirit to you and show you my words. Because I called and you refused; I stretched out my hand and there was none who regarded it. You have rejected all my counsel and have not heeded my rebukes. I in turn will laugh at your destruction; I will mock when what you feared comes upon you. When sudden calamity strikes and destruction falls like a tempest, when tribulation and anguish come upon you — then you will call upon me and I will not hear; they will rise early and not find me, because they hated discipline and did not receive the fear of the Lord, nor were they persuaded by my counsel, and despised all my correction. Therefore they shall eat the fruit of their own way and be filled with their own devices. The turning away of the simple will slay them, and the prosperity of fools will destroy them. But whoever listens to me will rest without fear and will enjoy abundance, with the terror of evils removed. Chapter II.

My son, if you receive my words and hide my commandments with you, so that your ear heeds wisdom — incline your heart to understanding. If you call upon wisdom and incline your heart to prudence; if you seek her as silver and search for her as for hidden treasure — then you will understand the fear of the Lord and find the knowledge of God, for the Lord gives wisdom, and from his mouth

come prudence and knowledge. He will preserve the salvation of the upright, and protect those who walk in simplicity, guarding the paths of justice and the ways of his saints. Then you will understand justice and judgment and equity — every good path. When wisdom enters your heart and knowledge is pleasing to your soul, discretion will watch over you and understanding will guard you, to deliver you from the evil way, and from the man who speaks perverse things. Those who forsake the right path and walk in dark ways, who rejoice in doing evil and delight in the wickedness of others — whose ways are crooked and whose paths are devious. To deliver you also from the strange woman, from the outsider who flatters with her words; who forsakes the companion of her youth and forgets the covenant of her God. For her house leads down to death, and her paths to the departed spirits. None who go to her return, nor do they reach the paths of life. That you may walk in the way of good men and keep to the paths of the righteous. For the upright will live in the land, and the innocent will remain in it. But the wicked will be cut off from the earth, and the treacherous will be uprooted from it.

My son, do not forget my law. Chapter III. Let your heart keep my commandments, for length of days and years of life and peace will they add to you. Let not mercy and truth forsake you. Bind them around your neck; write them on the tablet of your heart, and you will find favor and good understanding in the sight of God and man. Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will direct your paths. Do not be wise in your own eyes. Fear God and turn away from evil. It will be health to your navel and refreshment to your bones. Honor the Lord with your wealth and with the first fruits of all

Proverbs.

Give your fill to the poor, and your barns will be filled to abundance, and your vats will overflow with wine. My son, do not reject the discipline of the Lord, and do not weary when you are corrected by him. For the Lord corrects those he loves, and as a father he is pleased with a son. Blessed is the man who finds wisdom and who abounds in prudence. The acquisition of it is better than the trading of silver and gold; its fruits are the finest and purest. Wisdom is more precious than all riches, and nothing one might desire can compare with it. Length of days is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor; her ways are beautiful ways, and all her paths are peaceful. She is a tree of life to those who take hold of her, and blessed is the one who holds fast to her. The Lord by wisdom founded the earth; by understanding he established the heavens. By his knowledge the depths broke open, and the clouds drop down the dew. My son, do not let these things slip away from you. Keep my law and my counsel, and it shall be life for your soul and grace for your throat. Then you will walk safely in your way, and your foot will not stumble. If you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you rest, your sleep will be sweet. Do not be afraid of sudden terror or of the onslaught of the wicked. For the Lord will be at your side, and he will guard your foot from being caught. Do not withhold good from one who is able to receive it; if you are able, do good yourself. Do not say to your friend: Go and come back, and tomorrow I will give to you, when you are able to give at once. Do not plan evil against your friend when he trusts in you. Do not contend with a man without cause, when he has done you no harm. Do not envy the unjust man, nor imitate his ways, for every mocker is an abomination to the Lord, but he speaks intimately with the humble. Poverty is from the Lord in the house of the wicked, but the dwellings of the just he blesses. He himself mocks the mockers, but he gives grace to the meek. The wise shall possess glory, but shame is the portion of fools. Chapters 3-4.

Hear, O children, the discipline of a father, and pay attention that you may know prudence. I give you a good gift; do not forsake my law. For I was a son to my father, tender and the only one in the sight of my mother; and he taught me and said to me: Let your heart receive my words; keep my commandments and you will live. Get wisdom, get understanding. Do not forget, and do not turn away from the words of my mouth. Do not forsake her, and she will keep you; love her, and she will guard you. The beginning of wisdom is this: get wisdom, and in all your getting, get understanding. Take hold of her and she will exalt you; she will honor you when you embrace her. She will place on your head a garland of grace; she will bestow on you a crown of beauty. Hear, my son, and receive my words, so that the years of your life may be many. I will show you the way of wisdom; I will lead you in the paths of uprightness. When you walk, your steps will not be hampered, and if you run, you will not stumble. Hold on to discipline; do not let her go. Guard her, for she is your life. Do not delight in the paths of the wicked, nor let the way of evildoers please you. Flee from it and do not pass through it; turn away from it and pass on. For the Lord does not sleep unless they have done evil, and sleep is not taken from them unless they have caused someone to stumble. They eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence. But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, which shines brighter and brighter until full day. The way of the wicked is like deep darkness; they do not know over what they stumble. My son, be attentive to my words; incline your ear to my sayings. Let them not escape from your sight; keep them in the midst of your heart. For they are life to those who find them, and

Proverbs

is health to all flesh. Above all else guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it. Keep away from you a deceitful mouth, and put devious lips far from you. Let your eyes look directly ahead, and let your gaze be fixed straight before you. Make level paths for your feet, and all your ways will be firm. Do not turn to the right or to the left; keep your foot from evil. For the Lord knows the ways that are to the right, but those to the left are perverse. He himself will make your paths straight, and lead your ways in peace.

Chapter V. My son, pay attention to my wisdom, and incline your ear to my understanding, so that you may keep your thoughts and your lips preserve knowledge. Do not give heed to the deceitfulness of a woman. For the lips of a strange woman drip honey, and her throat is smoother than oil. But her end is as bitter as wormwood, and her tongue is sharp as a two-edged sword. Her feet go down to death, and her steps reach to the underworld. She does not walk in the path of life; her ways are unstable and you cannot know them. Now therefore, my son, listen to me, and do not depart from the words of my mouth. Keep your way far from her, and do not go near the door of her house. Lest you give your honor to others, and your years to the cruel; lest strangers be filled with your strength, and your labors go to the house of a foreigner; and you groan at your latter end, when your flesh and your body are consumed, and you say: Why did I hate discipline, and my heart despised reproof? I did not listen to the voice of my teachers, nor inclined my ear to those who instructed me. I was almost in utter ruin in the midst of the congregation and assembly. Drink water from your own cistern, and running water from your own well. Let your fountains be dispersed abroad, and streams of water in the streets. Let them be only your own, and not shared with strangers.

Let your own fountain be blessed, and rejoice with the wife of your youth. As a loving deer and a graceful doe, let her breasts satisfy you at all times, and always be enraptured with her love. Why should you be enraptured, my son, with an immoral woman, and be embraced in the arms of a seductress? For the Lord sees the ways of man, and considers all his paths. The iniquities of the wicked will ensnare him, and he will be held with the cords of his sin. He will die for lack of discipline, and in the greatness of his folly he will go astray.

Chapter VI. My son, if you have put up security for your neighbor, if you have shaken hands in pledge for a stranger, you have been trapped by what you said, ensnared by the words of your mouth. So do this, my son, to free yourself, since you have fallen into your neighbor's hands: go quickly, humble yourself, and press your plea with your neighbor. Allow no sleep to your eyes, no slumber to your eyelids. Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the snare of the fowler. Go to the ant, you sluggard; consider her ways and be wise. She has no commander, no overseer or ruler, yet she prepares her food in summer and gathers her provisions at harvest. How long will you sleep, O sluggard? When will you arise from your sleep? A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest, and poverty will come upon you like a traveler, and want like an armed man. But if you are diligent, your harvest will come like a spring, and poverty will flee far from you. A worthless person, a wicked man, goes about with a crooked mouth; he winks his eyes, signals with his feet, points with his fingers, with perverted heart devises evil, continually sowing discord. Therefore his calamity will come suddenly; in an instant he will be broken beyond healing. There are six things the Lord hates, seven that are detestable to him:

Proverbs.

his eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood, a heart that devises wicked plans, feet that are swift in running to evil, a false witness who speaks lies, and one who sows discord among brothers. My son, keep your father's commands and do not forsake your mother's law; bind them continually upon your heart and tie them around your neck. When you walk, they will guide you; when you sleep, they will watch over you; and when you awake, they will speak to you. For the commandment is a lamp, and the law is light, and the reproofs of discipline are the way of life: to keep you from the evil woman, from the flattering tongue of a loose woman. Do not lust after her beauty in your heart, nor let her captivate you with her eyelids. For the price of a harlot is scarcely a loaf of bread, yet an adulteress hunts for a precious life. Can a man take fire to his chest without his clothes being burned? Or can he walk on hot coals without his feet being scorched? So is he who goes in to his neighbor's wife: whoever touches her shall not be innocent. It is not a great crime when a man steals to satisfy his soul when he is hungry. Yet if caught he must repay sevenfold, he must give all the wealth of his house and may even lose his life. But a man who commits adultery lacks judgment; whoever does so destroys himself. He will get wounds and dishonor, and his reproach will never be wiped out. For jealousy arouses a husband's fury, and he will show no mercy when he takes revenge. He will not accept any compensation; he will refuse a bribe however great it is. Chapter 7.

My son, keep my words and store up my commands within you. Honor the Lord and you will be well; do not forsake him for a stranger. Keep my commands and live, keep my law as the apple of your eye. Bind them on your fingers;

write them on the tablet of your heart. Say to wisdom, "You are my sister," and call understanding your nearest kin, that they may keep you from the immoral woman, from the seductive words of the wayward woman. At the window of my house I looked through the lattice and I saw among the simple ones a young man lacking judgment, walking down the street near her corner, going in the direction of her house in the dark of the evening, in the twilight of the night and the darkness. And there a woman came to meet him dressed as a prostitute, with crafty intent to capture souls. She is loud and defiant; her feet never stay at home. Now in the street, now in the squares, at every corner she lurks. She seizes him and kisses him, and with a brazen face she says to him: "I have made my peace offerings; today I have fulfilled my vows. So I came out to meet you, longing to see you, and I have found you. I have spread my bed with tapestry, colorful coverings of Egyptian linen. I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon. Come, let us drink our fill of love until morning; let us delight ourselves with love. For my husband is not at home; he has gone on a long journey. He has taken a bag of money with him; he will return home on the day of the full moon." With her many persuasive words she led him astray; she seduced him with her smooth talk. He followed her at once, like an ox going to the slaughter, like a deer stepping into a noose, not knowing it will cost him his life, until an arrow pierces his liver. Like a bird darting into a snare, he does not know that it will cost him his life. Now therefore, my son, listen to me; pay attention to what I say. Do not let your heart turn to her ways or stray into her paths. For she has brought down many victims; indeed, all her slain are a mighty host.

Proverbs.

and wisdom will be added to him. Teach the just man and he will hasten to receive it. The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and knowledge of the holy ones is understanding. Through me your days will be multiplied and years of life will be added to you. If you are wise, you shall be so for yourself; if you are a scoffer, you alone shall bear the evil. A foolish and shameless woman, full of allurements and knowing nothing at all, sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the high places of the city, to call to those who pass by the way and go on their journeys: "Whoever is simple, let him turn aside to me." And to the foolish she says: "Stolen waters are sweeter, and hidden bread is more pleasant." And he did not know that giants are there, and that her guests are in the depths of hell. For whoever shall go in to her shall descend to hell; and he who turns away from her shall be saved.

A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish son is the sorrow of his mother. Treasures of wickedness profit nothing, but righteousness delivers from death. The Lord does not afflict the soul of the righteous with hunger, but he overthrows the plotting of the wicked. A slack hand causes poverty, but the hand of the diligent makes rich. He who sends lies feeds the winds, and he himself follows after flying birds. He who gathers in harvest is a wise son, but he who sleeps in summer is a son of shame. The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the just, but iniquity covers the mouth of the wicked. The memory of the just is with praise, but the name of the wicked shall rot. The wise in heart will receive commandments, but a babbling fool shall fall. He who walks honestly walks securely, but he who perverts his ways shall be found out. He who winks with the eye causes sorrow; the foolish in lips shall be beaten. The mouth of the just is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked is covered with iniquity. Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all offenses.

On the lips of the wise is found wisdom, but the rod is for the back of him who lacks sense. Wise men lay up knowledge, but the mouth of the foolish draws near to ruin. The wealth of the rich is his strong city; the poverty of the poor is their destruction. The work of the righteous leads to life; the fruit of the wicked leads to sin. He who heeds instruction is on the path of life, but he who ignores reproof goes astray. Lips that conceal hatred have deceit, and he who speaks slander is a fool. In many words there shall not want sin, but he who restrains his lips is most wise. The tongue of the just is as choice silver; the heart of the wicked is of little worth. The lips of the just instruct many, but those who are ignorant shall die in the poverty of their heart. The blessing of the Lord makes rich, and he adds no sorrow with it. A fool does mischief as it were in sport, but wisdom is for the prudent man. What the wicked fears will come upon him; the desire of the righteous will be granted. As a storm passing, so the wicked shall be no more; but the righteous is an everlasting foundation. As vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is the lazy man to those who send him. The fear of the Lord prolongs days, but the years of the wicked shall be shortened. The expectation of the just is joy, but the hope of the wicked shall perish. The way of the Lord is strength to the upright, but it is ruin to the workers of iniquity. The righteous shall never be moved, but the wicked shall not dwell in the land. The mouth of the just brings forth wisdom, but the perverse tongue shall be cut off. The lips of the righteous consider what is pleasing, but the mouth of the wicked speaks perversity.

A false balance is an abomination to the Lord, but a just weight is his delight. Where pride is, there also is disgrace, but where humility is, there also is wisdom. The integrity of the upright guides them, but the crookedness of the treacherous

Proverbs.

Riches will not profit in the day of wrath, but righteousness will deliver from death. The righteousness of the blameless will direct his way, but the wicked will fall by his own wickedness. The righteousness of the upright will deliver them, but the unfaithful will be caught by their own schemes. When a wicked man dies, his hope perishes, and the expectation of the anxious comes to nothing. The righteous is delivered from trouble, and the wicked takes his place. A hypocrite with his mouth destroys his neighbor, but through knowledge the righteous will be delivered. When the righteous prosper, the city rejoices, and when the wicked perish, there are shouts of joy. Through the blessing of the upright a city is exalted, but by the mouth of the wicked it is overthrown. He who despises his neighbor lacks sense, but a man of understanding holds his tongue. A gossip betrays a confidence, but a trustworthy man keeps a secret. Where there is no guidance, a people falls, but in an abundance of counselors there is safety. He who puts up security for a stranger will suffer, but whoever avoids such commitments is safe. A gracious woman gains honor, and ruthless men gain only wealth. A merciful man does good to his own soul, but a cruel man troubles himself. The wicked earns deceptive wages, but he who sows righteousness reaps a sure reward. Kindness leads to prosperity, but the pursuit of evil leads to death. The perverse heart is an abomination to the Lord, but He delights in those whose ways are blameless. Though hand joins in hand, the wicked will not go unpunished, but the descendants of the righteous will be delivered. Like a gold ring in a pig's snout is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion. The desire of the righteous ends only in good, but the hope of the wicked comes to nothing. One person gives freely, yet gains even more; another withholds unduly, but comes to poverty. A generous person will prosper, and whoever refreshes others will be refreshed. He who withholds grain, the people will curse him,

but blessing will come upon the head of him who sells it. He who rises early seeking good finds favor, but he who searches out evil, it will come upon him. He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous will flourish like a green leaf. He who troubles his own house will inherit the wind, and the fool will be servant to the wise. The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who wins souls is wise. If the righteous receives his due on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner. Chapter 13.

He who loves discipline loves knowledge, but he who hates correction is foolish. A good man obtains favor from the Lord, but a man of wicked schemes He will condemn. A man cannot be established through wickedness, but the root of the righteous will not be moved. A wife of noble character is her husband's crown, but a disgraceful wife is like decay in his bones. The thoughts of the righteous are just, but the counsel of the wicked is deceitful. The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood, but the mouth of the upright will deliver them. The wicked are overthrown and are no more, but the house of the righteous stands firm. A man is known by his learning, but a vain and foolish man will earn contempt. Better is a poor man who is self-sufficient than one who is glorified yet lacks bread. The righteous man cares for the needs of his animals, but the kindest acts of the wicked are cruel. He who works his land will have plenty of food, but he who chases fantasies lacks judgment. He who is pleasant lives freely, but in his reproof he leaves behind only shame. The desire of the wicked will bring ruin, but the root of the righteous will flourish. Through the sin of his lips a man falls into trouble, but the righteous will escape from such trouble. From the fruit of his lips a man is filled with good things, and the work of his hands brings its own reward. The way of a fool seems right in his own eyes,

Proverbs.

He who is wise heeds counsel. A fool immediately shows his anger, but one who overlooks an insult is clever. One who speaks what he knows is a witness of justice, but one who lies is a deceitful witness. There is one who is pierced as with a sword through recklessness; but the tongue of the wise brings healing. The lip of truth shall be established forever, but a lying witness speaks only for a moment. Deceit is in the hearts of those who devise evil, but those who counsel peace have joy. No harm will befall the just whatever happens; but the wicked shall be filled with evil. Lying lips are an abomination, but those who deal faithfully are his delight. A shrewd man conceals his knowledge, but the heart of fools proclaims folly. The hand of the diligent shall rule, but the idle shall be put to forced labor. Anxiety in the heart of a man depresses it, but a good word makes it glad. He who neglects loss for a friend's sake is just, but the way of the wicked leads them astray. A deceitful man shall not find gain, but the substance of a man is precious gold. In the path of justice there is life, but the devious path leads to death. Chapter 13.

A wise son heeds his father's instruction, but a scoffer does not listen when rebuked. From the fruit of his mouth a man is satisfied with good, but the soul of the wicked craves evil. He who guards his mouth protects his soul, but he who speaks rashly will come to ruin. The sluggard desires but does not have; the soul of the diligent is richly supplied. A just man hates a lying word, but the wicked brings shame and disgrace. Justice guards the innocent way; wickedness overthrows the sinner. One may appear rich yet have nothing; another may appear poor yet have great wealth. The ransom of a man's life is his wealth, but the poor man does not hear rebuke. The light of the just gives joy, but the lamp of the wicked shall be put out. Among the proud there are always quarrels, but those who take counsel together are guided by wisdom. Wealth gained hastily shall be diminished, but what is gathered little by little by hand shall increase. Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life. He who wrongs another brings harm upon himself, but he who fears the commandment shall be at peace. The wicked soul errs in sins, but the just are merciful and compassionate. The law of the wise is a fountain of life, to turn away from the snares of death. Good instruction gives grace, but the way of the contemptuous is a pitfall. The shrewd man acts with deliberation, but the fool lays open his folly. The messenger of the wicked falls into evil, but a faithful envoy brings healing. Poverty and shame come to him who rejects discipline, but he who heeds correction will be honored. When desire is fulfilled it delights the soul; fools abhor those who flee evil. He who walks with the wise grows wise, but a companion of fools will suffer. Evil pursues sinners, but the just are rewarded with good. A good man leaves an inheritance to his children's children, and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just. Much food is in the fields of the poor, but some are swept away without justice. He who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him diligently. The just man eats to the satisfying of his soul, but the belly of the wicked shall want. Chapter 14.

A wise woman builds her house, but the foolish tears it down with her own hands. He who walks uprightly and fears God is despised by one who walks a crooked way. In the mouth of the fool is a rod of pride, but the lips of the wise protect them. Where there are no oxen, the manger is empty;

Proverbs,

seeks learning, but the mouth of fools feeds on foolishness. All the days of the poor are evil, but a secure mind is like a continual feast. Better is a little with the fear of the Lord than great and unsatisfying treasures. Better to be called to herbs with love than to a fatted calf with hatred. A hot-tempered man stirs up strife, but one who is patient calms disputes. The way of the lazy is like a hedge of thorns, but the path of the upright is without stumbling. A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish man despises his mother. Folly is joy to one who lacks sense, but a man of understanding walks straight. Plans fail where there is no counsel, but with many advisers they are established. A man rejoices in the answer of his mouth, and a word in due season, how good it is. The way of life leads upward for the wise, that he may turn away from the depths below. The Lord tears down the house of the proud, but he establishes the boundaries of the widow. The thoughts of evil are an abomination to the Lord, but gracious words are pure and will be established by him. He who is greedy for gain troubles his own household, but he who hates bribes will live. By mercy and faithfulness sins are atoned for, and by the fear of the Lord one turns from evil. The mind of the righteous ponders how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked pours out evil. The Lord is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous. The light of the eyes rejoices the heart, and good news refreshes the bones. The ear that listens to life-giving reproof will dwell among the wise. He who ignores discipline despises his own soul, but he who heeds reproof gains understanding. The fear of the Lord is instruction in wisdom, and humility comes before glory. Chapter XVI.
The plans of the heart belong to man, but the answer of the tongue is from the Lord. All the ways of a man are open before his eyes; the Lord weighs the spirit. Commit your works to the Lord, and your thoughts will be established. The Lord has made everything for its purpose, even the wicked for the day of trouble. Everyone who is arrogant is an abomination to the Lord; be assured, he will not go unpunished. By justice a king builds up the land. The beginning of the good way is to do justice; it is more acceptable to God than sacrifice. By mercy and truth iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of the Lord one turns from evil. When a man's ways please the Lord, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him. Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues with injustice. The heart of man plans his way, but the Lord directs his steps. An oracle is on the lips of a king; his mouth does not err in judgment. A just balance and scales are the Lord's; all the weights in the bag are his work. Evildoing is an abomination to kings, for the throne is established by righteousness. Righteous lips are the delight of a king, and he loves one who speaks what is right. A king's wrath is a messenger of death, and a wise man will appease it. In the light of a king's face there is life, and his favor is like the clouds that bring spring rain. To get wisdom is better than gold; to get understanding is to be chosen rather than silver. The path of the upright turns away from evil; whoever guards his way preserves his life. Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall. It is better to be of a lowly spirit with the poor than to divide the spoil with the proud. Whoever gives thought to the word will discover good, and blessed is he who trusts in the Lord. The wise of heart is called discerning, and sweetness of speech increases persuasiveness. Good sense is a fountain of life to him who has it, but the instruction of fools is folly. The heart of the wise makes his speech judicious and adds persuasiveness to his lips. Gracious words are like a honeycomb, sweetness to the soul and health to the body. There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end

Proverbs.

leads to death. The soul of the laborer labors for himself, because his mouth urges him on. A foolish man digs up evil, and fire burns on his lips. A perverse man stirs up strife, and a talkative one separates friends. An unjust man entices his friend and leads him in a way that is not good. He who devises evil with deceitful eyes, biting his lips, shall bring it to pass. A crown of dignity is old age, which is found in the ways of justice. The patient man is better than the strong man, and he who rules his own spirit is better than the conqueror of cities. Lots are cast into the lap, but they are disposed of by the Lord. Chapter 17.

Better is a dry morsel with joy than a house full of victims with strife. A wise servant shall rule over foolish sons, and shall divide the inheritance among the brothers. As silver is tried by fire and gold in the furnace, so the Lord tries hearts. The evildoer obeys an unjust tongue, and a liar heeds deceitful lips.
