For that which was made will be punished together with him who made it. Therefore there will be no regard for idols among the nations, because the creatures of God have become an abomination and a temptation to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of fools. For the idea of making idols was the beginning of fornication, and the invention of them was the corruption of life. For they did not exist from the beginning, nor will they endure forever. For human vanity brought them into the world, and therefore their end has been found swiftly. For a father, consumed by bitter grief at the untimely death of his child, made an image of him who had been suddenly taken from him, and now honored as a god one who was then a dead man, and established among his servants rites and sacrifices. Then, in time, as the wicked custom grew strong, this error was kept as law, and by the command of tyrants graven images were worshiped. And those whom men could not honor openly because they lived too far away, they brought their image from afar and made a visible likeness of the honored king, so that they might honor as present the one who was absent. And the eagerness of the craftsman helped even those who did not know him to honor him more. For he, wishing to please the one who employed him, strove with all his art to make the likeness as fine as possible. And the multitude of people, drawn in by the beauty of the work, now regarded as a god one who a short time before had been honored merely as a man. And this was the snare of human life, that men, whether enslaved by grief or by rulers, gave the name that ought not to be shared to stocks and stones. And it was not enough for them to err in the knowledge of God, but also living in a great war of ignorance, they call so many and so great evils peace. For either they slaughter their children in sacrifice, or

Wisdom.

...performing dark sacrifices, or holding vigil-feasts full of madness, neither keeping life nor marriage holy: but one kills another out of envy, or grieves him by adultery, and all things are confounded — the blood of murder, theft and deceit, corruption and unfaithfulness, disorder and perjury, tumult, destruction of good things, pollution of souls, perversion of birth, instability of marriage, disorder of adultery and shamelessness. For the worship of infamous idols is the beginning, cause, and end of all evil. For either they rave in their rejoicing, or they prophesy lies, or they live unjustly, or they quickly commit perjury. For while they trust in lifeless idols, swearing wickedly, they expect not to be harmed. But both things will come upon them justly, because they thought wrongly of God, devoting themselves to idols, and swore unjustly in deceit, despising righteousness. For it is not the power of those by whom they swear, but the punishment of sinners always follows those who transgress. Chapter XV.

But you, our God, are gracious and true, patient, and ordering all things in mercy. For if we sin, we are yours, knowing your greatness; and if we sin not, we know that we are counted with you. For to know you is perfect righteousness, and to know your righteousness and your power is the root of immortality. For neither did the evil invention of men lead us into error, nor the unfruitful labor of painters — a form stained with varied colors, whose aspect arouses in the senseless a longing, and they love the image of a dead figure without a soul. Lovers of evil things are worthy of death — those who hope in such things, and those who make them, and those who love them, and those who worship them. But also the potter, pressing soft clay laboriously, shapes vessels for our use, each one made from the same clay; and from the same clay he fashions vessels for clean uses and similarly those that serve contrary purposes. What use is made of each vessel the potter himself is the judge. And with much labor he fashions from the same clay the man who was himself but a little while ago made of earth, and after a short time returns to that from which he was taken; yet the debt of the soul is not considered. But his concern is not that he labors, nor that his life is short, but he competes with goldsmiths and silversmiths, and imitates workers in bronze, and counts it his glory that he fashions things of little worth. His heart is ashes, and his hope vainer than the earth, and his life of less account than clay; because he did not know the one who fashioned him, and who breathed into him an active soul, and who breathed into him a vital spirit. But they have considered our life a pastime, and our manner of living a pursuit of gain, and that one must make money even from evil. For this man, who above all others knows that he sins, fashions from earthly material fragile vessels and carved things. But all foolish and exceedingly wretched men are the enemies of your people — they who said that all the idols of the nations are gods — idols that have no eyes to see, no nostrils to breathe air, no ears to hear, no fingers on their hands to feel, and whose feet are too slow to walk. For a man made them, and one who has borrowed his own spirit fashioned them. No man can fashion a god like himself. For since he is mortal, he fashions a dead thing with his wicked hands. He is better than the things he worships, because he at least lived when he was mortal, but they never have. Moreover, they worship even the most miserable of animals. For being without sense...

Wisdom

Compared to these, all other things are inferior. And from the appearance of none of these animals can anyone discern good things. Yet they fled, giving praise to God and blessing to Him. Chapter 16.

For these and similar reasons, those worthy of torment suffered, and were destroyed by a multitude of beasts. For your people, in contrast to those torments, you provided well: you gave them the desire for delectable food, preparing a novel taste for them — a new kind of sustenance — so that those who longed for food, on account of what was shown and sent to them, might be turned away even from necessary appetite. But they themselves, soon made destitute, tasted a new food. For it was fitting that destruction should come upon those practicing tyranny without excuse; but to your people, it was only shown how their enemies were being destroyed. For there came upon them a fierce serpent with its wrath, destroying through the behavior of perverse vipers. But your anger did not last forever; they were troubled for a short time as a correction, having a sign of salvation as a reminder of the commandment of your law. For whoever turned was saved not by what he saw, but by you, the Savior of all. And by this you showed your enemies that you are the one who delivers from all evil. Those were killed by the bites of locusts and flies, and no healing was found for their souls, because they deserved to be destroyed by such means. But your children were not overcome even by the teeth of serpents, for your mercy came and healed them. For they were tormented in remembrance of your words, and were swiftly saved, lest they fall into deep forgetfulness and become unable to receive your help. For neither herb nor poultice healed them, but your word, Lord, which heals all things. You are the Lord who holds power over life and death,

and you bring down to the gates of death and bring back. A man indeed destroys a soul through his own wickedness; and when the spirit goes forth it does not return, nor can it call back the soul that has been received. But to escape your hand is impossible. The wicked, who refused to acknowledge you, were scourged by the strength of your arm: by strange rains and hail and relentless storms, and were consumed by fire. What was marvelous was this: that in water, which extinguishes all things, fire burned more fiercely. For the universe defends the righteous. At one time the flame was moderated so as not to consume the creatures sent against the impious, so that they themselves might see and know that they suffer persecution by the judgment of God. And at another time, fire blazed even above the power of water, to destroy an unjust nation of the earth. In return for this, you nourished your people with food of angels and gave them bread from heaven ready to hand, providing all delight and suited to every taste. This substance of yours showed the sweetness you have toward your children; and serving each one's desire, it turned into whatever each one wished. But snow and ice endured the force of fire without melting, so that they might know that fire blazing in hail and running down in rain destroyed the crops of enemies. Again this was so that the just might be nourished. Fire even forgot its own power. For creation, serving you its Creator, rages in torment against the unrighteous, and grows gentle in benefiting those who trust in you. Therefore at that time also, transformed in all ways, it served your all-nourishing grace according to the desire of those who sought you, so that your children whom you loved, O Lord, might learn that it is not the variety of fruits that nourishes man, but

Wisdom.

They had guides for their unknown journeys: from the sun without harm, O good host, you proclaimed. For those were worthy to be deprived of light, and to be kept in darkness as in a prison — they who had kept your sons shut up, through whom the uncorrupted light of the law was beginning to be given to the world; while they were planning to kill the infants of the righteous, and one child having been exposed and saved, you took away a multitude of their children and destroyed them together in the mighty water. That night was known beforehand to our fathers, that knowing for certain by what oaths they had put their trust, they might be of good cheer. So the deliverance of the righteous and the destruction of their enemies were expected by your people. For as you punished our adversaries, so you called us to yourself and glorified us. For the holy children of good men offered sacrifice in secret, and with one consent they made a holy law, that the saints should share alike in the same blessings and dangers, the fathers already having sung out praises. But on the other side there sounded an ill-according cry of the enemies, and a lamentable noise was carried abroad for children that were bewailed. The servant was punished with the same punishment as the master; and a common man suffered the same as the king. So all together had innumerable dead with one kind of death; nor were the living sufficient to bury them: for in one moment the nobler portion of them was destroyed. For with all their sorceries they could not prevail: nor did their skill in collecting herbs avail them, because then your Almighty Word leaped down from heaven, out of your royal throne, as a fierce warrior, into the midst of a land of destruction, and brought your unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.

Then suddenly visions of horrible dreams troubled them greatly, and terrors came upon them unlooked for. And one thrown here, another there, half dead, showed the cause of his death. For the visions that disturbed them did foretell these things, lest they should perish without knowing why they suffered. But the trial of death touched the righteous also, and there was a multitude destroyed in the wilderness: but the wrath endured not long. For then the blameless man made haste, and stood forth to defend them; and bringing the shield of his holy ministry, even prayer and the propitiation of incense, set himself against the wrath, and so brought the calamity to an end, declaring that he was your servant. So he overcame the destroyer, not with strength of body, nor force of arms, but with a word subdued him that punished, alleging the oaths and covenants made with the fathers. For when the dead were now fallen down by heaps one upon another, standing between, he stayed the wrath, and parted the way to the living. For in his long garment was the whole world, and in the four rows of the stones was the glory of the fathers graven, and your Majesty upon the diadem of his head. Unto these the destroyer gave place, and was afraid of them: for it was enough that they only tasted of the wrath.

But upon the wicked, punishment came even to the last without mercy. For God knew beforehand even their future actions: that though they themselves had permitted the people to go, and had sent them out with great care, they would repent and pursue them. For whilst they were yet mourning and lamenting at the graves of the dead, they took up another foolish device; and pursued as fugitives those whom they had entreated to depart. For a worthy fate drew them unto this end, and made them forget those things that had happened, that they might fulfill the punishment which was yet lacking for their torments.

Wisdom Prologue

kept in remembrance: so that those whom torments had filled with punishment, the same marvelous one transformed: while others found a new death. For all creation from the beginning was refashioned according to your commands, so that your servants might be kept unharmed. For the cloud overshadowed their camp: and where there was dry land, water appeared: and in the Red Sea a way without obstacle: and the field springing up from the deep without measure, through which all passed over whom the covering of your hand, so that your children might see your miracles and wonders. Like horses they fed freely, and like lambs they leaped up, magnifying you, O Lord, who delivered them. For they still remembered the things that had come to pass in their sojourn: how instead of producing animals the earth brought forth gnats, and instead of fishes the river cast up a multitude of frogs. And at the last they saw a new kind of birds, and were led on by desire to ask for dainty meats. For to satisfy their longing, food was brought them even from the sea: and afflictions came upon the sinners not without those signs that were given before by the force of thunderbolts. For they suffered justly according to their own wickedness. For they had practiced a more detestable inhospitality: for some refused to receive strangers when they came to them: but these brought guests into bondage that had done well to them. And not only so: but they also regarded others with contempt, while those who had received with gladness the same customs were tormented with afflictions. They were struck moreover with blindness: as those others were at the doors of the just man, when they were covered with sudden darkness.

And as it is converted, as in an instrument of music the sound changes, all things keep their own sound. And from the sight itself it can be estimated. In the water, those born continued in grace: and things born to swim transferred to land. Fire prevailed over its own power in water: water forgot its nature of quenching. Flames on the other hand did not harm the flesh of corruptible animals as they walked about: neither did they melt that which was easily melted, like ice, but in all things. In all things, O Lord, you magnified your people, and honored them, and did not despise them, being present with them in every time and place.

Here begins the Prologue of the Book of Ecclesiasticus, son of Jesus son of Sirach.

Many and great things have been delivered to us through the Law and the Prophets and the others who have followed them, for which things Israel ought to be commended for learning and wisdom: because not only must those who read attain to understanding, but also they who desire to learn must be able to profit those without, both in speaking and in writing. My grandfather Jesus, after he had much given himself to the diligent study of the law, and the prophets, and the other books of our fathers, and had gotten therein good judgment, was drawn on also himself to write something pertaining to learning and wisdom: so that those who desire to learn, giving attention to these things, might profit much more in living according to the law. You are entreated therefore to come with benevolence and attention to the reading, and to have indulgence in cases where, despite our diligent labor in interpreting, we may seem to fail in some of the phrases. For the words of the Hebrews have not the same force in them when translated into another tongue. And not only these, but the law itself, and the prophets, and the rest of the books, have no small difference when they are spoken in their original language.

Ecclesiasticus.

as they are spoken among themselves. For in the thirty-eighth year of the reign of Ptolemy Euergetes, after coming as a young man to Egypt, and having spent much time there, I found books left behind of no small or insignificant learning. I therefore thought it both good and necessary that I myself should devote some diligence and labor to the translation of this book, and with much sleepless effort I have in the course of time brought this work to completion, so that those who wish to apply their minds to learning may know how to order their conduct according to the law of the Lord.

Here ends the Prologue. Here begins the Book of Ecclesiasticus, Chapter 1.
All wisdom is from the Lord God, and was with him forever, and is before all time. The sand of the sea, and the drops of rain, and the days of eternity — who has numbered these? The height of heaven, and the breadth of the earth, and the depth of the abyss — who has measured these? Who has searched out the wisdom of God that precedes all things? Wisdom was created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from eternity. The word of God on high is the fountain of wisdom, and her ways are everlasting commandments. To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed? Who has known her subtleties? There is one most high Creator, all-powerful and mighty, and greatly to be feared, who sits upon his throne and is the Lord God. He created her in the Holy Spirit, and saw her and numbered her and measured her. And he poured her out upon all his works, and upon all flesh according to his gift, and he has given her freely to those who love him. The fear of the Lord is glory and exultation, gladness and a crown of rejoicing.

The fear of the Lord shall delight the heart and shall give gladness and joy and length of days. With him who fears God it shall go well in his last days, and on the day of his death he shall be blessed. The love of God is honorable wisdom; and those to whom she appears love her, beholding and knowing her great works. The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and it was created with the faithful in the womb; it walks with chosen women, and is known with the just and faithful. The fear of the Lord is the crown of wisdom, making peace and perfect health to flourish. Religiosity will guard and justify the heart, granting joy and gladness. With him who fears God it shall go well at the last, and in the days of his end he shall be blessed. The fullness of wisdom is to fear God, and fullness comes from her fruits. She shall fill all her house with her offspring, and the storehouses with her treasures. The fear of the Lord is a crown of wisdom, filling the house with peace and the fruit of salvation; both are gifts of God. Wisdom distributes knowledge and understanding of prudence, and exalts the glory of those who hold fast to her. The root of wisdom is to fear God; her branches are long life. In the treasuries of wisdom is understanding and knowledge of religion; but to sinners wisdom is an abomination. The fear of the Lord drives out sin. For he who is without fear cannot be justified, for the wrath of his pride shall be his downfall. A patient man will bear for a time, and afterward joy shall be restored to him. A man of good sense will conceal his words for a time, and the lips of many shall declare his wisdom. In the treasuries of wisdom is instruction; but to the sinner the practice of God is an abomination. My son, if you desire wisdom, keep justice, and God will grant it to you freely. For wisdom and discipline are the fear of the Lord, and that which pleases him is faithfulness and meekness.

Ecclesiasticus.

A father builds up his sons' houses; but a mother's curse tears up the foundations. Do not glory in dishonoring your father, for it is no glory to you but shame. A man's glory is the honor of his father, and a son's disgrace is a father without honor. Son, support your father in his old age, and do not grieve him during his life; and if his mind fail, be considerate, and do not despise him in your strength. For the almsgiving of a father will not be forgotten. For the sins of the mother, good will be restored to you; and in righteousness it will be built up for you; and in the day of tribulation you will be remembered; and your sins will melt away like frost in fair weather. How ill-famed is he who forsakes his father; and he is cursed by God who angers his mother. Son, carry out your works in gentleness, and you will be loved above the glory of men. The greater you are, humble yourself in all things, and before God you will find grace; for the power of God alone is great, and He is honored by the humble. Seek not what is too high for you, and search not into things beyond your strength; but what God has commanded you, think on these always, and do not be curious in His many works. For it is not necessary for you to see with your eyes what is hidden. In superfluous matters do not meddle overmuch, and in His many works you will not be curious. For many things beyond human understanding have been shown to you. For suspicion has brought many down, and has held their minds in vanity. A hard heart will fare badly in the end; and he who loves danger will perish in it. A heart that walks two ways will not have success; and the perverse of heart will give scandal thereby. An evil heart will be burdened with sorrows, and a sinner adds sin upon sin. The assembly of the proud will have no healing; for the root of sin will take hold among them and not be understood. The heart of the wise is understood in wisdom; and a good ear will hear wisdom with all desire. A wise and understanding heart will abstain from sins, and will have success in works of righteousness. Water quenches flaming fire, and almsgiving withstands sins; and God who repays is mindful of those who show kindness. Remember it for hereafter, and in the time of your falling you will find a firm foundation.

Chapter 4.

Son, do not defraud the poor of alms, and do not turn away your eyes from the poor. Do not despise the hungry soul, and do not provoke a poor man in his poverty. Do not afflict the heart of the needy, and do not delay a gift to someone in need. Do not reject the petition of one who is troubled, and do not turn away your face from the poor. Do not turn your eyes away from the needy out of anger, and do not give those who ask occasion to curse you. For the prayer of one who curses you in the bitterness of his soul will be heard; and He who made him will hear it. Make yourself agreeable to the congregation of the poor, and humble your soul before an elder, and bow your head before a great man. Incline your ear to the poor without sadness, and pay your debts, and answer him peaceably in gentleness. Deliver him who suffers injustice from the hand of the proud, and do not be faint-hearted in your soul. In judging, be merciful to orphans as a father, and to their mother as a husband: and you will be as an obedient son of the Most High, and He will have more mercy on you than a mother. Wisdom breathes life into her children, and receives those who seek her, and will walk before them in the way of righteousness. Whoever loves her loves life; and whoever watches for her will be filled with her joy. Those who hold fast to her will inherit life; and wherever she enters, God will bless them. Those who serve her will serve God; and those who love her

Ecclesiasticus.

God loves wisdom. Whoever listens to her will judge nations, and whoever contemplates her will dwell secure. If a man trusts in her, he will possess her as an inheritance, and his descendants will be established in her; for she walks with him in temptation and chooses him from the beginning. Fear and dread and trial she will bring upon him, and she will torture him with the discipline of her teaching until she has tested him in his thoughts and trusted his soul. Then she will strengthen him and lead him on a straight path to herself, and she will gladden him and reveal her secrets to him, and she will store up in him knowledge and understanding of justice. But if he goes astray, she will forsake him and hand him over to his enemies. My son, observe the right time, and beware of evil. Do not be ashamed on account of your soul to say the truth. For there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that brings glory and grace. Do not show partiality against yourself, nor against your own life. Do not be ashamed to turn away from a neighbor in his fall, nor to withhold a word for his salvation. Do not hide your wisdom for the sake of your appearance. For wisdom is recognized through speech, and understanding and knowledge and doctrine through the word of the wise, and steadfastness through the works of justice. Do not contradict the word of truth in any way, but be ashamed of the falsehood of your ignorance. Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not strive against the current of a river. Fight for justice for your soul, and even unto death strive for what is right, and God will fight your enemies for you. Do not be eager with your tongue, nor slack and idle in your works. Do not be like a lion in your own house, frightening your household and oppressing those subject to you.

Do not stretch out your hand to receive and close it when you should give. Chapter V. Do not set your heart on unjust possessions, and do not say, "I have enough to live on." For nothing will avail in the time of vengeance and punishment. Do not follow your strength in the desire of your heart, and do not say, "How powerful am I?" or "Who will bring me down for what I have done?" For God will surely exact vengeance. Do not say, "I have sinned, and what harm has come to me?" for the Most High is slow to repay. Do not be without fear concerning atonement for sins, and do not add sin upon sin, and do not say, "The mercy of the Lord is great; he will have mercy on the multitude of my sins." For mercy and wrath are with him, and his wrath rests upon sinners. Do not delay to turn to the Lord, and do not postpone it from day to day; for the wrath of the Lord will come suddenly, and in the time of punishment he will destroy you. Do not be anxious for unjust wealth, for it will not benefit you in the day of reckoning and punishment. Do not winnow yourself with every wind, and do not walk in every path; for so every sinner is proven by a double tongue. Be steadfast in the way of the Lord and in the truth of your understanding and knowledge, and let the word of peace and justice accompany you. Be gentle in hearing the word of God so that you may understand it, and with wisdom offer a true response. If you have understanding, answer your neighbor; but if not, let your hand be over your mouth, lest you be caught in a foolish word and put to shame. Honor and glory come from wise speech, but the tongue of the foolish is his own downfall. Do not be called a slanderer in your life, and do not be caught and put to shame by your tongue. For upon a thief there is shame and repentance, and a most evil mark upon the double-tongued slanderer.

Ecclesiasticus.

But hatred and enmity and reproach — justify both the small and the great, my son. (Chapter 3.)
Do not become an enemy to a friend on account of his first offense, for an improper and reproachful spirit will be inherited by the wicked: and every envious sinner is double-tongued. Do not exalt yourself in the thoughts of your soul like a bull, lest your strength be crushed through foolishness, and your leaves be consumed and your fruits lost, and you be left like a dry tree in the desert. For a wicked soul will destroy the one who has it: and gives it as a joy to his enemies, and leads it into the lot of the ungodly. A sweet word multiplies friends and softens enemies: and a gracious tongue abounds in a good man. Let there be many who are at peace with you, but let your counselor be one in a thousand. If you possess a friend, test him first and do not trust him too quickly. For there is a friend according to his own time, and he will not remain in the day of trouble. And there is a friend who turns to enmity, and there is a friend who will reveal quarrel and strife and reproaches. And there is a friend who is a companion at the table, and will not remain in the day of need. If a friend remains steadfast, he will be to you as yourself, and will act with confidence in your household. If he humbles himself before you and hides from your face, you will have lost a good friendship. Separate yourself from your enemies, and be watchful of your friends. A faithful friend is a strong protection: and he who finds one finds a treasure. A faithful friend has no equal: and no weight of gold and silver can match the goodness of his faith. A faithful friend is a medicine of life and immortality: and those who fear the Lord will find such a friend. Whoever fears God will likewise have a good friendship: for according to him so also will his friend be.

My son, from your youth receive instruction: and until your old age you will find wisdom. Come to her as one who plows and sows, and wait for her good fruits. For in working with her you will labor but a little, and soon you will eat of her produce. How very harsh is wisdom to the unlearned: and the foolish will not remain with her. As a stone of testing, so shall she prove them, and they will not delay to cast her aside. For the wisdom of doctrine is according to her name, and she is not manifest to many. But she is known to all those who are in the sight of God. Hear, my son, and receive the counsel of understanding, and do not reject my advice. Put your feet into her fetters and your neck into her chain. Submit your shoulder and carry her, and do not be weary of her bonds. Come to her with all your soul, and keep her ways with all your strength. Search for her and she will reveal herself to you: and when you have found her do not forsake her. For at last you will find rest in her, and she will be turned into your joy. And her fetters will be your strong defense and her chains a robe of glory. For there is beauty of life in her, and her bonds are a saving bond. You will put on her as a robe of glory, and you will place upon yourself a crown of rejoicing. My son, if you listen to me you will learn, and if you apply your mind you will become wise. If you incline your ear you will receive instruction: and if you love to listen you will become wise. Stand in the assembly of the elders who are wise, and join yourself to their wisdom with all your heart, that you may hear every discourse about God, and that proverbs of praise may not escape you. And if you see a man of understanding, go to him early, and let your foot wear out his doorstep.

Ecclesiasticus.

Do not contend with a powerful man, lest you fall into his hands. Do not quarrel with a rich man, lest he bring a lawsuit against you. For gold and silver have ruined many, and have reached even to the hearts of kings and overthrown them. Do not quarrel with a man who is a slanderer, and do not add fuel to his fire. Do not associate with an ignorant man, lest he speak ill of your family. Do not despise one who turns away from sin, nor reproach him for it. Remember that we are all subject to corruption. Do not mock a man in his old age, for some of us also grow old. Do not rejoice over a dead enemy; remember that we all die and wish to come to a good end. Do not neglect the discourse of wise elders, and converse among their proverbs, for from them you will learn wisdom and understanding, and how to serve great men without complaint. Do not miss the accounts of the elders, for they learned from their own fathers; from them you will learn understanding, and in time of need you will have an answer to give. Do not kindle the coals of sinners by rebuking them, lest you be burned by the flame of their fire. Do not stand against an insolent man, lest he sit as a spy upon your lips. Do not lend to one mightier than yourself; and if you lend, count it as lost. Do not be surety beyond your means; and if you have given surety, think of it as something you must repay. Do not give judgment against a judge, for he judges according to what is just. Do not go on a journey with a reckless man, lest he burden you with his troubles, for he goes according to his own will, and you will perish together through his foolishness. Do not pick a fight with an angry man, and do not go with a bold man into a deserted place, for blood is nothing to him, and where there is no help, he will strike you down. When you have no trustworthy counsel, do not act, for they cannot love except what is pleasing to themselves. Do not take counsel before a stranger, for you do not know what he will bring forth. Do not reveal your heart to every man, lest he repay you with ingratitude and reproach you. Chapter 10.

Do not be jealous over the wife of your bosom, lest she show you the malice of wicked teaching. Do not give power over your soul to a woman, lest she enter into your strength and you be put to shame. Do not look upon a flirtatious woman, lest you fall into her snares. Do not keep company with a dancing-girl, nor listen to her, lest you be caught by her wiles. Do not gaze upon a virgin, lest you be scandalized by her beauty. Do not give your soul to harlots, lest you destroy your inheritance. Do not look about in the streets of the city, nor wander in its squares. Turn your face away from a well-dressed woman, and do not gaze upon the beauty of another. Many have perished by the beauty of a woman, and by it desire burns like fire. Every woman who is a harlot is like dung in the way; she is trodden underfoot by all who pass by. Many have been ruined by admiring the beauty of another man's wife; for conversation with her burns like fire. Do not sit at all with another man's wife, nor lie with her upon a couch; and do not argue with her over wine, lest your heart turn toward her, and in your blood you slip into ruin. Do not forsake an old friend, for a new one will not be like him. A new wine is a new friend; when it grows old, you will drink it with pleasure. Do not envy the glory and riches of sinners, for you do not know what their downfall will be. Do not take pleasure in the wrong done by the unjust, knowing that the wicked will not go unpunished even to the grave. Stay far from a man who has power to kill.

Ecclesiasticus.

having the power to kill, and you will not suspect the fear of death. And if you approach him, commit nothing to him, lest perhaps he take away your life. Know the fellowship of death: because you shall walk in the midst of snares, and upon the arms of the grieving. According to your strength beware of your neighbor: and deal with the wise and prudent. Let just men be your companions: and glory in the fear of God: and let the thought of God be in your mind: and all your discourse on the commandments of the Most High. Works shall be praised by the hand of craftsmen: and the prince of the people by the wisdom of his speech: but the word of the ancients by their sense. A man full of tongue is terrible in his city: and he that is rash in his word shall be hated. Chapter 10.
A wise judge shall instruct his people: and the government of a man of understanding shall be well ordered. As the judge of the people is himself, so also are his ministers: and what manner of man the ruler of a city is, such also are they that dwell therein. An unwise king shall ruin his people: but cities shall be inhabited through the prudence of the rulers. The power of the earth is in the hand of God: and in his time he will raise up a profitable ruler over it. The power of a man is in the hand of God: and upon the person of the scribe he will lay honor. Remember not any injury done to your neighbor: and do nothing in works of injury. Pride is hateful before God and men: and all iniquity of nations is execrable. A kingdom is translated from one people to another because of injustices and injuries and diverse deceits. But nothing is more wicked to the covetous. What is more unworthy than earth and ashes? There is not a more wicked thing than to love money. For such a one even sets his own soul up for sale: because in his lifetime he has cast away his innermost self. All power is of short life: a lingering sickness grieves the physician. The physician cuts short a brief illness: so also the king is today, and tomorrow he shall die. For when a man dies, he shall inherit serpents and beasts and worms. The beginning of the pride of man is to fall off from God: because his heart is departed from him that made him: because pride is the beginning of all sin. He that holds to it shall be filled with curses: and it shall overturn him in the end. Therefore the Lord has disgraced the assemblies of the wicked: and has destroyed them unto the end. The Lord has overthrown the thrones of proud princes: and has set up the meek in their place. The Lord has made the roots of proud nations to wither: and has planted the humble of those nations. The Lord has overturned the lands of the nations: and has destroyed them even to the foundation. He has made some of them to wither and has destroyed them: and has made the memory of them to cease from the earth. The Lord has destroyed the memory of the proud: and has preserved the memory of those who are humble in mind. Pride was not made for men: nor wrath for the race of women. The seed of men shall honor him that fears God: but he that honors not shall dishonor the commandments of the Lord. In the midst of brethren their leader is in honor: and they that fear the Lord shall be in his eyes. The glory of the rich and honored and the poor is the fear of God: despise not the just poor man: and do not magnify the sinful rich man. The great man and the judge and the powerful is in honor: but there is none greater than he that fears God. They that are free shall serve a wise servant: and a man that is prudent and well instructed will not murmur: and he that is inferior shall not be honored. Do not boast in doing your work: and do not be slow in the time of distress. Better is he that labors and abounds in all things: than he that boasts himself and lacks bread. Son, preserve your soul in meekness: and give it honor according to its desert. To the sinner in his own soul

Ecclesiasticus.

Who will justify him? And who will honor one who dishonors his own soul? The poor man is honored through his discipline and fear of God: and there is a man who is honored for his wealth. But he who is glorified in poverty — how much more in wealth. And he who is glorified in wealth, let him fear poverty. Chapter 11.

Wisdom will exalt the head of the humble, and will make him sit in the midst of great men. Do not praise a man for his beauty, nor despise a man for his appearance. The bee is small among flying things, yet her fruit has the beginning of sweetness. Do not boast about your clothing and apparel, nor exalt yourself in the day of your honor, for the works of the Most High alone are wonderful, and his works are glorious and hidden and unseen. Many tyrants have sat upon a throne, and one whom no one would have thought of has worn the crown. Many mighty men have been greatly brought down, and the glorious have been delivered into the hands of others. Before you examine, do not find fault with anyone, and when you have examined, reprove justly. Before you hear, do not answer a word, and in the midst of elders do not interrupt. Do not meddle in matters that do not concern you, and in the judgment of sinners do not sit. My son, do not busy yourself with many matters, and if you are rich, you will not be free from sin. For if you pursue, you will not overtake, and if you flee, you will not escape. There is a man who labors and hurries and is in grief, and who is all the more lacking. There is a feeble man who needs help, who is very weak and full of poverty: and the eye of God looked upon him for good and lifted him out of his low estate and raised up his head, and many were amazed at him and gave honor to God. Good things and evil, life and death, poverty and wealth, are from God. Wisdom

and knowledge of the law are with the Lord: love and the ways of good things are with him. Error and darkness are created with sinners. He who exults in evil will grow old in evil. The gift of God remains with the just, and his advancement will have success forever. There is one who grows rich by living sparingly, and this is the portion of his reward: when he says, "I have found rest for myself, and now I will eat of my goods alone." And he does not know what time will pass, and death draws near, and he must leave all to others and die. Be steadfast in your covenant and be familiar with it, and grow old in the work of your commandments. Do not abide in the works of sinners. Trust in God and stay in your place, for it is easy in the eyes of God to make the poor man suddenly rich. The blessing of God hastens to reward the just, and in his honor his progress flourishes quickly. Do not say: "What do I need, and what good things shall come to me from this?" Do not say: "I have enough for myself, and what harm can come to me from now on?" In the day of good things, do not be forgetful of evils, and in the day of evils, do not be forgetful of good things: for it is easy before God on the day of death to repay each man according to his ways. The evil of an hour causes one to forget great luxury, and at the end of a man his deeds are revealed. Before death, do not praise any man, for a man is known by his children. Do not bring every man into your house, for many are the snares of the deceitful. For as the bowels of putrid things belch forth, and as a partridge is lured into a cage, and as a deer into a snare, so also is the heart of the proud: and like a scout who watches for the fall of his neighbor. For he turns good things to evil and lays ambushes, and puts a stain on the chosen. From a single spark a fire grows, and from one deceitful man bloodshed increases: but the sinful man

Ecclesiasticus.

He who is harsh in spirit toward you will endure your words and will not spare you from malice and bonds. Take care and listen diligently to what I have heard: for you walk with your own ruin. You will hear words as if in dreams: and you will keep watch all your life. Love God and call upon him for your salvation. Every living creature loves its own kind, and every person loves those like himself. Every creature associates with its own kind, and every person keeps company with those like himself. What does a wolf have in common with a lamb? So too the sinner with the just. What fellowship does a holy man have with a dog? Or what portion do the rich share with the poor? The wild ass is the lion's prey in the wilderness: so too the poor are the feeding ground of the rich. Humility is an abomination to the proud: so too the poor man is a reproach to the rich. When a rich man is shaken, he is supported by his friends: but when the humble man falls, he is driven away even by his acquaintances. When a rich man stumbles, many help him recover: he speaks arrogantly and they justify him. When the humble man errs, he is rebuked besides. He speaks wisely and is given no place. The rich man speaks and all are silent: and they carry his words up to the clouds. The poor man speaks and they say: Who is this? And if he stumbles, they will overthrow him. Good is a man's substance when there is no sin in his conscience: and poverty is very bitter in the mouth of the ungodly. The heart of a man changes his countenance, whether for good or for evil. A good heart and a good face you will scarcely find, and with great effort.

Blessed is the man who has not slipped with his mouth, and who has not been stung with the grief of sin. Happy is he who has not had sadness of soul and who has not fallen away from his hope. For the greedy and covetous man without reason there is trouble: and for the envious man what purpose does it serve? Whatever he gathers, another will enjoy in luxury. Who is he that is unkind to himself? To whom will he be good? He will not take pleasure in his own goods. He who envies himself, there is none worse than he: and this is the punishment of his wickedness. And if he does good, he does it unknowingly and unwillingly, and in the end reveals his malice. The eye of the envious man is wicked: he turns away his face and despises his own soul. The eye of the covetous man is insatiable in his share of iniquity: he will not be satisfied until he has consumed his own soul, drying it up. An evil eye looks toward evil things: and he will not be satisfied with bread, being in want, and at the table he shall be wretched. My son, if you have the means, treat yourself well and bring worthy offerings to God. Remember that death does not delay, and the covenant of the underworld has been shown to you. For the covenant of this world will pass away at death. Before your death, do good to your friend, and according to your ability, reach out and give to the poor. Do not deprive yourself of a good day, and let no part of a good gift pass you by. Will you not leave your sorrows and toils to others? In the division of a lot, give and receive, and justify your soul. Before your death, practice justice, for there is no seeking comfort in the underworld. All flesh grows old like grass, and like a leaf that flourishes on a green tree. Some are born and others fall away: so is the generation of flesh and blood — one ends and another is born. Every corruptible work will fail in the end: and he who does it will pass away with it. And every excellent work will be justified: and he who performs it will be honored in it. Blessed is the man who dwells in wisdom and who meditates on justice: and who in his understanding reflects on the watchful care of God. He who ponders God's ways in his heart, and understands his hidden things, going forth...

Ecclesiasticus

He who pursues her like a tracker, lying in wait along her paths, who peers through her windows and listens at her doors, who camps near her house and drives a stake in her walls, who pitches his tent close to her hand, and finds good shelter in her dwelling. He places his children under her care, and under her branches they shall dwell. She will shelter him from the heat under her protection, and he shall find rest in her glory. Chapter 15.

He who fears God will do good deeds, and he who holds fast to justice will attain her. She will come to meet him like a mother, and will receive him like a young bride. She will feed him with the bread of life and understanding, and give him water of saving wisdom to drink. He will be strengthened in her and will not be shaken; he will hold him and not be put to shame; she will exalt him among his neighbors. In the midst of the assembly she will open his mouth, and fill him with a spirit of wisdom and understanding, and clothe him with a robe of glory. She will store up for him joy and gladness, and he will inherit an everlasting name. Foolish people will not obtain her, and sinners will not encounter her. She is far removed from pride and deceit. Liars will not remember her, but truthful people will be found with her, and they will succeed until God's inspection comes. Praise is not fitting in the mouth of a sinner, for it has not been granted to him by God. For praise shall remain with the wisdom of God, and shall abound in the mouth of the faithful, and the Lord will give it to him. Do not say: "It is through God's doing that I fell away," for he does not do what he hates. Do not say, "He led me astray," for he has no need of sinful people. The Lord hates every kind of abomination and error, and it will not be loved by those who fear him. God made humanity from the beginning, and left them in the hand of their own counsel. He added his commandments and precepts. If you are willing to keep his commandments, they will preserve you and keep faith pleasingly forever. He has set before you fire and water; reach out your hand for whichever you wish. Before each person are life and death; whichever they prefer will be given to them. For the wisdom of God is great, he is mighty in power, and sees all things without ceasing. The eyes of God look upon those who fear him; he knows every deed of man. He has not commanded anyone to act wickedly, nor has he given anyone license to sin. For he did not desire a multitude of faithless and useless children. Chapter 16.

Do not rejoice in ungodly children if they multiply; do not delight in them if there is no fear of God in them. Do not trust in their life, and do not rely on their toil. For one who fears God is better than a thousand ungodly children. It is better to die childless than to leave ungodly children. Through one sensible person a city is populated, but through three ungodly ones it is made desolate. Many such things my eye has seen, and my ear has heard things even more striking than these. In the assembly of sinners a fire will be kindled, and wrath blazes up against a disobedient nation. The ancient giants did not obtain pardon for their sins; they were destroyed because they trusted in their own strength, and God did not spare their journey but struck them down and cast them away in their pride. He showed no mercy to the whole nation of those who perished, who lifted themselves up in their sins. And like six hundred thousand foot soldiers who were gathered in the hardness of their heart: even if there had been just one stiff-necked person, it would have been a wonder if he had gone unpunished. For mercy and wrath are with him; he is mighty to forgive and to pour out wrath. As great as his mercy is, so also is his correction: he judges a man according to his deeds.

Ecclesiasticus

He will judge what is his own. The sinner will not escape through robbery, and the patience of one who shows mercy will not be delayed. Every act of mercy will find its place with each person, according to the merit of their works and according to the understanding of their journey. Do not say: I will be hidden from God, and who from on high will remember me? In so great a creation I will not be known. For what is my soul among so vast a creation? Behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens, the abyss and all the earth, and all that is in them will tremble at his presence: mountains and hills together, and the foundations of the earth — when God looks upon them, they tremble with trembling. And in all these things the heart is without sense, yet every heart is known by him: and who understands his ways? And a storm which no human eye has seen? The works of God are many and hidden, but who shall declare the works of his justice, and who shall endure them? For the covenant is far from some, and the questioning of men reaches its end. One of little heart thinks vain things, and the imprudent and erring man thinks foolish things. Hear me, my son, and learn the discipline of understanding, and attend in your heart to my words: and I will speak in equity of discipline, and I will endeavor to set forth wisdom; and attend in your heart to my words: and I speak in equity of spirit of the virtues which God placed in his works from the beginning, and in truth I declare his knowledge. In the judgment of God his works are from the beginning: and from the institution of men he divided their portions and their beginnings among their nations. He adorned their works: they did not hunger nor labor, and they did not cease from their works. No man shall crowd his neighbor for eternity. Do not be unbelieving in him. After these things God looked upon the earth and filled it with his good things. And the soul of every living thing declared before his face, and to him is their return. Chapter XVII.

God created man from the earth, and made him according to his own image. And again he turned him back to it, and clothed him according to himself with strength. He gave them a number of days and time, and gave him power over the things upon the earth. He placed the fear of him over all flesh, and he has dominion over beasts and birds. He created from him a helper like himself; he gave them counsel, tongue, eyes, ears, and heart to think with; and he filled them with the discipline of understanding. He created in them the knowledge of the spirit; he filled their heart with understanding, and showed them good and evil. He set his eye upon their hearts, and showed them the greatness of his works, so that they might praise the name of his glory and tell of his wondrous works. And they shall declare the greatness of his works. He added to them discipline and gave them the law of life as an inheritance. He established an everlasting covenant with them, and showed them his justice and judgments. Their eyes saw the majesty of his glory, and their ears heard the honor of his voice, and he said to them: Beware of all wrongdoing. And he commanded each of them concerning his neighbor. Their ways are always before him; they are not hidden from his eyes. Over every nation he appointed a ruler, and the portion of God, Israel, was made manifest. And all their works are like the sun before God, and his eyes look without ceasing upon their ways. Their deeds are not hidden for iniquity, and all their iniquities are before God. Almsgiving from a man abides with him as a treasure, and his gracious deed shall preserve him like the apple of an eye; and afterward he shall rise and God will repay each one upon his own head, and will turn them into the lower parts of the earth. But to the penitent he has given the way of justice.

Ecclesiasticus (Sirach)

and justice: and they implored public and private judgments after your lusts, do not go: and turn away from your will. If you give your soul over to its desires, it will make you a joy to your enemies. Do not take delight in crowds, nor in their ways. Your constant companion is their transgression. Do not be indifferent in your promises of reward: and let nothing in the world be hidden from you. Your soul envies you. Chapter 19.
A drunken laborer will not grow rich: and he who despises small things will gradually decline. Wine and women make wise men fall away, and will reprove the sensible: and he who joins himself to harlots will be wicked. Rottenness and worms will inherit him: and he will be held up as a greater example: and he will be taken away from among the number of souls. He who believes quickly is light of heart and will be diminished: and he who sins against his own soul will be despised besides. He who rejoices in wickedness will be denounced: and he who hates correction will have his life diminished: and he who hates talkativeness extinguishes malice. He who sins against his own soul will not repent: and he who delights in wickedness will be devoured. Do not repeat a harsh word and it will multiply: and do not tell it to a friend or enemy, and if you have a fault, do not reveal it. For he will listen to you and watch you: and as if defending a sin, he will hate you: and so he will always be present with you. Have you heard a word against your neighbor? Let it die within you: knowing that it will not burst out of you. From a matter a fool is born: like the birth pangs of an infant. An arrow lodged in the thigh of a dog: so is a word in the heart of a fool. Correct a friend lest perhaps he did not understand and say I did not do it: or if he did it, lest he should do it again. Correct your friend first, lest perhaps he should not have said it: and if he said it, lest he repeat it. Correct a friend: for often a transgression occurs: and do not believe every word. There is one who slips with his tongue,

but not in his heart. For who has not offended with his tongue? Correct your friend before you threaten: and give place to the fear of the Most High: for the fear of God is all wisdom: And in that fear of God: and in all wisdom is the disposition of the law. But the wisdom of wickedness is not discipline: and the thoughts of sinners are not prudence. There is a cleverness that is abominable: and there is a fool who lacks wisdom. Better is a man who has less wisdom and lacks understanding in the fear of God: than one who abounds in understanding and transgresses the law of the Most High. There is an astuteness that is precise and yet unjust: and there is one who speaks a certain word declaring the truth. There is one who humbles himself wickedly, and his inward parts are full of deceit: and there is a just man who bows himself down with much humility: and there is a just man who inclines his face and pretends not to see what he does not know. And if through weakness of strength he is afraid to sin: if he finds the opportunity for evil, he will do evil. A man is known by his appearance: and a wise man is known by the look of his face. A man's clothing, and his laughter, and his gait, declare what he is. There is a correction that is deceitful and there is anger full of insult: and there is a judgment that is not proved to be good: and he who is silent is himself wise. Chapter 20.
How much better it is to reprove than to be angry: and not to hinder one who confesses in prayer. The lust of a eunuch deflowered a young maiden: so he who by violence does unjust judgment. How good it is for a reproved person to show repentance: for so you will escape voluntary sin. There is one who is silent and is found wise: and there is one who is hateful because he is too ready to speak. There is one who is silent because he has no sense to speak: and there is one who is silent knowing that the time calls for it. A wise man will be silent until the proper time:

Ecclesiasticus (Sirach)

The lewd and imprudent man will not observe the right time. He who uses many words injures his own soul, and he who takes authority for himself unjustly will be hated. There is a course of evil things for the undisciplined man, and discovery of it leads to his harm. There is a gift that is not worthless, and there is a gift whose recompense is double. There is humiliation for the sake of glory, and there is one who will lift up his head from a low estate. There is one who redeems many things for a small price, and repays them sevenfold. The wise man makes himself loved by his words, but the graces of fools are poured out in vain. The gift of a fool shall do you no good; his eyes are sevenfold. He gives little and reproaches much, and the opening of his mouth is an inflammation. Today he lends, and tomorrow he asks it back; such a man is hateful. A fool will have no friend, and there will be no thanks for his good deeds. For those who eat his bread are of a false tongue. How often and how many will mock him! For he does not distribute what he should have rightly, nor likewise what he should not have kept. The slip of a false tongue is as one who falls on the pavement; so the fall of the wicked shall come quickly. A foolish man is like a vain tale, and it shall be ever in the mouths of the undisciplined. From the mouth of a fool a proverb shall be rejected, for he does not speak it at the proper time. There is one who is kept from sinning by poverty, and is pricked in his rest. There is one who will destroy his soul through shame, and through a lack of prudence will lose what might have been his glory, and will destroy himself through false respect. There is one who for shame makes promises to a friend, and has made him an enemy for nothing. Reproach is an evil thing in a lying man, and it shall be ever in the mouth of the undisciplined. A thief is better than a man who is always lying; yet both shall inherit destruction. The ways of lying men are without honor, and their confusion is with them without ceasing. The wise man advances himself by his words, and a prudent man shall please great men. He who tills his land shall raise his harvest high, and he who works justice shall himself be exalted; but he who pleases great men shall escape iniquity. Gifts and presents blind the eyes of judges, and like one who is dumb in the mouth, they turn away corrections. Hidden wisdom and unseen treasure — what profit is there in either? Better is one who hides his foolishness than the man who hides his wisdom. Chapter 21.

My son, have you sinned? Do so no more, but pray for your former sins to be forgiven you. Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent; for if you draw near it, it will seize you. Its teeth are like the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men. All iniquity is like a two-edged sword; the wound it makes has no healing. Strife and injury will cause wealth to be destroyed, and the house of the arrogant shall be overthrown; so the substance of the proud shall be rooted out. The prayer of the poor man shall reach from his mouth to the ears of God, and judgment shall come swiftly to his aid. He who hates correction walks in the steps of a sinner, and he who fears the Lord will return to his own heart. He who is known from afar is bold of tongue, but the sensible man knows when he is about to slip. He who builds his house with another man's money is like one who gathers his stones in winter. The assembly of sinners is like tow gathered together, and their end is a flame of fire. The way of sinners is paved with smooth stones, but at its end is the pit of hell, and darkness, and torment. He who keeps justice shall maintain his understanding; the perfection of the fear of God is wisdom and understanding. He who is not wise in good shall not be instructed; but there is a folly that abounds in evil, and there is

Sirach (Ecclesiasticus)

Tears and sighs pierce the heart. One who throws stones at birds scares them away; one who reproaches a friend destroys friendship. If you have drawn a sword against a friend, do not despair, for there is a way back. If a friend opens his mouth in sadness, do not fear, for there is reconciliation; except in the case of insult, arrogance, pride, revealing of secrets, and a treacherous blow. In all these things a friend will flee. Stand by your friend in his poverty, so that you may also rejoice in his good fortune. In the time of his trouble remain faithful to him, so that you may be heir with him in his inheritance. Before fire rises the vapor and smoke of the furnace; so too does insult precede bloodshed and strife. I will not be ashamed to greet a friend; and I will not hide from his face; and if evil comes to me through him, I will endure it. Whoever hears will beware of him. Who will give a guard to my mouth and a sure seal upon my lips, so that I may not fall by them and my tongue destroy me?

O Lord, Father and Master of my life, do not abandon me to their counsel and design; do not let me fall by them. Who has set a scourge over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over my heart, so that in my ignorance I may not spare myself, and that my sins may not appear, and that the errors of my thoughts may not increase and my offenses multiply; lest I fall before my adversaries and my enemy rejoice over me? O Lord, Father and God of my life, do not give me proud eyes; turn away all desire from me. Take from me the lusts of the belly and let not the desires of the flesh take hold of me, and do not give me over to a shameless and foolish soul.

Hear, children, the instruction of the mouth; and he who keeps it will not perish by his lips, nor will he be scandalized in his most wicked works. The sinner will be caught in his vanity; and the proud and evil-speaking man will be scandalized by them. Let not your mouth be accustomed to swearing, for there is much falling in it. And let not the naming of God be frequent in your mouth; and do not associate with the names of holy ones; for you will not be held innocent of them. For as a servant who is constantly examined under the lash is not left without a mark, so also whoever swears and utters the Name will not be entirely cleansed from sin. A man who swears many oaths will be filled with iniquity, and the scourge will not depart from his house. If he offends, his sin will be upon him; and if he disregards it, he sins doubly; and if he swears in vain, he will not be justified. For his house will be filled with retribution. There is also another manner of speech that is contrary to death; let it not be found in the inheritance of Jacob. For from the merciful all these things will be taken away; and they will not delight in sins. Do not let your mouth be accustomed to undisciplined speech, for in it there is sinful talk. Remember your father and your mother, for you stand in the midst of great men; lest God forget you in their sight, and you be made foolish by your daily conduct, and suffer disgrace, and wish you had never been born, and curse the day of your birth. A man who is accustomed to insulting words will not be corrected all the days of his life. Two kinds of people multiply sins, and a third brings wrath and destruction. A hot-burning soul is like a blazing fire; it will not be quenched until it has devoured something. A wicked man in the desires of his flesh will not cease until he kindles a fire. To a fornicating man all bread is sweet; he will not grow weary of transgressing

Ecclesiasticus (Sirach)

...to the end. Every man who transgresses his own bed, saying in his soul, "Who sees me? Darkness surrounds me, the walls cover me, and no one looks upon me — what do I fear? The Most High will not remember my sins" — he does not understand that His eye sees all things, that such a man's fear is but the fear of human eyes. He did not know that the eyes of the Lord are far brighter than the sun, observing all the ways of men and the depths of the abyss, and looking into the hidden parts of the heart. All things were known to the Lord God before they were created; so also after their completion He beholds all things. This man will be punished in the streets of the city, and will be seized where he did not expect. So it is with a woman who leaves her husband and brings forth an heir by a stranger. For first she was disobedient to the law of the Most High; second, she forsook her husband; third, she committed adultery in fornication and brought forth children by another man. She shall be brought before the assembly, and judgment shall fall upon her children. Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bear no fruit. She shall leave her memory as a curse, and her dishonor shall not be blotted out. And they who remain shall acknowledge that nothing is better than the fear of God, and nothing sweeter than to observe the commandments of the Lord. It is great glory to follow the Lord, for length of days shall be received from Him.

Chapter (24):

Wisdom shall praise herself, and shall be honored in God. She shall glory in the midst of her people, and shall open her mouth in the assemblies of the Most High. She shall glorify herself in the presence of His power, and shall be exalted in the midst of her people. In the holy assembly she shall be admired, and among the chosen she shall have praise, and among the blessed she shall be blessed, saying: I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, the firstborn before all creation. I made an unfailing light to rise in the heavens, and like a mist I covered all the earth. I dwelt in the highest places, and my throne is in a pillar of cloud. I alone circled the vault of heaven and walked in the depths of the abyss, and walked upon the waves of the sea, and stood in all the earth. And in every people and in every nation I held primacy, and by my strength I have trodden down the hearts of all, both great and humble. And in all these things I sought rest, and I shall abide in the inheritance of the Lord. Then the Creator of all things commanded me, and He who created me rested in my tabernacle, and said to me: Dwell in Jacob, and take your inheritance in Israel, and put down roots among my chosen ones. From the beginning and before the ages I was created, and I shall not cease until the age to come, and in the holy dwelling place I ministered before Him. And thus I was established in Zion, and likewise I rested in the sanctified city, Jerusalem, and my power was there. I took root in an honored people, and my portion is in the inheritance of God, and my dwelling is in the fullness of the saints. I was exalted like a cedar in Lebanon, and like a cypress on Mount Zion. I was exalted like a palm tree in Cades, and like a rose plant in Jericho. Like a fair olive tree in the fields, and like a plane tree I was exalted beside the water in the streets. Like cinnamon and aromatic balm, I gave forth fragrance; like choice myrrh I gave a sweet odor: like storax and galbanum, and onycha and gum, and like frankincense not cut I filled my dwelling with fragrance:

Ecclesiasticus (Sirach)

And my fragrance is like pure balsam. I stretched out my branches like a terebinth, and my branches are branches of honor and grace. Like a vine I produced a sweet fragrance, and my blossoms are the fruit of honor and nobility. I am the mother of fair love, and of fear, and of knowledge, and of holy hope. In me is all grace of the way and of truth; in me is all hope of life and of virtue. Come to me, all you who desire me, and be filled with my fruits. For my spirit is sweet above honey, and my inheritance above honey and the honeycomb; my memory endures unto all generations. Those who eat me will still hunger, and those who drink me will still thirst. He who hears me will not be put to shame, and those who work through me will not sin; those who make me known will have eternal life. All these things are the book of life, and the covenant of the Most High, and the knowledge of truth. Moses commanded us a law in the precepts of justice, and an inheritance to the house of Jacob and the promises to Israel. He raised up for David his servant a most mighty king, seated on the throne of honor forever. He fills with wisdom like the Pison, and like the Tigris in the days of new things. He overflows with understanding like the Euphrates, and multiplies it like the Jordan at harvest time. He sends forth discipline like the light, and stands by like the Geon at the time of vintage. He who first came to understand her has not fully searched her out, and the weakest will not find her. For her thoughts are vaster than the sea, and her counsels deeper than the great abyss. I, Wisdom, have poured out rivers; I, like a canal from a mighty river, have given water. I said: I will water my garden and will water abundantly the fruits of my field. And behold,

my stream became a great river, and my river came near to a sea. For I cause the light of doctrine to shine forth for all like the dawn, and I will tell of it even to distant lands. I will penetrate all the lower parts of the earth, and will look upon all who sleep, and will enlighten all who hope in the Lord. I will still pour out teaching like prophecy, and leave it to those who seek wisdom; I will not cease from generation to generation unto the holy age. See that I have not labored for myself alone, but for all who seek truth. Three things are pleasing to my spirit, which are approved before God and men: concord among brothers, and love among neighbors, and a man and woman who are well suited to each other. Three kinds of persons my soul hates, and I am greatly grieved at their manner of life: a proud poor man, a lying rich man, and an old fool without understanding. What you have not gathered in your youth, how will you find it in your old age? How fitting is sound judgment in the aged, and understanding and counsel in those who are venerable! How fitting is wisdom in the elderly, and discernment and counsel in those who are honored! Experience is a crown to the aged, and their glory is the fear of God. The unsearchable things of the heart have been magnified, and I shall speak of them in ten sayings with my tongue. A man who rejoices in his children, living and seeing the subjugation of his enemies. Blessed is he who lives with a sensible woman, and who has not slipped with his tongue, and who has not served those unworthy of him. Blessed is he who finds a true friend, and who speaks of justice to an attentive ear. How great is the one who finds wisdom and understanding! But none surpasses the one who fears God. The fear of God is above all things. Blessed is the man to whom it is given to have the fear of God. He who holds to it — to whom shall he be compared?

(Title header: Ecclesiasticus / Sirach)

A warrior who fails through poverty, and a man of understanding who is despised, and one who turns from justice to sin — God has prepared him for the sword. Two kinds of things appeared to me as difficult and dangerous. A merchant is hardly free from negligence, and an innkeeper will not be justified from the sins of his lips. Chapter 27.

On account of poverty many have sinned, and he who seeks to enrich himself turns away his eyes. As a peg is driven between joined stones, so sin will wedge itself between buying and selling. Sin will be ground down between those who transgress. If you do not hold firmly to the fear of the Lord, your house will quickly be overthrown. As dust remains in the sieve when it is shaken, so do the troubles of a man in his own thoughts. The furnace tests the potter's vessels, and the trial of tribulation tests men. As the fruit of a tree reveals the care given it, so the word of a man reveals the thoughts of his heart. Praise no man before he has spoken, for this is the test of men. If you pursue justice, you shall obtain it and put it on as a garment of glory; you shall dwell with it and it shall protect you forever, and on the day of reckoning you shall find a firm foundation. Birds flock with their own kind, and truth returns to those who practice it. The lion lies in wait for prey always; so too sin waits for those who do evil. A man who is glad in wisdom abides like the sun, but a fool changes like the moon. Among the simple, keep your words for the right moment, and be constant in meditating. The telling of sins is odious, and the laughter of the wicked is in the pleasure of sin. Speech full of oaths makes the hair stand on end, and its irreverence stops up the ears. The shedding of blood in the quarrels of the proud, and the curses they utter, are grievous to hear. He who reveals the secrets of a friend destroys trust, and will not find a kindred soul. Love your neighbor and keep faith with him. But if you reveal his secrets, do not go after him. For as a man who has destroyed his friend, so is one who destroys the friendship of his neighbor. And as one who lets a bird slip from his hand, so have you let your neighbor go and will not catch him again. Do not pursue him, for he is gone far away. He has escaped like a gazelle from the snare, for his soul has been wounded. You can no longer bind him, and reconciliation is impossible. To reveal the secrets of a friend is the despair of an unhappy soul. He who winks with the eye devises evil things, and no one will cast him aside. In your presence he will speak sweetly and admire your words, but in the end he will twist his mouth and speak scandal about your words. I have heard many things, but none so bad as this; the Lord will hate him. He who throws a stone on high throws it on his own head, and the treacherous blow will wound the deceitful man. He who digs a pit will fall into it, and he who sets a stone for another will stumble on it, and he who lays a snare for another will perish by it. An evil plan returns upon the one who makes it, and he will not know from where it comes upon him. Mockery and reproach come from the proud, and vengeance will lie in wait for them like a lion. Those who rejoice at the fall of the just will perish in the snare, and pain will consume them before they die. Wrath and anger are abominable things, and the sinful man will continue in them. Chapter 28.

He who seeks vengeance will find vengeance from the Lord, and He will firmly remember his sins. Forgive your neighbor who has wronged you, and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray.

Men seek from God the remedy that they will not grant to one another. A person has no mercy on someone like himself, yet prays to God about his own sins. He who rarely controls his anger seeks reconciliation from God. Who will intercede for his sins? Remember your last days and cease your enmity. For decay and death threaten in his commandments. Remember the fear of the Lord and do not grow angry at once. Remember the covenant of the Most High and overlook your neighbor's ignorance. Refrain from strife and you will lessen your sins. For a hot-tempered man kindles strife, and a sinful man will disturb friends, and casts enmity among those who are at peace. For as the wood of the forest feeds a fire, so does a man's passion feed his anger, and according to his strength will he increase his wrath. A hasty quarrel kindles a fire, and a rushing dispute sheds blood, and a tongue that bears false witness brings death. If you blow upon a spark it will blaze up, and if you spit upon it, it will be quenched; and both come from your mouth. The whisperer and the double-tongued are accursed; for they have troubled many who were at peace. A third tongue has moved many and scattered them from nation to nation. It has destroyed fortified cities and overturned the houses of the great. It has brought down the strength of peoples and undone mighty nations. A third tongue has cast out virtuous women and deprived them of their labors. Whoever heeds it will find no rest, nor will he have a friend to comfort him. The blow of a whip raises a welt, but a blow of the tongue crushes bones. Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not as many as have fallen by the tongue. Blessed is the one who is sheltered from a wicked tongue, who has not passed through its wrath:

and who has not borne its yoke, and has not been bound with its chains. For its yoke is an iron yoke, and its chains are bronze chains. Its death is a most wicked death, and death itself is preferable to it. It will not endure forever, but it will find the paths of the unjust. It will not consume the just in its flame; those who forsake God will fall into it. It will blaze among them and will not be quenched; it will be sent upon them like a lion, and like a leopard it will maul them. Fence in your ears with thorns, and do not listen to a wicked tongue; make doors for your mouth and locks for your ears. Melt down your gold and silver, and make a balance for your words and a proper bridle for your mouth; and take heed lest you slip with your tongue and fall before your enemies who lie in wait for you, and your fall be incurable unto death.

Whoever shows mercy lends to his neighbor, and whoever prevails by hand follows the commandments. Lend first to your neighbor in his time of need, and in turn repay your neighbor in due time. Keep your word and deal faithfully with him, and in every season you will find what you need. Many have regarded lending as a windfall and have caused grief to those who helped them.
