Until they receive, they kiss the hands of the lender, and they humble their voice in making promises. But when repayment is due, they will ask for more time, and will speak words of weariness and complaint, and will make excuses about the time. If he is able to repay, he will be hostile; he will scarcely repay half, and will count it as a good find. But if not, he will defraud the lender of his money, and will have made an enemy for nothing; and will repay him with curses and insults, and for honor and kindness will return him contempt. Many

Galiattinus.

Not for the cause of wickedness should they be avoided: but they feared to be defrauded without cause. Nevertheless, be stronger in spirit toward the humble: and do not reproach him for the alms you give. For the sake of the commandment, take in the poor man: and because of his need, do not send him away empty. Spare your money for the sake of your brother and friend: and do not hide it under a stone to ruin it. Place your treasure in the commandments of the Most High: and it will profit you more than gold. Enclose your alms in the bosom of the poor and it will pray for you against all evil. A man's alms is like a purse with him: and the favor of a man it will preserve like the apple of the eye: and afterward it will rise up and repay them, rendering to each upon their heads. It will fight for you like a strong shield and spear against your enemy. A good man is surety for his neighbor: and one who has lost his sense of shame abandons him. Do not forget the kindness of your guarantor: for he gave his life for you. A sinner and an evil man flees from his guarantor. A sinner attributes the goods of the guarantor to himself: and ungratefully abandons the one who freed him. A man has made promises for his neighbor: and when he loses respect, he abandons him. A most wicked pledge has ruined many who were prospering: and tossed them like waves of the sea. It has driven powerful men into exile: and they wander among foreign peoples. A sinner who transgresses the command of the Lord will fall into an evil pledge: and one who attempts many things will fall into judgment. Recover your neighbor according to your ability: and take heed lest you yourself fall. The beginning of a man's life is water and bread and clothing: and a house protecting from shame. Better is the life of a poor man under a rough shelter than sumptuous meals in a foreign place without a home.

Let a small thing satisfy you instead of a great one: and you will not hear the reproach of wandering. It is a miserable life to go from house to house: and where one lodges, one dare not open one's mouth. He will entertain and feed and give drink to the ungrateful: and on top of this he will hear bitter words. "Pass on, stranger, from my table": and what he has at hand, he will refuse to others. "Go away from the face of my honored friends: I have need of my house for a kinsman." These things are grievous to a man of understanding: the rebuke of a householder and the reproach of a moneylender. c. xxx.

He who loves his son chastises him frequently: so that he may rejoice in him in his latter end, and not grope after the doors of his neighbors. He who teaches his son will be praised in him: and will glory in him in the midst of his household. He who teaches his son makes an enemy jealous: and in the midst of friends he will glory in him. His father is dead, and it is as if he were not dead: for he has left behind one like himself. In his lifetime he saw and rejoiced in him. In his death he was not grieved: nor was he confounded before his enemies. For he left behind a defender of his house against his enemies, and one who repays kindness to friends. For the souls of his sons he will bind up his wounds: and at every voice his heart will be troubled. An untamed horse becomes stubborn: and a pampered son becomes headstrong. Pamper your son and he will terrify you: play with him and he will make you sorrowful. Do not laugh with him lest you have sorrow: and in the end your teeth will be set on edge. Do not give him power in his youth: and do not overlook his follies. Bow down his neck in his youth and beat his sides while he is still a child: lest he grow stubborn and refuse to obey you: and there will be grief of soul to you. Teach your son and work with him: lest you stumble at his shameful behavior.

Ecclesiasticus.

Better is a poor man who is healthy and strong in body than a rich man who is feeble and afflicted with evil. The health of the soul in the sanctity of justice is better than all gold and silver, and a strong body is better than immeasurable wealth. There is no riches above the riches of the health of the body, and there is no gladness above the joy of the heart. Death is better than a bitter life, and eternal rest than continual sickness. Good things hidden in a closed mouth are like morsels of food set about a grave. What does a libation avail an idol? For it can neither eat nor smell. So is he who is persecuted by the Lord, bearing the reward of his iniquity. He looks on with his eyes and groans, like a eunuch embracing a virgin and sighing. Give not grief to your soul, and afflict not yourself in your own counsel. The joy of the heart is the life of a man, and a never-failing treasury of holiness, and the rejoicing of a man is length of life. Have mercy on your own soul, pleasing God, and contain yourself, gather your heart in his holiness, and drive away sadness far from you. For sadness has killed many, and there is no profit in it. Envy and anger shorten a man's days, and pensiveness will bring old age before the time. A cheerful and good heart will care for its meat and drink. Chapter XXXI.

Watching for riches will waste the flesh, and the thought thereof will drive away sleep. The thought of foreknowledge turns away the understanding, and a grievous sickness makes the soul sober. The rich man has labored in gathering riches together, and when he rests he shall be filled with his goods. The poor man has labored in his low way of life, and in the end he is still needy. He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that follows after corruption shall have his fill thereof. Many have been brought to fall for gold, and their destruction was present. Gold is a stumbling block to those who sacrifice to it; woe to them that eagerly follow after it, and every fool shall perish by it. Blessed is the rich man who is found without blemish, and who has not gone after gold, and has not put his hope in money and treasures. Who is he, and we will praise him? For he has done wonderful things in his life. Who has been tried thereby and made perfect, he shall have glory everlasting. He who could have transgressed and has not transgressed, and could have done evil things and has not done them. Therefore his goods are established in the Lord, and all the church of the saints shall declare his alms. If you sit at a great table, open not your mouth wide upon it. Say not: There are many things upon it. Remember that a wicked eye is an evil thing. What has been created more evil than an eye? Therefore it shall weep over all things it sees. Stretch not out your hand first, and be not disgraced by envy. Be not pressed in a banquet with wine. Understand what your neighbor would want. Use as a frugal man the things that are set before you, lest if you eat much, you be hated. Cease first for manners' sake, and be not unsatiable, lest you offend. And if you sit among many persons, reach not your hand out before them, and ask not to drink before others. How sufficient is a little wine for a man well taught, and in sleeping you shall not be troubled by it, and you shall feel no pain. Watching and choler and gripes are with an intemperate man; sound and wholesome sleep with a moderate man. He shall sleep till morning, and his soul shall be delighted with him. And if you have been forced to eat much, arise, go out, and vomit, and it shall refresh you, and you shall not bring sickness upon your body. Hear me, my son, and do not despise me, and in the end you shall find...

Ecclesiasticus.

You will find my words. In all your works be quick, and no illness will befall you. Those who love bread will bless generous lips, and their testimony of truth is trustworthy. The city murmured against the worst bread, and the testimony of its wickedness is true. Do not provoke those who love wine, for wine has destroyed many. Fire tests hard iron; so wine will expose the hearts of the proud when they drink it to drunkenness. Wine is an equal part of life for people when drunk soberly; if you drink it in moderation you will be sober. What is the life that is diminished by wine? What defrauds life? Death. Wine was created for joy, not for drunkenness from the beginning. The exultation of soul and body is wine drunk in moderation. Sobriety in drinking is health for the soul and body. Much wine drunk produces irritation, anger, and many ruins. Bitterness of soul comes from wine drunk without measure. The arrogance of drunkenness is the offense of the imprudent, diminishing virtue and causing wounds. At a wine banquet do not rebuke your neighbor, nor despise him in his joy. Do not speak words of reproach to him, nor press him in reproof. Chapter 32.

They have made you a leader; do not exalt yourself; be among them as one of themselves. Take care of them and so consider: after all your cares, lie down to rest, that you may be refreshed on their account, and receive as an ornament of grace a crown, and gain the dignity of their esteem. Speak, you who are older, for it becomes you. Speak with careful knowledge, and do not hinder the music. Where there is no audience, pour not out words, and do not be untimely in your wisdom. A little gem of carbuncle set in gold, and a comparison of music at a wine banquet. As in the fashioning of gold the mark of the emerald stands out, so does the melody of music at a pleasant and moderate wine banquet. Listen in silence, and for your reverence good grace will come to you. A young man, speak in your own cause only when necessary. If you are asked twice, let your answer be brief. In many things be as one who knows nothing; listen in silence while also seeking to learn. Among the great do not presume to speak, and where elders are, do not talk too much. Before hail comes lightning, and before shame comes favor, and for your reverence good grace will come to you; and at the hour of rising do not hold back. Run ahead first to your house, and there withdraw, and there take your rest, and carry out your plans, and not in luxury and proud speech. And above all these things, the blessing of God who made you, who has filled you to abundance with all his good things. Whoever fears God will receive his teaching, and those who keep watch for him will find blessing. Whoever seeks the law will be filled by it, but whoever acts deceitfully will be scandalized by it. Whoever fears God will find just judgment, and justice will kindle like a light. A sinful man will avoid correction, and according to his own will he will find a justification. A man of counsel will not lose understanding; a stranger and proud man will not know fear. Even after he has acted without counsel, he will be exposed by his own schemes. My son, do nothing without counsel, and after the deed you will not repent. Do not walk on a path of ruin, and you will not stumble on stones; do not trust yourself to a laborious road, lest you place a stumbling block before your soul. Beware also of your children, and be watchful over those of your household. In all your work trust in the faith of your soul, for this is the keeping of the commandments. Whoever believes in God heeds his commandments, and whoever trusts in him will not be diminished. Chapter 33.

Ecclesiasticus (Sirach)

No evil befalls those who fear God; but in temptation God will watch over him and deliver him from evils. The wise man does not hate commandments and justice, and he is not dashed about like a ship in a storm. A sensible man trusts in the law of God, and the law is faithful to him. He who openly acknowledges his questioning will prepare his word, and thus when he prays he will be heard, and he will preserve discipline and then will answer. The heart of a fool is like a cartwheel, and like a rolling axle his thoughts turn. A stallion is like a mocking friend: he neighs under every rider. Why does one day surpass another, when all light comes from the sun, and one year from another? They were separated by the Lord's knowledge, the sun having been made and the commandment kept. And he changed the seasons and the feast days thereof, and in those feast days they celebrated at the appointed hour. And God exalted and glorified some of them, and placed some of them in the number of days, and all men are from the earth, even as Adam was created from the earth. With his great discipline the Lord separated them and changed their ways. Of them he blessed and exalted; and of them he sanctified and drew to himself; and of them he cursed and humbled, and turned them to their separation; as clay of the potter in his hand, to fashion it and dispose of it. All his ways are according to his arrangement; so too is man in the hand of him who made him, and he will render to him according to his own judgment. Good is the opposite of evil, and life is the opposite of death; so too the sinner is the opposite of the just man. Look thus upon all the works of the Most High. Two and two, and one opposite the other. I, the last, have kept watch, and like one who gathers after the grape-pickers. By the blessing of God I also hoped, and like one who harvests I filled the winepress. Look, for I have not labored for myself alone, but

for all who seek discipline. Hear me, you great men and all people, and you rulers of the church, give ear. To son and wife, to brother and friend, do not give power over yourself in your lifetime, and do not give your possessions to another, lest you repent of it and have to beg for them. While you still live and have breath, let no flesh change you. It is better that your children should ask of you than that you should look to the hand of your sons. In all your works be excellent. Do not let a blemish diminish your glory. In the day of the end of the days of your life, and at the time of your departure, distribute your inheritance. For a donkey, fodder and a stick and a burden; for a servant, bread and discipline and work. Your servant works under discipline and seeks rest; leave his hands idle and he seeks freedom. A yoke and a strap bend a stiff neck, and continual tasks bend the behavior of a servant. Torture and chains are for a malicious slave; send him to work so that he is not idle. For idleness has taught much mischief. Set him to work, for so it is fitting. And if he does not obey, bend him with chains, but do not be excessive with any person. Do nothing harsh without judgment. If you have a faithful servant, let him be to you as your own soul. Treat him as a brother, for you have bought him with the blood of your life. If you wrong him unjustly, he will leave you, and if he departs and runs away, you do not know where to seek him. Chapter 34.

Vain hope and lies belong to the senseless man, and dreams lift up the imprudent. Like one who grasps at a shadow and chases the wind, so is he who pays attention to lying visions. One vision leads to another: the likeness of a face before a face. What can be made clean by the unclean? And what truth can come from a liar?

Emathie.

For the Lord is the judge, and there is no partiality with him. God will not accept the person of the poor, and he will hear the prayer of one who is wronged. He will not despise the prayer of the orphan, nor the widow when she pours out her complaint. Do not the tears of the widow run down her cheek, and is not her cry against him that causes them to fall? For from the cheek they go up to heaven, and the Lord who hears will not be pleased with them. He who worships God with delight shall be received, and his prayer shall reach to the clouds. The prayer of him who humbles himself shall pierce the clouds, and until it comes near it will not be consoled; and it will not depart until the Most High looks down. And the Lord will not be slow, but will judge the righteous and execute judgment; and the Almighty will have no patience with them: that he may crush the loins of the unmerciful and repay vengeance to the heathen; until he takes away the multitude of the proud and breaks the scepters of the unjust; until he renders to man according to his deeds, and according to the works of Adam, and according to his presumption; until he judges the cause of his people, and he will delight the just with his mercy. Chapter 36.
Mercy in time of tribulation is like a cloud of rain in the time of drought. Have mercy upon us, O God of all, and behold us, and show us the light of your mercies; and send down your fear upon the nations that have not sought you, that they may know that there is no God but you, that they may declare your wonders. Lift up your hand over the foreign nations, that they may see your power. As you have been sanctified in us before them, so you shall be magnified among us in their sight; that they may know you, as we also have known you, that there is no God besides you, O Lord. Renew your signs, and work new wonders. Glorify your hand and your right arm.

Stir up fury and pour out wrath. Take away the adversary and afflict the enemy. Hasten the time and remember the end, that they may declare your wonders. Let him who is saved be consumed in the flame of wrath, and let those who harm your people find destruction. Crush the head of the rulers of the enemies, who say there is none other besides us. Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, that they may know, as from the beginning, that there is no God but you; and they shall inherit, as from the beginning. Have mercy on your people, upon whom your name is invoked, and upon Israel, whom you have made equal to your firstborn. Have mercy on the city of your sanctuary, Jerusalem, the city of your rest. Fill Zion with your unspeakable virtues, and your people with your glory. Give testimony to those who were your creatures from the beginning, and raise up the prophecies that were spoken in your name. Give a reward to those that wait for you, that your prophets may be found faithful; and hear the prayers of your servants. According to the blessing of Aaron over your people, direct us in the way of justice, that all that dwell on the earth may know that you are the God, the beholder of all ages. The belly will consume all food; yet one food is better than another. The palate tastes game, and a senseless heart tastes words of lies. A perverse heart will cause grief, and a man of experience will resist it. A woman will receive every man, yet one daughter is better than another. The beauty of a woman cheers the face of her husband, and a man desires nothing more. If there is a healing tongue, and one of mitigation and mercy, such a husband is not found among the sons of men. He who possesses a good wife begins a good possession; she is a help like himself, and a pillar of rest. Where there is no hedge, the possession is plundered; and where there is no wife,

Ecclesiasticus

He who has no nest groans in want. And turning aside wherever he shelters, like one girded up, leaping from city to city. Chapter 37.

Every friend will say, "I too have made a friendship," but there is a friend who is a friend in name only. Is there not a grief even unto death? But a companion and friend shall be turned into an enemy. O most wicked presumption, where did you come from, to cover over dry malice and deceit? A companion rejoices with his friend in pleasures, but in the time of trouble he will be his adversary. A companion sympathizes with a friend for the belly's sake, and against an enemy he will take up a shield. Do not forget your friend in your heart, and do not be unmindful of him in your wealth. Do not take counsel with your sister, and from those who envy you, hide your counsel. Every counselor gives counsel, but there is a counselor for oneself alone. Guard your soul from a counselor. First find out what his need is, for he himself will think in his own heart, lest he cast a stake into the ground and say to you, "Your way is good," while standing opposite to see what will happen to you. With a godless man, discuss holiness; with an unjust man, justice; with a woman, her rivals. With the fearful man, talk of war; with a merchant, of trade. With a buyer, of selling; with a man envious of favors. With the impious, of piety; with the dishonest, of honesty. With an agricultural laborer, of every task; with a yearly worker, of completing the year; with a lazy servant, of much work. Do not rely on these in any counsel. But with a holy man, be constant; whomever you know to observe the fear of God, whose soul resembles yours. And a man of good counsel will establish

for you. For there is nothing better than he for you. The soul of a holy man declares truth at times, better than seven watchmen sitting on high to observe. And in all these things, pray to the Most High, that he may direct your way in truth. Before all your works, let a true word go before you, and before every action, a steady counsel. An evil word will change the heart; from it arise quarrels of passion; good and evil, life and death, and the tongue is always ruler over them. A skilled man has taught many, and is pleasant to his own soul. One who speaks sophistically is odious; he will be defrauded in everything. For grace has not been given to him by the Lord; he is defrauded of all wisdom. And a wise man is wise for his own soul, and the fruit of his understanding is praiseworthy. A wise man will fill others with blessings, and those who see him will praise him. The life of a man is counted in days, but the days of wise Israel are innumerable. A wise man shall inherit honor in his own right, and his name will live forever. My son, test your soul in your lifetime, and if it is wicked, give it no power. For not all things are good for all, and not every kind pleases every soul. Do not be greedy at every feast, and do not pour yourself out upon every food. For in much eating there will be sickness, and greediness will draw close to cholera. Many have died through gluttony, but he who is temperate will add to his life. Chapter 38.

Honor the physician for the need you have of him, for the Most High has created him. He is from God, and from a king he will receive gifts. The knowledge of the physician will lift up his head, and in the sight of great men he will be praised. The Most High has created medicine from the earth, and a prudent man will not refuse it. Was not bitter water made sweet by wood? The acquisition of

A wise man instructs his own people, and the fruits of his understanding are faithful.

Ecclesiasticus

He gave wisdom to men: and gave to human beings the knowledge of the Most High, to be honored in his wondrous works. With these he will ease pain, and the apothecary will make sweet-smelling ointments, and will prepare healing salves, and his works will not come to an end. For the peace of God is upon the face of the earth. Son, in your illness do not despise yourself, but pray to the Lord and he will heal you. Turn away from sin and direct your hands aright, and cleanse your heart from all offense. Give a sweet savor and a memorial of fine flour, and make a rich offering; then give place to the physician, for the Lord created him, and let him not depart from you, for his works are necessary. There is a time when success lies in the hands of physicians, for they will pray to the Lord to grant them success in giving relief and healing in order to preserve life. He who sins before his Maker will act defiantly toward the physician. Son, let tears fall for the dead, and as one who is suffering grievously begin to lament; wrap his body according to his due, and do not neglect his burial. Let your weeping be bitter and your mourning fervent; observe the mourning for one day or two, to avoid criticism. Then be comforted in your grief, for from grief comes death, and grief of heart bows down the strength. In desolation grief remains, and the life of the poor man weighs upon the heart. Do not give your heart to grief; put it away from you, remembering what the end will be for you. Do not forget, for there is no return, and you do him no good, and you will harm yourself. Remember my judgment, for yours also will be thus: yesterday was mine, and today is yours. When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance cease, and be comforted for him when his spirit has departed. Gain wisdom in your youth, and you will find it still with you in old age, and it will bring you honor:

for wisdom will fill a man. He who holds the plow and who glories in the goad, who drives oxen and is occupied with their labors, and whose talk is about bulls — he gives his heart to turning furrows, and his concern is for the fattening of heifers. So too is every craftsman and master workman who labors by night as well as by day; those who cut the signets of seals, and their diligence is to vary the engraving: they give their heart to the likeness of a picture, and keep watch to finish their work. So the smith sitting by the anvil, intent upon his iron-work: the flame of the fire scorches his flesh, and he contends with the heat of the furnace. The sound of the hammer deafens his ears, and his eyes look upon the pattern of the vessel. He gives his heart to finish the work, and is watchful to perfect its decoration. So the potter sitting at his work and turning the wheel with his feet: he is always deeply concerned with his work, and all his labor is by number. He fashions the clay with his arm, and makes it pliable with his feet; he gives his heart to finish the glazing, and he is careful to clean the furnace. All these rely on their hands, and each is skillful in his own work. Without them a city cannot be established, and men can neither sojourn nor live there, yet they are not sought out for the council of the people, nor do they attain eminence in the public assembly. They do not sit in the judge's seat, nor do they understand the covenant of judgment; they are not found using proverbs, but they maintain the fabric of the world, and their prayer is in the practice of their trade, giving their whole heart to it, and seeking out the law of the Most High.

Chapter 39. The wise man will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients, and will be occupied with the prophets. He will preserve the discourse of notable men.

Great occupation was created for all people, and a heavy yoke lies upon the children of Adam, from the day they come forth from their mother's womb until the day of their burial in the mother of all. Thoughts and fears of the heart, anticipation and the day of death: from one sitting on a glorious throne down to one humbled in dust and ashes; from one who wears purple and a crown down to one covered in rough linen — wrath, jealousy, tumult, wavering, and fear of death, continual anger and strife. And in the time of rest upon one's bed, the sleep of the night disturbs the mind. One rests for a little, as though nothing were the matter, and then in sleep the mind is beset with visions as in the day. One is troubled in the vision of one's heart, like one who has escaped from the battle. At the time of one's deliverance, one awakens and marvels that there was nothing to fear. Such things befall all flesh, from man to beast, and upon sinners sevenfold. Add to these: death, bloodshed, strife, and the sword; oppression, famine, ruin, and scourges. All these things were created for the wicked, and because of them came the flood. Everything that is of the earth shall return to the earth, and all waters flow back to the sea. Every bribe and injustice shall be blotted out, but faithfulness shall endure forever. The wealth of the unjust shall dry up like a river, and shall pass away with a great noise like thunder in rain. When they open their hands they shall rejoice; so shall transgressors waste away at the end. The children of the ungodly shall not multiply their branches; they are like impure roots upon stony ground. The reed by every water and river bank shall be plucked up before all grass. Grace is like a paradise of blessings, and mercy endures forever.

A sufficient living for a laborer shall be sweet to him, and in it you shall find treasure. The building of a city establishes its name, and by it a blameless woman is honored. Wine and music gladden the heart, and above both is the love of wisdom. The flute and the psaltery make sweet melody, and above both is a pleasant tongue. Grace and beauty delight the eye, and above both is the green of the field. A friend and companion are met together in due season, and above both is a wife with her husband. Brothers are a help in time of trouble, and mercy shall deliver them. Gold and silver give a firm footing, and above both is sound counsel. Riches and strength lift up the heart, and above these is the fear of the Lord. There is no diminishment in the fear of the Lord, and in it there is no need to seek help. The fear of the Lord is like a paradise of blessing, and it has covered all glory. My son, in the time of your life do not come to want; for it is better to die than to beg. A man who looks to another man's table — his life is not to be counted as life. He feeds his soul with the food of strangers. But a man of discipline and instruction keeps watch over himself. In the mouth of the imprudent poverty shall be sweet, and in his mouth a fire shall burn.

O death, how bitter is the thought of you to one who lives at peace among his possessions, to a man without worry, whose ways are prosperous in all things, and who is still able to enjoy food. O death, your judgment is welcome to a man in need, whose strength fails, who is worn out with age, burdened with all things, and who lacks faith and wisdom. Do not fear the judgment of death. Remember those who came before you and those who shall come after you — this judgment is from the Lord over all flesh; and what shall befall you is according to the good pleasure of the Most High.

Ecclesiasticus (Sirach).

For a thousand years in the grave there is no accusation of life. The sons of sinners are abominable sons, and those who associate with the houses of the ungodly — the inheritance of the children of sinners shall perish, and with their seed shall come continual reproach. A godless father is reproached by his son, for his sake he was brought to dishonor. Woe to you, ungodly men, who have forsaken the law of the Lord Most High. If you were born, you are born to a curse; and if you die, a curse shall be your portion. All things that are of the earth shall return to the earth; so the ungodly shall go from a curse to destruction. The mourning of men is about their bodies, but the evil name of sinners shall be blotted out. Take care of a good name, for this shall continue with you more than a thousand great treasures of gold. A good life has a number of days, but a good name endures forever. Keep discipline in peace, my children. Hidden wisdom and hidden treasure — what profit is there in either? Better is the man who hides his foolishness than the man who hides his wisdom. Return to the truth in these things that proceed from my mouth. For it is not good to be irreverent in all things, and not all things please all men in faith. Guard yourself from your father and mother in matters of fornication; from a ruler and a powerful man in matters of lying; from a prince and a judge in matters of wrongdoing; from a congregation and people in matters of injustice; from a companion and a friend in matters of injustice; from the place where you dwell, in matters of theft; from the truth of God and His covenant; from reclining at table with bread; from salutation; from a harlot woman; and from the face of a known relation. Do not turn your face away from your kinsman; and do not take away his portion and fail to restore it. Do not look upon another man's wife;

do not search out his maidservant, nor draw near to her bed. Guard yourself from friends in matters of improper speech; and when you have given, do not reproach.

Do not repeat a word in your hearing; for the revealing of a hidden word, and you shall truly be without shame; and you shall find favor in the sight of all men. Do not be confounded for all these things; and do not accept a person so as to sin. Of the law of the Most High and His covenant, and of judgment to justify the ungodly; of the words of companions and of travelers; and of the giving of inheritance to friends; of the equality of balances and weights; of acquiring much and little; of the corruption of buying and selling; and of the much discipline of children; and of making a wicked servant's side bleed. Under a wicked woman, it is good to be bound. Where there are many hands, shut them; and whatever you hand over, count and weigh it; and write down all that you give and receive. Of the discipline of the senseless and foolish; and of the aged who are judged by the young — and you shall be instructed in all things, and well regarded in the sight of all men. A daughter is a hidden treasure to her father; anxiety over her takes away sleep, lest in her youth she become an adulteress; and living with a husband she become hateful; lest she defile herself in her virginity and be found pregnant in her father's house; lest having dwelt with a husband she transgress; or at the very least become barren. Over a wayward daughter keep strict watch, lest she make you a reproach to your enemies, a byword in the city and an assembly of the people, and put you to shame in the multitude. Do not look upon every person for their beauty, and do not linger in the midst of women. For from garments comes the moth, and from a woman comes iniquity.

Ecclesiasticus.

various kinds of beasts and all cattle and the creeping creatures of the deep. For his sake the journey's end is made firm, and by his word all things are set in order. We shall say much and yet fall short of his glory; the sum of all our words is: He is all things. Where shall we find strength to glorify him? For he is himself the Almighty above all his works. The Lord is terrible and exceeding great, and his power is wonderful. When you glorify the Lord, exalt him as much as you can, for he will surpass even that, and his magnificence is beyond measure. Bless the Lord and exalt him as much as you are able, for he is beyond all praise. Exalting him, fill yourselves with strength. Do not weary yourselves, for you will never reach the end. Who has seen him that he might declare him? Who can magnify him as he truly is? Many things greater than these lie hidden. We have seen but a few of his works. The Lord made all things, and to those who are godly he gave wisdom. [Chapter 44]

Let us now praise glorious men and our fathers in their generations. The Lord has wrought great glory through his magnificence from the beginning. Men who ruled in their kingdoms, men renowned for their power, giving counsel by their understanding, and declaring prophecies — leaders of the people by their counsels and by their knowledge of learning meet for the people, wise and eloquent in their instructions. They sought out musical tunes and published verses of scripture. Rich men furnished with virtue, living peaceably in their dwellings. All these were honored in their generations and were the glory of their times. There are some of them who have left a name behind them that their praises might be reported. And some there be who have no memorial, who are perished as if they had never been born and their children after them.

But these were men of mercy, whose righteous deeds have not been forgotten. Their good things shall continue with their seed, and their inheritance to their children's children. Their bodies are buried in peace, but their name lives on from generation to generation. The congregation will declare their wisdom and the assembly will proclaim their praise. Enoch pleased God and was translated, that he might give repentance to the nations. Noah was found perfect and righteous; in the time of wrath he was taken in exchange for the world. Therefore was a remnant left upon the earth, when the flood came. Everlasting covenants were made with him, that all flesh should not be destroyed by a flood. Abraham was the great father of a multitude of nations, and there was none found like him in glory. He kept the law of the Most High and was in covenant with him. In his flesh he established the covenant, and when he was proved he was found faithful. Therefore the Lord assured him by an oath that the nations should be blessed in his seed; that he would multiply him as the dust of the earth and exalt his seed as the stars; and cause them to inherit from sea to sea and from the river unto the ends of the earth. And Isaac he did in like manner for the sake of Abraham his father. The blessing of all men and the covenant he confirmed upon the head of Jacob. He acknowledged him in his blessings and gave him an inheritance and divided him his portion in twelve tribes. And he preserved for him men of mercy, and he found grace in the sight of all flesh. [Chapter 45]

Moses was beloved of God and men, whose memory is blessed. He made him like the glory of the saints and magnified him in the fear of his enemies.

Ecclesiasticus.

And in his words he showed wonders to please. He glorified him in the sight of kings and commanded him before his own; and showed him his glory. In faith and meekness he made him holy, and chose him out of all flesh. He heard him and his voice, and brought him into a cloud. And he gave him commandments before his face, and the law of life and instruction, to teach Jacob the covenant, and Israel his judgments. He exalted Aaron his brother, and one like to himself of the tribe of Levi. He made an everlasting covenant with him, and gave him the priesthood of the people; and he made him blessed in glory. And he girded him about with a girdle of justice, and clothed him with a robe of glory, and crowned him with kingly ornaments. He put upon him a garment of honor, and breeches, and a tunic, and surrounded him with many golden bells on every side, that as he went there might be a sound, and a noise made that might be heard in the temple, for a memorial to the children of his people. He gave him a holy vestment of gold and blue and purple, the work of a skillful workman; with judgment and truth adorned. He twisted round cords, and a work of curiously devised gems set in gold, and the work of a lapidary engraved upon them for a memorial, according to the number of the tribes of Israel. And he set a crown of gold upon his mitre, marked with the sign of holiness; an ornament of honor and a work of virtue, desirable to the eyes for its beauty. Before him there were none so beautiful, even from the beginning. No stranger was clothed with them, but only his sons, and his grandchildren for all time. His sacrifices were consumed with fire every day. Moses filled his hands, and he anointed him with holy oil. This was made to him an everlasting covenant, and to his seed as the days of heaven, to execute the office of the priesthood, and to have praise, and to glorify his people in his name. He chose him out of all that lived to offer sacrifice to God, incense and a sweet odor for a memorial, to make reconciliation for his people. He gave him power in his commandments, in the covenants of his judgments, that he should teach Jacob his testimonies, and give light to Israel in his law. For against him strangers stood up, and out of envy the men in the desert surrounded him who were with Dathan and Abiron, and the congregation of Core in wrath. The Lord God saw it and it pleased him not, and they were consumed in the fury of his wrath. He wrought wonders upon them, and consumed them with flaming fire. Then he added glory to Aaron, and gave him an inheritance, and divided him the firstfruits of the fruits of the earth. He prepared bread for him in the first place unto fullness, for the sacrifices of the Lord they shall eat also, which he gave to him and to his seed. But among the nations he shall not inherit, and there is no portion for him among the people, for the Lord himself is his portion and inheritance. Phinees the son of Eleazar is the third in glory, in imitating him in the fear of the Lord, and standing firm in the reverence of the people; with goodness and readiness of heart he pleased God Israel. Therefore he established for him a covenant of peace, to be the prince of the sanctuary and of his people, that there should be to him and to his seed the dignity of the priesthood forever. And the covenant of David, the king of the tribe of Judah, the inheritance of him and his seed, that he might give wisdom to our heart to judge his people in justice, that their good things might not be abolished, and their glory for all generations. Chapter 46.

Joshua the son of Nun was valiant in war, the successor of Moses among the prophets, who was great according to his name, and was very great for the saving of the elect of God, to overthrow the enemies that rose up against them, that he might get the inheritance for Israel. How great was the glory he obtained when he lifted up his hands and drew his sword against the cities! Who before him had stood so firm? For the Lord himself led the fight. Was it not through his wrath

The sun was held back, and one day became as two: he called upon the Most High Power when enemies pressed him from every side, and the great and holy God heard him, hurling great hailstones of mighty force. He rushed against the hostile nation and destroyed his adversaries in the descent, so that the nations might know his power, that it is no easy thing to fight before God — and he followed after the mighty. And in the days of Moses he showed mercy, both he and Caleb the son of Jephonne: they stood against the enemy, kept the people from sin, broke the murmuring of wickedness. And these two, set apart, were preserved from danger out of six hundred thousand foot soldiers, to lead them into their inheritance, into a land flowing with milk and honey. And the Lord gave Caleb strength, and his vigor remained with him even into old age, so that he climbed to the heights of the land, and his descendants held the inheritance. And all the children of Israel saw that it is good to follow the holy God. And the judges, each by his own name — whose hearts were not corrupted, who did not turn away from the Lord — may their memory be held in blessing. Their bones shall flourish in their place, and their name shall endure forever, the glory of holy men passing on to their children. Samuel, beloved of the Lord his God, a prophet of the Lord, renewed the kingdom and anointed rulers over his people. By the law of the Lord he judged the assembly, and he beheld the God of Jacob, and by his faithfulness he was proven a prophet. He was known to be faithful in his words, because he saw the God of light. He called upon the Lord Almighty when the Philistines pressed in from every side at the offering of an unweaned sacrifice. And the Lord thundered from heaven, and in a great sound made his voice heard, and crushed the princes of Tyre and all the leaders of the Philistines. Before the time of the end of his life

he bore witness before the Lord and his anointed: he took no money from anyone, not even sandals, and no man accused him. And after this he slept, and he made known to the king and showed him the end of his life: and he lifted up his voice from the earth in prophecy, to blot out the wickedness of the people. Chapter 47.

After these things Nathan the prophet arose in the days of David, and as fat is separated from flesh, so was David from the children of Israel. He played with lions as though they were lambs, and he dealt with bears as he did with lambs of the flock. In his youth did he not slay the giant and take away the reproach of the people? When he swung his hand with the sling stone he struck down the pride of Goliath, calling upon the Lord Almighty. And the Lord gave strength to his right hand to cut down a mighty man in battle and to exalt the horn of his people. So they glorified him among ten thousands, and praised him in the blessings of the Lord, offering him a crown of glory. He crushed the enemies on every side and destroyed the Philistines his adversaries unto this day. He broke their power forever. In all his works he gave praise to the Holy One, and to the Most High with words of glory. With all his heart he praised the Lord, and he loved the God who made him, and the Lord gave him power against his enemies. He set singers before the altar, and by their voices made sweet melodies. He gave beauty to the festivals and ordered the seasons to their full completion, that they might praise the holy name of the Lord and magnify the holiness of God from morning. The Anointed One cleansed his sins and exalted his horn forever. And he gave him a covenant of kingship and a throne of glory in Israel. After him arose a wise son, and through him he cast down all the power of the enemies.

Ecclesiasticus.

The hearts and hands of the people were moved, and the women in labor suffered pain. They called upon the merciful Lord, spreading their hands toward heaven, and the holy Lord God quickly heard their voice. The sin of those people was not remembered, nor did he deliver them to their enemies, but he purified them by the hand of Isaiah, the holy prophet. He destroyed the camp of the Assyrians, and his angel crushed them. For Hezekiah did what was pleasing to God, and walked boldly in the way of his father David, as Isaiah the great and faithful prophet had commanded him. In his days the sun went backward, and he added years to the life of the king. By a great spirit he saw the last things, and comforted those who mourned in Zion forever. He revealed things to come, and hidden things before they came to pass.

The memory of Hezekiah is composed like a blend of incense, a work of a perfumer. In every mouth his memory shall be sweetened as honey, and as music at a banquet of wine. He was divinely directed in the repentance of the people, and took away the abominations of wickedness: and directed his heart toward the Lord, and in the days of sinners he strengthened piety. Except David and Hezekiah and Josiah, all committed sin, for the kings of Judah forsook the law of the Most High, and they despised the fear of God. They gave their kingdom to others, and their glory to a foreign nation. They set fire to the chosen city of holiness, and made its roads desolate, by the hand of Jeremiah. For they treated him badly, he who was consecrated a prophet from his mother's womb: to overthrow and to root out and to destroy, and then to build and to renew. Ezekiel, who saw the glorious vision, which was shown to him in the chariot of the cherubim. He also remembered the enemies in the rain, to benefit those who showed the right ways. And the bones of the twelve prophets spring up from their place. For they strengthened Jacob, and redeemed themselves by confident faith. Let Zerubbabel also be remembered, for he was as a signet ring on the right hand, and also Joshua the son of Josedech: who in their days built the house, and raised up the holy temple to the Lord, prepared for everlasting glory. And Nehemiah is memorable for a long time, who raised up for us our fallen walls, and set up the gates and bars, and rebuilt our homes. No one was born on earth like Enoch, for he was taken up from the earth. And Joseph, who was born a prince of his brethren, the support of his people, the ruler of his brethren, the support of his people: and his bones were visited, and after death they prophesied. Seth and Shem obtained glory among men, and above every living soul in the origin of Adam.

Chapter 50.

Simon, son of Onias, the high priest, who in his life propped up the house, and in his days fortified the temple. The height of the temple was also founded by him: the double building and the high walls of the temple. In his days the wells of water sprang forth, and they were filled above measure like the sea. He who took care of his nation and delivered it from destruction. He who prevailed to enlarge the city, who obtained glory in the conduct of the people, and enlarged the entrance of the house and the court. Like the morning star in the midst of a cloud, and like the full moon in its days: and like the sun shining forth, so did he shine in the temple of God. Like a rainbow giving light in the bright clouds, and like the flower of roses in the days of spring: and like the lilies that are at the water's edge, and like the sweet-smelling incense in the days of summer. Like a bright fire and incense burning in the fire: like a vessel of solid gold adorned with every precious stone. Like an olive tree putting forth its fruit:

Like a cypress tree raising itself in height. In receiving the robe of glory and being clothed in the perfection of virtue: and in ascending to the holy altar he gave glory to the sanctification of the year. And in receiving the portions from the hands of the priests, himself standing beside the altar, with a crown of his brethren about him like a plantation of cedars on Mount Lebanon: so around him they stood like branches of a palm tree, all the sons of Aaron in their glory. And the offering of the Lord being in the hands of the priests before the whole congregation of Israel: and completing his service at the altar, he stretched forth his hand to make libation, and offered of the blood of the grape. He poured it out at the base of the altar, a divine fragrance to the Most High Prince. Then the sons of Aaron shouted; they sounded with beaten trumpets, and made a great sound to be heard as a memorial before God. Then all the people together made haste and fell upon their faces upon the earth to worship the Lord their God, and to give prayer to the Almighty God Most High. And the singers also lifted up their voices; in the great house the sound resounded, full of sweetness. And the people besought the Lord Most High in prayer, until the honor of the Lord was accomplished, and they completed his service. Then descending he lifted up his hands over all the congregation of the children of Israel, to give glory to God with his lips, and to glory in his name. And he repeated his prayer, wishing to show the power of God. And he prayed more to the Lord of all, who does great things in all the earth; who increased our days from our mother's womb, and deals with us according to his mercy. May he grant us joyfulness of heart, and may there be peace in our days in Israel for the days of eternity: may Israel believe that the mercy of God is with us, that he might deliver us in his days. Two nations my soul abhors, and the third is not a nation which I hate. Those who sit on mount Seir, and the Philistines, and the foolish people that dwell in Shechem. The doctrine of wisdom and discipline was written in this book by Jesus the son of Sirach of Jerusalem: who renewed wisdom from his heart. Blessed is he who meditates on these good things. Whoever lays them to heart shall be wise always. For if he practices these things he shall be capable of all things: because the light of God is his guide.

The Prayer of Jesus son of Sirach

I will give thanks to you, O Lord, O King, and I will praise you, God my Savior. I will give thanks to your name, for you have been my helper and protector, and have delivered my body from destruction: from the snare of an unjust tongue, and from the lips of those who devise lies: and in the sight of those who stood by you were made my helper. And you delivered me according to the multitude of the mercy of your name, from those who roared ready to devour me, from the hands of those who sought my life, and from the gates of afflictions which surrounded me: from the pressure of the flame which surrounded me, and in the midst of the fire I was not consumed. From the depths of the belly of hell, and from a defiled tongue, and from a lying word, from an unjust king, and from an unjust tongue, my soul shall praise the Lord even to death. And my life was drawing near to destruction below. They surrounded me on every side, and there was no one to help. I looked for the help of men, and there was none. I remembered your mercy, O Lord, and your works which are from the beginning of the world: how you deliver those who wait for you, O Lord, and save them from the hands of the nations. You have exalted my dwelling upon the earth, and I have prayed in the face of death. I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, that he would not forsake me in the day of my trouble, and in the time of the proud.

with his help, I will praise your name continually, and I will praise it in confession, and my prayer was heard. And you rescued me from perdition, and you delivered me from the time of iniquity. Therefore I will give thanks and speak praise to you, and I will bless the name of the Lord, whose servant I am even now in my youth. Before I wandered, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer; I asked for it before my time, and even to the very last I shall seek it, and it shall flourish like a ripening grape. My heart rejoiced in it, my foot walked in the straight path, and from my youth I searched for it. I inclined my ear a little, and I received it. I found much wisdom within myself, and I profited greatly from it. I will give wisdom and I will give glory. I took counsel that I might practice it; I was zealous for the good and I shall not be confounded. My soul was illumined by it, and in practicing it I was confirmed. I stretched out my hands on high, and in its wisdom my soul was enlightened, and it illuminated my ignorances. I directed my soul toward it, and in understanding I found it. I possessed with it a heart from the beginning; therefore I shall not be forsaken. My belly was troubled in seeking it; therefore I shall possess a good possession. For the Lord gave me a tongue as my reward, and with it I will praise him. Come to me, you unlearned, and gather yourselves under the yoke of discipline. Why do you still hold back, and what do you say about these things? Your souls are greatly in need. I opened my mouth and I spoke. Buy for yourselves wisdom without silver, and put your necks under her yoke, and let your soul receive discipline. For it is close at hand to find it. See with your own eyes, that I labored but a little, and found for myself great rest. Take up discipline,

with a great multitude of arguments, and to possess abundant gold in it: let your soul rejoice in his mercy, and you shall not be confounded in his praise. Work your works before the time, and he will give you your reward in his own time. Here ends the Book of Matthias. The Prayer of Solomon. And Solomon knelt down before the whole assembly of Israel, and he spread out his hands toward heaven and said: O Lord God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven above or on earth below, who keeps your covenant and mercy with your servants who walk before you with all their heart. You kept your word to your servant David my father, what you spoke with your mouth and fulfilled with your hand, as it is this day. And now, O Lord God of Israel, keep what you promised to your servant David my father, saying: You shall not lack a man before me to sit on the throne of Israel. But only if your children take heed of their way, to walk before me as you have walked before me. And now, Lord God of Israel, let your word be confirmed which you spoke to your servant David. But will God indeed dwell with men on earth? If heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain you, how much less this house which I have built? But turn toward the prayer of your servant and toward his supplication, O Lord, and hear the plea of prayer which your servant prays before you. Let your eyes be open toward this house day and night, toward the place of which you said you would put your name there; and when your servant prays toward this place, hear the supplication of your servant and of your people; and when he prays in this place, hear from your dwelling place in heaven, and when you hear, forgive. If a man sins against another. Here ends the Prayer of Solomon. Here begins the Prologue to the Book of Ecclesiastes.

Isaiah

saturated with oil. Your land is desolate: your cities are burned with fire. Strangers devour your country before your face: and it shall be desolate as if destroyed by enemies. And the daughter of Zion shall be left as a shelter in a vineyard, and as a hut in a cucumber field, and as a besieged city. Unless the Lord of hosts had left us a seed, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah. Hear the word of the Lord, you rulers of Sodom: receive with your ears the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah. To what purpose do you offer me the multitude of your sacrifices, says the Lord? I am full. I desire not holocausts of rams and fat of fatlings and blood of calves and lambs and goats. When you came to appear before me, who required these things at your hands, that you should walk in my courts? Offer sacrifice no more in vain. Incense is an abomination to me. The new moons and the sabbaths and other festivals I will not endure. Your assemblies are wicked. My soul hates your new moons and your solemnities. They are become troublesome to me, I am weary of bearing them. And when you stretch forth your hands, I will turn away my eyes from you: and when you multiply prayer, I will not hear: for your hands are full of blood. Wash yourselves, be clean, take away the evil of your thoughts from my eyes. Cease to do evil, learn to do well, seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge for the fatherless, defend the widow: and then come and accuse me, says the Lord. If your sins be as scarlet, they shall be made white as snow: and if they be red as crimson, they shall be white as wool. If you be willing and will hear me, you shall eat the good things of the land. But if you will not and will provoke me to wrath, the sword shall devour you:

for the mouth of the Lord has spoken it. How has the faithful city become a harlot, full of judgment? Justice dwelt in it, but now murderers. Your silver is turned into dross: your wine is mixed with water. Your princes are faithless, companions of thieves. They all love bribes, they run after rewards. They judge not for the fatherless: and the widow's cause does not come to them. Therefore says the Lord God of hosts, the strong one of Israel: Ah, I will take comfort over my adversaries: and I will be revenged of my enemies. And I will turn my hand to you, and I will refine your dross as with lye, and I will take away all your tin: And I will restore your judges as they were before, and your counselors as of old. After this you shall be called the city of the just, a faithful city. Zion shall be redeemed in judgment: and they shall bring her back in justice. And he shall crush the wicked and the sinners together: and they that have forsaken the Lord shall be consumed. For they shall be confounded by the idols to which they have sacrificed. And you shall be ashamed of your gardens which you have chosen: if you shall be as an oak with the leaves falling off, and as a garden without water. And your strength shall be as the ashes of tow, and your work as a spark: and both shall burn together, and there shall be none to quench them. Chapter

You do not regard the work of his hands. Therefore my people have gone into captivity because they had no knowledge, and their nobles have died of hunger, and their multitude is parched with thirst. Therefore hell has enlarged its soul and opened its mouth without limit. And her mighty ones shall descend, and her pomp and her rejoicing shall come down to her. And man shall be bowed down, and the eyes of the lofty shall be humbled. And the Lord of hosts shall be exalted in judgment, and the holy God shall be sanctified in righteousness. And the lambs shall feed in their order, and strangers shall eat of the waste places of the fat ones. Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as it were with a cart rope. Who say: Let him make speed and hasten his work, that we may see it; and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, that we may know it. Woe to those who call evil good and good evil; who put darkness for light and light for darkness; who put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter. Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and prudent in their own sight. Woe to those who are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink. Who justify the wicked for a bribe, and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him. Therefore, as the tongue of fire devours stubble, and the flame consumes chaff, so their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall go up like dust. Because they have rejected the law of the Lord of hosts, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel. Therefore the anger of the Lord was kindled against his people, and he stretched out his hand against them and struck them, and the hills trembled, and their corpses were as refuse in the midst of the streets. In all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still. And he will lift up a banner to the nations from far away, and will whistle for them from the ends of the earth; and behold, they will come quickly and swiftly. None shall be weary or stumble among them; none shall slumber or sleep; neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes broken. Whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent; their horses' hooves shall seem like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind. Their roaring shall be like a lion; they shall roar like young lions, and they shall seize the prey and carry it safely away, and none shall deliver it. And in that day they shall roar against them like the roaring of the sea. And if one looks to the land, behold, darkness and distress; and the light is darkened in its clouds. Chapter VI.

In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple. Above it stood the seraphim; each one had six wings: with two he covered his face, and with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew. And one cried to another and said: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory. And the foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of him who called, and the house was filled with smoke. And I said: Woe is me, for I am undone, because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the Lord of hosts. Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having in his hand a live coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar. And he touched my mouth with it and said: Behold, this has touched your lips; your iniquity is taken away, and your sin is purged. And I heard the voice of the Lord saying: Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then I said: Here am I; send me. And he said: Go, and say to this people: Hear

Isaiah

...terror of thorns and briers: and it shall be for the pasture of oxen and for the treading down of cattle. Chapter 8.

And the Lord said to me: Take a great book and write in it with a man's pen: quickly take away the spoils, speedily take the prey. And I took unto me faithful witnesses: Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Barachiah. And I went to the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. And the Lord said to me: Call his name — make haste to strip the spoils, hasten to take away the prey — for before the child shall know how to call his father and his mother, the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of the Assyrians. And the Lord spoke to me again, saying: Forasmuch as this people has refused the waters of Shiloah that go softly, and rejoices in Rezin and the son of Remaliah; now therefore, behold, the Lord brings up upon them the waters of the river, strong and many, even the king of Assyria and all his glory: and he shall come up over all his channels and go over all his banks; and he shall pass through Judah, he shall overflow and go over, he shall reach even to the neck; and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel. Gather yourselves together, O peoples, and be broken in pieces; and give ear, all ye of far countries. Gird yourselves and be broken; take counsel together and it shall come to nought; speak the word and it shall not stand: for God is with us. For thus the Lord spoke to me with a strong hand, and instructed me that I should not walk in the way of this people, saying: Say ye not, A conspiracy. For all that this people says is a conspiracy. Neither fear their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; and let him be your fear and let him be your dread: and he shall be for a sanctuary, but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel:

for a snare and for a ruin to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. And many among them shall stumble, and fall, and be broken, and be snared, and be taken. Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples: and I will wait upon the Lord, who hides his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him. Behold, I and the children whom the Lord has given me are for signs and wonders in Israel from the Lord of hosts, who dwells in mount Zion. And when they shall say to you: Seek unto them that have familiar spirits, and unto wizards that peep and mutter — should not a people seek unto their God? for the living to the dead? To the law and to the testimony! If they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them. And they shall pass through it, hardly bestead and hungry; and when they shall be hungry, they shall fret themselves, and curse their king and their God. And they shall look upward and look unto the earth; and behold, trouble and darkness, dimness of anguish; and they shall be driven to darkness. Chapter 9.

Nevertheless the dimness shall not be such as was in her vexation, when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations. The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light; they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them has the light shone. Thou hast multiplied the nation, but hast not increased the joy. They joy before thee according to the joy in harvest, and as men rejoice when they divide the spoil. For thou hast broken the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, as in the day of Midian. For every battle of the warrior is with confused noise, and garments rolled in blood; but this shall be with burning and fuel of fire. For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon...

Isaiah.

And by my wisdom I have understood. And I have removed the boundaries of peoples; and I have plundered their princes; and I have brought down as one mighty those dwelling on high. And my hand has found the strength of the peoples as a nest, and as eggs that are gathered up that are left, so have I gathered up all the earth; and there was none that moved a wing, or opened the mouth, or made a sound. Shall the axe boast itself against him that heweth with it? or shall the saw exalt itself against him that moveth it? As if a rod should lift itself up against them that lift it up, and a staff exalt itself which is but wood. Therefore shall the Lord, the Lord of hosts, send among his fat ones leanness; and under his glory a burning shall be kindled like the burning of a fire. And the light of Israel shall be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame; and it shall burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day. And the glory of his forest and of his fruitful field, both soul and body shall consume away. And they shall flee away, and the remnant of the trees of his forest shall be few, that a child may write them. And it shall come to pass in that day, that the remnant of Israel shall not any more lean upon him that smote them, but shall lean upon the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, in truth. The remnant shall return, even the remnant of Jacob, unto the mighty God. For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, only a remnant of them shall return. A consumption is decreed, overflowing with righteousness. For a full end and a decreed destruction shall the Lord God of hosts make in the midst of all the earth. Therefore thus saith the Lord God of hosts: O my people that dwellest in Zion, be not afraid of the Assyrian. He shall smite thee with a rod, and his staff he shall lift up against thee, after the manner of Egypt. For yet a very little while, and the indignation shall cease, and mine anger shall cease at their destruction. And the Lord of hosts shall stir up against him a scourge, as in the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb; and his rod shall be over the sea, and he shall lift it up after the manner of Egypt. And it shall come to pass in that day, that his burden shall be taken away from off thy shoulder, and his yoke from off thy neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing. He is come to Aiath, he is passed through Migron; at Michmash he leaveth his baggage. They have gone over the pass; they have taken up their lodging at Geba. Ramah is afraid; Gibeah of Saul is fled. Cry aloud with thy voice, O daughter of Gallim; hearken to Laishah; O poor Anathoth. Madmenah is fleeing away; the inhabitants of Gebim are gathering to flee. As yet shall he halt at Nob this day; he shall shake his hand at the mount of the daughter of Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem. Behold, the Lord, the Lord of hosts, shall lop the boughs with terror; and those of high stature shall be hewn down, and the lofty shall be humbled. And the thickets of the forest shall be cut down with iron, and Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one. Chapter 11.

And there shall come forth a shoot out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots shall bear fruit. And the Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord. And he shall not judge by what his eyes see, nor decide by what his ears hear. But with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and decide with equity for the meek of the earth; and he shall strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked. And righteousness shall be the belt of his waist, and faithfulness the belt of his loins. The wolf shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the young goat. The calf and the lion and the fattened calf shall be together, and a little child shall lead them. The cow and the bear shall graze together; their young shall lie down together. The lion shall eat straw like the ox.

Isaiah

He shall eat straw, and the infant shall delight himself near the hole of the asp; and he that is weaned shall thrust his hand into the den of the basilisk. They shall not hurt nor kill in all my holy mountain: for the earth is full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea. In that day the root of Jesse, who stands as a sign for the peoples, him shall the nations seek; and his sepulcher shall be glorious. And it shall come to pass in that day that the Lord shall set his hand again to possess the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from the Assyrians, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Ethiopia, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea. And he shall lift up a standard for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel. And he shall gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four quarters of the earth. And the envy of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall perish. Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not trouble Ephraim. But they shall fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines toward the sea; they shall plunder together the children of the east. Edom and Moab shall be the stretching out of their hands, and the children of Ammon shall obey them. And the Lord shall utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea; and with his mighty wind he shall shake his hand over the river, and shall smite it in its seven streams, so that men may walk across with dry feet. And there shall be a highway for the remnant of his people who shall remain from Assyria, as there was for Israel in the day when he came up out of the land of Egypt.

And in that day you shall say: I will give thanks to you, O Lord, for though you were angry with me, your anger is turned away, and you comforted me. Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and will not be afraid: for the Lord God is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation. Therefore with joy you shall draw water from the wells of salvation. And you shall say in that day: Give thanks to the Lord, call upon his name; make known his deeds among the peoples; proclaim that his name is exalted. Sing to the Lord, for he has done gloriously: let this be made known in all the earth. Shout and sing for joy, O inhabitant of Zion, for great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel.

The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw. Upon a dark mountain lift up a banner; raise your voice, lift your hands, and let the leaders enter the gates. I have commanded my sanctified ones; I have also called my mighty ones for my anger, even those who rejoice in my glory. The noise of a multitude in the mountains, like that of many people; a tumultuous noise of the kingdoms of nations gathered together. The Lord of hosts musters the army for battle. They come from a far country, from the end of heaven — the Lord and the weapons of his indignation — to destroy the whole land. Wail, for the day of the Lord is at hand; it will come as destruction from the Almighty. Therefore all hands will be limp, and every man's heart will melt; and they shall be afraid. Pangs and sorrows shall take hold of them; they shall be in pain as a woman in labor. They shall be amazed at one another; their faces shall be faces aflame. Behold, the day of the Lord comes, cruel, and full of indignation and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate; and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it. For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light; the sun shall be darkened at its rising, and the moon shall not shed its light. And I will punish the world for its evil, and the wicked for their iniquity. I will cause the arrogance of the proud to cease, and will lay low the haughtiness of the terrible. A man shall be more precious than fine gold, even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir. Therefore I will shake the heavens, and the earth shall be moved out of her place, in the wrath of the Lord of hosts, and in the day of his fierce anger.

Isaiah

And it shall be as a fleeing deer and as a sheep: and there shall be none to gather them. Every man shall turn to his own people, and each one shall flee to his own land. Everyone who is found shall be slain, and everyone who flees shall fall by the sword. Their infants shall be dashed to pieces before their eyes; their houses shall be plundered, and their wives ravished. Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, who shall not seek silver, nor desire gold; but with their bows they shall dash the young men to pieces, and they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eye shall not spare children. And Babylon, that glorious city, the pride of the Chaldeans, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. It shall never be inhabited, nor shall it be settled from generation to generation. Neither shall the Arabians pitch tent there, nor shall shepherds make their folds there; but wild beasts shall rest there, and their houses shall be full of serpents. And ostriches shall dwell there, and satyrs shall dance there, and owls shall answer there in its palaces, and sirens in its pleasant temples. [Chapter]

The time is near to come, and its days shall not be prolonged. For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land; and the stranger shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob. And the peoples shall take them and bring them to their place; and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord as servants and handmaids; and they shall take captive those who were their captors, and rule over their oppressors. And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give you rest from your sorrow, and from your trouble, and from the hard service in which you were made to serve, that you shall take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say: How the oppressor has ceased! The golden city has ceased! The Lord has broken the staff of the wicked,

the rod of the rulers, that struck the peoples in wrath with a continual stroke, that ruled the nations in anger, with a persecution that none restrained. The whole earth is at rest and is quiet; they break forth into singing. The fir trees also rejoice over you, and the cedars of Lebanon, saying: Since you were laid low, no woodcutter comes up against us. The underworld beneath is stirred up to meet you at your coming; it arouses the spirits of the dead to greet you, all who were leaders of the earth; it raises up from their thrones all who were kings of the nations. All of them shall speak and say to you: You too have become as weak as we! You have become like us! Your pride has been brought down to the underworld; the sound of your harps is gone. Maggots are spread beneath you, and worms cover you. How you have fallen from heaven, O morning star, son of the dawn! You have been cut down to the earth, you who laid low the nations! For you said in your heart: I will ascend into heaven; I will exalt my throne above the stars of God; I will sit on the mount of the congregation, on the sides of the north; I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the Most High. Yet you shall be brought down to the underworld, to the depths of the pit. Those who see you will stare at you and ponder over you: Is this the man who made the earth tremble, who shook kingdoms, who made the world like a desert and overthrew its cities, and did not let his prisoners go home? All the kings of the nations lie in glory, each in his own tomb; but you are cast out away from your grave, like a rejected branch, clothed with the slain, those pierced with the sword, who go down to the stones of the pit, like a trampled corpse. You will not be joined with them in burial, for you have destroyed your land and slain your people. May the descendants of evildoers never be named! Prepare slaughter for his sons, because of

Isaiah.

To those who dwell by the brick wall, speak of their plagues: whose suburbs of Heshbon are desolate. And the vine of Sibmah, the lords of the nations have beaten down its branches.
