They reached unto Jazer, they wandered through the wilderness: her branches spread over the sea. Therefore I will weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah. I will water you with my tears, O Heshbon and Elealeh: for the shouting over your harvest and your summer fruits is fallen. And gladness and joy are taken away from the fruitful field: and in the vineyards there shall be no singing nor rejoicing. No treader shall tread wine in the presses, for I have caused the shouting to cease. Therefore my heart shall sound like a harp for Moab, and mine inner parts for Kir-hareseth. And it shall come to pass that when Moab shall present himself, when he shall weary himself upon the high place, and shall come to his sanctuary to pray, he shall not prevail. This is the word that the Lord spoke concerning Moab at that time, and now the Lord has spoken, saying: Within three years, as the years of a hireling, the glory of Moab shall be contemned with all that great multitude; and the remnant shall be very small and feeble, not many. CHAPTER 17. The burden of Damascus. Behold, Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it shall be a ruinous heap. The cities of Aroer are forsaken: they shall be for flocks, which shall lie down, and none shall make them afraid. The fortress also shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Syria: they shall be as the glory of the children of Israel, saith the Lord of hosts. And in that day it shall come to pass that the glory of Jacob shall be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh shall wax lean: and it shall be as when the harvestman gathereth the corn, and reapeth the ears with his arm; and it shall be as he that gathereth ears in the valley of Rephaim. Yet gleaning grapes shall be left in it, as the shaking of an olive tree, two or three berries in the top of the uppermost bough, four or five in the outmost fruitful branches thereof. In that day shall a man look to his Maker, and his eyes shall have respect to the Holy One of Israel. And he shall not look to the altars which his hands have made, neither shall he have respect unto that which his fingers have wrought, and he shall not look to the groves and the images. In that day shall the cities of his strength be as a forsaken bough, and as an uppermost branch, which was left because of the children of Israel: and they shall be desolate. Because you have forgotten the God of your salvation, and have not been mindful of the rock of your strength. Therefore you shall plant pleasant plants and set out strange slips. In the day when you plant them, you make them grow. But the harvest shall be a heap in the day of grief and desperate sorrow. Woe to the multitude of many peoples, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters. The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters: but he shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far off, and shall be chased as the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like a rolling thing before the whirlwind. And behold at evening tide trouble; and before the morning he is not. This is the portion of them that spoil us, and the lot of them that rob us. CHAPTER 18. Woe to the land of the rustling of wings, which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia: that sendeth ambassadors by the sea, even in vessels of bulrushes upon the waters. Go, swift messengers, to a nation scattered and peeled, to a people terrible from their beginning onward; a nation meted out and trodden down, whose land the rivers have spoiled. All inhabitants of the world and dwellers on earth: when a banner is lifted up on the mountains, you will see it, and when the trumpet is blown, you will hear it. For thus the Lord said unto me: I will rest and consider in my dwelling place, like a clear heat upon herbs...

Isaiah

The light is clear: and like a cloud of dew in the day of harvest. Before the harvest, when all has blossomed and the unripe fruit is ripening, he will cut off the branches with pruning hooks, and those that are left he will cut away and remove, and they will be left together for the birds of the mountains and the beasts of the earth; and the birds will feed on them all summer, and all the beasts of the earth will feed on them all winter. At that time a gift will be brought to the Lord of hosts from a people torn and scattered, from a people terrible from this time forth, a nation powerful and conquering, whose land the rivers have divided — to the place of the name of the Lord of hosts, Mount Zion. Chapter 19.

The burden of Egypt. Behold, the Lord rides on a swift cloud and comes to Egypt; and the idols of Egypt will tremble before him, and the heart of Egypt will melt within it. And I will set Egyptians against Egyptians, and they will fight, every man against his brother, and every man against his neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom. And the spirit of Egypt will be emptied out within it, and I will confound its counsel; and they will inquire of their idols and of their diviners and of their mediums and of their sorcerers. And I will deliver Egypt into the hand of a cruel master, and a fierce king will rule over them, says the Lord of hosts. And the waters will fail from the sea, and the river will be wasted and dried up; and the canals will become foul, the streams of Egypt will diminish and dry up, the reeds and rushes will wither. The bare places by the Nile, by the bank of the Nile, and all the sown fields of the Nile will become dry and be blown away and be no more. And the fishermen will mourn, and all who cast hooks in the Nile will lament, and those who spread nets on the water will languish. The workers in combed flax and those who weave white cotton will be in despair. And the pools will dry up:

All those who make sluices and ponds to catch fish. The princes of Zoan are utterly foolish; the wise counselors of Pharaoh give stupid counsel. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am the son of the wise, a son of ancient kings"? Where then are your wise men? Let them tell you and make known what the Lord of hosts has purposed against Egypt. The princes of Zoan have become fools, the princes of Memphis are deluded; those who are the cornerstones of her tribes have led Egypt astray. The Lord has mingled within her a spirit of confusion; and they have made Egypt stagger in all its undertakings, as a drunken man staggers in his vomit. And there will be nothing for Egypt that head or tail, branch or reed, may do. In that day Egypt will be like women, and tremble with fear before the shaking of the hand of the Lord of hosts that he will shake over it. And the land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt; everyone to whom it is mentioned will fear because of the purpose of the Lord of hosts that he purposes against it. In that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the Lord of hosts. One of them will be called the City of the Sun. In that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to the Lord at its border; and it will be a sign and a witness to the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt. When they cry to the Lord because of their oppressors, he will send them a savior and defender, and deliver them. And the Lord will make himself known to the Egyptians, and the Egyptians will know the Lord in that day and worship with sacrifice and offering, and they will make vows to the Lord and perform them. And the Lord will strike Egypt, striking and healing, and they will return to the Lord, and he will listen to their pleas for mercy and heal them. In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria, and Assyria will come into Egypt, and

Isaiah

They have fled far away. Therefore I said: turn away from me, I will weep bitterly. Do not labor to comfort me over the destruction of the daughter of my people. For it is a day of slaughter and trampling and of weeping to the Lord God of hosts in the valley of vision. Breaking down the walls and crying to the mountain. And Elam took up the quiver, with chariots of men and horsemen, and the shield shall uncover the walls. And your choicest valleys shall be full of chariots, and the horsemen shall set themselves in array at the gate: and the covering of Judah shall be revealed. And you shall see in that day the armory of the house of the forest, and the breaches of the city of David shall be many. And you gathered the waters of the lower pool, and you numbered the houses of Jerusalem, and you broke down houses to fortify the wall. And you made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool, but you did not look to him who made it, and you did not see him who fashioned it long ago. And the Lord God of hosts called in that day to weeping and mourning, to baldness and to girding with sackcloth: and behold joy and gladness, slaying oxen and killing sheep, eating meat and drinking wine. Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die. And it was revealed in my ears by the Lord of hosts: surely this iniquity shall not be forgiven you until you die, says the Lord God of hosts. Thus says the Lord God of hosts: Go, enter to him who dwells in the tabernacle, to Shebna the steward of the temple, and say to him: What are you doing here, or who gave you the right to be here? For you have cut out a tomb for yourself here, you have hewn your tomb on high, and carved a dwelling for yourself in the rock. Behold, the Lord will carry you away violently, as a cock is carried away, and will surely cover you. He will surely roll you up tightly like a ball

and throw you into a large and broad land. There you shall die, and there shall your glorious chariots be, you shame of your master's house. I will drive you from your office, and from your station shall you be pulled down. And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, and I will clothe him with your robe and strengthen him with your belt, and I will commit your authority into his hand, and he shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. And the key of the house of David I will lay upon his shoulder, and he shall open and none shall shut, and he shall shut and none shall open. And I will fasten him as a nail in a sure place, and he shall be a throne of glory to his father's house. And they shall hang upon him all the glory of his father's house, the offspring and the issue, all vessels of small quantity, from the vessels of cups even to all the vessels of pitchers. In that day, says the Lord of hosts, shall the nail that is fastened in the sure place give way and be broken and fall, and the burden that was upon it shall be cut off: for the Lord has spoken. Chapter 23.

The burden of Tyre. Howl, you ships of the sea, for it is laid waste, the place from which they used to come: from the land of Chittim it is revealed to them. Be still, you inhabitants of the coastland, you merchants of Sidon, who cross over the sea they have replenished you. And on great waters the grain of the Nile, the harvest of the river, was her revenue, and she was the marketplace of nations. Be ashamed, O Sidon, for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the sea, saying: I have not labored nor given birth, I have not reared young men nor brought up virgins. When the report comes to Egypt, they will be in anguish over the report about Tyre. Cross over to Tarshish, howl, you inhabitants of the coastland! Is this your joyful city whose origin is from days of old, whose feet carried her to dwell far away? Who has purposed this against Tyre, the crowning city, whose merchants were princes, whose traders were

Isaiah

The Lord of hosts has decreed this, to bring down the pride of all glory, and to humble all the renowned of the earth. Pass through your land like a river, O daughter of the sea: there is no more a girdle for you. He stretched out his hand over the sea, he shook the kingdoms. The Lord has given commandment against Canaan, to destroy its strongholds. And he said: You shall glory no more, you who have suffered reproach, O virgin daughter of Sidon. Arise and pass over to Chittim: there also you shall have no rest. Behold, the land of the Chaldeans — such a people was not until now — Assyria founded it. They led its mighty men into captivity: they undermined its houses, they laid it in ruin. Howl, you ships of the sea, because the stronghold is laid waste. And it shall come to pass in that day that Tyre shall be forgotten seventy years, according to the days of one king. After seventy years it shall be with Tyre as in the song of the harlot. Take a harp, go about the city, O harlot that hast been forgotten. Play well, sing many songs, that you may be remembered. And it shall come to pass after seventy years that the Lord will visit Tyre, and she shall return to her hire, and shall commit fornication with all the kingdoms of the world upon the face of the earth. And her merchandise and her hire shall be holy to the Lord. It shall not be treasured nor laid up: for her merchandise shall be for them that dwell before the Lord, to eat sufficiently, and for durable clothing.

Behold, the Lord will lay waste the earth and make it desolate, and he will distress the face thereof, and scatter abroad the inhabitants thereof. And it shall be as with the people, so with the priest; and as with the servant, so with his master; as with the maid, so with her mistress. As with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the lender, so with the borrower. The earth shall be utterly emptied and utterly despoiled: for the Lord has spoken this word. The earth mourns and fades away, the world languishes and fades away, the proud people of the earth do languish. The earth also is defiled under the inhabitants thereof; because they have transgressed the laws, changed the ordinances, broken the everlasting covenant. Therefore the curse has devoured the earth, and they that dwell therein are desolate: therefore the inhabitants of the earth are burned, and few men left. The new wine mourns, the vine languishes, all the merry-hearted do sigh. The mirth of timbrels ceases, the noise of those who rejoice ends, the joy of the harp ceases. They shall not drink wine with a song; strong drink shall be bitter to them that drink it. The city of vanity is broken down: every house is shut up, that no man may come in. There is a crying for wine in the streets; all joy is darkened, the mirth of the land is gone. In the city is left desolation, and the gate is smitten with destruction: because these things shall be in the midst of the land in the midst of the peoples. As when the olive tree is beaten, and as the gleaning grapes when the vintage is done. These shall lift up their voice, they shall shout: for the majesty of the Lord they shall cry aloud from the sea. Therefore glorify the Lord in the east, even the name of the Lord God of Israel in the islands of the sea. From the uttermost part of the earth have we heard songs: glory to the righteous. But I said: My leanness, my leanness, woe unto me! The treacherous dealers have dealt treacherously; yea, the treacherous dealers have dealt very treacherously. Fear, and the pit, and the snare are upon you, O inhabitant of the earth. And it shall come to pass that he who flees from the noise of the fear shall fall into the pit; and he who comes up out of the midst of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for the floodgates from on high are opened.

Isaiah

and the foundations of the earth shall be shaken. With breaking the earth shall be broken, with crushing it shall be crushed, with trembling it shall tremble. The earth shall reel back and forth like a drunkard, and shall sway like a hut; its transgression shall weigh heavily upon it, and it shall fall and not rise again. And it shall come to pass in that day that the Lord shall punish the host of heaven on high, and the kings of the earth on earth. And they shall be gathered together as prisoners in a pit, and shall be shut up in a prison; and after many days they shall be visited. Then the moon shall be abashed and the sun ashamed, when the Lord of hosts shall reign on mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before his elders shall be glory. Chapter 25.

O Lord, you are my God; I will exalt you, I will give thanks to your name; for you have done wonderful things, plans formed long ago, faithful and sure. For you have made the city a heap, the fortified city a ruin, the palace of strangers is a city no more; it shall never be rebuilt. Therefore the strong peoples will glorify you; the city of ruthless nations will fear you. For you have been a stronghold to the poor, a stronghold to the needy in his distress, a shelter from the storm and a shade from the heat. For the breath of the ruthless is like a storm against a wall, like heat in a dry place. You will subdue the noise of strangers; as heat by the shade of a cloud, the triumph of the ruthless shall be brought low. And in this mountain the Lord of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of well-aged wine, of rich food full of marrow, of aged wine well refined. And he will swallow up on this mountain the covering that is cast over all peoples, the veil that is spread over all nations; he will swallow up death forever. And the Lord God will wipe away tears from

all faces; and the reproach of his people he will take away from all the earth: for the Lord has spoken. And it shall be said in that day: Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, that he might save us. This is the Lord; we have waited for him; we will be glad and rejoice in his salvation. For the hand of the Lord will rest on this mountain, and Moab shall be trodden down under him as straw is trodden down in the water of a dung heap. And he will spread out his hands in the midst of it as a swimmer spreads his hands out to swim, but the Lord will lay low his pride together with the skill of his hands. And the high fortifications of his walls he will bring down, lay low, and cast to the ground, to the dust. Chapter 26.

In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: We have a strong city; salvation will God appoint for walls and ramparts. Open the gates, that the righteous nation that keeps faith may enter. The ancient error is gone; you will keep peace, perfect peace, because they trust in you. Trust in the Lord forever, for the Lord God is an everlasting rock. For he has humbled the inhabitants of the height, the lofty city. He lays it low, lays it low to the ground, casts it to the dust. The foot tramples it, the feet of the poor, the steps of the needy. The path of the righteous is level; you make straight the way of the righteous. In the path of your judgments, O Lord, we wait for you; your name and your remembrance are the desire of our soul. My soul yearns for you in the night; my spirit within me earnestly seeks you. For when your judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness. Though grace is shown to the wicked, he does not learn righteousness. In the land of the upright he deals corruptly and does not see the majesty of the Lord. O Lord, your hand is lifted up, but they do not

Isaiah

Ephraim: and the fading flower of his glorious beauty, which is at the head of the fat valley, shall be like an early fig before the summer; which when he that looks upon it sees, while it is yet in his hand he eats it up. In that day the Lord of hosts shall be for a crown of glory, and for a diadem of beauty, unto the residue of his people: and for a spirit of judgment to him that sits in judgment, and for strength to those who turn back the battle at the gate. But these also have erred through wine, and through strong drink are gone astray. The priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink, they are swallowed up of wine, they have gone astray through strong drink; they err in vision, they stumble in judgment. For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean. Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little. For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people. To whom he said, This is the rest wherewith you may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear. But the word of the Lord was unto them precept upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little; that they might go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken. Wherefore hear the word of the Lord, you scornful men, that rule this people which is in Jerusalem. Because you have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves. Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation: he that believes shall not make haste. Judgment also will I lay to the line, and righteousness to the plummet: and the hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies, and the waters shall overflow the hiding place. And your covenant with death shall be annulled, and your agreement with hell shall not stand; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, then you shall be trodden down by it. From the time that it goes forth it shall take you: for morning by morning shall it pass over, by day and by night: and it shall be a vexation only to understand the report. For the bed is shorter than that a man can stretch himself on it: and the covering narrower than that he can wrap himself in it. For the Lord shall rise up as in mount Perazim, he shall be wroth as in the valley of Gibeon, that he may do his work, his strange work; and bring to pass his act, his strange act. Now therefore be not mockers, lest your bands be made strong: for I have heard from the Lord God of hosts a consumption, even determined upon the whole earth. Give ear, and hear my voice; hearken, and hear my speech. Does the plowman plow all day to sow? does he open and break the clods of his ground? When he has made plain the face thereof, does he not cast abroad the fitches, and scatter the cummin, and cast in the principal wheat and the appointed barley and the rye in their place? For his God does instruct him to discretion, and does teach him. For the fitches are not threshed with a threshing instrument, neither is a cart wheel turned about upon the cummin; but the fitches are beaten out with a staff, and the cummin with a rod. Bread corn is bruised; but he will not ever be threshing it, nor break it with the wheel of his cart, nor bruise it with his horsemen. This also comes forth from the Lord of hosts, who is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in working. Woe to Ariel, Ariel

Isaiah

A year is added to a year; the feasts have revolved: I will press hard on Ariel, and it shall be sorrowful and mourn, and it shall be to me as Ariel. And I will surround you like a sphere, and cast up a mound against you, and set up fortifications against you. You shall be brought low, you shall speak from the earth, and your speech shall be heard from the ground. And your voice shall be from the earth like a spirit medium, and your speech shall murmur from the dust. And the multitude of those who fan you shall be like fine dust, and the multitude of those who prevailed against you shall be like flying chaff. And suddenly, quickly, she shall be visited by the Lord of hosts with thunder and earthquake, and great noise of whirlwind and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire. And the multitude of all the nations that have fought against Ariel, even all who have warred against her and have prevailed over her, shall be as a dream of a night vision. As when a hungry man dreams, and behold he eats; but he awakes, and his soul is empty: and as when a thirsty man dreams, and behold he drinks; but he awakes, and behold he is faint and his soul is thirsty: so shall the multitude of all nations be that fight against Mount Zion. Be astonished and wonder; fluctuate and be unsteady: be drunk, but not with wine; stagger, but not with strong drink: for the Lord has poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep. He has closed your eyes, the prophets; and your rulers, the seers, he has covered. And the vision of all is become to you as the words of a sealed book, which men deliver to one who is learned, saying: Read this, and he says: I cannot, for it is sealed. And the book is delivered to one who is not learned, saying: Read this, and he says: I cannot read.

And the Lord said: Because this people draws near to me with their mouth, and honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me, and their fear toward me is a commandment of men learned by rote: therefore, behold, I will again do a marvelous work and a wonder among this people. For the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hidden. Woe to those who are deep in heart to hide their counsel from the Lord, and whose works are in the dark, who say: Who sees us? Who knows us? This your perversity is as if the clay should think against the potter, and the work say to the maker: You did not make me; or the thing formed say to him who formed it: You have no understanding. Is it not yet a very little while, and Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field shall be counted for a forest? And in that day the deaf shall hear the words of the book, and out of their gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind shall see. The meek shall increase their joy in the Lord, and the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel: because the terrible one is brought to nothing, and the scorner is consumed, and all those who watch for iniquity are cut off: those who made a man to offend in word, and laid a trap for him who reproved in the gate, and turned aside the just for a thing of nothing. Therefore thus says the Lord, who redeemed Abraham, concerning the house of Jacob: Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall his face now grow pale: but when he sees his children, the work of my hands, in the midst of him, they will sanctify my name, and sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall fear the God of Israel. Those who err in spirit will come to understanding, and those who grumble will accept instruction.

Chapter 30. And he says: Woe to the rebellious children, who take counsel, but not of me; and who cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin: who walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked of my mouth;

Isaiah

...but the things worthy of a ruler he will consider, and he himself will stand over the leaders. Rise up, you wealthy women, and hear my voice; you complacent daughters, give ear to my speech. In days and years you who are complacent will be troubled. For the harvest is finished; the gathering will come no more. Be dismayed, you prosperous women; be troubled, you who are complacent; strip yourselves bare and put on sackcloth upon your loins. Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine. Upon the land of my people thorns and briers shall spring up; how much more upon all the houses of joy in the exultant city. For the palace has been forsaken, the crowded city deserted; the strongholds have become dens forever. The joy of the wild donkeys, the pastures of flocks; until the Spirit is poured upon us from on high. Then the desert shall become a fertile field, and the fertile field shall be considered a forest. Justice shall dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness shall abide in the fertile field. The work of righteousness shall be peace, and the effect of righteousness shall be quietness and assurance forever. My people shall dwell in a peaceful habitation, in secure dwellings, and in quiet resting places. But hail shall bring the forest low, and the city shall be utterly humbled. Blessed are you who sow beside all waters, who let the feet of the ox and donkey range freely. (Chapter 33)

Woe to you who destroy, will you not yourself be destroyed? And you who plunder, will you not yourself be plundered? When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; when you have stopped plundering, you will be plundered. O Lord, have mercy on us; we wait for you. Be our strength every morning, our salvation in time of trouble. At the sound of your voice, peoples flee; when you rise up, nations are scattered. And your spoil shall be gathered as the locust is gathered; as a swarm of locusts rushes about...

...the ditches will be full of them. The Lord is exalted, for he dwells on high; he has filled Zion with justice and righteousness. He will be the stability of your times, abundance of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge; the fear of the Lord is his treasure. Behold, their valiant ones cry aloud outside; the messengers of peace weep bitterly. The roads lie waste; the wayfarer has ceased. He has broken the covenant, he has despised the cities, he has no regard for people. The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is confounded and has withered away. Sharon has become like a desert, and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves. Now I will arise, says the Lord; now I will be exalted, now I will lift myself up. You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble; your breath is a fire that will consume you. And the peoples will be as if burned to lime, like thorns cut down that are burned in the fire. Hear, you who are far off, what I have done; and you who are near, acknowledge my might. The sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling has seized the godless: Who among us can dwell with the consuming fire? Who among us can dwell with everlasting burning? He who walks righteously and speaks uprightly, who despises unjust gain, who shakes his hands free of bribes, who stops his ears from hearing of bloodshed and shuts his eyes from looking on evil — he will dwell on the heights; his refuge will be the fortresses of rocks; bread will be given him; his water will be sure. Your eyes will behold the king in his beauty; they will see a land that stretches afar. Your heart will muse on the terror of the past: Where is he who counted? Where is he who weighed? Where is he who counted the towers? You will see no more the insolent people, the people of an obscure speech that you cannot comprehend, stammering in a tongue that you cannot understand. Look upon Zion, the city...

Isaiah

The eyes of your people will see Jerusalem as a wealthy dwelling place, a tent that cannot be moved; its pegs will never be pulled out forever, and none of its ropes will be broken. For there the Lord will be glorified among us, the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king; he will save us. Your ropes are loosened; they could not hold the mast firm nor spread the sail. Then the spoil of much plunder was divided; the lame took the prey, and no one said, "I am sick." The people who dwell in it will have their iniquity taken away. Chapter 34.

Draw near, O nations, and hear; and listen, O peoples. Let the earth hear and all that fills it; the world and all that comes from it. For the Lord's wrath is upon all nations, and his fury upon all their armies. He has devoted them to destruction, he has given them over to slaughter. Their slain shall be cast out, and the stench of their corpses shall rise. The mountains shall run with their blood, and all the host of heaven shall rot away. The heavens shall be rolled up like a scroll, and all their host shall wither like a leaf withering on a vine, or as a fig withers on a fig tree. For my sword has drunk its fill in the heavens; behold, it descends upon Edom, upon the people I have devoted to judgment. The sword of the Lord is filled with blood; it is gorged with fat, with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams. For the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Edom. Wild oxen shall fall with them, and young steers with the mighty bulls. Their land shall be soaked with blood, and their soil made rich with fat.

For it is the day of the Lord's vengeance, the year of recompense for the cause of Zion. And its streams shall be turned into pitch, and its soil into sulfur; its land shall become burning pitch. Night and day it shall not be quenched; its smoke shall go up forever. From generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it forever and ever. But the hawk and the porcupine shall possess it, the ibis and the raven shall dwell in it. He shall stretch the line of confusion over it, and the plumb line of emptiness. Its nobles shall be no more, nor shall they proclaim a king there; all its princes shall be nothing. Thorns shall grow over its strongholds, nettles and thistles in its fortresses. It shall be the haunt of jackals, an abode for ostriches. And wild animals shall meet with hyenas; the wild goat shall cry to his fellow. Indeed, there the night bird settles and finds for herself a resting place. There the tree snake makes its nest and lays eggs and gathers her young under her shadow; there also the vultures are gathered, each one with her mate. Seek and read from the book of the Lord: not one of these shall be missing; none shall be without her mate. For his mouth has commanded, and his Spirit has gathered them. He has cast the lot for them; his hand has divided it out to them with the line; they shall possess it forever; from generation to generation they shall dwell in it. Chapter 35.

The wilderness and the dry land shall be glad; the desert shall rejoice and blossom like a lily. It shall blossom abundantly and rejoice with joy and singing. The glory of Lebanon shall be given to it, the majesty of Carmel and Sharon. They shall see the glory of the Lord, the majesty of our God. Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees. Say,

Isaiah

The Lord will deliver us. Have the gods of the nations delivered each his own land from the hand of the king of Assyria? Where is the god of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Have they delivered Samaria from my hand? Who among all the gods of these lands has delivered his land from my hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem from my hand? And they were silent and answered him not a word, for the king had commanded, saying: Do not answer him. And Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and told him the words of the Rabshakeh. Chapter 37.

And it came to pass, when King Hezekiah heard it, that he tore his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth and went into the house of the Lord. And he sent Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz. And they said to him: Thus says King Hezekiah: This day is a day of tribulation and rebuke and blasphemy, for the children have come to the point of birth and there is no strength to bring forth. It may be that the Lord your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master has sent to blaspheme the living God, and will rebuke the words which the Lord your God has heard. Lift up a prayer therefore for the remnant that is left. And the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah, and Isaiah said to them: Thus shall you say to your master: Thus says the Lord: Do not be afraid because of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me. Behold, I will send a spirit upon him, and he shall hear a rumor and return to his own land, and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land. So the Rabshakeh returned,

and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that he had departed from Lachish. And he heard concerning Tirhakah king of Ethiopia, saying: He has come out to fight against you. And when he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah saying: Thus shall you speak to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your God in whom you trust deceive you, saying: Jerusalem shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria. Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, destroying them utterly, and shall you be delivered? Have the gods of the nations delivered those whom my fathers destroyed: Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph, and the children of Eden who were in Telassar? Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena and Ivah? And Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it, and he went up to the house of the Lord, and spread it before the Lord. And Hezekiah prayed to the Lord, saying: O Lord of hosts, God of Israel, who dwells between the cherubim, you are God, you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; you made heaven and earth. Incline your ear, O Lord, and hear; open your eyes, O Lord, and see; and hear all the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to blaspheme the living God. Truly, O Lord, the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and their lands, and have cast their gods into the fire, for they were no gods but the work of men's hands, wood and stone, and they destroyed them. Now therefore, O Lord our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are the Lord God. And Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Because you have prayed to me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria, this is the word which the Lord has spoken against him: The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and mocked you;

Isaiah

I said: I shall not see the Lord God in the land of the living; I shall behold man no more, nor the inhabitant of the place of rest. My generation is ended and rolled away from me, like a shepherd's tent. My life is cut off as by a weaver; while I was yet beginning, he cut me off. From morning until evening you will make an end of me; I was hoping until morning. Like a lion he has broken all my bones. From morning until evening you will make an end of me. Like a young swallow so will I cry; I will meditate like a dove. My eyes are weakened looking upward. Lord, I suffer violence; answer for me. What shall I say, or what will he answer for me, since he himself has done it? I will recount to you all my years in the bitterness of my soul. Lord, if man lives by these things, and the life of my spirit is in all such things, you will correct me and make me live; behold, in peace my bitterness is most bitter. But you have delivered my soul that it should not perish; you have cast all my sins behind your back. For hell shall not confess to you, nor shall death praise you; they that go down into the pit shall not look for your truth. The living, the living, he shall give praise to you, as I do this day; the father shall make your truth known to his children. Lord, save me, and we will sing my psalms all the days of our life in the house of the Lord. And Isaiah commanded that they take a lump of figs and lay it as a plaster upon the wound, and he should be healed. And Hezekiah said: What shall be the sign that I shall go up to the house of the Lord? Chapter 39.

At that time Merodach-Baladan, son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and gifts to Hezekiah; for he had heard that he had been sick and had recovered. And Hezekiah was glad of them, and showed them the house of his spicery and the silver and gold and

ointments and precious oil and all his storehouses and all that was found in his treasuries. There was nothing in his house nor in all his dominion that Hezekiah showed them not. Then Isaiah the prophet came to king Hezekiah and said to him: What did these men say, and whence came they to you? And Hezekiah said: They are come from a far country unto me, from Babylon. And he said: What have they seen in your house? And Hezekiah said: All things that are in my house they have seen; there is nothing among my treasures that I have not shown them. Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah: Hear the word of the Lord of hosts. Behold, the days come that all that is in your house and that which your fathers have stored up until this day shall be carried to Babylon; nothing shall be left, says the Lord. And of your sons that shall issue from you, whom you shall beget, they shall take away, and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon. And Hezekiah said to Isaiah: The word of the Lord which you have spoken is good. And he said: Let there be peace and truth in my days. Chapter 40.

Comfort, comfort my people, says your God. Speak to the heart of Jerusalem and call to her; for her evil is accomplished, her iniquity is forgiven. She has received from the hand of the Lord double for all her sins. A voice of one crying in the desert: Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight in the wilderness the paths of our God. Every valley shall be exalted and every mountain and hill shall be brought low; and the crooked shall become straight and the rough places plain. And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh together shall see that the mouth of the Lord has spoken. The voice of one saying: Cry. And I said: What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all the glory thereof is as the flower of the field. The grass has withered

Isaiah

shall be confounded. Who has formed a god, or molded an image that is profitable for nothing? Behold, all who share in it shall be confounded. For the craftsmen themselves are human. They shall all assemble and stand, and they shall fear and be confounded together. The blacksmith with his file worked in the coals and with hammers fashioned it, and worked with the strength of his arm. He shall be hungry and faint: he shall drink no water and shall grow weary. The carpenter stretched out his rule, he formed it with a plane. He made it into squares and shaped it with a compass; and he made it in the likeness of a man, a handsome person, dwelling in a house. He cut down cedars, and took the holm tree and the oak that stood among the trees of the forest. He planted the pine tree which the rain nourished: and it became fuel for man. He took some of it and warmed himself; and he kindled it and baked bread: and of the rest he made a god and worshiped it; he made a graven image and bowed down before it. Half of it he burned with fire; over the coals thereof he roasted flesh and ate his fill; and he warmed himself and said, Aha, I am warm, I have seen the fire. And of the rest thereof he made a god and his graven image. He bows down to it and worships it and beseeches it, saying: Deliver me, for you are my god. They have not known nor understood: for their eyes are shut so that they cannot see; and their hearts, that they cannot understand. They do not consider in their minds, nor have the knowledge nor the understanding to say: Half of it I burned in the fire, and I baked bread on its coals; I roasted flesh and ate it: and shall I make the residue thereof an idol? Shall I bow down to a block of wood? The portion thereof is ashes. A foolish heart has led him astray, and he cannot deliver his soul, nor can he say: Is there not a lie in my right hand? Remember these things, O Jacob and Israel, for you are my servant.

I have formed you; you are my servant, O Israel; you shall not be forgotten by me. I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud and your sins like a mist. Return to me, for I have redeemed you. Sing, O heavens, for the Lord has done it; shout, O depths of the earth; break forth into singing, O mountains, O forest and every tree in it. For the Lord has redeemed Jacob and glorified himself in Israel. Thus says the Lord, your Redeemer, who formed you from the womb: I am the Lord, who made all things, who alone stretched out the heavens, who spread out the earth. I am he who frustrates the signs of diviners and makes fools of those who divine; who turns wise men back and makes their knowledge foolish; who confirms the word of his servant and fulfills the counsel of his messengers; who says of Jerusalem, It shall be inhabited, and of the cities of Judah, They shall be built; and I will raise up their ruins; who says to the deep, Be dry, and I will dry up your rivers; who says of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and he shall fulfill all my purpose. Who says to Jerusalem, You shall be built, and to the temple, Your foundation shall be laid. Chapter 45.

Thus says the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped, to subdue nations before him and to loose the belts of kings, to open doors before him and that gates may not be closed: I will go before you and level the exalted places; I will break in pieces the gates of bronze and cut through the bars of iron. I will give you the treasures of darkness and the hoards in secret places, that you may know that it is I, the Lord, the God of Israel, who call you by your name. For the sake of my servant Jacob, and Israel my chosen, I call you by your name; I name you, though you do not know me. I am the Lord, and there is no other; besides me there is no God. I equip you, though you do not know me, that people may know, from the rising of the sun and from the west, that there is none besides me.

Isaiah

There is no God but me. I am the Lord and there is no other, forming light and creating darkness, making peace and creating evil. I am the Lord who does all these things. Drop down, O heavens, from above, and let the clouds rain down the Just One; let the earth open and bring forth a savior, and let justice spring up at the same time. I, the Lord, have created him. Woe to him who strives with his maker, a potsherd among the potsherds of the earth. Shall the clay say to the potter: What are you making, and your work is without hands? Woe to him who says to his father: What are you begetting, and to the woman: What are you bringing forth? Thus says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, his maker: Ask me of things to come concerning my children, and concerning the work of my hands, give me charge. I have made the earth and I created man upon it. I, with my hands, stretched out the heavens, and I have given commandment to all their host. I have raised him up in justice, and I will direct all his ways. He shall build my city and he shall let go my captives, not for ransom nor for gifts, says the Lord God of hosts. Thus says the Lord: The labor of Egypt and the merchandise of Ethiopia and of the Sabeans, men of stature, shall come over to you and shall be yours. They shall walk after you, they shall go bound in chains; and they shall worship you and shall make supplication to you. Surely God is in you, and there is no God besides you. Verily you are a God that hides yourself, O God of Israel, the Savior. They are all confounded and ashamed, the makers of idols have gone together into confusion. But Israel is saved by the Lord with an everlasting salvation. You shall not be confounded and you shall not be ashamed forever and ever; because thus says the Lord who created the heavens. He is God himself who formed the earth and made it; he himself is its maker. He did not create it in vain; he formed it to be inhabited. I am the Lord and there is no other. I have not spoken in secret, in a dark place of the earth. I have not said to the seed of Jacob: Seek me in vain.

I am the Lord who speaks justice, who declares right things. Gather yourselves together and come, draw near together, you that are saved from among the gentiles. They have no knowledge who carry about the wood of their graven image and pray to a god that cannot save. Declare and come near, and consult together. Who has announced this from the beginning, who has foretold it from that time? Have not I, the Lord, and there is no God else besides me? A just God and a Savior, there is none besides me. Be converted to me and you shall be saved, all the ends of the earth; for I am God and there is no other. I have sworn by myself, the word of justice shall go out of my mouth and shall not return; for every knee shall bow to me and every tongue shall swear. Therefore in the Lord shall they say, are my justices and my empire. To him they shall come. And all that fight against him shall be confounded. In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified and praised. Chapter 46.

Bel is broken, Nebo is destroyed; their idols are put upon beasts and cattle. Your burdens of heavy weight even unto weariness, are fainted and fallen together; they could not save the bearer, and the soul itself shall go into captivity. Hear me, O house of Jacob, all the remnant of the house of Israel, who are carried by my womb, who are borne up by my womb. Even to your old age I am the same, and to your grey hairs I will carry you. I have made you and I will bear you; I will carry and I will save. To whom have you likened me and made me equal, and compared me, as if I were like? You that contribute gold out of the bag and weigh out silver in the scales, and hire a goldsmith to make a god, and they fall down and worship. They bear him on their shoulders and carry him and set him in his place, and he shall stand and shall not move from his place. But when they shall cry to him he shall not

Isaiah

He will hear of tribulation but will not save them. Remember this and be confounded: return, transgressors, to the heart. Remember the former ages, for I am God, and there is no other God, nor is there any like me, who declare from the beginning things to come, and from ancient times things not yet done, saying: My counsel shall stand, and all my will shall be done. I call a bird of prey from the east, and from a far country the man of my will. I have spoken and will bring it to pass: I have created and will do it. Hear me, you hard of heart, who are far from justice. I have brought my justice near, it shall not be far off; and my salvation shall not tarry. I will give salvation in Zion, and my glory in Israel. Chapter 47.

Come down, sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon; sit on the ground, there is no throne for the daughter of the Chaldeans; for you shall no more be called tender and delicate. Take the millstone and grind flour: uncover your shame, strip off your train, pass over the rivers. Your nakedness shall be uncovered, yes, your shame shall be seen. I will take vengeance, and no man shall resist me. Our redeemer, the Lord of hosts is his name, the Holy One of Israel. Sit in silence and get into darkness, O daughter of the Chaldeans; for you shall no more be called the lady of kingdoms. I was angry with my people, I have polluted my inheritance, and given them into your hand. You showed them no mercy; you made your yoke very heavy upon the aged. You said, I shall be a lady forever, so that you did not lay these things to heart, nor did you remember your latter end. Therefore hear now this, you given to pleasures, who dwell securely, who say in your heart: I am, and there is none besides me. I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children. But these two things shall come to you in a moment, in one day: the loss of children and widowhood. All these things shall come upon you

because of the multitude of your sorceries, and for the great abundance of your enchantments. For you have trusted in your wickedness, and have said: None sees me. Your wisdom and your knowledge, it has turned you aside; and you have said in your heart: I am, and there is no one besides me. Therefore shall evil come upon you; you shall not know its origin; and mischief shall fall upon you, which you shall not be able to put away; and desolation shall come upon you suddenly, which you do not know. Stand now with your enchantments, and with the multitude of your sorceries, wherein you have labored from your youth; if perhaps you may prevail, if perhaps you may be stronger. You are wearied in the multitude of your counsels. Let now the astrologers stand up and save you, those who gaze at the stars, who at the new moons predict what shall come upon you. Behold, they are as stubble; the fire has burned them. They shall not deliver themselves from the power of the flame: this is no coal to warm at, nor fire to sit before. Such are they to you with whom you have labored, your merchants from your youth; they have wandered every one to his own way; there is no one to save you. Chapter 48.

Hear this, O house of Jacob, who are called by the name of Israel, and have come out of the waters of Judah; who swear by the name of the Lord, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in righteousness. For they call themselves of the holy city, and stay themselves upon the God of Israel; the Lord of hosts is his name. I have declared the former things from the beginning; and they went forth out of my mouth, and I proclaimed them; suddenly I acted, and they came to pass. Because I knew that you are obstinate, and your neck is an iron sinew, and your brow is bronze; I have declared it to you from of old; before it came to pass I proclaimed it to you, lest you should say: My idol has done them, and my graven image and my molten image have commanded them. You have heard; see all this.

Isaiah

He will give them water to drink. And I will make all my mountains a road, and my highways shall be exalted. Behold, these shall come from far away, and behold, those from the north and from the sea, and these from the south. Give praise, O heavens, and let the earth rejoice; let the mountains give praise with jubilation, because the Lord has comforted his people and will have mercy on his poor. And Zion said: The Lord has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me. Can a woman forget her infant, so as not to have mercy on the son of her womb? And if she should forget, yet I will not forget you. Behold, I have engraved you upon my hands; your walls are ever before my eyes. Your builders have come; those who destroy you and lay you waste shall go out from you. Lift up your eyes round about and see: all these have gathered together and have come to you. As I live, says the Lord, you shall be clothed with all of these as with an ornament, and you shall bind them on as a bride does. For your wastes and your desolate places and your ruined land — now you shall be too narrow for your inhabitants, and those who swallowed you up shall be far away. The children of your barrenness shall yet say in your ears: The place is too narrow for me; make room for me to dwell. And you shall say in your heart: Who has fathered these for me? I was barren and brought forth no children; I was taken captive and exiled — and who has reared these? I was left alone; where then have these come from? Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will lift up my hand to the nations, and raise my standard to the peoples. And they shall bring your sons in their arms, and carry your daughters on their shoulders. Kings shall be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. With their faces to the ground they shall bow down to you, and lick the dust of your feet. And you shall know that I am the Lord; those who wait for me shall not be put to shame. Can the prey be taken from the mighty, or the captive of the strong be rescued?

For thus says the Lord: Even the captive of the mighty shall be taken away, and what was seized by the strong shall be rescued. I will contend with those who contend with you, and I will save your children. And I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh, and they shall be drunk with their own blood as with new wine. And all flesh shall know that I am the Lord, your Savior, and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob. Chapter 50.

Thus says the Lord: Where is this bill of divorce of your mother by which I put her away? Or which of my creditors is it to whom I have sold you? Behold, for your iniquities you were sold, and for your transgressions your mother was put away. For I came and there was no man; I called and there was no one to answer. Is my hand too short to redeem, or have I no power to deliver? Behold, by my rebuke I dry up the sea, I make rivers a desert; their fish stink for lack of water and die of thirst. I clothe the heavens with darkness and make sackcloth their covering. The Lord God has given me a learned tongue, that I should know how to sustain with a word him who is weary. Morning by morning he wakens my ear to hear as those who are taught. The Lord God has opened my ear, and I was not rebellious; I turned not backward. I gave my back to those who struck me, and my cheeks to those who pulled out my beard; I did not hide my face from shame and spitting. But the Lord God helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced. Therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame. He who vindicates me is near. Who will contend with me? Let us stand together. Who is my adversary? Let him come near to me. Behold, the Lord God is my helper. Who will condemn me? Behold, all of them shall wear out like a garment; the moth shall eat them up.

Isaiah

In the streams beneath the projecting rocks.
In the parts of the streams is your portion: this
is your lot. And to them you poured out a libation:
you offered sacrifice. Shall I not be angry for these
things? Upon a high and lofty mountain
you set your bed: and there you went up
to offer sacrifices. And behind the door and the doorpost
you set your memorial: for beside me you have uncovered
yourself and received another. You enlarged
your bed and made a covenant with them. You
loved their bed with open hand: and adorned
yourself with royal ointment: and multiplied
your perfumes. You sent your messengers
far off: and were brought down even to
hell. In the multitude of your ways you labored:
yet you did not say, I will rest. You found
life in your hand: therefore you were not
grieved. For whom were you anxious and afraid?
You have lied, and have not remembered me,
nor thought of me in your heart. For I held
my peace and was as one not seeing: and you
forgot me. I will declare your justice: and
your works shall not profit you. When you cry,
let your gathered ones deliver you. And the
wind shall carry them all away: the breeze shall
take them. But he that puts his trust in me shall
inherit the land and possess my holy mountain: and
he shall say, Cast up, cast up, prepare the way:
take away the stumbling blocks out of the way of my people.
For thus says the high and lofty One who
inhabits eternity, and whose name is Holy.
He dwells in the high and holy place: and also
with the contrite and humble spirit: to revive
the spirit of the humble and to revive the heart of the contrite.
For I will not contend forever:
nor will I be always angry: for the spirit would
fail before me, and the souls which I have made.
For the iniquity of his covetousness I
was angry and struck him: I hid
and was indignant. And he went on in the way
of his own heart. I have seen his ways and healed him:

and brought him back: and restored consolations
to him and to those who mourn for him. I create
the fruit of the lips, peace: peace to him that is far
off and to him that is near, says the Lord: and I have healed him.
But the wicked are like the troubled sea
which cannot rest: and its waves cast up
mire and dirt. There is no
peace, says my God, to the wicked. Chapter 58.

Cry out, do not cease: lift up your voice like a trumpet
and announce to my people their sins
and to the house of Jacob their transgressions. For they seek
me day by day and desire to know my ways: as
a nation that has done justice and has not
forsaken the judgment of their God. They ask
of me the judgments of justice: they desire to draw near to God.
Why have we fasted and you have not seen: why have we
humbled our souls and you have not known? Behold,
in the day of your fast your own will is found:
and you exact payment from all your debtors.
Behold you fast unto contention and strife and strike with the fist wickedly. Do
not fast as you have done until this day:
to make your cry to be heard on high.
Is this such a fast as I have chosen: for a man
to afflict his soul for a day?
Is it to wind his head about like a circle
and to spread sackcloth and ashes? Will you call
this a fast and a day acceptable
to the Lord? Is not this rather the fast
that I have chosen? Loose the bands of wickedness:
undo the heavy burdens.
Let those who are oppressed go free:
and break every yoke. Share your bread with the hungry:
and bring the poor wanderers into your house. When you see the naked, cover him:
and do not hide yourself from your own flesh. Then shall your light break
forth like the morning: and your health
shall spring forth quickly. And your justice shall go before your face:
and the glory of the Lord shall gather you up. Then
shall you call and the Lord will hear: you shall cry
and he shall say, Here I am. If you take away from the midst

for the Lord your God is merciful.

Isaiah

against his own witnesses and his enemies. He will repay the islands. And those who are in the west shall fear the name of the Lord, and those who are in the east shall fear his glory. When he shall come like a violent river, whom the spirit of the Lord drives: and the redeemer shall come to Zion, and to those who turn from iniquity in Jacob, says the Lord. This is my covenant with them, says the Lord. My spirit which is in you, and my words which I have put in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your children, says the Lord, from this time and for evermore. Chapter 60.

Arise, be enlightened, O Jerusalem, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you. For behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and a mist the peoples: but the Lord shall arise upon you, and his glory shall be seen upon you. And the nations shall walk in your light, and kings in the brightness of your rising. Lift up your eyes round about and see: all these are gathered together, they have come to you. Your sons shall come from afar, and your daughters shall rise up at your side. Then you shall see and overflow, and your heart shall wonder and be enlarged. When the multitude of the sea shall be converted to you, the strength of the nations shall come to you. The multitude of camels shall cover you, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah. All those from Sheba shall come, bringing gold and frankincense, and announcing praise to the Lord. All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered together to you, the rams of Nebaioth shall minister to you: they shall be offered upon my acceptable altar, and I will glorify the house of my majesty. Who are these that fly as clouds, and as doves to their windows? For the islands wait for me, and the ships of the sea from the beginning, that I may bring your sons from afar, their silver and their gold with them, to the name of the Lord your God, and to the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you. And the children of strangers shall build up your walls, and their kings shall minister to you. For in my wrath I struck you,

and in my reconciliation I had mercy on you. And your gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day or night; that the strength of the nations may be brought to you, and their kings may be brought. For the nation and the kingdom that will not serve you shall perish: and the nations shall be utterly wasted. The glory of Lebanon shall come to you, the fir tree, and the box tree, and the pine tree together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary, and I will glorify the place of my feet. And the children of those who afflicted you shall come bowing down to you, and all those that slandered you shall worship at the steps of your feet, and shall call you the city of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel. Because you were forsaken and hated and there was none that passed through you, I will make you an everlasting pride, a joy from generation to generation. And you shall suck the milk of the nations, and you shall be nursed with the breasts of kings. And you shall know that I am the Lord your Savior, and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob. For bronze I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver, and for wood bronze, and for stones iron. And I will make your overseers peace, and your rulers righteousness. Violence shall no more be heard in your land, neither wasting nor destruction within your borders; and you shall call your walls Salvation, and your gates Praise. The sun shall no more be your light by day, neither for brightness shall the moon give light to you: but the Lord shall be your everlasting light, and your God your glory. Your sun shall no more go down, neither shall your moon withdraw; for the Lord shall be your everlasting light, and the days of your mourning shall be ended. Your people also shall be all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified. The smallest shall become a thousand, and the least a mighty nation. I am the Lord; in its time I will do this swiftly. Chapter 61.

Isaiah

You are righteous, and a warrior to save. Why then is your garment red, and your clothing like that of one who treads in the winepress? I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the nations there was no man with me. I trod them down in my anger, and trampled them in my wrath. Their blood was sprinkled upon my garments, and I stained all my clothing. For the day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redemption had come. I looked about and there was no helper; I sought and there was none to assist. So my own arm brought me salvation, and my own indignation sustained me. I trod them down in my fury and made them drunk with my wrath, and I poured out their strength upon the earth. I will recall the mercies of the Lord, the praise of the Lord for all that he has granted us, and the great goodness to the house of Israel which he gave them according to his clemency and according to the multitude of his mercies. And he said: Surely they are my people, children who will not be unfaithful. And he became their savior. In all their affliction he was not afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and in his mercy he redeemed them, and he lifted them up and carried them all the days of old. But they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit. So he turned against them as an enemy, and he himself fought against them. Then he remembered the days of old, of Moses and his people. Where is he who brought them out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? Where is he who placed his Holy Spirit among them? Who led Moses by the right hand with his glorious arm, who divided the waters before them to make himself an everlasting name? Who led them through the deep like a horse in the desert, not stumbling, like a beast in the open field,

going down. The Spirit of the Lord was their guide. So you led your people to make yourself a glorious name. Look down from heaven, and see from your holy and glorious dwelling. Where is your zeal and your might? The yearning of your heart and your compassion are withheld from me. For you are our Father; though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us, you, O Lord, are our Father, our Redeemer; from of old that is your name. Why, O Lord, do you make us stray from your ways and harden our hearts so that we do not fear you? Return for the sake of your servants, the tribes of your heritage. Your holy people possessed your sanctuary only for a little while; our enemies have trampled it down. We have become like those over whom you have never ruled, like those who are not called by your name. Chapter 64.

O that you would tear open the heavens and come down, so that the mountains would quake at your presence — as when fire kindles brushwood and the fire causes water to boil — to make your name known to your adversaries, so that the nations might tremble at your presence. When you did awesome deeds that we did not expect, you came down; the mountains quaked at your presence. From ages past no one has heard, no ear has perceived, no eye has seen any God besides you, who works for those who wait for him. You meet those who gladly do right, those who remember you in your ways. But you were angry, and we sinned; because of our sins we have long been in your hand, and shall we be saved? We have all become like one who is unclean, and all our righteous deeds are like a filthy cloth. We all fade like a leaf, and our iniquities, like the wind, take us away. There is no one who calls on your name, or attempts to take hold of you. For you have hidden your face from us, and have delivered us into the hand of our iniquity. Yet, O Lord, you are our Father; we are

Isaiah

They shall not plant and another eat. For as the days of a tree shall be the days of my people: and the works of their hands shall grow old. My chosen shall not labor in vain: nor bring forth children for trouble: for they are the seed of the blessed of the Lord, and their offspring with them. And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will hear: while they are yet speaking, I will hear. The wolf and the lamb shall feed together: and the lion shall eat straw like the ox: and dust shall be the serpent's food. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, saith the Lord. ch. 66

Thus saith the Lord: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What manner of house will you build me: and what place shall be my rest? My hand made all these things: and all these things were made, saith the Lord. But to whom shall I have respect: but to him that is poor and little, and of a contrite spirit, and that trembleth at my words? He that sacrificeth an ox, is as if he slew a man. He that killeth a beast, as if he should brain a dog. He that offereth an oblation, as if he should offer swine's blood. He that remembereth incense, as if he should bless an idol. All these things have they chosen in their ways: and their soul is delighted in their abominations. Therefore I also will choose their mockeries: and will bring upon them the things they feared: because I called and there was none that would hear: I have spoken and they did not listen. And they did evil in my sight: and chose the things that displease me. Hear the word of the Lord, you that tremble at his word. Your brethren that hate you and cast you out for my name's sake, have said: Let the Lord be glorified, and we shall see in your joy: but they shall be confounded. A voice of the people from the city, a voice from the temple, a voice of the Lord rendering recompence to his enemies. Before she travailed she brought forth: before her pain came she was delivered of a man child.

Who hath heard such a thing? and who hath seen the like? Shall the earth bring forth in one day? or shall a nation be brought forth at once? because Sion hath been in labour and hath brought forth her children. Shall not I that make others to bring forth children, myself bring forth, saith the Lord? Shall I, that give generation to others, be barren, saith the Lord thy God? Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad with her, all you that love her. Rejoice for joy with her, all you that mourn for her: That you may suck and be filled with the breasts of her consolations: that you may milk out and flow with delights from the abundance of her glory. For thus saith the Lord: Behold I will bring upon her as it were a river of peace, and as an overflowing torrent the glory of the Gentiles, which you shall suck. You shall be carried at the breasts and upon the knees they shall caress you. As one whom the mother caresseth, so will I comfort you: and you shall be comforted in Jerusalem. You shall see and your heart shall rejoice: and your bones shall flourish like an herb. And the hand of the Lord shall be known to his servants, and he shall be angry with his enemies. For behold the Lord will come with fire, and his chariots are like a whirlwind: to render his wrath in indignation, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For the Lord shall judge by fire, and by his sword unto all flesh: and the slain of the Lord shall be many. They that were sanctified and thought themselves clean in the gardens behind one door within, they that did eat swine's flesh and the abomination and the mouse: they shall be consumed together, saith the Lord. But I know their works and their thoughts: I come to gather all nations and tongues: and they shall come and shall see my glory. And I will set a sign among them: and I will send of them that shall be saved to the nations, into the sea, into Africa, into Lydia: them that draw the bow,

Prologue                                    Jeremiah

to Italy and Greece, to the distant islands, to those who have not heard of me and have not seen my glory. And they shall proclaim my glory among the nations, and they shall bring all your brothers from all nations as an offering to the Lord, on horses and in chariots and in litters and on mules and in wagons, to my holy mountain Jerusalem, says the Lord, just as the children of Israel bring an offering in a clean vessel to the house of the Lord. And I will take some of them as priests and Levites, says the Lord. For as the new heavens and the new earth which I make shall endure before me, says the Lord God, so shall your offspring and your name endure. From new moon to new moon, and from sabbath to sabbath, all flesh shall come to worship before me, says the Lord. And they shall go forth and look on the dead bodies of the men who have rebelled against me. For their worm shall not die, their fire shall not be quenched, and they shall be an abhorrence to all flesh. Here ends Isaiah. Here begins the prologue to the prophet Jeremiah.
The prophet Jeremiah, about whom this prologue is written, seems to some — among the Hebrews as with Isaiah, Hosea, and certain other prophets — to be rustic, but in understanding he is their equal, having prophesied in the same spirit. The simplicity of his speech comes from the place where he was born. For he was an Anathothite, which is to this day a small village a few miles from Jerusalem. He was a priest, consecrated in his mother's womb, and he dedicated his virginity to serving the evangelical man of Christ's church. He began to prophesy as a boy, and witnessed the captivity of the city and of Judea not only in spirit but with his own eyes. Already the ten tribes of Israel had been carried by the Assyrians into Media; already foreign colonists possessed the lands. Thus he prophesied only in Judah and Benjamin, and the ruins of his own city

pleased him with the fourfold alphabet, which we have rendered in the measures of meter and verse. Moreover, we have corrected the order of the visions, which among both Greeks and Latins is entirely confused, restoring it to its original form. As for the book of Baruch, his secretary, which among the Hebrews is neither read nor has a preface: for all these things we are cursed by rivals, against whom I must respond point by point in individual small works. And I endure this because you ask it of me. Indeed, it would have been more expedient to put an end to their fury by my silence; but every day some new piece of writing provokes the madness of the envious. Here ends the prologue. Here begins Jeremiah the prophet, Chapter One.
The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin. The word of the Lord came to him in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign; and it came also in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah the son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the deportation of Jerusalem in the fifth month. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you came forth from the womb I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations. Then I said: Ah, Lord God! Behold, I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth. But the Lord said to me: Do not say "I am only a youth"; for to all to whom I send you, you shall go, and whatever I command you, you shall speak. Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you, says the Lord. Then the Lord put forth his hand and touched my mouth; and the Lord said to me: Behold, I have put my words in your mouth. See, I have set you this day over nations and over kingdoms, to pluck up and to break down and to destroy and to overthrow, and to build

Jeremiah

and laments. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: What do you see, Jeremiah? And I said: I see a watching rod. And the Lord said to me: You have seen well, for I will watch over my word to perform it. And the word of the Lord came to me a second time, saying: What do you see? And I said: I see a boiling pot, and its face is from the face of the north. And the Lord said to me: From the north evil shall be spread over all the inhabitants of the land. For behold, I will call together all the families of the kingdoms of the north, says the Lord, and they shall come and shall set every one his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem, and against all its walls round about, and against all the cities of Judah. And I will pronounce my judgments against them touching all their wickedness, who have forsaken me and have offered sacrifice to strange gods and have adored the works of their own hands. You therefore gird up your loins, and arise and speak to them all that I command you. Fear not at their presence, for I will make you not afraid of their looks. For behold, I have made you this day a fortified city, and an iron pillar, and a bronze wall over all the land, to the kings of Judah, to the princes thereof, and to the priests, and to all the people of the land. And they shall fight against you and shall not prevail, for I am with you, says the Lord, to deliver you. Chapter 2.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Go and cry in the hearing of Jerusalem, saying: Thus says the Lord: I have remembered you, pitying the youth and the love of your espousals when you followed me in the desert, in a land that is not sown. Israel is holy to the Lord, the firstfruits of his increase. All that devour him shall offend: evils shall come upon them, says the Lord. Hear the word of the Lord, O house of Jacob, and all the families

of the house of Israel. Thus says the Lord: What iniquity have your fathers found in me, that they have gone far from me and walked after vanity and become vain? And they said not: Where is the Lord who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, who led us through the desert, through a land uninhabited and pathless, through a land of drought and the image of death, through a land through which no man passed and where no man dwelt. And I brought you into the land of Carmel to eat the fruit thereof and the best things thereof. And when you entered, you defiled my land and made my inheritance an abomination. The priests did not say: Where is the Lord? And they that held the law did not know me, and the pastors transgressed against me, and the prophets prophesied in Baal and followed idols. Therefore I will yet contend in judgment with you, says the Lord, and with your children I will plead.
