But when they came into the midst of the city, Ishmael the son of Nathaniah and the men with him slew them and cast them into the midst of the pit. But ten men were found among them who said to Ishmael: Do not kill us, for we have stores in the field, wheat and barley and oil and honey. So he refrained and did not kill them with their brothers. Now the pit into which Ishmael had cast all the dead bodies of the men whom he had killed because of Gedaliah was the one that King Asa had made because of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael the son of Nathaniah filled it with the slain. Then Ishmael carried away captive all the rest of the people who were in Mizpah, the king's daughters and all the people who remained in Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had committed to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam. And Ishmael the son of Nathaniah took them captive and

Jeremiah.

The famine about which you are anxious will follow you into Egypt and there you will die. Every man who has set his face to go into Egypt to dwell there shall die by the sword, by famine, and by plague. None of them shall survive or escape from the evil that I will bring upon them: for thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel. As my anger and my wrath were poured out on Jerusalem, so my wrath will be poured out on you when you enter Egypt: and you shall become an oath and a horror and a curse and a reproach, and you shall see this place no more. The word of the Lord is upon you, O remnant of Judah. Do not go into Egypt. Know and understand that I have warned you this day: for you have gone astray at the cost of your lives. For you sent me to the Lord your God, saying: Pray for us to the Lord our God, and whatever the Lord our God says, declare it to us and we will do it. And I have declared it to you this day: but you have not obeyed the voice of the Lord your God in anything that he sent me to tell you. Now therefore know for certain that you shall die by the sword, by famine, and by plague in the place where you desire to go and live. Chapter 42.

When Jeremiah had finished speaking to all the people all these words of the Lord their God, with which the Lord their God had sent him to them, Azariah the son of Hoshaiah and Johanan the son of Kareah and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah: You are telling a lie. The Lord our God did not send you to say: Do not go to Egypt to live there: but Baruch the son of Neriah has set you against us, to deliver us into the hands of the Chaldeans, that they may kill us or carry us into exile to Babylon. So Johanan the son of Kareah did not obey,

nor did all the commanders of the forces and all the people obey the voice of the Lord to remain in the land of Judah. But Johanan the son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces took all the remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations to which they had been driven, to live in the land of Judah: men, women, children, the daughters of the king, and every person whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch the son of Neriah: and they came into the land of Egypt, for they did not obey the voice of the Lord: and they came as far as Tahpanhes. Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes: Take large stones in your hands and hide them in the mortar of the pavement that is at the entrance to the house of Pharaoh in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah: and say to them. Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will send and take Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and he will set his throne above these stones that I have hidden, and he will spread his royal canopy over them. And he will come and strike the land of Egypt, giving those who are destined for death to death, and those destined for captivity to captivity, and those destined for the sword to the sword. He will kindle a fire in the temples of the gods of Egypt and burn them and carry their people into captivity. And he will wrap himself in the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his cloak, and he will depart from there in peace. And he will shatter the obelisks of the temple of the Sun that is in the land of Egypt, and the temples of the gods of Egypt he will burn with fire. Chapter 43.

The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews living in the land of Egypt: those living at Migdol, at Tahpanhes, at Memphis, and in the land of Pathros: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: You have seen all

Jeremiah.

This evil which I have brought upon Jerusalem and upon all the cities of Judah — behold, they are desolate this day, and there is no inhabitant in them — because of their wickedness which they have committed to provoke me to anger, in that they went to burn incense and to serve other gods whom they knew not, neither they nor you nor your fathers. And I sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, saying: Do not do this abominable thing that I hate. But they did not listen or incline their ear to turn from their wickedness, to burn no incense to other gods. Therefore my wrath and my anger were poured out and burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, and they have become a waste and a desolation as at this day. And now thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: Why do you commit this great evil against yourselves, to cut off from you man and woman, infant and child, from the midst of Judah, leaving yourselves none to remain, in provoking me to anger with the works of your hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt where you have come to live, so that you may be cut off and become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth? Have you forgotten the evil of your fathers, and the evil of the kings of Judah, and the evil of their wives, and your own evil, and the evil of your wives, which they committed in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem? They have not humbled themselves to this day, nor have they feared, nor walked in my law and in my statutes that I set before you and before your fathers. Therefore thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will set my face against you for harm, to cut off all Judah. And I will take the remnant of Judah, those who have set their faces to come to the land of Egypt to live there, and they shall all perish in the land of Egypt; they shall fall by the sword and by famine; they shall perish, from the least to the greatest, by the sword and by famine; and they shall become an oath, a horror, a curse, and a reproach. I will punish those who dwell in the land of Egypt as I punished Jerusalem, with the sword, with famine, and with pestilence, so that none of the remnant of Judah who have come to live in the land of Egypt shall escape or survive to return to the land of Judah — to which they long to return to dwell there — for they shall not return except some fugitives.

Then all the men who knew that their wives had burned incense to other gods, and all the women who stood by, a great assembly, and all the people who lived in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah: As for the word that you have spoken to us in the name of the LORD, we will not listen to you. But we will do everything that we have vowed: burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, as we did, we and our fathers, our kings and our officials, in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem; for then we had plenty of food and prospered and saw no disaster. But since we ceased burning incense to the queen of heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything and have been consumed by the sword and by famine. And said the women: Was it without our husbands' approval that we made offerings to the queen of heaven and poured out drink offerings to her? Then Jeremiah said to all the people, men and women, and all the people who had given him this answer: As for the burnt offerings that you offered in the cities of Judah and

Jeremiah

The floods of Egypt swell and its currents rise: Egypt rises up like a river, and its waters shall move and surge, and it shall say: I will rise and cover the earth, and destroy the city and its inhabitants. Mount your horses and charge in your chariots, and let the warriors go forth: Ethiopians and Libyans bearing shields, and Lydians taking up and shooting arrows. For that day belongs to the Lord God of hosts, a day of vengeance, that he may take vengeance on his enemies. The sword shall devour and be satisfied, and shall drink its fill of their blood. For the Lord God of hosts holds a sacrifice in the land of the north, by the river Euphrates. Go up to Gilead and take balm, O virgin daughter of Egypt. In vain you multiply remedies; there is no healing for you. The nations have heard of your shame, and your cry has filled the land. For the strong man has stumbled against the strong, and they have both fallen together. The word which the Lord spoke to Jeremiah the prophet, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon would come and strike the land of Egypt. Declare it in Egypt, and proclaim it in Migdol; proclaim it also in Memphis and in Tahpanhes: Stand fast and prepare yourself, for the sword shall devour all around you. Why have your mighty men been swept away? They did not stand because the Lord thrust them down. They stumbled, yes, they fell one upon another, and they said: Arise and let us return to our own people and to our native land, away from the oppressing sword. They gave Pharaoh king of Egypt the name Noise that lets the time pass. As I live, says the King whose name is the Lord of hosts, surely as Tabor is among the mountains and as Carmel is by the sea, so he shall come. Make yourself vessels for exile, O daughter dwelling in Egypt, for Memphis shall become a waste, desolate and uninhabited. Egypt is a beautiful and well-favored heifer,

but destruction comes from the north. Her hired soldiers also who were in her midst like fattened calves: they too turned and fled together, and could not stand, for the day of their calamity has come upon them, the time of their punishment. Her voice moves like a serpent; for they march with an army and come against her with axes as those who cut down trees. They have cut down her forest, says the Lord, though it cannot be searched, because they are more numerous than locusts and without number. The daughter of Egypt is put to shame; she has been given into the hand of the people of the north. The Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Behold, I will punish Amon of Alexandria, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, and her gods, and her kings—Pharaoh and those who trust in him. I will give them into the hand of those who seek their lives, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his servants. And afterward it shall be inhabited as in the days of old, says the Lord. But as for you, do not fear, O Jacob my servant, and do not be dismayed, O Israel. For behold, I will save you from afar, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob shall return and be at rest and at ease, and none shall make him afraid. Fear not, O Jacob my servant, says the Lord, for I am with you; for I will make a full end of all the nations to which I have driven you, but of you I will not make a full end. I will discipline you in just measure, and I will by no means leave you unpunished. Chapter 46.

The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza. Thus says the Lord: Behold, waters are rising out of the north and shall become an overflowing torrent; they shall overflow the land and all that fills it, the city and those who dwell in it. The people shall cry out, and all the inhabitants shall wail.

Jeremiah.

Away from the noise of the chariots of war and their horsemen, from the rumbling of their wheels and the multitude of their axles. Fathers did not look back to their children, their hands being slack, because of the day that is coming to devastate all the Philistines, and to destroy Tyre and Sidon with all their remaining allies. For the Lord will devastate the Philistines, the remnant of the island of Caphtor. Baldness has come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is silenced; and the remnant of their valleys — how long will you gash yourselves? O sword of the Lord, how long before you are quiet? Return to your scabbard; rest and be still. How can it be quiet, when the Lord has given it a charge against Ashkelon and against the seacoast — there he has appointed it.

Concerning Moab. Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Woe to Nebo, for it is laid waste and put to shame. Kiriathaim is taken, the stronghold is put to shame and broken down. There is no more praise of Moab; in Heshbon they have devised evil against her. Come, let us cut her off from being a nation. Therefore you too, Dimon, shall be brought to silence; the sword shall pursue you. A voice of crying from Horonaim: desolation and great destruction. Moab is broken; cry out; announce it to the little ones. For by the ascent of Luhith they go up weeping; for in the descent of Horonaim the enemies have heard a cry of destruction. Flee! Save your lives! Be like a wild shrub in the desert. For because you trusted in your strongholds and your treasures, you also shall be taken. And Chemosh shall go into exile, his priests and his officials together. The destroyer shall come upon every city, and no city shall escape; the valley shall perish and the plain shall be destroyed, as the Lord has spoken. Give wings to Moab, for she would fly away; her cities shall become a desolation,

without inhabitant. Cursed is he who does the work of the Lord with slackness, and cursed is he who keeps back his sword from bloodshed. Moab has been at ease from his youth and has settled on his dregs; he has not been emptied from vessel to vessel, nor has he gone into exile; so his taste remains in him and his scent is not changed. Therefore behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I shall send to him those who pour from vessel to vessel, and they shall pour him out and empty his vessels and break his jars in pieces. Then Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, their confidence. How can you say, "We are heroes and mighty men of war"? Moab is laid waste and her cities have gone up in flames, and her chosen young men have gone down to slaughter, declares the King, whose name is the Lord of hosts. The calamity of Moab is near at hand, and his affliction hastens swiftly. Mourn for him, all you who are around him, and all who know his name; say, "How is the mighty scepter broken, the glorious staff!" Come down from glory, and sit in thirst, O inhabitant of Dibon, for the destroyer of Moab has come up against you; he has destroyed your strongholds. Stand by the road and watch, O inhabitant of Aroer! Ask the man fleeing and the woman escaping; say, "What has happened?" Moab is put to shame, for it is broken. Wail and cry out! Announce by the Arnon that Moab is laid waste. Judgment has come upon the tableland: upon Holon, and Jahzah, and Mephaath, and Dibon, and Nebo, and Beth-diblathaim, and Kiriathaim, and Beth-gamul, and Beth-meon, and Kerioth, and Bozrah, and all the cities of the land of Moab, far and near. The horn of Moab is cut off,

Jeremiah.

The horn of Moab is broken and his arm shattered, says the Lord. Make him drunk, for he has lifted himself against the Lord. Moab shall wallow in his vomit and shall himself also be in derision. For Israel was a derision to you: was he found among thieves? For as often as you spoke of him, you shook your head. Leave the cities and dwell in the rock, you inhabitants of Moab, and be like the dove that makes its nest in the sides of the cave's mouth. We have heard the pride of Moab; he is exceedingly proud, his loftiness and his arrogance and his pride and the haughtiness of his heart. I know his wrath, says the Lord, but it shall not be so; his lies shall not so effect it. Therefore will I howl for Moab, and I will cry out for all Moab; my heart shall mourn for the men of Kir-heres. O vine of Sibmah, I will weep for you with the weeping of Jazer: your plants have gone over the sea, they reach even to the sea of Jazer: the plunderer has fallen upon your summer fruits and upon your vintage. Joy and gladness is taken from the plentiful field and from the land of Moab; and I have caused wine to fail from the winepresses: none shall tread with shouting; their shouting shall be no shouting. From the cry of Heshbon even unto Elealeh, and even unto Jahaz, have they uttered their voice, from Zoar even unto Horonaim, as a heifer of three years old: for the waters also of Nimrim shall be desolate. Moreover I will cause to cease in Moab, says the Lord, him that offers in the high places, and him that burns incense to his gods. Therefore my heart shall sound for Moab like pipes, and my heart shall sound like pipes for the men of Kir-heres: because the riches that he has gotten are perished. For every head shall be bald, and every beard clipped: upon all the hands shall be cuttings, and upon the loins sackcloth. And on all the housetops of Moab and in the streets thereof there is lamentation everywhere: for I have broken Moab

like a vessel wherein is no pleasure, says the Lord. How is it broken down! How have they howled! How has Moab turned the back with shame! So shall Moab be a derision and a dismay to all them about him. For thus says the Lord: Behold, he shall fly as an eagle, and shall spread his wings over Moab. Kerioth is taken, and the strongholds are seized. The heart of the mighty men of Moab at that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pangs. And Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he has magnified himself against the Lord. Fear and the pit and the snare shall be upon you, O inhabitant of Moab, says the Lord. He that flees from the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that gets up out of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for I will bring upon it, even upon Moab, the year of their visitation, says the Lord. They that fled stood under the shadow of Heshbon because of the force: but a fire shall come forth out of Heshbon, and a flame from the midst of Sihon, and shall devour the corner of Moab and the crown of the head of the tumultuous ones. Woe to you, O Moab! The people of Chemosh perish: for your sons are taken captives, and your daughters captives. Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days, says the Lord. Thus far is the judgment of Moab. Chapter 49.

Concerning the children of Ammon. Thus says the Lord: Has Israel no sons? Has he no heir? Why then does their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in the cities thereof? Therefore behold, the days come, says the Lord, that I will cause an alarm of war to be heard against Rabbah of the children of Ammon; and it shall be a desolate heap, and her daughters shall be burned with fire: then shall Israel possess those who possessed him, says the Lord. Howl, O Heshbon, for Ai is spoiled: cry, daughters of Rabbah, gird yourselves with sackcloth; lament and run to and fro among the hedges; for their king shall go into captivity, and his priests and

Jeremiah.

Their flocks and herds shall be taken; their hides and all their vessels and their camels shall be carried off; and a terror shall come upon them on every side. Flee, depart in haste; dwell in the depths, you who inhabit the region, says the Lord. For Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devised a plan against you and formed a purpose against you. Rise up and go up against a nation that is at ease and dwells securely, says the Lord. Its gates are not guarded, and none dwell alone. Their camels shall become plunder, and their many cattle a spoil; and I will scatter them to every wind, even those who are cut off at the corners, and from all their borders I will bring their calamity upon them, says the Lord. And the region shall become a lair of dragons, a desolation forever. No man shall dwell there, nor shall any son of man inhabit it. The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: I will break the bow of Elam, the chief of their might, and I will bring upon Elam the four winds from the four corners of heaven; and I will scatter them to all these winds, and there shall be no nation where the fugitives of Elam shall not come. And I will cause Elam to be dismayed before their enemies, and before those who seek their life. And I will bring evil upon them, even my fierce anger, says the Lord; and I will send the sword after them, until I have consumed them; and I will set my throne in Elam, and will destroy from there the king and the princes, says the Lord. But in the latter days I will restore the fortunes of Elam, says the Lord. Chapter 50.

The word that the Lord spoke concerning Babylon and concerning the land of the Chaldeans by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet. Declare among the nations and announce; lift up a standard, proclaim, and do not conceal it. Say:

Babylon is taken, Bel is put to shame, Merodach is dismayed. Her images are put to shame, her idols are dismayed. For a nation has come up against her from the north; it shall make her land a desolation, and none shall dwell in it; both man and beast have fled. In those days and at that time, says the Lord, the children of Israel shall come, they and the children of Judah together; they shall go, weeping as they go, and they shall seek the Lord their God. They shall ask the way to Zion; their faces shall be set toward it; they shall come and join themselves to the Lord in an everlasting covenant that shall not be forgotten. My people have been lost sheep; their shepherds have led them astray; they have turned them away on the mountains; they have gone from mountain to hill, forgetting their resting place. All who found them devoured them, and their enemies said: We have not sinned, because they sinned against the Lord, the true habitation of justice, even the Lord, the hope of their fathers. Flee from the midst of Babylon, go out of the land of the Chaldeans, and be like the he-goats before the flocks. For behold, I am stirring up and bringing against Babylon a great assembly of nations from the land of the north; and they shall array themselves against her; from there she shall be taken. Their arrows are like those of a skilled warrior; none shall return in vain. And the land of the Chaldeans shall become a plunder; all who plunder her shall be satisfied, says the Lord. Because you rejoiced and exulted, you who plunder my heritage; because you have grown fat like a heifer at grass and neigh like stallions, your mother is greatly put to shame; she who bore you is confounded. Behold, she shall be the last of the nations, a wilderness, dry land, and a desert. Because of the anger of the Lord she shall not be inhabited; she shall be wholly desolate. Everyone who passes by

Thomas

In the fourth month of the reign of Zedekiah, on the ninth day of the month, famine overtook the city, and there was no food for the people of the land. Then the city was broken open, and all the men of war fled and went out of the city at night by way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king's garden, even though the Chaldeans surrounded the city; and the king went by way of the plain. But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king, and they overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was scattered from him. So they captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, which is in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced judgment on him. And the king of Babylon killed the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes; he also killed all the princes of Judah in Riblah. Then he put out the eyes of Zedekiah; and the king of Babylon bound him in chains and carried him to Babylon, and put him in prison until the day of his death. Now in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, who served the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem. He burned the house of the Lord and the king's house; all the houses of Jerusalem, that is, all the houses of the great, he burned with fire. And all the army of the Chaldeans who were with the captain of the guard broke down all the walls of Jerusalem all around. Then Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive some of the poor of the people, and the rest of the people who remained in the city, and those who had defected to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude. But the captain of the guard left some of the poor of the land as vinedressers and farmers. The Chaldeans also broke the bronze pillars that were in the house of the Lord, and the carts and the bronze sea that were in the house of the Lord, and carried all their bronze to Babylon. They also took away the pots, the shovels, the trimmers, the bowls, the spoons, and all the bronze utensils used in service. The captain of the guard took away the firepans and the basins, the things of gold and silver. The two pillars, one sea, and the twelve bronze bulls that were under the bases, which King Solomon had made for the house of the Lord — the bronze of all these vessels was beyond weight. Concerning the pillars: the height of one pillar was eighteen cubits, and a measuring line of twelve cubits could measure its circumference; it was hollow, and its thickness was four fingers. A capital of bronze was on it; the height of one capital was five cubits, with a network and pomegranates all around on the capital, all of bronze. The second pillar was the same, with pomegranates. There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides; all the pomegranates, a hundred on the network all around. The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three doorkeepers. He also took out of the city an officer who had charge of the men of war, seven men of the king's close associates who were found in the city, the principal scribe of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the midst of the city. And Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took these and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah. Then the king of Babylon struck them and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was carried away captive from its own land. These are the people whom Nebuchadnezzar carried away captive in the seventh year: three thousand and twenty-three Jews. In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, eight hundred and thirty-two persons from Jerusalem.

Jeremiah.

In the day of his fierce anger. Mem. From on high he sent fire into my bones, and it prevailed against me. He spread a net for my feet, he turned me back; he has made me desolate and faint all day long. Ayin. The yoke of my transgressions is bound by his hand: they are wreathed, and come up upon my neck. My strength has failed: the Lord has delivered me into their hands, from whom I am not able to rise. Samech. The Lord has taken away all my mighty men from the midst of me: he has called an assembly against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trodden as in a winepress the virgin daughter of Judah. Ayn. For these things I weep; my eye, my eye runs down with water, because the comforter that should relieve my soul is far from me. My children are desolate, because the enemy prevailed. Phe. Zion spreads forth her hands, and there is none to comfort her. The Lord has commanded concerning Jacob, that his adversaries should be round about him. Jerusalem is as a menstruous woman among them. Sade. The Lord is righteous; for I have rebelled against his commandment. Hear, I pray you, all people, and behold my sorrow. My virgins and my young men are gone into captivity. Coph. I called for my lovers, but they deceived me. My priests and my elders gave up the ghost in the city, while they sought their meat to relieve their souls. Res. See, O Lord, for I am in distress: my bowels are troubled; my heart is turned within me, for I have grievously rebelled. Abroad the sword bereaves, at home there is as it were death. Sin. They have heard that I sigh, and there is none to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my trouble; they are glad that thou hast done it. Thou wilt bring the day that thou hast called, and they shall be like unto me. Thau. Let all their wickedness come before thee; and do unto them as thou hast done unto me for all my transgressions. For my sighs are many, and my heart is faint.

Aleph. II. How has the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger! He has cast down from heaven to earth the glory of Israel, and remembered not his footstool in the day of his anger. Beth. The Lord has swallowed up all the habitations of Jacob, and has not pitied: he has thrown down in his wrath the strongholds of the daughter of Judah; he has brought them down to the ground; he has polluted the kingdom and its princes. Gymel. He has cut off in his fierce anger all the horn of Israel; he has drawn back his right hand from before the enemy, and he burned against Jacob like a flaming fire, which devours round about. Deleth. He has bent his bow like an enemy; he has stood with his right hand as an adversary, and slain all that were pleasant to the eye. In the tabernacle of the daughter of Zion he has poured out his fury like fire. He. The Lord has become like an enemy; he has swallowed up Israel. He has swallowed up all her palaces; he has destroyed his strongholds, and has increased in the daughter of Judah mourning and lamentation. Vau. And he has violently taken away his tabernacle, as if it were of a garden; he has destroyed his places of assembly. The Lord has caused the solemn feasts and sabbaths to be forgotten in Zion, and has despised in his fierce anger the king and the priest. Zay. The Lord has cast off his altar; he has abhorred his sanctuary; he has given up into the hand of the enemy the walls of her palaces; they have made a noise in the house of the Lord, as in the day of a solemn feast. Heth. The Lord has purposed to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion; he has stretched out a line, he has not withdrawn his hand from destroying; therefore he made the rampart and the wall to lament; they languished together. Theth. Her gates are sunk into the ground; he has destroyed and broken her bars; her king and her princes are among the nations. The law is no more; her prophets also find no

by a vision from the Lord. Joel. They have cast themselves to the ground; the elders of the daughter of Zion sit in silence; they have thrown dust on their heads; they have put on sackcloth; the virgins of Jerusalem have bowed their heads to the ground. Koph. My eyes are spent with weeping; my stomach is churned; my bile is poured out on the ground because of the destruction of the daughter of my people, because infants and babes faint in the streets of the city. Jod. They cry to their mothers, "Where is bread and wine?" as they faint like the wounded in the streets of the city, as their life is poured out on their mothers' bosom. Mem. What can I say for you, to what compare you, O daughter of Jerusalem? What can I liken to you, that I may comfort you, O virgin daughter of Zion? For vast as the sea is your ruin; who can heal you? Nun. Your prophets have seen for you false and deceptive visions; they have not exposed your iniquity to restore your fortunes, but have seen for you oracles that are false and misleading. Samech. All who pass along the way clap their hands at you; they hiss and wag their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem: "Is this the city that was called the perfection of beauty, the joy of all the earth?" Pe. All your enemies rail against you; they hiss, they gnash their teeth, they cry: "We have swallowed her!" Ayin. The Lord has done what he purposed; he has carried out his word, which he commanded long ago; he has thrown down without pity; he has made the enemy rejoice over you and exalted the might of your foes. Tsade. Their heart cried to the Lord. O wall of the daughter of Zion, let tears stream down like a torrent day and night! Give yourself no rest, your eyes no respite! Koph. Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the night watches! Pour out your heart like water before the presence of the Lord!

Lift your hands to him for the lives of your children, who faint for hunger at the head of every street. Resh. Look, O Lord, and see! With whom have you dealt thus? Should women eat the fruit of their womb, the children of their tender care? Should priest and prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord? Sin. In the streets lie the young and the old; my young women and my young men have fallen by the sword; you have killed them in the day of your anger, slaughtering without pity. Tav. You summoned as if to a festival day my terrors on every side, and on the day of the anger of the Lord no one escaped or survived; those whom I held and raised my enemy destroyed. Chapter 3. Aleph.

I am the man who has seen affliction under the rod of his wrath. Aleph. He has driven me and brought me into darkness without any light. Aleph. Surely against me he turns his hand again and again the whole day long. Beth. He has made my flesh and my skin waste away; he has broken my bones. Beth. He has besieged and enveloped me with bitterness and tribulation. Beth. He has made me dwell in darkness like the dead of long ago. Gimel. He has walled me about so that I cannot escape; he has made my chains heavy. Gimel. Though I call and cry for help, he shuts out my prayer. Gimel. He has blocked my ways with blocks of stone; he has made my paths crooked. Daleth. He is a bear lying in wait for me, a lion in hiding. Daleth. He turned aside my steps and tore me to pieces; he has made me desolate. Daleth. He bent his bow and set me as a target for his arrow. He. He drove into my kidneys the arrows of his quiver. He. I have become the laughingstock of all peoples, the object of their taunts all day long. He. He has filled me with bitterness; he has sated me with wormwood. Vav. He has made my teeth grind on gravel

Lamentations (Jeremiah)

He has fed me with ashes. Vau. My soul is cast off, I have forgotten good things. Vau. And I said, my end and my hope from the Lord is lost. Zain. Remember my poverty and transgression, the wormwood and the gall. Zain. I will remember and be mindful, and my soul shall languish within me. Zain. Thinking on these things in my heart, I will have hope. Heth. The mercies of the Lord that we are not consumed, because his compassions do not fail. Heth. They are new every morning: great is your faithfulness. Heth. The Lord is my portion, says my soul: therefore will I wait for him. Teth. The Lord is good to those who hope in him, to the soul that seeks him. Teth. It is good to wait with silence for the salvation of the Lord. Teth. It is good for a man when he has borne the yoke from his youth. Jod. He shall sit alone and be silent: because he has taken it up upon himself. Jod. He shall put his mouth in the dust: if so there may be hope. Jod. He shall give his cheek to him who strikes him: he shall be filled with reproaches. Caph. For the Lord will not cast off forever. Caph. For if he has cast off, he will also have mercy according to the multitude of his mercies. Caph. For he has not humbled from his heart: nor has he cast off the children of men. Lamed. To crush under his feet all the prisoners of the earth. Lamed. To turn aside the judgment of a man before the face of the Most High. Lamed. To subvert a man in his cause: the Lord has not approved. Mem. Who is he that said a thing should be done, when the Lord commanded it not? Mem. Shall not both evil and good proceed out of the mouth of the Most High? Mem. Why does a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins? Nun. Let us search and examine our ways, and let us return to the Lord. Nun. Let us lift up our hearts with our hands to God in the heavens. Nun. We have done wickedly and provoked you to wrath:

therefore you are inexorable. Samech. You have covered yourself with anger and pursued us: you have slain and shown no mercy. Samech. You have set a cloud before you, so that our prayer cannot pass through. Samech. You have made me an outcast and cast me off, and placed me in the midst of the people. Phe. All our enemies have opened their mouths against us. Phe. Fear and the snare have come upon us: desolation and destruction. Phe. My eye has poured out streams of water for the destruction of the daughter of my people. Ain. My eye is afflicted and did not cease: because there was no rest. Ain. Until the Lord looked down and saw from heaven. Ain. My eye has wasted my soul because of all the daughters of my city. Sade. They have hunted me like a bird, those who were my enemies without cause. Sade. My life has sunk into the pit, and they have laid a stone upon me. Sade. Waters flowed over my head: I said, I am cut off. Coph. I called upon your name, O Lord, out of the lowest pit. Coph. You heard my voice: hide not your ear from my sighing and my cry. Caph. You drew near on the day I called upon you: you said, fear not. Res. O Lord, you have pleaded the cause of my soul: you have redeemed my life. Res. O Lord, you have seen my wrong: judge my cause. Res. You have seen all their vengeance and all their devices against me. Sin. You have heard their reproach, O Lord, and all their devices against me. Sin. The lips of those who rose against me and their plots against me all day long. Sin. Behold their sitting down and their rising up: I am their song. Thau. You will render them a recompense, O Lord, according to the work of their hands. Thau. You will give them a shield of heart: your labor. Thau. You will pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of the Lord. Caph. Chapter 4. Aleph. How is the gold become dim, how is the finest color changed: they are scattered

Preface                                                    Baruch.

There was famine and tempest. The women of Zion were humiliated, and the virgins in the cities of Judah. The princes were hanged by their hands; the faces of the elders were not honored. The young men were abused shamefully, and the boys fell beneath the wood. The elders have ceased from the gate, the young men from their music. The joy of our heart has ceased; our choir is turned to mourning. The crown has fallen from our head; woe to us, for we have sinned. For this reason our heart is made sorrowful, and for these things our eyes are darkened. Because of Mount Zion, which is desolate, the foxes have walked upon it. But you, O Lord, remain forever; your throne from generation to generation. Why do you forget us forever, and forsake us for so long? Convert us, O Lord, to you, and we shall be converted; renew our days as from the beginning. But you have utterly rejected and been very wroth against us. Here ends the prayer of Jeremiah. Here begins the preface to the book of Baruch, written in the name of Jeremiah.

This book, which goes by the name of Baruch, is not found in the Hebrew canon, but only in the Vulgate edition; likewise the Epistle of Jeremiah. However, these things are written here for the knowledge of the reader, because they speak of Christ and of the last times. Here begins the Book of Baruch.

And these are the words of the book which Baruch, son of Nerias, son of Maasias, son of Sedecias, son of Sedei, son of Helcias, wrote in Babylon, in the fifth year, on the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans took Jerusalem and burned it with fire. And Baruch read the words of this book in the hearing of Jeconias, the son of Joachim, king of Judah, and in the hearing of all the people

who came to hear the book: in the hearing of the mighty, the sons of kings, and in the hearing of the elders, and in the hearing of all the people, from the least to the greatest, all those who dwelt in Babylon by the river Sud. And when they heard it, they wept and fasted and prayed before the Lord. And they collected money, each according to his means, and they sent it to Jerusalem, to Joachim the son of Helcias, the son of Salom, the priest, and to the priests, and to all who were found with him in Jerusalem, that they might receive back the vessels of the temple of the Lord which had been taken from the temple, to restore them to the land of Judah — on the tenth day of the month of Sivan — the silver vessels which Sedecias the son of Josias, king of Judah, had made, after Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon had taken Jechonias and the princes and the skilled men and the nobles of the land of Jerusalem captive, and brought them bound to Babylon. And they said: Behold, we send you money; buy with it burnt offerings and incense, and make oblations, and offer a sin offering at the altar of the Lord our God. And pray for the life of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, and for the life of Balthasar his son, that their days may be as the days of heaven above the earth; and that the Lord may give us strength and enlighten our eyes, that we may live under the shadow of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, and under the shadow of Balthasar his son, and that we may serve them many days, and find favor in their sight. And pray for us to the Lord our God, for we have sinned against the Lord our God, and his wrath has not turned away from us to this day. And you shall read this book which we have sent to you, to be proclaimed in the temple of the Lord on a solemn day and on a suitable occasion. And you shall say: To the Lord our God belongs justice, but to us the shame of our faces, as it is this day:

Baruch.

to all of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to our kings and our princes, to our priests and our prophets, and to our fathers. We have sinned before the Lord our God, and we have not believed, putting no trust in him; we were not obedient to him, and we did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God to walk in his commandments which he gave us. From the day when he led our fathers out of the land of Egypt until this day, we have been disobedient to the Lord our God, and scattered, turning away so as not to hear his voice. And many evils and curses clung to us, which the Lord commanded Moses his servant, who led our fathers out of the land of Egypt to give us a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is this day. And we did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God, according to all the words of the prophets whom he sent to us; and every one of us followed the inclination of his own wicked heart, to serve strange gods, and to do evil in the sight of the Lord our God. Chapter II.

Therefore the Lord our God has carried out the sentence he pronounced against us, and against our judges who governed Israel and Jerusalem, and against our kings and our princes, and against all Israel and Judah; that the Lord would bring upon us great disasters such as have never happened under heaven, such as happened in Jerusalem according to what is written in the law of Moses, that a man should eat the flesh of his own son and the flesh of his own daughter. And he has given them into the hand of all the kingdoms surrounding us, to be a reproach and a desolation among all the peoples where the Lord has scattered us. We have been brought low and not high, because we have sinned against the Lord our God, by not listening to his voice. To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us and to our fathers belongs shame of face, as it is this day.

For the Lord has pronounced all these evils against us that have come upon us; yet we have not entreated the favor of the Lord by turning away each one from the thoughts of his wicked heart. The Lord has kept the disaster ready and has brought it upon us, for the Lord is righteous in all his works that he has commanded us; yet we have not obeyed his voice, to walk in the commandments of the Lord that he set before us.

And now, O Lord God of Israel, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and with signs and wonders and with great power and an outstretched arm, and have made yourself a name, as it is this day: we have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly, O Lord our God, against all your ordinances. Let your anger turn away from us, for we are left, few in number, among the nations where you have scattered us. Hear, O Lord, our prayers and our supplications, and for your own sake deliver us, and grant us favor in the sight of those who have carried us into exile; so that all the earth may know that you are the Lord our God, for Israel and his descendants are called by your name. O Lord, look down from your holy dwelling and consider us; incline your ear, O Lord, and hear; open your eyes, O Lord, and see; for the dead who are in Hades, whose spirits have been taken from their bodies, will not give glory or justice to the Lord; but the person who is deeply grieved, who walks bowed and feeble, with failing eyes and a famished soul, will give you glory and righteousness, O Lord. For we do not present our plea before you, O Lord our God, on the ground of the righteousness of our fathers, but because you have sent out your wrath and your anger upon us, as

Baruch.

So that you may know where long life and strength are, where the light of the eyes and peace are. Who has found his place? And who has entered into his treasuries? Where are the princes of the nations, and those who rule over the beasts that are upon the earth? Those who sport among the birds of the air, who hoard silver and gold in which men trust, and there is no end to their acquiring? Those who work silver and are anxious about it, yet their works are past finding out. They have been cut off and have gone down to the underworld, and others have risen up in their place. Younger men have seen the light, have dwelt upon the earth. But the way of knowledge they have not known, nor have they understood her paths, nor have their children received her. She is far from their face. She has not been heard of in Canaan, nor has she been seen in Teman. The sons of Agar also who seek for wisdom upon the earth, the merchants of Meran and Teman, and the storytellers and the seekers of understanding: have not known the way of wisdom, nor remembered her paths. O Israel, how great is the house of God, and how vast the place of his possession! It is great and has no end, it is high and immense. There were the giants famous from the beginning, who were of great stature and knew war. The Lord did not choose them, nor did they find the way of knowledge; therefore they perished. And because they had not wisdom, they perished through their own foolishness. Who has gone up into heaven and taken her, and brought her down from the clouds? Who has gone over the sea and found her, and brought her above fine gold? There is none that is able to know her ways, nor any that can search out her paths. But he who knows all things knows her, and has found her out with his understanding: he who prepared the earth for evermore, and filled it with cattle and four-footed beasts; who sends forth the light and it goes, and called it, and it obeyed him with trembling. And the stars gave light in their watches and were glad. He called them and they said, Here we are. And they shone with cheerfulness to him that made them. This is our God, and there shall be no other compared to him. He found out all the way of knowledge, and gave it to Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved. Afterwards he was seen upon the earth and conversed with men.

This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endures forever. All those who keep it shall attain life; but those who forsake it shall die. Turn, O Jacob, and take hold of it; walk toward its brightness, in the light thereof. Give not your glory to another, nor your dignity to a foreign nation. Blessed are we, O Israel, for the things that are pleasing to God are made known to us. Be of good comfort, O people of God, the memorial of Israel. You have been sold to the nations, not for your destruction; but because you provoked God to wrath, you were delivered to your adversaries. For you have provoked him who made you, the eternal God, offering sacrifice to demons and not to God. You have forgotten God who brought you up, and you have grieved Jerusalem your nurse. For she saw the wrath of God coming upon you, and she said: Hear, O you neighbors of Zion, for God has brought upon me great mourning. For I have seen the captivity of my people, my sons and daughters, which the Eternal has brought upon them. I nourished them with joy, but I let them go with weeping and mourning. Let no one rejoice over me, a widow and desolate; I am left desolate by many because of the sins of my children, for they have turned away from the law of God. They have not known his righteousness, nor walked in the ways of his commandments.

Baruch.

of God; nor have they walked in the paths of his truth and justice. Let the borders of Zion come, and remember the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Eternal brought upon them. For he brought against them a nation from afar, a wicked nation of a foreign tongue, who had no reverence for the elderly, nor showed pity to the children. And they led away the beloved widows, and left the solitary daughters desolate. What can I do to help you? For he who brought these evils upon you will deliver you from the hand of your enemies. Go, my children, go forward: I am left alone and desolate. I have put off the garment of peace, and have clothed myself in sackcloth of supplication, and I will cry to the Most High in my days. Be of good courage, my children: cry to God, and he will deliver you from the power of the princes who are your enemies. For I have hoped in the Eternal for your salvation; and joy has come to me from the Holy One, because of the mercy which shall soon come to you from your eternal Savior. For I sent you out with mourning and weeping: but God will bring you back to me with joy and gladness forever. For as the neighbors of Zion saw your captivity from God, so also shall they soon see your salvation from God, which shall come upon you with great honor and eternal splendor. My children, endure patiently the wrath that has come upon you. For your enemy has pursued you, but soon you will see his destruction and will tread upon his neck. My beloved walked on rough roads, led away like a flock carried off by enemies. Be of good courage, my children, and cry to God. For he who led you away will also remember you. And just as it was your intention to go astray from God, so when you return tenfold, you shall seek him. For he who brought evils upon you will again

bring upon you everlasting joy with your salvation. Take courage, O Jerusalem: for he who called you by name will comfort you. The wicked who afflicted you will perish, and those who rejoiced at your ruin will be punished. The cities that enslaved your children will be punished, and so will she who received your sons. For as she rejoiced at your ruin and was glad at your fall, so shall she grieve at her own desolation. And the exultation of her multitude shall be cut off, and her rejoicing shall be turned to mourning. For fire shall come upon her from the Eternal for many days, and she shall be inhabited by demons for a long time. Look around, O Jerusalem, toward the east, and see the joy that comes to you from God. Chapter ii.

Behold, your children come whom you sent away scattered; they come gathered together from the east to the west, at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the honor of God. O Jerusalem, put off your garment of mourning and affliction, and clothe yourself with the beauty and honor that comes to you from God, and with his everlasting glory. God will clothe you with the double garment of justice, and will place on your head the crown of eternal honor. For God will show your splendor to every nation under heaven. For your name shall be called by God forever: the peace of justice and the honor of piety. Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look toward the east, and see your children gathered from the rising to the setting sun, at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of God. For they went out from you on foot, led by enemies; but God will bring them back to you carried in honor as children of a kingdom. For God has ordained to humble every high mountain and the everlasting rocks, and to fill the valleys to make them level with the ground, so that Israel may walk safely in the glory of God. And the woods

Baruch.

Every tree of the pleasantness of Israel, by the command of God. For God will bring him with joy in the light of his majesty: with mercy and justice that are in him. Here follows the letter of the same epistle which Jeremiah sent to those led captive into Babylon by the king of the Babylonians: to announce to them what had been commanded him by God.

On account of the sins which you have sinned before God, you will be led captive into Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians. Therefore entering into Babylon you will be there for many years and for a long time, even to seven generations: but after this I will bring you out from there in peace. Now you will see in Babylon gods of gold and silver and stone and wood, carried upon shoulders: paraded to cause fear among the nations. Beware therefore lest you become like them in following foreign practices and be seized by fear of them. When you see the crowd before and behind, worshipping, say in your hearts: You alone are to be adored, Lord. For my angel is with you. He himself will require your souls. For their tongue is polished by the craftsman, and it is overlaid with gold and silver, yet it is false and cannot speak. And as for a young woman who loves ornaments: so are they made with gold. They certainly have golden crowns upon their heads; but the priests take away the gold and silver from them and spend it on themselves. They also give some of it to the prostitutes; and with that which they have received from the prostitutes, they adorn their gods. The gods cannot free themselves from rust and corruption. When they are dressed in purple garments, they wipe their faces clean of the house dust which is very plentiful upon them. One holds a scepter like a man who judges a region:

but he does not kill one who sins against him. He also has a sword and an axe in his hand, but he cannot save himself from war or from robbers. Therefore let it be known to you: that they are not gods. Do not therefore revere them. Just as a broken vessel of a man becomes useless: such also are their gods. When they are set up in a house, their eyes are full of dust from those who come in. And just as the gates are shut about him who offended the king: or just as a dead man being brought to burial, so the priests secure the doors with locks and bars, lest they be plundered by robbers. They light candles for them: and many indeed, of which they cannot see any. They are like beams within the house. Their hearts, they say, are eaten by serpents that creep from the earth; and they devour their bodies and clothing, and they feel it not. Their faces are blackened with smoke that is in the house. Upon their bodies and upon their heads fly owls and swallows and birds also, and cats likewise. Therefore know that they are not gods. Do not therefore fear them. The gold also which they have for beauty, unless someone wipes off the rust, they will not shine. Even when they were being cast they did not feel it: they are bought at any price, in whom there is no spirit. Having no feet they are carried upon shoulders: showing their own worthlessness to men. Let those also who worship them be confounded. Therefore if they fall to the ground by themselves, they cannot rise: and if one sets them upright they cannot stand by themselves; but they will be placed like dead men. The offerings made to them, their priests sell and misuse: and likewise their wives also, not giving any share to the sick or the poor. Women in childbed and menstruating touch their sacrifices. Knowing therefore from these things that they are not gods: do not fear them.

Prologue. Ezekiel.

And the spirit moves through every region: and the clouds, when commanded by God, travel through the entire world, fulfilling what they are commanded. Fire sent from above to consume mountains and forests does what is appointed to it. None of these things are like the Israelites or like the powers of their God. Therefore we should not suppose or say that those idols are gods: for they cannot judge, nor help mankind. Knowing therefore that they are not gods, do not fear them. They neither curse kings nor bless them. They show no wonders in the heavens: they shine not like the sun, nor give light like the moon. The beasts are better than they, for the beasts can flee to shelter and help themselves. In no way therefore is it clear to us that they are gods: therefore do not fear them. As in a cucumber garden a scarecrow guards nothing, so are the wooden and silver and gilded gods of the nations. Similarly, like a dead body thrown into the darkness, are those wooden and gilded and silvered gods of the nations. From purple and crimson they cannot protect themselves: you may know therefore that they are not gods. They will even be devoured by worms in the end, and will be a reproach in the land. Better is a just man who has no idols: for he shall be far from reproach. Here ends the book of Baruch, and begins the prologue to the prophet Ezekiel.

The prophet Ezekiel was taken captive to Babylon with King Jehoiachin of Judah, and there he prophesied to those who had been taken captive with him, who had given themselves up beyond what Jeremiah's prophecies required, and who still expected to see the city of Jerusalem standing, which Jeremiah had foretold would fall.

In the thirtieth year of his age and the fifth year of captivity, he turned again to speak to the captives. And although he came later than Jeremiah, Jeremiah prophesied in Judea while he prophesied in Chaldea. His style is neither especially polished nor entirely rustic, but is a middle course between both. He himself was a priest, as was Jeremiah: the beginning and end of his book are wrapped in greater obscurity. But the common edition of his text does not differ greatly from the Hebrew. I am quite puzzled therefore as to why, if we have the same translators for all the books, they should have rendered some the same and others differently. Read therefore this book also according to our translation: for since it is written in cola and comata it gives a clearer meaning to the reader. But if some friends have urged me to address these matters, let no one compel them to write. But I fear lest what is more significantly said in Greek happen to them -- that they be called "sagolidori," which means "eaters of filth." Here ends the prologue. Here begins the prophet Ezekiel. Chapter 1.

And it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth day of the month, as I was among the captives by the river Chebar, that the heavens were opened and I saw visions of God. On the fifth day of the month, which was the fifth year of the captivity of King Jehoiachin, the word of the Lord came to Ezekiel the son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans, by the river Chebar. And the hand of the Lord was there upon him. And I looked, and behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud with fire enfolding itself. And brightness was around it: and out of the midst of the fire, as it were the appearance of electrum -- that is, out of the midst of the fire. And in the midst of it

Ezekiel.

The likeness of the four living creatures, and this was their appearance. They had the likeness of a man. Each one had four faces, and each one had four wings. Their feet were straight feet; and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot: and they sparkled like the color of burnished bronze. And they had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides; and they four had their faces and their wings. Their wings were joined one to another; they did not turn as they went; each one went straight forward. As for the likeness of their faces, each had the face of a man, and the face of a lion on the right side, and the face of an ox on the left side; and each of the four had the face of an eagle above. Their faces and their wings were stretched upward. Two wings of every one were joined one to another, and two covered their bodies. And every one went straight forward. Where the spirit was to go, they went; and they did not turn as they went. As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, and like the appearance of lamps. The fire went up and down among the living creatures; and the fire was bright, and out of the fire went forth lightning. And the living creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning. Now as I beheld the living creatures, behold one wheel upon the earth beside the living creatures, with his four faces. The appearance of the wheels and their work was like unto the color of a beryl: and they four had one likeness: and their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel. When they went, they went upon their four sides: and they turned not when they went. As for their rings, they were so high that they were dreadful; and their rings were full of eyes round about them four. And when the living creatures went, the wheels went by them:

and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up. Wherever the spirit was to go, they went, and the wheels were lifted up alongside them, for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels. When those went, these went; and when those stood, these stood; and when those were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up alongside them: for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels. And the likeness of the firmament upon the heads of the living creatures was as the color of the terrible crystal, stretched forth over their heads above. And under the firmament their wings were straight, the one toward the other. Each one had two, which covered on this side, and every one had two, which covered on that side, their bodies. And I heard the sound of their wings, like the sound of great waters, as the voice of the Almighty. When they went, it was the sound of a tumult, like the sound of an army. When they stood, they let down their wings. And when there was a voice from the firmament that was over their heads, they stood, and let down their wings. And above the firmament that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, in appearance like a sapphire stone: and upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as the appearance of a man above upon it. And I saw as the color of amber, as the appearance of fire round about within it, from the appearance of his loins even upward, and from the appearance of his loins even downward, I saw as it were the appearance of fire, and it had brightness round about. As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness round about. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord.

Chapter 2

And I saw and fell upon my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke. And he said to me: Son of man, stand upon your feet, and I will speak to you. And the spirit entered into me after he spoke to me, and he set me upon my feet. And I heard him speaking to me and saying: Son of man, I send you to the children of Israel—

Ezekiel.

to the apostate nations that have turned away from me. Their fathers broke my covenant up to this day: and the children are hard of face and of stubborn heart, to whom I send you. And you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: whether they will hear or whether they will forbear, for they are a rebellious house, yet they shall know that a prophet has been among them. And you, son of man, do not fear them, nor their words: for rebels and thorns are with you, and you dwell among scorpions. Do not fear their words, nor be dismayed at their looks, for they are a rebellious house. You shall speak my words to them, whether they hear or whether they forbear, for they are rebellious. But you, son of man, hear what I say to you: be not rebellious like that rebellious house. Open your mouth and eat what I give you. And I looked, and a hand was stretched out to me, and in it was a written scroll: and he spread it before me, and it was written within and without: and there were written in it lamentations and mourning and woe. Chapter 3.

And he said to me: Son of man, eat what you find here. Eat this scroll, and go speak to the house of Israel. So I opened my mouth, and he caused me to eat that scroll. And he said to me: Son of man, your belly shall eat and your bowels shall be filled with this scroll that I give you. And I ate it, and it was in my mouth as sweet as honey. And he said to me: Son of man, go to the house of Israel and speak my words to them. For you are not sent to a people of a strange speech and of a hard language, but to the house of Israel: not to many peoples of strange speech and hard language, whose words you cannot understand. Surely, if I sent you to them, they would listen to you. But the house of Israel will not listen to you, for they will not listen to me.

For all the house of Israel are of stubborn brow and hard heart. Behold, I have made your face strong against their faces, and your forehead strong against their foreheads: like adamant, harder than flint have I made your forehead. Do not fear them, nor be dismayed at their looks, for they are a rebellious house. And he said to me: Son of man, all my words that I shall speak to you receive in your heart and hear with your ears: and go to those of the captivity, to the children of your people, and speak to them and say to them: Thus says the Lord God, whether they will hear or forbear. Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the voice of a great rushing: Blessed be the glory of the Lord from his place: and the voice of the wings of the living creatures touching one another, and the voice of the wheels alongside them, and the voice of a great rushing. So the Spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went in bitterness, in the heat of my spirit, but the hand of the Lord was strong upon me. And I came to the captives at Tel Abib, who dwelt by the river of Chebar, and I sat there where they sat, and I remained there seven days, overwhelmed among them. And at the end of seven days, the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel: therefore hear the word from my mouth and warn them from me. If I say to the wicked, You shall surely die, and you give him no warning, nor speak to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life, the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at your hand. Yet if you warn the wicked, and he does not turn from his wickedness nor from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquity: but you will have saved your life. But if a righteous man turns away from

Ezekiel.

And you, son of man, take for yourself a sharp sword, use it as a barber's razor and pass it over your head and your beard; then take scales for weighing and divide the hair. A third part you shall burn with fire in the midst of the city, when the days of the siege are completed; and you shall take a third part and strike it with the sword all around the city; and a third part you shall scatter to the wind, and I will draw out a sword after them. And you shall take from there a small number and bind them in the hem of your garment; and from these again you shall take some, throw them into the midst of the fire, and burn them in the fire. From there a fire will spread to all the house of Israel. Thus says the Lord God: This is Jerusalem. I have set her in the midst of the nations, and countries are all around her. But she has rebelled against my ordinances in doing wickedness more than the nations, and against my statutes more than the countries that are all around her. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have been more turbulent than the nations that are all around you, and have not walked in my statutes nor kept my judgments, nor even done according to the judgments of the nations that are all around you: therefore thus says the Lord God. Behold, I, even I, am against you, and I myself will execute judgments in your midst in the sight of the nations; and I will do among you what I have never done, and the like of which I will never do again, because of all your abominations. Therefore fathers shall eat their sons in your midst, and sons shall eat their fathers; and I will execute judgments on you, and scatter to every wind all who remain of you. Therefore, as I live, says the Lord God: Surely, because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your detestable things and with all your abominations, I will also diminish you; my eye will not spare, and I will have no pity.

A third part of you shall die of plague and be consumed with famine in your midst; a third part shall fall by the sword all around you; and a third part I will scatter to every wind, and I will draw a sword after them. Thus my anger shall be spent and I will cause my fury to rest upon them, and I will be satisfied; and they shall know that I, the Lord, have spoken in my zeal, when I have spent my fury upon them. Moreover I will make you a waste and a reproach among the nations that are all around you, in the sight of all who pass by. So it shall be a reproach, a taunt, a warning, and an astonishment to the nations that are all around you, when I execute judgments upon you in anger and in fury and in furious rebukes. I, the Lord, have spoken: when I send against you the terrible deadly arrows of famine which I will send to destroy you; and I will increase the famine upon you and cut off your supply of bread. So I will send against you famine and wild beasts, and they will bereave you. And plague and blood shall pass through you, and I will bring a sword upon you. I the Lord have spoken. Chapter 6.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them, and say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God. Thus says the Lord God to the mountains, to the hills, to the ravines, and to the valleys: Behold, I will bring a sword upon you, and I will destroy your high places. Your altars shall be demolished and your incense altars shall be broken; and I will throw down your slain before your idols. And I will lay the dead bodies of the people of Israel before their idols; and I will scatter your bones around your altars throughout all your settlements. The cities shall be laid waste and the high places shall be ruined and made desolate, and your altars will be ruined and

Ezekiel.

They shall be constrained, and their idols shall cease, and their shrines shall be destroyed, and their works shall be blotted out, and those slain shall fall in their midst, and you shall know that I am the Lord. And I will leave among you those who escape the sword among the nations, when I shall scatter you through the countries; and those of you who are delivered shall remember me among the nations where they are carried captive, because I was broken with their whorish heart which has departed from me, and with their eyes which went astray after their idols; and they shall loathe themselves for the evils which they have committed in all their abominations; and they shall know that I am the Lord, and that I have not said in vain that I would do this evil to them. Thus says the Lord God: Strike with your hand and stamp with your foot, and say, Alas, for all the evil abominations of the house of Israel, because they shall fall by sword, by famine, and by pestilence. He that is far off shall die of the pestilence, and he that is near shall fall by the sword, and he that remains and is besieged shall die by the famine. Thus will I accomplish my fury upon them, and you shall know that I am the Lord, when their slain men shall be among their idols round about their altars, upon every high hill, upon all the tops of the mountains, and under every green tree, and under every thick oak, wherever they offered sweet savor to all their idols. And I will stretch out my hand upon them, and make the land desolate and waste from the desert to Diblath in all their habitations, and they shall know that I am the Lord. Chapter 7.

Moreover the word of the Lord came to me, saying: And you, son of man, thus says the Lord God to the land of Israel: An end has come, the end has come upon the four corners of the land. Now the end is upon you, and I will send my anger upon you, and I will judge you according to your ways, and I will lay upon you all your abominations. And my eye shall not spare you, neither will I have pity, but I will lay your ways upon you,

and your abominations shall be in your midst, and you shall know that I am the Lord. Thus says the Lord God: Disaster after disaster! Behold, it comes. An end has come, the end has come; it has awakened against you. Behold, it comes. Doom has come upon you, O inhabitant of the land. The time has come, the day is near, a day of tumult, and not of rejoicing upon the mountains. Now I will shortly pour out my fury upon you and accomplish my anger upon you, and I will judge you according to your ways and will lay upon you all your abominations. And my eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity; I will lay your ways upon you, and your abominations shall be in your midst, and you shall know that I am the Lord who strikes. Behold the day! Behold, it has come. Doom has gone out, the rod has blossomed, pride has budded, violence has risen up into a rod of wickedness. None of them shall remain, none of their multitude, none of their wealth; neither shall there be wailing for them. The time has come, the day draws near. Let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn, for wrath is upon all their multitude. For the seller shall not return to what has been sold, even though their life is still among the living. For the vision concerns the whole multitude, and it shall not be turned back; and no one shall strengthen himself in the iniquity of his life. Blow the trumpet, let everything be prepared, yet no one goes to battle. For my wrath is upon all their multitude. The sword is outside, and pestilence and famine are within. He that is in the field shall die by the sword, and he that is in the city shall be devoured by famine and pestilence, and those who escape shall flee to the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, each for his iniquity. All hands shall be feeble, and all knees shall flow with water. They shall gird themselves with sackcloth, and horror shall cover them, and shame shall be upon every face, and baldness upon all their heads. They shall cast their silver into the streets, and their gold shall be as filth. Their silver

Ezekiel

These were the elders. And he brought me into the inner court of the house of the Lord. And behold, at the door of the temple of the Lord, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five men with their backs to the temple of the Lord and their faces toward the east, and they were worshipping toward the rising sun. And he said to me: "Surely you have seen, son of man. Is it a light thing for the house of Judah to commit the abominations which they have committed here? For they have filled the land with violence and have provoked me to anger. And behold, they put the branch to their nose. Therefore I will also act in fury: my eye shall not spare, nor will I have pity; and though they cry in my ears with a loud voice, I will not hear them." Chapter [9].

And he cried in my ears with a loud voice, saying: "The punishment of the city has drawn near, and every man has his weapon of destruction in his hand. And behold, six men came from the way of the upper gate which faces north, each with his weapon of slaughter in his hand. One man among them was clothed in linen, with a writer's inkhorn at his side. And they came in and stood beside the bronze altar. And the glory of the Lord of Israel had gone up from the cherub, on which it rested, to the threshold of the house. And he called to the man clothed in linen, who had the writer's inkhorn at his side. And the Lord said to him: 'Pass through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and groan over all the abominations that are committed in it.' And to the others he said in my hearing: 'Pass through the city after him and strike. Let not your eye spare, and have no pity. Kill old men, young men, virgins, little children, and women, to utter destruction: but do not touch any man on whom is the mark; and begin at my sanctuary.' So they began with the elders who were before the house. And he said to them: 'Defile the house and fill the courts with the slain. Go out.' And they went out and struck down those in the city. And when they had finished, I was left alone, and I fell upon my face and cried out, saying: 'Ah, Lord God! Will you destroy all the remnant of Israel in pouring out your fury upon Jerusalem?' And he said to me: 'The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great: the land is full of blood, and the city full of perversity. For they say: The Lord has forsaken the land, and the Lord does not see. As for me, my eye shall not spare, nor will I have pity: I will bring their deeds upon their heads.'" Chapter 10.

And I looked, and behold, in the firmament that was over the head of the cherubim there appeared above them something like a sapphire stone, in appearance resembling a throne. And he said to the man clothed in linen: "Go in among the whirling wheels under the cherubim, and fill your hands with burning coals from between the cherubim, and scatter them over the city." And he went in before my eyes. Now the cherubim were standing on the south side of the house when the man went in, and a cloud filled the inner court. And the glory of the Lord went up from the cherub to the threshold of the house, and the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was filled with the brightness of the glory of the Lord. And the sound of the wings of the cherubim was heard as far as the outer court, like the voice of God Almighty when he speaks. And when he had commanded the man clothed in linen, saying: "Take fire from between the wheels, from between the cherubim," he went in and stood beside a wheel. And he stretched out

Ezekiel.

a hand from among the cherubim toward the fire that was between the cherubim, and took some and put it into the hands of the one clothed in linen, who took it and went out. And there appeared in the cherubim the form of a human hand under their wings. And I looked, and behold, four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside one cherub and another wheel beside another cherub; and the appearance of the wheels was like the gleam of a beryl stone. And as for their appearance, the four had the same likeness, as if a wheel were within a wheel.
