When they went, they went in any of their four directions without turning as they went, but followed in the direction the head faced without turning as they went. And their whole body, their backs, their hands, their wings, and the wheels were full of eyes all around — the four wheels. As for the wheels, they were called in my hearing, the whirling wheels. Each one had four faces: the first face was the face of a cherub, the second face was a human face, the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle. Then the cherubim rose up — this was the living being I saw by the river Chebar. When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved beside them; and when the cherubim lifted their wings to rise from the ground, the wheels would not turn from beside them. When the cherubim stood still, the wheels stood still, and when they rose up, the wheels rose up with them, for the spirit of the living beings was in them. Then the glory of the Lord departed from the threshold of the temple and stood over the cherubim. While I watched, the cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the earth, and the wheels rose with them. They stood at the entrance of the east gate of the Lord's house, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them. These were the living beings I had seen beneath the God of Israel by the river Chebar; and I knew that they were cherubim. Each one had four faces and four wings, with the likeness of human hands under their wings. Their faces looked like the faces I had seen by the river Chebar. Each one moved straight ahead.

Chapter 11.

Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the east gate of the Lord's house, which faces east. And there at the entrance of the gate were twenty-five men; among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, leaders of the people. The Lord said to me: "Son of man, these are the men who are plotting evil and giving wicked counsel in this city. They say, 'Haven't the houses just been rebuilt? This city is the cooking pot, and we are the meat.' Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man." Then the Spirit of the Lord came upon me, and he told me to speak. He said: "This is what the Lord says: That is what you have been saying, O house of Israel, but I know what is going through your mind. You have killed many people in this city and filled its streets with the dead. Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord says: The bodies you have thrown there are the meat, and this city is the pot, but I will drive you out of it. You fear the sword, so I will bring a sword against you, declares the Sovereign Lord. I will drive you out of the city and deliver you into the hands of foreigners, and I will execute judgment on you. You will fall by the sword, and I will execute judgment on you at the borders of Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord. This city will not be a pot for you, nor will you be the meat inside it; I will execute judgment on you at the borders of Israel. And you will know that I am the Lord, for you have not followed my decrees or kept my laws but have conformed to the standards of the nations around you." Now while I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. Then I fell facedown and cried out in a loud voice, "Alas, Sovereign Lord!"

Ezekiel.

He lived — Prophets of Israel who prophesied toward Jerusalem and who saw visions of peace for her, when there is no peace, says the Lord God. And you, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy out of their own hearts, and prophesy against them. Say: Thus says the Lord God. Woe to those who sew pillows under every elbow and make veils for the heads of persons of every stature, to hunt souls. When they caught souls of my people, they kept those souls alive, and they profaned me among my people for handfuls of barley and pieces of bread, to kill souls that should not die and to keep alive souls that should not live, by lying to my people who listen to lies. Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against your pillows with which you hunt souls, and I will tear them from your arms, and I will let the souls go, even the souls that you hunt to make them fly. I will also tear off your veils and deliver my people out of your hand, and they shall be no more in your hand as prey, and you shall know that I am the Lord. Because with lies you have grieved the heart of the righteous, whom I have not made sad, and strengthened the hands of the wicked, so that he would not turn from his wicked way and live: therefore you shall see no more false visions, and you shall divine no more divinations, and I will deliver my people out of your hand, and you shall know that I am the Lord.

Then came certain of the elders of Israel to me and sat before me. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, these men have set up their idols in their heart and put the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face. Should I be at all inquired of by them? Therefore speak to them and say to them: Thus says the Lord God. Every man of the house of Israel who sets up his idols in his heart and puts the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and comes to the prophet: I the Lord will answer him who comes according to the multitude of his idols, that I may take the house of Israel in their own heart, because they are all estranged from me through their idols. Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God. Repent and turn yourselves from your idols, and turn away your faces from all your abominations. For every man of the house of Israel, or of the strangers that sojourn in Israel, who separates himself from me and sets up his idols in his heart and puts the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and comes to a prophet to inquire of me: I the Lord will answer him myself. And I will set my face against that man and will make him a sign and a proverb, and I will cut him off from the midst of my people, and you shall know that I am the Lord. And if the prophet be deceived when he has spoken a thing, I the Lord have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand upon him and will destroy him from the midst of my people Israel, and they shall bear the punishment of their iniquity. The punishment of the prophet shall be even as the punishment of him that seeks unto him, that the house of Israel may no more go astray from me, neither be polluted any more with all their transgressions: but that they may be my people and I may be their God, says the Lord of hosts. The word of the Lord came again to me, saying: Son of man, when a land sins against me by trespassing grievously, then will I stretch out my hand upon it and will break the staff of bread thereof and will send famine upon it and will cut off man and beast from it. Though these three men — Noah, Daniel, and Job — were in it, they would by their righteousness deliver only their own souls, says the Lord of hosts. If I cause evil beasts to pass through the land and they ravage it so that it is desolate, so that no man may pass through because of the beasts...

Ezekiel

I adorned you with ornaments. I put bracelets on your arms, and a necklace around your neck, and a ring on your nose, and earrings in your ears, and a beautiful crown on your head. You were adorned with gold and silver, and clothed in fine linen and silk and embroidered cloth. You ate the finest flour, honey, and oil, and you grew exceedingly beautiful. You became a queen, and your fame spread among the nations because of your beauty, for it was perfect through the splendor I had bestowed upon you, says the Lord God.
But you trusted in your beauty and used your fame to become a prostitute, and you lavished your favors on every passerby. You took some of your garments and made for yourself high places adorned with various colors, and you played the harlot upon them, as has never happened nor shall ever come to pass. You also took the beautiful jewelry I had given you, of my gold and my silver, and made for yourself male images, and played the harlot with them. You took your embroidered garments and covered them with them. And you set before them my oil and my incense, and my bread which I had given you — the finest flour, oil, and honey with which I nourished you — and offered it before them as a pleasing aroma. And it came to pass, says the Lord God, that you took your sons and your daughters whom you had borne to me, and sacrificed them to be devoured. Was your harlotry a small thing, that you slaughtered my children and delivered them up? And after all your abominations and harlotries you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, and were wallowing in your blood.
And it came to pass after all your wickedness — woe, woe to you, says the Lord God — that you built yourself a brothel and made yourself a public place in every street. At the head of every road you built your sign of prostitution, and you made your beauty an abomination.

You spread your legs to everyone who passed by and multiplied your harlotries. You also played the harlot with the Egyptians, your neighbors, great of flesh, and multiplied your harlotry to provoke me to anger. Behold, I will stretch out my hand against you, and take away your allotted portion. I will deliver you to those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who are ashamed of your lewd behavior. You also played the harlot with the Assyrians, because you were still not satisfied. Indeed, you multiplied your harlotry even in the land of Canaan with the Chaldeans, and yet you were still not satisfied. How can I make your heart clean, says the Lord God, when you do all these things, the deeds of a brazen prostitute? You built your brothel at the head of every road, and made your place of licentiousness in every street. Yet you were not like a prostitute who increases her price; rather you were like an adulterous wife who receives strangers instead of her husband. To all prostitutes, gifts are given; but you gave your gifts to all your lovers, and bribed them to come to you from every side to commit harlotry with you. Thus in your harlotry you were the opposite of other women, for no one solicited you; and in that you gave payment, and no payment was given to you, you are the very opposite. Therefore, O harlot, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God: Because your shame has been poured out, and your nakedness uncovered in your harlotries with your lovers, and with all your abominable idols, and in the blood of your children which you gave to them; behold, I will gather all your lovers to whom you were pleasing, and all those you loved, with all those you hated. I will gather them against you from every side, and I will uncover your nakedness before them.

Ezekiel.

before them. And they shall see all your shame; and I will judge you with the judgments of adulteresses and of those who shed blood. And I will give you into their hands in blood and fury and jealousy. And they shall destroy your brothel and pull down your high places. And they shall strip you of your garments and take away your jewels. And they shall leave you naked and full of shame; and they shall bring a multitude against you. And they shall stone you with stones and thrust you through with their swords. And they shall burn your houses with fire and execute judgments upon you in the sight of many women. And you shall cease from playing the harlot, and shall give no more hire. And my fury toward you shall rest, and my jealousy shall depart from you. I will be quiet and no longer angry, because you have not remembered the days of your youth, but have provoked me in all these things. Therefore I also have brought your ways upon your own head, says the Lord God; and you shall not commit this lewdness above all your abominations. Behold, everyone who uses proverbs shall use this proverb against you: As is the mother, so is her daughter. You are the daughter of your mother, who despised her husband and her children; and you are the sister of your sisters, who despised their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite. And your elder sister is Samaria, she and her daughters who dwell at your left hand. And your younger sister, who dwells at your right hand, is Sodom and her daughters. Yet you have not walked in their ways nor done according to their abominations; but, as if that were too little, you were more corrupt than they in all your ways. As I live, says the Lord God, Sodom your sister, she and her daughters, have not done as you and your daughters have done. Behold, this was the iniquity of your sister Sodom: pride, fullness of bread and abundance of idleness was in her and in her daughters; neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.

And they were haughty and committed abomination before me; therefore I took them away as I saw fit. Neither has Samaria committed half of your sins; but you have multiplied your abominations more than they, and have justified your sisters by all your abominations which you have done. You therefore bear your own shame, for you have judged your sisters; through your sins that you have committed more abominable than they, they are more righteous than you. Yes, be also confounded and bear your shame, in that you have justified your sisters. And I will bring again their captivity, the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and the captivity of Samaria and her daughters, and the captivity of your captives in the midst of them; that you may bear your own shame and may be confounded in all that you have done, in that you are a comfort to them. And your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, shall return to their former estate, and Samaria and her daughters shall return to their former estate, and you and your daughters shall return to your former estate. For your sister Sodom was not mentioned by your mouth in the day of your pride, before your wickedness was uncovered, as at the time of the reproach of the daughters of Syria and all that are round about her, the daughters of the Philistines who despise you round about. You have borne your lewdness and your abominations, says the Lord. For thus says the Lord God: I will deal with you as you have done, who have despised the oath in breaking the covenant. Nevertheless I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish with you an everlasting covenant. And you shall remember your ways and be ashamed, when you shall receive your sisters, your elder and your younger; and I will give them to you for daughters, but not by your covenant. And I will establish my covenant with you, and you shall know that I am the Lord; that you may remember and be confounded, and never open your mouth any more because of your shame, when I am reconciled to you

Ezekiel. Chapter 17.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, put forth a riddle and speak a parable to the house of Israel, and say: Thus says the Lord God. A great eagle, with great wings, long-limbed, full of feathers and of varied plumage, came to Lebanon, and took the top of the cedar. He plucked off the topmost of the young twigs thereof, and carried it into the land of Canaan: he set it in a city of merchants. He also took of the seed of the land, and planted it in a fruitful field; he placed it beside many waters, and set it as a willow tree. And it grew, and became a spreading vine of low stature, whose branches turned toward him, and the roots thereof were under him: so it became a vine, and brought forth branches, and shot forth sprigs. There was also another great eagle with great wings and many feathers: and, behold, this vine did bend her roots toward him, and shot forth her branches toward him, that he might water it by the furrows of her plantation. It was planted in a good soil by many waters, that it might bring forth branches, and that it might bear fruit, that it might be a goodly vine. Say: Thus says the Lord God. Shall it prosper? Shall he not pull up the roots thereof, and cut off the fruit thereof, that it wither? All the leaves of her spring shall wither, without great power or many people to pluck it up by the roots thereof. Behold, it is planted: shall it prosper? Shall it not utterly wither, when the east wind touches it? It shall wither in the furrows where it grew. Moreover the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Say now to the rebellious house: Do you not know what these things mean? Tell them: Behold, the king of Babylon has come to Jerusalem, and has taken its king and its princes, and led them with him to Babylon. And he has taken one of the royal family and made a covenant with him, and has put him under an oath: he has also taken away the mighty of the land, that the kingdom might be base, that it might not lift itself up, but that by keeping his covenant it might stand. But he rebelled against him by sending his ambassadors into Egypt, that they might give him horses and many troops. Shall he prosper? Shall he escape who does such things? Or shall he break the covenant and be delivered? As I live, says the Lord God, surely in the place where the king dwells who made him king, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke, even with him in the midst of Babylon shall he die. Neither shall Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company help him in the war, when they cast up mounds and build siege-works to cut off many lives. Since he despised the oath by breaking the covenant, when, behold, he had given his hand, and has done all these things, he shall not escape. Therefore thus says the Lord God: As I live, surely my oath that he has despised, and my covenant that he has broken, I will recompense upon his own head. And I will spread my net over him, and he shall be taken in my snare, and I will bring him to Babylon and will plead with him there for his trespass that he has committed against me. And all his fugitives with all his troops shall fall by the sword, and they who remain shall be scattered toward every wind: and you shall know that I the Lord have spoken it. Thus says the Lord God: I will also take of the top of the high cedar, and will set it out; from the topmost of its young twigs I will pluck a tender one, and I will plant it upon a high and lofty mountain. On the mountain height of Israel will I plant it, and it shall bring forth boughs, and bear fruit, and be a noble cedar. And under it shall dwell all birds of every wing; in the shade of its branches they shall dwell. And all the trees of the field shall know that I the Lord have brought down the high tree, and exalted the low tree, have dried up the green tree, and have made the dry tree flourish. I

Ezekiel. Chapter 18.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: What do you mean by using this proverb in the land of Israel, saying: "The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge"? As I live, says the Lord God, this proverb shall no more be used by you in Israel. Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine. The soul that sins shall die. If a man is just and does what is lawful and right, and has not eaten upon the mountains, nor lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, nor defiled his neighbor's wife, nor approached a menstruating woman, nor oppressed any person, but has restored the debtor's pledge, has taken nothing by robbery, has given his bread to the hungry, and has covered the naked with a garment, has not lent at interest or taken any profit, has withheld his hand from iniquity, and has executed true judgment between man and man, has walked in my statutes and kept my ordinances faithfully — this man is just; he shall surely live, says the Lord God.

If he has begotten a son who is a robber, a shedder of blood, who does any one of these things, and who does none of those duties, but even has eaten on the mountains, and defiled his neighbor's wife, has oppressed the poor and needy, has taken by robbery, has not restored the pledge, and has lifted up his eyes to the idols, has committed abomination, has lent at interest and taken profit — shall he then live? He shall not live. He has done all these abominations; he shall surely die; his blood shall be upon himself.

Now behold, if he has begotten a son who sees all the sins which his father has done, and fears, and does not do likewise — has not eaten on the mountains, nor lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, nor defiled his neighbor's way, has not oppressed anyone, nor withheld a pledge, nor taken by robbery, but has given his bread to the hungry and covered the naked with a garment, has withheld his hand from harming the poor, has not taken interest or profit, has executed my judgments, and has walked in my statutes — he shall not die for his father's iniquity; he shall surely live.

His father, because he practiced extortion, robbed his brother, and did what is not good among his people — behold, he shall die for his iniquity. Yet you say: "Why should not the son bear the punishment of the father?" When the son has done what is lawful and right, and has kept all my statutes and done them, he shall surely live. The soul that sins shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, nor shall the father bear the iniquity of the son. The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon himself, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon himself.

But if the wicked man turns away from all his sins that he has committed, and keeps all my statutes and does what is lawful and right, he shall surely live; he shall not die. None of the transgressions that he has committed shall be remembered against him; for the righteousness that he has done he shall live. Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked, says the Lord God, and not rather that he should turn from his way and live? But if a just man turns away from his justice and commits iniquity, according to all the abominations that the wicked man practices — shall he live? All his righteous deeds that he has done shall not be remembered; in his treachery that he has committed, and in his sin that he has sinned, in these he shall die.

Yet you say: "The way of the Lord is not fair." Hear now, O house of Israel: Is my way not fair? Is it not rather your ways that are not fair? When a just man turns away from his justice and commits iniquity —

Ezekiel.

They provoked me and would not hear me. Each one did not abandon their abominations, nor did they forsake the idols of Egypt. And I said I would pour out my indignation upon them and fulfill my anger against them in the midst of the land of Egypt. But I acted for the sake of my name, that it should not be profaned before the nations in whose midst they were, among whom I had made myself known to them, to bring them out of the land of Egypt. So I cast them out of the land of Egypt and led them into the desert. And I gave them my commandments and showed them my judgments, by which, if a man does them, he shall live. Moreover I also gave them my sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them, that they might know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them. But the house of Israel provoked me in the desert; they did not walk in my statutes, and they despised my judgments, by which, if a man does them, he shall live; and they greatly profaned my sabbaths. Then I said I would pour out my fury upon them in the desert to consume them. But I acted for my name's sake, that it should not be profaned before the nations in whose sight I had brought them out. Yet I also lifted up my hand to them in the desert, that I would not bring them into the land which I had given them, flowing with milk and honey, the most excellent of all lands; because they rejected my judgments and did not walk in my statutes, and profaned my sabbaths: for their heart went after their idols. Nevertheless my eye spared them, and I did not destroy them, nor did I make an end of them in the desert. And I said to their children in the wilderness: Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers, nor observe their judgments, nor defile yourselves with their idols. I am the Lord your God. Walk in my statutes and keep my judgments and do them; and hallow my sabbaths, and they shall be a sign between me and you, that you may know that I am the Lord your God. But the children rebelled against me and did not walk in my statutes, and did not keep my judgments to do them, which if a man does, he shall live in them; they profaned my sabbaths. Then I said I would pour out my fury upon them and accomplish my anger against them in the desert. Nevertheless I withdrew my hand and acted for my name's sake, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations before whose eyes I had brought them out. I also lifted up my hand against them in the desert to scatter them among the nations and to disperse them through the lands, because they had not executed my judgments, but had rejected my statutes and profaned my sabbaths, and their eyes were fixed after their fathers' idols. Therefore I also gave them statutes that were not good, and judgments whereby they should not live; and I polluted them in their own gifts, in that they caused to pass through the fire all that opened the womb, that I might make them desolate, to the end that they might know that I am the Lord. Therefore speak to the house of Israel, O son of man, and say to them: Thus says the Lord God. Your fathers also blasphemed me in this, in that they trespassed against me: when I had brought them into the land for which I had lifted up my hand to give it to them, then they saw every high hill and every thick tree, and they offered there their sacrifices, and there they presented the provocation of their offering, and there they made their sweet savor, and they poured out there their drink offerings. Then I said to them: What is this high place to which you go? And its name is called Bamah to this day. Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God. Are you not polluted after the manner of your fathers, and do you not commit fornication after their abominations? And when you offer your gifts, when you make your sons pass through the fire, you defile yourselves with all your idols to this day; and shall I be inquired of by you, O house of Israel? As I live, says the Lord God, I will not

Ezekiel.

The sword, the sword is sharpened and also polished. It is sharpened to make a slaughter; it is polished to flash like lightning. You who move the scepter of my son, you have cut down every tree. I have given it to be polished, that it may be handled. The sword is sharpened, and it is polished, in the hand of the slayer. Cry and howl, son of man, for it is against my people, against all the princes of Israel — they are delivered to the sword together with my people. Smite therefore upon your thigh, for it is tested; and why, seeing it despises even the rod? It shall be no more, says the Lord God. You therefore, son of man, prophesy and smite your hands together; and let the sword be doubled the third time, the sword of the slain. It is the sword of the great slaughter, which causes men to be amazed and to melt at heart, and multiplies the ruins. I have set the point of the sword against all their gates, that the heart may melt and the ruins be multiplied. Ah, it is made bright, it is wrapped up for the slaughter. Go one way or the other, to the right hand or to the left, wherever your face is directed. I will also smite my hands together and I will cause my fury to rest: I the Lord have spoken it. The word of the Lord came to me again, saying: Also, son of man, appoint two ways that the sword of the king of Babylon may come; both shall come forth from the same land. And he shall choose a place at the head of the way to the city. You shall appoint a way for the sword to come to Rabbath of the children of Ammon, and to Judah in Jerusalem the fortified. For the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination; he made his arrows bright, he consulted with images, he looked in the liver. At his right hand was the divination for Jerusalem, to set battering rams, to open the mouth in the slaughter, to lift up the voice with shouting, to set battering rams against the gates, to cast a mount, and to build a siege fort.

And it shall be to them as a false divination in their sight, to those who have sworn oaths; but he will call iniquity to remembrance, that they may be seized. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have made your iniquity to be remembered, in that your transgressions are revealed, so that in all your doings your sins appear — because you are come to remembrance, you shall be taken by the hand. And you, O unhallowed wicked prince of Israel, whose day has come, at the time of the iniquity of the end, thus says the Lord God: Remove the turban, take off the crown; this shall be no more as it was. Exalt the humble and abase the proud. I will overturn, overturn, overturn it; and it shall be no more, until he comes whose right it is, and I will give it him. And you, son of man, prophesy and say, Thus says the Lord God concerning the children of Ammon and concerning their reproach. Say: The sword, the sword is drawn; for the slaughter it is polished, to consume because of the glittering — while they see vanity to you, while they divine a lie to you — to bring you upon the necks of the wicked who are slain, whose day has come, at the time of iniquity of the end. Return it to its sheath. In the place where you were created, in the land of your birth, I will judge you. I will pour out my indignation upon you; I will blow against you in the fire of my wrath, and deliver you into the hands of brutish men, skilled in destruction. You shall be fuel for the fire; your blood shall be in the midst of the land; you shall be no more remembered, for I the Lord have spoken it. Chapter 22.

The word of the Lord came to me, saying: Now, son of man, will you judge the bloody city? Then show her all her abominations. You shall say: Thus says the Lord God — the city that sheds blood in the midst of herself, that her time may come, and makes idols against herself to defile herself. In her blood —

Ezekiel.

And I consumed them. And I have returned their deeds upon their own heads, says the Lord God.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother, and they committed fornication in Egypt. In their youth they committed fornication. There their breasts were pressed, and the nipples of their virginity were bruised. Their names were: the elder, Oholah; and her sister, Oholibah. And they became mine, and they bore sons and daughters. Now their names: Samaria is Oholah, and Jerusalem is Oholibah.

Oholah therefore fornicated against me, and was mad after her lovers, after the Assyrians who came near: clothed with blue, princes and rulers, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding upon horses. And she bestowed her fornications upon them, the choicest men of Assyria all of them, and with all those on whom she doted, with all their idols she defiled herself. Neither did she forsake her fornications from Egypt; for in her youth they had lain with her, and they had bruised her virgin breasts, and poured their fornication upon her. Therefore I delivered her into the hand of her lovers, into the hand of the Assyrians, upon whom she doted. They uncovered her nakedness; they took her sons and her daughters, and slew her with the sword. And she became famous among women; for they had executed judgment upon her.

And when her sister Oholibah saw this, she was more corrupt in her inordinate love than she, and in her fornications more than the fornications of her sister: she doted upon the Assyrians her neighbours, captains and rulers clothed most gorgeously, horsemen riding upon horses, all of them desirable young men. Then I saw that she was defiled, that they took both one way. And she increased her fornications: for she saw men portrayed upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans portrayed with red colour, girded with girdles upon their loins, exceeding in dyed attire upon their heads, all of them princes to look to, after the manner of the Babylonians of Chaldea, the land of their nativity. And as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea. And the Babylonians came to her into the bed of love, and they defiled her with their whoredom, and she was polluted with them, and her mind was alienated from them. So she discovered her fornications, and discovered her nakedness. Then my mind was alienated from her, like as my mind was alienated from her sister. Yet she multiplied her fornications, in calling to remembrance the days of her youth, wherein she had played the harlot in the land of Egypt. For she doted upon their paramours, whose flesh is as the flesh of asses, and whose issue is like the issue of horses. Thus you called to remembrance the lewdness of your youth, in bruising your teats by the Egyptians for the paps of your youth.

Therefore, O Oholibah, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will raise up your lovers against you, from whom your mind is alienated, and I will bring them against you on every side: the Babylonians, and all the Chaldeans, Pekod, and Shoa, and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them: all of them desirable young men, captains and rulers, great lords and renowned, all of them riding upon horses. And they shall come against you with chariots, wagons, and wheels, and with an assembly of people. And they shall set judgment before you, and they shall judge you according to their judgments. And I will set my jealousy against you, and they shall deal furiously with you. They shall take away your nose and your ears; and your remnant shall fall by the sword. They shall take your sons and your daughters; and your residue shall be devoured by fire.

Ezekiel

Fire shall devour you. And they shall strip you of your garments and take away your beautiful vessels. And I will make your wickedness cease from you, and your fornication from the land of Egypt. You shall not lift your eyes toward them, and you shall remember Egypt no more, because thus says the Lord God. Behold, I will deliver you into the hands of those whom you hate, into the hands of those with whom you are filled with loathing. And they shall deal with you in hatred, and they shall take away all you have worked for and leave you naked and bare, and the shame of your fornications shall be uncovered. Your wickedness and your fornications have brought this upon you, because you have fornicated after the nations among whom you were defiled with their idols. You have walked in the way of your sister, and I will give her cup into your hand. Thus says the Lord God: You shall drink of your sister's cup, which is deep and wide. You shall be for laughter and derision, which holds very much: you shall be filled with drunkenness and sorrow, with the cup of desolation and grief, even the cup of your sister Samaria. And you shall drink it and drain it, and you shall gnaw its fragments, and you shall tear your own breasts: for I have spoken it, says the Lord God. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have forgotten me and have cast me behind your back, bear also your wickedness and your fornications. And the Lord said to me: Son of man, will you judge Oolah and Oolibah? Declare to them their abominations, for they have committed adultery, and blood is on their hands, and they have committed fornication with their idols; and moreover, the sons they bore to me they offered to them to be devoured. Besides this they have done to me: they have defiled my sanctuary on that day, and they have profaned my sabbaths. And when they had sacrificed their sons to their idols, they also went into my sanctuary on that day to defile it; and this they did in the midst of my house.

They sent for men coming from far away, to whom a messenger was sent. And behold, they came, for whom you washed yourself, painted your eyes with stibium, and adorned yourself with ornaments. You sat upon a most beautiful bed, and a table was set before you. You placed my incense and my ointment upon it, and the voice of a great multitude at ease was there. And to the men of the multitude brought from the wilderness, they put bracelets on their hands and beautiful crowns upon their heads. And I said to her who was worn out in adulteries: now she will continue to commit fornication. And they went in to her as they would go in to a harlot, so they went in to Oolah and Oolibah, vile women. But just men shall judge them with the judgment of adulteresses and with the judgment of those who shed blood, because they are adulteresses and blood is on their hands. For thus says the Lord God: Bring up a company against them and make them an object of terror and plunder. Let the company stone them and cut them down with their swords; they shall slay their sons and daughters and burn their houses with fire. Thus they shall remove wickedness from the land, and all women shall take warning and not commit wickedness as you have done. And they shall recompense your wickedness upon you, and you shall bear the sins of your idols; and you shall know that I am the Lord God. Chapter 24.

And the word of the Lord came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, saying: Son of man, write down the name of this day, this very day: the king of Babylon has set himself against Jerusalem this very day. And speak a parable to the rebellious house and say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Set on the pot, set it on, and also pour water into it. Gather the pieces into it:

Ezekiel.

I will give you as a possession to the peoples of the east, and they shall set up their encampments among you and pitch their tents among you. They shall eat your crops and drink your milk. I will make Rabbah a pasture for camels and the Ammonites a resting place for flocks. Then you will know that I am the Lord, for this is what the Lord God says. Because you clapped your hands and stamped your feet and rejoiced with all your contempt for the land of Israel, therefore I will stretch out my hand against you and give you as plunder to the nations. I will cut you off from the peoples and eliminate you from the countries and destroy you. Then you will know that I am the Lord. This is what the Lord God says. Because Moab and Seir said, "Look, the house of Judah is like all the other nations," therefore I will lay open the flank of Moab, beginning at its frontier towns — Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim — the glory of that land. I will give it along with Moab to the peoples of the east, so that the Ammonites will no longer be remembered among the nations. And I will execute judgments upon Moab. Then they will know that I am the Lord. This is what the Lord God says. Because Edom took revenge on the house of Judah and became guilty by taking vengeance upon them, therefore this is what the Lord God says: I will stretch out my hand against Edom and remove from it people and animals, and I will make it desolate. Those in Teman and Dedan will fall by the sword. I will take my vengeance on Edom by the hand of my people Israel, and they will deal with Edom according to my anger and fury, and they shall know my vengeance, declares the Lord God. This is what the Lord God says. Because the Philistines acted in vengeance and took revenge with malice in their hearts, destroying with age-old hostility, therefore this is what the Lord God says: I will stretch out my hand against the Philistines and

I will cut off the Cherethites and destroy the rest of the seacoast. I will execute great acts of vengeance on them with furious rebukes, and they will know that I am the Lord when I lay my vengeance upon them. Chapter 26.
In the eleventh year, on the first of the month, the word of the Lord came to me: Son of man, because Tyre said of Jerusalem, "Aha, the gate of the peoples is broken; it has swung open to me. I shall be replenished now that she is laid waste," therefore this is what the Lord God says: I am against you, O Tyre, and I will bring many nations up against you, as the sea brings up its waves. They will destroy the walls of Tyre and pull down her towers. I will scrape away her rubble and make her a bare rock. She will become a place to spread fishnets, in the middle of the sea, for I have spoken, declares the Lord God, and she will become plunder for the nations. Her daughters on the mainland will be slain by the sword, and they will know that I am the Lord. For thus says the Lord God: I will bring against Tyre from the north Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, with horses, chariots, cavalry, and a great army. Your daughters on the mainland he will kill by the sword. He will build siege works against you, heap up a mound against you, and raise a wall of shields against you. He will direct the blow of his battering rams against your walls and demolish your towers with his weapons. His horses will be so many that their dust will cover you; your walls will shake at the noise of cavalry, wagon wheels, and chariots when he enters your gates like warriors entering a captured city. With the hooves of his horses he will trample all your streets; he will kill your people with the sword, and your strong pillars will fall to the ground. They will plunder your riches and loot your merchandise.

Ezekiel.

And they shall destroy your walls and throw down your fine houses; they shall cast your stones and your timber and your dust into the sea. And I will cause the sound of your songs to cease, and the sound of your harps shall be heard no more. I will make you a bare rock; you shall be a place for the spreading of nets, and you shall never be rebuilt, for I the Lord have spoken, says the Lord God. Thus says the Lord God to Tyre: Shall not the coastlands shake at the sound of your fall, at the cry of your wounded, when the slaughter is made in the midst of you? Then all the princes of the sea shall come down from their thrones and lay aside their robes and strip off their embroidered garments. They shall clothe themselves with trembling; they shall sit on the ground and tremble every moment and be appalled at you. And they shall raise a lamentation over you and say to you: How you have perished, you who were inhabited from the seas, O renowned city, which was mighty on the sea, she and her inhabitants, who imposed their terror on all who dwelt there! Now shall the coastlands tremble in the day of your fall; yes, the coastlands that are by the sea shall be troubled at your departure. For thus says the Lord God: When I shall make you a desolate city, like the cities that are not inhabited; when I shall bring up the deep upon you, and great waters shall cover you; when I bring you down with those who descend into the pit, to the people of old, and I shall set you in the low parts of the earth, in places desolate of old, with those who go down to the pit, so that you will not be inhabited; and I shall give glory in the land of the living — I will make you a terror, and you shall be no more; though you be sought for, yet you shall never be found again, says the Lord God. Chapter 27. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Now, son of man, take up a lamentation for Tyre, and say to Tyre, who dwells at the entrance of the sea, merchant of the peoples to many coastlands: Thus says the Lord God: O Tyre, you have said, I am perfect in beauty. Your borders are in the heart of the seas. Your builders made your beauty perfect; they built all your planks of fir trees from Senir; they took a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you. Of oaks from Bashan they made your oars; your deck they made of ivory from the isles of the Kittim. Fine embroidered linen from Egypt was used for your sail and served as your banner; blue and purple from the coasts of Elishah was your awning. The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers; your skilled men, O Tyre, were in you; they were your pilots. The elders of Gebal and her skilled men were in you, caulking your seams; all the ships of the sea with their mariners were in you to barter for your wares. Men of Persia and Lud and Put were in your army, your men of war; they hung shield and helmet in you; they gave you your splendor. The men of Arvad with your army were on your walls all around, and men of Gammad were in your towers; they hung their shields upon your walls all around; they made your beauty perfect. Carthaginians were your merchants; because of the abundance of all kinds of wealth, with silver, iron, tin, and lead they traded in your markets. Greece, Tubal, and Meshech, they were your merchants; they traded the persons of men and vessels of bronze for your merchandise. From the house of Togarmah they traded horses, horsemen, and mules for your wares. The men of Dedan were your merchants. Many coastlands were your markets. They brought you in payment ivory tusks and ebony. Syria was your merchant. Because of your many goods they traded emerald, purple,

Ezekiel

and against them who dwell among you, the Lord God has humbled you and dissolved all your strength; therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will bring a sword upon you, and will cut off from you man and beast. And the land of Egypt shall be made desolate and waste; and they shall know that I am the Lord. Because you said, The river is mine, and I made it; therefore, behold, I am against you and against your rivers. And I will give the land of Egypt to be a desolation and a waste, by the sword, from the tower of Syene even to the borders of Ethiopia. No human foot shall pass through it, nor any beast's foot; neither shall it be inhabited for forty years. I will make the land of Egypt desolate in the midst of desolate countries, and her cities shall be laid waste in the midst of cities that are laid waste, for forty years. And I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and will disperse them throughout the lands; for thus says the Lord God. After forty years I will gather Egypt from the peoples among whom they have been scattered, and I will bring back the captivity of Egypt and settle them in the land of Pathros, their native land, the land from which they came. And there they shall be a lowly kingdom, and among kingdoms it shall be the lowest. And it shall no longer exalt itself above the nations; and I will diminish them, so that they shall not rule over the nations; and they shall no more be the confidence of the house of Israel, calling their sin to remembrance when they turn after them; and they shall know that I am the Lord God. In the twenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me: Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made his army labor hard against Tyre; every head was made bald, and every shoulder was rubbed bare; yet neither he nor his army received payment from Tyre for the labor that they did against it. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; and he shall carry off her wealth and plunder her spoil and take her prey; and it shall be the wages for his army. I have given him the land of Egypt as his payment for which he labored, says the Lord God. In that day I will cause a horn to spring up for the house of Israel, and I will open your lips among them; and they shall know that I am the Lord. Chapter 30. The word of the Lord came to me: Son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord God: Wail, alas for the day! For the day is near, the day of the Lord is near; it will be a day of clouds, a time of doom for the nations. A sword shall come upon Egypt, and anguish shall be in Ethiopia when the slain fall in Egypt, and her wealth is carried away, and her foundations are torn down. Ethiopia, and Libya, and Lydia, and all the mixed people, and Chub, and the men of the land that is in league — they shall fall by the sword. Thus says the Lord God: Those who support Egypt shall fall, and its proud might shall come down; from the tower of Syene they shall fall by the sword, says the Lord of hosts. And they shall be laid waste in the midst of desolate countries, and their cities shall be in the midst of ruined cities; and they shall know that I am the Lord, when I set fire to Egypt, and all her allies are broken. In that day, messengers shall go out from me in ships to strike the confident Ethiopians with terror; and anguish shall come upon them in the day of Egypt's doom; for it is surely coming. Thus says the Lord God: I will put an end to the wealth of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He and his people with him, the most ruthless of nations, shall be brought in to destroy the land; and they shall draw their swords against

Ezekiel.

Egypt, and they will fill the land with the slain; and I will make the channels of the rivers dry, and will deliver the land into the hand of the wicked; and I will lay waste the land and its fullness by the hand of strangers. I the Lord have spoken. Thus says the Lord God: I will also destroy the idols, and I will cause the images to cease from Memphis; and there shall be no more a prince from the land of Egypt. And I will put fear in the land of Egypt; and I will make the land desolate, and I will set fire in Tahpanhes, and I will execute judgments upon Alexandria. And I will pour out my fury upon Pelusium, the strength of Egypt, and I will cut off the multitude of Alexandria, and I will set fire in Egypt. Pelusium shall have great anguish, and Alexandria shall be torn asunder, and Memphis shall have daily distresses. The young men of Heliopolis and Bubastis shall fall by the sword, and these cities shall go into captivity. In Tahpanhes also the day shall be darkened, when I shall break there the scepters of Egypt; and the pomp of her strength shall cease. A cloud shall cover her, and her daughters shall go into captivity. I will execute judgments upon Egypt, and they shall know that I am the Lord. And it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh of the month, that the word of the Lord came to me saying: Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and lo, it has not been bound up to be healed, to put a bandage to bind it, giving it strength to hold the sword. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and will break his arms, the strong and that which was broken, and I will cause the sword to fall out of his hand. And I will scatter Egypt among the nations, and will disperse them through the countries. And I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, and put my sword in his hand; and I will break Pharaoh's arms, and he shall groan before him with the groanings of a deadly wounded man. And I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon; and the arms of Pharaoh shall fall down. And they shall know that I am the Lord, when I shall put my sword into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall stretch it out upon the land of Egypt. And I will scatter Egypt among the nations, and disperse them through the countries; and they shall know that I am the Lord. Chapter 31.

And it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first of the month, that the word of the Lord came to me saying: Son of man, speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude: To whom are you like in your greatness? Behold, Assyria was like a cedar in Lebanon, beautiful in branches and thick shade, and of high stature; and its top was among the thick boughs. The waters nourished it, the deep made it to grow high; the rivers ran around its roots, and sent out streams to all the trees of the field. Therefore its height was exalted above all the trees of the field, and its boughs were multiplied, and its branches grew long because of the great waters. All the birds of the air made their nests in its boughs, and under its branches all the animals of the field gave birth, and under its shadow dwelt all great nations. Thus it was beautiful in its greatness, in the length of its branches, for its roots were near great waters. The cedars in the garden of God could not hide it; the fir trees were not like its boughs, and the plane trees were not like its branches; nor was any tree in the garden of God like it in beauty. I made it beautiful with a multitude of branches, so that all the trees of Eden envied it, that were in the garden of God. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because it is lifted up in height

Ezekiel

in its height and gave its top its fullness, its abundant foliage, and its height was raised above all the trees of the field, and I delivered it into the hand of the mightiest of nations. He shall deal with it according to its wickedness. And I have cast it out; and strangers, the most terrible of the nations, have cut it down and left it. On the mountains and in all the valleys its branches have fallen, and its boughs have been broken in all the ravines of the earth; and all the peoples of the earth have gone down from its shade and left it. On its fallen trunk all the birds of the sky have settled, and among its boughs all the beasts of the field have made their home. Therefore no trees of the waters shall exalt themselves in their height, nor shall they set their tops among the thick boughs, nor shall any tree that drinks water stand in its height; for they are all delivered to death, to the lowest parts of the earth, in the midst of the children of men, with those who go down to the pit. Thus says the Lord God: On the day he went down to the grave, I covered him with the deep, and I restrained his rivers, and the great waters were held back. I put Lebanon in mourning for him, and all the trees of the field fainted because of him. I made the nations shake at the sound of his fall, when I cast him down to the grave with those who go down to the pit. And all the trees of Eden, the choicest and best of Lebanon, all that drink water, were comforted in the depths of the earth. They also went down with him to the grave, with those killed by the sword; and those who were his strong arm dwelt in his shade among the nations. To whom are you thus equal in glory and in greatness among the trees of Eden? Yet you shall be brought down with the trees of Eden to the lowest parts of the earth. In the midst of the uncircumcised you shall lie, with those slain by the sword.

This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, says the Lord God. Chapter 32.

And it came to pass in the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, on the first day of the month, that the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, take up a lamentation over Pharaoh king of Egypt, and say to him: You are like a lion of the nations, and you are like a dragon in the sea. You burst forth in your rivers, and troubled the waters with your feet, and fouled their rivers. Therefore thus says the Lord God: I will spread my net over you with a company of many peoples, and they will haul you up in my net. And I will cast you on the ground; I will hurl you on the open field, and will cause all the birds of the sky to settle on you, and I will satisfy the beasts of the whole earth with you. And I will lay your flesh on the mountains, and fill the valleys with your carcass. And I will water the land even to the mountains with your blood that flows from you, and the ravines shall be full of you. When I put you out, I will cover the sky and make its stars dark; I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give its light. All the bright lights of the sky I will make dark over you, and I will bring darkness over your land, says the Lord God. I will also trouble the hearts of many peoples when I bring your destruction among the nations, into lands you have not known. And I will make many peoples appalled at you, and their kings shall be horrified because of you, when I brandish my sword before them; they shall tremble every moment, every man for his own life, in the day of your fall. For thus says the Lord God: The sword of the king of Babylon shall come upon you. By the swords of the mighty I will cause your multitude to fall. All these nations are most ruthless. And they shall plunder the pride of Egypt, and all its multitude shall be destroyed. I will also destroy all its livestock that were beside many waters; and no more

Ezekiel.

I was profaned among the nations where you went; but I will sanctify my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, which you have profaned in their midst; and the nations shall know that I am the Lord, says the Lord God, when I shall be sanctified in you before their eyes. For I will take you from among the nations, and gather you out of all countries, and will bring you into your own land. Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean; from all your filthiness and from all your idols, will I cleanse you. A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you. And I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh. And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my judgments and do them. And you shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers; and you shall be my people, and I will be your God. I will also save you from all your uncleannesses; and I will call for the grain, and will increase it, and lay no famine upon you. And I will multiply the fruit of the tree, and the increase of the field, that you shall receive no more reproach of famine among the heathen. Then shall you remember your own evil ways, and your doings that were not good, and shall loathe yourselves. Not for your sakes do I this, says the Lord God, be it known unto you; be ashamed and confounded for your own ways, O house of Israel. Thus says the Lord God: In the day that I shall have cleansed you from all your iniquities, I will also cause you to dwell in the cities, and the wastes shall be rebuilt. And the desolate land shall be tilled, whereas it lay desolate in the sight of all that passed by. And they shall say: This land that was desolate is become like the garden of Eden; and the waste and desolate and ruined cities are become fenced and inhabited. Then the heathen that are left round about you shall know that I the Lord

have built the ruined places and planted what was desolate; I the Lord have spoken it, and I will do it. Thus says the Lord God: I will yet for this be inquired of by the house of Israel, to do it for them; I will increase them with men like a flock. As the holy flock, as the flock of Jerusalem in her solemn feasts; so shall the waste cities be filled with flocks of men; and they shall know that I am the Lord. Chapter 37.

The hand of the Lord was upon me, and carried me out in the spirit of the Lord, and set me down in the midst of a valley which was full of bones. And he caused me to pass by them round about: and, behold, there were very many in the open valley; and, lo, they were very dry. And he said unto me: Son of man, can these bones live? And I answered: O Lord God, you know. Again he said unto me: Prophesy upon these bones, and say unto them: O ye dry bones, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God unto these bones: Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and you shall live. And I will lay sinews upon you, and will bring up flesh upon you, and cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and you shall live; and you shall know that I am the Lord. So I prophesied as I was commanded: and as I prophesied, there was a noise, and behold a shaking, and the bones came together, bone to his bone. And when I beheld, lo, the sinews and the flesh came up upon them, and the skin covered them above: but there was no breath in them. Then said he unto me: Prophesy unto the wind, prophesy, son of man, and say to the wind: Thus says the Lord God: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live. So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army. Then he said unto me: Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel.

Ezekiel.

They say: Our bones are dried up and our hope is lost, and we are cut off. Therefore prophesy and say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will open your graves and bring you out of your sepulchres, O my people, and I will bring you into the land of Israel. And you shall know that I am the Lord, when I have opened your graves and brought you up out of your graves, O my people. And I shall put my spirit in you and you shall live. And I will cause you to rest upon your own soil, and you shall know that I the Lord have spoken and done it, says the Lord God. And the word of the Lord came to me saying: And you, son of man, take for yourself one stick and write upon it: for Judah and for the children of Israel his companions. And take another stick and write upon it: for Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions. And join them one to another into one stick, and they shall become one in your hand. And when the children of your people shall speak to you saying, Will you not show us what you mean by these things? Say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph which is in the hand of Ephraim and the tribes of Israel his companions, and I will put them together with the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, and they shall be one in my hand. And the sticks on which you write shall be in your hand before their eyes, and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the nations to which they have gone, and will gather them from every side and bring them into their own land. And I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king shall be king over all of them. They shall no longer be two nations, nor shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more. Nor shall they defile themselves any more with their idols and their abominations and all their transgressions, and I will save them from all their dwelling places

in which they have sinned, and I will cleanse them. And they shall be my people, and I will be their God. And my servant David shall be king over them, and they shall all have one shepherd. They shall walk in my judgments and observe my statutes and do them. And they shall dwell in the land that I gave to my servant Jacob, in which your fathers dwelt, and they shall dwell there, they and their children and their children's children forever, and David my servant shall be their prince forever. And I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them. And I will establish them and multiply them and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them forevermore. And my tabernacle shall be with them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. And the nations shall know that I the Lord sanctify Israel, when my sanctuary shall be in the midst of them forevermore. Chapter 38.

And the word of the Lord came to me saying: Son of man, set your face against Gog, the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him and say to him: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. And I will turn you about and put hooks in your jaws and bring you out with all your army, horses and horsemen, all of them clothed in full armor, a great host with buckler and shield, all of them wielding swords. Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya are with them, all of them with shield and helmet. Gomer and all his troops; the house of Togarmah from the far north and all its troops, and many peoples with you. Prepare yourself, yes, equip yourself, you and all your hosts that are assembled about you, and you shall be their guard. After many days you will be mustered. In the latter years you will come into the land that is restored from the sword, gathered from many peoples, upon the mountains of Israel which had been

Ezekiel.

my holy name no more; and the nations shall know that I am the Lord, the Holy One of Israel. Behold, it has come and it is done, says the Lord God. This is the day of which I have spoken. And the inhabitants of the cities of Israel shall go forth and shall set on fire and burn the weapons, the shields and the spears, the bows and the arrows, and the handstaves and the lances, and they shall burn them with fire for seven years. They shall not take wood from the fields, neither shall they cut down any from the forests; for they shall burn the weapons with fire, and they shall plunder those who plundered them and despoil those who despoiled them, says the Lord God. And it shall come to pass on that day that I will give to Gog a place for burial in Israel, the valley of the travelers to the east of the sea, and it shall stop the passage of travelers, and there they shall bury Gog and all his multitude, and they shall call it the Valley of the Multitude of Gog. And the house of Israel shall be burying them for seven months, in order to cleanse the land. All the people of the land shall bury them, and it shall bring them renown on the day on which I shall be glorified, says the Lord God. And they shall appoint men to continually pass through the land to bury and search out those remaining on the face of the earth, to cleanse it. After seven months they shall begin to search, and those who pass through the land shall go about it. When any sees a human bone, he shall set up a marker by it, until the burial men have buried it in the Valley of the Multitude of Gog. The name of the city shall be Hamonah; thus shall they cleanse the land. And you, son of man, thus says the Lord God: Speak to every bird and to all the beasts of the field, Assemble and come, gather from every side to my sacrificial feast which I am preparing for you, a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, that you may eat flesh and drink blood. You shall eat the flesh of the mighty and drink the blood of the princes of the earth:

of rams, of lambs, and of goats, of bulls, all of them fatlings of Bashan. You shall eat fat until you are full and drink blood until you are drunk, at the sacrificial feast which I am preparing for you. And you shall be satisfied at my table with horses and riders, with mighty men and all the men of war, says the Lord God. And I will set my glory among the nations, and all the nations shall see my judgment that I have executed, and my hand that I have laid upon them. The house of Israel shall know that I am the Lord their God, from that day forward. And the nations shall know that the house of Israel went into captivity for their iniquity, because they dealt treacherously with me, and I hid my face from them and gave them into the hand of their adversaries, and they all fell by the sword. According to their uncleanness and their transgressions I dealt with them, and I hid my face from them. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Now I will restore the fortunes of Jacob and have mercy on the whole house of Israel, and I will be jealous for my holy name. They shall bear their shame and all the treachery they have committed against me, when they dwell securely in their land with none to make them afraid, when I have brought them back from the peoples and gathered them from the lands of their enemies, and in them I have vindicated my holiness in the sight of many nations. Then they shall know that I am the Lord their God, when I have gathered them to their own land and left none of them behind, and I will not hide my face any more from them, for I have poured out my Spirit upon the house of Israel, says the Lord God. In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was struck down, on that very day, the hand of the Lord was upon me, and he brought me to the city in visions of God.

Ezekiel.

of God. He brought me into the land of Israel and set me down on a very high mountain, on which was something like the structure of a city to the south. He brought me there, and I saw a man whose appearance was like bronze, with a linen cord and a measuring rod in his hand. He was standing in the gateway and said to me: Son of man, look with your eyes and hear with your ears, and pay attention to everything I am going to show you, for you have been brought here so that it might be shown to you. Declare to the house of Israel everything you see. And behold, there was a wall all around the outside of the temple, and in the man's hand was a measuring rod six cubits and a handbreadth long. He measured the thickness of the wall structure, one rod; and the height, one rod. Then he went to the gate that faced east, climbed its steps, and measured the threshold of the gate, one rod wide; and each alcove was one rod long and one rod wide; the space between the alcoves was five cubits; and the threshold of the gate next to the vestibule of the gate on the inner side was one rod. He measured the vestibule of the gateway, eight cubits; and its jambs, two cubits. The vestibule of the gate was on the inner side. The alcoves of the eastern gate were three on each side, all three the same size, and the jambs on either side were the same size. He measured the width of the gateway, ten cubits, and the length thirteen cubits. The space in front of the alcoves was one cubit on either side. Each alcove was six cubits on each side. He measured the gate from the roof of one alcove to the roof of the other, twenty-five cubits wide, opening opposite opening.

He made the facade sixty cubits long, up to the front of the court all around; and before the face of the gate reaching to the front of the vestibule of the inner gate was fifty cubits. With narrow windows in the alcoves and in their jambs inside the gate all around, and likewise in the vestibules, windows all around on the inside, and on the jambs were carved palm trees. He brought me into the outer court, and there were chambers and a pavement made for the court all around. Thirty chambers faced the pavement. The pavement ran alongside the gates, corresponding to the length of the gates; this was the lower pavement. Then he measured the distance from the front of the lower gate to the front of the inner court on the outside, a hundred cubits on the east and on the north. The gate facing north—he measured its length and its width, its alcoves, three on each side, its jambs and its vestibule, having the same measurements as the first gate. Its length was fifty cubits, and its width twenty-five cubits. Its windows, its vestibule, and its palm trees were according to the size of the gate that faced east. Seven steps led up to it, and its vestibule was ahead of them. The inner gate faced the outer gate on the north and east. He measured from one gate to the other, a hundred cubits. Then he brought me toward the south, and I saw a gate facing south. He measured its jambs and its vestibule; they had the same measurements as the others. The gate and its vestibule had windows all around; it was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide. Seven steps led up to it, and its vestibule was in front of them; it had palm trees on either side on its jambs; and the inner court had

Ezekiel.

[He measured] in the south road. And he measured from gate to gate along the south road: one hundred cubits. And he brought me into the inner court by the south gate, and measured the gate according to the upper measurements — its chambers, its front, and its vestibule — with the same measurements as before; and its windows and its vestibule in circuit: fifty cubits in length and twenty-five cubits in width; and the vestibule around it in length twenty-five cubits and in width five cubits. And its vestibule faced the outer court, with palm trees on its front, and there were eight steps by which one ascended to it. And he brought me into the inner court by the east gate, and measured the gate according to the upper measurements — its chambers and its front and its vestibules as before; and its windows and its vestibules. In circuit: fifty cubits in length and twenty-five cubits in width; and the vestibule — that is, of the court of the recess — and palm trees placed on its front, one on each side; and it had eight steps of ascent. And he brought me to the gate that faced north. And he measured it according to the upper measurements — its chambers, its front, and its vestibule, and its windows in circuit: fifty cubits in length and twenty-five cubits in width; and its vestibule faced the outer court, with palm trees on its front on either side, and eight steps of ascent. And at each of the little treasury chambers there was a door on the front of the gates. There they were to wash the burnt offerings. And in the vestibule of the gate there were two tables on this side and two tables on that side, upon which the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering were to be slaughtered. And on the outer side, as one goes up to the entrance of the gate facing north, there were two tables; and on the other side of the vestibule of the gate, two tables. Four tables on this side and four tables on that side at the sides of the gate: eight tables, upon which they were to slaughter.

And four tables for the burnt offerings were of hewn stone, a cubit and a half long and a cubit and a half wide and one cubit high — on these they were to lay the instruments with which the burnt offerings and sacrifices were slaughtered. And their ledges were a handbreadth wide, turned inward all around; and on the tables was the flesh of the offering. And beyond the inner gate were the chambers of the singers in the inner court, which was on the side of the gate facing north; and their front was toward the south — one on the side of the east gate, which faced toward the north. And he said to me: This treasury chamber that faces south is for the priests who have charge of the temple; and the treasury chamber that faces north is for the priests who have charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, who alone among the sons of Levi may come near to the Lord to minister to him. And he measured the court: one hundred cubits long and one hundred cubits wide, foursquare; and the altar was in front of the temple. And he brought me into the vestibule of the temple and measured the vestibule: five cubits on this side and five cubits on that side; and the breadth of the gate was three cubits on each side; and the length of the vestibule was twenty cubits, and the width eleven cubits. And by eight steps one ascended to it, and there were columns in the front, one on this side and one on that side.

And he brought me into the temple and measured the fronts: six cubits wide on this side and six cubits wide on that side — the width of the tabernacle. And the width of the entrance was ten cubits, and the sides of the entrance were five cubits on this side and five cubits on that side. And he measured its length: forty cubits, and its width —

Ezekiel.

against the separate building, and another structure pressing toward the north, facing a length of one hundred cubits on the north side, and a width of fifty cubits, with twenty cubits of the inner court, and the pavement of stone of the outer court, where there was a portico next to a triple portico. And beside the chambers, a walkway ten cubits wide facing inward, one cubit wide. And the doors toward the north, where the treasuries were, lower in the upper portions, because the portico supported what projected from them from the lower and middle parts of the building. For there were three stories, and they did not have columns as the columns of the courts did. Therefore they projected above the lower and middle levels by fifty cubits from the ground. And the outer gallery corresponding to the treasuries that were in the way of the outer court before the treasuries: its length was fifty cubits, because the length of the treasuries of the outer court was fifty cubits, and the length before the face of the temple was one hundred cubits. And below these treasuries there was an entrance from the east for those entering from the outer court, in the width of the gallery of the court that was facing the eastern way toward the separate building. And there were treasuries before the building, and a way before their face, like the arrangement of the treasuries that were on the north side. According to their length thus, and their width, their entrances and arrangements and their doors were like the doors of the treasuries that faced south. There was a door at the head of the way, which was before the vestibule of the separate building, for those entering by the eastern way. And he said to me: The northern treasuries and the southern treasuries which are before the separate building, these are

the holy treasuries, in which the priests who draw near to the Lord eat in the holy of holies. There they shall place the holy of holies, and the offering for sin, and the offering for trespass. For the place is holy. When the priests go out, they shall not go out of the holy places into the outer court, but there they shall lay down the garments in which they minister, because they are holy, and shall put on other garments, and so shall approach the people. And when he had finished measuring the interior of the house, he led me out by the way of the gate that looked toward the eastern way, and he measured it all around. He measured toward the east wind five hundred reeds by the measuring reed all around. And he measured toward the north wind five hundred reeds by the measuring reed all around. And toward the south wind he measured five hundred reeds by the measuring reed all around. And toward the west wind he measured five hundred reeds by the measuring reed. By the four winds he measured it: in length five hundred cubits, and in width five hundred cubits. And a wall divides between the sanctuary and the people's place. Chapter 43.

And he brought me to the gate that looked toward the eastern way. And behold, the glory of the God of Israel came in by the way of the east, and his voice was like the sound of many waters, and the earth shone with his majesty. And I saw a vision according to the appearance which I had seen when he came to destroy the city, and the appearance was according to the vision which I had seen by the river Chebar. And I fell upon my face. And the majesty of the Lord entered the temple by the way of the gate looking toward the east. And the spirit lifted me up:

Ezekiel.

And he brought me into the inner court. And behold, the glory of the Lord filled the house. And I heard one speaking to me from the house. And the man who stood beside me said to me: Son of man, this is the place of my throne and the place of the soles of my feet, where I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel forever. And the house of Israel shall no more defile my holy name, they and their kings, by their fornications, and by the carcasses of their kings, and by the high places, who set their threshold by my threshold, and their posts by my posts, and there was only a wall between me and them. And they defiled my holy name by the abominations which they committed, wherefore I consumed them in my anger.
